## Statement

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $U\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open subset which, with the topology of [[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]], is path-connected and simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]), and let $\alpha$ be a $C^1$ one-form on $U$ with $d\alpha=0$ ([[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]]); here closedness of a $C^1$ one-form means that in an inertial chart ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) one has $\alpha=\sum_i a_i\,dx^i$ with $\partial_i a_j=\partial_j a_i$, the exterior derivative being understood by this coefficient formula ([[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]], [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]]). Then:

(a) there is a $C^2$ function $F:U\to\mathbb R$ with $dF=\alpha$;

(b) for any two piecewise-$C^1$ paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1$ in $U$ ([[def-piecewise-c1-path-connected-conservative-and-path-independent]]) with the same endpoints, the integrals of $\alpha$ along them are equal, and consequently the integral of $\alpha$ along every piecewise-$C^1$ loop in $U$ vanishes.

If $\alpha$ is smooth, $F$ may be taken smooth.

**Conventions (what the objects mean here).** Fix one inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ and put $\Omega:=x(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^4$; by [[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]] the chart $x$ is a diffeomorphism of $A$ onto $\mathbb R^4$ carrying the model's topology, and every other inertial chart $x'$ satisfies $x'=M^{-1}(x-b)$ for an invertible matrix $M$ and a vector $b$. The $C^1$ one-form $\alpha$ is represented in the chart as $\alpha=\sum_i a_i\,dx^i$ with coefficient functions $a_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^1$; write $A:=(a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4):\Omega\to\mathbb R^4$ for the coefficient field, so that $A$ is $C^1$ and closedness reads $\partial_i a_j=\partial_j a_i$ on $\Omega$. For a piecewise-$C^1$ path $\gamma$ in $U$ the integral is $\int_\gamma\alpha:=\int_{x\circ\gamma}A\cdot d\mathbf r$, the vector-field line integral of [[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]. For a $C^1$ function $F:U\to\mathbb R$ with $\tilde F:=F\circ x^{-1}$, the differential $dF$ is the one-form whose chart coefficients are the partial derivatives $\partial_i\tilde F$, and $dF=\alpha$ means $\partial_i\tilde F=a_i$ on $\Omega$ for all $i$. Under the transition $x'=M^{-1}(x-b)$ the chain rule gives $a'_j=\sum_i M^i_j a_i$, $\partial_j\tilde F'=\sum_i M^i_j\,\partial_i\tilde F$ and $(x'\circ\gamma)'=M^{-1}(x\circ\gamma)'$, so the integral $\int_\gamma\alpha$ and the identity $dF=\alpha$ do not depend on which inertial chart is used; likewise, $F$ being $C^2$, respectively smooth, is chart-independent. It therefore suffices to prove the following statement about the open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ and the $C^1$ closed field $A$: every closed piecewise-$C^1$ path in $\Omega$ has zero $A$-integral, the $A$-integral is path-independent on $\Omega$, and there is a $C^2$ function $\tilde F$ on $\Omega$ with $\nabla\tilde F=A$ which can be taken smooth when $A$ is smooth.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), a nonempty open subset $U\subseteq A$ that is path-connected and simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]) in the topology of [[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]], and a $C^1$ one-form $\alpha$ on $U$ with $d\alpha=0$ in the coefficient sense of the Statement ([[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]], [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]]).

[F1] An inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ is a diffeomorphism of $A$ onto $\mathbb R^4$ for the model's topology (which is independent of the chart), the transitions between inertial charts are the affine bijections $x'=M^{-1}(x-b)$, and every inertial chart belongs to the same smooth structure ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[F2] $U$ is nonempty and path-connected, and for every $u\in U$ the fundamental group $\pi_1(U,u)$ has exactly one element; equivalently, every based loop at $u$ is path-homotopic relative to the endpoints to the constant loop at $u$ ([[def-simply-connected]], [[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]], [[def-homotopy-relative-and-path-homotopy]], [[def-nullhomotopic-map-and-contractible-space]]).

[F3] A path homotopy relative to the endpoints from a loop $\gamma$ at $p$ to the constant loop is a continuous $H:I\times I\to U$ with $H(s,0)=\gamma(s)$, $H(s,1)=p$ and $H(0,t)=H(1,t)=p$, where $I=[0,1]$ ([[def-homotopy-relative-and-path-homotopy]]).

[F4] For a piecewise-$C^1$ path $\gamma:[a,b]\to\mathbb R^n$ and a continuous field $F$ on a set containing its trace, $\int_\gamma F\cdot d\mathbf r$ is the sum of the integrals of $\langle F(\gamma(t)),v_i(t)\rangle$ over an admissible partition with continuous derivative extensions $v_i$, the value being independent of the admissible partition ([[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]], [[lem-line-integrals-are-independent-of-the-piecewise-c1-partition]], [[def-piecewise-c1-path-operations-and-oriented-reparametrizations]]).

[F5] Reversal, concatenation and reparametrization: $\int_{\gamma^-}F\cdot d\mathbf r=-\int_\gamma F\cdot d\mathbf r$; if $\alpha,\beta:[0,1]\to\mathbb R^n$ are piecewise-$C^1$ with $\alpha(1)=\beta(0)$ then $\int_{\alpha*\beta}F\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_\alpha F\cdot d\mathbf r+\int_\beta F\cdot d\mathbf r$; and an oriented piecewise-$C^1$ reparametrization with increasing derivative leaves the integral unchanged ([[thm-line-integrals-under-reversal-and-concatenation]], [[thm-line-integrals-under-oriented-reparametrization]], [[def-piecewise-c1-path-operations-and-oriented-reparametrizations]]).

[F6] On an open star-shaped $W\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, a $C^1$ field $F:W\to\mathbb R^n$ is closed if and only if it is exact, if and only if it is conservative, if and only if it is path-independent, if and only if the integral along every closed piecewise-$C^1$ path in $W$ vanishes; a conservative field is path-independent and has vanishing closed-path integrals; and for $C^1$ $\varphi:W\to\mathbb R$ and piecewise-$C^1$ $\gamma$ in $W$ one has $\int_\gamma\nabla\varphi\cdot d\mathbf r=\varphi(\gamma(\text{end}))-\varphi(\gamma(\text{start}))$ ([[cor-closed-exact-and-conservative-equivalence-on-star-shaped-domains]], [[cor-conservative-fields-are-path-independent-and-have-zero-circulation]], [[thm-gradient-theorem-for-line-integrals]]).

[F7] Euclidean structure and compactness: $|z|_2$ and the distance $d_2$ on $\mathbb R^n$ satisfy the triangle inequality and $|tz|_2=|t|\,|z|_2$, so every ball $B(z,r)=\{y:|y-z|_2<r\}$ is convex; a continuous image of a compact space is compact; a closed box $\{y:a_k\le y_k\le b_k\}$ in $\mathbb R^n$ is compact, and a subset of $\mathbb R^n$ is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded; a continuous map on a compact metric space is uniformly continuous ([[def-p-norms-on-rn]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-compactness]], [[thm-heine-borel-rn]], [[thm-heine-cantor-metric]]).

[F8] For every real $\varepsilon>0$ there is a natural number $m\ge1$ with $1/m<\varepsilon$ ([[cor-archimedean-reciprocal]]).

[F9] Calculus: the chain rule for composites of differentiable functions; a function whose first partial derivatives exist and are continuous is totally differentiable, so a function with continuous partial derivatives of order up to $k$ is $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]; and the first fundamental theorem of calculus for continuous integrands ([[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], [[thm-ftc-first-part]], [[def-derivative]], [[def-continuity-real]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Fix an inertial chart $x$ and put $\Omega:=x(U)$; by [F1] the chart is a diffeomorphism onto $\mathbb R^4$, so $\Omega$ is a nonempty open subset of $\mathbb R^4$, and because $x|_U:U\to\Omega$ is a homeomorphism it induces a bijection between the continuous loops at $p$ in $U$ and those at $x(p)$ in $\Omega$ and a bijection between homotopies relative to the endpoints of such loops (via composition with $x$ and $x^{-1}$); hence $\Omega$ is path-connected and $\pi_1(\Omega,u)$ has exactly one element for every $u\in\Omega$ by [F2]. Write $\alpha=\sum_i a_i\,dx^i$ in the chart with $C^1$ coefficients $a_i$ and $\partial_i a_j=\partial_j a_i$, set $A:=(a_1,\dots,a_4)$, and recall from the conventions of the Statement that $\int_\gamma\alpha=\int_{x\circ\gamma}A\cdot d\mathbf r$ for piecewise-$C^1$ $\gamma$, that $dF=\alpha$ means $\partial_i\tilde F=a_i$ for $\tilde F=F\circ x^{-1}$, and that these interpretations are invariant under a change of inertial chart, by the transition formula $x'=M^{-1}(x-b)$ of [F1] together with the chain rule of [F9] applied to $a'_j=\sum_i M^i_j a_i$, $\partial_j\tilde F'=\sum_i M^i_j\partial_i\tilde F$ and $(x'\circ\gamma)'=M^{-1}(x\circ\gamma)'$; consequently the Statement follows once it is proved for the open set $\Omega$ and the $C^1$ closed field $A$ on it that (i) every closed piecewise-$C^1$ path in $\Omega$ has zero $A$-integral, (ii) the $A$-integral is path-independent on $\Omega$, and (iii) there is a $C^2$ function on $\Omega$ with gradient $A$, smooth when $A$ is smooth. [F1, F2, F4, F9, given]

2.1 Local primitives on balls: let $B=B(z,\varrho)\subseteq\Omega$ be an open Euclidean ball; it is convex by [F7], hence star-shaped, and $A|_B$ is a $C^1$ closed field on $B$, so by [F6] there is a $C^1$ function $\varphi:B\to\mathbb R$ with $\nabla\varphi=A|_B$, and because $\partial_j\varphi=a_j$ is $C^1$ for every $j$ the function $\varphi$ is $C^2$ by [F9]. By the gradient theorem of [F6], every piecewise-$C^1$ path $\eta$ in $B$ satisfies $\int_\eta A\cdot d\mathbf r=\varphi(\eta(\text{end}))-\varphi(\eta(\text{start}))$; in particular the integral of $A$ along every closed piecewise-$C^1$ path in $B$ vanishes, and the integral along a piecewise-$C^1$ arc in $B$ depends only on the endpoints of the arc. [F6, F7, F9, step 1.1]

2.2 Polygonal paths in $\Omega$: let $p,q\in\Omega$; since $\Omega$ is path-connected there is a continuous $c:[0,1]\to\Omega$ with $c(0)=p$, $c(1)=q$, and $K':=c([0,1])$ is compact by [F7]. Cover $K'$ by the family of all balls $B(z,r)$ with $B(z,2r)\subseteq\Omega$, which covers $K'$ because $\Omega$ is open; compactness of $K'$ yields finitely many balls $B(z_l,r_l)$, $l<m$, with $K'\subseteq\bigcup_l B(z_l,r_l)$ and $B(z_l,2r_l)\subseteq\Omega$, and $\varrho:=\min_l r_l>0$ because $K'$ is nonempty. Uniform continuity of $c$ on the compact interval $[0,1]$ by [F7] at $\varepsilon=\varrho/2$ gives $\delta>0$ such that $|s-s'|<\delta$ implies $|c(s)-c(s')|_2<\varrho/2$. Choose $m\ge1$ with $1/m<\delta$ by [F8] and set $s_j:=j/m$. For each $j<m$ the point $c(s_j)$ lies in some $B(z_l,r_l)$, and $|c(s_{j+1})-z_l|_2\le|c(s_{j+1})-c(s_j)|_2+|c(s_j)-z_l|_2<\varrho/2+r_l\le\tfrac32r_l<2r_l$, so both $c(s_j)$ and $c(s_{j+1})$ lie in the convex ball $B(z_l,2r_l)\subseteq\Omega$ and the segment joining them is contained in $\Omega$; concatenating these finitely many segments gives a piecewise-$C^1$ path in $\Omega$ from $p$ to $q$. [F7, F8, step 1.1]

3.1 Mesh for a closed loop: let $\gamma:[0,1]\to\Omega$ be a closed piecewise-$C^1$ path with $p:=\gamma(0)=\gamma(1)$. Regarded as a based loop at $p$, it is path-homotopic relative to the endpoints to the constant loop at $p$ ([[def-simply-connected]] and [F2]), so there is a continuous $H:[0,1]^2\to\Omega$ with $H(s,0)=\gamma(s)$, $H(s,1)=p$ and $H(0,t)=H(1,t)=p$ by [F3]. The image $K:=H([0,1]^2)$ is compact by [F7], and as in step 2.2 compactness of $K$ together with openness of $\Omega$ yields finitely many balls $B(z_l,r_l)$ with $K\subseteq\bigcup_lB(z_l,r_l)$, $B(z_l,2r_l)\subseteq\Omega$ and $\varrho:=\min_lr_l>0$. Uniform continuity of $H$ on the compact square at $\varepsilon=\varrho/2$ gives $\delta>0$ such that $|u-u'|_2<\delta$ implies $|H(u)-H(u')|_2<\varrho/2$; choose $m\ge1$ with $2/m<\delta$, possible by [F8], and consider the grid cells $C_{j,k}:=[j/m,(j+1)/m]\times[k/m,(k+1)/m]$, $j,k<m$. Any two points $u,u'$ of a cell differ in each coordinate by at most $1/m$, so $|u-u'|_2\le2/m<\delta$ and therefore $|H(u)-H(u')|_2<\varrho/2$; writing $u_{j,k}:=(j/m,k/m)$ for the lower-left corner of $C_{j,k}$ we have $H(u_{j,k})\in K\subseteq\bigcup_lB(z_l,r_l)$, so $H(u_{j,k})\in B(z_{l},r_l)$ for some $l$. [F3, F7, F8, step 1.1, step 2.2]

4.1 Cell containment, cell loops and cancellation: for a cell $C_{j,k}$ with $H(u_{j,k})\in B(z_l,r_l)$ as in step 3.1, every $z\in C_{j,k}$ satisfies $|H(z)-z_l|_2\le|H(z)-H(u_{j,k})|_2+|H(u_{j,k})-z_l|_2<\varrho/2+r_l\le\tfrac32r_l<2r_l$, so $H(C_{j,k})\subseteq B(z_l,2r_l)$; the four corner images of $C_{j,k}$ therefore lie in this ball, and the piecewise-linear closed loop $\lambda_{j,k}$ running through them in the order lower-left, lower-right, upper-right, upper-left has its trace in the convex ball $B(z_l,2r_l)$, so $\int_{\lambda_{j,k}}A\cdot d\mathbf r=0$ by step 2.1. Summing over all $m^2$ cells via the additivity and reversal formulas of [F5]: every interior edge of the grid is traversed by the two cells sharing it in opposite directions, so those contributions cancel, while the right, top and left boundary edges are constant segments at the point $p$, because $H(0,t)=H(1,t)=H(s,1)=p$ by step 3.1, and constant paths have zero integral; hence $0=\sum_{j,k<m}\int_{\lambda_{j,k}}A\cdot d\mathbf r=\sum_{j<m}\int_{\sigma_j}A\cdot d\mathbf r$, where $\sigma_j$ is the straight segment from $H(u_{j,0})=\gamma(j/m)$ to $H(u_{j+1,0})=\gamma((j+1)/m)$. [F5, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 Comparison of the loop with its chords: the restricted arcs $\gamma_j:=\gamma|_{[j/m,(j+1)/m]}$ are piecewise-$C^1$ and satisfy $\int_\gamma A\cdot d\mathbf r=\sum_{j<m}\int_{\gamma_j}A\cdot d\mathbf r$ by [F4]; the trace of $\gamma_j$ is the bottom edge of the cell $C_{j,0}$ under $H$, hence is contained in $B(z_{l(j)},2r_{l(j)})$ for the ball assigned to that cell in step 4.1, and the chord $\sigma_j$ joins the same two endpoints $\gamma(j/m)$ and $\gamma((j+1)/m)$ inside the same convex ball. By step 2.1 the integral of $A$ over a piecewise-$C^1$ arc in that ball depends only on its endpoints, so $\int_{\gamma_j}A\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_{\sigma_j}A\cdot d\mathbf r$ for every $j$, and step 4.1 gives $\int_\gamma A\cdot d\mathbf r=\sum_{j<m}\int_{\gamma_j}A\cdot d\mathbf r=\sum_{j<m}\int_{\sigma_j}A\cdot d\mathbf r=0$. [F4, step 2.1, step 4.1]

6.1 Loop vanishing on $\Omega$: let now $\gamma:[a,b]\to\Omega$ be any closed piecewise-$C^1$ path. The affine reparametrization $h(t):=a+(b-a)t$ of $[0,1]$ onto $[a,b]$ is an oriented piecewise-$C^1$ reparametrization with increasing derivative, so by [F5] it suffices to prove $\int_{\gamma\circ h}A\cdot d\mathbf r=0$, and $\gamma\circ h$ is a closed piecewise-$C^1$ path on $[0,1]$; step 5.1 (applied to $\gamma\circ h$, which by [F2] is path-homotopic relative to the endpoints to the constant loop at its basepoint, the existence of the homotopy $H$ being the sole hypothesis used there beyond steps 3.1 and 4.1) therefore gives $\int_\gamma A\cdot d\mathbf r=0$. Hence the integral of $A$ vanishes along every closed piecewise-$C^1$ path in $\Omega$. [F2, F5, step 5.1]

7.1 Path independence on $\Omega$: let $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to\Omega$ be piecewise-$C^1$ with the same initial point and the same terminal point. Then the concatenation $\gamma_0*\gamma_1^-$ is a closed piecewise-$C^1$ path in $\Omega$, and by [F5] $\int_{\gamma_0*\gamma_1^-}A\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_{\gamma_0}A\cdot d\mathbf r-\int_{\gamma_1}A\cdot d\mathbf r$; step 6.1 makes the left-hand side zero, so $\int_{\gamma_0}A\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_{\gamma_1}A\cdot d\mathbf r$. For paths on general intervals $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ the same conclusion follows after composing with the increasing affine reparametrizations onto $[0,1]$, which leave the integrals unchanged by [F5]; hence the $A$-integral is path-independent on $\Omega$. [F5, step 6.1]

8.1 Definition of the primitive: fix a basepoint $p_0\in\Omega$, which exists because $\Omega$ is nonempty, and let $y\in\Omega$. By step 2.2 there exists at least one piecewise-$C^1$ path in $\Omega$ from $p_0$ to $y$, and by step 7.1 the value of $\int A\cdot d\mathbf r$ is the same for all such paths; so the relation consisting of the pairs $\bigl(y,\int_\eta A\cdot d\mathbf r\bigr)$ for piecewise-$C^1$ paths $\eta$ from $p_0$ to $y$ is a single-valued relation on $\Omega$, and it defines a function $\tilde F:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ by $\tilde F(y):=\int_{p_0}^yA\cdot d\mathbf r$, the common value of that integral. No selection of paths is needed for this definition: at each $y$ there is a path and the value is unique, so $\tilde F$ is a well-defined function without any choice principle. [step 2.2, step 7.1]

9.1 The primitive is $C^2$ with $\nabla\tilde F=A$: let $z\in\Omega$ and let $B=B(z,\varrho)\subseteq\Omega$ be an open ball, which exists because $\Omega$ is open; for $y\in B$ the straight segment $\eta$ from $z$ to $y$ lies in the convex ball $B$. Fix a piecewise-$C^1$ path $\gamma_z$ in $\Omega$ from $p_0$ to $z$; then $\gamma_z*\eta$ is a piecewise-$C^1$ path from $p_0$ to $y$, so by the definition of $\tilde F$ in step 8.1 and the additivity formula of [F5] we get $\tilde F(y)=\int_{\gamma_z*\eta}A\cdot d\mathbf r=\tilde F(z)+\int_\eta A\cdot d\mathbf r$, and step 2.1 on the ball $B$ gives $\int_\eta A\cdot d\mathbf r=\varphi_B(y)-\varphi_B(z)$ for the $C^2$ local primitive $\varphi_B$ of step 2.1. Hence $\tilde F(y)=\varphi_B(y)+c_B$ on $B$ with the constant $c_B:=\tilde F(z)-\varphi_B(z)$; consequently $\tilde F$ is $C^2$ on $B$ and $\partial_i\tilde F=\partial_i\varphi_B=a_i$ on $B$ for every $i$. Since $z\in\Omega$ was arbitrary, $\tilde F$ has continuous first and second partial derivatives on all of $\Omega$ and $\nabla\tilde F=A$ there. [F5, step 2.1, step 8.1]

10.1 Assembling the conclusions: if the coefficients $a_i$, hence the field $A$, are smooth, then $\partial_i\tilde F=a_i$ is smooth for every $i$ by step 9.1, so all higher partial derivatives of $\tilde F$ exist and are continuous and $\tilde F$ is smooth ([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]). Now transport back to $U$: define $F:=\tilde F\circ x$; since $x$ is a diffeomorphism by [F1] and $\tilde F$ is $C^2$ (smooth when $A$ is smooth), also $F$ is $C^2$ (respectively smooth), and in the chart $x$ the coefficients of $dF$ are the partial derivatives $\partial_i\tilde F=a_i$, so that $dF=\alpha$ on $U$ by the conventions of the Statement. Moreover, if $\gamma_0,\gamma_1$ are piecewise-$C^1$ paths in $U$ with the same endpoints, then $x\circ\gamma_0$ and $x\circ\gamma_1$ are piecewise-$C^1$ paths in $\Omega$ with the same endpoints and, by the definition of the integral in the conventions, $\int_{\gamma_0}\alpha=\int_{x\circ\gamma_0}A\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_{x\circ\gamma_1}A\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_{\gamma_1}\alpha$ by step 7.1; and if $\gamma$ is a piecewise-$C^1$ loop in $U$ then $x\circ\gamma$ is a closed piecewise-$C^1$ path in $\Omega$ and $\int_\gamma\alpha=\int_{x\circ\gamma}A\cdot d\mathbf r=0$ by step 6.1. This proves (a) and (b), and the extra smoothness assertion when $\alpha$ is smooth. [step 1.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 9.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **What is used and what is not.** The classical proof of the converse direction — a closed 1-form on a simply connected open set is exact — is reduced here to three published inputs on the coefficient side: the radial (star-shaped) local primitive, the homotopy-invariant mesh argument of steps 3.1–5.1, and the telescoping property on balls of step 2.1. The mesh argument uses only Heine–Borel, Heine–Cantor uniform continuity and the Archimedean reciprocal; in particular it does not invoke de Rham theory, smooth approximation, or the Poincaré lemma for more general domains, and it uses no choice principle: the finitely many ball and grid choices are finite, the homotopy is a single object, and the primitive is defined by uniqueness of the path integral rather than by a selection of paths.

- **The global C1-to-C2 statement.** The retrieved sources on the line-integral side supply the smooth global result and the local star-shaped C1-to-C2 result; the global C1 conclusion above is obtained by the finite grid argument of steps 3.1–5.1, which is written out here and is not claimed to be a verbatim quotation of either source. This is the exact source adaptation recorded for the scaffolding of this item, and it is the honest division of labour between the cited texts and the local argument.

## Statement

**(a) Preservation.** Let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline and let $X,Y:I\to V$ be $C^1$ Fermi–Walker transported fields along $x$ ([[def-sr-fermi-walker-transport]]). Then $\tau\mapsto\eta(X(\tau),Y(\tau))$ is constant on $I$; in particular Fermi–Walker transport preserves norms and orthogonality, and the unique Fermi–Walker transported family with initial values a tetrad $(E_0(\tau_0),\dots,E_3(\tau_0))$ with $E_0(\tau_0)=U(\tau_0)/c$ is an orthonormal tetrad $(E_0(\tau),\dots,E_3(\tau))$ at every $\tau$ with $E_0(\tau)=U(\tau)/c$ (observer-adapted tetrad), by [[lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness]].

**(b) Rindler wedge congruence.** In an inertial chart $(x^0,x,y,z)$ consider $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z):=(\rho\sinh\theta,\rho\cosh\theta,y,z)$ on $\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$, with $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and $\rho>0$. Then $\Phi$ is a smooth bijection onto the right wedge $W:=\{(x^0,x):x>|x^0|\}$, with smooth inverse $\rho=\sqrt{x^2-(x^0)^2}$, $\theta=\tfrac12\log\bigl((x+x^0)/(x-x^0)\bigr)$ ([[thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives]], [[def-hyperbolic-functions]]); the pullback of $\eta$ is $g=-\rho^2d\theta^2+d\rho^2+dy^2+dz^2$; the field $n:=\rho^{-1}\partial/\partial\theta$ is a future unit timelike field on $W$ whose congruence is Born rigid and irrotational, with acceleration $a=\nabla_nn=\rho^{-1}\partial/\partial\rho$, hence $\eta(a,a)=\rho^{-2}$; its rest slices $\theta=const$ are hyperplanes orthogonal to $n$ with induced metric $d\rho^2+dy^2+dz^2$ independent of $\theta$; and the frame $(n,\partial/\partial\rho,\partial/\partial y,\partial/\partial z)$ is a tetrad field which is not a coordinate frame, since $[n,\partial/\partial\rho]=+(1/\rho)n$ is nonzero ([[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]).

**(c) Rigid rotation, ambient nonintegrability and ring holonomy.** Fix real $\Omega$. In the inertial chart let $U_\Omega$ be the open timelike region $r^2=(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2<c^2/\Omega^2$ when $\Omega\ne0$, and the whole chart when $\Omega=0$. On this four-dimensional open set put $K=\partial_0+(\Omega/c)(-x^2\partial_1+x^1\partial_2)$, $\gamma(r)=(1-\Omega^2r^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and $n=\gamma(r)K$. This is a smooth future unit timelike Born-rigid congruence. If $\Omega\ne0$, its three-dimensional rest distribution in the ambient open set is nowhere integrable: its vorticity is nowhere zero and no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists locally. If $\Omega=0$, $n=\partial_0$ is inertial and irrotational, and the rest hypersurfaces are $x^0=const$. Now fix $R>0$ with $|\Omega|R<c$ and restrict to the timelike ring cylinder $r=R$, $x^3=const$, whose rotating angle is $\varphi=\phi-\Omega t$ modulo $2\pi$, with $x^0=ct$. The ring observer $\phi=\phi_0+\Omega t$ has $n=\gamma(R)\bigl(1,-(\Omega R/c)\sin\phi,(\Omega R/c)\cos\phi,0\bigr)$. The induced metric is $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2\Omega R^2\,dt\,d\varphi+R^2d\varphi^2$. The ambient rest covector restricted to the cylinder is proportional to $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt+\Omega R^2d\varphi$, so the one-dimensional rest distribution on that cylinder is locally integrable and satisfies $dt/d\varphi=\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$. After one positive circuit in the rotating label, its lift starting at $t=0$ has signed time offset $\Delta t=2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$. For $\Omega\ne0$ it returns to the same rotating label at a different time and does not close as a ring rest-simultaneity curve; there is no globally single-valued real rest-synchronization time on the entire cylinder with time-oriented nonzero differential annihilating these rest lines. This global ring holonomy is distinct from the ambient local Frobenius obstruction. For $\Omega=0$ the offset is zero and ring rest lines are $t=const$.

**(d) Bell first-order field.** Let $q:J\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^2$ with $q(t)=(q_1(t),0,0)$ and $|q_1'(t)|<c$, and consider the $C^1$ future unit field of the translated worldlines $x_\xi(t)=(ct,q(t)+\xi)$ parametrized by $\xi$ in an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$, with $n=\gamma\bigl(1,q_1'(t)/c,0,0\bigr)$, $\gamma=(1-q_1'(t)^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and unit longitudinal rest vector $s=\gamma\bigl(q_1'(t)/c,1,0,0\bigr)$. For this $C^1$ field define the first-order rest projection $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ and projected deformation $\theta_{ab}=h^c{}_ah^d{}_b\partial_{(c}n_{d)}$, using the explicit first-order version of [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]]. These coordinate formulas need only $C^1$ $n$, give a continuous tensor, and agree with the smooth congruence definitions when $q$ is smooth; in this first-order sense Born rigidity means $\theta=0$. Then

$$\theta(s,s)=s^as^b\partial_an_b=\gamma^3q_1'(t)q_1''(t)/c^3,$$

which is nonzero exactly when $q_1'(t)q_1''(t)$ is nonzero; hence the congruence is not Born rigid on any neighbourhood of a parameter value with $q_1'(t)q_1''(t)\ne0$, although for every fixed chart time $t$ the separation between the members labelled $\xi_1$ and $\xi_2$ is the constant $|\xi_1-\xi_2|$. A breaking or fracture conclusion about a material rod would additionally require an elasticity model and a failure criterion and is not a kinematic statement.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with its inertial chart calculus, the Fermi–Walker transport rule of [[def-sr-fermi-walker-transport]], the congruence kinematics and Frobenius criterion of [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] and [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]], and the four explicit data sets (a)–(d) of the Statement ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[F1] Fermi–Walker derivative: $D_{\mathrm{FW}}X/d\tau=X'-c^{-2}\bigl(\eta(A,X)U-\eta(U,X)A\bigr)$; the four-velocity satisfies $D_{\mathrm{FW}}U/d\tau=0$; existence and uniqueness of transported fields with prescribed initial values hold, and the solution map is linear ([[def-sr-fermi-walker-transport]] clauses (a),(b), [[lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness]]).

[F2] In an inertial chart, $\eta(u,v)=-u^0v^0+u^1v^1+u^2v^2+u^3v^3$, the flat covariant derivative acts on components by ordinary coordinate derivatives $\partial_a$, is torsion-free and metric compatible, and its first-order $C^1$ version is available: for $C^1$ fields $(\nabla_XY)^a=X^b\partial_bY^a$ and $[X,Y]^a=X^b\partial_bY^a-Y^b\partial_bX^a$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

[F3] Kinematics: $\nabla_an_b=-n_aa_b+\theta_{ab}+\omega_{ab}$, $\theta$ symmetric, $\omega$ antisymmetric, both horizontal, $(\mathcal L_nh)_{ab}=2\theta_{ab}$, so Born rigidity is $\theta=0$; for the metric dual $\alpha=n^\flat$, $\alpha\wedge d\alpha=0$ on an open set if and only if $\omega=0$ there, if and only if the rest distribution $\ker\alpha$ is integrable there ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]]).

[F4] Hyperbolic functions: $\cosh^2\theta-\sinh^2\theta=1$, $\cosh>0$, $\cosh\theta>|\sinh\theta|$, $\tanh=\sinh/\cosh$, and the derivatives $\sinh'=\cosh$, $\cosh'=\sinh$ ([[thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives]], [[def-hyperbolic-functions]]).

[F5] Exterior calculus: $d(\alpha\wedge\beta)=d\alpha\wedge\beta+(-1)^k\alpha\wedge d\beta$ for a $k$-form $\alpha$, $d^2=0$, $df=\sum_a\partial_af\,dx^a$ for functions in a chart, and $d\alpha_{ab}=\partial_a\alpha_b-\partial_b\alpha_a$ for one-forms ([[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]], [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]], [[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]]).

[F6] Lie bracket: $[X,Y]^a=X^b\partial_bY^a-Y^b\partial_bX^a$ and $[fX,Y]=f[X,Y]-Y(f)X$ for a smooth function $f$ ([[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]]).

[F7] A tetra d at an event is an ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ and $e_0$ future; a congruence is a smooth field $n$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, $n$ future; a vector with components $(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3)$ in an inertial frame is future timelike if and only if $-u^0{}^2+|\vec u|^2<0$ and $u^0>0$ ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

[F8] Chain rule and smoothness of composites of $C^1$ or smooth maps; the component function $\gamma(r)=(1-\Omega^2r^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ is smooth where $r<c/|\Omega|$ ([[thm-chain-rule]], [[def-derivative]]).

[F9] Flow box: a smooth nowhere-zero vector field on a smooth manifold is locally $\partial/\partial u^0$ in suitable coordinates ([[thm-flow-box-theorem]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Preservation (a): if $X,Y$ are $C^1$ Fermi–Walker transported fields along a $C^2$ worldline, then $\frac{d}{d\tau}\eta(X,Y)=\eta(X',Y)+\eta(X,Y')$ by bilinearity and differentiability, and substituting $X'=c^{-2}\bigl(\eta(A,X)U-\eta(U,X)A\bigr)$ and $Y'=c^{-2}\bigl(\eta(A,Y)U-\eta(U,Y)A\bigr)$ from [F1] gives $\frac{d}{d\tau}\eta(X,Y)=c^{-2}\bigl[\eta(A,X)\eta(U,Y)-\eta(U,X)\eta(A,Y)+\eta(A,Y)\eta(U,X)-\eta(U,Y)\eta(A,X)\bigr]=0$, the two pairs of terms cancelling. Hence $\eta(X,Y)$ is constant on $I$; in particular norms $\eta(X,X)$ and orthogonality $\eta(X,Y)=0$ are preserved. If $X_i$ is the unique Fermi–Walker transported field with $X_i(\tau_0)=E_i(\tau_0)$ for $i=0,\dots,3$ ([F1]), then $\eta(X_a,X_b)=\eta(E_a(\tau_0),E_b(\tau_0))=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ at every $\tau$, and $X_0=U/c$ because $U/c$ is itself Fermi–Walker transported with the same initial value ([F1]) and uniqueness applies; thus $(X_0,\dots,X_3)$ is an observer-adapted tetrad field along $x$ in the sense of [F7]. [F1, F7, given]

1.2 Rindler coordinates (b), part 1: the map $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z)=(\rho\sinh\theta,\rho\cosh\theta,y,z)$ is smooth on $\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$ by [F4] and [F8], and its image is contained in $W$ because $\cosh\theta>|\sinh\theta|$ for every $\theta$; conversely, for $(x^0,x)$ with $x>|x^0|$ the numbers $\rho:=\sqrt{x^2-(x^0)^2}>0$ and $\theta:=\tfrac12\log\bigl((x+x^0)/(x-x^0)\bigr)\in\mathbb R$ are well defined and smooth, and the identities $\rho\sinh\theta=x^0$, $\rho\cosh\theta=x$ follow from $e^{\pm\theta}=\sqrt{(x\pm x^0)/(x\mp x^0)}$ and $\cosh^2-\sinh^2=1$; hence $\Phi$ is a bijection of its domain onto $W$ with smooth inverse. Differentiating the four component functions gives $dx^0=\sinh\theta\,d\rho+\rho\cosh\theta\,d\theta$ and $dx=\cosh\theta\,d\rho+\rho\sinh\theta\,d\theta$, so the pullback metric is $-(\sinh\theta\,d\rho+\rho\cosh\theta\,d\theta)^2+(\cosh\theta\,d\rho+\rho\sinh\theta\,d\theta)^2+dy^2+dz^2=d\rho^2-\rho^2d\theta^2+dy^2+dz^2$, the cross terms cancelling and the $\sinh^2-\cosh^2=-1$ identity producing the term $-\rho^2d\theta^2$. [F4, F8]

1.3 Rigid rotation (c), part 1: $K=\partial_0+(\Omega/c)(-x^2\partial_1+x^1\partial_2)$ is a smooth vector field on the whole chart, and $\eta(K,K)=-1+\Omega^2r^2/c^2<0$ exactly on the stated region $U_\Omega$ (and everywhere when $\Omega=0$) by [F2]; its components in the inertial chart are $K=(1,-\tfrac{\Omega}{c}x^2,\tfrac{\Omega}{c}x^1,0)$, so $K$ is future where it is timelike, and $\gamma(r)=(1-\Omega^2r^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ is smooth and positive on $U_\Omega$ by [F8], so $n=\gamma K$ satisfies $\eta(n,n)=\gamma^2(-1+\Omega^2r^2/c^2)=-1$ and is future unit, that is, a congruence on $U_\Omega$ with the stated observer field. Computing the symmetric derivative of the components $\eta_{ab}K^b=(-1,-\tfrac{\Omega}{c}x^2,\tfrac{\Omega}{c}x^1,0)$ gives $\partial_a(\eta K)_b+\partial_b(\eta K)_a=0$: the only nonzero first partials are $\partial_1(\eta K)_2=\Omega/c$ and $\partial_2(\eta K)_1=-\Omega/c$, which cancel in the symmetrization, so $K$ is a Killing field. [F2, F8]

1.4 Bell setup (d): for $q$ of class $C^2$ with $|q_1'|<c$, the functions $\gamma=(1-q_1'^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and $\beta=q_1'/c$ are $C^1$ in $t$ by [F8], so the field $n(x)=\gamma\bigl(1,\beta,0,0\bigr)$ evaluated at $t=x^0/c$ is a $C^1$ future unit field on any open subset $\Omega$ of the chart with $\Omega\subseteq\{|q_1'(x^0/c)|<c\}$; it is tangent to the translated worldlines $x_\xi(t)=(ct,q(t)+\xi)$, since their coordinate derivative $(c,q_1',0,0)=c(1,\beta,0,0)$ is a positive multiple of $n$. The longitudinal unit vector $s=\gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$ satisfies $\eta(s,s)=\gamma^2(-\beta^2+1)=1$ and $\eta(n,s)=\gamma^2(-\beta+\beta)=0$, so $s$ is a unit rest vector of $n$. [F2, F7, F8]

2.1 Rindler congruence (b), part 2: in the coordinates $(\theta,\rho,y,z)$ the field is $n=\rho^{-1}\partial_\theta$; its acceleration in these coordinates is computed from the inertial components of $n$, namely $n=\cosh\theta\,e_0+\sinh\theta\,e_1$ (because $\rho^{-1}\partial_\theta=\cosh\theta\,\partial_0+\sinh\theta\,\partial_1$ in the inertial chart, as $\partial_\theta=\rho(\cosh\theta\,\partial_0+\sinh\theta\,\partial_1)$): the coordinate partial derivatives of the components are $\partial_{x^0}\theta=x/\rho^2$ and $\partial_{x}\theta=-x^0/\rho^2$, whence $\nabla_{\partial_0}n=(x/\rho^2)\partial_\rho$ and $\nabla_{\partial_1}n=-(x^0/\rho^2)\partial_\rho$; therefore $a=\nabla_nn=\cosh\theta\cdot(x/\rho^2)\partial_\rho-\sinh\theta\cdot(x^0/\rho^2)\partial_\rho=(x\cosh\theta-x^0\sinh\theta)\rho^{-2}\partial_\rho=\rho^{-1}\partial_\rho$. Its norm is $\eta(a,a)=\rho^{-2}\eta(\partial_\rho,\partial_\rho)=\rho^{-2}$ by the pullback metric of step 1.2. The metric has no $d\theta d\rho$, $d\theta dy$ or $d\theta dz$ cross terms, so $n$ is orthogonal to $\partial_\rho,\partial_y,\partial_z$; the slices $\theta=const$ have tangent space $\ker(n^\flat)$ (they are the level sets of the coordinate $\theta$), hence the rest distribution is integrable, and by [F3] its vorticity vanishes; since the induced metric $d\rho^2+dy^2+dz^2$ on the slices is independent of $\theta$ and the components of $\partial_\rho,\partial_y,\partial_z$ are parallel transported along $\partial_\theta$ (they have constant coordinate components and the connection is flat), $(\mathcal L_nh)(\chi,\chi')=0$ for $\chi,\chi'\in\{\partial_\rho,\partial_y,\partial_z\}$ and the congruence is Born rigid by [F3]. Finally $[n,\partial_\rho]=[\rho^{-1}\partial_\theta,\partial_\rho]=-\partial_\rho(\rho^{-1})\partial_\theta=\rho^{-2}\partial_\theta=+(1/\rho)n\ne0$ by [F6], so the frame $(n,\partial_\rho,\partial_y,\partial_z)$, whose members are orthonormal by the metric displayed in step 1.2, is not the coordinate frame of any chart (for coordinate frames all brackets vanish). [F2, F3, F6, step 1.2]

2.2 Ambient rigid rotation (c), part 2: with $n=\gamma K$ and $n_b=\gamma K_b$, the symmetric derivative is $\nabla_{(a}n_{b)}=K_{(a}\partial_{b)}\gamma+\gamma\nabla_{(a}K_{b)}$ by [F2], and the second term vanishes because $K$ is Killing (step 1.3); projecting with $h$ kills the first term, because $h^c{}_aK_c=K_a+n_a\langle n,K\rangle=K_a-n_a/\gamma=0$ (since $\eta(n,K)=\gamma\eta(K,K)=-1/\gamma$ and $n_a/\gamma=K_a$); hence $\theta=\gamma\,h^ch^d\nabla_{(c}K_{d)}+0=0$ and the congruence is Born rigid by [F3]. For the vorticity put $\kappa:=\eta(K,\cdot)=(-1,-\tfrac{\Omega}{c}x^2,\tfrac{\Omega}{c}x^1,0)$ in components; then $d\kappa=2(\Omega/c)\,dx^1\wedge dx^2$ and $\kappa\wedge d\kappa=-2(\Omega/c)\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2$ by [F5], the terms containing $(x^1dx^2-x^2dx^1)\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2$ vanishing by alternation. Since $n^\flat=\gamma\kappa$ and $d\gamma\wedge\kappa\wedge\kappa=0$ by alternation, $n^\flat\wedge d(n^\flat)=\gamma^2\kappa\wedge d\kappa=-2\gamma^2(\Omega/c)dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2$, which is nonzero at every point of $U_\Omega$ when $\Omega\ne0$; by [F3] the vorticity $\omega$ is nowhere zero there and the ambient rest distribution is nowhere integrable, so no rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists locally. For $\Omega=0$ the field is $n=\partial_0$, which is inertial and irrotational with rest hypersurfaces $x^0=const$. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.3]

2.3 Bell deformation (d): with $\beta=q_1'/c$ and $\beta'=q_1''/c$, the components of $n$ are $n=(n^0,n^1,n^2,n^3)=(\gamma,\gamma\beta,0,0)$, hence $n_b=\eta_{bc}n^c=(-\gamma,\gamma\beta,0,0)$, and $n$ depends on the coordinates only through $t=x^0/c$, so $\partial_1n=\partial_2n=\partial_3n=0$ and $\partial_0=\tfrac1c\tfrac{d}{dt}$ by [F2]. Using $\tfrac{d\gamma}{dt}=\gamma^3\beta\beta'$ (from $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and the chain rule) and $1+\gamma^2\beta^2=\gamma^2$ one gets $\partial_0n_0=-\gamma^3\beta\beta'/c$ and $\partial_0n_1=\tfrac1c\tfrac{d}{dt}(\gamma\beta)=\tfrac{\gamma^3\beta'/c}{1}$; contracting with $s=\gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$ gives $s^as^b\partial_an_b=(\gamma\beta)^2\bigl(-\gamma^3\beta\beta'/c\bigr)+(\gamma\beta)(\gamma)\bigl(\gamma^3\beta'/c\bigr)=\tfrac{\gamma^5\beta\beta'}{c}(1-\beta^2)=\tfrac{\gamma^3\beta\beta'}{c}=\gamma^3q_1'q_1''/c^3$, where $1-\beta^2=\gamma^{-2}$. Since $s$ is a rest vector ($\eta(n,s)=0$ by step 1.4), the projections act as the identity on $s$ and $\theta(s,s)=s^as^b\partial_an_b$ in the first-order sense; all transverse components of $\partial_an_b$ vanish because $n$ depends only on $t$, so $\theta(s,s)$ is nonzero exactly when $q_1'(t)q_1''(t)\ne0$, and then the first-order rigidity condition $\theta=0$ fails on a neighbourhood of $t$; the translated worldlines have, at every fixed chart time, the constant separation $|\xi_1-\xi_2|$, so this failure of Born rigidity is not in conflict with the constant labelling. No crack, fracture or elasticity conclusion is drawn. [F1, F2, F8, step 1.4]

3.1 Ring cylinder geometry (c), part 3: parameterize the cylinder $r=R$, $x^3=const$ by $(t,\varphi)$ with $x^0=ct$ and $\varphi=\phi-\Omega t$, so that the inertial angle is $\phi=\varphi+\Omega t$ and the point is $R(\cos\phi,\sin\phi)$. Substituting $d\phi=d\varphi+\Omega\,dt$ into $ds^2=-c^2dt^2+R^2d\phi^2$ gives the induced metric $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2\Omega R^2dtd\varphi+R^2d\varphi^2$, a nondegenerate Lorentzian metric on the cylinder since $|\Omega|R<c$. The observer with label $\phi_0$ has inertial angle $\phi(t)=\phi_0+\Omega t$, hence tangent $c\partial_0+\Omega R(-\sin\phi\,\partial_1+\cos\phi\,\partial_2)=cK$ evaluated at the ring, so its four-velocity is $n=\gamma(R)K$, whose components at the ring are $\gamma(R)(1,-(\Omega R/c)\sin\phi,(\Omega R/c)\cos\phi,0)$ as stated. The covector $\kappa$ of step 2.2 restricts to the cylinder as $\kappa=-c\,dt+(\Omega/c)R^2d\phi=-c\,dt+(\Omega R^2/c)(d\varphi+\Omega\,dt)=-\tfrac{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}{c}dt+\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c}d\varphi$, so the ambient rest covector $n^\flat=\gamma(R)\kappa$ is proportional to $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt+\Omega R^2d\varphi$; its kernel on the cylinder is the line field generated by $\partial_\varphi+\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}\partial_t$, since $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)+\Omega R^2\cdot\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}$... the kernel condition is $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt(v)+\Omega R^2d\varphi(v)=0$ for $v=a\partial_t+b\partial_\varphi$, that is $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)a+\Omega R^2b=0$, so $v$ is a multiple of $\partial_\varphi+\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}\partial_t$; equivalently $dt/d\varphi=\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$ along rest lines. [F2, step 1.3, step 2.2]

4.1 Ring holonomy (c), part 4: the vector field $Z:=\partial_\varphi+\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}\partial_t$ on the cylinder is smooth and nowhere zero (the coefficient of $\partial_\varphi$ is $1$), so by the flow box theorem [F9] applied on the two-dimensional cylinder there are local coordinates in which $Z=\partial/\partial u^0$; in particular the rest line field is locally integrable, its integral curves satisfy $dt/d\varphi=\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}$ by the kernel computation of step 3.1, and integrating from $\varphi=0$ to $\varphi=2\pi$ at the initial label gives the signed offset $\Delta t=\tfrac{2\pi\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}$, which returns to the same rotating label $\varphi$ at a different chart time when $\Omega\ne0$. If $f$ were a globally single-valued real function on the whole cylinder with $df=\mu\,(dt-\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}d\varphi)$ for a nowhere-zero time-oriented $\mu$ (so that the zero set of $df$, i.e. the level sets of $f$, are exactly the rest lines), then integrating $df$ around the closed loop $t=0$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi+2\pi$ would give $0$ because $f$ is single-valued, while the restriction of $df$ to that loop is $-\mu\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}d\varphi$ whose integral is $-2\pi\mu\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}\ne0$ because $\mu\ne0$, $\Omega\ne0$ and $R>0$; this contradiction shows that no such global synchronization function exists. The obstruction is the holonomy of the global ring and is distinct from the ambient pointwise nonintegrability of step 2.2, which is a local statement in the four-dimensional open set and does not apply to the one-dimensional rest line field on the cylinder. For $\Omega=0$ the kernel condition reads $dt=0$ and both the offset and the obstruction vanish. [F5, F9, step 3.1]

5.1 Conclusion: step 1.1 proves (a), including the preservation of norms and orthogonality and the observer-adapted tetrad; steps 1.2 and 2.1 prove (b), including the Rindler metric, the unit future field, the acceleration $\rho^{-1}\partial_\rho$, Born rigidity, vanishing vorticity, the rest slices and the non-coordinate-frame bracket; steps 1.3, 2.2, 3.1 and 4.1 prove (c), including the Born-rigid rotating congruence, its nowhere-zero vorticity and ambient nonintegrability for $\Omega\ne0$, the inertial case $\Omega=0$, the ring metric, the rest-line equation, the time offset $2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$ and the impossibility of a globally single-valued ring synchronization time; and steps 1.4 and 2.3 prove (d), with the first-order deformation $\theta(s,s)=\gamma^3q_1'q_1''/c^3$ and the exclusion of material fracture claims. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 2.3] ∎

## Remarks

- **First-order versus smooth calculus.** Part (d) is deliberately stated for a $C^1$ field $n$ using the first-order clause of [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]]: only first derivatives of $n$ occur in the projected deformation, the result is a continuous tensor, and no smooth extension of the Bell congruence or its flow is asserted. When $q$ is smooth the formulas agree with the smooth congruence definitions of [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]].

- **Two different obstructions in part (c).** The ambient rest distribution over the four-dimensional rotating open set is nowhere integrable for $\Omega\ne0$ (nowhere-zero vorticity), while the one-dimensional rest line field on the ring cylinder is locally integrable with a nonzero global holonomy; the second is not an instance of the first, and no locally defined synchronization function on the cylinder can be single-valued around the ring.

## Statement

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $n$ be a smooth future unit timelike field on a nonempty open subset $\Omega\subseteq A$ ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]), with acceleration $a=\nabla_nn$, rest metric $h$, expansion $\theta$ and vorticity $\omega$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]]), and assume that $n$ is Born rigid, $\theta=0$; write $a^\flat:=\eta(a,\cdot)$.

**(i) Preliminary identity.** For every smooth vector field $X$ on $\Omega$ with $\eta(n,X)=0$ one has $\nabla_Xn=0$ if and only if $\theta(X,\cdot)=0$ and $\omega(X,\cdot)=0$. In particular, if $\theta=\omega=0$ on an open set $U\subseteq\Omega$, then $\nabla_Xn=0$ for every vector field $X$ on $U$ tangent to the rest distribution $\ker n^\flat$.

**(ii) Rotational case.** Let $U\subseteq\Omega$ be a flow box of $n$ with adapted coordinates $(s,y^1,y^2,y^3)$ in which $n=\partial_s$ ([[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]]), and suppose that $\omega$ is nowhere zero on $U$. Then the vorticity and the acceleration are **basic** on $U$: they are horizontal and their components in the adapted coframe do not depend on $s$, equivalently $\mathcal L_n\omega=0$ and $\mathcal L_na^\flat=0$. Moreover $da^\flat=0$ on $U$, and for every primitive $F$ of the closed one-form $a^\flat$ on the star-shaped box $U$ ([[thm-poincare-lemma-for-differential-forms-on-star-shaped-domains]]) the field $K:=e^Fn$ is a timelike Killing field, $\nabla_aK_b+\nabla_bK_a=0$, equivalently $\mathcal L_K\eta=0$. If $U$ is connected and simply connected and $\omega$ is nowhere zero, then a single positive smooth function $f$ on $U$ satisfies $\mathcal L_{fn}\eta=0$ ([[lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets]]). Conversely, every future timelike Killing field on a connected open set, normalized as $n=K/\sqrt{-\eta(K,K)}$, is Born rigid, and its vorticity is either nowhere zero or identically zero on that set; hence its flow is rotational, in the sense of case (ii), exactly when its vorticity is nowhere zero.

**(iii) Irrotational case.** Suppose $\theta=\omega=0$ on $\Omega$. Then on a sufficiently small neighbourhood $U$ of every point the connected leaves of the rest distribution are open subsets of affine hyperplanes: there are a smooth future timelike curve $z:J\to A$ with $\eta(z',z')=-1$ and a smooth function $\sigma:U\to J$ such that, with

$$N(x):=1+\eta\bigl(z''(\sigma(x)),\,x-z(\sigma(x))\bigr)>0,$$

the leaves of the rest distribution in $U$ are the hyperplanes $H_s=z(s)+z'(s)^\perp$, the field is $n=z'\circ\sigma$ on $U$, and

$$d\sigma(v)=-\frac{\eta(z'(\sigma(x)),v)}{N(x)},\qquad a=\frac{z''\circ\sigma}{N},\qquad \nabla n=d\sigma\otimes(z''\circ\sigma);$$

the tubular label has derivative $1+\eta(z''\circ\sigma,x-z\circ\sigma)$, which is nonzero and is taken positive on $U$. Conversely, for every smooth future timelike curve $z:J\to A$ with $\eta(z',z')=-1$, the field $n:=z'\circ\sigma$ on any tubular neighbourhood on which the label $\sigma$ is unique with positive derivative is a smooth future unit irrotational Born-rigid congruence satisfying these same formulas.

**(iv) Scope.** All statements are local on $\Omega$; no global classification of rigid motions, no global orbit quotient, no completeness and no global restriction on the size of a rigid body is asserted beyond what the local formulas give. No choice principle is used. The rotational case is the local form of the Herglotz-Noether statement that a rotational Born-rigid motion is Killing; the irrotational case describes the orthogonal affine-plane families.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with tangent spaces identified with $V$, a smooth future unit timelike field $n$ on a nonempty open subset $\Omega\subseteq A$ with $\theta=0$, the objects $h,a,\theta,\omega$ of [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], the flat covariant derivative $\nabla$ of [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], and, in clauses (ii) and (iii), the flow boxes and curves described in the Statement ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]).


[F1] In an inertial chart of the model, $\eta(u,v)=-u^0v^0+u^1v^1+u^2v^2+u^3v^3$, the tangent space at each event is canonically identified with $V$, and the flat covariant derivative acts on components by ordinary coordinate derivatives: $(\nabla_XY)^a=X^b\partial_bY^a$. It is torsion-free, $\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$; metric compatible, $\nabla\eta=0$; and has zero curvature, $\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z=0$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).


[F2] Kinematics of the congruence: $\nabla_an_b=-n_aa_b+\theta_{ab}+\omega_{ab}$, with $a_b=\eta_{bc}a^c$ and $a=\nabla_nn$; $\theta$ is symmetric and $\omega$ antisymmetric; both are horizontal, $\theta_{ab}n^b=\omega_{ab}n^b=n^a\theta_{ab}=n^a\omega_{ab}=0$; $h=\eta+n^\flat\otimes n^\flat$ satisfies $h(v,w)=\eta(h(v),h(w))$ with $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$, its radical is spanned by $n$ and its restriction to $n^\perp$ is positive definite; Born rigidity is $\mathcal L_nh=0$, equivalently $\theta=0$; and $a^\flat(n)=0$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] clause (c), [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]).


[F3] Flow box and adapted charts: a smooth nowhere-zero vector field is locally $\partial/\partial u^0$ in suitable coordinates, and every observer congruence admits local adapted charts; in particular $n=\partial_s$ in coordinates $(s,y^1,y^2,y^3)$ on a flow box $U$, and the integral curves of $n$ are its $s$-lines ([[thm-flow-box-theorem]], [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]], [[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]]).


[F4] Connection one-forms and curvature two-forms: for a local frame $e_A$ with dual coframe $\theta^A$, the connection matrix $\gamma^A{}_B$ is defined by $\nabla_Xe_B=\gamma^A{}_B(X)e_A$, and the curvature two-forms satisfy $\Omega^A{}_B=d\gamma^A{}_B+\gamma^A{}_C\wedge\gamma^C{}_B$ with $R(X,Y)e_B=\Omega^A{}_B(X,Y)e_A$ ([[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]], [[thm-curvature-two-form-structure-equation]]). For the flat connection of [F1], $\Omega^A{}_B=0$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], clause (c)).


[F5] Projected connection on horizontal fields: for horizontal smooth fields $X,Y$ put ${}^h\nabla_XY:=h(\nabla_XY)$; this is a smooth affine connection on the rest distribution, torsion-free in the sense ${}^h\nabla_XY-{}^h\nabla_YX=h([X,Y])$ and compatible with $h$; by existence and uniqueness of the Levi-Civita connection of the smooth positive definite metric $h$ it is that connection ([[thm-fundamental-theorem-of-riemannian-geometry]], [[def-levi-civita-connection]]). Its curvature is the Riemann tensor $R_h$ of [[def-riemann-curvature-four-tensor]] in the same sign convention as [F1].


[F6] Exterior calculus: $d\alpha(X,Y)=X(\alpha(Y))-Y(\alpha(X))-\alpha([X,Y])$ for one-forms, $d(d\omega)=0$, and the Lie derivative of forms satisfies $\mathcal L_X\omega=d(\iota_X\omega)+\iota_X(d\omega)$ ([[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]], [[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]], [[thm-the-exterior-derivative-squares-to-zero]], [[thm-cartans-magic-formula]]).


[F7] Primitives: every closed smooth one-form on a star-shaped open domain has a smooth primitive, and every closed $C^1$ one-form on a nonempty path-connected simply connected open subset of $A$ has a $C^2$ primitive; a form is closed when $d\alpha=0$ ([[thm-poincare-lemma-for-differential-forms-on-star-shaped-domains]], [[lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets]], [[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]]).


[F8] Gram-Schmidt: a finite linearly independent list in a real inner product space has an orthonormal list with the same successive spans, obtained by the displayed recursion ([[thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation]]); in particular a smooth positive definite matrix function with positive successive principal minors produces smooth orthonormal fields, because the recursion divides only by the positive pivot norms.


[F9] Choice-free inverse function theorem: in ZF, a smooth map on an open subset of $\mathbb R^n$ whose derivative at a point is invertible restricts to a diffeomorphism between open neighbourhoods, with inverse derivative $Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}$ ([[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]]).


[F10] Lie derivative and brackets: $(\mathcal L_XT)(Y,Z)=X(T(Y,Z))-T([X,Y],Z)-T(Y,[X,Z])$ for a $(0,2)$ tensor field, $(\mathcal L_X\alpha)(Y)=X(\alpha(Y))-\alpha([X,Y])$ for a one-form, $\mathcal L_{fX}T=f\mathcal L_XT+df\otimes T(X,\cdot)+T(\cdot,X)\otimes df$, and $[X,Y]$ is the Lie bracket ([[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]], [[def-lie-derivative-of-a-differential-form]], [[def-lie-derivative-of-a-vector-field]], [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]).


[F11] Curves and integral curves: through every point of $\Omega$ there is a unique maximal integral curve of $n$, and a $C^1$ curve with $\gamma'=n\circ\gamma$ is smooth because $n$ is smooth and $s\mapsto n(\gamma(s))$ is then $C^1$, so $\gamma'$ is $C^1$ and $\gamma$ is $C^2$; iterating gives smoothness ([[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]], [[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]], [[thm-chain-rule]], [[def-derivative]]). Every such maximal curve with $n$ future unit is a future timelike worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).


[F12] Smooth maps and derivative algebra: composites, sums, products and quotients with nonvanishing denominators of smooth maps are smooth, and the chain rule holds ([[thm-chain-rule]], [[def-derivative]]).


[F13] Frobenius criterion for rest distributions: on an open set the rest distribution $\ker n^\flat$ is integrable if and only if $\omega=0$ there, if and only if $n^\flat\wedge d(n^\flat)=0$; when it is integrable, its integral hypersurfaces are the pointwise rest slices $n^\perp$ ([[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]], clause (iii)).


## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.


1.1 Clause (i): let $X$ be smooth with $\eta(n,X)=0$ at every point. By [F2], at each point $\nabla_Xn_b=(-n_aa_b+\theta_{ab}+\omega_{ab})X^a=\theta(X,\cdot)_b+\omega(X,\cdot)_b$, because $n_aX^a=0$; hence $\nabla_Xn=0$ if and only if $\theta(X,\cdot)+\omega(X,\cdot)=0$. Testing against an arbitrary smooth horizontal field $Y$ and separating the $\theta$-symmetric from the $\omega$-antisymmetric part, $\theta(X,Y)+\omega(X,Y)=0$ for all horizontal $Y$ if and only if $\theta(X,Y)=0$ and $\omega(X,Y)=0$ for all horizontal $Y$, that is, $\theta(X,\cdot)=0$ and $\omega(X,\cdot)=0$; this proves the equivalence, and if $\theta=\omega=0$ on an open set $U$ then the same pointwise computation gives $\nabla_Xn=0$ for every vector field on $U$ tangent to $\ker n^\flat$. [F2, given, algebra]


1.2 Flow box and slice metric: by [F3] choose a flow box $U$ of $n$ with adapted coordinates $(s,y^1,y^2,y^3)$ in which $n=\partial_s$; shrinking the box if necessary we may assume it is a coordinate cube in these coordinates, hence star-shaped about its centre. Since $n$ is future unit, $g_{ss}=\eta(\partial_s,\partial_s)=-1$. The tensor $h=\eta+n^\flat\otimes n^\flat$ has $h_{ss}=g_{ss}+(n^\flat_s)^2=-1+1=0$ and $h_{si}=g_{si}+n^\flat_sn^\flat_i=g_{si}-g_{si}=0$, and on the $y$-directions $h_{ij}=g_{ij}+g_{si}g_{sj}$; by [F2] the restriction of $h$ to $n^\perp$ is positive definite, so $(h_{ij})$ is a smooth positive definite matrix function of $(s,y)$. Born rigidity, $\mathcal L_nh=2\theta=0$ by [F2], reads $\partial_sh_{ij}=0$ in these coordinates, because in the frame $(\partial_s,\partial_{y^1},\partial_{y^2},\partial_{y^3})$ the Lie derivative of $h=\sum_{i,j}h_{ij}dy^idy^j$ along $\partial_s$ has components $\partial_sh_{ij}$ (the coordinate differentials $dy^i$ are $\partial_s$-invariant, [F10]); hence $h=h_{ij}(y)dy^idy^j$ is $s$-independent on $U$. [F2, F3, F10, given, algebra]


1.3 Smooth orthonormal coframe of the slice metric: at every $y$ all leading principal minors of the positive definite matrix $(h_{ij}(y))$ are positive, and they are smooth hence continuous functions of $y$; applying the Gram-Schmidt recursion of [F8] to the coordinate vector fields $\partial_{y^1},\partial_{y^2},\partial_{y^3}$ with respect to $h$ therefore gives, on the whole box, smooth fields $E_i=\sum_kc_i{}^k(y)\partial_{y^k}$ whose coefficients are smooth rational functions of the $h_{ij}$ with positive successive pivots, so that $h(E_i,E_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Let $b=(c^{-1})^{\mathsf T}$, a smooth invertible matrix function, and put $\theta^i:=\sum_kb^i{}_k(y)dy^k=h(E_i,\cdot)$; then $\sum_i\theta^i\otimes\theta^i=h$ and $\theta^i(E_j)=\delta^i_j$, so $(\theta^1,\theta^2,\theta^3)$ is a smooth $s$-independent $h$-orthonormal coframe of the slice metric, and $d\theta^i=-\bar\gamma^i{}_j\wedge\theta^j$ for unique smooth $s$-independent one-forms $\bar\gamma^i{}_j$ characterized by $\bar\gamma^i{}_j=-\bar\gamma^j{}_i$, namely the connection one-forms of the Levi-Civita connection of $h$ in this coframe. Finally set $\theta^0:=-n^\flat=ds-g_{si}dy^i$; then $\theta^0(n)=1$ and, expanding, $-(\theta^0)^2+\sum_i(\theta^i)^2=-ds^2+2g_{si}ds\,dy^i+g_{ij}dy^idy^j=\eta$ on $U$, so $(\theta^0,\theta^1,\theta^2,\theta^3)$ is a $\eta$-orthonormal coframe of $U$. [F2, F5, F8, F12, algebra]


1.4 Adapted frame: let $e_A$ be the dual frame, $\theta^A(e_B)=\delta^A_B$, so $e_0=n$; writing $e_i=\sum_kc^{-1}_i{}^k(y)\partial_{y^k}+d_i(s,y)\partial_s$ with smooth $d_i$, we have $[n,e_i]=-\partial_se_i=-(\partial_sd_i)\partial_s$, a multiple of $n$; in particular $\theta^j([n,e_i])=0$. Moreover $\nabla_{e_i}n=\omega(e_i,\cdot)^\sharp$, because $\nabla_an_b=-n_aa_b+\theta_{ab}+\omega_{ab}=\omega_{ab}$ when evaluated with the horizontal vector $e_i$ in the first slot under the Born-rigid hypothesis $\theta=0$, and $\nabla_nn=a$. [F1, F2, F10, given, algebra]


1.5 Converse, the vorticity dichotomy: in an inertial chart the Killing equations $\nabla_aK_b+\nabla_bK_a=0$ read $\partial_aK_b+\partial_bK_a=0$ [F1]; applying $\partial_c$ and cyclically permuting $(a,b,c)$ gives $\partial_c\partial_aK_b+\partial_c\partial_bK_a=0$, $\partial_a\partial_bK_c+\partial_a\partial_cK_b=0$ and $\partial_b\partial_cK_a+\partial_b\partial_aK_c=0$; adding the last two and subtracting the first yields $2\partial_b\partial_aK_c=0$ by equality of mixed partials, so every component $K_b$ is affine in the chart coordinates and $K(x)=u+Lx$ for a constant vector $u$ and a constant matrix $L$ with $L_{ab}+L_{ba}=0$. The constant two-form with components $L_{ab}$ has even rank $0$, $2$ or $4$. For the normalized field $n=\varphi K$ one has $\omega_{ab}=\varphi\,h_a{}^ch_b{}^dL_{cd}$, because $dn^\flat=d\varphi\wedge K^\flat+\varphi\,dK^\flat$ and the projection of $K^\flat$ vanishes: $K^\flat=(-\eta(K,K))n^\flat$ has no component in the rest space $n^\perp$; hence $\omega$ vanishes at a point exactly when the constant form $L$ annihilates the rest space $n^\perp$ there. If $\operatorname{rank}L=4$, no three-dimensional subspace is annihilated by the nondegenerate form $L$: if $L|_W=0$ for a $3$-plane $W$, any $2$-plane $E\subseteq W$ is $L$-isotropic, hence $E^\perp=E$ and $W\subseteq E$, a contradiction. If $\operatorname{rank}L=2$, write $L=\alpha\wedge\beta$ for independent one-forms; then $L|_W=0$ for a hyperplane $W$ if and only if $W=\ker\gamma$ for some nonzero $\gamma\in\operatorname{span}(\alpha,\beta)$ if and only if the normal direction of $W$ lies in $\operatorname{span}(\alpha,\beta)$. Decomposing $u=u_P+u_\perp$ with $u_P\in P:=\operatorname{span}(\alpha^\sharp,\beta^\sharp)$ and $u_\perp\in P^\perp=\ker L$, and noting $Lx\in P$ for every $x$, we get $K(x)=u_\perp+(u_P+Lx)\in u_\perp+P$; hence the normal of $n^\perp$ lies in $\operatorname{span}(\alpha,\beta)$ if and only if $u_\perp=0$, a condition independent of $x$. Therefore, on the connected set $O$, either $u_\perp=0$ and $\omega\equiv0$, or $u_\perp\ne0$ and $\omega$ is nowhere zero. This is the dichotomy asserted in clause (ii), with "rotational" meaning that the vorticity has no zeros. [F1, F2, F10, algebra]


1.6 Irrotational case, the label and the formulas: on a small enough neighbourhood $U$ of a point of the curve consider $f(s,x):=\eta(z'(s),x-z(s))$, smooth with $f(s,z(s))=0$ and $\partial_sf(s,x)=\eta(z''(s),x-z(s))-\eta(z'(s),z'(s))=N(x)$, where $N(x):=1+\eta(z''(\sigma(x)),x-z(\sigma(x)))$ is to be evaluated at the label $s=\sigma(x)$ below; in particular $\partial_sf(s,z(s))=1>0$. In an inertial chart the map $(s,x)\mapsto(f(s,x),x)$ has at $(s,z(s))$ the block derivative $\begin{pmatrix}1&\partial_xf\\0&I\end{pmatrix}$, which is invertible; by the choice-free inverse function theorem [F9] there is a uniquely determined smooth function $\sigma$ with $f(\sigma(x),x)=0$ on a neighbourhood $U$, and shrinking $U$ keeps $N>0$ because $N(z(s))=1$ and $N$ is continuous. On $U$ the level sets of $\sigma$ are exactly the leaves: $\sigma$ is constant exactly along $D$, and each level is an open subset of a hyperplane $z(s)+z'(s)^\perp$. Differentiating $f(\sigma(x),x)=0$ in a direction $v$ gives $0=N(x)\,d\sigma(v)+\eta(z'(\sigma(x)),v)$, which is the displayed formula for $d\sigma$, and $n=z'\circ\sigma$ on $U$ because both are future unit vectors orthogonal to the same leaf. Finally $\nabla_vn=\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{t=0}z'(\sigma(x+tv))=z''(\sigma(x))\,d\sigma(v)$ gives $\nabla n=d\sigma\otimes(z''\circ\sigma)$, and $a=\nabla_nn=d\sigma(n)\,z''(\sigma)=z''(\sigma)/N$ because $d\sigma(n)=-\eta(z'(\sigma),n)/N=1/N$ as $\eta(z'(\sigma),n)=\eta(n,n)=-1$. [F2, F9, F11, F12, given, algebra]


2.1 Connection coefficients, entries with a $0$: define one-forms $\gamma^0{}_i=\gamma^i{}_0:=a_i\theta^0-\omega_{ij}\theta^j$ and $\gamma^i{}_j:=\bar\gamma^i{}_j-\omega_{ij}\theta^0$, where $a_i:=a^\flat(e_i)$ and $\omega_{ij}:=\omega(e_i,e_j)$. We claim that $\gamma^A{}_B(X)=\theta^A(\nabla_Xe_B)$ for all $A,B$; since the right-hand side is the connection matrix of the Levi-Civita connection in this frame by [F4], this identifies $\gamma$ and gives in particular the skew relations $\gamma^0{}_i=\gamma^i{}_0$ and $\gamma^i{}_j=-\gamma^j{}_i$. For the entries with a zero index: $\theta^0(\nabla_ne_i)=a_i$, because $0=n(\eta(n,e_i))=(\nabla_nn^\flat)(e_i)+n^\flat(\nabla_ne_i)$ gives $n^\flat(\nabla_ne_i)=-a_i$ and $\theta^0=-n^\flat$; $\theta^i(\nabla_ne_j)=\theta^i(\nabla_{e_j}n)+\theta^i([n,e_j])=\omega(e_j,e_i)+0=-\omega_{ij}$ by step 1.4; and $\theta^0(\nabla_{e_j}e_i)=\omega_{ji}=-\omega_{ij}$, because $0=e_j(\eta(n,e_i))=(\nabla_{e_j}n^\flat)(e_i)+n^\flat(\nabla_{e_j}e_i)=\omega_{ji}+n^\flat(\nabla_{e_j}e_i)$. Thus $\gamma^0{}_i(e_0)=\gamma^i{}_0(e_0)=a_i$ and $\gamma^0{}_i(e_j)=\gamma^i{}_0(e_j)=-\omega_{ij}$. [F2, F4, step 1.4, algebra]


2.2 Irrotational case, leaves: assume now $\theta=\omega=0$ on $\Omega$. By step 1.1, $\nabla_Xn=0$ for every vector field $X$ tangent to the rest distribution $D=\ker n^\flat$; in particular, in an inertial chart, all first partial derivatives of the components of $n$ along directions in $D$ vanish. The distribution $D$ is integrable by the Frobenius criterion [F13], because $\omega=0$. Let $S$ be a connected leaf of $D$ through a point $p$. For a $C^1$ curve $\gamma$ in $S$ the tangent $\gamma'$ takes values in $D\subseteq\ker n^\flat$ and $\frac{d}{dt}n(\gamma(t))=\nabla_{\gamma'}n=0$, so $n$ is constant on $S$ with value $n_0:=n(p)$; consequently the tangent space of $S$ at each of its points is $D=n_0^\perp$, and integrating the constant fields of $n_0^\perp$ shows that $S$ is an open subset of the affine hyperplane $p+n_0^\perp$. Choosing a maximal integral curve of $n$ through a point (its parameter has speed $1$, since $\eta(n,n)=-1$) and shrinking to a neighbourhood $U$ of one of its points over which the labels of the next step are unique, we obtain a smooth future timelike curve $z:J\to A$ with $z'=n\circ z$, $\eta(z',z')=-1$, such that the leaf through $z(s)$ is $z(s)+z'(s)^\perp$. [F2, F11, F13, given, algebra]


2.3 Irrotational case, converse: conversely let $z:J\to A$ be smooth with $\eta(z',z')=-1$, let $\sigma$ be a smooth function on a tubular neighbourhood $U$ whose level sets are $z(s)+z'(s)^\perp$ with $N>0$, and put $n:=z'\circ\sigma$; then $n$ is smooth and future unit, its rest distribution is the tangent distribution of the $\sigma$-levels, which is integrable, and for $X$ tangent to a level one has $\nabla_Xn=\nabla_X(z'\circ\sigma)=z''(\sigma)\,d\sigma(X)=0$ because $d\sigma$ vanishes on the level directions. By the computation of step 1.1 this gives $\theta(X,Y)+\omega(X,Y)=0$ for all horizontal fields $X,Y$; the rest distribution is integrable, so $\omega=0$ by the Frobenius criterion [F13]; hence $\theta(X,Y)=0$ for all horizontal $X,Y$, that is, $\theta=0$. Thus $n$ is a smooth future unit irrotational Born-rigid congruence satisfying the same formulas $\nabla n=d\sigma\otimes(z''\circ\sigma)$, $a=z''(\sigma)/N$ and $N=1+\eta(z''(\sigma),x-z(\sigma))$ as in step 1.6, with the label derivative $1+\eta(z''\circ\sigma,x-z\circ\sigma)=N$ positive on $U$. [F2, F12, F13, step 1.1, step 1.6, algebra]

## Example

In an inertial chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ of the affine Minkowski model with metric $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ let the observer be at rest at the spatial origin, so that its worldline is $x^1=x^2=x^3=0$, let $T>0$, and let $q:=x^{-1}\bigl(cT,\tfrac35cT,0,0\bigr)$, an event of chart time $T$ and spatial coordinate $(3cT/5,0,0)$. With $e_-:=x^{-1}\bigl(\tfrac25cT,0,0,0\bigr)$ and $e_+:=x^{-1}\bigl(\tfrac85cT,0,0,0\bigr)$ one has $q-e_-=\bigl(\tfrac35cT,\tfrac35cT,0,0\bigr)$ and $e_+-q=\bigl(\tfrac35cT,-\tfrac35cT,0,0\bigr)$; both displacements have $\eta$-square $-\tfrac{9}{25}c^2T^2+\tfrac{9}{25}c^2T^2=0$ and positive time component, hence are future null, so the radar protocol applies with emission $e_-$, reflection $q$ and reception $e_+$ ([[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]], [[lem-sr-radar-midpoint-for-inertial-observer]]). Since the observer is inertial, its proper time between the chart times $\lambda_-=\tfrac25cT$ and $\lambda_+=\tfrac85cT$ is $(\lambda_+-\lambda_-)/c$ up to one additive constant, so the radar assignments are $\tau_{\mathrm{rad}}(q)=\tfrac12\bigl(\tfrac25T+\tfrac85T\bigr)=T$, the chart time of $q$, and $\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}(q)=\tfrac{c}{2}\bigl(\tfrac85T-\tfrac25T\bigr)=\tfrac35cT$, the chart distance of $q$ from the observer. The same computation for $q':=x^{-1}\bigl(cT,\tfrac45cT,0,0\bigr)$ gives $e'_-=x^{-1}\bigl(\tfrac15cT,0,0,0\bigr)$, $e'_+=x^{-1}\bigl(\tfrac95cT,0,0,0\bigr)$, radar time $T$ and radar distance $\tfrac45cT$. Hence the two events $q$ and $q'$ of equal chart time are radar-simultaneous, with radar distances equal to their chart distances, in agreement with [[lem-sr-radar-midpoint-for-inertial-observer]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with chart $x$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), $T>0$, the observer worldline $W=\{x^{-1}(\lambda,0,0,0):\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$ at rest at the spatial origin, the events $q=x^{-1}(cT,\tfrac35cT,0,0)$, $e_-=x^{-1}(\tfrac25cT,0,0,0)$, $e_+=x^{-1}(\tfrac85cT,0,0,0)$ and $q'=x^{-1}(cT,\tfrac45cT,0,0)$, $e'_-=x^{-1}(\tfrac15cT,0,0,0)$, $e'_+=x^{-1}(\tfrac95cT,0,0,0)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L1] Chart and frame: $x^{-1}(\lambda,r_1,r_2,r_3)=o+\lambda e_0+r_1e_1+r_2e_2+r_3e_3$, the coordinate basis is $\eta$-orthonormal with $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$, and the spatial part of a displacement is measured by the Euclidean norm of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]] ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L2] Future null criterion: a nonzero vector $v=v^0e_0+v^1e_1+v^2e_2+v^3e_3$ is future null exactly when $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v^0>0$; indeed the closure of the future cone is $\{v:v^0\ge|v_{\mathrm{vec}}|\}$ in the coordinates of the frame, and on the null cone $v^0=|v_{\mathrm{vec}}|$, so for $v\ne0$ the condition $v^0>0$ is exactly $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

[L3] Radar midpoint lemma: for a future unit $n$, events $e_\pm=o+\lambda_\pm n$ with $\lambda_-<\lambda_+$ and an event $q$, the conditions "$q-e_-$ future null and $e_+-q$ future null" hold if and only if $q=o+\tfrac{\lambda_-+\lambda_+}{2}n+u$ with $u\in n^\perp$ and $|u|=(\lambda_+-\lambda_-)/2$; in that case the midpoint is $m=\tfrac{e_-+e_+}{2}$, the event $q$ lies in the slice $H(m,n)$, and its rest distance in that slice is $(\lambda_+-\lambda_-)/2$ ([[lem-sr-radar-midpoint-for-inertial-observer]], [[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]]).

[L4] Radar protocol: an observer with proper-time function $\tau$ assigns to a reflection event $q$ reached from $e_-=x(s_-)$ and connected to $e_+=x(s_+)$ by future null segments the values $\tau_{\mathrm{rad}}(q)=\tfrac12\bigl(\tau(s_-)+\tau(s_+)\bigr)$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}(q)=\tfrac{c}{2}\bigl(\tau(s_+)-\tau(s_-)\bigr)$ ([[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]]).

[L5] Proper time of an inertial observer: for the straight worldline $\lambda\mapsto o+\lambda e_0$ the proper-time function satisfies $\tau'(\lambda)=c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(e_0,e_0)}=1/c$, hence $\tau(\lambda)=\lambda/c+\mathrm{const}$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The events of the statement are $e_-=o+\tfrac25cT\,e_0$, $e_+=o+\tfrac85cT\,e_0$, $q=o+cT\,e_0+\tfrac35cT\,e_1$ and $m:=x^{-1}(cT,0,0,0)=o+cT\,e_0$ by [L1]; the observer direction is $n:=e_0$, future unit. With $u:=\tfrac35cT\,e_1\in n^\perp$ one has $q=m+u$ and $|u|=\tfrac35cT=\tfrac12\bigl(\tfrac85cT-\tfrac25cT\bigr)=(\lambda_+-\lambda_-)/2$, so condition (ii) of [L3] holds; by the implication (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i) of [L3] the displacements $q-e_-$ and $e_+-q$ are future null and the radar protocol applies with emission $e_-$, reflection $q$ and reception $e_+$. ## Example

In an inertial chart $x$ let the chart $x'$ be related to $x$ by a boost of speed $v=3c/5$ along the first spatial axis, $\gamma=5/4$, so that $x'^0=\tfrac54\bigl(x^0-\tfrac35x^1\bigr)$ and $x'^1=\tfrac54\bigl(x^1-\tfrac35x^0\bigr)$ ([[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]], [[def-lorentz-boost]]). Let $L_0=5$ and let the rod at rest in $x'$ have endpoints on the worldlines $x'^1=0$ and $x'^1=5$, with vanishing transverse coordinates. Solving the transition for $x^1$ as a function of $x^0$ gives $x^1=\tfrac35x^0$ on the first worldline and $x^1=\tfrac35x^0+4$ on the second, so at every equal $x$-time the endpoints are separated by $4=L_0/\gamma$ in the frame $x$. Explicit witness: the events $p:=x^{-1}(5,3,0,0)$ and $r:=x^{-1}(5,7,0,0)$ are simultaneous in $x$ (both have $x^0=5$) and separated by $4$; their $x'$-coordinates are $x'(p)=(4,0,0,0)$ and $x'(r)=(1,5,0,0)$, so they are not simultaneous in $x'$ but their $x'$-separation is $5=L_0$. Comparing events at equal $x'$-time instead: the events of the two worldlines with $x'^0=4$ are $x^{-1}(5,3,0,0)$ and $x^{-1}(35/4,37/4,0,0)$, the second of which has $x'^1=5$; at equal $x'$-time $4$ the endpoints are separated by $5$, the rest length. Thus the frame $x$ assigns length $4$ to a rod of rest length $5$ at rest in $x'$, exactly the contraction $L_0/\gamma$ of clause (ii) of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]], and the comparison uses the simultaneity slice of the measuring frame in the sense of [[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Two inertial charts $x$, $x'$ of the affine Minkowski model related by the boost of speed $v=3c/5$ along the first axis with $\gamma=5/4$, the number $L_0=5$, the two worldlines $x'^1=0$ and $x'^1=5$ at rest in $x'$ with zero transverse coordinates, and the witness events $p=x^{-1}(5,3,0,0)$, $r=x^{-1}(5,7,0,0)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L1] The transition is $x'^0=\gamma\bigl(x^0-\tfrac35x^1\bigr)$, $x'^1=\gamma\bigl(x^1-\tfrac35x^0\bigr)$, $x'^2=x^2$, $x'^3=x^3$ with $\gamma=5/4$ ([[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]], [[def-lorentz-boost]]).

[L2] Length comparison (clause (ii) of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]]): two worldlines at rest in $x'$ with $x'$-separation $L_0$ have $x$-separation $L_0/\gamma$ at equal $x$-times, while at equal $x'$-times their $x'$-separation is $L_0$.

[L3] Simultaneity relative to a chart is equality of the chart's time coordinate, and the events simultaneous with $p$ in the frame $x$ are the slice $H(p,e_0)$ of the measuring frame ([[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 On the worldline $x'^1=c$ the transition reads $\gamma(x^1-\tfrac35x^0)=c$, so $x^1=\tfrac35x^0+c/\gamma=\tfrac35x^0+\tfrac45c$; for $c=0$ this is $x^1=\tfrac35x^0$ and for $c=L_0=5$ it is $x^1=\tfrac35x^0+4$. Hence at every fixed $x^0$ the $x$-separation of the two worldlines is $4=L_0/\gamma$ as asserted. [L1, L2, algebra]

1.2 The witness events: $x'(p)=\bigl(\tfrac54(5-\tfrac35\cdot3),\tfrac54(3-\tfrac35\cdot5),0,0\bigr)=(4,0,0,0)$ and $x'(r)=\bigl(\tfrac54(5-\tfrac35\cdot7),\tfrac54(7-\tfrac35\cdot5),0,0\bigr)=(1,5,0,0)$; the first lies on $x'^1=0$ and the second on $x'^1=5$, both have $x^0=5$ hence are simultaneous in $x$ and separated by $7-3=4$; their $x'$-times $4$ and $1$ differ, their $x'$-separation is $5$. [L1, L3, algebra]

1.3 Equal $x'$-time comparison: on the second worldline, $x'^0=\tfrac54\bigl(x^0-\tfrac35(\tfrac35x^0+4)\bigr)=\tfrac45x^0-3$; setting $x'^0=4$ gives $x^0=35/4$ and then $x^1=\tfrac35\cdot\tfrac{35}{4}+4=\tfrac{37}{4}$, so the two events $x^{-1}(5,3,0,0)$ and $x^{-1}(35/4,37/4,0,0)$ have equal $x'$-time $4$; their $x'^1$-coordinates are $0$ and $5$, so at equal $x'$-time the separation is the rest length $5$. [L1, L2, algebra]

2.1 Conclusion: the frame $x$ assigns to the rod the length $4$ at its own equal-$x$-time slice, which is exactly $L_0/\gamma=5/(5/4)=4$ of clause (ii) of [L2]; the same pair of worldlines has $x'$-separation $5$ at equal $x'$-times, and the witness events show explicitly that the equal-$x$ and the equal-$x'$ comparisons involve different pairs of events. ## Remarks

- **Which events are being compared.** The two witness events of step 1.2 are simultaneous in $x$ and not in $x'$, while the two events of step 1.3 are simultaneous in $x'$ and not in $x$; the contracted and the rest lengths therefore refer to different pairs of events on the same two worldlines, which is exactly the content of clause (ii) of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]].

- **No optical claim.** The length $4$ assigned by $x$ is the distance of the rod's endpoints on a simultaneity slice of $x$; it is not an appearance or a photograph, and no light-propagation or measurement model is involved.

## Example

Let $x$ and $x'$ be inertial charts related by a boost of parameter $v=3c/5$ along the first axis ($\gamma=5/4$, [[def-lorentz-boost]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

(a) **Collinear case.** A worldline with coordinate velocity $w=(4c/5,0,0)$ in $x$ has, by clause (iv) of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]], $w'_1=(4c/5-3c/5)/(1-(3/5)(4/5))=(c/5)/(13/25)=5c/13$, so $|w'|=5c/13<c$; the Galilean sum $7c/5$ is not the transformed velocity.

(b) **Transverse case.** A worldline with $w=(0,c/2,0)$ has $w'_1=(0-3c/5)/(1-0)=-3c/5$ and $w'_2=(c/2)/((5/4)(1-0))=2c/5$, hence $|w'|=\sqrt{9/25+4/25}\,c=(\sqrt{13}/5)c<c$.

(c) **Null limit.** For $w=(c,0,0)$ the formula gives $w'_1=(c-3c/5)/(1-3/5)=c$ and $|w'|=c$: a null worldline is null in every inertial chart.

The three cases verify the velocity transformation and the subluminality statement of clause (iv) of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Two inertial charts $x$, $x'$ related by the boost of parameter $v=3c/5$ along the first axis with $\gamma=5/4$, and the three coordinate velocities $w=(4c/5,0,0)$, $w=(0,c/2,0)$, $w=(c,0,0)$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L1] Clause (iv) of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]]: for a $C^1$ future timelike worldline with coordinate velocity $w$, $|w|<c$, in the chart $x$, the coordinate velocity in $x'$ is $w'_1=(w_1-v)/(1-vw_1/c^2)$ and $w'_\perp=w_\perp/\bigl(\gamma(1-vw_1/c^2)\bigr)$, with positive denominators, and $|w'|<c$, with $|w'|=c$ exactly when $|w|=c$.

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Collinear case: with $w_1=4c/5$, $w_\perp=0$, $v=3c/5$, the denominator of [L1] is $1-\tfrac35\cdot\tfrac45=1-\tfrac{12}{25}=\tfrac{13}{25}>0$ and $w'_1=\tfrac{c/5}{13/25}=\tfrac{5c}{13}$; hence $w'=(5c/13,0,0)$ and $|w'|=5c/13<c$ because $5/13<1$.
