## Definition

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $I$ be an order-convex subset of
$\mathbb{R}$ with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]), and let curves
$x:I\to A$ and their derivatives be as in
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]: the displacement
$x(s+h)-x(s)$ is taken in the affine structure of
[[def-affine-space-and-displacement]], and $x'(s)\in V$, when it exists, is the
limit of the difference quotients, read in the coordinate calculus of
[[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]] in any inertial chart
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]],
[[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]]).

### (a) Inertial worldlines

A curve $x:I\to A$ is **inertial** (also called **uniform** or **straight**)
when there are a parameter value $s_0\in I$, an event $p\in A$ and a vector
$d\in V$, with $d$ future timelike
([[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]), such that

$$x(s)=p+(s-s_0)\,d\qquad\text{for every }s\in I.$$

The affine action is defined for every real parameter and every vector, so the
display defines a map $I\to A$
([[def-affine-space-and-displacement]]); its image is
$x[I]=\{p+\lambda d:\lambda=s-s_0,\ s\in I\}$, and a restriction of an inertial
worldline to a subinterval of $I$ is inertial with the same $d$. Its tangent is
the constant vector $d$: in the chart $x_A$ of an inertial frame the coordinate
path is the affine function $s\mapsto x_A(p)+(s-s_0)E^{-1}(d)$, whose difference
quotients equal the constant $E^{-1}(d)$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]), so $x'(s)=d$ at
every $s\in I$ by clause (a) of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]; the same computation gives
$C^k$ regularity for every $k\ge1$. Since the constant tangent $d$ is future
timelike by hypothesis, an inertial curve is a future timelike worldline of the
model ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (c)). If two inertial worldlines
$x(s)=p+(s-s_0)d$ and $y(t)=p'+(t-t_0)d'$ have the same image and the same
direction of traversal, that is $d'=\alpha d$ with $\alpha>0$, then $p'$ lies in
the image of $x$, so $p'=p+\mu d$ for some real $\mu$, and

$$y(t)=x\bigl(s_0+\mu+\alpha(t-t_0)\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }t\text{ in the domain of }y,$$

an increasing affine reparametrization; conversely every increasing affine
reparametrization of an inertial worldline is inertial with the same image. This
computation uses only the affine axioms and $d\ne0$.

### (b) Piecewise inertial worldlines

Let $a<b$ be real numbers with $[a,b]\subseteq I$. A curve $x:[a,b]\to A$ is
**piecewise inertial** when there are a finite partition
$a=s_0<s_1<\dots<s_m=b$, events $p_1,\dots,p_m\in A$ and future timelike vectors
$d_1,\dots,d_m\in V$ such that

$$x(s)=p_i+(s-s_{i-1})\,d_i\qquad\text{for every }s\in[s_{i-1},s_i]\text{ and every }i=1,\dots,m,$$

and consecutive pieces agree at the partition points, that is
$p_{i+1}=p_i+(s_i-s_{i-1})d_i=x(s_i)$ for $i=1,\dots,m-1$. The joining condition
makes the piecewise formulas define a single function on $[a,b]$, whose tangent
on each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ is the constant $d_i$ and whose finite
one-sided difference-quotient tangents at an interior partition point $s_i$ are
$d_i$ from the left and $d_{i+1}$ from the right; at the endpoints $a$ and $b$
the one-sided quotients are $d_1$ and $d_m$. Hence a piecewise inertial curve is
a piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline on $[a,b]$ in the weak sense of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] — no continuous extension of the
derivative to the closed pieces is required, and the tangents are future timelike
at every smooth point and on both sides of every corner — and it is
$C^1$ on $[a,b]$ if and only if $d_1=d_2=\dots=d_m$. The events $x(s_i)$ with
$0<i<m$ are the **corners** of the itinerary, and the itinerary is a **two-leg
itinerary** when $m=2$.

### (c) Scope

The definition asserts the existence of no worldlines beyond the explicitly
parametrized straight and piecewise straight ones, and it attaches no clock
reading to any curve: readings of ideal clocks are the subject of the model's
postulates, not of this definition. No choice principle is used, since every
object is finitely parametrized and every operation is finite-dimensional.

## Statement

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space and
let $v,w\in V$ be future timelike vectors. Put
$a:=\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}>0$ and $b:=\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}>0$, the timelike lengths of
$v$ and $w$. Then:

**(i)** $-\eta(v,w)\ge ab>0$.

**(ii)** Equality $-\eta(v,w)=ab$ holds if and only if $v$ and $w$ are
positive proportional, that is $w=tv$ for some real $t>0$, or $v=tw$ for some
real $t>0$.

**(iii)** Consequently $-\eta(v,w)>ab$ whenever $v$ and $w$ are not positive
proportional, and $\eta(v,w)<0$ in every case.

**(iv)** For two past timelike vectors $v,w$ the same inequality
$-\eta(v,w)\ge\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}\,\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$ holds, with equality if and
only if they are positive proportional, because $-v$ and $-w$ are future
timelike and $\eta(-v,-w)=\eta(v,w)$.

The statement uses only $\eta$ and the future cone $C^+$ and involves no chart,
frame or choice principle.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ and future timelike vectors $v,w\in V$, with $a:=\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}>0$ and $b:=\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}>0$.

[F1] Inertial frames and charts: at every event $o\in A$ there is an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$; its ordered basis is $\eta$-orthonormal with $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$, its first vector $e_0$ lies in $C^+$, and $E(u):=\sum_a u^ae_a$ is a linear isomorphism $E:\mathbb{R}^4\to V$, so every vector $u\in V$ has unique coordinates $u=u^0e_0+u_s$ with $u_s=u^1e_1+u^2e_2+u^3e_3$ ([[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[F2] Cone coordinates: in an $\eta$-orthonormal basis whose first vector is timelike the timelike set is the disjoint union $T=T_+\cup T_-$ with $T_+=\{u:u^0>|u_s|\}$ and $T_-=\{u:u^0<-|u_s|\}$, and $T_+$, $T_-$ are exactly the two connected components of $T$; the time orientation selects one component $C^+$ and $C^-:=T\setminus C^+$ is the other, so with the basis of [F1], where $e_0\in C^+$, one has $C^+=T_+$ and $C^-=T_-=-C^+$; hence $u$ is future timelike if and only if $u^0>|u_s|$, and $u$ is past timelike if and only if $-u$ is future timelike ([[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

[F3] Spatial and bilinear structure: for a frame of [F1], the spatial three-space $S:=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)=\{z\in V:\eta(e_0,z)=0\}$ carries the restriction $\delta:=\eta|_S$, which is positive definite, and $|z|:=\sqrt{\delta(z,z)}$ is a norm on $S$ with $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ a $\delta$-orthonormal basis; since $\eta$ is bilinear, for all $u=u^0e_0+u_s$ and $u'=u'^0e_0+u'_s$ one has $\eta(u,u')=-u^0u'^0+\delta(u_s,u'_s)$, and in particular $\eta(u,u)=-(u^0)^2+|u_s|^2$ ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

[L4] Finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality: for reals $a_0,\dots,a_{n-1}$ and $b_0,\dots,b_{n-1}$ one has $\big(\sum_{k<n}a_kb_k\big)^2\le\big(\sum_{k<n}a_k^2\big)\big(\sum_{k<n}b_k^2\big)$ and $\big|\sum_{k<n}a_kb_k\big|\le\sqrt{\sum_{k<n}a_k^2}\,\sqrt{\sum_{k<n}b_k^2}$; equality holds in the first display if and only if the two lists are proportional in the sense that there is a pair $(\lambda,\mu)\neq(0,0)$ of reals with $\lambda a_k=\mu b_k$ for every $k<n$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]]).

[L5] Square roots and monotonicity of squaring: every real $c\ge0$ has a unique $\sqrt c\ge0$ with $(\sqrt c)^2=c$ ([[thm-of-square-roots]]); for $x,y\ge0$ one has $x\le y\iff x^2\le y^2$ and $x<y\iff x^2<y^2$ ([[lem-of-square-monotone]]); for $c>0$ the root notation is the rational power $c^{1/2}$ ([[def-rational-power]]).

[L6] Order arithmetic of $\mathbb{R}$: a product of two positive reals is positive and a product of a positive and a negative real is negative ([[lem-of-sign-rules]]); inequalities may be added, and a constant may be added to both sides of an inequality ([[lem-of-add-order]]); and for reals $x,y$ exactly one of $x<y$, $x=y$, $x>y$ holds, a product of reals vanishes only if a factor vanishes, and $x\ge0$ means $x>0$ or $x=0$ ([[def-ordered-field]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Fix an event $o\in A$ and an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with its basis and chart, and write $v=v^0e_0+v_s$, $w=w^0e_0+w_s$ with spatial parts $v_s,w_s\in S$; the coordinates are unique by [F1] and the spatial parts lie in $S$ by the definition of $S$ in [F3]. [given, F1, F3, choose]

2.1 Since $v$ and $w$ are future timelike, [F2] gives $v^0>|v_s|$ and $w^0>|w_s|$; as $|v_s|,|w_s|\ge0$ by [F3], this yields $v^0>0$, $w^0>0$, and by strict monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives $(v^0)^2>|v_s|^2$ and $(w^0)^2>|w_s|^2$, so $a^2=(v^0)^2-|v_s|^2>0$ and $b^2=(w^0)^2-|w_s|^2>0$, whence $a=\sqrt{(v^0)^2-|v_s|^2}>0$ and $b=\sqrt{(w^0)^2-|w_s|^2}>0$ by uniqueness of the nonnegative root. [step 1.1, F2, F3, L5, L6]

2.2 By bilinearity [F3], $-\eta(v,w)=v^0w^0-\delta(v_s,w_s)$; applying the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality [L4] to the coordinates of $v_s$ and $w_s$ in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ gives $|\delta(v_s,w_s)|\le|v_s|\,|w_s|$, hence $\delta(v_s,w_s)\le|v_s|\,|w_s|$ and $-\eta(v,w)\ge x$ for $x:=v^0w^0-|v_s|\,|w_s|$. [step 1.1, F3, L4, algebra]

3.1 The algebraic identity $x^2-\big((v^0)^2-|v_s|^2\big)\big((w^0)^2-|w_s|^2\big)=\big(v^0|w_s|-w^0|v_s|\big)^2\ge0$ holds by expansion, so $x^2\ge a^2b^2$; moreover $x=w^0\,(v^0-|v_s|)+|v_s|\,(w^0-|w_s|)$ is a sum of a positive real and a nonnegative real, so $x>0$ and in particular $x\ge0$. [step 2.1, L6, algebra]

4.1 Since $x\ge0$ and $ab>0$ with $x^2\ge(ab)^2$, monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives [L5] gives $x\ge ab$, and with step 2.2 this yields $-\eta(v,w)\ge ab>0$, which is (i); equivalently $\eta(v,w)\le-ab<0$. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, L5, L6]

5.1 Assume now $-\eta(v,w)=ab$. Then the chain $ab=-\eta(v,w)\ge x\ge ab$ of steps 2.2 and 4.1 is equality at both places, so $\delta(v_s,w_s)=|v_s|\,|w_s|$, and from $x=ab$ and the identity of step 3.1 we get $\big(v^0|w_s|-w^0|v_s|\big)^2=x^2-(ab)^2=0$, that is $v^0|w_s|=w^0|v_s|$. [step 2.2, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Case $v_s=0$: then $v^0|w_s|=w^0|v_s|=0$ by step 5.1, and $v^0>0$, so $|w_s|=0$ and hence $w_s=0$; therefore $v=v^0e_0$ and $w=w^0e_0$ with $v^0,w^0>0$, and $v=(v^0/w^0)w$ exhibits $v$ as a positive multiple of $w$. [step 2.1, step 5.1, L6]

6.2 Case $w_s=0$: symmetrically $w^0|v_s|=v^0|w_s|=0$ with $w^0>0$ gives $v_s=0$, and $v^0>0$ gives $w=(w^0/v^0)v$, so $w$ is a positive multiple of $v$. [step 2.1, step 5.1, L6]

6.3 Case $v_s\neq0$ and $w_s\neq0$: the equality $\delta(v_s,w_s)=|v_s|\,|w_s|>0$ of step 5.1 is the equality case of the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality [L4] for two nonzero lists, so there are reals $(\lambda,\mu)\neq(0,0)$ with $\lambda v_s=\mu w_s$; here $\lambda\neq0$ (otherwise $w_s=0$) and $\mu\neq0$ (otherwise $v_s=0$), so $v_s=cw_s$ with $c:=\mu/\lambda$, and then $\delta(v_s,w_s)=c\,|w_s|^2$ while $|v_s|=|c|\,|w_s|$, so $c\,|w_s|^2=|c|\,|w_s|^2$ with $|w_s|^2=\delta(w_s,w_s)>0$; hence $c=|c|\ge0$, and $c>0$ because $c\,|w_s|^2=|v_s|\,|w_s|>0$; finally $v^0|w_s|=w^0|v_s|=w^0c|w_s|$ with $|w_s|>0$ gives $v^0=cw^0$, so $v=v^0e_0+cw_s=c\,(w^0e_0+w_s)=cw$ with $c>0$. [step 5.1, L4, L5, L6, algebra]

7.1 The three cases of steps 6.1-6.3 exhaust the possibilities, so equality $-\eta(v,w)=ab$ forces $v$ and $w$ to be positive proportional; this is the forward implication of (ii). [step 6.1, step 6.2, step 6.3]

8.1 Conversely, if $v=tw$ with $t>0$, then bilinearity gives $-\eta(v,w)=-t\,\eta(w,w)=tb^2$ and $-\eta(v,v)=-t^2\eta(w,w)=t^2b^2$, so $a=tb$ by uniqueness of the nonnegative square root, whence $-\eta(v,w)=tb\cdot b=ab$; the case $w=tv$ is identical, and together with step 7.1 this proves (ii). [step 2.1, F3, L5, algebra]

9.1 For (iii): if $v$ and $w$ are not positive proportional then equality fails by (ii), so $-\eta(v,w)>ab$ by step 4.1, while $\eta(v,w)<0$ holds in every case again by step 4.1. [step 4.1, step 7.1, step 8.1]

10.1 For (iv): if $v,w$ are past timelike then $-v,-w$ are future timelike by [F2], with $-\eta(-v,-v)=-\eta(v,v)$, $-\eta(-w,-w)=-\eta(w,w)$ and $\eta(-v,-w)=\eta(v,w)$ by bilinearity [F3]; steps 4.1, 7.1 and 8.1 applied to $-v,-w$ therefore give $-\eta(v,w)=-\eta(-v,-w)\ge ab$, with equality exactly when $-v,-w$ are positive proportional, that is exactly when $v,w$ are positive proportional. [step 4.1, step 7.1, step 8.1, F2, F3] ∎

## Statement

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space.

**(a) Sum of two future timelike vectors.** If $v,w\in V$ are future timelike,
then $v+w$ is future timelike and
$$\sqrt{-\eta(v+w,v+w)}\ \ge\ \sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}+\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)},$$
with equality if and only if $v$ and $w$ are positive proportional.

**(b) Convexity and concavity along segments.** If $v,w$ are future timelike,
then $tv+(1-t)w$ is future timelike for every real $t\in[0,1]$, so the set of
future timelike vectors is convex; moreover
$$\sqrt{-\eta\big(tv+(1-t)w,\ tv+(1-t)w\big)}\ \ge\ t\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}+(1-t)\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$$
for every $t\in[0,1]$, with equality for $0<t<1$ if and only if $v$ and $w$ are
positive proportional.

**(c) Finite sums.** If $k\ge1$ and $v_1,\dots,v_k\in V$ are future timelike,
then $v_1+\cdots+v_k$ is future timelike and
$$\sqrt{-\eta\Big(\sum_{i=1}^k v_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^k v_i\Big)}\ \ge\ \sum_{i=1}^k\sqrt{-\eta(v_i,v_i)},$$
with equality if and only if all $v_i$ are positive multiples of one single
future timelike vector.

The inequalities are those of the model's $\eta$ and are independent of any
chart; they are the reversed (Lorentzian) forms of the triangle inequality of
the spatial Euclidean structure.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$.

[F1] Inertial frames and cone coordinates: at every event there is an inertial frame, and in its coordinates $u=u^0e_0+u_s$ with spatial part $u_s\in S=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ one has $\eta(u,u')=-u^0u'^0+\delta(u_s,u'_s)$ for all $u,u'\in V$ and $u\in C^+\iff u^0>|u_s|$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

[F2] The spatial form $\delta$ is positive definite on $S$, $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\delta$-orthonormal, $|z|:=\sqrt{\delta(z,z)}$ is the induced norm, and for $z,z'\in S$ one has $\delta(z,z')=\sum_{i=1}^3 z^iz'^i$ and $|z|=\sqrt{(z^1)^2+(z^2)^2+(z^3)^2}$; the norm satisfies $|z|\ge0$, $|z|=0\iff z=0$, $|\lambda z|=|\lambda|\,|z|$ and the triangle inequality $|z+z'|\le|z|+|z'|$ ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]], [[cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm]]).

[F3] Reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality ([[lem-sr-reverse-cauchy-schwarz-for-future-timelike-vectors]]): if $v,w$ are future timelike and $a:=\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}$, $b:=\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$, then $-\eta(v,w)\ge ab>0$, and equality $-\eta(v,w)=ab$ holds if and only if $v$ and $w$ are positive proportional, that is $w=tv$ or $v=tw$ for some real $t>0$.

[L4] Square roots and monotonicity of squaring: every real $c\ge0$ has a unique $\sqrt c\ge0$ with $(\sqrt c)^2=c$ ([[thm-of-square-roots]]); for $x,y\ge0$ one has $x\le y\iff x^2\le y^2$ and $x<y\iff x^2<y^2$ ([[lem-of-square-monotone]]).

[L5] Order arithmetic of $\mathbb{R}$: inequalities may be added and a constant may be added to both sides of an inequality ([[lem-of-add-order]]); for $c>0$ one has $a<b\iff ac<bc$, and a product of two positive reals is positive ([[lem-of-sign-rules]]); and for reals $x,y$ exactly one of $x<y$, $x=y$, $x>y$ holds, while a product vanishes only if a factor vanishes ([[def-ordered-field]]).

[L6] Induction principle: if a property $P$ satisfies $P(1)$ and $P(k)\Rightarrow P(k+1)$ for every integer $k\ge1$, then $P(k)$ holds for every integer $k\ge1$ ([[thm-induction-principle]], applied to the shift $k\mapsto k-1$ of the natural-number form).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Fix an event $o\in A$ and an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with its coordinates; by [F1] every vector $u$ is written uniquely as $u=u^0e_0+u_s$ with $u_s\in S$, the pairing is $\eta(u,u')=-u^0u'^0+\delta(u_s,u'_s)$, and $u\in C^+\iff u^0>|u_s|$. [given, F1, choose]

2.1 Let $v,w$ be future timelike. Then $(v+w)^0=v^0+w^0>|v_s|+|w_s|\ge|v_s+w_s|=|(v+w)_s|$: the first inequality adds the two strict inequalities $v^0>|v_s|$ and $w^0>|w_s|$ that [F1] gives from future timelikeness, the second is the triangle inequality of the spatial norm, and the displayed equalities are additivity of coordinates; hence $v+w$ is future timelike. [step 1.1, F1, F2, L5]

3.1 Let $a:=\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}$, $b:=\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$ and $C:=\sqrt{-\eta(v+w,v+w)}$, which is a positive real by step 2.1; bilinearity and symmetry of $\eta$ give $C^2=-\eta(v+w,v+w)=-\eta(v,v)-2\eta(v,w)-\eta(w,w)=a^2+b^2+2\,(-\eta(v,w))$, and $-\eta(v,w)\ge ab$ by the reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, so multiplying by the positive number $2$ and adding the constant $a^2+b^2$ yields $C^2\ge a^2+b^2+2ab=(a+b)^2$. [step 2.1, F1, F3, L5, algebra]

3.2 For $t\in(0,1)$ the vectors $tv$ and $(1-t)w$ are future timelike: $(tv)^0=tv^0>t|v_s|=|tv_s|$ because $t>0$ preserves the strict inequality and $|tv_s|=t|v_s|$ by the coordinate formula $|z|=\sqrt{(z^1)^2+(z^2)^2+(z^3)^2}$ of [F2] together with uniqueness of the nonnegative root, and symmetrically $(1-t)w^0>(1-t)|w_s|=|(1-t)w_s|$; for $t=0$ and $t=1$ the vector $tv+(1-t)w$ equals $w$ respectively $v$, which are future timelike. [step 2.1, F2, L4, L5]

3.3 For the base case $k=1$ of (c): a future timelike vector $v_1$ is its own sum, $\sqrt{-\eta(v_1,v_1)}\ge\sqrt{-\eta(v_1,v_1)}$ holds with equality, and $v_1=1\cdot v_1$ exhibits $v_1$ as a positive multiple of the single future timelike vector $u:=v_1$, so the equality characterization of (c) is satisfied for $k=1$. [step 2.1, L5, algebra]

4.1 Since $C\ge0$ and $a+b\ge0$ with $C^2\ge(a+b)^2$, monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives [L4] gives $C\ge a+b$: this is the inequality of (a). [step 3.1, L4]

4.2 For $t\in(0,1)$, (a) applied to the future timelike vectors $tv$ and $(1-t)w$ of step 3.2 gives $tv+(1-t)w$ future timelike and $\sqrt{-\eta(tv+(1-t)w,tv+(1-t)w)}\ge\sqrt{-\eta(tv,tv)}+\sqrt{-\eta((1-t)w,(1-t)w)}=t\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}+(1-t)\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$, the two displayed equalities using bilinearity and uniqueness of the nonnegative root; this is the inequality of (b) on the open interval. [step 3.2, F1, F3, L4, algebra]

5.1 Equality holds in (a) if and only if $C=a+b$, which by monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives [L4] is equivalent to $C^2=(a+b)^2$, hence, subtracting the common term $a^2+b^2$ from the two displays of step 3.1 and multiplying by $1/2$, to $-\eta(v,w)=ab$, and by the equality case of the reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality [F3] to $v$ and $w$ being positive proportional; this proves (a). [step 4.1, F3, L4, L5, algebra]

5.2 Induction step, membership and inequality: assume $k\ge1$ and that the claim of (c) holds for the integer $k$; let $v_1,\dots,v_{k+1}$ be future timelike and put $s:=v_1+\cdots+v_k$, which is future timelike by the induction hypothesis; applying (a) of steps 2.1 and 4.1 to the future timelike vectors $s$ and $v_{k+1}$ gives $s+v_{k+1}=v_1+\cdots+v_{k+1}$ future timelike and $\sqrt{-\eta(s+v_{k+1},s+v_{k+1})}\ge\sqrt{-\eta(s,s)}+\sqrt{-\eta(v_{k+1},v_{k+1})}\ge\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sqrt{-\eta(v_i,v_i)}+\sqrt{-\eta(v_{k+1},v_{k+1})}$, the second inequality being the induction hypothesis. [step 4.1, L5, algebra]

6.1 Equality in the interior inequality of (b) for $0<t<1$ holds if and only if $tv$ and $(1-t)w$ are positive proportional, by the equality case of (a) established in step 5.1 applied to the interior inequality of (b) of step 4.2; since $t>0$ and $1-t>0$, this is equivalent to $v$ and $w$ being positive proportional; at $t=0$ and $t=1$ the inequality reduces to an identity $b\ge b$ or $a\ge a$, and the statement makes no interior equality claim there, so (b) is proved. [step 4.2, step 5.1, L5]

6.2 Induction step, equality characterization: with the notation of step 5.2, if equality holds for the $k+1$ vectors, then both inequalities in the chain of step 5.2 are equalities; the second equality means that the equality case of the induction hypothesis applies to $v_1,\dots,v_k$, so there are a future timelike $u$ and reals $c_1,\dots,c_k>0$ with $v_i=c_iu$ and $s=(\sum_{i=1}^kc_i)u$; the first equality is the equality case of (a) for $s$ and $v_{k+1}$, so $s$ and $v_{k+1}$ are positive proportional, and since $s\neq0$ this gives $v_{k+1}=c_{k+1}u$ for some real $c_{k+1}>0$, so all $k+1$ vectors are positive multiples of the single future timelike vector $u$; conversely, if $v_i=c_iu$ with $c_i>0$ and $u$ future timelike for $i=1,\dots,k+1$, then $v_1+\cdots+v_{k+1}=(\sum_ic_i)u$ and bilinearity with uniqueness of the nonnegative root give $\sqrt{-\eta(\sum_iv_i,\sum_iv_i)}=(\sum_ic_i)\sqrt{-\eta(u,u)}=\sum_i\sqrt{-\eta(v_i,v_i)}$, so equality holds. [step 5.2, step 5.1, F1, L4, L5, algebra]

7.1 By [L6], applied to the property "$v_1,\dots,v_k$ future timelike implies the conclusions of (c) for these vectors", the base case of step 3.3 and the induction steps 5.2 and 6.2 prove (c) for every integer $k\ge1$: membership and inequality from step 5.2, and the equality characterization from step 6.2. [step 3.3, step 5.2, step 6.2, L6] ∎

## Statement

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let
$d\in V$ be a future timelike displacement and put $T:=\sqrt{-\eta(d,d)}>0$ and
$n:=d/T$. Then:

**(i)** $\eta(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future timelike, so $n$ is a future unit
timelike vector.

**(ii)** For every event $o$ there is an inertial frame
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the model with $e_0=n$.

**(iii)** For the inertial chart $x$ of any such frame one has
$x(o+\lambda d)=(\lambda T,0,0,0)$ for every real $\lambda$; in particular
$x(o)=0$ and $x(o+d)=(T,0,0,0)$. Consequently, for any two events $p,q$ with
$q-p=d$, the chart of such a frame represents the displacement $q-p$ by the
coordinate vector $(T,0,0,0)$: the spatial coordinates of $p$ and $q$ agree and
their time coordinates differ by $T$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ and a future timelike displacement $d\in V$, with $T:=\sqrt{-\eta(d,d)}>0$ and $n:=d/T$.

[F1] Inertial frames and charts: for every event $o$ and every $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis $(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)$ of $V$ with future first vector and positive orientation, $(o;f_0,\dots,f_3)$ is an inertial frame; its chart is $x(r)=E^{-1}(r-o)$ with $E(u)=\sum_a u^ae_a$ the frame's linear isomorphism, and every vector $u$ has unique coordinates $u=u^0e_0+u_s$, $u_s\in S=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]]).

[F2] Cone coordinates: in an inertial frame with first vector in $C^+$ one has $C^+=\{u:u^0>|u_s|\}$ and $C^-=\{u:u^0<-|u_s|\}$, and $\eta(u,u)=-(u^0)^2+|u_s|^2$; the restriction of $\eta$ to $S$ is positive definite, $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is orthonormal for it, and $|z|^2=\delta(z,z)$ for $z\in S$ ([[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]).

[F3] The passive boost $B(\beta)$ is defined for every parameter $\beta\in\mathbb{R}^3$ with $|\beta|<1$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]]); it is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with inverse $B(-\beta)$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]], [[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]); and if $u$ is future timelike with $\eta(u,u)=-1$ and coordinates $(u^0,u_s)$, then the parameter $\beta:=u_s/u^0$ satisfies $|\beta|<1$ and $B(\beta)u=f_0$, where $f_0$ is the first vector of the frame used for the coordinates ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]] (iv)).

[F4] Lorentz maps preserve the metric and the orientation class: for a linear Lorentz map $L$ one has $\eta(Lv,Lw)=\eta(v,w)$ for all $v,w$; the composition and the inverse of Lorentz maps are Lorentz maps, and the proper orthochronous ones form a group; if $L$ is proper, then the oriented volume form $\epsilon$ of [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]] is preserved, $\epsilon(Lv_0,\dots,Lv_3)=\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)$; and $\epsilon$ takes the value $1$ on every positively oriented $\eta$-orthonormal basis, so a tuple of four vectors with $\epsilon$-value $1$ is positively oriented ([[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]], [[lem-volume-form-is-independent-of-the-oriented-frame]]).

[L5] Square roots and monotonicity: every real $c\ge0$ has a unique $\sqrt c\ge0$ with $(\sqrt c)^2=c$ ([[thm-of-square-roots]]); for $x,y\ge0$ one has $x<y\iff x^2<y^2$ ([[lem-of-square-monotone]]).

[L6] Order arithmetic of $\mathbb{R}$: multiplication of an inequality by a positive real preserves it, and a product of positives is positive ([[lem-of-sign-rules]]); a constant may be added to both sides and inequalities may be added ([[lem-of-add-order]]); and the order is trichotomous and transitive, with $1>0$ ([[def-ordered-field]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 By bilinearity of $\eta$ and $T^2=-\eta(d,d)$ one has $\eta(n,n)=\eta(d,d)/T^2=(-T^2)/T^2=-1$, so $n$ is timelike and $\eta(n,n)=-1$; moreover $d$ is nonzero because it is timelike, so $n=d/T$ is nonzero. [given, F1, L5, L6, algebra]

2.1 Fix an event $o$ and an inertial frame $(o;f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)$ with chart $y$, and write $n=n^0f_0+n_s$ in its coordinates; since $n$ is timelike, [F2] puts it in $C^+$ or $C^-$, and since $n=d/T$ with $d^0>|d_s|\ge0$ and $T>0$ its first coordinate satisfies $n^0=d^0/T>0$, so $n$ lies in $C^+=\{u:u^0>|u_s|\}$ and is future timelike; in particular $n^0>|n_s|\ge0$. [step 1.1, given, F1, F2, L5, L6]

3.1 From $1=-\eta(n,n)=(n^0)^2-|n_s|^2$ we get $(n^0)^2=1+|n_s|^2>|n_s|^2$; setting $\beta:=n_s/n^0$ (the coordinate column, identified with the vector $\beta^1f_1+\beta^2f_2+\beta^3f_3$ of $S$) one has $|\beta|^2=\delta(\beta,\beta)=|n_s|^2/(n^0)^2<1$, hence $|\beta|<1$ by strict monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives and $|\beta|\ge0$; thus the passive boost $B(\beta)$ is defined. [step 2.1, F2, F3, L5, L6, algebra]

4.1 By [F3] (iv), applied to the future timelike unit vector $n$ with coordinates $(n^0,n_s)$, the boost satisfies $B(\beta)n=f_0$; and $B(\beta)$ is proper orthochronous with inverse $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$. [step 3.1, F3]

5.1 Define $e_0:=n=B(\beta)^{-1}f_0$ and $e_i:=B(\beta)^{-1}f_i$ for $i=1,2,3$; then $e_a=B(\beta)^{-1}f_a$ for all $a$, so $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\eta(f_a,f_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ because a Lorentz map preserves $\eta$, and the ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\eta$-orthonormal with future first vector $e_0=n$; it is positively oriented because $B(\beta)^{-1}$ is proper and preserves the oriented volume form, so $\epsilon(e_0,\dots,e_3)=\epsilon(f_0,\dots,f_3)=1$ for the positively oriented basis $(f_a)$, whence the basis $(e_a)$ is positively oriented. Therefore $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is an inertial frame with $e_0=n$, which is (ii). [step 4.1, F1, F4]

6.1 For the chart $x=E^{-1}(\cdot-o)$ of any inertial frame $(o;e_0,\dots,e_3)$ with $e_0=n$ one has $E(1,0,0,0)=e_0=n$ and $d=Tn$, so $x(o+\lambda d)=E^{-1}(\lambda d)=\lambda T\,E^{-1}(n)=\lambda T\,(1,0,0,0)=(\lambda T,0,0,0)$ for every real $\lambda$, since $E^{-1}$ is linear; in particular $x(o)=0$ and $x(o+d)=(T,0,0,0)$, which is (iii). [step 5.1, F1, algebra]

7.1 Consequently, for events $p,q$ with $q-p=d$, linearity of $E^{-1}$ gives $x(q)-x(p)=E^{-1}(q-p)=(T,0,0,0)$, so the spatial coordinates of $p$ and $q$ agree and their time coordinates differ by $T$; together with steps 1.1, 2.1, 5.1 and 6.1 this proves (i), (ii) and (iii). [step 6.1, F1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $c>0$ and let $x:[a,b]\to A$ be a future timelike worldline with $a<b$
([[def-interval]]) that is piecewise $C^1$ with partition
$a=s_0<s_1<\dots<s_m=b$ in the weak sense of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], with future timelike interior
tangents and finite one-sided difference-quotient tangents. Put $p:=x(a)$,
$q:=x(b)$ and $d:=q-p$. Then $d$ is future timelike. More precisely, writing
$\xi^a:=x_A^a\circ x$ for the coordinate path of the chart $x_A$ of any inertial
frame, one has
$$\xi^0(b)-\xi^0(a)>0\qquad\text{and}\qquad|\xi_{\mathrm{vec}}(b)-\xi_{\mathrm{vec}}(a)|<\xi^0(b)-\xi^0(a),$$
where $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean spatial norm of
[[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]. Consequently $p\ne q$,
the number $\sqrt{-\eta(d,d)}$ is a positive real number, and in every inertial
chart the time component of $d$ is positive and dominates the Euclidean norm of
its spatial part, which is exactly the coordinate description of future
timelikeness in that chart. No completeness, compactness beyond the given compact
interval, or choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A real $c>0$; an inertial frame with chart $x_A$ and coordinate path $y:=\xi=(y^0,z)$ of a piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline $x:[a,b]\to A$, $a<b$, with partition $a=s_0<\dots<s_m=b$, future timelike interior tangents and finite one-sided difference-quotient tangents ([[def-interval]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[F1] The weak piecewise class ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]): $x$ is $C^1$ on every open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ with future timelike tangent $x'$ there, and the finite one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at both ends of every piece exist; no continuous extension of the open-piece derivative to the closed piece is assumed.

[F2] Improper integrability and endpoint increments ([[lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability]]): for the piece $(\alpha,\beta)=(s_{i-1},s_i)$ with the notation $\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}g=\lim_{u\downarrow\alpha}\int_u^rg+\lim_{v\uparrow\beta}\int_r^vg$ of that lemma, one has $y^0{}'\ge|z'|\ge0$ and $y^0{}'>0$ on $(\alpha,\beta)$; every coordinate derivative is absolutely improperly Riemann integrable with signed improper integral its endpoint increment, so $\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}y^{j}{}'=y^j(\beta)-y^j(\alpha)$ in the oriented convention of [[def-oriented-integral]]; the improper values are additive under subdivision; and $D=x(b)-x(a)$ is nonzero future causal, with $D^0>0$ and $|D_{\mathrm{spatial}}|\le D^0$ in every inertial chart.

[F3] Chart metric and cone coordinates ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]): in the chart of an inertial frame (first basis vector future) a vector $v$ with coordinates $(v^0,v_s)$ is future timelike exactly when $v^0>|v_s|$, and $-\eta(v,v)=(v^0)^2-|v_s|^2$; $\eta$ is bilinear.

[L4] Norm inequalities ([[cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm]], [[thm-norm-inequality-for-the-vector-valued-integral]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]): the spatial Euclidean norm satisfies the triangle inequality, finite sums included; and for vector-valued functions on an interval, $\bigl\|\int_c^d f\bigr\|\le\int_c^d\|f\|$ whenever $f$ is Riemann integrable.

[L5] Monotonicity and positivity of the Riemann integral ([[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[thm-nonnegative-continuous-with-zero-integral-vanishes]], [[def-oriented-integral]]): if $g_1\le g_2$ pointwise on $[c,d]$ then $\int_c^d g_1\le\int_c^d g_2$; and if a nonnegative continuous real function on $[c,d]$ has positive value at some point, then its integral over $[c,d]$ is positive.

[L6] Order arithmetic of $\mathbb{R}$ ([[def-ordered-field]]): the order is transitive, and a finite sum of positive reals is positive.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Fix the inertial frame and write $y=\xi=x_A\circ x=(y^0,z)$ with $z=(y^1,y^2,y^3)$; the partition has $m\ge1$ pieces, and on each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the tangent $x'$ is future timelike, so by [F3] $y^0{}'(u)>|z'(u)|\ge0$ at every $u\in(s_{i-1},s_i)$. [given, F1, F3]

2.1 The hypotheses of [F2] are satisfied: $x$ is $C^1$ on the open pieces, the one-sided difference-quotient derivatives are finite, and the interior tangents are future timelike, hence in particular nonzero future causal; therefore clauses (a)-(d) of [F2] apply to each piece $(\alpha,\beta)=(s_{i-1},s_i)$. [step 1.1, F1, F2]

3.1 Per piece: the difference $g_i:=y^0{}'-|z'|$ is continuous and positive on $(\alpha,\beta)$ by step 1.1, so for any $\alpha<u<v<\beta$ its integral over $[u,v]$ is positive by [L5]; the improper integral $\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}g_i$ dominates that truncated integral, and the additive decomposition of [F2] gives $\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}g_i=\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}y^0{}'-\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}|z'|$, so $\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}|z'|<\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}y^0{}'=y^0(\beta)-y^0(\alpha)$ with the last equality from [F2]; in particular $y^0(\beta)-y^0(\alpha)>0$. [step 2.1, F2, L5]

3.2 Per piece the spatial increment satisfies $|z(\beta)-z(\alpha)|=\bigl\|\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}z'\bigr\|\le\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}|z'|$: for $\alpha<u<v<\beta$ the vector norm inequality of [L4] gives $\bigl\|\int_u^vz'\bigr\|\le\int_u^v|z'|$, and letting $u\downarrow\alpha$, $v\uparrow\beta$ with the endpoint-increment limits of [F2] and continuity of the norm yields the claim. [step 2.1, F2, L4]

4.1 Summing the finitely many pieces, with $\Delta_iz:=z(s_i)-z(s_{i-1})$: $|z(b)-z(a)|\le\sum_{i=1}^m|\Delta_iz|\le\sum_{i=1}^m\int_{(s_{i-1},s_i)}|z'|<\sum_{i=1}^m\int_{(s_{i-1},s_i)}y^0{}'=y^0(b)-y^0(a)$, where the first inequality is the finite triangle inequality [L4], the second is step 3.2, the strict inequality is step 3.1 together with positivity of the finite sum of the positive differences $\int_{(s_{i-1},s_i)}(y^0{}'-|z'|)$ [L6], and the final equality is additivity over the partition from [F2]; in particular $y^0(b)-y^0(a)>0$ and $|z(b)-z(a)|<y^0(b)-y^0(a)$. [step 3.2, F2, L4, L6]

5.1 Consequently, in this chart the displacement $d=q-p$ has coordinates $(y^0(b)-y^0(a),\,z(b)-z(a))$ with positive time component strictly dominating the spatial norm, so $d$ is future timelike by the coordinate criterion [F3]; since the inertial chart was arbitrary, the same conclusion holds in every inertial chart. Hence $p\ne q$ ($d\ne0$ because it is timelike), and by bilinearity [F3] one has $-\eta(d,d)=(y^0(b)-y^0(a))^2-|z(b)-z(a)|^2>0$, so $\sqrt{-\eta(d,d)}$ is a positive real number, and the time component of $d$ dominates in every inertial chart — the coordinate description of future timelikeness. [step 4.1, F3, L4]

6.1 The argument uses only the weak piecewise class on the compact interval $[a,b]$, truncated Riemann integrals and their one-sided limits, and the finite sum over the $m$ pieces: no completeness of $\mathbb{R}$ is invoked beyond what the cited integral suppliers use on compact intervals, no compactness assumption beyond the interval $[a,b]$ is made, and no choice principle is used. [step 5.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $c>0$ and let $x:[a,b]\to A$ be a future timelike worldline with $a<b$
([[def-interval]]) that is piecewise $C^1$ with partition
$a=s_0<s_1<\dots<s_m=b$ in the weak sense of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], with total proper time
$\Delta\tau(x)$ of [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]]. Put $p:=x(a)$, $q:=x(b)$
and $T:=\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}$, a positive real number
([[lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline]]). Then:

**(i) Endpoint bound.** $c\,\Delta\tau(x)\le T$.

**(ii) Equality case.** $c\,\Delta\tau(x)=T$ if and only if $x$ is a strictly
increasing reparametrization of the straight segment from $p$ to $q$: there is a
continuous strictly increasing surjection $\sigma:[a,b]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(a)=0$, $\sigma(b)=1$, $C^1$ on every open piece of a finite weak
piecewise partition of $[a,b]$, with $\sigma'(s)>0$ at every point of each open
piece and finite positive one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at both
endpoints of every piece, without any requirement that $\sigma'$ extend
continuously there, such that $x(s)=p+\sigma(s)(q-p)$ for every $s\in[a,b]$;
equivalently, every open-piece tangent $x'(s)$ is a positive multiple of
$q-p$.

**(iii) Strictness.** If the image of $x$ is not contained in the straight
segment $\{p+\lambda(q-p):0\le\lambda\le1\}$, then $c\,\Delta\tau(x)<T$. In
particular, if $x$ is piecewise inertial and its piece tangents $d_1,\dots,d_m$
are not all positive multiples of one another (equivalently, its image is not
contained in the straight segment), then the inequality is strict, while a
piecewise inertial itinerary whose piece tangents are all positive multiples of
one another has the straight segment as image and attains the bound.

**(iv) Straight worldlines attain the bound.** For the worldline
$x_s(s):=p+\frac{s-a}{b-a}(q-p)$ one has $c\,\Delta\tau(x_s)=T$; more generally
every worldline whose image is the straight segment and which is traversed in
the future direction attains the bound.

**(v) Scope.** The theorem concerns the affine Minkowski model with a fixed
positive constant $c$; it is a statement about the weak piecewise $C^1$ future
timelike class, including the ordinary Riemann special case (H); it does not
identify proper time with any clock reading, and it asserts nothing about
maximality of geodesics in curved spacetimes or in Lorentzian manifolds with
different global structure.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A real $c>0$; a weak piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline $x:[a,b]\to A$, $a<b$, with partition $a=s_0<\dots<s_m=b$; $p=x(a)$, $q=x(b)$, $d=q-p$, $T=\sqrt{-\eta(d,d)}$.

[F1] Endpoint displacement ([[lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline]]): $d=q-p$ is future timelike, so $T>0$, and in every inertial chart the time component of $d$ is positive and dominates the norm of its spatial part.

[F2] Rest frame of the displacement ([[lem-sr-rest-frame-of-a-future-timelike-displacement]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]): $n:=d/T$ is future unit timelike, for every event $o$ there is an inertial frame with first vector $n$, and for the chart $\xi$ of any such frame $\xi(o+\lambda d)=(\lambda T,0,0,0)$ for every real $\lambda$; in particular with $o:=p$ one has $\xi(p)=(0,0,0,0)$ and $\xi(q)=(T,0,0,0)$.

[F3] Weak piecewise structure and proper time ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability]], [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[def-oriented-integral]]): $x$ is $C^1$ on each open piece with future timelike interior tangent and has finite one-sided difference-quotient tangents; on a piece $(\alpha,\beta)$ with coordinate path $y=(y^0,z)$ one has $y^0{}'>|z'|\ge0$, the density $g=\sqrt{(y^0{}')^2-|z'|^2}=\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ has a finite positive improper integral $\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}g$ in the two-sided convention, the signed improper integral of $y^0{}'$ over the piece equals $y^0(\beta)-y^0(\alpha)$, improper values are additive under subdivision, and the finite piece sums are independent of the admissible partition; $\Delta\tau(x)=c^{-1}\sum_i\int_{(s_{i-1},s_i)}g$, the based proper-time function is strictly increasing, and under the corner hypothesis (H) the improper values coincide with the ordinary Riemann integrals, agreeing with [[def-sr-proper-time]] in the globally $C^1$ case.

[F4] Cone coordinates and metric ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]): in an inertial chart a vector with coordinates $(v^0,v_s)$ is future timelike exactly when $v^0>|v_s|$, and $-\eta(v,v)=(v^0)^2-|v_s|^2$; a constant-tangent worldline on $[a,b]$ with tangent the future timelike $w$ has total proper time $c^{-1}(b-a)\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$.

[L5] Square roots and monotonicity ([[thm-of-square-roots]], [[lem-of-square-monotone]]): every real $c\ge0$ has a unique $\sqrt c\ge0$ with $(\sqrt c)^2=c$; for $x,y\ge0$ one has $x\le y\iff x^2\le y^2$.

[L6] Monotonicity and positivity of the Riemann integral ([[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[thm-nonnegative-continuous-with-zero-integral-vanishes]]): $g_1\le g_2$ pointwise on $[u,v]$ implies $\int_u^vg_1\le\int_u^vg_2$, and a nonnegative continuous function on $[u,v]$ that is positive somewhere has positive integral.

[L7] Zero derivative gives a constant ([[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]]): a continuous real function on an order-convex interval whose derivative vanishes at every interior point is constant.

[L8] Order arithmetic ([[def-ordered-field]], [[def-interval]]): the order is transitive, a finite sum of nonnegative reals is nonnegative and vanishes only if every term vanishes, and a finite sum of positive reals is positive.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 By [F1] $d$ is future timelike and $T>0$; put $n:=d/T$ and fix, by [F2], the inertial frame with origin $p$ and first vector $n$, with chart $\xi$ and coordinate path $y=\xi\circ x=(y^0,z)$; then $\xi(p)=(0,0,0,0)$ and $\xi(q)=(T,0,0,0)$, so $y(a)=(0,0,0,0)$ and $y(b)=(T,0,0,0)$. [given, F1, F2, choose]

2.1 On every open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the tangent is future timelike, so [F3] and [F4] give $y^0{}'>|z'|\ge0$; the density is $g_i=\sqrt{(y^0{}')^2-|z'|^2}$ with finite positive improper integral, and setting $f_i:=g_i$ and $h_i:=y^0{}'-f_i$ one has $h_i\ge0$ and $f_i\le y^0{}'$ pointwise on the piece, because $0\le (y^0{}')^2-|z'|^2\le(y^0{}')^2$ and $f_i,y^0{}'\ge0$ with monotonicity of the square root [L5]. [step 1.1, F3, F4, L5]

3.1 Endpoint bound: $c\,\Delta\tau(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\int_{(s_{i-1},s_i)}f_i\le\sum_{i=1}^m\int_{(s_{i-1},s_i)}y^0{}'=y^0(b)-y^0(a)=T$, where the first equality is the definition of $\Delta\tau$ in [F3], the inequality is termwise monotonicity of the improper integrals from step 2.1 together with positivity of each term, the middle equality combines the endpoint increments of [F3] for $y^0{}'$ with additivity under the partition, and the last equality is $y^0(b)-y^0(a)=\xi^0(q)-\xi^0(p)=T$ from step 1.1; this is (i). [step 2.1, F3, L6]

4.1 Assume now $c\,\Delta\tau(x)=T$. Then by step 3.1 and additivity, $\sum_{i=1}^m\int_{(s_{i-1},s_i)}h_i=0$ with every term $\ge0$ by step 2.1, so by [L8] every term vanishes; since each $h_i$ is continuous and nonnegative on the open piece, $h_i\equiv0$ there: if $h_i(u_0)>0$ at some point, continuity gives $h_i\ge h_i(u_0)/2>0$ on a compact interval around $u_0$ inside the piece, whose ordinary integral is then positive by [L6], and the improper integral dominates it, a contradiction. [step 2.1, step 3.1, L6, L8]

5.1 Consequently $f_i^2=(y^0{}')^2$ on each piece, so $|z'|^2=(y^0{}')^2-f_i^2=0$ and hence $z'=0$ there; each coordinate of $z$ is continuous on the closed piece with vanishing derivative on its interior, so by [L7] each coordinate is constant on the closed piece, and since consecutive pieces share their corner values, $z\equiv z_0$ for a single $z_0\in\mathbb{R}^3$ on all of $[a,b]$. [step 4.1, F3, L7, algebra]

6.1 Hence for every $s\in[a,b]$ the coordinates of $x(s)$ are $(y^0(s),z_0)$; by linearity of $\xi^{-1}$ and step 1.1, $x(s)=p+\frac{y^0(s)}{T}\,d+w_0$ with $w_0$ the vector whose coordinates are $(0,z_0)$, and evaluating at $s=a$, where $x(a)=p$ and $y^0(a)=0$, gives $w_0=0$; thus $x(s)=p+\sigma(s)\,d$ for $\sigma(s):=\frac{y^0(s)}{T}$, and $\sigma$ is continuous with $\sigma(a)=0$ and $\sigma(b)=1$. [step 5.1, F2, algebra]

7.1 Properties of $\sigma$: it is $C^1$ on every open piece with $\sigma'=y^0{}'/T>0$ by step 2.1; its one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at the piece endpoints are the one-sided quotients of $y^0$ divided by $T$, hence finite and positive because the corresponding one-sided tangent of $x$ is future timelike, so its time component strictly dominates the spatial norm [F3, F4]; and it is strictly increasing: for $s<t$ in $[a,b]$ the restricted worldline $x|_{[s,t]}$ is again weak piecewise future timelike, and its proper time satisfies $\Delta\tau_{[s,t]}(x)=c^{-1}\sum\int_{(\text{induced pieces})}f$ with $f=y^0{}'$ on all open pieces by step 5.1, so by the endpoint increments and additivity of [F3] this equals $c^{-1}(y^0(t)-y^0(s))$, while the based proper-time function is strictly increasing by [F3]; hence $y^0(t)-y^0(s)>0$ and $\sigma(t)>\sigma(s)$. [step 6.1, F3, F4, algebra]

8.1 This proves the forward implication of (ii): the $\sigma$ of step 6.1 and step 7.1 is a continuous strictly increasing surjection $[a,b]\to[0,1]$ with $\sigma(a)=0$, $\sigma(b)=1$, $C^1$ on the open pieces of the partition of $x$, with $\sigma'>0$ there and finite positive one-sided quotient derivatives, and $x(s)=p+\sigma(s)d$. The tangent form of the statement is immediate in this direction, since $x'(s)=\sigma'(s)\,d$ with $\sigma'(s)>0$ at every differentiable point of every open piece. [step 6.1, step 7.1, algebra]

9.1 Conversely, suppose $x(s)=p+\sigma(s)(q-p)=p+\sigma(s)d$ for a $\sigma$ as in (ii) with respect to a finite weak piecewise partition of $[a,b]$; then on each open piece the tangent is $\sigma'(s)d$ with $\sigma'(s)>0$, so $x$ is again a weak piecewise future timelike worldline with that partition, its coordinate path in the chart of step 1.1 is $y^0=T\sigma$, $z=0$, and its density is $f=\sqrt{(y^0{}')^2}=y^0{}'=T\sigma'$; therefore $c\,\Delta\tau(x)=\sum\int f=\sum\int y^0{}'=y^0(b)-y^0(a)=T(\sigma(b)-\sigma(a))=T$, using for the middle equality the endpoint increments and additivity of [F3] applied to $x$ with that partition; this is the reverse implication of (ii), and the stated equivalence with 'every open-piece tangent is a positive multiple of $q-p$' holds because the representation gives such tangents, and conversely a weak piecewise worldline all of whose open-piece tangents are positive multiples of $d$ has each piece on an affine line in direction $d$ through its initial corner, so by the joining condition all pieces lie on the single line through $p$ in direction $d$, and the assignment $s\mapsto\sigma(s)$ by $x(s)=p+\sigma(s)d$ is a strictly increasing continuous piecewise $C^1$ reparametrization onto $[0,1]$. [step 8.1, F3, F4, algebra]

10.1 For (iii): by (ii), $c\,\Delta\tau(x)=T$ forces $x$ to be a reparametrization with $\sigma$ valued in $[0,1]$, so the image of $x$ is contained in $\{p+\lambda d:0\le\lambda\le1\}$; hence if the image is not contained in the straight segment the inequality is strict. If $x$ is piecewise inertial with constant piece tangents $d_1,\dots,d_m$, then: if all $d_i$ are positive multiples of one another, say $d_i=\alpha_i u$ with $u$ future timelike and $\alpha_i>0$, then all legs lie on the line through $p$ in direction $u$ and the parameter $\sigma$ defined by $x=p+\sigma d$ is continuous, piecewise affine and strictly increasing with image $[0,1]$, so the image is exactly the straight segment and the bound is attained by step 9.1; conversely, if the image is contained in the straight segment, each leg's tangent is parallel to $d$ and future timelike, hence a positive multiple of $d$ by [F4], so all $d_i$ are positive multiples of one another; this proves (iii). [step 9.1, F4, algebra]

10.2 For (iv): $x_s(s)=p+\frac{s-a}{b-a}d$ has constant tangent $\frac{1}{b-a}d$, a future timelike vector, so it is a weak piecewise (indeed $C^1$) future timelike worldline, and $\sigma(s)=\frac{s-a}{b-a}$ satisfies the conditions of (ii): it is continuous, strictly increasing, maps $[a,b]$ onto $[0,1]$, is $C^1$ with positive constant derivative, and $x_s=p+\sigma d$; by step 9.1, $c\,\Delta\tau(x_s)=T$. More generally, any weak piecewise future timelike worldline whose image is the straight segment from $p$ to $q$ and which is traversed in the future direction satisfies the representation of (ii) by the argument in step 9.1 and hence attains the bound. [step 9.1, F4, algebra]

[step 10.2, F3] ∎

## Statement

Adopt as physical assumptions the postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]],
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and
[[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]], and let $c$ and the SI
conventions be those of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let $p$
and $q$ be events with $q-p$ future timelike, put
$T:=\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}>0$, and let $x_s:[a,b]\to A$ be the straight
(inertial) future timelike worldline from $p$ to $q$,
$x_s(s):=p+\frac{s-a}{b-a}(q-p)$. Let $x:[a,b]\to A$ be a piecewise $C^1$
future timelike worldline from $p$ to $q$ in the weak sense of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], with total proper time
$\Delta\tau(x)$ defined by [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]]. Then, as
conditional statements about ideal clocks of the adopted model and not about any
actual apparatus:

**(i)** An ideal clock carried along $x_s$ from $p$ to $q$ reads between the
parameter values $a$ and $b$ the time $c^{-1}T$.

**(ii)** An ideal clock carried along $x$ from $p$ to $q$ reads $\Delta\tau(x)$,
and $\Delta\tau(x)\le c^{-1}T$, with equality if and only if $x$ is a strictly
increasing reparametrization of the straight segment from $p$ to $q$ in the
sense of [[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]] (ii).

**(iii)** If $x$ is piecewise inertial
([[def-sr-inertial-and-piecewise-inertial-worldline]]) and its image is not
contained in the straight segment from $p$ to $q$, then
$\Delta\tau(x)<c^{-1}T$ strictly; so among ideal clocks carried between the same
two events along future timelike piecewise $C^1$ histories of the weak class of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (including its ordinary Riemann
special case (H)) the straight inertial clock records the largest reading, and
every history whose image is not the straight segment records a strictly
smaller one.

**(iv)** The two numbers $\Delta\tau(x)$ and $c^{-1}T$ are determined by the
parametrized histories and the model's conversion constant alone: the integrand
$\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ of [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]] involves no chart, so
the comparison is a definite pair of clock readings attached to the same pair of
endpoint events and involves no simultaneity convention.

**Scope and qualification.** The statement inherits the idealizations of its
postulates (ideal pointlike clocks with no acceleration-dependent reading term,
prescribed histories, flat classical spacetime, the fixed conversion constant
$c$); it asserts no measurement outcome, contains no statistical inference, and
carries no claim that real clocks or the physical world are exactly described by
the model. The conclusion is conditional on the named postulates and does not
follow from the geometry alone.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] (A1), [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] (A2) and [[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] (A3); the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] with the fixed conversion constant $c>0$; events $p,q$ with $q-p$ future timelike, $T=\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}>0$; the straight worldline $x_s(s)=p+\frac{s-a}{b-a}(q-p)$ on $[a,b]$, $a<b$; and a weak piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline $x:[a,b]\to A$ from $p$ to $q$ with total proper time $\Delta\tau(x)$.

[A1] Inertial covariance ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]): the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space is the spacetime of the framework, and the model's equations are covariant under the affine maps whose linear part preserves $\eta$, has determinant $+1$ and maps $C^+$ onto $C^+$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[A2] Ideal clock reading rule ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] (i)): along a curve whose coordinate representation in an inertial chart is $C^1$ with everywhere future timelike derivative, an ideal clock reads between parameters $a<b$ the value $c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}\,\mathrm ds$, with no additional acceleration-dependent term.

[A3] Clock hypothesis for the general worldline class ([[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] (ii)): an ideal clock carried along a future timelike worldline of the model, including an accelerated one and a weak piecewise $C^1$ one with finitely many kinks, reads between two parameter values the proper-time difference $\Delta\tau$ of [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]] (for weak piecewise $C^1$ histories), with no term depending on acceleration, jerk or any higher derivative; the reading does not depend on an increasing regular change of parameter.

[L4] Endpoint bound and flat maximum ([[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]]): for the weak piecewise future timelike $x$ from $p$ to $q$, $c\Delta\tau(x)\le T$; equality holds exactly for the strictly increasing reparametrizations of the straight segment in the sense of that theorem's clause (ii); and if the image of $x$ is not contained in the straight segment, in particular if $x$ is piecewise inertial with piece tangents not all positive multiples of one another, then $c\Delta\tau(x)<T$, while a piecewise inertial itinerary whose tangents are all positive multiples of one another attains the bound.

[L5] Proper-time definition and chart independence ([[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]], [[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]): $\Delta\tau(x)=c^{-1}\sum_i\int_{(s_{i-1},s_i)}\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ is defined through the intrinsic integrand $\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$, is independent of the inertial chart and of the admissible partition, and for the straight worldline with constant tangent $d/(b-a)$ equals $c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(d,d)}$, the straight-segment value of [[def-sr-proper-time]].

[L6] Bilinearity and roots ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[thm-of-square-roots]]): $\eta$ is bilinear, so $-\eta(\lambda d,\lambda d)=\lambda^2(-\eta(d,d))$ for real $\lambda$, and $\sqrt{\lambda^2T^2}=\lambda T$ for every real $\lambda>0$; every nonnegative real has a unique nonnegative square root.

[L7] Piecewise inertial histories ([[def-sr-inertial-and-piecewise-inertial-worldline]]): a piecewise inertial worldline is a weak piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline with constant future timelike tangents on the open pieces.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The straight worldline $x_s$ has constant tangent $w:=\frac{1}{b-a}(q-p)$, which is future timelike because $q-p$ is future timelike and $\frac{1}{b-a}>0$; hence $x_s$ is a $C^1$ future timelike worldline from $p$ to $q$, and $x$ is a weak piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline from $p$ to $q$ by hypothesis, so both are histories of the class covered by the clock postulates [A2] and [A3]. [given, A1, A3, L5, L7]

2.1 By the reading rule [A2] applied to the $C^1$ history $x_s$, the ideal clock reads $c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x_s',x_s')}\,\mathrm ds=c^{-1}(b-a)\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$; by bilinearity [L6], $-\eta(w,w)=\frac{1}{(b-a)^2}(-\eta(q-p,q-p))=\frac{T^2}{(b-a)^2}$, so $\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}=\frac{T}{b-a}$ and the reading is $c^{-1}T$; this is (i). [step 1.1, A2, L6, algebra]

2.2 By the clock hypothesis [A3] for the weak piecewise class, the ideal clock carried along $x$ from $p$ to $q$ reads $\Delta\tau(x)$, which by [L5] equals the intrinsic proper-time value $c^{-1}\sum_i\int_{(s_{i-1},s_i)}\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$. [step 1.1, A3, L5]

3.1 Endpoint comparison: by [L4] the endpoint bound gives $c\,\Delta\tau(x)\le T$, equivalently $\Delta\tau(x)\le c^{-1}T$ because $c>0$; and equality holds if and only if $x$ is a strictly increasing reparametrization of the straight segment from $p$ to $q$ in the sense of [[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]] (ii); this proves (ii). [step 2.1, step 2.2, L4]

4.1 Strict case: if $x$ is piecewise inertial with piece tangents not all positive multiples of one another, then its image is not contained in the straight segment and [L4] gives $c\,\Delta\tau(x)<T$, that is $\Delta\tau(x)<c^{-1}T$. Since the straight clock reads $c^{-1}T$ by (i) and every weak piecewise history reads at most $c^{-1}T$ by (ii) with equality only for the straight-segment reparametrizations, the straight inertial clock records the largest reading among the histories of the class, and every history whose image is not the straight segment records strictly less — for a continuous history from $p$ to $q$ contained in the straight segment has the whole segment as image, so 'image not contained' and 'image not the straight segment' agree; this proves (iii). [step 3.1, L4, L7]

5.1 Chart independence: the proper-time integrand $\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ is formed from $\eta$ and the tangent alone, and [L5] records that $\Delta\tau(x)$ is independent of the inertial chart and of the partition; likewise $T=\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}$ is the interval of the intrinsic displacement, and the rest-frame computation of [L4] realizes it as the coordinate value in any inertial frame with first vector $(q-p)/T$, so both numbers are determined by the parametrized histories and the fixed constant $c$; since the two readings are attached to the same events $p$ and $q$, no simultaneity convention enters. This is (iv). [step 3.1, step 4.1, L5, L6]

6.1 Scope: the deduction used the adopted postulates [A1]-[A3] and the mathematical endpoint theorem [L4]; the conclusion is conditional on those idealizations (ideal clocks without an acceleration-dependent term, prescribed histories, flat spacetime, fixed $c$), asserts no measurement outcome and no statistical inference, and claims nothing about real clocks or about nature; no choice principle is used beyond the published suppliers. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 5.1, A1, A2, A3, L4, L5] ∎

conventions be those of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Fix an
inertial frame with chart $x$, a duration $T>0$ in seconds and a speed $v$ with
$0<|v|<c$; put $\gamma:=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. Define two histories (parameter
$t$ in seconds, with $x^0=ct$):

- **stay-at-home**: $x_{\mathrm{stay}}(t):=x^{-1}(ct,0,0,0)$ for
  $t\in[0,2T]$;
- **traveler**: $x_{\mathrm{travel}}(t):=x^{-1}(ct,vt,0,0)$ for $t\in[0,T]$ and
  $x_{\mathrm{travel}}(t):=x^{-1}(ct,v(2T-t),0,0)$ for $t\in[T,2T]$.

Then:

**(i)** $x_{\mathrm{stay}}$ is the inertial future timelike worldline from
$p:=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$ to $q:=x^{-1}(2cT,0,0,0)$, and $x_{\mathrm{travel}}$ is a
piecewise inertial future timelike worldline from $p$ to $q$ whose two pieces
have the constant tangents $(c,v,0,0)$ and $(c,-v,0,0)$, with the corner
$r:=x^{-1}(cT,vT,0,0)$; the image of $x_{\mathrm{travel}}$ contains the three
events $p,r,q$, which are not collinear in the affine model, so the image of
$x_{\mathrm{travel}}$ is not contained in the straight segment from $p$ to $q$.

**(ii)** Conditional on the postulates, an ideal clock carried from $p$ to $q$
along $x_{\mathrm{stay}}$ reads $2T$, while an ideal clock carried from $p$ to
$q$ along $x_{\mathrm{travel}}$ reads
$2T/\gamma=2T\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}$; hence at the reunion event $q$ the traveling
clock is behind the stay-at-home clock by
$2T(1-1/\gamma)=2T\bigl(1-\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}\bigr)>0$.

**(iii)** The conclusion is a comparison of two clock readings at the common
events $p$ and $q$; it does not depend on a simultaneity convention or on the
inertial frame used to describe the histories, because both readings are
proper-time integrals of the two histories.

**(iv)** Scope and idealization: the scenario is a conditional model statement;
the instantaneous turn at $r$ idealizes a turnaround of finite duration, the
clocks are ideal with no acceleration-dependent reading term, spacetime is flat,
and no gravitational, quantum, apparatus or statistical effect is modeled; no
measurement is reported. The conclusion is conditional on the adopted postulates
and does not assert that nature is exactly described by the model.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and [[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]]; the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] with fixed $c>0$; an inertial frame with chart $x$; a duration $T>0$ and a speed $v$ with $0<|v|<c$; $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; the two histories $x_{\mathrm{stay}}$ and $x_{\mathrm{travel}}$ of the statement, with $p=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$, $r=x^{-1}(cT,vT,0,0)$ and $q=x^{-1}(2cT,0,0,0)$.

[A1] Inertial covariance ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]): the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space is the spacetime of the framework, and the model's equations are covariant under the affine maps preserving $\eta$, orientation and the future cone.

[A2] Ideal-clock reading rule ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] (i)): along a $C^1$ history with everywhere future timelike derivative the ideal clock reads, between parameters $a<b$, the value $c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}\,\mathrm ds$, with no acceleration-dependent term.

[A3] Clock hypothesis for the piecewise class ([[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] (ii)): an ideal clock carried along a future timelike worldline of the model, including a weak piecewise $C^1$ one with finitely many kinks, reads the proper-time difference $\Delta\tau$ of [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]], with no term depending on acceleration, jerk or higher derivatives.

[L4] Inertial and piecewise inertial worldlines ([[def-sr-inertial-and-piecewise-inertial-worldline]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]): a curve with constant tangent $d$ along an interval is inertial when $d$ is future timelike; a two-piece curve with constant future timelike tangents $d_1,d_2$ joining at a corner is a piecewise inertial weak piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline; and in the chart a coordinate vector $(w^0,w_s)$ is future timelike exactly when $w^0>|w_s|$.

[L5] Proper times of straight and piecewise straight histories ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]): a straight history with constant tangent $w$ over a parameter interval of length $L$ has proper time $c^{-1}L\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$; a two-leg history has total proper time the sum of its leg values; and the values depend only on the intrinsic integrand $\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ and the parameter interval, not on the inertial chart.

[L6] Same-endpoint clock comparison ([[pthm-sr-same-endpoint-clock-comparison]]): for a weak piecewise future timelike history from $p$ to $q$ with $q-p$ future timelike, the clock reading along the straight history is $c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}$ and is the largest among the readings of the class, with strict inequality for every history whose image is not the straight segment; the conclusion is conditional on the same postulates.

[L7] Endpoint theorem ([[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]]): for the weak piecewise future timelike class, $c\,\Delta\tau\le\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}$ with the stated equality and strictness clauses.

[L8] Roots, monotonicity and order ([[thm-of-square-roots]], [[lem-of-square-monotone]], [[def-ordered-field]]): $a\ge0$ has a unique nonnegative square root; for $x,y\ge0$, $x<y\iff x^2<y^2$; and $0<|v|<c$ gives $0<v^2/c^2<1$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The stay-at-home history has parameter path $(ct,0,0,0)$, hence constant tangent $(c,0,0,0)$ with $c>0=|0|$, so it is future timelike and inertial, running from $p$ at $t=0$ to $q$ at $t=2T$. The traveler's first piece has parameter path $(ct,vt,0,0)$ on $[0,T]$, hence constant tangent $(c,v,0,0)$ with $c>|v|$, and its second piece has parameter path $(ct,v(2T-t),0,0)$ on $[T,2T]$, hence constant tangent $(c,-v,0,0)$ with $c>|-v|$; at $t=T$ both formulas give the point $(cT,vT,0,0)$, so the two pieces join at the corner $r$ and define a two-leg piecewise inertial future timelike worldline from $p=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$ at $t=0$ to $q=x^{-1}(2cT,0,0,0)$ at $t=2T$. [given, L4, algebra]

2.1 The three events $p,r,q$ have coordinate columns $(0,0,0,0)$, $(cT,vT,0,0)$, $(2cT,0,0,0)$; the affine line through $p$ and $q$ consists of the columns $\lambda(2cT,0,0,0)$ with second coordinate $0$, and $r$ has second coordinate $vT\ne0$ because $v\ne0$ and $T>0$, so $r$ is not on that line; as affine charts preserve collinearity, $p,r,q$ are not collinear, and since the image of $x_{\mathrm{travel}}$ contains them it is not contained in the straight segment from $p$ to $q$. [step 1.1, L4, algebra]

2.2 By the reading rule [A2] applied to the $C^1$ history $x_{\mathrm{stay}}$ between the parameter values $0$ and $2T$, the stay-at-home clock reads $c^{-1}\int_0^{2T}\sqrt{-\eta((c,0,0,0),(c,0,0,0))}\,\mathrm dt=c^{-1}\cdot2T\cdot c=2T$, in agreement with the straight-segment value of [L5]. [step 1.1, A2, L5, algebra]

2.3 By the clock hypothesis [A3] the traveler's clock reads $\Delta\tau(x_{\mathrm{travel}})$ of [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]]; the two legs have constant tangents $(c,v,0,0)$ and $(c,-v,0,0)$ with the same interval value $-c^2+v^2=-c^2(1-v^2/c^2)$, so by [L5] each leg contributes $c^{-1}T\sqrt{c^2-v^2}=T\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}=T/\gamma$ and the total reading is $2T/\gamma=2T\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}$. [step 1.1, A3, L5, L8, algebra]

3.1 Comparison: by [L8] $0<v^2/c^2<1$, so $0<1-v^2/c^2<1$ and $\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}<1$ by strict monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives, whence $2T/\gamma<2T$ and the traveler is behind by $2T(1-1/\gamma)=2T(1-\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2})>0$; this is the strict case of the clock-comparison theorem [L6], consistent with step 2.1, since the image of $x_{\mathrm{travel}}$ is not the straight segment. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, L6, L7, L8, algebra]

4.1 Both readings are proper-time integrals of the respective histories — the integrand $\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ is built from $\eta$ and the tangent alone, and [L5] records that the values do not depend on the inertial chart — and both are attached to the common events $p$ and $q$; no simultaneity convention or preferred inertial frame enters the comparison, which is (iii). [step 2.3, step 3.1, L5]

5.1 Scope: the instantaneous turn at $r$ idealizes a turnaround of finite duration, the clocks are ideal with no acceleration-dependent reading term, spacetime is flat and $c$ is fixed; the conclusion is a conditional statement about ideal clocks of the adopted model, asserts no measurement outcome and no statistical inference, and claims nothing about real clocks, gravity or quantum effects; no choice principle is used beyond the published suppliers. This is (iv). [step 3.1, step 4.1, A1, A2, A3, L4, L5, L6] ∎

## Scope caveats for the twin reunion

This remark delimits the interpretation of the proper-time comparison of the
twin reunion ([[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]]) in the adopted model, with the ideal clock assumptions of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and
[[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] and the SI conventions of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. It proves nothing new; it
records what the earlier items do and do not assert.

## Acceleration is not an additional aging term

In the model the reading of an ideal clock between two events of its history is
the proper-time integral of its worldline, by clause (i) of
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] for $C^1$ histories and by clause (ii) of
[[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] for the weak piecewise $C^1$
class ([[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]]); no term depending on the
four-acceleration ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]) or on any
higher derivative of the history appears, and the clock hypothesis is precisely
the exclusion of such terms. The corner of the piecewise inertial history is an
idealization: a physical turnaround occupies a finite parameter interval, the
worldline is then $C^1$ or smooth there, and its proper time is still the
integral. The endpoint bound and strictness clause of
[[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]] apply to every weak
piecewise history, so the comparison with the stay-at-home clock survives the
smoothing of the corner, and the strict inequality remains because a smoothed
itinerary still does not have the image of the straight segment.

## The comparison is not symmetric in the model

One history of the reunion is the straight segment from $p$ to $q$; the other
contains the corner event $r$ of [[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]], and
the three events $p,r,q$ are not collinear: in the chart of that item their
coordinate columns are $(0,0,0,0)$, $(cT,vT,0,0)$ and $(2cT,0,0,0)$ with
$vT\ne0$. Every change of inertial chart is an affine bijection
([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]) and maps collinear
triples to collinear triples, so no change of inertial frame maps the image of
the stay-at-home history onto the image of the traveler's history, nor fixes both
endpoints and exchanges the two histories. The two twins are therefore not
related by an inertial change of description, and the difference of readings is
a model consequence of the different histories, not a consequence of who is
'really moving': the symmetric time-dilation relation of
[[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]] (i) concerns the two frames,
while the reunion comparison concerns the two clock readings at the single
common event $q$.

## Synchronization bookkeeping at the turn

In each momentary inertial rest frame of the traveler the stay-at-home clock runs
slow by the factor $1/\gamma$, and the traveler may legitimately apply the
time-dilation relation between events that are simultaneous in that momentary
frame ([[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]] (i),
[[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]]). But the two legs use different
inertial frames. With $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and the turn event $r$ of
[[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]], the outbound rest frame's chart
$x'$ satisfies $x'^0=\gamma\bigl(x^0-\frac vc x^1\bigr)$, so its slice through
$r$ has $x'^0=\gamma cT(1-v^2/c^2)=cT/\gamma$ and meets the stay-at-home
worldline $x^1=0$ at $x^0=\frac{1}{\gamma}\cdot\frac{cT}{\gamma}=cT(1-v^2/c^2)$,
that is at coordinate time $t=T(1-v^2/c^2)=T/\gamma^2$; the inbound rest frame's
chart $x''$ satisfies $x''^0=\gamma\bigl(x^0+\frac vc x^1\bigr)$, and its slice
through $r$ meets the same worldline at $x^0=cT(1+v^2/c^2)$, that is at
coordinate time $t=T(1+v^2/c^2)$. The two slices differ by
$2Tv^2/c^2$ in coordinate time, and the identity
$$2T=\frac{T}{\gamma^2}+\frac{2Tv^2}{c^2}+\frac{T}{\gamma^2},$$
which only uses $1/\gamma^2=1-v^2/c^2$, inserts this gap into the traveler's two
leg-by-leg accounts and reproduces the stay-at-home reading $2T$ at the reunion,
in agreement with the conditional comparison result
[[pthm-sr-same-endpoint-clock-comparison]]. The naive reciprocity statement
'each twin judges the other's clock to run slow' therefore compares different
pairs of events for the two travelers — events simultaneous in different
momentary frames — and does not apply to the reunion comparison, which concerns
the two clock readings at the single common event $q$.

## Empirical qualification

Everything above is a conditional statement about ideal clocks in the adopted
model: the clocks are ideal with no acceleration-dependent reading term, the
histories are prescribed, spacetime is flat and $c$ is fixed
([[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]],
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]). No measurement, apparatus, calibration,
sampling or uncertainty model is involved, and no claim is made about real
clocks or about nature; real clock comparisons would additionally require
apparatus and uncertainty analysis and are outside this remark.

## Example

Worked computation in the chart $x$ of an inertial frame with
$\eta_0=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; the vectors below are coordinate columns
in the frame's basis.

**(a)** For $v:=(5,3,0,0)$ and $w:=(5,-3,0,0)$ one has
$\eta(v,v)=\eta(w,w)=-25+9=-16$, so the timelike lengths are
$\sqrt{16}=4$ each, and $\eta(v,w)=-25-9=-34$, so $-\eta(v,w)=34\ge4\cdot4=16$;
the inequality is strict because $v$ and $w$ are not positive proportional.

**(b)** For $w':=2v=(10,6,0,0)$ one has $\eta(w',w')=-64$ and
$\sqrt{-\eta(w',w')}=8$, while $\eta(v,w')=-50+18=-32$, so
$-\eta(v,w')=32=4\cdot8$: this is the equality case of the reversed
Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, attained by the positive proportional pair
$(v,2v)$.

**(c)** Reverse triangle: $v+w=(10,0,0,0)$ has
$-\eta(v+w,v+w)=100$, so its root is $10\ge4+4=8$, again strict because $v$ and
$w$ are not positive proportional. For $u:=(5,0,0,0)$, of timelike length $5$,
one has $-\eta(v,u)=25\ge4\cdot5=20$ and $v+u=(10,3,0,0)$ with
$\sqrt{-\eta(v+u,v+u)}=\sqrt{100-9}=\sqrt{91}\ge4+5=9$, since $91>81$.

**(d)** Each of $v$, $w$, $w'$ and $u$ is future timelike ($5>3$, $5>3$,
$10>6$ and $5>0$ in the first coordinate against the spatial norm), so all
inequalities above are instances of the future timelike hypotheses of
[[lem-sr-reverse-cauchy-schwarz-for-future-timelike-vectors]] and
[[cor-sr-reverse-triangle-and-future-cone-convexity]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An inertial frame with chart $x$ and $\eta_0=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and the coordinate vectors $v=(5,3,0,0)$, $w=(5,-3,0,0)$, $w'=(10,6,0,0)$, $u=(5,0,0,0)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L1] Pairing in the frame: $\eta(r,r')=-r^0r'^0+r^1r'^1+r^2r'^2+r^3r'^3$ for coordinate vectors $r,r'$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

[L2] Causal classification and cone coordinates: $r$ is timelike when $\eta(r,r)<0$, and in a frame with future first vector $r$ is future timelike exactly when $r^0>|r_s|$ with $|r_s|=\sqrt{(r^1)^2+(r^2)^2+(r^3)^2}$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

[L3] Reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality: for future timelike $r,s$ with $a=\sqrt{-\eta(r,r)}$, $b=\sqrt{-\eta(s,s)}$ one has $-\eta(r,s)\ge ab$, with equality exactly when $r$ and $s$ are positive proportional ([[lem-sr-reverse-cauchy-schwarz-for-future-timelike-vectors]]).

[L4] Reversed triangle inequality: for future timelike $r,s$ one has $r+s$ future timelike and $\sqrt{-\eta(r+s,r+s)}\ge\sqrt{-\eta(r,r)}+\sqrt{-\eta(s,s)}$, with equality exactly when $r$ and $s$ are positive proportional ([[cor-sr-reverse-triangle-and-future-cone-convexity]]).

[L5] Square roots and monotonicity: every real $c\ge0$ has a unique $\sqrt c\ge0$ with $(\sqrt c)^2=c$, so in particular $\sqrt{16}=4$; for $x,y\ge0$ one has $x<y\iff x^2<y^2$ ([[thm-of-square-roots]], [[lem-of-square-monotone]]).

[L6] Elementary order arithmetic in $\mathbb{R}$: the order is trichotomous and transitive ([[def-ordered-field]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Evaluating the diagonal form [L1] on the given coordinate vectors gives $\eta(v,v)=-25+9=-16$, $\eta(w,w)=-25+9=-16$, $\eta(w',w')=-100+36=-64$, $\eta(u,u)=-25$, $\eta(v,w)=-25-9=-34$, $\eta(v,w')=-50+18=-32$, $\eta(v,u)=-25$, $\eta(v+w,v+w)=\eta((10,0,0,0),(10,0,0,0))=-100$ and $\eta(v+u,v+u)=-100+9=-91$. [given, L1, algebra]

2.1 By [L2] each of the four vectors is future timelike: $v^0=5>3=|v_s|$, $w^0=5>3=|w_s|$, $(w')^0=10>6=|(w')_s|$ and $u^0=5>0=|u_s|$; this is (d). [step 1.1, L2, algebra]

## Example

Worked computation in the inertial chart $x$ with metric
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Let $T>0$, let $v$ with $0<|v|<c$ and put
$\gamma:=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; let $p:=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$,
$r:=x^{-1}(cT,vT,0,0)$ and $q:=x^{-1}(2cT,0,0,0)$, the parameter in each
coordinate being the laboratory time $t$ in seconds, so that the coordinate
columns displayed are those of the events in the chart with $x^0=ct$.

**(a)** The straight worldline from $p$ to $q$ has displacement
$d:=(2cT,0,0,0)$, with $-\eta(d,d)=4c^2T^2$ and elapsed proper time
$c^{-1}2cT=2T$.

**(b)** The two-leg itinerary $p\to r\to q$, with the parameter on each leg in
$[0,T]$, has first-leg displacement $(cT,vT,0,0)$ with
$-\eta=c^2T^2(1-v^2/c^2)$, hence proper time
$c^{-1}cT\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}=T/\gamma$, and second-leg displacement
$(cT,-vT,0,0)$ with the same value; its two-leg total proper time is
$2T/\gamma$.

**(c)** Comparison: $2T/\gamma<2T$ for every $v$ with $0<|v|<c$, in agreement
with the endpoint bound and with its strictness clause, since the image of the
two-leg itinerary contains the event $r$, which is not on the straight segment
from $p$ to $q$. Numerical specialization $v=3c/5$ (so $\gamma=5/4$): the
readings are $8T/5$ and $2T$, with difference $2T/5$.

**(d)** Equality without affine parametrization: on $[0,1]$ let
$\mu(s):=(s^2+s)/2$, a strictly increasing $C^1$ surjection of $[0,1]$ onto
itself with $\mu'(s)=s+1/2>0$; the worldline
$y(s):=x^{-1}(2cT\mu(s),0,0,0)$ has the straight segment $pq$ as image and
elapsed proper time $c^{-1}\int_0^1 2cT\mu'(s)\,\mathrm ds=2T$: equality in the
endpoint bound does not require the affine parametrization, only a
future-directed strictly increasing one.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An inertial frame with chart $x$ and $\eta_0=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; a duration $T>0$ in seconds and a speed $v$ with $0<|v|<c$; $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; the events $p=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$, $r=x^{-1}(cT,vT,0,0)$, $q=x^{-1}(2cT,0,0,0)$; the two-leg coordinate itinerary $p\to r\to q$ and the reparametrized straight worldline $y(s)=x^{-1}(2cT\mu(s),0,0,0)$ with $\mu(s)=(s^2+s)/2$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).
