## Statement

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, and let
$\mathcal D=(p;(P_1,\dots,P_N);(P'_1,\dots,P'_K))$ be a mass-specified
conserving collision datum of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]],
causal and on-shell, all of whose legs are nonzero; write
$Q:=Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$ for the common side total.

**(a)** If $Q$ is future timelike with invariant mass $M$, then $M$ is the
common invariant mass of both sides, $Q$ has the center-of-momentum frame of
[[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]] with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$, and in that frame

$$Mc^2=\sum_{\text{legs of a side}}E_{e_0}(\text{leg})\qquad\text{for each side};$$

each massive leg $\ell=mU$ has $E_{e_0}(\ell)=mc^2\gamma_\ell\ge mc^2$ with
$\gamma_\ell:=-\eta(U/c,e_0)$ and equality if and only if $U=ce_0$, and each
null leg has $E_{e_0}>0$. Hence for each side
$S\in\{\mathrm{in},\mathrm{out}\}$,

$$M\ \ge\ \sum_{\text{massive legs }\ell\in S}m_\ell,$$

with equality if and only if $S$ is massive-only and every massive leg of $S$
has four-velocity $ce_0$ (all massive particles of that side at rest in the
center-of-momentum frame).

**(b)** If $Q$ is future null, then every leg is null, all legs are mutually
parallel in one future null direction, $M=0$ by the convention of
[[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]\,(b), and no
center-of-momentum frame exists.

**(c)** Suppose the incoming side is two-leg, $P_i=m_iU_i$ with $m_i>0$, and
put $n_2:=U_2/c$ (the future unit observer comoving with the second leg),
$\gamma:=-\eta(U_1/c,n_2)\ge1$ and $E:=E_{n_2}(P_1)=m_1c^2\gamma$. Then

$$M^2=m_1^2+m_2^2+\frac{2m_2E}{c^2}.$$

Consequently, if the outgoing side is mass-specified with massive masses
$\mu_1,\dots,\mu_L$, $L\ge1$ (it may also contain null legs), the datum can
conserve only if

$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{l=1}^L\mu_l\Bigr)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\Bigr],\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T:=E-m_1c^2\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{l=1}^L\mu_l\Bigr)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2\Bigr].$$

**(d)** If $P_1,P_2$ are future null and there is an inertial frame with
$P_i=(E_i/c)(e_0+s_i)$, $E_i>0$, $s_1,s_2$ unit spatial vectors with
$s_2=-s_1$, then $Q$ is future timelike and $M=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c^2$. More
generally, with $s_1,s_2$ unit spatial vectors in that frame and
$\sigma:=s_1\cdot s_2\in[-1,1]$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]]), if
$\theta\in[0,\pi]$ is their Euclidean angle, so that $\cos\theta=\sigma$, then
$Q$ is future timelike for $\theta\ne0$ with

$$M=\frac{\sqrt{2E_1E_2(1-\cos\theta)}}{c^2},$$

while for $\theta=0$ the total $Q$ is future null, $M=0$ and no
center-of-momentum frame exists. In particular, a conserving on-shell
collision datum whose incoming side is a single null leg and whose outgoing
side contains at least one massive leg does not exist.

**(e)** All clauses are conditional implications from the hypotheses of a
conserving, causal, on-shell datum. They assert no interaction, no existence
of a conservation process for prescribed legs, no cross section, amplitude or
probability, and no empirical fact.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the affine Minkowski model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; $c>0$; a
mass-specified conserving causal on-shell collision datum with nonzero legs;
the additional hypotheses of clauses (a)–(d) as stated.

[F1] ([[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]], Definition): a datum
conserves when $Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$; a mass-specified datum is
on-shell, with recorded mass $m>0$ on each massive leg and $0$ on each null
leg; a causal datum has every leg in $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$; a massive leg
$P=mU$ has $U$ future timelike with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and recorded mass
$m=m(P)=\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$; one compares the sides only through their
totals.

[F2] ([[lem-sr-finite-future-causal-sums]], Statement): if $P_1,\dots,P_N$,
$N\ge1$, are nonzero future causal vectors then $\sum_iP_i$ is nonzero future
causal, and future timelike if some $P_i$ is future timelike; for
$v,w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ one has $-\eta(v,w)\ge0$, with equality if and only
if $v=0$, or $w=0$, or both are nonzero future null with $w=\lambda v$,
$\lambda>0$; and $E_n$ and $q_n$ are additive over finite sums of elements of
$\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$, with $E_n(\sum_iP_i)>0$ when the $P_i$ are nonzero future
causal.

[F3] ([[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]], Statement): for future timelike $Q$
with invariant mass $M$, an inertial frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ exists and in it
$q_{e_0}(Q)=0$, $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$; conversely $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ forces
$e_0=Q/(Mc)$; and a nonzero future null vector has no center-of-momentum
frame.

[F4] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement): for
$P=mU$ with $m>0$, $U$ future timelike with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and $n$ future
unit, one has $\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$, $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$ and
$T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)\ge0$, with $\gamma=1$ if and only if $U=cn$; and for
nonzero future null $P$, $E_n(P)=c|q_n(P)|>0$.

[F5] ([[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]], Definition): the
invariant mass of a future timelike total $Q$ is
$M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$; if the total is future null then $M=0$ by
convention; the side totals are the finite sums of the legs.

[F6] ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], Definition):
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$ and $q_n(P)=h(P)$ for $P\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$.

[F7] ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], Definition): $\eta$ is symmetric and
bilinear, so $\eta(\sum_iP_i,\sum_jP_j)=\sum_{i,j}\eta(P_i,P_j)$ for finite
families.

[F8] ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] and
[[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]): in an inertial
frame, $S=\mathrm{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)=e_0^\perp$ with positive definite
restriction $\delta$, a unit spatial vector is $s\in S$ with $\delta(s,s)=1$,
and $\delta(s_1,s_2)=s_1\cdot s_2$; a vector with components
$(v^0,v_s)$ satisfies $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+|v_s|^2$.

[F9] ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]], Statement): for real $a_i,b_i$,
$|\sum_{i=1}^3a_ib_i|\le(\sum_i a_i^2)^{1/2}(\sum_i b_i^2)^{1/2}$; hence
$|s_1\cdot s_2|\le1$ for unit spatial vectors.

[F10] ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]): a nonzero vector has exactly
one causal character; it is timelike when $\eta(v,v)<0$, null when
$\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\ne0$, and future null when moreover $v\in
\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$; the closed cones meet only at $0$.

[F11] ([[def-rational-power]] and [[lem-rational-power-laws]]): for $a\ge0$
the number $\sqrt a$ is the unique nonnegative square root of $a$, and for
$a,b\ge0$ one has $\sqrt{ab}=\sqrt a\sqrt b$; in particular
$\sqrt{4E_1E_2}=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}$ for $E_1,E_2>0$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** read both sides as the same future causal total, use the
center-of-momentum frame where the total is timelike, and compute the
pairwise Lorentz products for the two-leg and null-leg clauses.

1.1 The datum conserves, so $Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}=Q$ by [F1], and every side is a finite nonempty list of nonzero future causal vectors; hence by [F2] $Q$ is nonzero future causal, $E_n$ and $q_n$ are additive over each side, and if some leg of a side is future timelike then that side's total $Q$ is future timelike. [F1, F2]

1.2 Assume $Q$ future timelike with invariant mass $M$; by [F3] the frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ exists and satisfies $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ and $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$; by [F4], a massive leg $\ell=mU$ has $E_{e_0}(\ell)=mc^2\gamma_\ell$ with $\gamma_\ell=-\eta(U/c,e_0)\ge1$ and $\gamma_\ell=1$ if and only if $U=ce_0$, and a null leg satisfies $E_{e_0}(\ell)=c|q_{e_0}(\ell)|>0$. [F3, F4, F6]

1.3 For $v,w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$: by [F2] $-\eta(v,w)\ge0$, with equality exactly in the three listed cases; consequently, if $Q=\sum_iP_i$ with all $P_i$ nonzero future causal, [F7] gives $-\eta(Q,Q)=\sum_{i,j}-\eta(P_i,P_j)$, a sum of nonnegative terms each of which vanishes only when the corresponding pair is zero or parallel future null. [F2, F7]

1.4 For the two-leg incoming side of (c), $P_i=m_iU_i$ and $n_2=U_2/c$ is future unit; by [F7] and $\eta(U_i,U_i)=-c^2$ one has $\eta(P_1,P_1)=-m_1^2c^2$, $\eta(P_2,P_2)=-m_2^2c^2$, and $\eta(P_1,P_2)=m_2c\,\eta(P_1,n_2)=-m_2E$ because $E=E_{n_2}(P_1)=-c\,\eta(P_1,n_2)$ by [F6]; hence $-\eta(Q,Q)=m_1^2c^2+m_2^2c^2+2m_2E$. [F1, F6, F7]

1.5 For the null pair of (d), in the displayed inertial frame the vectors $P_i=(E_i/c)(e_0+s_i)$ satisfy $\eta(P_i,P_i)=(E_i/c)^2(-1+\delta(s_i,s_i))=0$ and are nonzero future null (their components in the frame are $(E_i/c)(1,s_i)$ with $|s_i|=1$); by [F7] and [F8], $\eta(P_1,P_2)=(E_1E_2/c^2)(-1+\sigma)$ with $\sigma=s_1\cdot s_2=\delta(s_1,s_2)\in[-1,1]$ by [F9], so $-\eta(Q,Q)=2E_1E_2(1-\sigma)/c^2$. [F7, F8, F9, F10]

2.1 Under the hypothesis of (a), additivity of $E_{e_0}$ over each side [step 1.1] and $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$ [step 1.2] give $Mc^2=\sum_{\text{legs of a side}}E_{e_0}(\text{leg})$ for each of the two sides, since both sides have total $Q$; and $M=M(Q)$ is the invariant mass of the common total, hence the common invariant mass of both sides. [F3, F5, step 1.1, step 1.2]

2.2 Under the hypothesis of (b), $Q$ is future null and nonzero: every leg is null, because if some leg were future timelike then $Q$ would be future timelike by [step 1.1] and a nonzero vector has exactly one causal character by [F10]. Pairwise, [step 1.3] applied to the incoming list, whose total is $Q$, gives $0=-\eta(Q,Q)=\sum_{i,j}-\eta(P_i,P_j)$ over the incoming legs as a sum of nonnegative terms, so each term vanishes and for $i\ne j$ the nonzero future null legs $P_i,P_j$ are parallel with $P_j=\lambda P_i$, $\lambda>0$; fixing the first incoming leg makes every incoming leg a positive multiple of it, and the same argument applied to the outgoing list makes every outgoing leg a positive multiple of the first outgoing leg $P'_1$. Since $Q=\lambda P_1$ and $Q=\lambda'P'_1$ with $\lambda,\lambda'>0$, the two directions coincide and all legs lie in one future null direction. Then $M=0$ by the convention of [F5], and no center-of-momentum frame exists by [F3] applied to the nonzero future null total. [F3, F5, F10, step 1.1, step 1.3]

2.3 Under the hypothesis of (c), $M$ is defined: $-\eta(Q,Q)=m_1^2c^2+m_2^2c^2+2m_2E>0$ by [step 1.4] because $m_1,m_2,c>0$ and $E=m_1c^2\gamma\ge m_1c^2>0$ by [F4], so $Q$ is future timelike; hence [F5] and [step 1.4] give $M^2=-\eta(Q,Q)/c^2=m_1^2+m_2^2+2m_2E/c^2$. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 1.4]

2.4 Under the hypothesis of (d), if $\sigma<1$ then $-\eta(Q,Q)=2E_1E_2(1-\sigma)/c^2>0$ by [step 1.5], while $Q=P_1+P_2$ is nonzero future causal by [F2], so $Q$ is future timelike and [F5] gives $M^2=-\eta(Q,Q)/c^2=2E_1E_2(1-\sigma)/c^4$, hence $M=\sqrt{2E_1E_2(1-\sigma)}/c^2$ by [F11] with $\sigma=\cos\theta$; for the antiparallel case $s_2=-s_1$ one has $\theta=\pi$ and $\cos\theta=-1$, giving $M=\sqrt{4E_1E_2}/c^2=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c^2$ by [F11]. [F2, F5, F11, step 1.5]

2.5 Under the hypothesis of (d) with $\sigma=1$, i.e. $\theta=0$: by [step 1.5] $\eta(Q,Q)=0$, and $Q=P_1+P_2$ is nonzero future causal by [step 1.1], hence future null by [F10]; therefore $M=0$ by [F5], and no center-of-momentum frame exists by [F3]. [F3, F5, F10, step 1.1, step 1.5]

2.6 A conserving on-shell datum with a single null incoming leg and an outgoing side containing a massive leg does not exist: its incoming total $Q$ would be that single future null leg, while its outgoing side would contain a future timelike leg, so $Q_{\mathrm{out}}=Q$ would be future timelike by [step 1.1]; a vector cannot be both future null and future timelike by [F10], and conservation would force the two totals to be equal. [F10, step 1.1]

3.1 Under the hypothesis of (a), split each side into its massive and null legs: by [step 1.2] each massive leg contributes $m_\ell c^2\gamma_\ell\ge m_\ell c^2$ with $\gamma_\ell=1$ exactly when $U_\ell=ce_0$, and each null leg contributes $E_{e_0}>0$; substituting into [step 2.1] gives $M=\sum_{\text{massive}}m_\ell+\sum_{\text{massive}}m_\ell(\gamma_\ell-1)+\sum_{\text{null}}E_{e_0}/c^2\ \ge\ \sum_{\text{massive}}m_\ell$, with equality if and only if no null leg occurs and every massive leg has $\gamma_\ell=1$, that is $U_\ell=ce_0$. [step 1.2, step 2.1]

4.1 Under the hypothesis of (c), if the datum conserves and the outgoing side is mass-specified with massive masses $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_L$ and possibly null legs, then [step 3.1] applied to that side gives $M\ge\sum_l\mu_l$; combining with [step 2.2], $\bigl(\sum_l\mu_l\bigr)^2\le M^2=m_1^2+m_2^2+2m_2E/c^2$, so $E\ge\frac{c^2}{2m_2}\bigl[(\sum_l\mu_l)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\bigr]$ by rearrangement; subtracting $m_1c^2$ from both sides and expanding $(\sum_l\mu_l)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2=(\sum_l\mu_l)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2-2m_1m_2$ gives the equivalent bound on $T=E-m_1c^2$. [step 2.2, step 3.1]

5.1 Clause (a) is [step 2.1] with [step 3.1], clause (b) is [step 2.2], clause (c) is [step 2.3] with [step 4.1], and clause (d) is [step 2.4], [step 2.5] and [step 2.6]; clause (e) records the conditional scope of these implications and asserts nothing further. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 2.4, step 2.5, step 2.6, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Postulate

Adopt as physical assumptions of the relativistic particle model, on top of the
flat spacetime model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and the SI unit
conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], together with
the framework's idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks and ideal light
signals:

**(i) Mass and momentum.** Every massive classical particle of the model
carries a positive constant invariant mass parameter $m>0$ and has
four-momentum $P=mU$, where $U$ is the four-velocity of its future timelike
worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]],
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]); $P$ is a vector of $V$
whose SI unit is kilogram metre per second. The formula is adopted only for
$m>0$; the case $m=0$ is not defined by it and is the separate premise
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. In particular $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$
is a consequence of the four-velocity normalisation, not a separate
assumption.

**(ii) Observer measurement identification.** Relative to a future unit
observer $n$, the model identifies the measured energy of the particle with
$E_n(P)$, its measured spatial momentum with $q_n(P)$, its kinetic energy with
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and its rest energy with $mc^2$, where $E_n,q_n,T_n$ are
the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; the
units are the joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. This clause is a formulation
convention identifying mathematical quantities with the quantities the model
calls measured; it is not a measurement report and no experiment is claimed.

**(iii) Isolated collision balance.** In an isolated collision of particles at
an event — the interaction being confined to that event, with no external
agent acting — the sum of the incoming four-momenta equals the sum of the
outgoing four-momenta, in the sense of the collision data of
[[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]: the model adopts
$Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$ for such an isolated datum. No particular
collision is asserted to occur, and no mechanism, probability, cross section
or amplitude is supplied by this clause.

**(iv) Equation of motion for a stipulated force.** Whenever an interaction is
described by a stipulated force law $F$, that is a map assigning to an event
and a future timelike four-velocity a vector of $V$ on a stated domain, the
model's particle equation is $m\,dU/d\tau=F(x,U)$ along the worldline, with
$dU/d\tau$ the proper-time derivative of
[[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]], so that the stipulated $F$
is the four-force of the motion. A particular force law, and the existence,
uniqueness and domain of solutions of the resulting equation, are not adopted
here and belong to a separate model.

Empirical support for these assumptions is a nonlogical relation of the
framework, not a proof; the idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks,
ideal light signals and flat spacetime are inherited and travel to every
consumer of this premise.

## Postulate

Adopt as a separate model premise for ideal massless particles, independent of
[[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] whose formula $P=mU$ uses $m>0$ and does
not define a massless case:

**(i) The object.** An ideal massless particle of the model is described by a
nonzero future null vector $P\in V$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]) whose SI unit is kilogram
metre per second ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]). Such a $P$
is not of the form $mU$ for any $m>0$ and any future timelike $U$ with
$\eta(U,U)=-c^2$: a positive multiple of a timelike vector is timelike, and
the zero vector is neither timelike, null nor spacelike, so the massive
formula $P=mU$ of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] degenerates
to $0$ at $m=0$ and does not describe a nonzero null momentum. The particle
therefore has no four-velocity, no proper-time parametrisation and no rest
frame. Its scale is fixed by a measured energy in an observer's frame.

**(ii) Observer identification.** Relative to a future unit observer $n$, the
model identifies the measured energy and spatial momentum of the particle with
the quantities $E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$ and $q_n(P)=h(P)$ of
[[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]. Necessarily
$E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$, by
[[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(i), and no rest mass, rest
energy or kinetic energy is assigned to the particle — the definition of
$T_n$ requires a rest-mass parameter $m$ and no such parameter is introduced
here. This clause is a formulation convention identifying mathematical
quantities with the quantities the model calls measured; it is not a
measurement report and no experiment is claimed.

**(iii) No identification with light or quantum objects.** The ideal massless
particle is not identified here with light, with a classical wave or with any
quantum object: no frequency, wavelength, quantisation, polarisation or
Planck constant enters this premise, and the identification of light with
massless particles requires the wave model and its own postulates on a
separate page.

**(iv) No process.** This premise asserts no interaction of massless
particles and no decay or production process; such processes require a
stipulated dynamics. Empirical support for the assumption is a nonlogical
relation of the framework, not a proof, and the idealisations inherited from
the flat spacetime model and the ideal-point description travel to every
consumer of this premise.

## Statement

Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] and
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. Then the following conditional
physical claims hold in the flat classical model, with the units of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]].

**(a) Massive particle.** Let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$,
four-momentum $P=mU$ and a future unit observer $n$. Its measured energy
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$, spatial momentum $q_n(P)=h(P)$ and kinetic energy
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ satisfy $E_n(P)>0$, $T_n(P)\ge0$ and the mass-shell
identity $E_n(P)^2=m^2c^4+c^2|q_n(P)|^2$; $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if the
particle is at rest in the observer's frame ($U=cn$). In an inertial frame
whose stationary observer is $n=e_0$, the components are $P=(E/c,\mathbf p)$
with $E=E_{e_0}(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $\mathbf p=q_{e_0}(P)=m\gamma_w\mathbf w$
for the coordinate velocity $\mathbf w$, and under a passive boost the
components transform as the components of the vector $P$; the combination
$E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m^2c^4$ is frame-independent.

**(b) Four-force.** Along a $C^2$ worldline with four-acceleration $A$, the
four-force $F=\dot P$ satisfies $\eta(P,F)=0$ and $F=mA$; in an inertial frame
$F=\gamma\,(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\ \mathbf f)$ and
$dE/dt=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$, where $\mathbf f=d\mathbf p/dt$ is the
coordinate three-force. The constancy of $m$ is used; if instead $m$ is a
$C^1$ variable mass parameter, then $\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,dm/d\tau$, and the
constant-mass identities are not transferred to variable-mass systems.

**(c) System mass.** For a finite nonempty system of particles all of whose
four-momenta are nonzero future causal and whose total four-momentum $Q$ is
future timelike, the invariant mass $M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$ satisfies: in the
center-of-momentum frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ one has
$Mc^2=\sum_iE_{e_0}(P_i)$; every massive constituent has
$E_{e_0}(P_i)\ge m_ic^2$, with equality exactly when it is at rest in that
frame, and every massless constituent has $E_{e_0}(P_i)>0$. Hence
$M\ge\sum_im_i$ over the massive constituents, with equality if and only if
the system is massive-only and all its constituents are at rest in the
center-of-momentum frame. If $Q$ is future null, then $M=0$, all constituents
are massless with parallel momenta, and no center-of-momentum frame exists.

**(d) Massless particle.** An ideal massless particle has
$E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$, has no rest frame and is not $mU$ for any $m>0$; it is
not obtained from the massive formula by setting $m=0$.

**(e) Necessary collision thresholds.** Suppose that, under the adopted
isolated-collision balance, an isolated collision occurs whose incoming legs
are massive particles of constant masses $m_1,\dots,m_N$ and whose outgoing
legs are massive particles of masses $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_K$ and possibly ideal
massless particles. Let $M$ be the invariant mass of the common total
four-momentum $Q$. Then the necessary inequalities $M\ge\sum_im_i$ and
$M\ge\sum_j\mu_j$ hold; if the incoming side is a projectile of mass $m_1$
and a target of mass $m_2$ at rest in the observer frame of the target, with
projectile energy $E$ and kinetic energy $T=E-m_1c^2$ in that frame, then

$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\Bigr],\qquad T\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2\Bigr],$$

and a single incoming massless particle cannot collide into an outgoing state
containing a massive particle. These are kinematic necessity statements under
the adopted conservation: they do not assert that any collision occurs, do
not fix probabilities, amplitudes or cross sections, and are not empirical
findings.

**(f) Scope.** All clauses are conditional on the two postulates and on the
stated idealisations; the conclusions carry the same idealisations. No
measurement, precision, statistical or empirical claim is made.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the adopted premises [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] and
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]; the flat Minkowski model
$(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with $c>0$; for (a) a massive particle with constant $m>0$
and future unit observer $n$; for (b) a $C^2$ worldline; for (c) a finite
nonempty system of particles with nonzero future causal four-momenta; for (e)
an isolated collision with massive incoming and outgoing legs as stated.

[F1] ([[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], Postulate (i) and (ii)): every
massive classical particle carries a positive constant mass parameter $m>0$
and has four-momentum $P=mU$; relative to a future unit observer $n$ the model
identifies the measured energy with $E_n(P)$, the measured spatial momentum
with $q_n(P)$, the kinetic energy with $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and the rest
energy with $mc^2$; the SI unit of $P$ is kilogram metre per second.

[F2] ([[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]], Postulate (i) and (ii)):
an ideal massless particle is described by a nonzero future null vector $P$,
with measured energy and spatial momentum identified with $E_n(P)$ and
$q_n(P)$; it is not of the form $mU$ for any $m>0$ and future timelike $U$
with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and it has no four-velocity, no proper-time
parametrisation and no rest frame.

[F3] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (a) and (b)):
for nonzero future causal $P$ and future unit $n$, $E_n(P)>0$ and the mass
shell and null identities hold; for $P=mU$ with $m>0$, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and
$\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$, one has $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$,
$T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)\ge0$, $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $U=cn$, and
$m(P)=m$.

[F4] ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]], Statement (a)–(c)): in an
inertial frame with $n=e_0$ the components are
$(P^0,P^1,P^2,P^3)=(E_n(P)/c,q^1,q^2,q^3)$ and the mass-shell identity holds
in components; for $P=mU$ with chart coordinate velocity $w$ one has
$E=m\gamma_wc^2$, $\mathbf p=m\gamma_w\mathbf w$; under a passive boost the
components transform as the components of $P$, the combination
$E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2$ is invariant and equals $m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike
$P$ and $0$ for future null $P$.

[F5] ([[lem-sr-four-force-and-work-energy-identities]], Statement (a)–(d)):
with $F=\dot P$ the four-force of
[[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]] along a $C^2$ worldline,
$F=mA$, $\eta(P,F)=0$, $F=\gamma(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\mathbf f)$,
$dE/dt=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$ for constant $m$, and
$\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,dm/d\tau$ for a $C^1$ variable mass parameter.

[F6] ([[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]], Definition): side
totals are finite sums; the invariant mass of a future timelike total $Q$ is
$M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$; for a future null total $M=0$ by convention; a
center-of-momentum frame of a nonzero total is an inertial frame with
$q_{e_0}(Q)=0$.

[F7] ([[lem-sr-finite-future-causal-sums]], Statement): for nonzero future
causal $P_1,\dots,P_N$, the total $Q=\sum_iP_i$ is nonzero future causal and
is future timelike if some $P_i$ is future timelike; $-\eta(v,w)\ge0$ for
$v,w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ with equality if and only if $v=0$, or $w=0$, or both
are nonzero future null with $w=\lambda v$, $\lambda>0$; $E_n$ and $q_n$ are
additive over finite sums, with $E_n(Q)>0$.

[F8] ([[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]], Statement (a) and (c)): for future
timelike $Q$ with invariant mass $M$ there is an inertial frame with
$e_0=Q/(Mc)$, $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ and $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$; a nonzero future null
vector has no center-of-momentum frame.

[F9] ([[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]], Definition): a collision
datum consists of an event and two finite nonempty lists of legs with side
totals; it conserves when the totals are equal; a mass-specified datum is
on-shell with recorded masses; a causal datum has all legs in
$\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$.

[F10] ([[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]], Statement (a), (c) and
(d)): for a mass-specified conserving causal on-shell datum with nonzero legs
and future timelike total $Q$ of invariant mass $M$, each side satisfies
$M\ge\sum m_\ell$ over its massive legs with equality exactly when the side is
massive-only and all its massive legs are at rest in the center-of-momentum
frame; for the two-leg incoming side $P_i=m_iU_i$ with $n_2=U_2/c$,
$\gamma=-\eta(U_1/c,n_2)$ and $E=E_{n_2}(P_1)=m_1c^2\gamma$, one has
$M^2=m_1^2+m_2^2+2m_2E/c^2$, giving the stated thresholds for an outgoing
massive-mass sum $\sum_j\mu_j$; and a conserving datum with a single null
incoming leg and an outgoing massive leg does not exist.

[F11] ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], Definition): in the
framework's conventions the four-momentum has the unit kilogram metre per
second and the observer energy the unit joule.

[F12] ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and
[[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]): a nonzero vector is timelike when
$\eta(v,v)<0$ and null when $\eta(v,v)=0$; $\eta$ is bilinear, so
$\eta(mU,mU)=m^2\eta(U,U)$ and $0\cdot U=0$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** quote the two adopted premises for the physical
identification, then apply the page's mathematical suppliers clause by clause;
the collision thresholds are the necessary conditions of the collision lemma
under the adopted balance.

1.1 The adopted premises [F1] and [F2] provide the physical identification: for a massive particle the model's measured energy, spatial momentum, kinetic energy and rest energy are $E_n(P),q_n(P),T_n(P),mc^2$ with $P=mU$ and $m>0$ constant, and for an ideal massless particle they are $E_n(P),q_n(P)$ with $P$ a nonzero future null vector, no rest mass, rest energy or kinetic energy being assigned; [F11] fixes the units. [F1, F2, F11]

1.2 For $P=mU$ with $m>0$, $U$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and $n$ future unit, [F3] gives $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$ with $\gamma=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)\ge0$, $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $U=cn$, the mass-shell identity $E_n(P)^2=m^2c^4+c^2|q_n(P)|^2$ and $m(P)=m$; [F4] adds the frame components $(E/c,\mathbf p)$ with $E=m\gamma_wc^2$, $\mathbf p=m\gamma_w\mathbf w$, the passive-boost transformation law and the invariance $E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m^2c^4$. [F3, F4]

1.3 For every nonzero future null $P$ and future unit $n$, [F3] gives $E_n(P)=c|q_n(P)|>0$; [F2] gives that such a $P$ has no four-velocity, proper time or rest frame; and [F12] shows that $m=0$ in the massive formula yields $0\cdot U=0\ne P$, while $m>0$ yields $\eta(mU,mU)=-m^2c^2<0$, so $mU$ is timelike and cannot equal the null $P$: no $m\ge0$ produces $P$ from $P=mU$. [F2, F3, F12]

1.4 Along a $C^2$ worldline with four-force $F=\dot P$, [F5] gives the identities $\eta(P,F)=0$, $F=mA$ for constant $m$, the frame form $F=\gamma(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\mathbf f)$, $dE/dt=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$, and the variable-mass identity $\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,dm/d\tau$. [F5]

1.5 For nonzero future causal $P_1,\dots,P_N$, [F7] makes $Q=\sum_iP_i$ nonzero future causal, future timelike if some $P_i$ is future timelike, additive in $E_n$ and $q_n$ with $E_n(Q)>0$, and gives the equality characterization of $-\eta(v,w)=0$ for $v,w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$; [F6] and [F8] give the invariant-mass convention, the existence of the center-of-momentum frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ and $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$ when $Q$ is future timelike, and the nonexistence of such a frame when $Q$ is nonzero future null. [F6, F7, F8]

1.6 The collision data of (e), under the adopted isolated-collision balance of [F1]'s postulate, form a mass-specified, conserving, causal, on-shell collision datum with nonzero legs in the sense of [F9], whose incoming side contains the massive legs of masses $m_1,\dots,m_N$; [F10] then supplies the side inequalities $M\ge\sum m_\ell$ with their equality cases, the two-leg identity $M^2=m_1^2+m_2^2+2m_2E/c^2$ with its thresholds, and the impossibility of a single null incoming leg with an outgoing massive leg. [F1, F9, F10]

2.1 Clause (a): [step 1.1] identifies the measured quantities with $E_n,q_n,T_n,mc^2$ and [step 1.2] supplies $E_n(P)>0$, $T_n(P)\ge0$, the mass-shell identity, the rest criterion $T_n(P)=0\iff U=cn$, the frame components, the boost transformation law and the frame independence of $E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m^2c^4$. [step 1.1, step 1.2]

2.2 Clause (b): [step 1.1] makes $\dot P$ the model's four-force and $E_n(P)$ its measured energy, and [step 1.4] gives $\eta(P,F)=0$, $F=mA$, $F=\gamma(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\mathbf f)$ and $dE/dt=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$ for constant $m$, together with the variable-mass identity and the warning that the constant-mass identities are not transferred to variable-mass systems. [step 1.1, step 1.4]

2.3 Clause (c), timelike total: assume $Q$ future timelike with invariant mass $M$; by [step 1.5] the center-of-momentum frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ exists and $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$, and additivity gives $Mc^2=E_{e_0}(Q)=\sum_iE_{e_0}(P_i)$. Each massive constituent satisfies $E_{e_0}(P_i)=m_ic^2\gamma_i\ge m_ic^2$ with equality exactly when $U_i=ce_0$ by [step 1.2], and each massless constituent satisfies $E_{e_0}(P_i)=c|q_{e_0}(P_i)|>0$ by [step 1.3]; hence $M=\sum_{\text{massive}}m_i+\sum_{\text{massive}}m_i(\gamma_i-1)+\sum_{\text{massless}}E_{e_0}(P_i)/c^2\ \ge\ \sum_{\text{massive}}m_i$, with equality if and only if the system is massive-only and every massive constituent has $\gamma_i=1$, that is is at rest in the center-of-momentum frame. [step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.5]

2.4 Clause (c), null total: if $Q$ is future null, then [step 1.5] gives $M=0$ by the convention and the nonexistence of a center-of-momentum frame; moreover $0=-\eta(Q,Q)=\sum_{i,j}-\eta(P_i,P_j)$ with each term nonnegative by [step 1.5], so each term vanishes and the equality characterization forces every $P_i$ to be nonzero future null and parallel to any other, that is all constituents are massless with parallel momenta. [step 1.5]

2.5 Clause (d): for an ideal massless particle [step 1.1] identifies the measured energy and momentum with $E_n$ and $q_n$, and [step 1.3] gives $E_n(P)=c|q_n(P)|>0$; the same step gives that $P$ has no four-velocity, proper time or rest frame, that $P\ne mU$ for every $m>0$, and that no $m\ge0$ produces $P$ from the massive formula. [step 1.1, step 1.3]

2.6 Clause (e): the collision data of [step 1.6] form a conserving mass-specified causal on-shell datum; its incoming side contains the massive legs of masses $m_1,\dots,m_N$, so $Q$ is future timelike by [step 1.5] and the invariant mass $M$ is defined; [step 1.6] then gives $M\ge\sum_im_i$ and, applied to the outgoing side with massive-mass sum $\sum_j\mu_j$, $M\ge\sum_j\mu_j$; in the two-leg projectile-target case with $n_2=U_2/c$, [step 1.6] gives $M^2=m_1^2+m_2^2+2m_2E/c^2$, and combining this with $M\ge\sum_j\mu_j$ yields the two displayed threshold inequalities by rearrangement, while the one-null-leg impossibility is the last statement of [step 1.6]. No interaction, probability, amplitude or cross section is asserted. [step 1.5, step 1.6]

3.1 Collecting: clause (a) is [step 2.1], clause (b) is [step 2.2], clause (c) is [step 2.3] together with [step 2.4], clause (d) is [step 2.5] and clause (e) is [step 2.6]; clause (f) records that every conclusion is conditional on the two adopted postulates and the stated idealisations, with no measurement or empirical claim, and no empirical premise is used in this deduction. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 2.4, step 2.5, step 2.6] ∎

## Example

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, $m>0$, and let
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) in which a massive particle has
four-velocity $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$
([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e)) with
$w=(3c/5,0,0)$, so that $\gamma_w=5/4$. Then its four-momentum is $P=mU$ with
components $(5mc/4,\,3mc/4,\,0,\,0)$. Relative to the stationary observer
$n=e_0$: $E_n(P)=5mc^2/4$, $q_n(P)$ has coordinates $(3mc/4,0,0)$, the
kinetic energy is $T_n(P)=mc^2/4$, and the mass shell
$E_n(P)^2-c^2|q_n(P)|^2=m^2c^4$ reads
$25m^2c^4/16-9m^2c^4/16=m^2c^4$. The exact kinetic energy
$mc^2/4=0.25\,mc^2$ exceeds the Newtonian expression
$\tfrac12m|w|^2=9mc^2/50=0.18\,mc^2$; the comparison is a numerical
specialisation, not a limiting claim and not a measurement.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the affine Minkowski model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; $c>0$; $m>0$; an
inertial frame in which $w=(3c/5,0,0)$ and $\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$.

[F1] ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], clause (e)): in the
chart the four-velocity is $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$ with
$\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and the frame components are read in
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[F2] ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]], Definition):
the spatial part of a frame vector lies in $S=e_0^\perp$ with
$|w|^2=\sum_i(w^i)^2$ for $w=\sum_iw^ie_i$, and $w=(3c/5,0,0)$ means
$w^1=3c/5$, $w^2=w^3=0$.

[F3] ([[lem-rational-power-laws]] and [[def-rational-power]]): for positive
reals the rational-power laws hold, so $(1-r)^{-1/2}$ for $0\le r<1$ is the
positive number whose square is $(1-r)^{-1}$; in particular
$(16/25)^{-1/2}=5/4$ since $(4/5)^2=16/25$ and $(4/5)^{-1}=5/4$.

[F4] ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]], clause (b)):
$E_n(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $q_n(P)=\sum_im\gamma_ww^ie_i$ for $P=mU$.

[F5] ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], Definition):
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ for $P=mU$ with $m>0$ and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$.

[F6] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (a)(ii)):
for future timelike $P$ the mass-shell identity
$E_n(P)^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2|q_n(P)|^2$ holds, and $m(P)=m$ for $P=mU$.

## Verification

1.1 The Lorentz factor: by [F2], $|w|^2=(3c/5)^2=9c^2/25$, so $|w|^2/c^2=9/25$ and $1-|w|^2/c^2=16/25$; hence $\gamma_w=(16/25)^{-1/2}=5/4$ by [F1] and [F3]. [F1, F2, F3]

1.2 The four-momentum: [F1] gives $U=\gamma_w(c,w)=(5c/4,\,3c/4,\,0,\,0)$ in the frame components, so $P=mU$ has components $(5mc/4,\,3mc/4,\,0,\,0)$. [F1, F2]

2.1 The observer quantities: by [F4], $E_n(P)=m\gamma_wc^2=5mc^2/4$ and $q_n(P)=m\gamma_w w=(5m/4)(3c/5,0,0)=(3mc/4,0,0)$; by [F5], $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2=5mc^2/4-mc^2=mc^2/4$. [F4, F5, step 1.1]

3.1 The mass shell: by [step 2.1], $E_n(P)^2-c^2|q_n(P)|^2=25m^2c^4/16-c^2(9m^2c^2/16)=25m^2c^4/16-9m^2c^4/16=16m^2c^4/16=m^2c^4$, in agreement with [F6] and $m(P)=m$. [F6, step 1.2, step 2.1]

3.2 The Newtonian comparison: $\tfrac12m|w|^2=\tfrac12m(9c^2/25)=9mc^2/50$, while [step 2.1] gives $T_n(P)=mc^2/4$; since $1/4=25/100$ exceeds $9/50=18/100$, the exact kinetic energy exceeds the Newtonian expression at this speed, the comparison being a numerical specialisation of the two formulas and not a limit claim. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 All displayed quantities of the example are verified: $P=(5mc/4,3mc/4,0,0)$, $E_n(P)=5mc^2/4$, $q_n(P)=(3mc/4,0,0)$, $T_n(P)=mc^2/4$, the mass shell $E_n(P)^2-c^2|q_n(P)|^2=m^2c^4$, and $T_n(P)>9mc^2/50$; no measurement or limiting statement is asserted. [step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

## Example

In the setting of [[ex-sr-four-momentum-at-beta-three-fifths]], let
$B(\beta)$ be the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] with parameter
$\beta=3/5$ along $e_1$, and let $P'$ be the components of $P$ after the
coordinate change $x'=B(\beta)x$ with $v=3c/5$. Then
$P'=(mc,0,0,0)$: the energy becomes $E'=mc^2$ and the spatial momentum
vanishes, and the mass shell gives $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=m^2c^4$. The
observer energy of the same particle thus changes from $5mc^2/4$ to $mc^2$
while the invariant mass stays $m$; in particular $T_{e'_0}(P)=0$ in the new
frame, the frame of the particle's rest.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the affine Minkowski model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; $c>0$; $m>0$; the
inertial frame and particle of the $\beta=3/5$ example, so that
$w=(3c/5,0,0)$; the passive boost $B(\beta)$ with $\beta=3/5$ along $e_1$ and
$v=3c/5$.

[F1] ([[ex-sr-four-momentum-at-beta-three-fifths]], Example): in the original
frame $P=mU$ with $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$, $\gamma_w=5/4$, and $P$ has components
$(5mc/4,3mc/4,0,0)$, observer energy $5mc^2/4$ and spatial momentum
$(3mc/4,0,0)$.

[F2] ([[def-lorentz-boost]] and
[[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]): the boost with parameter
$\beta=(v/c)s$, $|v|<c$, has $\gamma_v=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and matrix
$B^0{}_0=\gamma_v$, $B^0{}_i=B^i{}_0=-\gamma_v(v/c)s_i$; it is a proper
orthochronous Lorentz map and is invertible.

[F3] ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]], clause (i)): under a
coordinate change $x'=\Lambda x+b$ the components of a vector transform as
$P'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bP^b$; applied to $\Lambda=B(\beta)$ this gives
$E'=\gamma_v(E-vp_\parallel)$, $p'_\parallel=\gamma_v(p_\parallel-vE/c^2)$,
$p'_\perp=p_\perp$ with $p_\parallel$ the component of $\mathbf p$ along $s$.

[F4] ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]], clauses (a) and (c)): in an
inertial frame with stationary observer $e_0$ the components are
$(E_{e_0}(P)/c,q^1,q^2,q^3)$, and the combination
$E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2$ is invariant with value $m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike
$P$.

[F5] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (b)): for
$P=mU$ with $m>0$, $U$ future timelike with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and $n$ future
unit, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ with $\gamma=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$, and
$T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $U=cn$.

## Verification

1.1 By [F1], $E=E_{e_0}(P)=5mc^2/4$ and $\mathbf p=(3mc/4,0,0)$, so with the boost direction $s=e_1$ the parallel component is $p_\parallel=3mc/4$ and $\mathbf p_\perp=0$; by [F2], $\beta=3/5$ gives $v=3c/5$ and $\gamma_v=(1-9/25)^{-1/2}=5/4$. [F1, F2]

2.1 Apply [F3]: $E'=\gamma_v(E-vp_\parallel)=\frac54\bigl(\frac{5mc^2}{4}-\frac{3c}{5}\cdot\frac{3mc}{4}\bigr)=\frac54\bigl(\frac{25mc^2-9mc^2}{20}\bigr)=\frac54\cdot\frac{16mc^2}{20}=\frac54\cdot\frac{4mc^2}{5}=mc^2$, and $p'_\parallel=\gamma_v(p_\parallel-vE/c^2)=\frac54\bigl(\frac{3mc}{4}-\frac{3c}{5}\cdot\frac{5mc^2}{4c^2}\bigr)=\frac54\bigl(\frac{3mc}{4}-\frac{3mc}{4}\bigr)=0$, while $\mathbf p'_\perp=\mathbf p_\perp=0$; hence $P'=(mc,0,0,0)$. [F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The mass shell in the new frame: by [F4] applied in the primed inertial frame, $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=m^2c^4$; substituting $E'=mc^2$, $\mathbf p'=0$ by [step 2.1] gives $m^2c^4-0=m^2c^4$, and $m(P)=m$ since the invariant combination is unchanged. [F4, step 2.1]

4.1 The observer energy of the particle in the new frame is $E_{e'_0}(P)=cP'^0=mc^2$ by [F4] and [step 2.1], so the kinetic energy $T_{e'_0}(P)=E_{e'_0}(P)-mc^2=0$; by [F5], $T_{e'_0}(P)=0$ if and only if $U=ce'_0$, so the particle is at rest in the new frame, whose time vector is the particle's four-velocity up to $c$; in particular the observer energy changed from $5mc^2/4$ to $mc^2$ while the invariant mass stayed $m$. [F4, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 All claims of the example are verified: the boost with parameter $3/5$ along $e_1$ sends $P=(5mc/4,3mc/4,0,0)$ to $P'=(mc,0,0,0)$ with $E'=mc^2$ and vanishing spatial momentum, the mass shell reads $m^2c^4$ in both frames, and the new frame is the particle's rest frame. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Example

Let $m>0$ and let two massive particles at a common event have four-momenta
$P_1=m\gamma(c,w)$ and $P_2=m\gamma(c,-w)$ with $w=(3c/5,0,0)$ and
$\gamma=5/4$. Their total is $Q=P_1+P_2=(5mc/2,0,0,0)$, which is future
timelike with invariant mass $M=5m/2$. Since the first basis vector $e_0$
already equals $Q/(Mc)$, the displayed frame is a center-of-momentum frame;
moreover $M=5m/2>2m=m_1+m_2$, and the mass excess
$(M-2m)c^2=mc^2/2$ equals the total kinetic energy of the two particles
relative to $e_0$ ($mc^2/4$ each). Thus the rest mass of the system is not the
sum of the rest masses of its parts. The computation is exact at
$\gamma=5/4$ and asserts no collision.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the affine Minkowski model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; $c>0$; $m>0$; an
inertial frame in which $P_1=m\gamma(c,w)$, $P_2=m\gamma(c,-w)$ with
$w=(3c/5,0,0)$ and $\gamma=5/4$.

[F1] ([[ex-sr-four-momentum-at-beta-three-fifths]], Example): at
$w=(3c/5,0,0)$ one has $\gamma_w=5/4$, and $P=mU$ with $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$ has
components $(5mc/4,3mc/4,0,0)$, observer energy $E_{e_0}(P)=5mc^2/4$, spatial
momentum $q_{e_0}(P)$ with coordinates $(3mc/4,0,0)$ and kinetic energy
$T_{e_0}(P)=mc^2/4$.

[F2] ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] and
[[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]): the frame basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is
$\eta$-orthonormal with $\eta(e_0,e_0)=-1$ and $\eta(e_i,e_i)=1$, $\eta$ is
bilinear, components of a sum of vectors add, and for a vector with
components $(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)$ one has
$\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2$.

[F3] ([[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]], Definition): the
total $Q$ of a finite list is the finite sum, and if $Q$ is future timelike
then its invariant mass is $M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$.

[F4] ([[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]], Statement (a)): for future timelike
$Q$ with invariant mass $M$ an inertial frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ exists, and
in it $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ and $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$.

[F5] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (b)): for
$P=mU$ with $m>0$, $U$ future timelike with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and $n$ future
unit, $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$ and $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ with
$\gamma=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$, and $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $U=cn$.

[F6] ([[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]], Statement (a)): for a
mass-specified conserving causal on-shell collision datum
([[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]) with future timelike total $Q$
of invariant mass $M$, each side satisfies $M\ge\sum m_\ell$ over its massive
legs, with equality if and only if the side is massive-only and every massive
leg is at rest in the center-of-momentum frame.

## Verification

1.1 With $w=(3c/5,0,0)$ and $\gamma=5/4$, [F1] applied to $P_1=m\gamma(c,w)$ gives the components $P_1=(5mc/4,3mc/4,0,0)$; replacing $w$ by $-w$ leaves $\gamma$ unchanged and changes the sign of the spatial part, so $P_2=m\gamma(c,-w)$ has components $(5mc/4,-3mc/4,0,0)$. Both $P_i$ are $m$ times the four-velocity $\gamma(c,\pm w)$ of a massive particle, hence future timelike with $\eta(P_i,P_i)=-m^2c^2$. [F1, F2]

1.2 By [F2] components add, so $Q=P_1+P_2=(5mc/2,0,0,0)$; then $\eta(Q,Q)=-(5mc/2)^2<0$, so $Q$ is future timelike ($Q^0>0$), and [F3] gives $M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c=(5mc/2)/c=5m/2$. [F2, F3]

2.1 The displayed frame is a center-of-momentum frame: $Q/(Mc)=(5mc/2,0,0,0)/((5m/2)c)=(1,0,0,0)=e_0$, so by [F4] $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ and $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2=5mc^2/2$; by [F5] each particle has $T_{e_0}(P_i)=mc^2(\gamma-1)=mc^2/4$, so the total kinetic energy relative to $e_0$ is $mc^2/2$. [F4, F5, step 1.2]

3.1 Strictness of the mass inequality: the triple $(p;(P_1,P_2);(P_1,P_2))$ with any event $p$ is a mass-specified conserving causal on-shell collision datum with nonzero legs, so [F6] gives $M\ge m_1+m_2=2m$ for the common total; equality would require every massive leg to satisfy $T_{e_0}(P_i)=0$, hence $U_i=ce_0$ by [F5], contradicting $T_{e_0}(P_i)=mc^2/4>0$ from [step 2.1]. Therefore $M>2m$, in agreement with $M=5m/2$ from [step 1.2]. [F5, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Mass excess: $(M-2m)c^2=(5m/2-2m)c^2=mc^2/2$, which equals the total kinetic energy computed in [step 2.1]; hence the invariant mass of the system exceeds the sum of the rest masses of its parts by the total kinetic energy in the center-of-momentum frame, and the rest mass of the system is not the sum of the rest masses of its parts. [step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Example

In the setting of [[ex-sr-equal-mass-head-on-collision-mass]], the datum with
incoming side $(P_1,P_2)$ and the single outgoing vector
$Q=(5mc/2,0,0,0)=(5m/2)c\,e_0$ is an on-shell conserving collision datum: $Q$
is massive with mass $5m/2$ and four-velocity $ce_0$, and $P_1+P_2=Q$. The
outgoing rest mass $5m/2$ exceeds the incoming sum $2m$ by $m/2$, and the
incoming total kinetic energy $mc^2/2=(M-2m)c^2$ has become rest energy. The
final state is not unique: the same total $Q$ is also the sum of two outgoing
massive legs at rest with masses $m$ and $3m/2$ (four-velocities $ce_0$), so
four-momentum conservation fixes only the total, not the number or masses of
the outgoing particles. The datum is a mathematical configuration and no
interaction is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the affine Minkowski model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; $c>0$; $m>0$; the
inertial frame and the incoming four-momenta $P_1,P_2$ of the equal-mass
example.

[F1] ([[ex-sr-equal-mass-head-on-collision-mass]], Example): in the displayed
frame $P_1,P_2$ are the four-momenta of two massive particles of mass $m$ with
components $(5mc/4,\pm3mc/4,0,0)$, their total is
$Q=P_1+P_2=(5mc/2,0,0,0)$, $Q$ is future timelike with invariant mass
$M=5m/2$, the displayed frame is a center-of-momentum frame, each particle has
kinetic energy $mc^2/4$ there, and $(M-2m)c^2=mc^2/2$ is the total kinetic
energy.

[F2] ([[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]], Definition): a collision
datum records an event and the incoming and outgoing legs with side totals
formed as finite sums, and conserves when the totals are equal; a leg $P$ is
massive with mass $m'>0$ if $P=m'U'$ for some future timelike $U'$ with
$\eta(U',U')=-c^2$; a mass-specified datum is on-shell with recorded masses,
and a causal datum has all legs in $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$.

[F3] ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]] and
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]): the frame basis is
$\eta$-orthonormal with $\eta(e_0,e_0)=-1$, components of sums and scalar
multiples are computed componentwise, and for $\lambda>0$ the vector
$\lambda(ce_0)$ has components $(\lambda c,0,0,0)$.

[F4] ([[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]], Statement (a)): for a
mass-specified conserving causal on-shell datum with future timelike total $Q$
of invariant mass $M$, each side satisfies $M\ge\sum m_\ell$ over its massive
legs, with equality if and only if the side is massive-only and every massive
leg is at rest in the center-of-momentum frame.

[F5] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (b)): for

## Example

Let $e_0,e_1$ be the first two vectors of an inertial frame, $E_1,E_2>0$, and
let $P_1=(E_1/c)(e_0+e_1)$, $P_2=(E_2/c)(e_0-e_1)$. Both are nonzero future
null vectors with $E_{e_0}(P_i)=E_i$, and their total is
$Q=((E_1+E_2)/c)e_0+((E_1-E_2)/c)e_1$, a future timelike vector with
invariant mass $M=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c^2$; for $E_1=E_2=E$ this gives
$Q=(2E/c)e_0$ and $M=2E/c^2$. If instead $P_2=(E_2/E_1)P_1$ (parallel
momenta), then $Q$ is future null, $M=0$ by convention and there is no
center-of-momentum frame. In the opposite-direction case with $E_1\ne E_2$
the first basis vector is not the center-of-momentum vector; the
center-of-momentum frame exists by [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]] but
differs from the displayed frame. The arithmetic is exact and no measurement
is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the affine Minkowski model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; $c>0$; the first two
vectors $e_0,e_1$ of an inertial frame; $E_1,E_2>0$; the vectors
$P_1=(E_1/c)(e_0+e_1)$ and $P_2=(E_2/c)(e_0-e_1)$.

[F1] ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] and
[[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]): the frame basis is $\eta$-orthonormal with
$\eta(e_0,e_0)=-1$, $\eta(e_1,e_1)=1$, $\eta(e_0,e_1)=0$; $\eta$ is bilinear,
so $\eta(P_1,P_2)=(E_1E_2/c^2)\bigl(\eta(e_0,e_0)-\eta(e_1,e_1)\bigr)$ and
components add.

[F2] ([[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], Statement): in an
$\eta$-orthonormal basis whose first vector is timelike,
$\mathrm{cl}(C^+)=\{v:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ for the naming of $C^+$ containing the
first vector, and $C^+$ is closed under multiplication by positive reals.

[F3] ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]): a vector is null when
$\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\ne0$, timelike when $\eta(v,v)<0$, and future null when
it is null and lies in $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$.

[F4] ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], Definition):
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$ for $P\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ and future unit $n$.

[F5] ([[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]], Definition): the
total of a finite list is the finite sum; the invariant mass of a future
timelike total is $M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$; for a future null total $M=0$ by
convention.

[F6] ([[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]], Statement (a)–(c)): a future
timelike $Q$ with invariant mass $M$ has an inertial frame with
$e_0=Q/(Mc)$ and $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$; if an inertial frame satisfies
$q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ then $e_0=Q/(Mc)$; a nonzero future null vector has no
center-of-momentum frame.

[F7] ([[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]], Statement (d)): for future
null $P_i=(E_i/c)(e_0+s_i)$ with unit $s_i$ and $\sigma=s_1\cdot s_2$, the
total is future timelike for $\sigma<1$ with
$M=\sqrt{2E_1E_2(1-\sigma)}/c^2$, and for $\sigma=1$ ($\theta=0$, parallel
spatial directions) it is future null with $M=0$ and no center-of-momentum
frame.

[F8] ([[lem-rational-power-laws]] and [[def-rational-power]]): for $a>0$ the
nonnegative square roots multiply, so
$\sqrt{4E_1E_2/c^2}=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c$ for $E_1,E_2>0$ and $c>0$.

## Verification

1.1 Both vectors are nonzero future null: by [F1] and [F2], $P_1$ has components $(E_1/c)(1,1,0,0)$, so $v^0=E_1/c=|v_s|$ and $\eta(P_1,P_1)=(E_1/c)^2(-1+1)=0$ with $P_1\ne0$; [F3] then makes $P_1$ future null, and the same computation with the sign of the second component reversed applies to $P_2=(E_2/c)(e_0-e_1)$. [F1, F2, F3]

1.2 The observer energies are the stated ones: by [F4] and [F1], $E_{e_0}(P_1)=-c\,\eta(P_1,e_0)=-c(E_1/c)\bigl(\eta(e_0,e_0)+\eta(e_1,e_0)\bigr)=E_1$ and likewise $E_{e_0}(P_2)=-c(E_2/c)(-1)=E_2$. [F1, F4]

1.3 The total: components add by [F1], so $Q=P_1+P_2=((E_1+E_2)/c)e_0+((E_1-E_2)/c)e_1$; then $\eta(Q,Q)=-(E_1+E_2)^2/c^2+(E_1-E_2)^2/c^2=-4E_1E_2/c^2<0$, so $Q$ is future timelike with $Q^0>0$, and [F5] and [F8] give $M=\sqrt{4E_1E_2/c^2}/c=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c^2$. [F1, F5, F8]

2.1 Center-of-momentum frame and the equal-energy case: by [F4]-type computation in the frame, $q_{e_0}(Q)=Q+\eta(Q,e_0)e_0=((E_1-E_2)/c)e_1$, so the displayed frame is a center-of-momentum frame exactly when $E_1=E_2$; for $E_1=E_2=E$ one has $Q=(2E/c)e_0$, $M=2E/c^2$ and $Q/(Mc)=e_0$, while for $E_1\ne E_2$ the center-of-momentum vector $Q/(Mc)$ has a nonzero $e_1$ component and differs from $e_0$, the frame existing by [F6]. [F6, step 1.3]

2.2 The parallel case: if $P_2=(E_2/E_1)P_1$ then $Q=(1+E_2/E_1)P_1$ is a positive multiple of the nonzero future null $P_1$, hence future null by [F2] and [F3]; the case $\sigma=1$ of [F7] (the two vectors as the two legs of the trivially conserving datum $(p;(P_1,P_2);(P_1,P_2))$) gives the same conclusion, and [F5] then sets $M=0$ while [F6] shows that no center-of-momentum frame exists. [F2, F3, F5, F6, F7, step 1.1]

3.1 All claims of the example are verified: the future null vectors $P_1,P_2$ have observer energies $E_1,E_2$; their total is future timelike with $M=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c^2$, equal to $2E/c^2$ when $E_1=E_2=E$; the displayed frame is the center-of-momentum frame exactly in that equal-energy case and otherwise differs from it; and parallel momenta give a future null total with $M=0$ and no center-of-momentum frame. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Example

Let $m>0$, $\mu>0$ and consider a conserving causal on-shell collision datum
whose incoming side is two massive legs, a projectile of mass $m$ with energy
$E$ measured by the rest observer $n_2$ of the target, and a target of mass
$m$ at rest in that observer's frame, and whose outgoing side is massive with
masses $m$, $m$ and $\mu$. By
[[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]\,(c) with $m_1=m_2=m$ and
$\sum_l\mu_l=2m+\mu$,

$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m}\bigl[(2m+\mu)^2-2m^2\bigr]=mc^2+2\mu c^2+\frac{\mu^2c^2}{2m},$$

equivalently $T=E-mc^2\ \ge\ 2\mu c^2+\dfrac{\mu^2c^2}{2m}$. For $\mu=m$
this reads $E\ge7mc^2/2$ and $T\ge5mc^2/2$. These are necessary kinematic
thresholds under the adopted balance of the datum; the datum need not exist
for any concrete interaction and no process is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the affine Minkowski model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; $c>0$; $m>0$;
$\mu>0$; a conserving causal on-shell collision datum with the stated
incoming and outgoing legs, the incoming legs being $P_i=mU_i$,
$i\in\{1,2\}$, and $n_2:=U_2/c$ the rest observer of the target.

[F1] ([[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]], Statement (c)): for a
mass-specified conserving causal on-shell datum with nonzero legs whose
incoming side is two-leg with $P_i=m_iU_i$, $m_i>0$, and with
$n_2=U_2/c$, $\gamma=-\eta(U_1/c,n_2)\ge1$, $E=E_{n_2}(P_1)=m_1c^2\gamma$
and invariant mass $M$ of the future timelike total, one has
$M^2=m_1^2+m_2^2+2m_2E/c^2$; if the outgoing side is mass-specified with
massive masses $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_L$ (possibly with null legs), then the
datum can conserve only if
$E\ge\frac{c^2}{2m_2}\bigl[(\sum_l\mu_l)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\bigr]$ and
$T:=E-m_1c^2\ge\frac{c^2}{2m_2}\bigl[(\sum_l\mu_l)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2\bigr]$.

[F2] ([[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]], Definition): a collision
datum records an event and the incoming and outgoing legs with side totals
formed as finite sums; it conserves when the totals are equal; a
mass-specified datum is on-shell with recorded masses, and a causal datum has
all legs in $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$.

[F3] ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], Definition): $U_2$ is
the four-velocity of a future timelike worldline with $\eta(U_2,U_2)=-c^2$,
and $n_2=U_2/c$ is future unit; $E_{n_2}(P_1)$ is the projectile energy
measured by the observer comoving with the target, so the target is at rest
in that observer's frame.

[F4] ([[def-rational-power]] and [[lem-rational-power-laws]]): for positive
reals the rational-power laws hold, so the displayed algebraic rearrangements
of positive expressions are legitimate; in particular
$\mu^2c^2/(2m)=(c^2/2m)\mu^2$ for $2m>0$.

## Verification

1.1 The hypotheses of [F1] are met by the stated datum: by [F2] it is a conserving causal on-shell datum with the two massive incoming legs $P_1=mU_1$ (projectile) and $P_2=mU_2$ (target), and by [F3] $n_2=U_2/c$ is the future unit observer comoving with the target, in whose frame the target is at rest and $E=E_{n_2}(P_1)$ is the projectile energy; so the datum can conserve only if the threshold inequality of [F1] holds. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Substituting $m_1=m_2=m$ and $\sum_l\mu_l=2m+\mu$ into the threshold of [F1] gives $E\ge\frac{c^2}{2m}\bigl[(2m+\mu)^2-m^2-m^2\bigr]$ and $T=E-mc^2\ge\frac{c^2}{2m}\bigl[(2m+\mu)^2-4m^2\bigr]$. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 Expanding $(2m+\mu)^2-2m^2=2m^2+4m\mu+\mu^2$ and dividing by $2m>0$ gives $m+2\mu+\mu^2/(2m)$; multiplying by $c^2$ and using [F4] yields $E\ge mc^2+2\mu c^2+\frac{\mu^2c^2}{2m}$. [F4, step 2.1]

4.1 The kinetic-energy form: $T=E-mc^2\ge\bigl(mc^2+2\mu c^2+\frac{\mu^2c^2}{2m}\bigr)-mc^2=2\mu c^2+\frac{\mu^2c^2}{2m}$; for $\mu=m$ this gives $T\ge2mc^2+\frac{mc^2}{2}=\frac{5mc^2}{2}$ and, adding $mc^2$, $E\ge\frac{7mc^2}{2}$. [step 3.1]

5.1 Summary: for a conserving causal on-shell datum with a projectile and a co-moving target of equal mass $m$ and an outgoing massive side of total mass $2m+\mu$, the projectile energy in the target frame must satisfy $E\ge mc^2+2\mu c^2+\frac{\mu^2c^2}{2m}$, equivalently $T\ge2\mu c^2+\frac{\mu^2c^2}{2m}$, reducing to $E\ge7mc^2/2$ and $T\ge5mc^2/2$ at $\mu=m$; these are necessary kinematic thresholds under the adopted balance, not a claim that any process occurs. [step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Statement refuted

The four-momentum of an ideal massless particle is obtained by setting $m=0$
in $P=mU$, where $U$ is a future timelike four-velocity with
$\eta(U,U)=-c^2$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the affine Minkowski model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; $c>0$; an inertial
frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$; a future timelike $U$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$
([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]); the observer quantities
$E_n$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] for a future
unit observer $n$.

[F1] ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], Definition): $\eta$ is a symmetric
bilinear form on $V$, so $\eta(v,0)=0$ and $\eta(0,0)=0$ for all $v$, and
$\eta(\lambda v,\mu w)=\lambda\mu\,\eta(v,w)$ for real $\lambda,\mu$; in an
$\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis $\eta(e_0,e_0)=-1$, $\eta(e_1,e_1)=1$ and
$\eta(e_0,e_1)=0$.

[F2] ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], Definition): $v$ is
timelike when $\eta(v,v)<0$, null when $v\ne0$ and $\eta(v,v)=0$, spacelike
when $\eta(v,v)>0$, and the zero vector is none of timelike, null or
spacelike.

[F3] ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], Definition): an inertial
frame's basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\eta$-orthonormal with $e_0\in C^+$, so
$e_0$ is future timelike and $\eta(e_0,e_0)=-1$.

[F4] ([[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], Statement): in an
$\eta$-orthonormal basis whose first vector is timelike,
$\mathrm{cl}(C^+)=\{v:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ for the naming of $C^+$ containing the
first vector, where $v=v^0e_0+v_s$ and $|v_s|=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}$.

[F5] ([[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], Definition): a vector
is future null when it is nonzero, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v$ lies in
$\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$, and future causal when it is future timelike or future
null.

[F6] ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], Definition):
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$ for $P\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$.

[F7] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (a)): for
nonzero future causal $P$, $E_n(P)>0$ and, for future null $P$,
$E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|$.

## Counterexample

1.1 The case $m=0$: for the future timelike $U$ one has $0\cdot U=0$, so the massive formula at $m=0$ produces the zero vector; by [F1] and [F6], $\eta(0,0)=0$ and $E_n(0)=-c\,\eta(0,n)=0$, and by [F2] the zero vector is not a nonzero future null vector since it is not null (nullity requires $P\ne0$). [F1, F2, F6]

1.2 The witness of a genuine massless momentum: in the inertial frame of [F3] choose $E>0$ and set $P:=(E/c)(e_0+e_1)$. Then [F1] gives $\eta(P,P)=(E/c)^2\bigl(\eta(e_0,e_0)+2\eta(e_0,e_1)+\eta(e_1,e_1)\bigr)=(E/c)^2(-1+0+1)=0$ and $P\ne0$; its coordinates are $(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)=(E/c)(1,1,0,0)$, so $v^0=E/c=|v_s|$ and [F4] places $P$ in $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$; hence $P$ is future null by [F5]. Moreover $E_{e_0}(P)=-c\,\eta(P,e_0)=-(E)\bigl(\eta(e_0,e_0)+\eta(e_1,e_0)\bigr)=E>0$ by [F1] and [F6], in agreement with [F7]. [F1, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7]

2.1 The case $m>0$: for every $m>0$, [F1] gives $\eta(mU,mU)=m^2\eta(U,U)=-m^2c^2<0$, so $mU$ is timelike by [F2]; if $mU=P$ then $\eta(mU,mU)=\eta(P,P)=0$, a contradiction with $mU$ timelike. Therefore no $m>0$ produces the future null witness $P=mU$, and by [step 1.1] no $m=0$ does either: no value $m\ge0$ in the massive formula $P=mU$ produces the massless momentum $P$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 Combining the two cases, the statement is refuted: setting $m=0$ in $P=mU$ gives the zero vector, which is not a nonzero future null four-momentum and has zero energy in every frame, while a nonzero future null four-momentum such as the witness of [step 1.2] is not of the form $mU$ for any $m\ge0$. A massless four-momentum is therefore a separate model primitive, not the degenerate case of the massive formula. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

## Statement refuted

The kinetic energy $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ of a massive particle is a property of
the particle alone, independent of the observer $n$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the affine Minkowski model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; $c>0$; $m>0$;
$w=(3c/5,0,0)$; $U=\gamma(c,w)$ with $\gamma=5/4$; $P=mU$; the observers
$n_1=e_0$ of the displayed inertial frame and $n_2=U/c$.

[F1] ([[ex-sr-four-momentum-at-beta-three-fifths]], Example): with
$w=(3c/5,0,0)$ and $\gamma=5/4$ the four-momentum $P=mU$ has
$E_{e_0}(P)=5mc^2/4$, spatial momentum $(3mc/4,0,0)$ and kinetic energy
$T_{e_0}(P)=mc^2/4$.

[F2] ([[ex-sr-four-momentum-boost-to-rest]], Example): in the frame obtained by
the passive boost with parameter $3/5$ along $e_1$ one has $E'=mc^2$,
$\mathbf p'=0$, the mass shell $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=m^2c^4$, and that frame
is the particle's rest frame, its four-velocity being $c\,e'_0$.

[F3] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (b)): for
$P=mU$ with $m>0$, $U$ future timelike with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and $n$ future
unit, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ with $\gamma=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$, and
$T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $U=cn$.

[F4] ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], Definition):
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and $E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$; the invariant mass
$m(P)$ depends on the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone and hence on no observer.

[F5] ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], clause (c)): a point
observer of the model at an event is a future unit timelike vector $n$ with
$\eta(n,n)=-1$, and the four-velocity of the observer's own worldline is $cn$;
the four-velocity $U$ of the particle satisfies $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$
([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(a)).

[F6] ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], Definition): $\eta$ is bilinear, so
$\eta(n_2,n_2)=c^{-2}\eta(U,U)=-1$ for $n_2=U/c$.

## Counterexample

1.1 Two observers: $n_1=e_0$ is future unit by definition of an inertial frame, and $n_2=U/c$ satisfies $\eta(n_2,n_2)=c^{-2}\eta(U,U)=-1$ by [F5] and [F6] and is future timelike; both are point observers of the particle in the sense of [F5], and $n_1\ne n_2$ because $U=\gamma(c,w)\ne c\,e_0$ has nonzero spatial part. [F5, F6]

1.2 Kinetic energies: in the frame of $n_1=e_0$, [F1] gives $T_{n_1}(P)=mc^2/4\ne0$; for $n_2=U/c$ one has $U=cn_2$, so [F3] gives $\gamma=-\eta(n_2,n_2)=1$ and $T_{n_2}(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)=0$. [F1, F3]

1.3 Energies and mass: $E_{n_1}(P)=5mc^2/4$ by [F1] and $E_{n_2}(P)=mc^2$ by [F2]; the invariant mass is $m(P)=m$ in both cases, depending on the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone by [F4]. [F2, F4]

2.1 The same particle and the same vector $P$ therefore have kinetic energy $mc^2/4$ for the observer $n_1$ and kinetic energy $0$ for the observer $n_2$, while $P$ and the invariant mass $m$ are unchanged; hence the displayed statement is false: $T_n(P)$ depends on the observer $n$, and so does $E_n(P)$ ($5mc^2/4$ versus $mc^2$), whereas the invariant mass does not. [step 1.2, step 1.3]

3.1 The refutation is complete: two future unit observers of the same massive particle give different values of $T_n(P)$ and of $E_n(P)$, so neither quantity is a property of the particle alone, while the invariant mass $m(P)=m$ is the same in both frames. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1] ∎

## Definition

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $c>0$ be the model's positive numerical constant, and let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set.

(a) A **stress-energy tensor** on $\Omega$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge0$ (with $C^0$ meaning continuous), is a $C^k$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field $T$ on $\Omega$ in the sense of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]: at every $p\in\Omega$ the map $T(p):V^*\times V^*\to\mathbb R$ is bilinear and symmetric, so in every inertial chart its components satisfy $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)).

(b) In each inertial chart $x$ of the model ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) define the component families $\varepsilon_x:=T^{00}$, $\pi_x^i:=T^{0i}/c=T^{i0}/c$ and $S_x^{ij}:=T^{ij}$. These are numerical component and scaling conventions involving the fixed positive number $c$; their transformation behaviour is inherited from $T$ and no physical units or measurement interpretation form part of this mathematical definition.

(c) When $k\ge1$, the **four-force density** of $T$ is the $C^{k-1}$ field whose inertial components are $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$, where $\partial_a$ are the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] and the sum over $a$ is the standard contraction of a contravariant index with a coordinate derivative. The components $\partial_aT^{ab}$ transform as a vector, so $f$ is a well-defined vector field on $\Omega$ independent of the inertial chart: under an inertial transition $x'=\Lambda x+a$ the components satisfy $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=\Lambda^b{}_d\,\partial_cT^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iv)), which is exactly the vector transformation law of clause (i) applied to the components $f^b$. For $k\ge1$ one says that $T$ is **locally conserved**, or **balanced**, on $\Omega$ when $f=0$ on $\Omega$, and that $T$ is **balanced against the four-force density** $f$ when $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$.

(d) The definition asserts no conservation of any prescribed symmetric field $T$: whether a given $T$ is conserved, whether it arises from an action or a matter model, and whether any of its integrals over a slice converges are separate hypotheses stated elsewhere. No choice principle is used. For a merely continuous tensor ($k=0$) the component conventions and pointwise contractions of (b) are defined, while the divergence, the four-force density and the balance terminology of (c) require the additional $C^1$ hypothesis; no derivative of a merely continuous field is asserted.

## Remarks

The symmetry condition in (a) is chart-independent by the rank-two component law ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)): if $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ in one inertial chart, then $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}=\Lambda^b{}_d\Lambda^a{}_cT^{dc}=T'^{ba}$ in every other. The constants $\varepsilon_x,\pi_x,S_x$ of (b) are numerical component conventions only; the physical readings of such components — energy density, momentum density, stress, force density — are model premises adopted separately in [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]] and used in [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]. Nothing in this definition requires the metric contraction $\eta_{ab}T^{ab}$ to have a sign, requires any energy condition, or asserts that a locally conserved field is the total stress-energy of an isolated system.

## Statement

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, $\Omega\subseteq A$ open, and let $T$ be a continuous symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]). Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest projection $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ and $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c). At a point $p\in\Omega$ define $\varepsilon:=T^{ab}n_an_b$, $\pi^a:=-c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$ and $S^{ab}:=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}$. Then: (a) $\pi$ lies in $n^\perp$, $S$ is symmetric and horizontal in both slots ($S^{ab}n_b=n_aS^{ab}=0$), and $$T^{ab}=\varepsilon\,n^an^b+c\,(n^a\pi^b+\pi^an^b)+S^{ab}.$$ (b) Contracting with $n$ gives $T^{ab}n_b=-\varepsilon n^a-c\pi^a$; hence $\varepsilon$ and $\pi$ are determined by $T$ and $n$, and the decomposition is unique among decompositions $T^{ab}=\varepsilon' n^an^b+c(n^a\pi'^b+\pi'^an^b)+S'^{ab}$ with $\pi'\in n^\perp$ and $S'$ symmetric horizontal: $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon$, $\pi'=\pi$, $S'=S$. (c) In any adapted inertial orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$, the numerical components of this decomposition are $\varepsilon=T^{00}$, $\pi^0=0$, $\pi^i=T^{0i}/c$ and $S^{0a}=S^{a0}=0$, $S^{ij}=T^{ij}$ for $i,j=1,2,3$. Define isotropic rest stress to mean $S^{ab}=p h^{ab}$ for a real scalar $p$, where $h^{ab}:=\eta^{ab}+n^an^b$. Thus $S=0$ means vanishing rest stress, and is the isotropic case $p=0$; isotropy permits any $p$, including nonzero pressure or tension. These are numerical tensor identities. Physical adoption of the energy/momentum-density reading is a separate model premise; this mathematical lemma asserts no observer measurement. No choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with inertial chart $x$, its constant metric components $\eta_{ab}$, the inverse components $\eta^{ab}$ and the index conventions of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]] and [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]; a continuous symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field $T$ on $\Omega$ ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]], [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]); a future unit vector $n\in V$, so $n_an^a=\eta(n,n)=-1$, with $n^\perp=\{v:\eta(n,v)=0\}$ and $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)). All components below are taken at one fixed point and the components $T^{ab}$ are those of $T$ in an inertial chart.

[F1] Rest-space projector. The map $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ is linear and idempotent, has image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\operatorname{span}(n)$, satisfies $h(n)=0$ and $\eta(n,h(v))=0$ for all $v$; in components $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$, so $h^a{}_bn^b=0=n_a h^a{}_b$ and $h^a{}_ch^c{}_b=h^a{}_b$. ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c))

[F2] Component conventions and symmetry: $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$, $\delta^a{}_b=h^a{}_b-n^an_b$, and index lowering commutes with the algebra. ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]])

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Projector identities. From [F1], $n_an^a=-1$; $h^a{}_bn^b=0$, $n_ah^a{}_b=0$ and $h^a{}_ch^c{}_b=h^a{}_b$; moreover $\delta^a{}_c=h^a{}_c-n^an_c$. [F1, given]

2.1 Expansion and horizontality. Using $\delta^a{}_c\delta^b{}_d=(h^a{}_c-n^an_c)(h^b{}_d-n^bn_d)$ from step 1.1 and the symmetry $T^{cd}=T^{dc}$ of [F2], expand $$T^{ab}=(h^a{}_c-n^an_c)(h^b{}_d-n^bn_d)T^{cd}=S^{ab}-n^b\,h^a{}_cT^{cd}n_d-n^a\,h^b{}_dT^{dc}n_c+n^an^b\,n_cn_dT^{cd};$$ with the definitions of $\varepsilon$, $\pi$ and $S$ this is $T^{ab}=S^{ab}+c\,n^b\pi^a+c\,n^a\pi^b+\varepsilon\,n^an^b$. Moreover $\pi\in n^\perp$ because $n_a\pi^a=-c^{-1}n_ah^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c=0$, and $S$ is symmetric because $h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}=h^b{}_dh^a{}_cT^{dc}$; finally $S^{ab}n_b=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}n_b=0$ and $n_aS^{ab}=0$ by step 1.1, so $S$ is horizontal in both slots. This proves (a). [F2, step 1.1]

2.2 Frame components (c). In an adapted inertial orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$ one has $n^a=\delta^a_0$ and $n_a=-\delta_a^0$; hence $h^0{}_0=0$, $h^0{}_j=h^i{}_0=0$ and $h^i{}_j=\delta^i_j$ for $i,j=1,2,3$. Substituting into the definitions gives $\varepsilon=T^{00}$; $\pi^a=-c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c=c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{b0}$, so $\pi^0=0$ and $\pi^i=T^{i0}/c=T^{0i}/c$; and $S^{ab}=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}$ gives $S^{0a}=S^{a0}=0$ and $S^{ij}=T^{ij}$. [step 1.1, given]

3.1 Contraction and uniqueness (b). Contracting the expansion of step 2.1 with $n_b$ and using step 1.1, $T^{ab}n_b=\varepsilon\,n^a(n_bn^b)+c\,(n^a\pi^bn_b+\pi^a\,n_bn^b)+S^{ab}n_b=-\varepsilon n^a-c\pi^a$. If $T^{ab}=\varepsilon'n^an^b+c(n^a\pi'^b+\pi'^an^b)+S'^{ab}$ is another decomposition with $\pi'\in n^\perp$ and $S'$ symmetric horizontal, then contracting with $n_an_b$ gives $\varepsilon'=T^{ab}n_an_b=\varepsilon$, contracting with $n_b$ and comparing with the identity just proved gives $-c\pi'^a=-\varepsilon n^a-\varepsilon'(-n^a)-c\pi^a=-c\pi^a$, hence $\pi'=\pi$ as $c>0$; then $S'=T-\varepsilon n\otimes n-c(n\otimes\pi+\pi\otimes n)=S$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, given]

4.1 Clauses (a), (b) and (c) are proved in steps 2.1, 3.1 and 2.2. The isotropic rest stress $S^{ab}=ph^{ab}$ is a definition, with $p=0$ exactly when $S=0$; the identities hold at every point of $\Omega$ and use only that $T$ is a continuous symmetric $(2,0)$ field, while the physical reading of $\varepsilon$, $\pi$ and $S$ as measured energy density, momentum density and stress is a separate model premise not asserted here. No choice principle is used. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎
