## Statement

Under the matter premises of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]: (a) If $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field solving the adopted field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$, then the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]) satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$, in every inertial chart. (b) If $\rho>0$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted dust equations, then $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely if $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ and $\rho>0$ then the dust equations hold. (c) If $\varepsilon,P$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted fluid equations, then $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely conservation of that $T$ implies the two fluid equations. (d) For a $C^1$ symmetric tensor field prescribed on $\Omega$ that is not obtained from one of the adopted models together with its field equations, no conservation is asserted; a conservation statement about such a field is an additional explicit premise. (e) The theorem is a conditional deduction from the adopted model equations; it asserts no interaction, force law, cross section, measurement or empirical fact, and its conclusions inherit the scope of the postulate. Under the already stated homogeneous dust reading, the tensor boost computation has the conditional physical interpretation $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho$. For comoving identical massive particles with fixed rest mass $m$, rest number density $\nu$ and $\rho=\nu mc^2$, a rest rectangular parcel has boosted simultaneous volume $1/\gamma$ times its rest volume (the parallel length contracts and transverse lengths are unchanged), so its particle density is $\gamma\nu$; the adopted massive-particle reading gives each particle energy $\gamma mc^2$. Thus the two factors in $\gamma^2\rho$ correspond respectively to particle energy and volume/density. This is conditional model interpretation for that homogeneous particle realization, not a derivation of the continuum from microscopic dynamics, a claim about arbitrary tensors, or empirical evidence.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with inertial chart $x$ and its index conventions ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), the adopted matter model equations and readings of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]], the particle premises and homogeneous dust reading of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], and the force-density/conservation terminology of [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]] (conservation of a $C^1$ symmetric field $T$ means $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$, and the force density is chart-independent).

[F1] Scalar divergence identity: for the smooth scalar field and Hilbert tensor of the adopted model, $\partial_aT^{ab}=K(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi))\partial^b\varphi$; in particular any solution of $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ has conserved Hilbert tensor. ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]], [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]])

[F2] Dust equivalence: for $C^1$ $\rho>0$ and a $C^1$ future unit field $n$, $\partial_a(\rho\,n^an^b)=0$ if and only if $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$. ([[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]])

[F3] Perfect-fluid identity: for the field $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$, $\partial_aT^{ab}=n^b(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta)+((\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP)$, and $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ if and only if both bracket expressions vanish. ([[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]])

[F4] Massive-particle reading: a particle of rest mass $m$ and four-velocity $U=m^{-1}P$ has energy $E=\gamma mc^2$ in a frame where its speed parameter is $v$ with $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; a rest rectangular parcel's parallel length contracts by the factor $1/\gamma$ while transverse lengths are unchanged. ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]], [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]], [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]])

[F5] Transformation laws: under an inertial transition the components of a $C^1$ type-$(2,0)$ field transform by the rank-two law $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$, and its coordinate divergence transforms as a vector, $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=\Lambda^b{}_c\partial_aT^{ac}$, so conservation is a chart-independent statement. ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]], [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii),(iv))

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Clause (a). The adopted scalar model includes the field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$; [F1] then gives $\partial_aT^{ab}=K\cdot0\cdot\partial^b\varphi=0$ on $\Omega$. By [F5] the vanishing is independent of the inertial chart in which the components are computed. [F1, F5, given]

1.2 Clause (b). The adopted dust model is exactly the pair of equations $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$ with $\rho>0$; the forward direction of [F2] gives $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ for $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$, and the reverse direction gives that conservation with $\rho>0$ implies both equations. [F2, given]

1.3 Clause (c). The adopted fluid model is the pair of equations obtained by setting both bracket expressions of [F3] to zero; by the equivalence in [F3] this is exactly $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ for $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$, in both directions. [F3, given]

1.4 Clause (d). The definition [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]] states explicitly in its clause (d) that it asserts no conservation of any prescribed symmetric field, and the present theorem derives conservation only from the adopted model equations of clauses (a)–(c); accordingly for a $C^1$ symmetric field prescribed on $\Omega$ that is not obtained from one of the adopted models together with its field equations, no conservation is asserted, and any conservation statement about such a field would be an additional explicit premise. [given]

1.5 Clause (e), conditional homogeneous-dust reading. Consider a homogeneous dust realization with comoving identical particles of rest mass $m>0$ and rest number density $\nu>0$, so that the adopted reading gives $\rho=\nu mc^2$, and consider a rest rectangular parcel of rest volume $V_0$. Take the tensor $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$ in the rest frame, where $n=e_0$, so that $T^{00}=\rho$ and all other components vanish. The passive boost with parameter $\beta$ along the parcel's motion direction has $\Lambda^0{}_0=\gamma$ and is proper orthochronous ([[def-lorentz-boost]]), so the rank-two law of [F5] gives $T'^{00}=\Lambda^0{}_a\Lambda^0{}_bT^{ab}=(\Lambda^0{}_0)^2\rho=\gamma^2\rho$; thus $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\nu mc^2=(\gamma mc^2)(\gamma\nu)$. In a frame related to the rest frame by that boost the simultaneous volume of the parcel is $V_0/\gamma$ by the length-contraction part of [F4] (parallel length $1/\gamma$, transverse lengths unchanged), so the particle number density in that frame is $\nu'=N/(V_0/\gamma)=\gamma\nu$; by the massive-particle reading [F4] each particle carries energy $\gamma mc^2$. Hence the two factors in $\gamma^2\rho$ correspond respectively to particle energy and volume/density in the boosted frame. This is a conditional interpretation of the factorization within the homogeneous particle realization; it is not a derivation of the continuum model from microscopic dynamics. [F4, F5, given]

2.1 Clauses (a), (b), (c) and (d) are steps 1.1–1.4 and clause (e) is step 1.5. Every conservation conclusion is a conditional deduction from the adopted model equations; the theorem asserts no interaction, force law, cross section, measurement or empirical fact, contains no empirical premise and makes no claim about arbitrary prescribed tensors. All choices are finite; no choice principle is used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 1.5] ∎

## Statement

Let $x$ be an inertial chart, let $\bar K$ be a closed spatial box and $s_1<s_2$, and let $T$ be the total stress-energy tensor of a system in the situation of [[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]]: $T$ is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$, satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ there (for the adopted models this is the conclusion of [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]; for any other system it is an explicit premise), and satisfies the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces for $i=1,2,3$. Put $Q^b(s):=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ and $P^b:=Q^b/c$. Then: (a) $Q^b(s)$ is finite for every $s\in[s_1,s_2]$ and $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$; (b) consequently $P^b$ is independent of $s\in[s_1,s_2]$; if $P$ is future timelike, its invariant mass $\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$ is independent of $s$ as well; (c) if the side flux does not vanish, the exact balance is the finite-flux identity of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]], and no conservation is asserted; (d) no transformation law for $P^b$ under a change of inertial chart or slicing is asserted: without an admissible-region flux argument, $P^b$ is a chart-component integral and is not claimed to be a four-vector; no noncompact, asymptotic or gravitational-energy statement is made, and the reading of $P^b$ as the system's four-momentum is the model's interpretation of the integral, not a measurement.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with inertial chart $x$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), a closed spatial box $\bar K$, times $s_1<s_2$, and the total tensor $T$ of the isolation premise [[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]] with its stated hypotheses; $Q^b(s)=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ and $P^b=Q^b/c$; the conservation of $T$ is either the conclusion of [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]] for the adopted models or an explicit premise for any other system.

[F1] Finite-flux theorem: for a $C^1$ symmetric field on a neighbourhood of the box, $Q^b(s)=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ is finite and continuous in $s$, and for $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$ the slice balance $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K}\partial_aT^{ab}\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big)$$ holds; if the force density vanishes on $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$ and $T^{ib}=0$ on the side faces, then $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$. ([[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(b),(c), [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]])

[F2] Total four-momentum and invariant mass: for a vector $P=\sum_bP^be_b$ built from a chase of chart components $P^b$, if $P$ is future timelike then its invariant mass is $\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c>0$, and if $P$ is future null the convention assigns mass $0$. ([[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]])


## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Clause (a). By the isolation premise, $T$ is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$; [F1] applied to this box gives that $Q^b(s)$ is finite and continuous for every $s\in[s_1,s_2]$, and since $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on the box and the zero side-flux condition holds on its spatial faces, the balance identity of [F1] reduces to $Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=0$, i.e. $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$. [F1, given]

1.2 Clauses (c) and (d). If the side flux does not vanish, the exact statement available is the full balance identity of [F1] with its side-flux terms; the derivation above never establishes the vanishing of the differences, so no conservation of $Q^b$ is asserted in that case. The argument is carried out entirely in one inertial chart: $Q^b$ is defined by the chart components $T^{0b}$ of $T$ and no transformation law for $Q^b$ or $P^b$ under a change of chart or of slicing is used or claimed; the identification of $P^b$ with the system's four-momentum is the model's reading of the integral, not a measurement, and no noncompact or asymptotic limit is taken. [F1, given]

2.1 Clause (b). Evaluating clause (a) with $(s_1,s_2)$ replaced by any pair $r<s$ in $[s_1,s_2]$ gives $Q^b(s)=Q^b(r)$ for all $r,s$ in the interval, so $Q^b$ is constant there and $P^b=Q^b/c$ is constant as well. Form the vector $P:=\sum_bP^be_b$ in the frame of the chart; since the components are constant in $s$, $\eta(P,P)$ is a constant real number, so if $P$ is future timelike its invariant mass $\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$ is independent of $s$, and if it is future null the assigned mass $0$ is likewise independent. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Clauses (a) and (b) are steps 1.1 and 2.1 and clauses (c) and (d) are step 1.2. The theorem is a finite conditional deduction on one box in one inertial chart; it asserts no four-vector transformation law, no noncompact or gravitational-energy statement and no measurement; for the adopted models the conservation hypothesis is supplied by [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]], and for any other system it is an explicit premise of the isolation postulate. All choices are finite; no choice principle is used. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Two force carriers

The force vocabulary of this framework has two distinct mathematical carriers. On a massive particle worldline the four-force is $F=\dot P=dP/d\tau$ ([[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]]), and its identities are conditional on the adopted particle dynamics [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]. In the continuum the force carrier is the four-force density $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ of a symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]). Neither object is a force law: the definition of $\dot P$ asserts no equation of motion, and the definition of $f$ asserts no conservation and no interaction.

## Conservation is conditional

The page's conservation statements are conditional deductions. Local conservation of the scalar, dust and fluid tensors is proved from the adopted model equations of [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]; for any other matter the conservation of $T$ must be adopted or derived separately, and no conservation is asserted for an arbitrary prescribed symmetric field. Integrated conservation additionally requires the isolation premise of [[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]] and is asserted only for finite boxes and slices in one inertial chart [[pthm-sr-integrated-conservation-for-isolated-matter]]; it does not supply a four-vector transformation law for the slice integrals and does not extend to noncompact regions.

## Exclusions

The framework contains no gravity, no electromagnetic coupling, no derivation of an equation of state, no energy conditions — the printed dominant-energy-condition inequality of the Crowell source p. 191 is defective and is not used — no angular-momentum theorem and no empirical premise; no measurement, apparatus or uncertainty claim is made anywhere on this page. The energy conditions, the electromagnetic field stress tensor and its coupling to charged matter, and angular-momentum flux are developed, if at all, by other frameworks or pairs of the library, not here.

## Example

In an inertial frame $x$ let dust at rest have constant rest coefficient $\rho>0$, so $T^{ab}=\rho\,\delta^a_0\delta^b_0$ and the only nonzero component is $T^{00}=\rho$. Under the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along the $x^1$ axis with parameter $\beta$, $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, the primed components are $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2\beta\rho,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2\beta^2\rho,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=0,$$ all other components zero; equivalently $T'=\rho\,n'\otimes n'$ with $n'$ the image of $e_0$ under the boost.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and chart $x$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]); $\rho>0$ constant; the field $T^{ab}=\rho\,\delta^a_0\delta^b_0$, which is $C^1$, symmetric and constant; the passive boost along $e_1$ with parameter $\beta\in(-1,1)$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[def-rational-power]]).

[F1] Rank-two component law: under the inertial transition $x'=\Lambda x+a$ the components transform as $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$; the boost is proper orthochronous with inverse $B(-\beta)$. ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii), [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]])

[F2] Conservation terminology: a constant symmetric field has vanishing force density $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=0$, and dust tensors $\rho\,n\otimes n$ with constant future unit $n$ and constant $\rho>0$ are conserved by the dust equivalence. ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]], [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]])

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Boosted components. The boost matrix has $\Lambda^0{}_0=\gamma$, $\Lambda^0{}_1=\Lambda^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$, $\Lambda^1{}_1=\gamma$ and preserves the other two spatial directions ([[def-lorentz-boost]]). Since $T^{ab}=\rho\,\delta^a_0\delta^b_0$, [F1] gives $T'^{ab}=\rho\,\Lambda^a{}_0\Lambda^b{}_0$; using $\Lambda^0{}_0=\gamma$, $\Lambda^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$, $\Lambda^2{}_0=\Lambda^3{}_0=0$ this is $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho$, $T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2\beta\rho$, $T'^{11}=\gamma^2\beta^2\rho$ and $T'^{22}=T'^{33}=T'^{02}=T'^{03}=T'^{12}=T'^{13}=0$. [F1, given]

2.1 Factorization and conservation. The primed components are exactly those of $\rho\,n'\otimes n'$ with $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$, $n'^2=n'^3=0$: indeed $\eta(n',n')=-\gamma^2+\gamma^2\beta^2=-1$ and $n'^0>0$, so $n'$ is future unit and is the image of $e_0$ under the boost. All primed components are constant in the primed chart, so $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=0$, consistent with the dust equivalence [F2] applied to the constant unit field $n'$ and constant $\rho>0$. [F2, given, step 1.1]

3.1 The primed coordinate coefficient $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho$ is the numerical factorization $\gamma^2\rho=\gamma\cdot(\gamma\rho)$; its source interpretation as one energy factor and one volume factor belongs to the separately adopted dust model reading and is not proved by this component computation. The example is a component computation and asserts no interaction, no dynamics and no measurement. [step 2.1] ∎

## Example

Let $T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$ be the perfect-fluid tensor of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]], with $n$ future unit. In an inertial frame in which $n=e_0$ (fluid at rest) the components are $T^{00}=\varepsilon$, $T^{11}=T^{22}=T^{33}=P$ and all other components zero. Under the passive boost along $x^1$ with parameter $\beta$, $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, the primed components become $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta^2+P,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=P,$$ all remaining components zero, and the observer contraction $T^{ab}(e_0')_a(e_0')_b=T'^{00}$ differs from $\varepsilon$ by $(\gamma^2-1)(\varepsilon+P)$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with inertial frame and chart $x$, constant $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]); $C^1$ data $\varepsilon,P$, a future unit field $n$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]); the perfect-fluid field $T$ of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; the passive boost along $e_1$ with $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $|\beta|<1$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]], [[def-rational-power]]).

[F1] Rank-two component law $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$ under the inertial transition. ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii))

[F2] Observer decomposition: for a continuous symmetric field $T$ and future unit observer $n$ the contraction $\varepsilon=T^{ab}n_an_b$ is the energy density component of the unique observer decomposition, and in an adapted frame with $n=e_0$ it equals $T^{00}$. ([[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]])

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Rest-frame components. With $n=e_0$, $n^a=\delta^a_0$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$: $T^{00}=(\varepsilon+P)(n^0)^2+P\eta^{00}=(\varepsilon+P)-P=\varepsilon$; $T^{ii}=(\varepsilon+P)(n^i)^2+P\eta^{ii}=0+P=P$ for $i=1,2,3$; and $T^{0i}=(\varepsilon+P)n^0n^i+P\eta^{0i}=0$. [given]

2.1 Observer contraction in the rest frame. By [F2] applied to the observer $e_0$ the contraction is $\varepsilon=T^{ab}(e_0)_a(e_0)_b=T^{00}$, consistent with step 1.1. [F2, step 1.1]

2.2 Boosted components. The boost matrix has $\Lambda^0{}_0=\Lambda^1{}_1=\gamma$, $\Lambda^0{}_1=\Lambda^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$ and preserves the other two spatial directions. Substituting the rest-frame components of step 1.1 into [F1] and summing the nonzero terms gives $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\varepsilon+\gamma^2\beta^2P=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P$, $T'^{01}=\gamma(-\gamma\beta)\varepsilon+(-\gamma\beta)\gamma P=-\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta$, $T'^{11}=\gamma^2\beta^2\varepsilon+\gamma^2P=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta^2+P$, $T'^{22}=T'^{33}=P$, $T'^{23}=0$ and $T'^{02}=T'^{03}=T'^{12}=T'^{13}=0$. ## Example

Let $|\beta|<1$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$. In an inertial chart let $n$ be the constant field with components $n^0=\gamma$, $n^1=\gamma\beta$, $n^2=n^3=0$, and let $\rho(t,x)=\rho_0(x^2,x^3)$ be a positive $C^1$ function of the transverse coordinates only. Then $(\rho,n)$ satisfies the dust equations and $T^{ab}=\rho\,n^an^b$ is a conserved dust stress-energy field whose slice integrals over finite boxes are constant, even though its $x^1$-face flux need not vanish.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with inertial chart $x$ and constant $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]); $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}>0$ ([[def-rational-power]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]); the constant field $n=(\gamma,\gamma\beta,0,0)$ and the positive $C^1$ profile $\rho=\rho_0(x^2,x^3)$; $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$.

[F1] Dust equivalence: for a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ and $C^1$ $\rho>0$, the field $T^{ab}=\rho\,n^an^b$ is conserved, $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$, if and only if $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; under conservation every integral curve of $n$ is an affine straight line. If only $\rho\ge0$ is assumed, the inertial-flow conclusion is asserted on $\{\rho>0\}$. ([[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]])

[F2] Slice balance: $Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K}f^b\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^3\big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K_i^+}T^{ib}-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K_i^-}T^{ib}\big)$ for finite boxes. ([[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(b), [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]])

[F3] A constant field has vanishing partial derivatives, since each coordinate partial derivative is the derivative of a constant one-variable restriction. ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]])

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 $(n,\rho)$ satisfies the dust equations. By the definitions of $\gamma$ and the Minkowski metric, $\eta(n,n)=-(n^0)^2+(n^1)^2=-\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=-1$, and $n^0=\gamma>0$ in the chart's time orientation, so $n$ is a future unit timelike constant field; by [F3] $\partial_an^b=0$ and hence $n^a\partial_an^b=0$. The profile depends only on $x^2,x^3$, so $n^a\partial_a\rho=\gamma(\partial_0\rho+\beta\partial_1\rho)=0$; and $\partial_an^a=0$, so $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=n^a\partial_a\rho+\rho\,\partial_an^a=0$. By [F1] the field $T^{ab}=\rho\,n^an^b$ is conserved. [F1, F3, given]

1.2 Nonnegative variant and support. If $\rho_0\ge0$ is allowed to vanish, the same equations $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$ hold, and [F1] gives conservation, with the inertial-flow statement on $\{\rho_0>0\}$; a compactly supported nonnegative transverse profile gives the same exact solution and the same finite-box constancy. The profile is independent of $x^1$, so a nonzero profile is not compactly supported in all three spatial variables; the flow lines are $x^1=\beta x^0+\text{const}$, $x^2,x^3$ constant. [F1, given]

2.1 Finite slice integrals are constant. Let $\bar K=[c_1,d_1]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$ and $Q^b(s)=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$. Since $T^{0b}=\rho\,n^0n^b=\gamma n^b\rho_0(x^2,x^3)$ is independent of $x^0$, each $Q^b(s)$ is constant in $s$. The same conclusion follows from [F2]: the force density vanishes by step 1.1, the transverse face terms vanish because $T^{2b}=T^{3b}=0$, and the two $x^1$-faces carry the same pointwise integrand $T^{1b}=\rho_0\gamma\beta n^b$ and enter with opposite signs, so their contributions cancel although the individual face flux need not vanish. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 The example exhibits a family of exact conserved dust solutions of the stated form with transverse profile and finite-box constancy of the slice integrals; it asserts no interaction, no dynamics of the profile beyond the displayed equations and no measurement. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Example

In an inertial chart $x$ of the affine Minkowski model with orthonormal basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval (the range of the coordinate $x^1$) and let $\rho,P:J\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$. Define the symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field $$T^{ab}(x):=\rho(x^1)\,e_0^ae_0^b+P(x^1)\,e_1^ae_1^b$$ on an open set $\Omega$ whose $x^1$-coordinates fill $J$ (a static uniaxial stress field along the $e_1$ direction, with $P<0$ representing tension). This is a $C^1$ symmetric stress-energy field in the sense of [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The inertial chart $x$ with coordinate partials $\partial_a$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), the interval $J$, the $C^1$ functions $\rho,P$, and the field $T$ above; in these components $e_0^a=\delta^a_0$ and $e_1^a=\delta^a_1$.

[F1] Force density and conservation terminology: for a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field $T$, the four-force density is the field with components $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$, and $T$ is locally conserved on $\Omega$ exactly when $f=0$ there. ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]])

[F2] If $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an interval and $g:I\to\mathbb R$ is continuous on $I$ and differentiable at every interior point with $g'=0$ there, then $g$ is constant on $I$. ([[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]])

[F3] Constant functions have zero partial derivatives, and the coordinate partial derivatives are the derivatives of the corresponding one-variable restrictions. ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]])

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Components of the force density. The components of $T$ are $T^{00}=\rho(x^1)$, $T^{11}=P(x^1)$ and $T^{ab}=0$ for all other pairs; these are $C^1$ in $x$, so the force density exists and has components $f^0=\partial_0T^{00}+\partial_1T^{10}=\partial_0\rho(x^1)=0$, $f^1=\partial_0T^{01}+\partial_1T^{11}=P'(x^1)$, and $f^2=f^3=0$, because the omitted terms involve the zero components and $\rho,P$ do not depend on $x^0$. [F1, F3, given]

2.1 Conservation is equivalent to constancy of $P$. By construction the set of values $x^1(p)$, $p\in\Omega$, is exactly the interval $J$ on which $\rho,P$ are defined. By step 1.1 and [F1], $T$ is conserved on $\Omega$ if and only if $P'=0$ at every interior point of $J$; by [F2] this holds if and only if $P$ is constant on $J$. The energy density $\rho$ is subject to no such condition: $\rho'$ never enters the divergence, because the only term containing $\rho$ is $T^{00}$, whose first index is contracted with $\partial_0$ and which is independent of $x^0$. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Consequently, a static uniaxial stress in equilibrium has uniform stress $P$ along the stressed direction, while its energy density may vary; when $P<0$ (tension) the tension must be constant. This is a component computation for the stated field; it asserts no material model, no equation of state and no force law. [step 2.1] ∎

## Example

In an inertial chart $x$ on affine Minkowski space ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]) define the smooth symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field by $T^{00}=x^0$, $T^{01}=T^{10}=x^1$, $T^{11}=x^0$, with every other component zero. This example computes its force density and checks the finite-box balance identity of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] on an explicit box with a nonzero net side flux.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The inertial chart with constant metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), the coordinate partial derivatives $\partial_a$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), the field $T$ above, and real numbers $t_1<t_2$, $x_1<x_2$, $c_2<d_2$, $c_3<d_3$; set $A:=(d_2-c_2)(d_3-c_3)>0$ and $B:=[t_1,t_2]\times[x_1,x_2]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$.

[F1] The box identity of the finite-flux theorem: for a $C^1$ symmetric field $T$ on a neighbourhood of $B$, $\int_Bf^b\,d^4x=\sum_a(\int_{F_a^+}T^{ab}\,d^3x-\int_{F_a^-}T^{ab}\,d^3x)$ with $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ and $F_a^\pm$ the faces $x^a=d_a,c_a$ of $B$. ([[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(a), [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]])

[F2] Coordinate derivatives: $\partial_0x^0=1$, $\partial_1x^1=1$, $\partial_0x^1=\partial_1x^0=0$, and partial derivatives of a function of one coordinate vanish in the other coordinates, as one-variable derivatives of the coordinate restrictions. ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]])

[F3] Riemann integrals of functions of a single coordinate over a box factor as the product of the one-dimensional integral and the transverse volume; constant integrals equal the constant times the volume. ([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]])

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Force density. By [F2], $f^0=\partial_0T^{00}+\partial_1T^{10}=1+1=2$, $f^1=\partial_0T^{01}+\partial_1T^{11}=0+0=0$ and $f^2=f^3=0$; hence $\int_Bf^0\,d^4x=2\operatorname{vol}(B)=2A(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$ by [F3], and the $b=1,2,3$ bulk integrals vanish. [F2, F3, given]

2.1 The $b=0$ identity. The temporal faces contribute $\int_{F_0^+}T^{00}-\int_{F_0^-}T^{00}=A\int_{x_1}^{x_2}x^0\Big|_{t_2}dx^1-A\int_{x_1}^{x_2}x^0\Big|_{t_1}dx^1=A(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$; the faces with $a=1$ contribute $\int_{F_1^+}T^{10}-\int_{F_1^-}T^{10}=A\int_{t_1}^{t_2}x^1\Big|_{x_2}dx^0-A\int_{t_1}^{t_2}x^1\Big|_{x_1}dx^0=A(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$; the transverse faces vanish because $T^{2b}=T^{3b}=0$. The sum of face differences is $2A(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$, equal to the bulk integral of step 1.1, verifying [F1] for $b=0$. [F1, F3, step 1.1]

2.2 The $b=1$ identity and the remaining components. For $b=1$, the temporal faces contribute $\pm A\int_{x_1}^{x_2}x^1\,dx^1$ with opposite signs, which cancel, and the faces with $a=1$ contribute $\pm A\int_{t_1}^{t_2}x^0\,dx^0$, which also cancel; the transverse faces vanish. Both sides of [F1] vanish, and the same is immediate for $b=2,3$ because all relevant components are zero. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 Numerical specialization: for transverse area $A=6$, temporal length $t_2-t_1=2$ and axis-one length $x_2-x_1=3$, the bulk integral is $2\cdot6\cdot2\cdot3=72$ and the two nonzero face differences are each $6\cdot2\cdot3=36$, whose sum is $72$. The example verifies the finite-box identity on a field with nonzero force density and nonzero net side flux; it asserts no matter model, no dynamics and no empirical fact. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Example

Let $k\ne0$ be a null covector, $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$, with $k^\sharp$ future, let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$, and let $\varphi(x):=f(k_ax^a+\theta_0)$ in an inertial chart; take $V\equiv0$ and $K>0$. Then $\varphi$ solves the massless scalar-field equation of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]], and its Hilbert stress-energy tensor is the conserved tensor $$T^{ab}=Kf'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)^2\,k^ak^b,$$ a nonnegative multiple of the rank-one future-null tensor $k^\sharp\otimes k^\sharp$ wherever $f'\ne0$ and the zero tensor wherever $f'=0$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with inertial chart $x$, constant $\eta_{ab}=\eta^{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), coordinate partials $\partial_a$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); a nonzero null covector $k$ with $k^\sharp$ future ($k^ak_a=0$, $k^a=\eta^{ab}k_b\ne0$, $k^0>0$) ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]); smooth $f$, $\theta:=k_ax^a+\theta_0$; $V\equiv0$, $K>0$; $\varphi=f\circ\theta$, a smooth scalar field ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

[F1] Chain rule: $\partial_a\varphi=f'(\theta)k_a$ and $\partial_a\partial_b\varphi=f''(\theta)k_ak_b$. ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]])

[F2] Scalar-field equation and Hilbert tensor: the field equation of the model with potential $V$ is $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$, and the Hilbert tensor of the density with this $V$ is $T^{ab}=K[\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab}(\tfrac12\partial_d\varphi\partial^d\varphi+V(\varphi))]$. ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]], [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]])

[F3] Divergence identity: $\partial_aT^{ab}=K(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi))\partial^b\varphi$; consequently any solution of the field equation has conserved Hilbert tensor. ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]])

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The field solves the massless equation. By [F1], $\partial_a\varphi=f'(\theta)k_a$ and $\partial_a\partial_b\varphi=f''(\theta)k_ak_b$; hence $\Box\varphi=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi=f''(\theta)\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$, because $k$ is null. With $V\equiv0$ this is exactly the scalar-field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ of [F2]. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 The stress-energy tensor. Substituting [F1] into the Hilbert formula of [F2] with $V\equiv0$ gives $\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi=f'(\theta)^2k^ak^b$ and $\partial_d\varphi\partial^d\varphi=f'(\theta)^2k_dk^d=0$, hence $T^{ab}=Kf'(\theta)^2k^ak^b$, which is symmetric. Wherever $f'(\theta)\ne0$ the coefficient $Kf'(\theta)^2$ is positive and $T$ is a positive multiple of the rank-one tensor $k^\sharp\otimes k^\sharp$ with nonzero future null generating vector $k^\sharp$; wherever $f'(\theta)=0$ all components vanish. For every future unit $n$, $T^{ab}n_an_b=Kf'(\theta)^2(k_an^a)^2\ge0$; in the inertial frame, $T^{00}=Kf'(\theta)^2(k^0)^2\ge0$ with $k^0>0$. [F1, step 1.1, given]

2.2 Conservation. Since $\varphi$ solves the field equation by step 1.1, [F3] gives $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$: the plane-wave tensor is conserved on the whole chart domain. [F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The example is an explicit conditional computation for the massless scalar model with a null plane-wave profile; it asserts no wave observation, no energy condition beyond the displayed nonnegativity and no measurement. [step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Statement refuted

If a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field $T$ is locally conserved, $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$, on a chart domain, then every finite axis-parallel slice integral $Q^b(s)=\int_KT^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ of it is independent of the slice parameter $s$; no separate side-flux hypothesis is needed.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An inertial chart $x$ on all of affine Minkowski space with constant metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) and coordinate partial derivatives $\partial_a$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). A field is balanced when its force density $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ vanishes ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]).

[F1] Slice balance: for $C^1$ $T$, $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$ and a finite axis-parallel box $[s_1,s_2]\times K$, $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K}f^b\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big),$$ with $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ and $K_i^\pm$ the faces $x^i=d_i$, $x^i=c_i$ of $K$. ([[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(b))

[F2] Coordinate partial derivatives of the coordinate functions: $\partial_0x^0=1$, $\partial_1x^1=1$, $\partial_0x^1=\partial_1x^0=0$, as one-variable derivatives of the coordinate restrictions. ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]])

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The field. Define the smooth symmetric field by $T^{00}=x^0$, $T^{01}=T^{10}=-x^1$, $T^{11}=x^0$, all other components zero. By [F2] its force density has components $f^0=\partial_0x^0+\partial_1(-x^1)=1-1=0$, $f^1=\partial_0(-x^1)+\partial_1x^0=0$ and $f^2=f^3=0$; hence $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on all of affine Minkowski space and $T$ is locally conserved. [F2, given]

2.1 The slice integral is not conserved. Let $L>0$, $c_2<d_2$, $c_3<d_3$, put $A=(d_2-c_2)(d_3-c_3)>0$ and $K=[0,L]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$, and let $Q^0(s)=\int_KT^{00}(s,x)\,d^3x=A\int_0^Lx^0(s)\,dx^1=ALs$. ## Statement refuted

Every $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field of the form $T^{ab}=F\eta^{ab}$, with $F$ a $C^1$ real function on a nonempty connected open chart domain $\Omega$ of the affine Minkowski model, is locally conserved on $\Omega$; in particular, writing a prescribed stress-energy tensor in the manifestly covariant form $F\eta^{-1}$ in every inertial chart would force its local conservation.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with an inertial chart $x$ and coordinate partial derivatives $\partial_a$, an inertial orthonormal frame with $\eta_{ab}=\eta^{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\eta^{ab}=\eta^{ba}$ constant in the chart ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), a nonempty connected open $\Omega\subseteq A$, and $F:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

[F1] Force density and conservation terminology: for a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field $T$, the four-force density is the vector field with components $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$, and $T$ is locally conserved on $\Omega$ exactly when $f=0$ on $\Omega$. ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]])

[F2] A function with continuous partial derivatives on an open set is totally differentiable there. ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]])

[F3] On a nonempty connected open subset of $\mathbb R^m$, a totally differentiable map has identically zero derivative if and only if it is constant. ([[thm-zero-derivative-on-connected-open-euclidean-set-iff-constant]])

[F4] Derivative rules: constant multiples of differentiable functions are differentiable with the constant pulled out. ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]])

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Force density of $F\eta^{-1}$. Since the components $\eta^{ab}$ are constant in the inertial chart, differentiating componentwise by [F4] gives $f^b=\partial_a(F\eta^{ab})=\eta^{ab}\partial_aF=\partial^bF$. Because the matrix $\eta^{ab}$ is invertible (it is the inverse of the nondegenerate form $\eta$), $f=0$ on $\Omega$ if and only if $\partial_aF=0$ for every $a$. [F1, F4, given]

2.1 Conservation forces constancy. By [F2] the $C^1$ function $F$ is totally differentiable, with derivative the covector of its partial derivatives; if $f=0$, step 1.1 gives $DF=0$, and [F3] gives that $F$ is constant on the connected open set $\Omega$; conversely a constant $F$ has $f=0$ by step 1.1. Hence $T=F\eta^{-1}$ is conserved exactly for constant $F$, and for nonconstant $F$ the continuous force density $f=\nabla F$ is not identically zero although it may vanish at points. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

2.2 Explicit witness. On $\Omega=\mathbb R^4$ (identified with an inertial chart) take $F(x)=(x^1)^2$, which is smooth and nonconstant. Then $\partial_0F=\partial_2F=\partial_3F=0$ and $\partial_1F=2x^1$, so $f=(0,2x^1,0,0)$: it vanishes exactly on the hyperplane $x^1=0$ and is nonzero at every point off that hyperplane. Thus the prescribed field $T^{ab}=F\eta^{ab}$ has nonzero force density on a nonempty open subset of $\Omega$, so it is not locally conserved, although $f$ vanishes at some points. [given, step 1.1]

3.1 Covariance does not imply conservation. Under an inertial transition $x'=\Lambda x+a$ with $\Lambda$ a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), the components of the same tensor transform by the rank-two law $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)); writing $F'(x'):=F(\Lambda^{-1}(x'-a))$ for the scalar, one gets $T'^{ab}=F'\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_d\eta^{cd}=F'\eta^{ab}$, because $\Lambda\eta^{-1}\Lambda^{\mathsf T}=\eta^{-1}$ for a Lorentz matrix. So the expression $F\eta^{-1}$ is manifestly covariant; yet by step 2.1 its local conservation is equivalent to constancy of the scalar $F$, which covariance does not require. [step 2.1]

4.1 The field of step 2.2 is a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field of the form $F\eta^{-1}$ on the connected open set $\mathbb R^4$ that is not locally conserved, refuting the statement. The example shows that covariance of a prescribed tensor expression and conservation of that tensor are independent properties: conservation is an additional premise. The prescribed field is not claimed to be the stress-energy tensor of any matter model of this page and no choice principle is used. [step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎

## Definition

Let $c > 0$ and let $x : I \to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline in the affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]) with four-velocity $U = dx/d\tau$ and four-acceleration $A = dU/d\tau$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), so that $\eta(U,U) = -c^2$ and $\eta(U,A) = 0$ pointwise, and $A(\tau)$ is spacelike whenever it is nonzero ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a),(b)).

**(a) Definition.** The **proper acceleration** of $x$ at the parameter value $\tau$ is the real number

$$a(\tau) := \sqrt{\eta(A(\tau),A(\tau))},$$

the nonnegative square root of [[def-rational-power]]. This is well defined for every $\tau \in I$. Indeed, fix an inertial chart of $A$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]); since $x$ is $C^2$, the component functions of $A$ are continuous, and $\eta(A,A)$ is a sum of products of continuous component functions, hence continuous, by [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]]. If $A(\tau) = 0$ then $\eta(A,A) = 0$ at $\tau$, and if $A(\tau) \neq 0$ then $A(\tau)$ is spacelike and $\eta(A,A) > 0$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); in both cases the argument of the square root is nonnegative, so $a(\tau)$ is a well-defined nonnegative real number for every $\tau \in I$. With the SI coordinate and unit conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], in which $x^0 = c t$ with $t$ in seconds and the spatial coordinates are in metres while $\eta$ has the dimensionless matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ in an inertial chart, the components of $A$ carry the unit metre per second squared and $\eta(A,A)$ carries the unit $(\text{metre per second squared})^2$, so $a$ carries the unit metre per second squared. The worldline is **uniformly accelerated** when $a$ is constant on $I$.

**(b) Agreement with the acceleration of a congruence.** Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset of $A$ and let $n : \Omega \to V$ be an observer congruence with acceleration field $a_{\mathrm{cg}} := \nabla_n n$, where $\nabla$ is the flat covariant derivative of [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (b)). If $x$ is a flow line of $n$ and $U = c n$ along $x$, then $A = c^2 a_{\mathrm{cg}}$ along $x$: the derivative along the worldline of the field $n$ is the covariant derivative $\nabla_{dx/d\tau} n = \nabla_{cn} n = c \nabla_n n = c\, a_{\mathrm{cg}}$, by the defining properties of the flat covariant derivative along curves ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] (d)), so $A = d(c n)/d\tau = c\, \nabla_{dx/d\tau} n = c^2 a_{\mathrm{cg}}$. Consequently $a = c^2 \sqrt{\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})}$ along $x$: the proper acceleration is $c^2$ times the magnitude of the congruence acceleration. In particular the proper acceleration of a congruence worldline is determined by the congruence field alone, and such a worldline is uniformly accelerated exactly when $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})$ is constant along it.

**(c) Reading and scope.** This item defines a quantity of the model and fixes its name, its unit and its physical reading. The model reads $a(\tau)$ as the magnitude that an ideal accelerometer carried along the worldline would register at $\tau$; this ideal-instrument identification is adopted with the model in the same sense as the framework's ideal-clock reading of proper time and is not derived here. No accelerometer response law, calibration, frequency dependence, force law or interaction is specified or asserted; the definition asserts nothing about which bodies follow which worldlines; no measurement outcome and no statistical, uncertainty or empirical claim is made. No choice principle is used.

## Remarks

- **Nonnegativity is the content of the well-definedness clause.** The projection of the four-acceleration on the orthogonal complement of the four-velocity is spacelike or zero ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (b)), so $\eta(A,A) \ge 0$ always, and $a$ vanishes exactly at the parameter values where $A = 0$, i.e. at the events where the worldline has vanishing four-acceleration. Nothing in the definition presumes that such events exist, or fail to exist.
- **The definition is stable under a change of proper-time origin only.** In this model the proper time of a worldline is unique up to an additive constant ([[def-sr-proper-time]]); $a$ is a function of $\tau$, so a translation of the origin translates $a$ without changing its values, and no other reparametrization is used in this definition.

## Statement

Let $c > 0$ and $\alpha > 0$, set $R := c^2/\alpha$, and let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski space with an inertial chart $x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, $x^0 = c t$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Let $x: \mathbb R \to A$ be the curve $x(\tau) := x^{-1}(R \sinh \theta, R \cosh \theta, 0, 0)$, where $\theta := \alpha \tau/c$.

(a) **Regularity, causal character and parametrization.** $x$ is $C^\infty$, and $x'(\tau) = c(\cosh \theta, \sinh \theta, 0, 0)$ is future timelike for every $\tau$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]), so $x$ is a future timelike worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]). Since $\eta(x',x') = -c^2$ is constant, the parameter $\tau$ is a proper-time parameter of the curve: the proper-time function $\tau$ of [[def-sr-proper-time]] satisfies $\tau(b) - \tau(a) = b - a$ for all $a < b$ in $\mathbb R$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]), and the four-velocity is $U := dx/d\tau = c(\cosh \theta, \sinh \theta, 0, 0)$ with $\eta(U,U) = -c^2$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a)).

(b) **Constant four-acceleration magnitude.** The four-acceleration $A := dU/d\tau = \alpha(\sinh \theta, \cosh \theta, 0, 0)$ satisfies $\eta(A,A) = \alpha^2$ and $\eta(U,A) = 0$. The chart coordinate velocity is $dx^1/dt = c \tanh \theta$, so $|dx^1/dt| < c$ for every $\tau$, and $x^1 = R \cosh \theta > R|\sinh \theta| = |x^0|$ for every $\tau$: the worldline lies in the right wedge $W := \{x^1 > |x^0|\}$ and its speed in the chart tends to $c$ only as $\tau \to \pm\infty$.

(c) **Rindler flow line.** Let $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z) := (\rho \sinh \theta, \rho \cosh \theta, y, z)$ on $\mathbb R \times (0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^2$ and let $n := \rho^{-1} \partial_\theta$ be the Rindler congruence of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b), whose pullback metric is $-\rho^2 d\theta^2 + d\rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2$ and whose congruence acceleration $a_{\mathrm{cg}} := \nabla_n n$ is $\rho^{-1} \partial_\rho$, with $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}}) = \rho^{-2}$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]]). Then $x$ is exactly the flow line $\Phi(\cdot, R, 0, 0)$ reparametrized by $\theta = \alpha \tau/c$, and along $x$ one has $A = c^2 a_{\mathrm{cg}}$: the four-acceleration of the worldline is $c^2$ times the congruence acceleration, and $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}}) = 1/R^2 = \alpha^2/c^4$ on the flow line $\rho = R$.

(d) **Asymptotic behaviour.** Along $x$ one has $x^1 - x^0 = R e^{-\theta} \to 0$ with $x^0 \to +\infty$ as $\tau \to +\infty$, and $x^1 + x^0 = R e^{\theta} \to 0$ with $x^0 \to -\infty$ as $\tau \to -\infty$: the worldline approaches each of the null planes $\{x^1 = x^0\}$ and $\{x^1 = -x^0\}$ asymptotically without meeting either, and the chart coordinate speed tends to $c$ at both ends.

(e) **Scope.** This is an exact kinematic computation in the affine model. It uses no force law, no mass, no clock hypothesis and no empirical input; beyond identifying the displayed parameter with the proper time of the curve, only the flow parametrization of the congruence is used. The curve is not asserted to be a geodesic and no statement is made about the forces that would maintain it. No choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with fixed $c>0$; an inertial chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with $x^0=ct$ and orthonormal basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]); $\alpha>0$, $R=c^2/\alpha$, $\theta=\alpha\tau/c$, and the curve $x(\tau)=x^{-1}(R\sinh\theta,R\cosh\theta,0,0)$ for $\tau\in\mathbb R$.

[L1] Model and chart: $x(p)=E^{-1}(p-o)$ for the frame isomorphism $E$, so specifying the four coordinates determines the event, and vector components are read in the orthonormal basis $(e_a)$ in which $\eta$ has matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L2] Differentiability of a curve $x:I\to A$ is defined through its coordinate representation $x_A\circ x$, with $x'(\tau)=E((x_A\circ x)'(\tau))$; the curve is $C^k$ when the coordinate map is ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (a)).

[L3] $\sinh u=(e^u-e^{-u})/2$, $\cosh u=(e^u+e^{-u})/2$, $\tanh u=\sinh u/\cosh u$, and $\cosh u>0$ for all real $u$ ([[def-hyperbolic-functions]]).

[L4] $\cosh^2u-\sinh^2u=1$, $(\sinh u)'=\cosh u$, $(\cosh u)'=\sinh u$, $\sinh$ is odd, $\cosh$ is even, $\tanh:\mathbb R\to(-1,1)$ is strictly increasing and onto, and $\tanh u\to\pm1$ as $u\to\pm\infty$ ([[thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives]]).

[L5] Differentiability and the chain rule: the derivative of a composite with an affine inner map is the product, $(\sinh\circ g)'=(\cosh\circ g)g'$, and sums, scalar multiples and products of differentiable functions are differentiable with the usual rules ([[def-derivative]], [[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]).

[L6] Coordinate criterion: in any inertial chart, $C^+=\{v:v^0>|v_s|\}$ and $\bar C^+=\{v:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$, where $v^0$ is the time component and $|v_s|$ the Euclidean norm of the spatial part ([[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]] (a)).

[L7] Causal classification: a vector $v$ is timelike if $\eta(v,v)<0$, spacelike if $\eta(v,v)>0$, and each nonzero timelike vector is future or past but not both ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

[L8] Proper time: for a $C^1$ future timelike worldline $x$, $\tau(b)-\tau(a)=c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x'(u),x'(u))}\,du$, defined up to an additive constant ([[def-sr-proper-time]]).

[L9] Proper-time parametrization: $\tau$ is $C^1$ and strictly increasing with $\tau'(s)=c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}>0$; the reparametrized curve $x\circ\rho$ has tangent $x'(s)/\tau'(s)$ at the proper-time parameter, and the derivative formula is the four-velocity ([[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]] (i),(iii),(iv)).

[L10] Four-velocity and four-acceleration: $U=x'/\tau'=cx'/\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$, and for $C^2$ curves $A=U'/\tau'$ is the derivative of $U$ with respect to the proper-time parameter ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] (a),(b)); $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and $\eta(U,A)=0$ with $A$ spacelike wherever it is nonzero ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a),(b)).

[L11] Observer congruence: a $C^1$ field $n$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ has future timelike flow lines; its acceleration field is $a_{\mathrm{cg}}=\nabla_nn$ with $\eta(n,a_{\mathrm{cg}})=0$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (b),(e)).

[L12] Covariant derivative along curves: for a $C^1$ curve $y$ and $C^1$ field $W$ along it, $\nabla_{\dot y}W$ is the ordinary derivative of $W\circ y$ in the canonical identification, and $\nabla_{fX}Y=f\nabla_XY$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] (a),(d)).

[L13] Rindler congruence: $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z)=(\rho\sinh\theta,\rho\cosh\theta,y,z)$ is a smooth bijection onto the right wedge $W$ with pullback metric $-\rho^2d\theta^2+d\rho^2+dy^2+dz^2$; $n=\rho^{-1}\partial_\theta$ is future unit timelike, Born rigid and irrotational, with $a_{\mathrm{cg}}=\rho^{-1}\partial_\rho$ and $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})=\rho^{-2}$ ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b)).

[L14] Exponential limits: $e^u\to+\infty$ as $u\to+\infty$ and $e^u\to0$ as $u\to-\infty$ ([[thm-exponential-limits-and-range]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (The tangent.) Writing $x$ in the chart, the coordinate functions are $\tau\mapsto R\sinh(\alpha\tau/c)$, $\tau\mapsto R\cosh(\alpha\tau/c)$, and the two constants $0$; differentiating with the chain rule and the hyperbolic derivative formulas gives $x'(\tau)=(R\frac{\alpha}{c}\cosh\theta,\,R\frac{\alpha}{c}\sinh\theta,\,0,\,0)=(c\cosh\theta,\,c\sinh\theta,\,0,\,0)$, because $R\alpha/c=c$ by $R=c^2/\alpha$. In particular the coordinate functions are $C^\infty$, since each derivative has the same form with $\sinh$ and $\cosh$ exchanged. [L1, L2, L3, L4, L5, algebra]

1.2 (Elementary hyperbolic identities.) From the exponential definitions, $\cosh\theta-\sinh\theta=e^{-\theta}$ and $\cosh\theta+\sinh\theta=e^{\theta}$; combined with $\cosh^2\theta-\sinh^2\theta=1$ and $\cosh\theta>0$ this gives $\cosh\theta>|\sinh\theta|\ge0$, hence $|\tanh\theta|<1$ for every $\theta$. [L3, L4, algebra]

1.3 (The curve is a Rindler flow line.) Substituting $\rho=R$, $y=z=0$ into $\Phi$ gives $\Phi(\theta,R,0,0)=(R\sinh\theta,R\cosh\theta,0,0)=x(\tau)$ with $\theta=\alpha\tau/c$; hence $x$ is exactly the flow line $\Phi(\cdot,R,0,0)$, reparametrized by the affine map $\tau\mapsto\theta=\alpha\tau/c$, and at $\rho=R$ the Rindler field is $n=R^{-1}\partial_\theta$ with acceleration $a_{\mathrm{cg}}=R^{-1}\partial_\rho$. [L1, L13, given]

2.1 ($x$ is a $C^\infty$ regular future timelike worldline.) By step 1.1 the coordinate functions are $C^\infty$, so $x$ is $C^\infty$ by [L2]; $\eta(x',x')=c^2(-\cosh^2\theta+\sinh^2\theta)=-c^2<0$ by step 1.2 and the matrix of $\eta$ in the frame, so $x'$ is timelike; and its time component is $x'^0=c\cosh\theta>c|\sinh\theta|=|(x')_s|$ by step 1.2, so $x'\in C^+$ by the coordinate criterion [L6]. Hence $x'$ is future timelike and nonzero, and $x$ is a future timelike worldline. [L6, L7, step 1.1, step 1.2]

2.2 (Chart speed and the wedge.) The chart time is $x^0=ct$ with $x'^0=c\cosh\theta$, so $dt/d\tau=\cosh\theta$ and, by step 1.1, $dx^1/dt=(dx^1/d\tau)/(dt/d\tau)=c\sinh\theta/\cosh\theta=c\tanh\theta$; step 1.2 gives $|dx^1/dt|=c|\tanh\theta|<c$. Also $x^1=R\cosh\theta>R|\sinh\theta|=|x^0|$ by step 1.2, so the worldline lies in $W=\{x^1>|x^0|\}$. [L1, L3, step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 (Proper-time parametrization and four-velocity.) By step 2.1 the curve is a $C^1$ future timelike worldline, so its proper-time function is $\tau(b)-\tau(a)=c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}\,du=c^{-1}\int_a^bc\,du=b-a$ by [L8] and step 2.1; thus the given parameter is a proper-time parameter of $x$ up to an additive constant, in agreement with [L9]. Consequently the four-velocity is $U=x'/\tau'=c(\cosh\theta,\sinh\theta,0,0)$ by [L10] and step 1.1, and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. [L8, L9, L10, step 1.1, step 2.1]

3.2 (Asymptotics.) From the addition formulas in exponential form of step 1.2, $x^1-x^0=R(\cosh\theta-\sinh\theta)=Re^{-\theta}$ and $x^1+x^0=R(\cosh\theta+\sinh\theta)=Re^{\theta}$, both strictly positive for every $\tau$. As $\tau\to+\infty$ we have $\theta\to+\infty$, so $e^{-\theta}\to0$ by [L14] and $x^0=R\sinh\theta\to+\infty$; as $\tau\to-\infty$ we have $\theta\to-\infty$, so $e^{\theta}\to0$ and $x^0\to-\infty$. Hence the worldline approaches both null planes asymptotically and meets neither. The chart speed satisfies $c\tanh\theta\to\pm c$ at the two ends by the limit statement of [L4]. [L4, L14, step 1.2, step 2.2]

4.1 (The four-acceleration and its magnitude.) Differentiating each component of $U$ in the proper-time parameter $\tau$ with the chain rule and the hyperbolic derivative formulas gives $A=U'=c(\sinh\theta,\cosh\theta,0,0)\tfrac{\alpha}{c}=\alpha(\sinh\theta,\cosh\theta,0,0)$. Then $\eta(A,A)=\alpha^2(-\sinh^2\theta+\cosh^2\theta)=\alpha^2$ and $\eta(U,A)=c\alpha(-\cosh\theta\sinh\theta+\sinh\theta\cosh\theta)=0$ by step 1.2; the second identity is consistent with [L10]. [L4, L5, L10, step 1.2, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 (Identification of the four-acceleration with $c^2a_{\mathrm{cg}}$.) Along $x$ one has $dx/d\tau=cn$ by steps 1.3 and 3.1 with $n=R^{-1}\partial_\theta$; since $n(\theta)$ is the ordinary derivative of $\Phi(\cdot,R,0,0)$, the covariant derivative of the field $n$ along the flow line is the ordinary derivative $\nabla_{dx/d\tau}n$, and by [L12] and [L11] it equals $\nabla_{cn}n=c\nabla_nn=ca_{\mathrm{cg}}$. Therefore $A=dU/d\tau=c\,d(n\circ x)/d\tau=c\nabla_{dx/d\tau}n=c^2a_{\mathrm{cg}}$. Substituting $\rho=R$ into $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})=\rho^{-2}$ from [L13] gives $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})=1/R^2=\alpha^2/c^4$. [L11, L12, L13, step 1.3, step 3.1]

5.1 (Scope.) Every step above is a finite-dimensional computation in the affine model from the cited definitional suppliers: the curve, its causal character, its proper-time parametrization, its four-acceleration, the identification $A=c^2a_{\mathrm{cg}}$ and the asymptotics. No force law, mass, geodesic property, clock hypothesis or empirical input was used, and no choice principle was used. [L11, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 4.2] ∎

## Statement

Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset of affine Minkowski space $A$, $c>0$, and let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field, $\eta(n,n)=-1$. Define the following first-order quantities in any inertial chart:

$$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b,\qquad h_{ab}:=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b,\qquad a^b:=n^c\partial_cn^b,\qquad\theta_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\partial_{(c}n_{d)},$$

where symmetrization means half the sum, $n_a:=\eta_{ab}n^b$, and $h(v,w):=h_{ab}v^aw^b$. Here $h$ is $C^1$ and $a,\theta$ are continuous. The rest projection $h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ is as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c). For $C^1$ fields and tensors define

$$(L_nh)_{ab}:=n^c\partial_ch_{ab}+h_{cb}\partial_an^c+h_{ac}\partial_bn^c.$$

These first-order coordinate formulas transform tensorially under affine inertial chart changes and agree, on smooth fields, with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] and the ordinary smooth Lie derivative. Say the $C^1$ field is **Born rigid** when $L_nh=0$; the identity $L_nh=2\theta$ makes this equivalent to $\theta=0$.

(a) Let $J$ be a nonempty open interval, $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ a nonempty open set, and $\Phi:J\times B\to\Omega$ an injective $C^2$ immersion with $\partial_s\Phi=n(\Phi)$. Put $e_I:=\partial_{\xi^I}\Phi$, $I=1,2,3$, and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi):=h(e_I,e_J)$ at $\Phi(s,\xi)$. Then $n,e_1,e_2,e_3$ are linearly independent, $G$ is symmetric positive definite at every point, and its entries are $C^1$. Thus for each $s$ it is a $C^1$ positive-definite material metric on $B$. If $n$ and $\Phi$ are smooth, $G$ is a smooth Riemannian metric, as in the original smooth branch.

(b) For all $I,J$,

$$\partial_sG_{IJ}=(L_nh)(e_I,e_J)=2\theta(e_I,e_J),\qquad\partial_\tau G_{IJ}=2c\theta(e_I,e_J),$$

where $\tau=s/c$ is the proper-time parameter along each flow line, whose four-velocity is $cn$. For a nonzero label direction $e_I$, put $\ell_I:=\sqrt{h(e_I,e_I)}>0$ and $u_I:=h(e_I)/\ell_I$. This $u_I$ is a horizontal unit rest vector, and

$$\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(u_I,u_I)\ell_I.$$

The alternative normalized material vector $e_I/\ell_I$ need not be horizontal, but has the same $\theta$ contraction because $\theta$ is horizontal. Positive/negative expansion gives positive/negative fractional change of this material rest length per proper time.

(c) If $\theta=0$, then $\partial_sG_{IJ}=0$ and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi)$ is constant in $s$ for each fixed label, with no restriction on material-label separation: the entire internal metric is preserved exactly. Conversely, a nonzero contraction $\theta(e_I,e_J)$ gives a nonzero derivative of that metric component at the point and hence nonconstancy on a neighbourhood. The smooth Born-rigid branch and its original conclusions are included.

(d) This is a local statement about the given family and its material metric. Integrating the material metric at a common flow parameter gives an internal label-space length; it does not identify that length with a finite endpoint distance on a single observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane without an additional argument. No matter model, elasticity, field equation, global rigidity theorem, boundary condition or choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with canonical identification $T_pA=V$, a nonempty open $\Omega\subseteq A$, a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n:\Omega\to V$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, an inertial chart, the first-order coordinate formulas of the statement, and, in (a)-(c), a nonempty open interval $J$, a nonempty open $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ and an injective $C^2$ immersion $\Phi:J\times B\to\Omega$ with $\partial_s\Phi=n(\Phi)$, with $e_I:=\partial_{\xi^I}\Phi$ and $G_{IJ}:=h(e_I,e_J)$.

[L1] The rest form and projection: $h(v,w)=\eta(v,w)+\eta(n,v)\eta(n,w)=\eta(h(v),h(w))$ with $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$; $h$ is symmetric with radical spanned by $n$ and is positive definite on $n^\perp$; the congruence acceleration $a:=\nabla_nn$ satisfies $\eta(n,a)=0$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (a),(b)).

[L2] Kinematic decomposition and Born rigidity: $\nabla_an_b=-n_aa_b+\theta_{ab}+\omega_{ab}$ with $\theta_{ab}=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}n_{d)}$ symmetric and horizontal in both slots, $\theta_{ab}n^b=n^a\theta_{ab}=0$, and $(L_nh)_{ab}=2\theta_{ab}$; Born rigidity, defined by $L_nh=0$, is therefore equivalent to $\theta=0$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (c),(d)).

[L3] In an inertial chart $\eta$ has constant components, $\partial_a\eta_{bc}=0$, and $(\nabla_XY)^a=X^b\partial_bY^a$; the same component formula and metric compatibility hold for $C^1$ data ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] (a),(c),(e)).

[L4] Derivatives of the components of a $C^1$ vector field $Y$ along a $C^1$ curve $y$ are ordinary derivatives, $(\nabla_{\dot y}Y)^a=\frac{d}{ds}(Y^a\circ y)$, and for $n$ future unit timelike the field $s\mapsto Y(y(s))$ is a $C^1$ field along $y$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] (d), [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]]).

[L5] Rest projection identities: $h\circ h=h$, $\operatorname{im}h=n^\perp$, $\ker h=\operatorname{span}(n)$, $h(n)=0$, $\eta(n,h(v))=0$, $v=-\eta(n,v)n+h(v)$, and $w\mapsto\sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$ is a norm on $n^\perp$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)).

[L6] Proper time: for a $C^1$ future timelike worldline $x$ one has $\tau(b)-\tau(a)=c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}\,du$; along a flow line of $n$ parametrized with tangent $x'=n$ this gives $d\tau/ds=1/c$, so $\partial_\tau=c\,\partial_s$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]]).

[L7] Four-velocity: $U=x'/\tau'=cx'/\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$; for a congruence flow line with $x'=n$ this is $U=cn$, and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] (a),(c), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a)).

[L8] Tensoriality: under an inertial chart change $x'=\Lambda x+b$ one has $J'^a=\Lambda^a_bJ^b$, $k'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b_ak_b$, $\partial'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b_a\partial_b$, and each contravariant index gains $\Lambda$ while each covariant index gains $\Lambda^{-1}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (i)-(iv)).

[L9] Total chain rule: for composable $C^1$ maps of open subsets of Euclidean spaces, $D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a)$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule]]).

[L10] Equality of mixed partials: for a $C^2$ map the second-order mixed partials in the two orders agree ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]).

[L11] Algebra of continuous functions: sums, scalar multiples and products of continuous real functions are continuous ([[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], claims 1 and 5), and sums, scalar multiples and products of differentiable functions are differentiable with $(fg)'=f'g+fg'$ ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], claim 3).

[L12] A continuous function on an order-convex interval whose derivative vanishes at every interior point is constant ([[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]]).

[L13] Smooth fields: the Lie bracket of smooth vector fields has coordinate components $[X,Y]^a=X^b\partial_bY^a-Y^b\partial_bX^a$, and for smooth data the coordinate expression of the Lie derivative of the covariant field $h$ is $n^c\partial_ch_{ab}+h_{cb}\partial_an^c+h_{ac}\partial_bn^c$ ([[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], [[prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket]], [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

[L14] Partial derivatives of a real function of several variables are defined by differentiating in one variable with the others fixed ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-derivative]]).

[L15] Model structure: $T_pA$ is canonically identified with $V$, so the differential of a map into $A$ may be read as a $V$-valued derivative ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Tensoriality and smooth agreement.) Fix an inertial chart and expand the definitions: $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$, $h_{ab}=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b$, $a^b=n^c\partial_cn^b$, $\theta_{ab}=\frac12h_a{}^ch_b{}^d(\partial_cn_d+\partial_dn_c)$, and $(L_nh)_{ab}=n^c\partial_ch_{ab}+h_{cb}\partial_an^c+h_{ac}\partial_bn^c$; under the inertial chart change the factors $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda^{-1}$ produced by [L8] contract pairwise with the Kronecker deltas, with the components of $n$ and of every derivative, so each displayed formula is a sum of products of components of $n$, of $\partial n$ and of the constant $\eta$, multiplied by the same index factors in the new chart; this is exactly the tensorial transformation law of [L8], and no connection terms appear by [L3]. [L3, L8, L9, L14]

1.2 (Two first-order identities.) Differentiating the identity $\eta(n,n)=-1$ in an inertial chart and using $\partial\eta=0$ of [L3] gives $2\eta_{ab}n^a\partial_cn^b=0$, that is $n_b\partial_cn^b=0$ for every $c$; contracting with $n^c$ and relabelling, $n^ca^c=n^c\eta_{ab}n^d\partial_dn^b=0$, so $a$ is $\eta$-orthogonal to $n$. Similarly, $h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\partial_cn_d=\partial_an_b+n_aa_b$: expand the two projectors, discard the two terms containing $n^d\partial_an_d$ and $n^cn^d\partial_cn_d$, both of which vanish by the first identity, and use $n^c\partial_cn_b=a_b$. [L1, L2, L3, L11, L14]

1.3 (Independence of the family directions.) Since $\Phi$ is an immersion, its differential $D\Phi(s,\xi)$ is injective at every point of $J\times B$, and the four partial derivatives $\partial_s\Phi,e_1,e_2,e_3$ are the columns of $D\Phi$; a linear relation $\mu\,\partial_s\Phi+\sum_I\lambda^Ie_I=0$ therefore has all coefficients zero. Substituting $\partial_s\Phi=n(\Phi(s,\xi))$ gives that $n(\Phi(s,\xi)),e_1,e_2,e_3$ are linearly independent at every point, so in particular $e_1,e_2,e_3$ are linearly independent and $\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)\cap\operatorname{span}(n(\Phi))=\{0\}$. [L15, given]

1.4 (The family is a congruence of worldlines; material fields.) For each fixed $\xi$ the curve $y_\xi(s):=\Phi(s,\xi)$ satisfies $y_\xi'(s)=n(\Phi(s,\xi))$, a nonzero future timelike vector with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ by [L1]; hence $y_\xi$ is a $C^1$ regular future timelike curve, and it is a future timelike worldline of the model. Its proper-time function satisfies $d\tau/ds=1/c$ and $\partial_\tau=c\partial_s$ by [L6]; the associated four-velocity is $U=cn$ by [L7]. For each $I$ the map $s\mapsto e_I(s,\xi)$ is a $C^1$ field along $y_\xi$ in the sense of [L4]. [L1, L4, L6, L7, given]

2.1 (The identity $L_nh=2\theta$.) Expanding $h_{ab}=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b$ and differentiating gives $(L_nh)_{ab}=n^c(n_a\partial_cn_b+n_b\partial_cn_a)+\partial_an_b+n_bn_c\partial_an^c+\partial_bn_a+n_an_c\partial_bn^c$; by the vanishing identities of step 1.2 this equals $\partial_an_b+\partial_bn_a+n_aa_b+n_ba_a$, which is twice the right-hand side of $2\theta_{ab}=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d(\partial_cn_d+\partial_dn_c)$ computed in step 1.2; hence $(L_nh)_{ab}=2\theta_{ab}$ and Born rigidity $L_nh=0$ is equivalent to $\theta=0$. [L2, L3, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 (Metricity of $G$ and its $C^1$ regularity.) $G_{IJ}(s,\xi)=h_{ab}(\Phi(s,\xi))e_I^a(s,\xi)e_J^b(s,\xi)$ is symmetric because $h$ is symmetric by [L1]. For $w=w^Ie_I\ne0$, $G(w,w)=h(w,w)=\eta(h(w),h(w))\ge0$ with equality if and only if $h(w)=0$, i.e. by [L5] if and only if $w\in\operatorname{span}(n(\Phi))$; step 1.3 shows that this forces $w=0$, so $G$ is positive definite at every point. Regularity: $\Phi$ is $C^2$, so the components of $e_I=\partial_{\xi^I}\Phi$ and of $\Phi$ are $C^1$ functions on $J\times B$; $n$ is a $C^1$ field, so the components $n_a(\Phi(s,\xi))$ are compositions of $C^1$ maps, and each $G_{IJ}$ is a sum of products of such $C^1$ functions, hence $C^1$ by [L11] applied componentwise with the partial derivatives of [L14]; when $n$ and $\Phi$ are smooth all these compositions and products are smooth. In particular, for each fixed $s$, $\xi\mapsto G_{IJ}(s,\xi)$ is a $C^1$ positive-definite Riemannian metric on $B$. [L1, L5, L11, L14, step 1.3, step 1.4, algebra]

2.3 (Derivative of the material directions.) On $J\times B$ the components satisfy $\partial_se_I^a=\partial_s\partial_{\xi^I}\Phi^a=\partial_{\xi^I}(n^a\circ\Phi)$, because the mixed partials of the $C^2$ map $\Phi$ commute by [L10] and $\partial_s\Phi=n(\Phi)$; applying the chain rule of [L9] to the composite $\xi\mapsto n^a(\Phi(s,\xi))$ with the other variables fixed gives $\partial_se_I^a=(\partial_bn^a)(\Phi)e_I^b$. Equivalently, $\partial_se_I=(\nabla_{e_I}n)(\Phi)$ by the component formula of [L3] for $C^1$ data. [L3, L9, L10, step 1.4]

3.1 (Evolution of the material metric.) Differentiate the product $G_{IJ}=h_{ab}(\Phi)e_I^ae_J^b$ with the product rule of [L11] and the total chain rule of [L9], using $\partial_s\Phi^c=n^c(\Phi)$ and step 2.3: $\partial_sG_{IJ}=(n^c\partial_ch_{ab})(\Phi)e_I^ae_J^b+h_{ab}(\Phi)(\partial_cn^a)(\Phi)e_I^ce_J^b+h_{ab}(\Phi)e_I^a(\partial_cn^b)(\Phi)e_J^c$. Relabelling the second term to $(h_{cb}\partial_an^c)(\Phi)e_I^ae_J^b$ and the third to $(h_{ac}\partial_bn^c)(\Phi)e_I^ae_J^b$ gives exactly $(L_nh)_{ab}(\Phi)e_I^ae_J^b$; by step 2.1 this is $2\theta_{ab}(\Phi)e_I^ae_J^b=2\theta(e_I,e_J)$, and multiplication by $\partial_\tau/\partial_s=c$ from [L6] gives $\partial_\tau G_{IJ}=2c\theta(e_I,e_J)$. [L6, L9, L11, step 2.1, step 2.3, algebra]

3.2 (Smooth branch.) If $n$ and $\Phi$ are smooth, step 2.2 gives that $G$ is a smooth metric on $B$ for each $s$; evaluating the $C^1$ formula of the statement, $(L_nh)_{ab}=n^c\partial_ch_{ab}+h_{cb}\partial_an^c+h_{ac}\partial_bn^c$ agrees with the ordinary smooth Lie derivative of the covariant field $h$ by [L13], and the identity $(L_nh)_{ab}=2\theta_{ab}$ of step 2.1 together with [L2] recovers the smooth congruence definitions of expansion and of Born rigidity. [L2, L13, step 2.1, step 2.2]

4.1 (Rest length and its fractional rate.) For a nonzero label direction $e_I$ put $\ell_I=\sqrt{G_{II}}>0$. Its $h$-normalized direction $u_I:=h(e_I)/\ell_I$ satisfies $h(u_I)=u_I$ and $h(u_I,u_I)=1$: indeed $h(h(v))=h(v)$ and $\eta(h(v),h(w))=h(v,w)$ by [L1] and [L5], with $\eta(h(e_I),h(e_I))=h(e_I,e_I)=\ell_I^2$, so $u_I$ is a horizontal unit vector. Because $\theta$ is horizontal and symmetric by [L2], $\theta(v,w)=\theta(h(v),h(w))$ for all $v,w$, so $\theta(e_I,e_I)=\ell_I^2\theta(u_I,u_I)$ and also $\theta(e_I/\ell_I,e_I/\ell_I)=\theta(u_I,u_I)$. Differentiating $\ell_I^2=G_{II}$ with the chain rule of [L9] and using step 3.1 gives $\partial_\tau\ell_I=(2\ell_I)^{-1}\partial_\tau G_{II}=c\theta(e_I,e_I)/\ell_I=c\theta(u_I,u_I)\ell_I$, which is the stated fractional rate. [L1, L2, L5, L9, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 (Born rigidity preserves the material metric exactly.) Suppose $\theta=0$ on the image of the family. Then by step 3.1 $\partial_sG_{IJ}(s,\xi)=0$ for every $(s,\xi)\in J\times B$. Fix $\xi\in B$; the function $s\mapsto G_{IJ}(s,\xi)$ is $C^1$ on the interval $J$ by step 2.2, hence continuous, with zero derivative at every point of $J$, so it is constant on $J$ by [L12]. As $I,J$ and $\xi$ were arbitrary, the entire internal metric $G$ is preserved exactly along each flow line, with arbitrary label separation. [L12, step 2.2, step 3.1]

4.3 (Nonrigidity gives local nonconstancy.) If $\theta(e_I,e_J)(s_0,\xi_0)\ne0$ at some point, then by step 3.1 $\partial_sG_{IJ}(s_0,\xi_0)=2\theta(e_I,e_J)(s_0,\xi_0)\ne0$; hence $G_{IJ}$ is not constant on any neighbourhood of $(s_0,\xi_0)$: a function that is constant near a point has vanishing derivative there. In particular the deformed metric component varies along the corresponding flow line. [step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 (Local nature and scope.) Everything proved was computed from the given family: the metric $G$ is obtained by evaluating $h$ on the material directions $e_I$ at the common flow parameter $s$ (equivalently $\tau=s/c$), so it is an internal label-space metric of the family. A finite endpoint distance on a single observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane would require a separate identification of a slice with the label space; no such identification, matter model, elasticity, field equation, global rigidity theorem or boundary condition has been used, and every step is a finite-dimensional algebraic or differential computation using only the cited suppliers, so no choice principle is used. [L6, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 4.2] ∎
