## Statement

Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and [[post-sr-causal-signal-propagation]], and the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] ($x^0 = c t$). Let $x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be the chart of an inertial frame ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) and let $W := \{x^1 > |x^0|\}$ be the right wedge. Let $\Phi$ and $n$ be the Rindler chart and congruence of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b): $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z) = (\rho \sinh \theta, \rho \cosh \theta, y, z)$ on $\mathbb R \times (0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^2$ with inverse $\rho = \sqrt{(x^1)^2 - (x^0)^2}$, $\theta = \frac12 \log((x^1+x^0)/(x^1-x^0))$, pullback metric $-\rho^2 d\theta^2 + d\rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2$, and acceleration field $a_{\mathrm{cg}} = \nabla_n n = \rho^{-1} \partial_\rho$. Fix $\rho_0 > 0$ and real $y_0,z_0$, and let $O$ be the congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_0$, $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$, parametrized by its proper time $\tau$ with $\theta = c \tau/\rho_0$; by [[def-sr-proper-acceleration]] its proper acceleration is $c^2/\rho_0$. Write $U(q) := q^0 + q^1$ and $V(q) := q^0 - q^1$ for events $q$, so that $U = \rho e^{\theta}$ and $V = -\rho e^{-\theta}$ on $W$, and write $\le$ and $J^+$, $J^-$ for the causal reachability relations of [[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]]. Then, conditionally on the adopted model:

(i) **Chart domain and light rays.** $\Phi$ is a smooth bijection of $\mathbb R \times (0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^2$ onto $W$ with the stated smooth inverse, so the chart domain is exactly $W$ and $\rho = 0$ is not part of its coordinate domain. The boundary of $W$ in the affine model is $\{x^1 = |x^0|\}$, with arbitrary $x^2,x^3$: it is the union of the two null half-planes $\{x^1 = x^0 \ge 0\}$ and $\{x^1 = -x^0 \ge 0\}$. These half-planes are portions of the full null planes appearing as causal horizons in (ii); the full planes are not the wedge boundary. Along the worldline $\rho = \rho_0$ one has $V = -\rho_0 e^{-\theta} \to 0^-$ and $U \to +\infty$ as $\theta \to +\infty$, while $U = \rho_0 e^{\theta} \to 0^+$ and $V \to -\infty$ as $\theta \to -\infty$. The future null straight lines of the model that lie in the plane $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$ and meet $O$ are exactly the lines of constant $V$ (on which $d\theta = +d\rho/\rho$) and the lines of constant $U$ (on which $d\theta = -d\rho/\rho$).

(ii) **Causal horizons.** An event $q$ satisfies $q \le p$ for some event $p$ of $O$ if and only if $V(q) < 0$; an event $q$ satisfies $p \le q$ for some event $p$ of $O$ if and only if $U(q) > 0$. Consequently no event with $V(q) \ge 0$ can ever influence $O$; this set contains the null plane $\{x^1 = x^0\}$, the left wedge $\{x^1 < -|x^0|\}$ and the future wedge $\{x^0 > |x^1|\}$; and no event with $U(q) \le 0$ can ever be influenced by $O$, a set containing the null plane $\{x^1 = -x^0\}$, the left wedge and the past wedge $\{x^0 < -|x^1|\}$. The null plane $\{x^1 = x^0\}$ is the boundary of the causal past of $O$ (the future horizon: the surface its worldline approaches as $\theta \to +\infty$), and the null plane $\{x^1 = -x^0\}$ is the boundary of the causal future of $O$ (the past horizon); every event of the left wedge is causally unrelated to $O$ in both directions. The same criteria with $O$ any other congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_1$, $y = y_1$, $z = z_1$ hold verbatim: the constants $\rho_0$, $y_0$, $z_0$ do not enter.

(iii) **Radar time and distance to a coaxial congruence reflector.** Fix $\rho_m > 0$ with $\rho_m \ne \rho_0$ and let $R_m$ be the congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_m$, $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$ (a second uniformly accelerated observer, coaxial with $O$, with proper acceleration $c^2/\rho_m$). Let $e_-$ be the event of $O$ at parameter $\theta_e$ (so $\tau(e_-) = \rho_0 \theta_e/c$ up to the base point of $\tau$), let $q_m$ be the event of $R_m$ lying on the future null straight line from $e_-$ in the plane $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$, and let $e_+$ be the event of $O$ lying on the future null straight line from $q_m$; the reflection at $q_m$ is idealized as instantaneous and as leaving $R_m$'s motion unchanged, as in [[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]]. Then $e_-, q_m, e_+$ exist uniquely, the Rindler time of $q_m$ is $\theta_m = \theta_e + |\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$, the return event satisfies $\theta(e_+) = \theta_e + 2|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ and $(\theta_e + \theta(e_+))/2 = \theta_m$, so the round trip lasts $2|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ in Rindler time and $(2\rho_0/c)|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ in $O$'s proper time. The radar protocol therefore assigns to $q_m$ the radar time $\tau_{\mathrm{rad}}(q_m) = (\rho_0/c) \theta_m$ plus the base constant of $\tau$ and the radar distance $\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}(q_m) = \rho_0 |\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$; within this coaxial family the radar-time level sets are exactly the Rindler simultaneity slices $\theta = \mathrm{const}$, i.e. the rest slices of the congruence ([[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]]). The radar distance is not the rest distance: in the slice $\theta = \theta_m$ the two worldlines are at rest distance $|\rho_m - \rho_0|$, whereas for $\rho_m = 2\rho_0$ the radar distance is $\rho_0 \log 2 < \rho_0$, because $\log$ is strictly increasing and $e > 2$ implies $\log 2 < \log e = 1$ ([[cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]). For every distinct positive reflector radius the notions differ: with $r = \rho_m/\rho_0$, one has $\log r < r - 1$ when $r > 1$ and $-\log r > 1 - r$ when $0 < r < 1$. The two distance formulas agree only at $r = 1$, where both have the continuous degenerate value zero. The coincident case is not a nonzero emission-reflection-reception triple of the protocol, whose distinct-reflector hypothesis remains in force. As $\rho_m \to 0^+$ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration $c^2/\rho_m$ diverges; as $\rho_m \to +\infty$ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance also grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration tends to $0$.

(iv) **Restrictions of the protocol.** No event with $V \ge 0$ --- in particular no event of the horizon plane $\{x^1 = x^0\}$, of the left wedge or of the future wedge --- can be assigned a radar time or radar distance by this protocol from $O$, because by (ii) it cannot causally precede any reception event on $O$: the required reflection-to-reception leg is impossible. Separately, every event with $U \le 0$ lacks an emission-to-reflection leg from $O$. Thus any event admitting this radar triple must satisfy $U > 0$ and $V < 0$, equivalently it must belong to $W$; the horizon is at infinite radar distance in the limit $\rho_m \to 0^+$. For example $q = x^{-1}(2\rho_0,0,y_0,z_0)$ has $U(q) = V(q) = 2\rho_0 > 0$. It is causally after $O$ at $\theta = 0$, since the displacement is $(2\rho_0,-\rho_0,0,0)$, future timelike, and it even lies on a future null ray from $O$ at $\theta = \log 2$, with displacement $(5\rho_0/4,-5\rho_0/4,0,0)$. Nevertheless it cannot send a causal return to $O$, so it receives no radar assignment from $O$. The protocol therefore does not extend to a global coordinate system of $A$.

(v) **Scope.** All clauses are conditional computations and readings in flat classical spacetime with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors, for the specified congruence worldlines. They are not empirical claims and contain no measurement, apparatus, source, detector or statistical content; gravitation, media, dispersion, finite resolution, quantum effects and material models of the reflector are excluded. No choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted model: affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with inertial chart $x$, $x^0=ct$; ideal clocks and light rays; the causal signal restriction; the Rindler chart and congruence data of the statement; $\rho_0>0$, real $y_0,z_0$; the worldline $O$ with $\theta=c\tau/\rho_0$; $U(q)=q^0+q^1$, $V(q)=q^0-q^1$; and, in (iii), $\rho_m>0$ with $\rho_m\neq\rho_0$ and the coaxial worldline $R_m$.

[L1] Adopted framework assumptions: the affine Minkowski model is the framework's spacetime; ideal clocks read the proper time of their worldline; ideal vacuum light rays are the future null straight lines with coordinate speed $c$; and an idealized signal transmission from $p$ to $q$ is admitted only if $q \in J^+(p)$ ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], [[post-sr-causal-signal-propagation]]).

[L2] Coordinates and model: in every inertial chart $x^0=ct$, $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ in the orthonormal frame, and points are determined by their coordinates ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L3] Rindler data: $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z)=(\rho\sinh\theta,\rho\cosh\theta,y,z)$ is a smooth bijection of $\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$ onto the right wedge $W=\{x^1>|x^0|\}$ with smooth inverse $\rho=\sqrt{(x^1)^2-(x^0)^2}$, $\theta=\frac12\log\frac{x^1+x^0}{x^1-x^0}$, pullback metric $-\rho^2d\theta^2+d\rho^2+dy^2+dz^2$; $n=\rho^{-1}\partial_\theta$ is future unit timelike with $a_{\mathrm{cg}}=\nabla_nn=\rho^{-1}\partial_\rho$ and $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})=\rho^{-2}$; the rest slices $\theta=\mathrm{const}$ are hyperplanes orthogonal to $n$ with induced metric $d\rho^2+dy^2+dz^2$ ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b)).

[L4] Congruence flow lines and proper acceleration: a flow line of $n$ with tangent $\rho n$ has four-velocity $cn$ and proper time $d\tau=\rho\,d\theta/c$; its proper acceleration is $c^2\sqrt{\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})}=c^2/\rho$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (b), [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] (a),(c), [[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a), [[def-sr-proper-acceleration]] (b)).

[L5] Causal structure: a vector is timelike iff $\eta(v,v)<0$ and null iff nonzero with $\eta(v,v)=0$, and each nonzero causal vector is future or past; $C^+=\{v:v^0>|v_s|\}$, $\bar C^+=\{v:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ in every inertial chart; $q\in J^+(p)$ iff the straight segment from $p$ to $q$ is a future causal path; and the causal reachability relations are those of [[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]] ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]] (a),(c), [[thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence]] (b), [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (a),(b)).

[L6] Radar protocol: the radar time of a reflected event $q$ with emission $e_-$ and reception $e_+$ on the observer's worldline is the midpoint proper time $\tau_{\mathrm{rad}}(q)=(\tau(s_-)+\tau(s_+))/2$ and the radar distance is $c(\tau(s_+)-\tau(s_-))/2$; the protocol is conditional on the existence of the three events and uses the symmetric half-split convention ([[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]]).

[L7] Rest distance: in a simultaneity slice of a future unit timelike $n$, the rest distance of two events is $\sqrt{\eta(q-p,q-p)}$ ([[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]] (a),(d)).

[L8] Logarithm: $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing with $\log 1=0$, $\log(xy)=\log x+\log y$ and $\log(1/x)=-\log x$; $\log$ is differentiable with $\log'x=1/x$, and the mean value theorem applies to it on closed intervals with the endpoint continuity supplied by differentiability ([[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]], [[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]], [[cor-mean-value-theorem]], [[cor-differentiable-implies-continuous]]).

[L9] Exponential and hyperbolic data: $e^u\to+\infty$ as $u\to+\infty$, $e^u\to0$ as $u\to-\infty$, $2<e<3$ with $\log e=1$; $\sinh u=(e^u-e^{-u})/2$, $\cosh u=(e^u+e^{-u})/2$, $\cosh^2u-\sinh^2u=1$, and $\cosh u\pm\sinh u=e^{\pm u}$ ([[thm-exponential-limits-and-range]], [[cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three]], [[def-hyperbolic-functions]], [[thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives]], [[thm-exponential-addition-formula]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Chart domain, wedge and boundary.) From [L3], $\Phi$ is a smooth bijection onto $W$ with the stated smooth inverse defined for $x^1>|x^0|$, so the coordinate domain is exactly $W$ and $\rho=0$ is excluded; on $W$ the coordinates satisfy $U=\rho e^{\theta}>0$ and $V=-\rho e^{-\theta}<0$, and conversely $U>0$ and $V<0$ define $W$, since $x^1=(U-V)/2>|x^0|=|U+V|/2$ is equivalent to $U>0,V<0$. The boundary is $x^1=|x^0|$, split into the two half-planes $x^1=x^0\ge0$ (where $V=0$, $U\ge0$) and $x^1=-x^0\ge0$ (where $U=0$, $V\le0$); these are the parts of the full null planes $V=0$ and $U=0$ that bound $W$, while the full planes extend beyond. [L2, L3, algebra]

1.2 (The worldline $O$ and its parametrization.) By [L3] the curve $\theta\mapsto\Phi(\theta,\rho_0,y_0,z_0)$ is a flow line of $n=\rho^{-1}\partial_\theta$ restricted to $\rho=\rho_0$; its tangent with respect to $\theta$ is $\partial_\theta=\rho_0 n$, so by [L4] its four-velocity is $cn$, its proper time satisfies $d\tau=\rho_0\,d\theta/c$, i.e. $\theta=c\tau/\rho_0$ up to an additive constant, and its proper acceleration is $c^2/\rho_0$. Along it, $U=\rho_0e^{\theta}$ and $V=-\rho_0e^{-\theta}$. [L3, L4, algebra]

1.3 (The future null lines of the plane through $O$.) Let $p,q$ be events in the plane $y=y_0$, $z=z_0$ and $w:=q-p$. Since $w^2=w^3=0$, one has $\Delta U:=U(q)-U(p)=w^0+w^1$, $\Delta V:=V(q)-V(p)=w^0-w^1$, and $\Delta U\Delta V=(w^0)^2-(w^1)^2$; hence $w\in\bar C^+$ iff $\Delta U\ge0$, $\Delta V\ge0$ and $\Delta U\Delta V\ge0$, and $w$ is future null iff in addition $\Delta U\Delta V=(w^2)^2+(w^3)^2=0$, i.e. iff either $\Delta V=0<\Delta U$ or $\Delta U=0<\Delta V$. Differentiating $U=\rho e^{\theta}$ and $V=-\rho e^{-\theta}$ along a curve in $W$ gives $dU=e^{\theta}(d\rho+\rho\,d\theta)$ and $dV=-e^{-\theta}(d\rho-\rho\,d\theta)$, so the future null lines through a point of $O$ in the plane are exactly the constant-$U$ lines ($d\theta=-d\rho/\rho$) and the constant-$V$ lines ($d\theta=+d\rho/\rho$). [L3, L5, algebra]

1.4 (The logarithmic inequality.) For $r>0$ with $r\neq1$, the mean value theorem applied to $\log$ on the interval between $1$ and $r$ gives $\log r-\log1=\frac{1}{c}(r-1)$ for some $c$ strictly between $1$ and $r$; since $c>1$ when $r>1$ this gives $\log r<r-1$, and since $0<c<1$ when $0<r<1$ it gives $-\log r>1-r$; equality holds only at $r=1$. In particular $\log2<2-1=1$, and also $e>2$ gives $\log2<\log e=1$ by strict increase of $\log$. [L8, L9, algebra]

2.1 (Causal criteria for the worldline $O$.) (Forward.) Let $q\le p$ with $p$ on $O$, so $w=p-q\in\bar C^+$; then $\Delta V=V(p)-V(q)\ge0$ and $V(p)=-\rho_0e^{-\theta_p}<0$, so $V(q)\le V(p)<0$. Similarly $\Delta U\ge0$ with $U(p)>0$ gives nothing yet, but the same argument with the roles of $U$ and $V$ reversed and the sign of $\rho_0 e^{\theta_p}$ shows $U(q)\le U(p)$; to obtain $U(q)>0$ from $p\le q$ one uses $w=q-p\in\bar C^+$: then $U(q)-U(p)\ge0$ and $U(p)=\rho_0e^{\theta_p}>0$, so $U(q)\ge U(p)>0$; and $V(q)\ge V(p)$ gives no upper bound. (Reverse.) Suppose $V(q)<0$; choose $\theta_p$ with $-\rho_0e^{-\theta_p}>V(q)$, i.e. $V(p)>V(q)$, which is possible because $-\rho_0e^{-\theta_p}\to0^-$ as $\theta_p\to+\infty$; then $\Delta V>0$, and $\Delta U=\rho_0e^{\theta_p}-U(q)$ and $\Delta U\Delta V$ tend to $+\infty$ as $\theta_p\to+\infty$ while the transverse displacement $(y_0-q^2,z_0-q^3)$ is fixed, so for all sufficiently large $\theta_p$ the three inequalities of step 1.3 hold and $q\le p$. Similarly, if $U(q)>0$, choose $\theta_p$ very negative so that $U(p)=\rho_0e^{\theta_p}<U(q)$ and $\Delta U>0$, while $\Delta V=V(q)+\rho_0e^{-\theta_p}\to+\infty$; then $\Delta U\Delta V\to+\infty$ and $p\le q$ for all sufficiently negative $\theta_p$. Hence the criteria, and since the construction used only the positivity of $\rho_0$ and the fixed transverse coordinates of the worldline, the same criteria hold for every congruence worldline $\rho=\rho_1$, $y=y_1$, $z=z_1$. The remaining consequences in (ii) follow by evaluating the signs of $U$ and $V$ on the horizon plane, the left wedge ($U<0<V$) and the future and past wedges. [L5, step 1.1, step 1.3, algebra]

2.2 (Limits along $O$ and along the reflector family.) By [L9], $\rho_0e^{-\theta}\to0$ and $\rho_0e^{\theta}\to+\infty$ as $\theta\to+\infty$, while $\rho_0e^{\theta}\to0$ and $\rho_0e^{-\theta}\to+\infty$ as $\theta\to-\infty$; hence along $O$, $V=-\rho_0e^{-\theta}\to0^-$ and $U\to+\infty$ as $\theta\to+\infty$, and $U\to0^+$ with $V\to-\infty$ as $\theta\to-\infty$. [L9, step 1.2, algebra]

2.3 (Clause (iii): the radar geometry.) Suppose first $\rho_m>\rho_0$. The constant-$V$ future null line from $e_-=(\theta_e,\rho_0)$ has $V=-\rho_0e^{-\theta_e}$, and its intersection with $\rho=\rho_m$ is at the unique $\theta_m$ with $-\rho_m e^{-\theta_m}=-\rho_0e^{-\theta_e}$, i.e. $\theta_m=\theta_e+\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)=\theta_e+|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ since $\rho_m>\rho_0$; the return leg must be the constant-$U$ line through $q_m=(\theta_m,\rho_m)$ (the constant-$V$ line leaves $\rho$ increasing), and it meets $\rho=\rho_0$ at the unique $\theta(e_+)$ with $\rho_0e^{\theta(e_+)}=\rho_me^{\theta_m}$, i.e. $\theta(e_+)=\theta_m+\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)=\theta_e+2\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)$. If instead $0<\rho_m<\rho_0$, the same computation with the roles of $U$ and $V$ exchanged, using the two formulas $U=\rho e^{\theta}$ and $V=-\rho e^{-\theta}$, gives $\theta_m=\theta_e+\log(\rho_0/\rho_m)$ and $\theta(e_+)=\theta_m+\log(\rho_0/\rho_m)$, i.e. in both cases $\theta_m=\theta_e+|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ and $\theta(e_+)=\theta_e+2|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ with midpoint $\theta_m$. Uniqueness of $q_m$ and $e_+$ holds because each constant-$U$ or constant-$V$ line meets each of the lines $\rho=\mathrm{const}>0$ exactly once, and $e_->q_m$ and $q_m\le e_+$ are future null by step 1.3. [step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 (Clause (i).) Step 1.1 gives the bijection, its domain, the boundary description and the identification of the horizon planes with $V=0$ and $U=0$ on the wedge closure; step 1.3 identifies the two families of future null lines in the plane through $O$ with the constant-$V$ and constant-$U$ lines and their differential equations; step 2.2 gives the asymptotic limits of $U$ and $V$ along $O$. [step 1.1, step 1.3, step 2.2]

3.2 (Clause (ii).) The two criteria are step 2.1; the stated consequences for the horizon planes, the left wedge and the future and past wedges follow by computing $U$ and $V$ there, using that $x^1<-|x^0|$ gives $U<0$ and $V>0$, $x^0>|x^1|$ gives $U>0,V>0$, and $x^0<-|x^1|$ gives $U<0,V<0$; the horizon interpretations as boundary of the causal past and future of $O$ follow from the two criteria together with the limits of step 2.2, and the invariance in $\rho_1,y_1,z_1$ is the last sentence of step 2.1. [step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

3.3 (Clause (iii): the radar assignments and the distance comparison.) By [L6] and step 2.3, the radar time is $\tau_{\mathrm{rad}}(q_m)=(\tau(e_-)+\tau(e_+))/2=(\rho_0/c)\theta_m+\tau_0$, since $\theta=c\tau/\rho_0+\mathrm{const}$ along $O$ by step 1.2, and the radar distance is $\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}(q_m)=c(\tau(e_+)-\tau(e_-))/2=\rho_0|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$; the radar-time level sets in the coaxial family are the sets $\theta_m=\mathrm{const}$, which are exactly the Rindler simultaneity slices because $q_m$ lies on the line $\rho=\rho_m$ at Rindler time $\theta_m$, and these slices are the rest slices of the congruence by [L3]. The rest distance in the slice $\theta=\theta_m$ is $|\rho_m-\rho_0|$ by [L7] and the induced metric $d\rho^2+dy^2+dz^2$ of [L3]. With $r=\rho_m/\rho_0\neq1$, the radar distance is $\rho_0|\log r|$ and the rest distance is $\rho_0|r-1|$, so by step 1.4 the radar distance is strictly smaller than the rest distance for $r>1$ and strictly larger for $0<r<1$, with equality only in the degenerate case $r=1$ in which both are zero; in particular at $\rho_m=2\rho_0$, $\rho_0\log2<\rho_0$. [L3, L6, L7, step 1.2, step 1.4, step 2.3, algebra]

3.4 (Clause (iv): the restrictions, and the example.) Let $q$ admit a radar triple $e_-,q,e_+$ from $O$; by the ideal-light and signal assumptions of [L1], the emission and reflection legs give $e_-\le q$ and $q\le e_+$ with $e_-,e_+$ on $O$, so by step 2.1's criteria $U(q)>0$ and $V(q)<0$, i.e. $q\in W$; conversely every event with $V\ge0$ fails $q\le p$ for all $p\in O$ and every event with $U\le0$ fails $p\le q$, so those events receive no radar assignment. For the example $q=x^{-1}(2\rho_0,0,y_0,z_0)$: $U(q)=V(q)=2\rho_0$, and its displacement from the event of $O$ at $\theta=0$ is $(2\rho_0,-\rho_0,0,0)$, with $\eta=-4\rho_0^2+\rho_0^2=-3\rho_0^2<0$ and positive time component, hence future timelike, so $q$ is causally after that event by [L5]; the displacement from the event of $O$ at $\theta=\log2$, namely $(\rho_0\sinh\log2,\rho_0\cosh\log2,0,0)=(\frac34\rho_0,\frac54\rho_0,0,0)$ by [L9], is $(5\rho_0/4,-5\rho_0/4,0,0)$, future null, so $q$ lies on a future null ray from $O$; but $V(q)=2\rho_0\ge0$, so by the criterion $q$ cannot reach any event of $O$ and receives no radar assignment, showing that the protocol does not extend even to events causally after $O$. [L1, L5, L9, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 (Clause (iii): the limiting cases.) As $\rho_m\to0^+$ we have $|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|\to+\infty$ by strict increase and unboundedness of $\log$ (equivalently $\log(\rho_0/\rho_m)\to+\infty$), so the round-trip proper time $(2\rho_0/c)|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ and the radar distance $\rho_0|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ grow without bound, while the reflector's proper acceleration $c^2/\rho_m\to+\infty$ by [L4]; as $\rho_m\to+\infty$ the same divergence of $|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ holds while $c^2/\rho_m\to0^+$. [L4, L8, step 3.3, algebra]

5.1 (Clause (v): scope.) Every clause was computed from the adopted model and the cited mathematical suppliers; the several limiting cases (equal radii excluded, the degenerate $r=1$ value, the two null half-planes versus the full horizon planes, the two limiting reflector radii) were treated explicitly. No apparatus, measurement, statistical or empirical input enters, no choice principle was used, and the statements are conditional model computations. [step 3.1, step 3.2, step 3.3, step 4.1, step 3.4] ∎

## Statement

Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] ($x^0 = c t$). Let $x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be the chart of an inertial frame ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Fix $R > 0$, a real $\Omega$ with $|\Omega| R < c$, a real $x^3_0$ and a real $\phi_0$, and put $\gamma := (1 - \Omega^2 R^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. A rigidly rotating circular ring of radius $R$ and height $x^3_0$ about the $x^3$-axis, with angular velocity $\Omega$, has material worldlines

$$W_{\phi_0}(t) := x^{-1}(c t,\; R \cos(\phi_0 + \Omega t),\; R \sin(\phi_0 + \Omega t),\; x^3_0),\qquad t \in \mathbb R.$$

(i) **The ring worldline and the ring congruence.** $W_{\phi_0}$ is a $C^\infty$ future timelike worldline with unit observer

$$n = \gamma\,\bigl(1,\;-(\Omega R/c)\sin(\phi_0+\Omega t),\;(\Omega R/c)\cos(\phi_0+\Omega t),\;0\bigr) = (\gamma/c)\,\partial_t|_{\varphi},$$

$\eta(n,n) = -1$, and four-velocity $U = c n = \gamma\,\partial_t|_{\varphi}$, $\eta(U,U) = -c^2$, where $\varphi := \phi - \Omega t$ is the rotating angular label of the ring material points; it is an unparametrized flow line of the rigid-rotation congruence $n = \gamma(r)\,[\partial_0 + (\Omega/c)(-x^2\partial_1 + x^1\partial_2)]$ restricted to $r = R$, and its proper time $\tau$ and the chart time $t$ satisfy $d\tau = dt/\gamma$, so $\tau = t/\gamma + \tau_0$ for an arbitrary proper-time origin $\tau_0$ on this worldline ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c), [[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).

(ii) **The guided-signal model.** Adopt, as an explicit model assumption of an ideal circular guide attached to the ring and of the signal and detector model below, and not as a consequence of the postulates: two ideal signals are emitted at the common emission event $W_{\phi_0}(0)$ into the guide, one in the positive angular direction and one in the negative angular direction (respectively co-rotating and counter-rotating for $\Omega > 0$, with these roles reversed for $\Omega < 0$), and in the inertial chart they follow the curves $C_+$ and $C_-$ given by $\phi_+(t) = \phi_0 + c t/R$ and $\phi_-(t) = \phi_0 - c t/R$ with radius $R$ and height $x^3_0$, i.e. each guided signal has chart angular rate $+c/R$ or $-c/R$ along the guide ('inertial tangential speed $c$ along the guide'); the detector is an ideal clock carried by the ring material point labelled $\varphi = \phi_0$. Each of $C_+$ and $C_-$ is a future null curve of the chart: its tangent has time component $c$ and spatial part of Euclidean length $c$, so the tangent has $\eta$-norm $0$ and positive time component ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

(iii) **Return times and differences.** The displayed guided curves have all-real mathematical extensions; emitted signals are their restrictions $t \ge 0$. On those extensions $C_+$ meets the worldline $W_{\phi_0}$ exactly at the chart times $2 \pi k R/(c - \Omega R)$, $k \in \mathbb Z$, and $C_-$ exactly at the chart times $2 \pi k R/(c + \Omega R)$, $k \in \mathbb Z$; the smallest positive meeting times are $t_1 := 2 \pi R/(c - \Omega R) > 0$ and $t_2 := 2 \pi R/(c + \Omega R) > 0$. Hence the two counter-propagating signals emitted at the same event reunite with the emitting material point at the reception events $W_{\phi_0}(t_1)$ and $W_{\phi_0}(t_2)$, each having gained exactly one circuit relative to that material point, and the chart-time difference of the two reunions is $t_1 - t_2 = 4 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2 R^2) > 0$ for $\Omega > 0$. The proper-time difference measured by the detector ideal clock is $(t_1 - t_2)/\gamma = 4 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 \sqrt{1 - \Omega^2R^2/c^2})$. For $\Omega = 0$ (inertial ring) $t_1 = t_2 = 2 \pi R/c$ and both differences vanish; for $\Omega < 0$ the sign of the first difference reverses and the roles of $C_+$ and $C_-$ are interchanged.

(iv) **Relation to the ring rest-synchronization holonomy.** On the fixed-height timelike cylinder $C = \{r = R,\ x^3 = x^3_0\}$, material worldlines have constant rotating label. Its rest lines instead vary $\varphi$ on an angular lift and satisfy $dt/d\varphi = \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2)$, being integral curves of $\partial_\varphi + [\Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2)]\,\partial_t$; for $\Omega = 0$ they are $t = \text{constant}$ circles; one circuit $\varphi \to \varphi + 2 \pi$ has the chart-time holonomy $\Delta t_h = 2 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2) = (t_1 - t_2)/2$ and the receiver proper-time holonomy $\Delta \tau_h = \Delta t_h/\gamma = 2 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 \sqrt{1 - \Omega^2R^2/c^2}) = (1/2)(t_1 - t_2)/\gamma$, exactly half of the detector proper-time difference of (iii); for $\Omega = 0$ both holonomies vanish. The ambient three-dimensional rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable for $\Omega \neq 0$, so no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists, while the one-dimensional rest distribution restricted to the fixed-height cylinder $C$ is locally integrable and has the global holonomy just computed, nonvanishing exactly when $\Omega \neq 0$; the return-time computation of (iii) uses only the guided null curves and the material worldline and does not use either integrability property ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c), [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]]).

(v) **Scope.** All quantities are conditional model computations for the specified ring, guide, signal and detector idealizations. The guided-signal curves are an adopted device model: the ideal vacuum light rays of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] are straight future null lines and do not circulate around the ring by themselves, and no assertion is made about optical fibers, refractive media, dispersion, absorption, finite resolution, apparatus calibration, interference phase or wave optics, or about one-way synchronization conventions between distinct ring observers; no measurement outcome, statistical inference or empirical claim is made, the values of $R$ and $\Omega$ are parameters and not measured quantities, and no choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $c>0$; an inertial chart $x$ with $x^0=ct$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ in the orthonormal frame; $R>0$, real $\Omega$ with $|\Omega|R<c$, real $x^3_0,\phi_0$, and $\gamma=(1-\Omega^2R^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; the ring worldlines $W_{\phi_0}(t)=x^{-1}(ct,R\cos(\phi_0+\Omega t),R\sin(\phi_0+\Omega t),x^3_0)$; the guided curves $C_\pm$ of clause (ii), adopted as the explicit device model of the statement; and the detector ideal clock carried by the material point $\varphi=\phi_0$.

[L1] Ideal clocks read the proper time of their worldline, and ideal vacuum light rays are the future null straight lines with coordinate speed $c$ in every inertial chart ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]).

[L2] In every inertial chart the coordinates are $x^0=ct$, the matrix of $\eta$ is $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ with dimensionless entries, and the interval carries $\mathrm m^2$ ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L3] Points of $A$ are determined by their inertial coordinates, and vector components are read in the orthonormal basis $(e_a)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L4] A curve $x:I\to A$ is differentiable precisely when its coordinate representation is, its tangent is the corresponding $V$-vector, and it is $C^k$ when that representation is; at a regular point the causal character and future direction of the curve are those of its tangent ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (a),(b)).

[L5] Causal classification: timelike means $\eta(v,v)<0$, null means $v\neq0$ and $\eta(v,v)=0$, and each nonzero causal vector is future or past but not both; $C^+=\{v:v^0>|v_s|\}$ and $\bar C^+=\{v:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ in every inertial chart ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]] (a)).

[L6] Four-velocity: $U=x'/\tau'=cx'/\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ along a $C^1$ future timelike worldline, and for a congruence flow line with tangent $x'=cn$ the four-velocity is $cn$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] (a),(c), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a)).

[L7] Proper time: for a $C^1$ future timelike worldline, $\tau(b)-\tau(a)=c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}\,du$, and the proper-time reparametrization is $C^1$ with tangent $x'/\tau'$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]] (i),(iii),(iv)).

[L8] Derivatives: $(\sin t)'=\cos t$, $(\cos t)'=-\sin t$, and the chain rule differentiates composites with affine inner maps ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule]], [[def-derivative]]).

[L9] Trigonometric identities: $\sin^2t+\cos^2t=1$, parity, addition formulas, quarter-turn shifts $\sin(t+\pi)=-\sin t$, $\cos(t+\pi)=-\cos t$, and $\sin t=0$ iff $t=m\pi$ ($m\in\mathbb Z$), with both sine and cosine $2\pi$-periodic ([[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]]).

[L10] Rigid rotation and the ring: on the timelike region $r^2<c^2/\Omega^2$ the field $n=\gamma(r)[\partial_0+(\Omega/c)(-x^2\partial_1+x^1\partial_2)]$ is a smooth future unit timelike Born-rigid congruence with nowhere-zero vorticity for $\Omega\neq0$; on the ring cylinder $r=R$, $x^3=\text{const}$, the induced metric is $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2\Omega R^2\,dt\,d\varphi+R^2d\varphi^2$, the ring observer $\phi=\phi_0+\Omega t$ has $n=\gamma(R)(1,-(\Omega R/c)\sin\phi,(\Omega R/c)\cos\phi,0)$, the one-dimensional rest distribution is locally integrable with $dt/d\varphi=\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$, one positive circuit has signed chart-time offset $\Delta t=2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$, and for $\Omega=0$ the ring is inertial with rest lines $t=\text{const}$ ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c)).

[L11] Frobenius: the ambient rest distribution of an observer congruence is integrable on an open set exactly where its vorticity vanishes; a locally integrable rank-one cylinder distribution is unaffected by the ambient obstruction ([[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]] (iii), [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (c),(d)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Tangent and invariants of the ring worldline.) With $\varphi:=\phi_0+\Omega t$, the coordinate functions of $W_{\phi_0}$ are $t\mapsto ct$, $t\mapsto R\cos\varphi$, $t\mapsto R\sin\varphi$ and the constant $x^3_0$; differentiating with [L8] gives $\dot W=(c,-\Omega R\sin\varphi,\Omega R\cos\varphi,0)$, and by [L2] and [L9], $\eta(\dot W,\dot W)=-c^2+\Omega^2R^2(\sin^2\varphi+\cos^2\varphi)=-c^2(1-\Omega^2R^2/c^2)=-c^2/\gamma^2<0$, while the time component is $\dot W^0=c>0$ and the spatial part has Euclidean norm $\Omega R<c$. [L2, L3, L8, L9, algebra]

1.2 (The guided curves are future null.) With $\varphi_\pm:=\phi_0\pm ct/R$ the curves $C_\pm$ have coordinate functions $t\mapsto ct$, $t\mapsto R\cos\varphi_\pm$, $t\mapsto R\sin\varphi_\pm$; differentiating gives tangents $(c,\mp c\sin\varphi_\pm,\pm c\cos\varphi_\pm,0)$, whose $\eta$-square is $-c^2+c^2(\sin^2+\cos^2)=0$ by [L2] and [L9], so the tangent is nonzero null, with time component $c$ equal to the Euclidean norm of its spatial part; hence each tangent lies in $\bar C^+\setminus\{0\}$ by [L5], so each of $C_\pm$ is a future null curve. [L5, L8, L9, algebra]

1.3 (Rest-synchronization data on the cylinder.) By [L10] the induced metric on the cylinder is $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2\Omega R^2dt\,d\varphi+R^2d\varphi^2$ with $c^2-\Omega^2R^2>0$ by $|\Omega|R<c$, and the one-dimensional rest distribution is locally integrable with $dt/d\varphi=\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$; one positive circuit $\varphi\mapsto\varphi+2\pi$ has chart-time offset $\Delta t_h=2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$, and for $\Omega=0$ the rest lines are $t=\text{const}$. For $\Omega\neq0$ the ambient rest distribution has nowhere-zero vorticity, so by [L11] it is nowhere integrable and admits no local rest-simultaneity hypersurface; the rank-one cylinder distribution is a separate locally integrable object, and no global single-valued rest time on the cylinder exists when $\Delta t_h\neq0$. [L10, L11, algebra]

1.4 (Agreement of sine and cosine pairs.) For real angles $\alpha,\beta$: if $\cos\alpha=\cos\beta$ and $\sin\alpha=\sin\beta$, then the addition formulas give $\cos(\alpha-\beta)=\cos\alpha\cos\beta+\sin\alpha\sin\beta=\cos^2\alpha+\sin^2\alpha=1$ and $\sin(\alpha-\beta)=\sin\alpha\cos\beta-\cos\alpha\sin\beta=0$ by [L9]; the zero-set statement puts $\alpha-\beta\in\pi\mathbb Z$, and the quarter-turn shifts give $\cos(m\pi)=(-1)^m$, so $\cos(\alpha-\beta)=1$ forces $m$ even, i.e. $\alpha-\beta=2\pi k$ for some $k\in\mathbb Z$. Conversely $\alpha-\beta=2\pi k$ implies $\cos\alpha=\cos\beta$ and $\sin\alpha=\sin\beta$ by the $2\pi$-periodicity of [L9]. [L9, algebra]

2.1 (Congruence data and proper time on the ring.) By [L10] the field $n=\gamma(R)(1,-(\Omega R/c)\sin\varphi,(\Omega R/c)\cos\varphi,0)$ is the unit observer of the ring material point and $W_{\phi_0}$ is its flow line; direct substitution with [L9] gives $\eta(n,n)=\gamma^2(-1+(\Omega^2R^2/c^2)(\sin^2+\cos^2))=\gamma^2(-1+\Omega^2R^2/c^2)=-1$, and $U:=cn=\gamma(1,-(\Omega R/c)\sin\varphi,(\Omega R/c)\cos\varphi,0)=(\gamma/c)\dot W$, coinciding with $\gamma\,\partial_t|_{\varphi}$ evaluated along the material line and with the four-velocity of [L6]. Since $\eta(\dot W,\dot W)=-c^2/\gamma^2$ by step 1.1, the proper-time integrand of [L7] is $c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(\dot W,\dot W)}=1/\gamma$, so $d\tau=dt/\gamma$ and $\tau=t/\gamma+\tau_0$. [L6, L7, L9, L10, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 (The meeting sets of the guided curves with the material worldline.) The guided signal $C_+$ meets $W_{\phi_0}$ at chart time $t$ exactly when the material point and the guided point coincide, i.e. exactly when $\cos(\phi_0+ct/R)=\cos(\phi_0+\Omega t)$ and $\sin(\phi_0+ct/R)=\sin(\phi_0+\Omega t)$; by step 1.4, applied to $\alpha=\phi_0+ct/R$ and $\beta=\phi_0+\Omega t$, this is equivalent to $(c/R-\Omega)t\in2\pi\mathbb Z$, i.e. to $t=2\pi kR/(c-\Omega R)$ for some $k\in\mathbb Z$. Similarly $C_-$ meets $W_{\phi_0}$ exactly when $-(c/R+\Omega)t\in2\pi\mathbb Z$, i.e. $t=2\pi kR/(c+\Omega R)$, $k\in\mathbb Z$. The angular labels of the two curves at a common meeting time differ by exactly one winding per unit of $k$ by construction. [L2, step 1.2, step 1.4, given]

3.1 (The ring worldline is a future timelike worldline and a congruence flow line.) By step 1.1 the coordinate functions are smooth compositions of affine maps with sine and cosine, so $W_{\phi_0}$ is $C^\infty$ by [L4]; its tangent is timelike with positive time component exceeding the spatial norm, so it is future timelike and regular by [L5], and $W_{\phi_0}$ is a future timelike worldline. By step 2.1 it is a flow line of the unit field $n$ of the rigid-rotation congruence restricted to $r=R$, with four-velocity $U=cn$ and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ in agreement with [L6], and its proper time is $\tau=t/\gamma+\tau_0$ by step 2.1. [L4, L5, L6, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 (Return times and the differences.) Since $|\Omega|R<c$, both $c-\Omega R>0$ and $c+\Omega R>0$; hence the smallest positive members of the two meeting sets of step 2.2 are $t_1=2\pi R/(c-\Omega R)$ and $t_2=2\pi R/(c+\Omega R)$, both positive, and the emitted signals reunite with the emitting material point at $W_{\phi_0}(t_1)$ and $W_{\phi_0}(t_2)$ after exactly one circuit relative to it. Their chart-time difference is $t_1-t_2=2\pi R\bigl[(c+\Omega R)-(c-\Omega R)\bigr]/((c-\Omega R)(c+\Omega R))=4\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$, which is positive for $\Omega>0$ and negative for $\Omega<0$. By step 3.1 the two receptions correspond to proper times $\tau=t_1/\gamma+\tau_0$ and $\tau=t_2/\gamma+\tau_0$ of the detector ideal clock, so the detector reads the proper-time difference $(t_1-t_2)/\gamma=4\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2\sqrt{1-\Omega^2R^2/c^2})$ by [L1] and step 2.1. [L1, L2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra]

5.1 (Holonomy and the factor-two relation.) By step 1.3 the chart-time holonomy of the ring rest lines over one circuit is $\Delta t_h=2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$; comparing with step 4.1 gives $t_1-t_2=2\Delta t_h$, i.e. $\Delta t_h=(t_1-t_2)/2$. Dividing by $\gamma$ using $d\tau=dt/\gamma$ of step 2.1 gives the receiver proper-time holonomy $\Delta\tau_h=\Delta t_h/\gamma=(1/2)(t_1-t_2)/\gamma$, exactly half the detector proper-time difference of step 4.1; explicitly $\Delta\tau_h=2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2\sqrt{1-\Omega^2R^2/c^2})$. [L10, step 2.1, step 1.3, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 (Inertial limit and reversed rotation.) If $\Omega=0$ then $\gamma=1$, the meeting sets of step 2.2 are both $2\pi kR/c$, so $t_1=t_2=2\pi R/c$ and both differences of step 4.1 and both holonomies of step 5.1 vanish; the rest lines are the $t=\text{const}$ circles of step 1.3. If $\Omega<0$, the factor $4\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$ of step 4.1 is negative, so the sign of $t_1-t_2$ is reversed, and the labels 'co-rotating' and 'counter-rotating' are interchanged because the material angular rate $\Omega$ now has the opposite sign to that of $C_+$. [L10, step 1.3, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 (Scope.) The computation used only: the inertial chart and the adopted guided curves and detector of clauses (ii) and (iii); the rigid-rotation data of the ring cylinder; the proper time and four-velocity suppliers; and the trigonometric suppliers. The adopted guided-signal model is not a consequence of the ideal-light postulate, whose rays are straight; no claim is made about media, apparatus, interference or measurement, and no choice principle was used in any step. [L1, L6, L10, step 2.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **The two differences are distinct quantities.** The detector proper-time difference of (iii) is the difference of the two reunion times of the counter-propagating signals at the emitting material point; the holonomy of (iv) is the synchronization offset accumulated around one circuit of the ring rest lines. They differ by exactly a factor two, and the factor-two relation is proved, not assumed.
- **The ambient Frobenius obstruction is not needed for the delay.** The return-time computation proceeds along the two guided null curves and the single material worldline and uses neither the nonintegrability of the ambient rest distribution nor the local integrability of the cylinder rest lines; those facts serve only to interpret clause (iv).

## Statement

Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and the SI conventions $x^0=ct$ of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] in an inertial chart ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Let $J$ be an open interval containing $0$, let $q:J\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ with $|q'(t)|<c$, set $\beta=q'/c$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, let $L>0$, and fix transverse coordinates $(y_0,z_0)$. The rocket and thread-element worldlines are $x_\xi(t)=x^{-1}(ct,q(t)+\xi,y_0,z_0)$, with labels in an open interval $I$ containing $[0,L]$; the rockets are labels $0,L$.

(a) Every member is $C^2$ future timelike: its chart-time tangent is $(c,q',0,0)$ with squared norm $-c^2/\gamma^2<0$. Its common proper-time function is $\tau(t):=\int_0^t\gamma(v)^{-1}dv$, and its proper four-velocity is $U=\gamma(c,q',0,0)$ with squared norm $-c^2$. All members have equal chart velocity and acceleration, $q',q''$, and their chart separation is the constant $L$.

(b) The four-dimensional extension is essential for applying the material-family lemma. Choose open transverse intervals $Y,Z$ containing $y_0,z_0$, put $\sigma:=c\tau$, let $t=t(\sigma)$ be the inverse on $c\tau(J)$, and set

$$\Phi(\sigma,\xi,y,z):=x^{-1}(ct(\sigma),q(t(\sigma))+\xi,y,z),\qquad(\xi,y,z)\in B:=I\times Y\times Z.$$

This is an injective $C^2$ immersion onto an open set, with $dt/d\sigma=\gamma/c$ and $\partial_\sigma\Phi=n(\Phi)$, where $n=\gamma(1,\beta,0,0)$ is a $C^1$ future unit field. Apply the first-order definitions in [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]], which agree with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] when smooth. The longitudinal unit rest vector is $s_\parallel:=\gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$, and

$$\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=\gamma^3q'q''/c^3.$$

This agrees with [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (d), is nonzero exactly where $q'q''\ne0$, and changes sign with that product. When $q$ is smooth the full original smooth-congruence branch is recovered. Restricting the extension to fixed $y_0,z_0$ gives the prescribed thread.

(c) For its material label tangent $e=\partial_\xi\Phi=(0,1,0,0)$, $h(e,e)=\gamma^2$ and $h(e)/\gamma=s_\parallel$. The vector $e/\gamma$ generally is not $s_\parallel$, but horizontality implies $\theta(e/\gamma,e/\gamma)=\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)$. The internal longitudinal material metric is $G_{11}=\gamma^2$, so its length at common flow parameter is

$$\mathcal L(t):=\int_0^L\sqrt{G_{11}}\,d\xi=\gamma(t)L.$$

It is an internal material metric length, not automatically the finite endpoint distance on one observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane. The local evolution is

$$\frac{d}{d\tau}\log\mathcal L=c\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=\gamma^3q'q''/c^2,\qquad\frac{d\mathcal L}{d\tau}=\gamma^4Lq'q''/c^2.$$

At a time with $q'=v$, $\mathcal L=L/\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}\ge L$, with equality exactly for $v=0$. Chart separation stays $L$; the material length is constant precisely when $q'{}^2$ is constant, and has nonzero local rate wherever $q'q''\ne0$.

(d) Under the stipulated material reading that thread elements follow these flow lines, the initial internal length is $\gamma(0)L$ and its relative factor is $\gamma(t)/\gamma(0)$. Relative to that initial state it stretches where $\gamma(t)>\gamma(0)$, shrinks where $\gamma(t)<\gamma(0)$, and has equal length where the factors agree. In the special initially resting case $q'(0)=0$, the initial length is $L$ and every state with $q'(t)\ne0$ has stretch factor $\gamma(t)>1$. No elasticity or failure criterion is supplied, so neither breaking nor a definite tension of an actual thread follows.

(e) The Rindler congruence in [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b) is Born rigid, with constant internal rest separations and unequal proper accelerations $c^2/\rho$ at distinct radial labels ([[def-sr-proper-acceleration]]). Equal chart-velocity and acceleration profiles in the translated family do not imply Born rigidity where $q'q''\ne0$. Constant chart separation and constant internal rest metric are distinct kinematic conditions.

(f) This is a conditional flat-spacetime deduction for prescribed worldlines and the stated material reading. It assumes no dynamical or elastic model, force law, material failure criterion, measurement or empirical fact, and asserts nothing about real threads or rockets. No choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $c>0$; an inertial chart $x$ with $x^0=ct$; an open interval $J\ni0$; a $C^2$ function $q:J\to\mathbb R$ with $|q'|<c$; $\beta=q'/c$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$; $L>0$; transverse $y_0,z_0$, intervals $Y\ni y_0$, $Z\ni z_0$; label interval $I\supset[0,L]$; the worldlines $x_\xi(t)=x^{-1}(ct,q(t)+\xi,y_0,z_0)$; and, in (b)-(c), the map $\Phi(\sigma,\xi,y,z)=x^{-1}(ct(\sigma),q(t(\sigma))+\xi,y,z)$ on $B=I\times Y\times Z$ with $\sigma=c\tau$.

[L1] The framework adopts the affine Minkowski model as spacetime with its causal structure ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L2] In every inertial chart $x^0=ct$, the matrix of $\eta$ is $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ in the orthonormal frame, and points are determined by their coordinates ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L3] A curve is $C^k$ exactly when its coordinate representation is; its tangent is read in $V$; a $C^2$ curve has $C^1$-in-parameter tangents ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (a)).

[L4] Causal classification and the chart criterion: timelike means $\eta(v,v)<0$ and $C^+=\{v:v^0>|v_s|\}$ in every inertial chart ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]] (a)).

[L5] Four-velocity of a $C^1$ future timelike worldline: $U=x'/\tau'=cx'/\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$, with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$; for $C^2$ curves the four-acceleration is the proper-time derivative of $U$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] (a),(b), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a)).

[L6] Proper time $\tau(t)=\int_0^t c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}\,dv$ up to a constant, and the reparametrization tangent $x'/\tau'$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).

[L7] The Lorentz factor of a future unit timelike $n$ relative to itself is $\gamma\ge1$ with $\gamma=1$ iff $\beta=0$; along a congruence flow line the four-velocity is $cn$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (d), (a)).

[L8] Material metric and its evolution: for a $C^2$ injective immersion $\Phi$ with material directions $e_I=\partial_{\xi^I}\Phi$, $G_{IJ}=h(e_I,e_J)$ is a $C^1$ positive-definite material metric; $\partial_\tau G_{IJ}=2c\theta(e_I,e_J)$; for nonzero $e_I$, $\ell_I=\sqrt{G_{II}}$ satisfies $\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(u_I,u_I)\ell_I$ with $u_I=h(e_I)/\ell_I$; $\theta=0$ makes $G$ constant in the flow parameter; horizontality of $\theta$ gives $\theta(e_I/\ell_I,e_I/\ell_I)=\theta(u_I,u_I)$ ([[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]] (a)-(d)).

## Example

Worked computation in the Rindler chart of [[pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar]]. Let $c > 0$, fix $\rho_0 > 0$ and take $y_0 = z_0 = 0$; let $O$ be the congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_0$ with Rindler time $\theta = c \tau/\rho_0$, and take the emission event $e_-$ at $\theta_e = 0$, so that $e_- = x^{-1}(0, \rho_0, 0, 0)$ in the inertial chart $x$.

(a) **Reflector at $\rho_m = 2\rho_0$.** The future null line from $e_-$ of constant $V$ has $V = -\rho_0$, and it meets $\rho = 2\rho_0$ at the Rindler time $\theta_m = \log 2$; using $\sinh(\log 2) = 3/4$ and $\cosh(\log 2) = 5/4$ ([[thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]) the reflection event is $q_m = x^{-1}(3\rho_0/2, 5\rho_0/2, 0, 0)$, and the return event is $e_+ = x^{-1}(\rho_0 \sinh(2\log 2), \rho_0 \cosh(2\log 2), 0, 0) = x^{-1}(15\rho_0/8, 17\rho_0/8, 0, 0)$ at Rindler time $\theta(e_+) = 2 \log 2$. Thus $(\theta_e + \theta(e_+))/2 = \log 2 = \theta_m$, the radar time assigned to $q_m$ is $(\rho_0/c) \log 2$ plus the base constant of $O$'s proper time, and the radar distance is $\rho_0 \log 2$. The two worldlines $\rho = \rho_0$ and $\rho = 2\rho_0$ are at rest distance $\rho_0$ in the slice $\theta = \log 2$; since $e > 2$ gives $\log 2 < 1$ ([[cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]), the radar distance is strictly smaller than the rest distance.

(b) **Reflector at $\rho_m = \rho_0/2$.** The future null line from $e_-$ of constant $U$ has $U = \rho_0$, and it meets $\rho = \rho_0/2$ at the Rindler time $\theta_m = \log 2$; using $\sinh(\log 2) = 3/4$ and $\cosh(\log 2) = 5/4$ the reflection event is $q'_m = x^{-1}(3\rho_0/8, 5\rho_0/8, 0, 0)$ and the return event is again $e_+ = x^{-1}(15\rho_0/8, 17\rho_0/8, 0, 0)$ at Rindler time $2 \log 2$. The radar time is again $(\rho_0/c) \log 2$ plus the base constant and the radar distance is again $\rho_0 \log 2$, while the rest distance in the slice $\theta = \log 2$ is now $\rho_0/2$; since $e < 3 < 4$ gives $\log 2 > 1/2$ ([[cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]), the radar distance is now strictly larger than the rest distance.

(c) The two cases (a)-(b) give the same radar distance $\rho_0\log2$ at distinct rest distances $\rho_0$ and $\rho_0/2$; this demonstrates noninjectivity of the assignment as the reflector radius varies. To prove that radar distance is not determined by the rest distance alone, also take $\rho_m=3\rho_0/2$. With the same emission at $\theta_e=0$, the reflection occurs at $\theta_m=\log(3/2)$, at $q''_m=x^{-1}(5\rho_0/8,13\rho_0/8,0,0)$, and the return occurs at $2\log(3/2)$, at $e''_+=x^{-1}(65\rho_0/72,97\rho_0/72,0,0)$. This reflector has rest distance $\rho_0/2$, equal to case (b), but radar distance $\rho_0\log(3/2)<\rho_0\log2$, because $3/2<2$ and $\log$ is strictly increasing. These equal inputs and unequal outputs prove the stated failure of dependence on rest distance alone. The original two cases both satisfy $\theta_m=(\theta_e+\theta(e_+))/2$ and have round-trip proper time $2\rho_0\log2/c$; the third case satisfies the same midpoint identity and has round-trip proper time $2\rho_0\log(3/2)/c$.

(d) **Scope.** Conditional model computation with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors in the flat classical model; no measurement, apparatus, source or statistical claim, and no empirical inference, is made, and the idealizations of [[pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar]] (v) are retained.

**Given:** $c>0$, $\rho_0>0$, $y_0=z_0=0$, the inertial chart $x$ with $x^0=ct$, the congruence worldlines $\rho=\rho_0$ (observer $O$) and $\rho=\rho_m$ (reflector) with Rindler time $\theta=c\tau/\rho_0$ on $O$, and the emission event $e_-=x^{-1}(0,\rho_0,0,0)$ at $\theta_e=0$; the radar protocol of [[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]] is applied with $O$ as observer.

## Example

Worked computation of the internal material length for the Bell congruence of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (d) and the material metric of [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]]. Fix $c > 0$ and $\alpha > 0$, let $J := (-c/\alpha, c/\alpha)$, put $q(t) := \frac12 \alpha t^2$ on $J$ and let $x_\xi(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t) + \xi, 0, 0)$ for $\xi$ in an open interval containing $[0,L]$, $L > 0$, in the inertial chart $x$ with $x^0 = c t$. Then $|q'(t)| = \alpha|t| < c$ on the two-sided domain $J$; write $\beta(t) := \alpha t/c$ and $\gamma(t) := (1 - \beta(t)^2)^{-1/2}$.

(a) The translated congruence field is $n = \gamma (1, \beta, 0, 0)$ and the material field $e := \partial_\xi$ is the constant $(0,1,0,0)$; since $\eta(n,e) = \gamma \beta$, the $h$-length of $e$ is $|e|_h = \sqrt{\eta(e,e) + \eta(n,e)^2} = \sqrt{1 + \gamma^2 \beta^2} = \gamma(t)$ ([[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]] (a), [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (d)). Hence the internal longitudinal material-metric length between labels $0$ and $L$ is $|e|_h L = \gamma(t) L > L$ for every $t \neq 0$, with minimum $L$ at $t = 0$, while the chart-frame separation is $q(t) + L - q(t) = L$ for every $t$ in $J$.

(b) The longitudinal expansion of the translated congruence is $\theta(s,s) = \gamma^3 q' q''/c^3 = \gamma^3 \alpha^2 t/c^3$, with unit rest vector $s = \gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$ ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (d)); it vanishes at $t = 0$ and is nonzero for every $t \neq 0$, negative for $t < 0$ and positive for $t > 0$. By [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]] (b) the internal longitudinal material metric component is $G_{11} = h(e,e) = \gamma(t)^2$ and its derivatives in geometric proper length $\sigma = c \tau$ are $d/d\sigma G_{11} = 2 \theta(e,e)$ and $d/d\tau G_{11} = 2 c \theta(e,e)$; with horizontal unit direction $h(e)/\gamma = s$, equivalently the fractional rate of change of the rest separation per unit proper time is $d/d\tau \log(\gamma L) = c \theta(s,s) = \gamma^3 \alpha^2 t/c^2$, and $d(\gamma L)/d \tau = \gamma^4 L \alpha^2 t/c^2$.

(c) Explicit check at $\alpha t = 3c/5$, i.e. $t = 3c/(5\alpha)$ in $J$: $\beta = 3/5$, $\gamma = 5/4$ and $\sinh$ and $\cosh$ are not needed; the rest separation is $5L/4 > L$, the internal metric component is $G_{11} = 25/16 > 1$, the expansion is $\theta(s,s) = (125/64)(3\alpha/(5c^2)) = 75\alpha/(64c^2)$, and the fractional rest-separation rate is $c \theta(s,s) = 75\alpha/(64c)$. At $t = 0$ the rest separation takes its minimum $L$ and the expansion vanishes; the domain is the two-sided interval $(-c/\alpha, c/\alpha)$, so both the decelerating branch $t < 0$ (negative expansion) and the accelerating branch $t > 0$ (positive expansion) are included.

(d) **Scope.** The length $\gamma(t)L$ is the integral of the local rest metric over the material-label segment at common flow parameter; no finite endpoint-hyperplane distance is inferred. The computation is exact kinematics of the specified family: it uses no elasticity, no material failure criterion, no force law, no measurement and no empirical claim, and it draws no conclusion about real threads; no choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $c>0$, $\alpha>0$, $J=(-c/\alpha,c/\alpha)$, $q(t)=\frac12\alpha t^2$ on $J$, $L>0$, an open label interval containing $[0,L]$, an inertial chart $x$ with $x^0=ct$, the worldlines $x_\xi(t)=x^{-1}(ct,q(t)+\xi,0,0)$, and $\beta=\alpha t/c$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$.

[L1] Model and chart: $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with coordinate identification $x(p)$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ in the orthonormal frame ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L2] Derivatives: $q'=\alpha t$, $q''=\alpha$, and the chain rule plus the total chain rule differentiate composites of the data functions ([[def-derivative]], [[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

[L3] Translated-congruence first-order data: the unit field is $n=\gamma(1,\beta,0,0)$, the unit longitudinal rest vector is $s=\gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$, and $\theta(s,s)=\gamma^3q'q''/c^3$, nonzero exactly where $q'q''\ne0$ ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (d), [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (c)).

[L4] Material metric: for an injective $C^2$ immersion with $\partial_s\Phi=n(\Phi)$ and material directions $e_I$, $G_{IJ}=h(e_I,e_J)$ and $\partial_sG_{IJ}=2\theta(e_I,e_J)$, i.e. $\partial_\tau G_{IJ}=2c\theta(e_I,e_J)$ with $\tau=s/c$; $\theta$ kills the $n$-component, so $\theta(e,e)=\gamma^2\theta(s,s)$ when $h(e)=\gamma s$ ([[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]] (a),(b),(d)).

[L5] Rest form: $h(e,e)=\eta(e,e)+\eta(n,e)^2$ for the first-order rest projection $h$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (a), [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]]).

**Proof technique:** direct.

2.1 (The unit field and the material direction.) 3.1 (Clause (a): the material length.) By step 2.1 the $h$-length of $e$ is $|e|_h=\sqrt{h(e,e)}=\gamma(t)>0$, so the internal longitudinal material-metric length between labels $0$ and $L$ at common flow parameter is $\int_0^L\sqrt{G_{11}}\,d\xi=\gamma(t)L$ by [L4]; since $\gamma^2=1/(1-\beta^2)>1$ for $t\ne0$ by step 1.1 and [L6], this exceeds $L$ for every $t\ne0$ and equals $L$ only at $t=0$ (where $\beta=0$). ## Definition

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $c>0$ with the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and let $m>0$.

(a) For $w\in S$ define the *Newtonian comparison momentum* and the *Newtonian comparison kinetic energy* of the pair $(m,w)$ by $$N_p(m,w):=mw,\qquad N_K(m,w):=\tfrac12\,m\,|w|^2,$$ where $mw$ is the scalar multiple of $w$ by the real number $m$ ([[def-linear-map]]) and $|w|^2=\delta(w,w)$ ([[def-integer-power]]). With the SI conventions these carry the units kilogram metre per second and joule respectively.

(b) Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval ([[def-interval]]) and let $y:I\to A$ have inertial coordinate path $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$; writing $r(t)=r^1(t)e_1+r^2(t)e_2+r^3(t)e_3$ with real functions $r^1,r^2,r^3$, at each parameter value $t$ where all three coordinate derivatives exist, define the *coordinate velocity* $w(t)\in S$ of the path by $$w(t):=(r^1)'(t)\,e_1+(r^2)'(t)\,e_2+(r^3)'(t)\,e_3,$$ the componentwise derivative of [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. For a path differentiable at every parameter value these are functions on $I$; otherwise they are defined on its differentiability set. The comparison functionals along the path are $t\mapsto N_p(m,w(t))$ and $t\mapsto N_K(m,w(t))$.

(c) The functionals $N_p$ and $N_K$ are comparison expressions built from a named inertial frame, the mass parameter $m$ and the path's coordinate velocity. They are not defined by, and do not presuppose, a separately developed Newtonian theory, and this definition asserts no approximation, correspondence, error bound or physical claim; those are the content of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]].

## Remarks

- **Well-definedness.** Clause (a) applies the scalar multiple of a vector of the real vector space $V$ (restricted to $S\subseteq V$) and the square of the norm $|\cdot|$ supplied by the frame's spatial structure, both total on $S$; clause (b) uses the componentwise derivative of a function $I\to\mathbb R^3$ and the unique expansion of a vector of $S$ in the ordered basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]. No division occurs and no choice principle is used.

- **No correspondence is asserted here.** The definition only names the two expressions that [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] compares with the model's adopted measured quantities, and the units are the ones fixed by [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. The derivative symbols in (b) are used only at points where the coordinate derivatives exist; no velocity is assigned to an arbitrary nondifferentiable path, and the physical correspondence consumers retain their stated differentiable future-timelike worldline hypotheses. The mass parameter $m>0$ is part of the definition's data; the definition itself attaches no dynamics, force or measurement to it.

## Statement

Let $z_0\in[0,1)$ and define $f:(-\infty,1)\to\mathbb R$ by $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}=\bigl((1-z)^{1/2}\bigr)^{-1}$, the reciprocal of the nonnegative square root, with rational powers as in [[def-rational-power]]; put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$.

(a) $f$ is differentiable on $(-\infty,1)$ with $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$, and twice differentiable there with $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$; in particular $|f''(z)|\le\tfrac34(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$ for every $z\in[0,z_0]$.

(b) For every $z\in[0,z_0]$ there is a real $R(z)$ with $$f(z)=1+\tfrac z2+R(z),\qquad |R(z)|\le K(z_0)\,z^2,$$ so $|f(z)-1|\le\tfrac z2+K(z_0)z^2$ for $z\in[0,z_0]$. Consequently, for every $\eta>0$, $$0\le z\le\min\!\left\{z_0,\frac{\eta}{\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0}\right\}\ \Longrightarrow\ |f(z)-1|\le\eta ;$$ the display is the quantitative form of $f(z)\to1$ as $z\to0^+$ used by [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]].

The lemma is a statement of real analysis about the single function $f$; it attaches no physical meaning to $z$ and makes no claim about a Lorentz factor or a physical velocity.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A real number $z_0\in[0,1)$; the function $f:(-\infty,1)\to\mathbb R$, $f(z)=(1-z)^{-1/2}=\bigl((1-z)^{1/2}\bigr)^{-1}$, with rational powers as in [[def-rational-power]]; and the constant $K(z_0)=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$.

[L1] For $a>0$ and rational $r$ the rational power $a^r$ is defined and positive, and $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$; on rational exponents it agrees with the real power $\exp(r\log a)$ ([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]], [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]]). In particular $1^{-1/2}=1$.

[L2] For real $\alpha$ the function $x\mapsto x^\alpha$ is differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ with derivative $\alpha x^{\alpha-1}$ ([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]).

[L3] The identity function $p_1(z)=z$ has derivative $1$, the affine map $g(z)=1-z$ has derivative $-1$, and derivatives obey the sum, scalar-multiple and chain rules on their stated domains ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule]]).

[L4] If $0\le z\le z_0$ then $0<1-z_0\le 1-z$, and for positive bases $a\le b$ and rational $r>0$ one has $a^r\le b^r$ (with equality exactly when $a=b$); reciprocals of positive elements reverse the order ([[lem-rational-power-monotone]], [[lem-of-inverse-positive]]).

[L5] Taylor's theorem with the Lagrange remainder: if $f$ has derivatives through order $n+1$ on the closed interval between $a$ and $x$ with endpoint continuity, and $|f^{(n+1)}(t)|\le M$ throughout that interval, then $|R_{n,a}f(x)|\le M\,|x-a|^{n+1}/(n+1)!$ ([[cor-taylor-remainder-bound]]).

[L6] Absolute value: $|u+v|\le|u|+|v|$, $|uv|=|u|\,|v|$, $|u|=u$ for $u\ge0$, and $|u|=0$ if and only if $u=0$ ([[def-abs-value]], [[lem-of-abs-value]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The composite form of $f$. Define $g:(-\infty,1)\to(0,\infty)$ by $g(z):=1-z$ and $h:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ by $h(y):=y^{-1/2}$. For every $z<1$ the base $1-z$ is positive, so $f=h\circ g$; and by [L1] the rational power $h(y)=y^{-1/2}$ equals the real power $\exp\bigl(-\tfrac12\log y\bigr)$, so the derivative statement of [L2] applies to $h$. [given, L1, L2]

1.2 The inner derivative. The constant function $z\mapsto1$ has derivative $0$ and the identity $p_1$ has $p_1'\equiv1$ by [L3]; the difference rule of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] therefore gives $g'(z)=-1$ for every $z\in(-\infty,1)$, and each point of $(-\infty,1)$ is a limit point of that interval. [L3]

2.1 The outer derivative. By [L2] with $\alpha=-\tfrac12$, the function $y\mapsto y^{-1/2}$ is differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ with derivative $\bigl(y^{-1/2}\bigr)'=-\tfrac12 y^{-3/2}$; by step 1.1 this is $h'$. [L2, step 1.1]

3.1 First derivative of $f$. Fix $z\in(-\infty,1)$. Then $g(z)=1-z>0$ is a limit point of $(0,\infty)$, so the chain rule [L3] applied to $f=h\circ g$ at $z$ gives $$f'(z)=h'\bigl(g(z)\bigr)g'(z)=-\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}\cdot(-1)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}.$$ [step 1.2, step 2.1, L3, algebra]

4.1 Second derivative of $f$. The function $z\mapsto\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$ is the scalar multiple by $\tfrac12$ of the composite of $g$ with $y\mapsto y^{-3/2}$; the rational power $y^{-3/2}$ agrees with the real power by [L1], so [L2] with $\alpha=-\tfrac32$ gives it derivative $-\tfrac32 y^{-5/2}$ on $(0,\infty)$, and the scalar rule and the chain rule [L3] give $$f''(z)=\tfrac12\Bigl(-\tfrac32(1-z)^{-5/2}\Bigr)(-1)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$$ for every $z\in(-\infty,1)$, which also covers the claim that $f$ is twice differentiable there. [step 3.1, L1, L2, L3, algebra]

5.1 Uniform bound on $[0,z_0]$. Let $z\in[0,z_0]$. By [L4], $0<1-z_0\le1-z$, so $(1-z_0)^{5/2}\le(1-z)^{5/2}$ and, taking reciprocals of positive elements, $(1-z)^{-5/2}\le(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$. Multiplying by $\tfrac34>0$ and using $f''>0$ by [L1] to read $|f''|=f''$ ([L6]) gives $|f''(z)|=f''(z)\le\tfrac34(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$ for every $z\in[0,z_0]$. [step 4.1, L1, L4, L6, algebra]

6.1 The Taylor remainder. Fix $z\in[0,z_0]$. Since $[0,z]\subseteq(-\infty,1)$, the function $f$ has derivatives through order $2$ on the closed interval between $0$ and $z$, continuous at the endpoints; by step 5.1 the second derivative is bounded there by $M:=\tfrac34(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$. Applying [L5] with $n=1$, $a=0$ and this $z$ gives, for $R(z):=R_{1,0}f(z)=f(z)-f(0)-f'(0)z$, $$|R(z)|\le\frac{M}{2!}\,z^2=\frac{3}{8}(1-z_0)^{-5/2}z^2=K(z_0)z^2 .$$ Here $f(0)=1^{-1/2}=1$ by [L1] and $f'(0)=\tfrac12$ by step 3.1, so the displayed expansion of $f$ is $f(z)=1+\tfrac z2+R(z)$. [step 3.1, step 5.1, L1, L5, algebra]

7.1 The quantitative limit. For $z\in[0,z_0]$, steps 6.1 and 3.1 give $|f(z)-1|=\bigl|\tfrac z2+R(z)\bigr|\le\tfrac z2+K(z_0)z^2=z\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z\bigr)\le z\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)$ by [L6] and $K(z_0)>0$, $z\le z_0$, which is the first displayed assertion of (b); if in addition $0\le z\le\eta/(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)$ for an $\eta>0$, then $|f(z)-1|\le\eta$, which is the second displayed assertion; and the bound is not asserted for $z$ outside $[0,z_0]$. [step 6.1, L1, L6, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The constants depend on $z_0$ alone, and the estimate is uniform over the whole interval $[0,z_0]$; as $z_0\uparrow1$ the constant $K(z_0)=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$ diverges, which is why no single constant serves on $[0,1)$ and why the bounded low-speed hypothesis of the physical consumers cannot be dropped. No physical quantity and no physical restriction are introduced here: $z$ is an arbitrary real parameter, and the two in-run consumers named in the statement are the items that apply this estimate to the model's velocities.

## Statement

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, let $n\in V$ be future unit with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and let $P=mU$ with $m>0$ and $U\in V$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$, $T_n(P)$ and $m(P)$ be the observer energy, spatial momentum, kinetic energy and invariant mass of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], put $h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c), and let $\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$ and $w:=h(U)/\gamma=c\,h(U/c)/\gamma\in n^\perp$ be the Lorentz factor and relative velocity of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d); then $u:=U/c$ satisfies $u=\gamma(n+w/c)$, $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$ and $\gamma=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$, $q_n(P)=m\gamma w$, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ and $m(P)=m$.

Let $z_0\in[0,1)$, suppose $z:=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$, put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, and let $f,R$ be as in [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]], so that $\gamma=f(z)$ and $\gamma=1+\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$. Then:

(a) $E_n(P)=mc^2+\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ and $T_n(P)=\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ for the common real number $R_E:=mc^2R(z)$, and $$|R_E|\le K(z_0)\,z\,m|w|^2=K(z_0)\,\frac{m|w|^4}{c^2},\qquad \Bigl|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2\Bigr|\le 2K(z_0)\,z\,\tfrac12m|w|^2 .$$

(b) $q_n(P)=mw+R_q$ with $R_q:=m(\gamma-1)w$, and $$|R_q|\le m|w|\Bigl(\frac z2+K(z_0)z^2\Bigr)\le\Bigl(\frac12+K(z_0)z_0\Bigr)z\,m|w| ;$$ moreover $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}=m\gamma|w|$ and $m(P)=m$.

(c) Every constant above depends only on $z_0$, so the estimates are uniform over all future unit $n$, all $m>0$ and all $P=mU$ with $|w|^2\le z_0c^2$; if $z=0$ (equivalently $w=0$, $U=cn$) then $R_E=R_q=0$, $E_n(P)=mc^2$, $q_n(P)=0$ and $T_n(P)=0$. The lemma is a statement about the mathematical model only; it asserts no measured quantity, no approximation of a physical theory and no error estimate for any experiment.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$, $c>0$, a future unit $n$, $P=mU$ with $m>0$ and $U$ future timelike with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, the projection $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$, the numbers $\gamma=-\eta(U/c,n)$ and $w=h(U)/\gamma$, a bound $z_0\in[0,1)$ with $z:=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$, and $K(z_0)=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$.

[L1] The observer quantities: $E_n(P)=-c\eta(P,n)$, $q_n(P)=h(P)\in n^\perp$, $m(P)=\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$ for nonzero future causal $P$, and $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ after the constant $m>0$ is fixed; $P=(E_n(P)/c)n+q_n(P)$ is the unique decomposition of $P$ along $n$ and $n^\perp$ ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]).

[L2] Projection and relative velocity: $h$ is linear with image $n^\perp$, kernel $\mathrm{span}(n)$, $h(n)=0$, and the restriction of $\eta$ to $n^\perp$ is positive definite with norm $|w|=\sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$; for future unit $u$ one has $\gamma=-\eta(n,u)\ge1$, $w=c\,h(u)/\gamma\in n^\perp$, $u=\gamma(n+w/c)$, $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$, $\gamma=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and $\gamma=1$ if and only if $u=n$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c),(d)).

[L3] Observer identities: for $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant and $U$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and $\gamma,w$ as above, one has $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)\ge0$, $q_n(P)=m\gamma w$, $m(P)=m$ and $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}=m\gamma|w|$ ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b)).

[L4] Uniform Taylor remainder: for $z_0\in[0,1)$ and $0\le z\le z_0$, $f(z)=(1-z)^{-1/2}=1+\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$; in particular $f(0)=1$ and $R(0)=0$ ([[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]]).

[L5] Model and powers: the model data are those of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]; $|w|^2=\eta(w,w)\ge0$ on $n^\perp$ and $z=|w|^2/c^2\ge0$; rational powers such as $(1-z)^{-1/2}$ are those of [[def-rational-power]] and integer powers those of [[def-integer-power]].

[L6] Absolute values: $|\lambda x|=|\lambda|\,|x|$, $|x|\ge0$, and $|x|=x$ for $x\ge0$ ([[def-abs-value]], [[lem-of-abs-value]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Relative velocity and the Taylor form of $\gamma$. The map $h$ is linear by [L2], so $h(U)=c\,h(U/c)$ and $w=h(U)/\gamma=c\,h(U/c)/\gamma$; the vector $u:=U/c$ is future unit and $\gamma=-\eta(n,u)\ge1$, so [L2]\,(d) gives $w\in n^\perp$, $u=\gamma(n+w/c)$, $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$ and $\gamma=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}=(1-z)^{-1/2}=f(z)$. By [L4] applied to $z\le z_0$ we have $\gamma=1+\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$; define $R_E:=mc^2R(z)$. [given, L2, L4, L5, algebra]

1.2 The observer identities. By [L3] at these data, $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$, $q_n(P)=m\gamma w$, $m(P)=m$ and $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}=m\gamma|w|$; define $R_q:=q_n(P)-mw=m(\gamma-1)w$. [given, L3, algebra]

1.3 Translating $z$ into norms. Since $z=|w|^2/c^2$, we have $mc^2z=m|w|^2$, and also $K(z_0)z^2mc^2=K(z_0)z\,m|w|^2=K(z_0)m|w|^4/c^2$. Both expressions are nonnegative because $m>0$, $K(z_0)>0$ and $|w|^2\ge0$. [given, L5, L6, algebra]

2.1 Part (a), the expansions. By steps 1.1 and 1.2, $E_n(P)=mc^2\bigl(1+\tfrac z2+R(z)\bigr)=mc^2+\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ using $mc^2\tfrac z2=\tfrac12m|w|^2$ from step 1.3, and $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2=\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ by the definition of $T_n$ in [L1]. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, L1, algebra]

2.2 Part (a), the bounds. By step 1.1, $|R_E|=mc^2|R(z)|\le mc^2K(z_0)z^2=K(z_0)zm|w|^2=K(z_0)m|w|^4/c^2$ using step 1.3; the second displayed bound is $|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2|=|R_E|\le K(z_0)zm|w|^2=2K(z_0)z\cdot\tfrac12m|w|^2$. [step 1.1, step 1.3, L4, L6, algebra]

2.3 Part (b). By step 1.2, $q_n(P)=m\gamma w=mw+R_q$ with $R_q=m(\gamma-1)w$; by [L6] and step 1.1, $|R_q|=m|\gamma-1|\,|w|=m|w|\,\bigl|\tfrac z2+R(z)\bigr|\le m|w|\bigl(\tfrac z2+K(z_0)z^2\bigr)\le m|w|\,z\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)$ because $z\le z_0$ and $K(z_0)\ge0$; the norm identity $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}=m\gamma|w|$ and $m(P)=m$ are those of step 1.2. [step 1.1, step 1.2, L4, L6, algebra]

3.1 Uniformity and the case $z=0$. The remainders $R_E=mc^2R(z)$ and $R_q=m(\gamma-1)w$ and the bounds of steps 2.2 and 2.3 depend on the state only through $z$, $m$ and $|w|$, and their constants depend on $z_0$ alone, so the estimates hold uniformly over all future unit $n$, all $m>0$ and all $P=mU$ with $|w|^2\le z_0c^2$. If $z=0$ then $\gamma=(1-z)^{-1/2}=1$ by step 1.1, so $u=n$ and $w=0$ by [L2]\,(d), whence $R(0)=0$ by [L4], $R_E=0$, $R_q=0$, and steps 1.2 and 2.1 give $E_n(P)=mc^2$, $q_n(P)=0$, $T_n(P)=0$; conversely $w=0$ gives $z=0$, and $U=cn$ is the same case. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, L1, L2, L4, algebra]

4.1 Conclusion. Steps 2.1 and 2.2 are clauses (a), step 2.3 is clause (b) including the norm identity and $m(P)=m$, and step 3.1 is clause (c) with the uniformity statement and the $z=0$ case; no step used more than the stated hypotheses $z\le z_0<1$, $m>0$ and the model's normalization, and the statement concerns the mathematical model only. [step 3.1, given] ∎

## Definition

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model and let $c>0$ be a fixed mathematical speed scale, with the coordinate convention $x^0=ct$, let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x$ and spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and write the points of $\mathbb R\times S$ as $(t,x)$.

(a) *Lorentz boost charts with a variable speed scale.* For $v\in S$ and a real $C>|v|$ put $\gamma_C(v):=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[def-rational-power]]) and define the affine map $\Phi_{v,C}:\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R\times S$ by $$\Phi_{v,C}(t,x):=\Bigl(\gamma_C(v)\bigl(t-\tfrac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2}\bigr),\ \ x+\tfrac{\gamma_C(v)-1}{|v|^2}\delta(v,x)\,v-\gamma_C(v)\,t\,v\Bigr)\quad(v\ne0),$$ with $\Phi_{0,C}:=\mathrm{id}$; when $|v|<c$, at $C=c$ this is the coordinate expression, in the convention $x^0=ct$, of the passive Lorentz boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: if an event has coordinates $(ct,x)$ in the unprimed inertial chart of the frame, then $\Phi_{v,c}(t,x)$ are its coordinates $(x'^0/c,\,x'^1,x'^2,x'^3)$ in the boosted inertial chart with parameter $v/c$.

(b) *Galilean boost.* For $v\in S$ define the affine map $G_v:\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R\times S$ by $G_v(t,x):=(t,\,x-tv)$.

(c) *Bounded chart region.* For reals $T,R>0$ put $D_{T,R}:=\{(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S:|t|\le T,\ |x|\le R\}$, with $|\cdot|$ the norm of the named frame.

(d) *Scope of the family.* The parameter $C$ is a variable speed scale inside a family of coordinate expressions; it is not a change of the model's adopted constant $c$, and the members with $C\ne c$ are auxiliary mathematical maps used only to state the limit of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]. Nothing here asserts a physical limit of the framework, and no limiting trajectory, force or interaction is defined.

## Remarks

- **Well-definedness.** For $v\ne0$ and $C>|v|$ the base $1-|v|^2/C^2$ lies in $(0,1]$; it equals $1$ only at $v=0$, which the nonvanishing branch excludes, so $\gamma_C(v)$ is a positive rational power ([[def-rational-power]]) and the displayed formulas assign to each pair $(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S$ a pair of elements of $\mathbb R\times S$, using the bilinear form $\delta$ and the vector-space operations of $S$. For $v=0$ the coefficient $(\gamma_C(0)-1)/|0|^2$ in the nonvanishing branch is the indeterminate form $0/0$, so the map is declared separately to be the identity; this is the same convention as in [[def-lorentz-boost]]. The family is total in the parameter: for every $v$ the admissible speeds are exactly $C>|v|$, an open interval, and $C=c$ belongs to it precisely when $|v|<c$.

- **The identification at $C=c$ is a substitution.** Writing $\beta:=v/c$ and $x^0:=ct$ in the definition of $B(\beta)$ in [[def-lorentz-boost]] gives $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta\cdot x)$ and $x'=x+\tfrac{\gamma-1}{|\beta|^2}(\beta\cdot x)\beta-\gamma\beta x^0$ with $\gamma=\gamma_c(v)$; since $\beta\cdot x=\delta(v,x)/c$, $|\beta|^2=|v|^2/c^2$ and $\beta x^0=(v/c)(ct)=vt$, this is exactly $x'^0/c=\gamma_c(v)(t-\delta(v,x)/c^2)$ and $x'=x+\tfrac{\gamma_c(v)-1}{|v|^2}\delta(v,x)v-\gamma_c(v)tv$, that is $\Phi_{v,c}$. The boost $B(v/c)$ is a linear map of $V$ acting on coordinates in the frame basis, while $\Phi_{v,c}$ is the induced affine coordinate expression on the chart domain $\mathbb R\times S$; those two descriptions agree by the displayed computation, which is why the definition records the identification rather than asserting a new map.

- **No uniform limit and no physical interpretation are asserted here.** The definition proves no limit of the family and states no convergence of trajectories; the bounded-region rate and the failure off bounded regions are proved in [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]. The variable $C$ is an auxiliary parameter of a mathematical family, not a change of the model's adopted constant $c$; the model's Lorentz form, time orientation and inertial frames are those of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], and no choice principle is used.
