## Statement

Assume AC and Countable Choice carried by the variational and Sobolev suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega$ be a bounded smooth graph domain in $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), $\varepsilon>0$ constant and $J$ an open interval. Let the bulk datum $f$ be jointly smooth up to $\overline\Omega\times J$ in the all-mixed-derivative sense of the parameter-preserving extension supplier, and let boundary families $g_D,\kappa$ be smooth in a fixed finite boundary atlas $\times\,J$. Then the Dirichlet problem $-\varepsilon\Delta u=f$, $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g_D$ has a unique solution on $\Omega\times J$; it has a single smooth ambient continuation near the closed spatial domain $\times\,J$. The Neumann problem $-\varepsilon\Delta u=f$, $\varepsilon\partial_\nu u=\kappa$ has such a solution precisely when

$$\int_{\Omega_j}f(\cdot,t)+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)=0\quad\text{for each component and every }t\in J.$$

It is unique modulo a separately chosen spatial constant on each component at each time. The normalization $\int_{\Omega_j}u(\cdot,t)=0$ gives a unique smooth family. Both solution operations are linear in their data; time differentiation commutes with them. Smoothness and estimates are local in compact time subintervals, with no uniform-in-$J$ requirement. The smooth ambient continuations are auxiliary and are not unique off the closed physical spatial region.

## Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** A bounded smooth graph domain $\Omega$ with a fixed finite boundary atlas ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]); $\varepsilon>0$ constant; an open time interval $J$; smooth bulk and boundary data; and the two weak solvability suppliers ([[lem-em-lift-specified-dirichlet-existence]], [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]).

[F1] **Weak solvers and estimates.** The Dirichlet and compatible Neumann weak problems have unique solutions in the declared classes with the stated normalisations, and the natural-boundary regularity and the Dirichlet higher-order boundary estimate are available with the Sobolev extension and embedding tools ([[lem-em-zero-boundary-coercivity]], [[lem-em-mean-zero-coercivity-on-a-c-one-domain]], [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], [[thm-higher-order-boundary-regularity-for-dirichlet-problems]], [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]], [[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]).

[F2] **Flattening, traces and calculus.** Chart flattening preserves local Sobolev classes with the chain rule; the first Green identity, the Euclidean divergence theorem, the difference-quotient tools, the weak Leibniz rule, half-space extension, compactly supported smooth density and the FTC/chain/algebra rules are available ([[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]], [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]], [[def-first-difference-quotient]], [[lem-difference-quotient-integration-by-parts]], [[thm-difference-quotient-characterisation-of-w-one-p-for-p-greater-than-one]], [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]], [[thm-wkp-extension-from-a-half-space]], [[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]], [[thm-ftc-first-part]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]).

[F3] **Riesz, completeness and Cauchy-Schwarz.** Bounded functionals on closed $L^2$ subspaces are represented, $L^2$ is complete and Cauchy-Schwarz holds ([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]], [[thm-riesz-fischer-completeness-of-l-p]], [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]).

[F4] **Parameter-preserving extension.** A fixed linear extension of smooth-domain fields preserves all parameters and smoothness up to the boundary ([[lem-em-parameter-preserving-smooth-extension-on-a-smooth-domain]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Fixed boundary lifts: in the graph coordinates $r=x_3-h(y)$ with the domain on $r<0$ and outward normal $\nu=(-\nabla h,1)/\sqrt{1+|\nabla h|^2}$, take a finite boundary partition and a fixed normal cutoff equal to one near $r=0$; for a localized Dirichlet datum $g_j(y,t)$ set the lift $L_Dg_j=\rho(r)g_j(y,t)$ with a larger fixed chart cutoff, and for a localized conormal datum $\kappa_j$ set $L_N\kappa_j=r\rho(r)\kappa_j(y,t)/(\varepsilon\sqrt{1+|\nabla h(y)|^2})$; at $r=0$ the coefficient terms with a differentiated factor vanish because of the factor $r$ while $\partial_\nu r=\sqrt{1+|\nabla h|^2}$, so $\varepsilon\partial_\nu L_N\kappa_j=\kappa_j$, and summing the finite chart pieces gives lifts with the exact datum that are linear, time-independent in their spatial profile, smooth on a spatial collar $\times\,J$ and bounded in $H^{k+2}$ by finite $C^{k+2}$ boundary seminorms. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Dirichlet branch: subtract the lift $L_Dg_D$ and apply the weak Dirichlet solver and the exact higher-order Dirichlet boundary estimate to the source $f+\varepsilon\Delta L_Dg_D$; the solution is unique and, by the regularity estimate iterated over $m$, lies in $H^m$ for every $m$ on compact time subintervals, hence has a smooth representative on the closed spatial domain times those subintervals; the estimate is local in time because all data seminorms are taken on compact subintervals. [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

2.2 Neumann weak existence: smooth boundary $\kappa$ defines a bounded boundary trace functional by Cauchy-Schwarz and the $H^1\to L^2(\partial\Omega)$ trace theorem, and the weak Neumann lemma gives existence exactly under the componentwise compatibility condition, with uniqueness modulo one spatial constant per component at each time; the mean-zero coercivity on each component gives $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|f\|_2+\|\kappa\|_{L^2(\partial\Omega)})$ after normalisation, and a bounded smooth graph domain has only finitely many components because a finite cover by connected one-sided graph patches meets only finitely many and every component meets one. [step 1.1, F1, F3, algebra]

3.1 Natural-boundary $H^2$ estimate: after subtracting the fixed lift $H=L_N\kappa$, the residual $w=u-H$ has homogeneous Neumann flux and source $f+\varepsilon\Delta H$, whose residual bulk integral vanishes under the original compatibility; flattening and localization change the datum to $\eta p-A\nabla z\cdot\nabla\eta+G\cdot\nabla\eta$ with $p\in L^2$ and $G\in H^1$, the exact terms accounting for the natural flux, and the tangential difference-quotient test $v=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2\delta_h^kz)$ — a supported $H^1$ test that need not vanish at the boundary — gives by [F2] and [F3] the uniform bound $\|\eta\nabla\delta_h^kz\|_2\le C(\|p\|_2+\|G\|_{H^1}+\|z\|_{H^1})$; passing to the limit and using Riesz representation supplies all second derivatives with a tangential factor, and the strong equation $-\operatorname{div}(A\nabla z)=p-\operatorname{div}G$ together with $A_{33}\ge\alpha>0$ recovers the remaining normal derivative, giving the natural-boundary $H^2$ estimate. [step 2.2, F2, F3, algebra]

4.1 Higher orders: if $w\in H^{k+1}$ with homogeneous Neumann data and datum in $H^k$, localize; the localized scalar datum lies in $H^k$ and the vector datum in $H^{k+1}$, tangential differentiation by a multi-index $\alpha$ of order $k$ keeps the principal matrix with scalar datum $D^\alpha_{\rm tan}p\in L^2$ and vector datum $D^\alpha_{\rm tan}G-\sum_{0<\beta\le\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\beta}(D^\beta_{\rm tan}A)\nabla D^{\alpha-\beta}_{\rm tan}z\in H^1$, since every commutator carries a coefficient derivative and uses derivatives of $z$ through order at most $k+1$; the tangentially differentiated flux need not vanish but is represented by these vector terms in the natural weak identity, to which step 3.1 applies; this controls order-$k+2$ derivatives with at most two normal factors, and expanding the strong equation on each half-patch and recovering successively larger normal counts through the sole $A_{33}$ principal term, with compact test supports lying in the half-patch interior, yields by the finite cover $\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|\kappa\|_{C^{k+2}(\partial\Omega)}+\|u\|_{H^1})$; tangential tests are justified by the half-space extension and compactly supported smooth density of [F2] without falsely using $H_0^1$ density. [step 3.1, F2, F1, algebra]

5.1 Strong equation and exact Neumann trace: after the estimates give all spatial orders, Sobolev embedding produces a $C^2$ representative on the closure; testing the weak equation against compact interior smooth functions makes the continuous residual $-\varepsilon\Delta u-f$ vanish pointwise by a nonnegative interior bump, and applying the first Green identity to the smooth representative and tests obtained from the fixed smooth Dirichlet lift gives $\int_{\partial\Omega}(\varepsilon\partial_\nu u-\kappa)q=0$ for every smooth boundary test $q$, so the continuous boundary difference vanishes pointwise by a nonnegative chart bump supported where it keeps one sign; the classical conormal equality is therefore recovered from the natural weak formulation rather than presupposed. [step 4.1, F2, F1, algebra]

6.1 Joint smoothness in $(x,t)$ and ambient continuation: differences and time derivatives of compatible data stay in the same compatible linear data space, weak $H^1$ continuity follows from the energy estimate, and applying the higher-order estimate to a difference quotient in time minus the solution for the differentiated data makes the error tend to zero in every $H^m$ on compact time patches, since bulk derivatives converge in $H^k$, boundary derivatives in the finite $C^{k+2}$ seminorms and the $H^1$ error tends to zero; induction gives all time derivatives as solutions for the differentiated data, higher-order Sobolev embedding gives one consistent family of all mixed boundary jets, and the fixed parameter-preserving extension [F4] supplies a single smooth ambient continuation; linearity in the data is clear from the construction. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, F4, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice inherited from the stated weak-existence, Sobolev extension and trace suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive, and let $\rho$ be smooth on the closure. Prescribe in the prescribed-data lemma either smooth Dirichlet data $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$, or smooth outward flux data $g$ with its compatibility condition as in the weak Neumann lemma. Then the weak solution of $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ in $\Omega$ with those data is $C^\infty$ on the closure $\overline\Omega$. For finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth $\rho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, the weak solution is smooth on each closed side. Edge and junction points, reentrant corners and coefficient loss of regularity are excluded. The existence claims are those of the two weak solvability lemmas; this lemma proves their classical upgrade on the declared domains.

## Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** A bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ with finite smooth boundary charts; a smooth uniformly positive coefficient $\varepsilon$ with constants $0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty$; smooth bulk data $\rho$ and the smooth boundary data of the Statement; the weak solution supplied by [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]] or [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces with piecewise smooth data in the transmission case.

[F1] **Weak existence.** Under the declared Choice, the Dirichlet and compatible Neumann weak problems have unique solutions in the declared classes, and the transmission problem with sheet charge has a weak solution ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]], [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]).

[F2] **Flattening.** A $C^k$ chart diffeomorphism maps local $W^{k,p}$ classes with bounded derivatives and the chain rule ([[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]], [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]).

[F3] **Difference quotients.** The first difference quotient, its discrete integration by parts, the increment estimate $\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^2(\Omega')}\le\|\partial_iu\|_{L^2}$, the converse characterization and the weak Leibniz rule are available ([[def-first-difference-quotient]], [[lem-difference-quotient-integration-by-parts]], [[thm-difference-quotient-characterisation-of-w-one-p-for-p-greater-than-one]], [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]]).

[F4] **Riesz, Cauchy-Schwarz and Sobolev tools.** Bounded functionals on closed subspaces of $L^2$ are represented by $L^2$ classes ([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]), Cauchy-Schwarz holds ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]), and integer-order Sobolev spaces have the Fourier characterization with inversion and the embedding into continuous functions for $m>j+3/2$ ([[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]], [[thm-l-two-fourier-inversion]], [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]).

[F5] **Calculus.** The gradient of a scalar is curl-free and the Laplacian is the Euclidean one ([[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]); the extension theorem extends smooth-domain classes to $\mathbb R^3$ ([[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Local reduction: in an interior patch, or in a flattened smooth boundary or interface patch, write the weak equation in divergence form $\int a_{ij}\partial_ju\,\partial_iv=\int fv+\int G_i\partial_iv$ with $\tilde a=|\det D\Phi^{-1}|D\Phi\,a\,D\Phi^{\mathsf T}$ uniformly elliptic by the positivity of the Jacobian bounds and the bounds on $D\Phi$ ([[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]]); Dirichlet data are removed by subtracting a smooth lift $g(y)\eta(t)$ built from a finite subordinate smooth partition and a normal cutoff, and smooth Neumann flux is converted to smooth volume data by a collar vector field $G$ with $G\cdot n=g$ and the divergence theorem, so in every case the local datum has the form $f\in C^\infty$ plus a divergence term with smooth $G$. [given, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

2.1 Tangential estimate: for a tangential direction $k$ put $w=\delta_h^ku$ and test the local weak identity with $v=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2w)$ for a cutoff $\eta$ supported in a smaller patch; the discrete integration by parts, the shifted product rule and the increment estimates of [F3] give the principal bound $\alpha\|\eta\nabla w\|_2^2$ against cutoff terms bounded by $C\|u\|_{H^1}[\|\eta\nabla w\|_2+\|w\|_2]$, with $\|\delta_ha\|_\infty\le\|\partial_ka\|_\infty$ and the $f,G$ contributions controlled by Cauchy-Schwarz; the absorption inequality $2AB\le(\alpha/2)A^2+2B^2/\alpha$ [F4] yields a bound $\|\eta\nabla\delta_h^ku\|_2\le C(\|u\|_{H^1}+\|f\|_{C^0}+\|G\|_{C^1})$ uniform in small $h$. [step 1.1, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 Weak second derivatives: the limit of the pairings of step 2.1 as $h\to0$ defines the distributional tangential derivative $\partial_k\partial_iu$ as a bounded functional in the $L^2$ norm on compactly supported smooth tests, which extends to the closed $L^2$ subspace they generate and is represented by an $L^2$ class through [F4]'s Riesz theorem, with no weak-subsequence selection; the same argument applied in all tangential directions gives every second derivative with at least one tangential index in flattened coordinates, and the interior patches allow all quotient directions. [step 2.1, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 Normal recovery: with compactly supported smooth tests the weak identity reads $-\operatorname{div}(a\nabla u)=f-\operatorname{div}G$ distributionally, so expanding the divergence gives $a_{33}\partial_{33}u=\operatorname{div}G-f-\sum_{(i,j)\ne(3,3)}a_{ij}\partial_{ij}u-\sum_{i,j}(\partial_ia_{ij})\partial_ju$ with every right-hand term in $L^2$ and $a_{33}\ge\alpha>0$; hence the remaining normal second derivative is an $L^2$ class and the local $H^2$ bound holds on each declared side. [step 3.1, F5, algebra]

5.1 Higher orders: differentiating the weak equation by tangential multi-indices and re-applying steps 2.1-4.1 raises the regularity by two tangential orders and then recovers the normal derivatives one by one through the same explicit equation; the exact coefficient commutators are finite combinations of lower-order derivatives and the data are smooth, so induction gives $u$ locally in $H^m$ for every $m$ on each declared side, with the Dirichlet tangential derivatives keeping zero trace and natural tests remaining admissible; the finite cover of the compact closure and the finitely many pieces give the global bounds on each side. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F2, F3, algebra]

6.1 Classical representative: the Sobolev extension theorem and the Fourier characterization with inversion [F4] convert $W^{m,2}$ membership for $m>j+3/2$ into $C^j$ classes, with derivatives agreeing with the weak ones by testing and Fubini and representatives agreeing by continuity; taking $m$ arbitrarily large gives a $C^\infty$ representative on each closed side, and the continuous boundary trace is the prescribed one by trace continuity and the classical strong equation; on closed side interiors the equation holds pointwise by the usual fundamental-lemma argument. [step 5.1, F4, F5, algebra]

7.1 Conclusion: existence is supplied by the weak Dirichlet, compatible Neumann and transmission lemmas [F1], and this argument upgrades it to the stated classical smoothness on the declared domains; edge and junction points, reentrant corners and coefficient loss of regularity are excluded by hypothesis, and the declared Choice hypotheses are transported explicitly. [step 1.1, step 6.1, F1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Put $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline{V}^{\,L^2}$. Then the curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity tending to infinity whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and the zero eigenspace is finite dimensional and must be retained when the topology allows it. Each eigenfield $u_j\in V$ satisfies the full graph-class variational identity $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda_j\int_\Omega u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$. The eigen equation is $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ distributionally with the PEC trace, and for every explicitly chosen mathematical speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and every initial displacement $q_0\in V$ and velocity $q_1\in H$, the associated second-order wave has coefficients $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with those initial coefficients. Its displacement lies in $C(\mathbb R;V)$ and its velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$; finite modal sums converge respectively in $C(K;V)$ and $C(K;H)$ on every compact time interval $K$. The finite-dimensional $\lambda=0$ sector is retained with $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. This speed is a positive abstract mathematical parameter, not a physical constant or prerequisite. No identification with every maximal tangential-trace realisation, and no lossy, open or non-smooth-domain spectral claim, is made.

## Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice; a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega$ with outward normal $n$ and bounded curvature on its compact boundary ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]); the graph spaces, the closure $X$, $V$ and $H$ of the Statement.

[F1] **First Green identity.** For $C^2$ fields on a bounded $C^1$ domain, $\int_\Omega(\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v-u\cdot\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}v)=\int_{\partial\Omega}(u\times\operatorname{curl}v)\cdot n\,dS$ and the analogous divergence identity ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]); the curl and divergence are those of the Euclidean cooordinates and $\Delta$ is the Euclidean Laplacian ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]).

[F2] **Solver, extensions and mean estimate.** The symmetric coercive variational solver is available under Countable Choice ([[lem-em-symmetric-coercive-variational-solver]]); bounded smooth domains extend $H^1$ functions to a fixed larger box ([[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]), and the mean-zero coercivity lemma bounds $\|u-\text{mean}\|_{L^2}$ by the gradient norm on bounded domains ([[lem-em-mean-zero-coercivity-on-a-c-one-domain]]).

[F3] **Compact self-adjoint spectral theorem.** A compact self-adjoint operator on a real Hilbert space has an orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues, finite-dimensional eigenspaces and eigenvalues tending to $0$; a compact operator is bounded ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-compact-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-compact-linear-operator]]).

[F4] **Dirichlet resolvent and density of gradients.** For every $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ there is a unique $u\in H_0^1\cap H^2$ with $(1-\Delta)u=f$, and the smooth zero-boundary fields $\varphi_j$ with $\varphi_j\to u$ in $H^2$ satisfy $\nabla\varphi_j\to\nabla u$ in the curl/div graph norm, so $\nabla u\in X$ ([[lem-em-dirichlet-resolvent-h-two-and-smooth-test-density]]).

[F5] **Hilbert-space tools.** Orthogonal decomposition by a closed subspace and Fourier expansion in a complete orthonormal system ([[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]], [[thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion]]); Cauchy-Schwarz in $L^2$ ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]); dominated convergence ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

[F6] **Calculus and ODE tools.** Square roots, sine and cosine derivatives, chain and algebra rules, the FTC and the zero-derivative-implies-constant corollary ([[thm-of-square-roots]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Gaffney identity: for smooth $u$ with $n\times u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, expanding $|\operatorname{curl}u|^2$ and $|\operatorname{div}u|^2$ and integrating by parts with [F1] cancels the interior second derivatives and leaves $\int_\Omega(|\operatorname{curl}u|^2+|\operatorname{div}u|^2-|\nabla u|^2)=\int_{\partial\Omega}(\operatorname{div}n)|u\cdot n|^2dS$, because on the boundary $u=(u\cdot n)n$ and the normal field may be extended by signed distance so that its normal derivative vanishes. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Boundary trace bound: in the normal collar of [F1], write $|u(y,0)|^2=|u(y,t)|^2-\int_0^t\partial_s|u(y,s)|^2ds$ and bound $|\partial_s|u|^2|\le2|u||\partial_su|$; averaging $t\in(0,h)$ and using $2ab\le\delta a^2+\delta^{-1}b^2$ with the bounded collar Jacobian and a finite chart partition gives $\|u\|_{L^2(\partial\Omega)}^2\le\delta\|\nabla u\|_2^2+C_\delta\|u\|_2^2$ for every $\delta>0$. [step 1.1, given, F6, algebra]

3.1 Combining steps 1.1 and 2.1 with the bounded curvature term and absorbing the gradient contribution for small $\delta$ gives $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|u\|_2+\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_2+\|\operatorname{div}u\|_2)$ for smooth PEC fields, while conversely the graph norm is bounded by $C\|u\|_{H^1}$; hence the graph completion $X$ is a closed $H^1$-subspace of $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with zero tangential trace, since the trace is continuous on $H^1$ and vanishes on the dense smooth PEC fields. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The inclusion $X\hookrightarrow L^2$ is compact: extend a bounded family in $X$ to a fixed larger box by [F2], replace each extension by its average $P_hu$ over cubes of side $h$, and use the rectangular mean estimate of [F2] to get $\|u-P_hu\|_2\le Ch\|\nabla u\|_2$ uniformly; $P_h$ has finite-dimensional range and bounded images, so choosing $h$ small and a finite $\varepsilon$-net in that finite-dimensional range gives a finite $\varepsilon$-net for the family; total boundedness in the complete space $L^2$ gives compact closure, so $X\to L^2$ and $V\to H$ are compact inclusions. [step 3.1, F2, F5, algebra]

4.2 On $X$ with the graph norm the shifted form $a(u,v)=\int_\Omega[\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v+\operatorname{div}u\operatorname{div}v+u\cdot v]$ is symmetric, bounded and coercive with $a(u,u)=\|u\|_{H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})}^2$, so the variational solver [F2] gives for every $f\in H$ a unique $K_0f\in X$ with $a(K_0f,v)=\int f\cdot v$ for all $v\in X$; $K_0$ is bounded $H\to X$ and hence bounded $H\to V$-graph and $H\to L^2$. [step 3.1, F2, algebra]

5.1 Divergence preservation: for $f\in H$ put $q=\operatorname{div}K_0f$; testing the defining identity with the admissible smooth PEC gradients $v=\nabla\varphi$ of zero-trace smooth $\varphi$ (for which $\operatorname{curl}\nabla\varphi=0$, $\operatorname{div}\nabla\varphi=\Delta\varphi$ and $n\times\nabla\varphi=0$) gives $\int_\Omega q(\Delta\varphi-\varphi)=0$ for all such $\varphi$, using $\int f\cdot\nabla\varphi=0$ (each $f\in V$ has zero distributional divergence and the pairing is continuous in $L^2$) and $\int K_0f\cdot\nabla\varphi=-\int q\varphi$. [step 4.2, F5, algebra]

6.1 For the datum $q\in L^2$ the Dirichlet resolvent [F4] gives $\varphi\in H^2\cap H_0^1$ with $(1-\Delta)\varphi=q$ and smooth zero-boundary approximants $\varphi_j\to\varphi$ in $H^2$ whose gradients $\nabla\varphi_j\to\nabla\varphi$ converge in the graph norm, so $\nabla\varphi\in X$; passing the identity of step 5.1 to the limit by $L^2$ continuity gives $\int q(\Delta\varphi-\varphi)=-\|q\|_2^2$, hence $\|q\|_2=0$ and $q=0$; therefore $K_0$ maps $H$ into $V$, and $K=K_0|_H$ is bounded $H\to V$ and compact $H\to H$ by step 4.1. [step 5.1, F4, F5, algebra]

7.1 Self-adjointness and trivial kernel: testing the defining equations of $Kf$ and $Kg$ with $Kg$ and $Kf$ respectively and using symmetry gives $(f,Kg)=a(Kf,Kg)=(Kf,g)$, so $K$ is self-adjoint; $(f,Kf)=\|\operatorname{curl}Kf\|_2^2+\|Kf\|_2^2>0$ for $f\ne0$, because $Kf=0$ would make $f$ orthogonal to the dense subspace $V$ of $H$, so $\ker K=\{0\}$. [step 4.2, step 6.1, F5, algebra]

8.1 By the compact self-adjoint spectral theorem [F3] applied to $K$, $H$ has an orthonormal basis $\{u_j\}$ of eigenfields $Ku_j=\kappa_ju_j$ with positive eigenvalues $\kappa_j$, finite multiplicities and $\kappa_j\to0$ (infinitely many only if $H$ is infinite dimensional, and any zero eigenvalue would contradict the trivial kernel); substituting into the full identity $a(Ku_j,v)=\int u_j\cdot v$ with $v\in X$, and using $\operatorname{div}u_j=0$ since $u_j\in V$, gives $\int\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=(\kappa_j^{-1}-1)\int u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$, so with $\lambda_j=\kappa_j^{-1}-1\ge0$ the eigenfields satisfy the full graph-class variational identity; testing with compactly supported smooth $v$ gives $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ distributionally with the inherited PEC trace. [step 7.1, F3, F1, algebra]

9.1 The space $V$ with $\|u\|_V^2=\|u\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_2^2$ is complete, being a closed subspace of the graph completion; the eigenidentity gives $(u,u_j)_V=(1+\lambda_j)(u,u_j)_H$, so $\{u_j/\sqrt{1+\lambda_j}\}$ is orthonormal in $V$ and its orthogonal complement vanishes, because orthogonality in $V$ forces all $H$-coefficients of $u$ to vanish; hence [F5] gives completeness in $V$ and the expansion $\|u\|_V^2=\sum_j(1+\lambda_j)|(u,u_j)_H|^2$. [step 8.1, F5, algebra]

10.1 Wave branch: for $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and data $q_0\in V$, $q_1\in H$ put $\alpha_j=(q_0,u_j)_H$ and $\gamma_j=(q_1,u_j)_H$; for $\lambda_j>0$ set $a_j(t)=\alpha_j\cos(v_{\mathrm{wave}}\sqrt{\lambda_j}t)+\gamma_j\sin(v_{\mathrm{wave}}\sqrt{\lambda_j}t)/(v_{\mathrm{wave}}\sqrt{\lambda_j})$, and for $\lambda_j=0$ set $a_j(t)=\alpha_j+t\gamma_j$; [F6] verifies the ODE and the initial values, and the positive-mode energy $|a_j'|^2+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_j|a_j|^2=|\gamma_j|^2+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_j|\alpha_j|^2$ is constant by [F6]. [step 9.1, F6, algebra]

11.1 Since only finitely many eigenvalues lie in any bounded set and the zero sector is finite dimensional, the positive eigenvalues are bounded away from zero; the constant-energy identity therefore controls the $V$-displacement tail and the $H$-velocity tail uniformly in time, and the initial $V\times H$ summability of steps 9.1 and 10.1 makes all tails tend to zero, so finite modal sums converge in $C(K;V)$ for displacement and in $C(K;H)$ for velocity on every compact time interval $K$ with the prescribed initial data; the derivative statement passes to the limit by [F6]'s FTC estimate, and the finite equations pass to the variational equation in the distribution-in-time sense by $\|u\|_V$-convergence and density, while uniqueness follows from uniqueness of each scalar ODE and the completeness of the eigenbasis. [step 10.1, F5, F6, algebra] ∎

The abstract speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ is a mathematical parameter of this lemma; no physical identification or open-domain spectral claim is made, and no lossy or maximal-trace statement is asserted.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), and let $X$ be exactly the curl/div graph-norm completion of smooth-on-the-closure fields with $\nu\times u=0$ defined in [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]. If $u\in X$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$ weakly, and $\lambda\ge0$ satisfies

$$\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda\int_\Omega u\cdot v\qquad(v\in X),$$

then $u\in H^m(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ for every integer $m\ge1$ and has a $C^\infty$ representative on the closure (indeed a smooth ambient extension to a neighbourhood of the closure). For each $m$, $\|u\|_{H^m}\le C_{m,\Omega,\lambda}\|u\|_{H^1}$. The equations $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u=\lambda u$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, $\nu\times u=0$ and $\partial_\nu u_n+(\operatorname{div}\nu)u_n=0$ hold classically, where $u_n=u\cdot\nu$ and the normal is extended constant along collar normal lines. This includes zero eigenvalues and disconnected domains; it asserts neither equality with every maximal tangential-trace realization nor smoothness of arbitrary finite-energy modal sums.

## Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice; a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega$ with compact boundary, outward unit normal $\nu$ extended smoothly as a unit field in a collar, boundary curvature $\kappa=\operatorname{div}\nu$ on the boundary; the graph completion $X$ and its properties from [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]; a field $u\in X$ with $\operatorname{div}u=0$ and the full-$X$ eigenidentity of the Statement.

[F1] **Graph completion and its H-one structure.** $X$ is a closed $H^1$ subspace of fields with zero tangential trace, its graph norm is equivalent to the $H^1$ norm, the trace operator on $H^1$ is bounded ([[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]], [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]), and smooth PEC fields are dense in $X$ by its definition. The spectral-closure item also proves the Gaffney identity $\int_\Omega(|\operatorname{curl}w|^2+|\operatorname{div}w|^2-|\nabla w|^2)=\int_{\partial\Omega}\kappa\,w_n^2\,dS$ for smooth PEC $w$.

[F2] **Admissible tests.** For a localized flattened triple $V=(V_1,V_2,V_3)$ supported away from the artificial chart sides with zero traces of $V_1,V_2$ at $s=0$, the odd extension of $V_1,V_2$ and the even extension of $V_3$ are $H^1$ across the interface, and mollification with a kernel even in $s$ followed by an even cutoff produces smooth PEC fields converging in $H^1$; the first-order gluing and half-space trace facts are those of [[lem-em-dirichlet-resolvent-h-two-and-smooth-test-density]] and [[thm-wkp-extension-from-a-half-space]]. Interior compactly supported tests are produced by ordinary mollification.

[F3] **Commutator and Riesz tools.** The cutoff/difference-quotient commutator estimate controls the lower-order terms with smooth multipliers ([[lem-cutoff-difference-quotient-commutator-estimate]]); $L^2(S)$ is a Hilbert space so bounded functionals are represented ([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]); Cauchy-Schwarz, dominated convergence and the algebra of derivatives are available ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]], [[thm-dominated-convergence]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]).

[F4] **Extensions and embeddings.** $W^{k,p}$ extension from the half-space and from bounded smooth domains, higher-order Sobolev embeddings, and a fixed parameter-preserving smooth extension of smooth-domain fields to an ambient neighbourhood ([[thm-wkp-extension-from-a-half-space]], [[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]], [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]], [[lem-em-parameter-preserving-smooth-extension-on-a-smooth-domain]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Polarizing the Gaffney identity [F1] gives, for smooth PEC $u,v$, $\int_\Omega(\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v+\operatorname{div}u\operatorname{div}v)=\int_\Omega\nabla u:\nabla v+\int_{\partial\Omega}\kappa\,u_nv_n\,dS$: the integration-by-parts boundary term before imposing the traces is $\sum_{i,j}\int_{\partial\Omega}(\nu_ju_j\partial_iv_i-\nu_ju_i\partial_iv_j)$, and at the boundary $u=u_n\nu$, $v=v_n\nu$ with $\nu\cdot\partial_i\nu=0$, so it reduces to $\kappa u_nv_n$; the sign is positive for an outward sphere with $\kappa=2/R$, and no convexity is assumed. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 By the $H^1$ equivalence and bounded trace of [F1] the identity of step 1.1 extends to all $u,v\in X$; combining it with $\operatorname{div}u=0$ and the eigenidentity of the Statement gives the weak mixed boundary identity $\int_\Omega\nabla u:\nabla v+\int_{\partial\Omega}\kappa\,u_nv_n\,dS=\lambda\int_\Omega u\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$; no classical normal derivative has been assumed. [step 1.1, given, F1, algebra]

3.1 Flattening: shrink smooth boundary charts and take a finite cover of the compact boundary with nested half-boxes $(y_1,y_2,s)$, $s>0$ inside, and cutoffs away from artificial sides; choose a smooth orthonormal frame $Q=(\tau_1,\tau_2,\nu)$ with $\tau_2=\nu\times\tau_1$ and write $u=QU$. The $H^1$ trace has $TU_1=TU_2=0$ while $TU_3$ is free, and by [F2] every localized $H^1$ triple with these two vanishing traces is an admissible test for the identity of step 2.1 after odd/even extension, mollification and cut off; pull back and extend by zero outside the chart. [step 2.1, given, F2, algebra]

4.1 Local coupled weak system: expanding $\nabla(QU)$ in step 2.1 and transporting the volume and surface measures produces a real symmetric smooth principal matrix $a^{ij}$, uniformly positive on the smaller half-box and scalar in the component indices, such that for all admissible triples $V$ $\sum_m\int a^{ij}\partial_jU_m\partial_iV_m+\int_B\beta U_3V_3=\int f\cdot V+\sum_i\int G_i\cdot\partial_iV+\int_BhV_3$, where $B=\{s=0\}$, $\beta=\kappa J_B$ is smooth and possibly signed, $f=\lambda JU+\sum_iC_i\partial_iU+C_0U\in L^2$, $G_i=B_iU\in H^1$ for smooth matrix coefficients, and $h\in H^1(B)$ is an allowed boundary datum; this follows by expanding the finite products, the two differentiated factors producing the scalar $a^{ij}$ because $Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I$, while terms with derivatives of $Q$ and $U$ enter $f$, $G$ or $h$. [step 3.1, F3, algebra]

5.1 Tangential mixed estimate: for $k=1,2$ put $W=\delta_h^kU$ and test with $V=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2W)$ on a nested patch; the test is admissible by [F2], discrete integration by parts and the shifted product rule give the principal term $\sum_m\int\eta^2a^{ij}(x+he_k)\partial_jW_m\partial_iW_m\ge\alpha\|\eta\nabla W\|_2^2$, and all remaining terms involve $\delta_ha$, $\nabla\eta$, $\nabla U$, $W$ and the Robin product; [F3] bounds them by $\epsilon\|\eta\nabla W\|_2^2+C_\epsilon\|U\|_{H^1}^2$ on the larger patch using $\|W\|_2\le C\|\partial_kU\|_2$ and $\|\delta_{-h}(\eta^2W)\|_2\le C(\|\eta\nabla W\|_2+\|W\|_2)$ from the elementary line formula and Cauchy-Schwarz, the trace estimate $\|Tz\|_2^2\le\epsilon\|\nabla z\|_2^2+C_\epsilon\|z\|_2^2$ absorbing the Robin and boundary-datum terms even when $\beta$ has either sign; choosing the finitely many epsilons small gives $\|\eta\nabla\delta_h^kU\|_2\le C(\|U\|_{H^1}+\|f\|_2+\|G\|_{H^1}+\|h\|_{H^1(B)})$ uniformly for small $h\ne0$. [step 4.1, F2, F3, algebra]

6.1 Normal recovery: by step 5.1 each distributional tangential derivative of every $\partial_iU_m$ is an $L^2$ class, since its pairing with a smooth test is the limit of $\int\delta_h^k(\partial_iU_m)\psi$ and is a bounded $L^2$ functional, represented by [F3]'s Riesz theorem; interior quotient tests give the same conclusion away from the boundary; hence the interior equation $-\partial_i(a^{ij}\partial_jU_m)=f_m-\partial_iG_{i,m}$ together with $a^{33}\ge\alpha>0$ yields $a^{33}\partial_{33}U_m=\partial_iG_{i,m}-f_m-\sum_{(i,j)\ne(3,3)}a^{ij}\partial_{ij}U_m-\sum_{i,j}(\partial_ia^{ij})\partial_jU_m$ with every right-hand term in $L^2$, so all three second normal derivatives are $L^2$ and $U\in H^2$ locally; this does not presuppose a classical Robin derivative. [step 5.1, F3, algebra]

7.1 Bootstrap with boundary commutators: suppose $U\in H^{r+1}$ locally, $r\ge1$; then $f\in H^r$ and $G\in H^{r+1}$ because the eigenvalue term is $\lambda JU$ and the coefficients are smooth. For a tangential multi-index $\alpha$ of order $r$ put $Z=D_y^\alpha U\in H^1$; its first two traces still vanish, and trace commutation is justified by extending localized $H^{r+1}$ classes with the integer-order half-space extension [F4], mollifying in that norm and passing the continuous $H^1$ trace identity to the limit. Applying the weak system of step 4.1 to $Z$ by tangential integration by parts leaves the same principal and Robin terms with bulk datum $D_y^\alpha f\in L^2$, divergence datum $\widetilde G_i=D_y^\alpha G_i-\sum_{0<\gamma\le\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\gamma}(D_y^\gamma a^{ij})\partial_jD_y^{\alpha-\gamma}U\in H^1$ and boundary commutator $\widetilde h=-\sum_{0<\gamma\le\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\gamma}(D_y^\gamma\beta)TD_y^{\alpha-\gamma}U_3\in H^1(B)$: indeed $|\alpha-\gamma|\le r-1$, so the indicated derivative is $H^2$ and its trace and tangential derivative traces are $L^2$ by the $H^1$ trace and the just-proved commutation. Steps 5.1-6.1 then give $Z\in H^2$, controlling total order $r+2$ with at most two normal derivatives; differentiating the normal-recovery equation of step 6.1 and inducting on the number of normal derivatives at fixed total order (the non-$(3,3)$ terms have strictly fewer normal derivatives, and all differentiated coefficients and data have the available order) yields $U\in H^{r+2}$; nested patches and the finite boundary/interior cover give $u\in H^m(\Omega)$ for every integer $m$ with $\|u\|_{H^m}\le C_{m,\Omega,\lambda}\|u\|_{H^1}$. [step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, F4, F3, algebra]

8.1 Classical conclusion: for each $j$ choose $m>j+3/2$; the extension theorem and higher-order Sobolev embedding [F4] give continuous derivatives through order $j$ on the closure, compatible by weak-derivative uniqueness, and the fixed parameter-preserving smooth extension [F4] applied to the (time-constant) field yields one actual smooth ambient representative near the whole closure; therefore all jets have continuous one-sided boundary limits. The interior variational equation gives $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u=\lambda u$ pointwise ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [F3]), the tangential trace $\nu\times u=0$ is classical, and the boundary identity of step 1.1 tested with arbitrary smooth compactly supported normal traces, admissible by [F2], gives $\partial_\nu u_n+\kappa u_n=0$ pointwise; the unit-normal collar extension ensures $\partial_\nu u_n=(\partial_\nu u)\cdot\nu$, which agrees with the classical identity $\operatorname{div}u=\partial_\nu u_n+\kappa u_n$ for zero tangential trace, so $\operatorname{div}u=0$ holds classically. [step 7.1, F4, F3, algebra]

9.1 The argument covers $\lambda=0$ and disconnected smooth domains, since no component is singled out and the local estimates are globalized over the finite cover; it makes no smoothness assertion for arbitrary finite-energy modal sums and no identification with a maximal tangential-trace realization, and the full Axiom of Choice is carried from the completion, trace, extension, Hilbert and Sobolev suppliers. [step 7.1, step 8.1, given, F1, algebra] ∎

## Example

The following are explicit mathematical verifications of clauses of [[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]] and [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]; no measurement, physical identification or empirical claim is made.

(i) At degree $l=0$ the outgoing radial function of the spherical Hankel lemma is $h_0(z)=-ie^{iz}/z$, so for $k,R>0$ the Dirichlet-to-Neumann coefficient of [[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]] is

$$t_0=\frac{k\,h_0'(kR)}{h_0(kR)}=ik-\frac1R,$$

whose real part $-1/R$ is negative and whose imaginary part $k$ is positive, exactly as the exact bounds of that lemma require in degree zero.

(ii) In the spherical shell $a<|x|<b$, the field $u(x)=\operatorname{grad}|x|^{-1}=-x/|x|^3$ is smooth on the closure, nonzero, normal to both boundary spheres, curl-free and divergence-free: $u=\nabla\Phi$ with $\Phi(x)=|x|^{-1}$ harmonic off the origin, so $\operatorname{curl}u=\operatorname{curl}\nabla\Phi=0$ and $\operatorname{div}u=\Delta\Phi=0$ there. Thus $u$ lies in the PEC class $X$ of the cavity spectral lemma with zero curl, and it has curl eigenvalue zero: eliminating all topology zero modes would incorrectly discard this explicit admissible vector field.

## Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** $k>0$, $R>0$, the shell $a<|x|<b$ with $0<a<b$, and the functions $h_0(z)=-ie^{iz}/z$ and $\Phi(x)=|x|^{-1}$.

[L1] The degree-zero outgoing radial function is $h_0(z)=-ie^{iz}/z$ and the DtN coefficients of the spherical Hankel lemma satisfy $-(l+1)/R\le\operatorname{Re}t_l\le-1/R$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}t_l\le k$, with $t_l=kh_l'(kR)/h_l(kR)$ ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]).

[L2] The curl of a gradient vanishes on its domain ([[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]]), and $\Phi(x)=|x|^{-1}$ is smooth and harmonic on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, so $\Delta\Phi=0$ there ([[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]]).

[L3] The complex exponential is entire with derivative itself and the algebra of derivatives holds ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]).

[L4] The graph completion $X$ of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] contains every smooth field on the closure with $\nu\times u=0$, and the curl form there has nonnegative eigenvalues with the topology zero modes retained.



## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Logarithmic differentiation of $h_0(z)=-ie^{iz}/z$ by [L3] gives $h_0'(z)=-ie^{iz}\cdot i/z+ie^{iz}/z^2=h_0(z)(i-1/z)$; hence $kh_0'(kR)/h_0(kR)=k(i-1/(kR))=ik-1/R$, so $\operatorname{Re}t_0=-1/R<0$ and $\operatorname{Im}t_0=k>0$, consistent with [L1]. [given, L1, L3, algebra]

1.2 Since $\Phi$ is smooth on the shell and $u=\nabla\Phi$, [L2] gives $\operatorname{curl}u=0$ and $\operatorname{div}u=\Delta\Phi=0$ on $a<|x|<b$; on the boundary sphere $|x|=c$ the field is $u=-x/c^3$, a nonzero multiple of the outward normal, so its tangential part vanishes and $u$ is in the PEC class $X$ by [L4]. [given, L2, L4, algebra]

2.1 Because $\operatorname{curl}u=0$ and $u\ne0$, the field $u$ belongs to the kernel of the curl form on $V=\{w\in X:\operatorname{div}w=0\}$: the eigenidentity of [L4] holds with $\lambda=0$, so the zero eigenspace is nontrivial and must be retained; discarding all topology zero modes would delete this admissible vector field. [step 1.2, L4, algebra] ∎



The computation in (i) is the degree-zero instance of the exact DtN bounds; the field in (ii) is the explicit topology zero mode of the spherical shell, and no claim is made about other eigenvalues, about lossy media or about maximal tangential-trace realisations beyond the class $X$ of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]].

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), declared by the surface-integral and parameter-integral conventions below. Let $t_0<T$ and let $h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T])$ in the extension sense: $h$ is the restriction of a $C^\infty$ function on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Let $d\Omega$ be the surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$ of total mass $\int_{S^2}d\Omega=4\pi$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and define the spherical-mean family $$M(x,s,v):=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}h(x+sn,v)\,d\Omega(n),\qquad (x,s,v)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times[t_0,T].$$ Then $M$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times[t_0,T]$ in the same extension sense, and for every multi-index $\alpha$ in $x$ and all integers $m,l\ge0$ $$D_x^\alpha\partial_s^m\partial_v^lM(x,s,v)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}D_x^\alpha\partial_s^m\partial_v^l\bigl[h(x+sn,v)\bigr]\,d\Omega(n),$$ where the right-hand integrand is the corresponding iterated partial derivative of the composed map $(x,s,v)\mapsto h(x+sn,v)$; in particular $\partial_s[h(x+sn,v)]=\nabla h(x+sn,v)\cdot n$, so the $s$-derivatives are directional derivatives along $n$. Consequently, for every $c>0$ the map $\tilde H(x,t,v):=(t-v)\,M(x,c(t-v),v)$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]\times[t_0,T]$ in the extension sense, and for every fixed $x\in\mathbb R^3$ the map $(t,v)\mapsto\tilde H(x,t,v)$ is $C^\infty$ on an open neighbourhood of the closed triangle $\{(t,v):t_0\le v\le t\le T\}$. Nothing here assumes decay, compact support or boundedness of $h$; the statement is local in $(x,s,v)$ and uses uniform bounds only on compact parameter sets.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; times $t_0<T$; a $C^\infty$ function $h$ on an open set $\mathbb R^3\times J$ with $[t_0,T]\subset J$; and the surface measure $d\Omega$ on the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$ of total mass $\int_{S^2}d\Omega=4\pi$.

[F1] A map is of class $C^k$ when every word iterated coordinate partial derivative of order at most $k$ exists and is continuous, and of class $C^\infty$ when it is $C^k$ for every $k$; $D^\alpha f=\partial_0^{\alpha_0}\cdots\partial_{m-1}^{\alpha_{m-1}}f$ is the canonical-order multi-index derivative, and partial derivatives are the one-variable derivatives along coordinate lines ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

[F2] Chain rule: if $f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and $g$ at $f(a)$, then $D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a)$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

[F3] Finite sums, scalar multiples and products of $C^k$ Euclidean maps are $C^k$, and composites of composable $C^k$ maps are $C^k$, for every $k\in\mathbb N$ ([[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]]); sums, scalar multiples and products of differentiable real functions differentiate by the sum, scalar-multiple and product rules ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]).

[F4] If all first partial derivatives of $q$ exist on a neighbourhood of $a$ and are continuous at $a$, then $q$ is totally differentiable at $a$ with total derivative the Jacobian matrix; if $q$ is totally differentiable at $a$, then for every direction $u$ the directional derivative exists and $D_uq(a)=Dq(a)u=\sum_j\partial_jq(a)u_j$, which for scalar $q$ is $\langle\nabla q(a),u\rangle$ with the gradient $\nabla q$ of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], [[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

[F5] Parameter integrals: if $K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is compact, measurable and of finite Lebesgue measure, $a<b$, and $f$ and $\partial_tf$ are continuous on a neighbourhood of $K\times[a,b]$, then $t\mapsto\int_Kf(x,t)\,dx$ is differentiable on $[a,b]$ with derivative $\int_K\partial_tf(x,t)\,dx$; the same conclusion holds, under the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], with surface measure on a fixed compact $C^1$ hypersurface in place of $K$; nothing is asserted for moving parameter sets or singularities crossing the integration set ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]]).

[F6] On a compact embedded $C^1$ hypersurface $S$ the surface integral is defined by the finite chart formula with Gram density; for signed functions with $\int_S|f|\,dS<\infty$ it is the difference of the integrals of the positive and negative parts; the notation of this item fixes $\int_{S^2}1\,d\Omega=4\pi$ for the unit sphere $S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:\langle n,n\rangle=1\}$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

[F7] For nonnegative measurable $f\le g$ one has $\int f\le\int g$, and $\int cf=c\int f$ for $c\ge0$ ([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]).

[F8] Mean value theorem: if $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$, then there is $c\in(a,b)$ with $f(b)-f(a)=f'(c)(b-a)$ ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]).

[F9] Closed boxes in $\mathbb R^m$ are compact in the Euclidean metric, and a continuous real-valued function on a nonempty compact metric space attains a maximum and a minimum ([[thm-heine-borel-rn]], [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]).

[F10] Cauchy-Schwarz: $|\sum_{j}u_jv_j|\le(\sum_ju_j^2)^{1/2}(\sum_jv_j^2)^{1/2}$ for real vectors, the right-hand factors being Euclidean norms ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$: every at most countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The setting and the reduction to the open set $\Omega$. Let $h$ also denote the $C^\infty$ function on the open set $\mathbb R^3\times J$ whose restriction to $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ is the $h$ of the statement, put $\Omega:=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times J$, an open subset of $\mathbb R^5$, and let $S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:\langle n,n\rangle=1\}$ carry the surface measure $d\Omega$ of total mass $4\pi$ of [F6]. Define $M(x,s,v):=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}h(x+sn,v)\,d\Omega(n)$ for $(x,s,v)\in\Omega$; its restriction to the closed set $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times[t_0,T]$ is the family of the statement, so every assertion proved below on $\Omega$, or on an open neighbourhood of a closed subset of $\Omega$, restricts to the corresponding extension-sense assertion of the statement. All surface integrals are read under the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention carried by [F5] and [F6]. [given, A1, F5, F6]

1.2 The composed integrand. Define $\Phi:\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^4$ by $\Phi(x,s,v,n):=(x+sn,v)$. Each component of $\Phi$ is a finite sum of products of coordinate functions, so $\Phi$ is $C^\infty$ on the open set $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$ by [F3], and $\Phi$ takes values in $\mathbb R^3\times J$. Hence $H:=h\circ\Phi$ is $C^\infty$ on $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$ by the composition clause of [F3], so every word iterated partial derivative $D^vH$ exists and is continuous on $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$ by [F1]. At $p=(x,s,v)\in\Omega$ and $n\in S^2$, the chain rule [F2], total differentiability of $h$ [F4] and $\partial_s\Phi(p,n)=(n,0)$ give $\partial_sH(p,n)=Dh(x+sn,v)(n,0)=\sum_{j<3}\partial_jh(x+sn,v)\,n_j=\langle\nabla h(x+sn,v),n\rangle$, the directional derivative of $h$ at $(x+sn,v)$ in direction $(n,0)$ [F4]; applying the same computation to the already differentiated integrands shows that the iterated derivatives $D_x^\alpha\partial_s^m\partial_v^lH(p,n)$ are the corresponding iterated partial derivatives of the composed map $(x,s,v)\mapsto h(x+sn,v)$, which is $H$ itself, and in particular that $\partial_s^mH(p,n)$ is the $m$-th iterated derivative at $\lambda=s$ of $\lambda\mapsto h(x+\lambda n,v)$. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4]

2.1 Local bounds on compact boxes. Let $K=\prod_{j<5}[a_j,b_j]$ be a nonempty closed box contained in $\Omega$. Then $K\times[-1,1]^3$ is a nonempty closed box in $\mathbb R^8$, hence compact by [F9], and by step 1.2 every $|D^vH|$ is continuous on the open set $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$, which contains $K\times[-1,1]^3$; so by [F9] each $|D^vH|$ attains a maximum there and $C_v:=\max_{K\times[-1,1]^3}|D^vH|$ is a finite nonnegative real number with $|D^vH(p,n)|\le C_v$ for all $(p,n)\in K\times S^2$, because $S^2\subseteq[-1,1]^3$. [given, step 1.2, F9]

2.2 Continuity of parameter sphere integrals. Claim: if $q:\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ is continuous with continuous first partial derivatives, $K\subseteq\Omega$ is a nonempty closed box and $|\partial_{p_j}q(p,n)|\le C_j$ for all $(p,n)\in K\times S^2$ and all $j<5$, then $\bigl|\int_{S^2}q(p,n)\,d\nu(n)-\int_{S^2}q(p_0,n)\,d\nu(n)\bigr|\le\bigl(\sum_{j<5}C_j^2\bigr)^{1/2}|p-p_0|$ for all $p,p_0\in K$, where $\nu:=d\Omega/4\pi$. Indeed, for fixed $n\in S^2$ the function $g(\lambda):=q(p_0+\lambda u,n)$, $u:=p-p_0$, is defined on $[0,1]$ because the box is convex, and the affine map $\lambda\mapsto(p_0+\lambda u,n)$ has constant partial derivatives, hence is totally differentiable by [F4]; the chain rule [F2] with total differentiability of $q$ [F4] therefore gives $g'(\lambda)=Dq(p_0+\lambda u,n)(u,0)=\sum_{j<5}\partial_{p_j}q(p_0+\lambda u,n)\,u_j$ at every $\lambda\in(0,1)$, and the mean value theorem [F8] bounds $|q(p,n)-q(p_0,n)|\le\sup_{\lambda}\bigl|\sum_j\partial_{p_j}q(p_0+\lambda u,n)\,u_j\bigr|\le\bigl(\sum_jC_j^2\bigr)^{1/2}|u|$ by Cauchy-Schwarz [F10] and the local bounds. Integrating this pointwise bound against $\nu$: the signed surface integral is the difference of the integrals of the positive and negative parts [F6], so $\bigl|\int_{S^2}q(p,\cdot)\,d\nu-\int_{S^2}q(p_0,\cdot)\,d\nu\bigr|\le\int_{S^2}|q(p,n)-q(p_0,n)|\,d\nu(n)\le\bigl(\sum_jC_j^2\bigr)^{1/2}|u|\int_{S^2}d\nu=\bigl(\sum_jC_j^2\bigr)^{1/2}|u|$, where the chart formula of [F6] with the monotonicity and scalar rules of [F7] gives monotonicity, the bound $\int_{S^2}c\,d\nu=c$ for constants $c\ge0$, and $\int_{S^2}d\nu=1$ from the normalisation $\int_{S^2}d\Omega=4\pi$ of [F6]. [given, step 1.2, F2, F4, F6, F7, F8, F10]

3.1 Induction: every word derivative of $M$ exists with the differentiated-integral formula, continuously. Claim: for every word $v$ in the five coordinate directions of $\Omega$, the iterated derivative $D^vM$ exists on $\Omega$ and equals $\int_{S^2}D^vH(p,n)\,d\nu(n)$, and this integral is continuous on $\Omega$. Prove the claim by induction on the length $r$ of the word. For $r=0$ it is the definition of $M$ in step 1.1 together with $\nu=d\Omega/4\pi$, and continuity is step 2.2 applied with $q:=H$, whose partial derivatives $D^{e_j}H$ are continuous with bounds $C_{e_j}$ on $K\times S^2$ by steps 1.2 and 2.1. Assume the claim for all words of length $r$; let $v$ be such a word and $j$ a coordinate direction, and fix $p_0\in\Omega$, a nonempty closed box $K\subseteq\Omega$ with $p_0$ in its interior and coordinate intervals $[a_j,b_j]$. For fixed coordinates other than the $j$-th and $t\in[a_j,b_j]$, put $Q(n,t):=D^vH(p(t),n)$, where $p(t)$ is the point of the $j$-th coordinate line with $j$-th coordinate $t$; then both $Q$ and $\partial_tQ=D^{v+e_j}H(p(t),n)$ are continuous on an open neighbourhood of $S^2\times[a_j,b_j]$ in $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, being restrictions of the continuous $D^vH$ and $D^{v+e_j}H$ of step 1.2. By the surface clause of [F5], $t\mapsto\int_{S^2}Q(n,t)\,d\Omega(n)$ is differentiable on $[a_j,b_j]$ with derivative $\int_{S^2}\partial_tQ(n,t)\,d\Omega(n)$; multiplying by the constant $1/4\pi$ (the scalar multiple rule for one-variable derivatives, [F3]) gives $\partial_j\int_{S^2}D^vH\,d\nu=\int_{S^2}D^{v+e_j}H\,d\nu$ on the line through $p_0$; with the induction hypothesis this shows $D^{v+e_j}M=\int_{S^2}D^{v+e_j}H\,d\nu$ on that line, hence on all of $\Omega$ since $p_0$ and $j$ are arbitrary, and this integral is continuous on $\Omega$ by step 2.2 applied to $q:=D^{v+e_j}H$, whose partial derivatives $D^{v+e_j+e_i}H$ are continuous by step 1.2 with bounds $C_{v+e_j+e_i}$ on $K\times S^2$ by step 2.1. This closes the induction. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, F1, F3, F5]

4.1 $M$ is $C^\infty$ and satisfies the displayed formula. By step 3.1 every word iterated partial derivative of $M$ exists and is continuous on the open set $\Omega$, so $M$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\Omega$ by [F1]; in particular its restriction to $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times[t_0,T]$ is $C^\infty$ in the extension sense of the statement. Every canonical-order derivative $D_x^\alpha\partial_s^m\partial_v^lM$ is one of the word derivatives covered by step 3.1, so it equals the sphere integral of the corresponding word derivative $D_x^\alpha\partial_s^m\partial_v^lH$ of the composed map, and step 1.2 identifies those integrands as the corresponding iterated partial derivatives of $(x,s,v)\mapsto h(x+sn,v)$; the asserted $s$-derivative statements are those of step 1.2. [step 1.2, step 3.1, F1]

5.1 The composed map $\tilde H$ and the local nature of the argument. Let $c>0$ and define $\tilde H(x,t,v):=(t-v)M(x,c(t-v),v)$ on the open set $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times J$. The map $\Psi(x,t,v):=(x,c(t-v),v)$ has components that are finite sums of products of coordinate functions, so it is $C^\infty$ by [F3] and takes values in $\Omega$; hence $(x,t,v)\mapsto M(\Psi(x,t,v))$ is $C^\infty$ by composition [F3] with step 4.1, and multiplying by the $C^\infty$ function $t-v$ gives that $\tilde H$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times J$ by [F3]. Since $[t_0,T]\subset J$ and the closed triangle $\Delta=\{(t,v):t_0\le v\le t\le T\}$ is contained in $[t_0,T]\times[t_0,T]\subset J\times J$, the restriction shows that $\tilde H$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]\times[t_0,T]$ in the extension sense, and for each fixed $x$ the map $(t,v)\mapsto\tilde H(x,t,v)$ is $C^\infty$ on the open neighbourhood $J\times J$ of $\Delta$. The whole argument used only the bounds of step 2.1 on compact parameter boxes and the compactness of $S^2$; no boundedness, decay or compact spatial support of $h$ was assumed or used. [step 2.1, step 4.1, F3] ∎
