## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the weak-solvability and regularity lemmas below ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in the local graph sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive, that is $\alpha|\xi|^2\le\xi\cdot\varepsilon(x)\xi\le\beta|\xi|^2$ for all $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ and $x\in\Omega$ and some $0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty$, and let $\rho$ be smooth on $\overline\Omega$. The Euclidean inner product is that of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]; at a boundary point with outward unit normal $\nu$ the outward conormal vector is $\varepsilon\nu$ and the outward conormal derivative is $\nu\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u$. Here $H^1(\Omega)$ and $H_0^1(\Omega)$ are the Sobolev spaces of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and the trace $T$ is that of the trace operator on the bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega$. Then:

(a) **Dirichlet.** For every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ there is exactly one weak solution $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $Tu=g$ of $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u\,dx=\int_\Omega\rho v\,dx$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$; it depends continuously on the data, $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|\rho\|_{L^2}+\|g\|_{H^{1/2}})$, has a $C^\infty$ representative on $\overline\Omega$, and satisfies the classical equations $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ in $\Omega$ and $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$.

(b) **Neumann.** Let $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ be a smooth outward conormal datum satisfying $\int_{\Omega_j}\rho\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g\,dS=0$ on every connected component $\Omega_j$ of $\Omega$. Then there is a weak solution of $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=\int_\Omega\rho v+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for all $v\in H^1(\Omega)$; it is unique up to a separately chosen additive constant on each component, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}u=0$ on every component gives a unique normalised solution which is $C^\infty$ on each closed component and satisfies the classical equations $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ in $\Omega$ and $\nu\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$. In particular on a connected domain the compatibility is $\int_{\partial\Omega}g=-\int_\Omega\rho$, with a single additive constant.

(c) **Transmission.** Let there be finitely many pairwise disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, let $\varepsilon$ be piecewise smooth on the closures of the resulting pieces and uniformly positive in the above sense, let $\rho$ be piecewise smooth on the closed pieces and let $\sigma$ be a smooth sheet charge on the union of the interfaces; the weak right-hand side is $\int_\Omega\rho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma\,Tv$, together with $\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ in the Neumann case. Prescribe either the smooth outer Dirichlet datum of (a), or the smooth outer Neumann datum of (b) with the componentwise compatibility condition $\int_{\Omega_j}\rho+\sum_{\Gamma\subset\Omega_j}\int_\Gamma\sigma+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$ for every component $\Omega_j$. With outer Dirichlet data the globally $H^1$ solution is unique; with outer Neumann data it exists exactly when that compatibility holds and is then unique modulo componentwise additive constants, the zero componentwise means making it unique; the equal one-sided traces and $C^\infty$ regularity on each closed side hold in either case, and the flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon\nabla u]=-\sigma$ in the sign convention of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], where $n$ is a chosen unit normal on the interface and $[\varepsilon\nabla u]=\varepsilon^+\nabla u^+-\varepsilon^-\nabla u^-$ is the difference from the $n$-positive side to the other.

Edge and junction points, reentrant corners, coefficient loss of regularity and general piecewise classical regularity beyond finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces are excluded. The existence content of all three parts is that of the two weak solvability lemmas; this theorem states the combined existence-and-regularity conclusions on the declared domains and adds no existence assertion beyond them.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]); a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ with the graph property of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]; a uniformly positive coefficient $\varepsilon$, smooth on the closure in parts (a)–(b) and piecewise smooth on the closed pieces with finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces in part (c); a smooth bulk datum $\rho$ (piecewise smooth in (c)); a smooth sheet charge $\sigma$ in (c); smooth boundary data $g$; the conventions $\operatorname{Sym}^3$, outward conormal vector $\varepsilon\nu$, outward conormal derivative $\nu\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u$, and the trace $T$ and spaces $H^1$, $H_0^1$ of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and the trace operator.

[L1] Weak prescribed-trace Dirichlet existence: for a bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega$, uniformly elliptic measurable $\varepsilon$, $\rho\in L^2(\Omega)$ and $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$, there is exactly one $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $Tu=g$ solving $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=\int_\Omega\rho v$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$, and $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|\rho\|_{L^2}+\|g\|_{H^{1/2}})$ ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]).

[L2] Smooth-domain elliptic regularity: on a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, with smooth uniformly positive $\varepsilon$ and smooth $\rho$ on the closure, the weak solution of $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ with smooth Dirichlet data, or with smooth compatible Neumann flux data, is $C^\infty$ on the closure and satisfies the classical equation and boundary data; for finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$ with piecewise smooth positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth $\rho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, the weak solution is smooth on each closed side ([[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]).

[L3] Weak Neumann and transmission existence: with $\ell(v)=\int_\Omega\rho v+\langle g,Tv\rangle$ on $H^1(\Omega)$ for $\rho\in L^2$ and $g\in H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$, a weak Neumann solution $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=\ell(v)$ for all $v\in H^1(\Omega)$ exists if and only if $\ell(1)=0$, and is then unique up to an additive constant, the normalisation $\int_\Omega u=0$ making it unique; on finitely many components compatibility and normalisation are imposed separately on each component; for finitely many disjoint smooth stationary interfaces with piecewise smooth uniformly elliptic $\varepsilon$, bulk $\rho\in L^2$ and prescribed sheet charge $\sigma$ defining a bounded trace functional on $H^1$, the same argument gives weak Dirichlet or compatible Neumann existence for the transmission problem, the globally $H^1$ potential has identical one-sided traces, and where the solution is classically smooth on each side integration by parts gives the jump $n\cdot[\varepsilon\nabla u]=-\sigma$ ([[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]).

[L4] Divergence theorem for bounded piecewise $C^1$ domains: for a bounded domain with the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation and a $C^1$ field on the closures of the pieces, the integral of the divergence equals the sum of the outward fluxes over the faces, counted once off the seam sets ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]]).

[L5] First Green identity: for a bounded $C^1$ domain and $u\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$, $v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, $\int_\Omega(v\Delta u+\nabla u\cdot\nabla v)=\int_{\partial\Omega}v\,\partial_\nu u\,dS$ ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The domain, coefficients, data and conventions of the Given paragraph above, with the smooth Dirichlet datum $g$, the smooth compatible outward conormal datum $g$, or the transmission configuration of the Statement.

1.1 **The Dirichlet branch: existence, uniqueness, exact trace, continuous dependence.** Let $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)\subset H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ and $\rho\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)\subset L^2(\Omega)$. By [L1] with the uniformly elliptic smooth coefficient $\varepsilon$ there is exactly one $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $Tu=g$ and $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=\int_\Omega\rho v$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$, and $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|\rho\|_{L^2}+\|g\|_{H^{1/2}})$; this gives the existence, uniqueness, exact prescribed trace and continuous dependence asserted in (a). [L1]

1.2 **The Neumann branch.** Let $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ and put $\ell(v):=\int_\Omega\rho v+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$; since $g$ is bounded and $T$ is bounded into $L^2(\partial\Omega)$, $\ell$ is a bounded linear functional on $H^1(\Omega)$ of the form required by [L3] with $H^{-1/2}$ density represented by the smooth function $g$. Testing the weak identity with the constant $1$ on a component $\Omega_j$ gives $0=\int_{\Omega_j}\nabla1\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=\ell(1_{\Omega_j})=\int_{\Omega_j}\rho+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g$, so the componentwise compatibility is necessary; it is also the hypothesis of the Statement. By [L3] there is then a weak solution, unique up to one additive constant per component, and the normalisation $\int_{\Omega_j}u=0$ makes it unique; on each connected component the upgrade part of [L2] applies with the smooth datum $g$ and gives $C^\infty$ local classical solutions satisfying $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ and $\nu\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=g$, the different choices of the additive constant changing nothing in the equation. On a connected $\Omega$ this is $0=\int_\Omega\rho+\int_{\partial\Omega}g$, that is $\int_{\partial\Omega}g=-\int_\Omega\rho$. [L2, L3, algebra]

1.3 **Transmission: weak existence, unique traces and the conditional jump.** In the configuration of part (c), let $\Lambda(v):=\int_\Omega\rho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma\,Tv$, a bounded functional on $H^1(\Omega)$ because $\sigma$ is smooth on the compact interface union and $T$ is bounded into $L^2$ of that finite union. With outer Dirichlet data the prescribed-data part and with outer Neumann data the weak Neumann part of [L3] apply with the additional bounded trace functional $\Lambda$; hence a globally $H^1$ weak solution exists, is unique for outer Dirichlet data, and for outer Neumann data exists exactly when $\Lambda(v)+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ vanishes on the constants of every component, that is when the stated compatibility holds, and is then unique modulo componentwise constants, the zero componentwise means fixing it. By the transmission part of [L3] the globally $H^1$ potential has identical one-sided traces, and wherever it is classically smooth on each side, integration by parts gives the jump $n\cdot[\varepsilon\nabla u]=-\sigma$ in the stated sign convention. [L3]

2.1 **Classical upgrade of the Dirichlet branch.** The solution of step 1.1 is the weak solution of $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ in $\Omega$ with the smooth Dirichlet datum $g$: for compactly supported test fields the weak identity is exactly the distributional equation $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$, where the divergence is that of a $C^1$ field once the classical upgrade below identifies $u$ as such, and the boundary values are the prescribed ones by trace uniqueness. Applying the Dirichlet part of [L2] with the smooth $\rho$ and smooth $g$ yields the $C^\infty$ representative on $\overline\Omega$ satisfying the classical equation and boundary values. [L2, step 1.1]

2.2 **Transmission: one-sided classical regularity and the unconditional jump.** The weak solution of step 1.3 is the weak solution of the transmission problem for the piecewise smooth positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth $\rho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$ of the Statement, with either the smooth outer Dirichlet datum or the smooth compatible outer Neumann datum. By the interface part of [L2] it is $C^\infty$ on each closed side; in particular it is classically smooth on each side of every interface, so the conditional jump identity of step 1.3 applies and the flux jump $n\cdot[\varepsilon\nabla u]=-\sigma$ holds unconditionally in the stated class. The equal one-sided traces are those of step 1.3, and on each closed side the classical equation $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ holds because the weak identity tested against compactly supported fields localized in the interior of a side is the distributional equation there. The interface integration by parts underlying the jump is the divergence theorem [L4] applied to the $C^1$ field $v\,\varepsilon\nabla u$ on the two pieces and the Green identity [L5]; the smooth chain and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] are the calculus conventions used in transporting the equation to the closed pieces, and the Euclidean pairings are those of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. [L2, L4, L5, step 1.3]

3.1 **Assembly and exclusions.** Part (a) is steps 1.1 and 2.1, part (b) is step 1.2, and part (c) is steps 1.3 and 2.2, with the definitions of the conormal vector and derivative fixed in the Statement. ## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the modal DtN/trace suppliers, covering the Countable Choice used by the local UCP supplier. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) whose exterior $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ is connected, let $k>0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$. Suppose $u$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$, solves $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ on $D$ with the Euclidean Laplacian $\Delta$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), vanishes on $\partial O$, and is outgoing in the class of [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]: its trace $f=u|_{S_R}$ lies in $H^{1/2}(S_R)$ and its normal derivative on $S_R$ is $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense of that lemma. Then $u=0$ on $D$. No decay rate, asymptotic expansion or pointwise Sommerfeld formula beyond the stated outgoing class is assumed.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); a bounded $C^\infty$ obstacle $O$ with connected exterior $D$; $k>0$; $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$; and a $C^\infty(\overline D)$ solution $u$ of $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ on $D$, vanishing on $\partial O$, outgoing in the modal class of the sphere DtN lemma, with trace $f=u|_{S_R}\in H^{1/2}(S_R)$ and normal derivative $T_Rf$.

[L1] First Green identity on a bounded $C^1$ domain: for real $w\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ and $v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, $\int_\Omega(v\Delta w+\nabla w\cdot\nabla v)\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}v\,\partial_\nu w\,dS$ ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]).

[L2] The Laplacian is $\Delta f=\operatorname{div}\nabla f=\sum_i\partial_i\partial_if$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]).

[L3] Bounded $C^k$ domains have the local graph property, so $D\cap B_R(0)$ is a bounded domain whose boundary is the disjoint union of the smooth pieces $\partial O$ and $S_R$ ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]).

[L4] Sphere DtN lemma: for $k,R>0$ the map $T_Rf=\sum_{l,m}t_lf_{lm}Y^R_{lm}$ is bounded $H^{1/2}(S_R)\to H^{-1/2}(S_R)$ with $\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0$ and $\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2>0$ for $f\ne0$; the function $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$, $r\ge R$, is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy exterior solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$ and normal derivative $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense ([[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]).

[L5] Bounded-potential unique continuation: for nonempty open connected $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, $V\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ and $\psi\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ with $\Delta\psi=V\psi$ distributionally, vanishing of $\psi$ on a nonempty open subset of $\Omega$ forces $\psi=0$ on $\Omega$ ([[thm-bounded-potential-weak-unique-continuation-in-three-dimensions]]).

**Choice accounting.** The Axiom of Choice is assumed in the Statement and is carried by the DtN/trace supplier [L4]; the local unique-continuation supplier [L5] carries Countable Choice, which AC supplies. The Green-identity, positivity and propagation steps below introduce no further choice.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The data and solution of the Given paragraph above.

1.1 **Green's identity on the truncated exterior and vanishing of the imaginary boundary pairing.** The truncated region $A:=D\cap B_R(0)$ is a bounded open set whose boundary is the disjoint union of $\partial O$ and $S_R$, with the outward normal of $A$ equal to the outer normal of $S_R$ and to the inward normal of $\partial O$ [L3]. Applying the first Green identity [L1] to the real and imaginary parts of $u$ and adding, with $v$ the corresponding part, gives the complex form $\int_A(\operatorname{Re}(\overline u\,\Delta u)+|\nabla u|^2)\,dx=\int_{\partial A}\operatorname{Re}(\overline u\,\partial_\nu u)\,dS$; the volume integrand is $\operatorname{Re}(\overline u(-k^2u))+|\nabla u|^2=|\nabla u|^2-k^2|u|^2$ by [L2] and the Helmholtz equation, so the volume term is real, and the inner boundary contributes zero because $u=0$ on $\partial O$. The boundary term is therefore the real number $\int_A(|\nabla u|^2-k^2|u|^2)\,dx$, and its imaginary part is zero: taking imaginary parts gives $\int_{S_R}\operatorname{Im}(\overline u\,\partial_\nu u)\,dS=0$. Since $\partial_\nu u=T_Rf$ on $S_R$ in the weak trace sense of [L4] and $f=u|_{S_R}$, the last identity is the vanishing of the imaginary part of the dual pairing, $\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=0$. [L1, L2, L3]

2.1 **The boundary trace vanishes.** By [L4] the imaginary pairing of the DtN operator is $\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2$ with every coefficient $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$. Since the left side is zero by step 1.1 and every term of the sum is nonnegative, every coefficient $f_{lm}$ vanishes, so $f=0$; consequently also $T_Rf=0$ and, by the trace identity of [L4], $\|f\|_{H^{1/2}(S_R)}=0$. [L4, step 1.1]

3.1 **Vanishing on the exterior of the large sphere.** Restricted to $\{r>R\}$, the field $u$ is an outgoing finite-local-energy solution of the Helmholtz equation with trace $f=0$ on $S_R$ and normal derivative $T_Rf=0$: $u$ is $C^\infty$ on the closed region $\{r\ge R\}$, hence in every $H^1(\{R<|x|<R_1\})$, and its trace and weak normal derivative on $S_R$ are the ones named in the statement. By the uniqueness clause of [L4] there is exactly one such solution, namely the outgoing series with coefficients $f_{lm}=0$; hence $u=0$ on $\{r>R\}$. Since $u$ also vanishes on $\partial O$, both regions on which the vanishing is known are nonempty open subsets of $D$ (the set $D\cap\{r>R\}$ is nonempty because $D$ is the exterior of a bounded obstacle), so $u$ vanishes on the nonempty open set $D\cap\{r>R\}$. [L4, step 2.1]

4.1 **Unique continuation on $D$.** The real and imaginary parts of $u$ are $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$, hence in $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$, and satisfy $\Delta w=-k^2w$ on $D$ because $\Delta u=-k^2u$; the coefficient $V\equiv-k^2$ lies in $L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ and $D$ is nonempty, open and connected. By step 3.1 each of them vanishes on the nonempty open subset $D\cap\{r>R\}$, so [L5] applied to $w=\operatorname{Re}u$ and $w=\operatorname{Im}u$ on $\Omega=D$ gives $\operatorname{Re}u=\operatorname{Im}u=0$ on $D$, that is, $u=0$ on $D$, as asserted. [L5, step 3.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, as used by the variational, Sobolev and compact-spectral suppliers and by the Fredholm alternative ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) whose exterior $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ is connected, let $k>0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$. Write $A:=B_R(0)\setminus\overline O$ and let $n$ be the outward unit normal field of $A$, so that on $\partial O$ the field $n$ points into $O$; put $\kappa:=\operatorname{div}n|_{\partial O}$ and, for a field $E$ on $\partial O$, $E_n:=E\cdot n|_{\partial O}$.

For a smooth $\mathbb C$-valued tangential field $e_T$ on $\partial O$ put
$$\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T:=\operatorname{div}\widetilde e_T-\partial_n(\widetilde e_T\cdot n)\quad\text{on }\partial O,$$
where $\widetilde e_T$ is any smooth extension of $e_T$ to a neighbourhood of $\partial O$; the expression is independent of the extension and equals the surface divergence of $e_T$ with respect to the Euclidean surface measure of $\partial O$. Write $\Delta$ for the Euclidean Laplacian ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), acting componentwise, and for a vector field $f=(f_1,f_2,f_3)$ on $S_R$ write $T_Rf:=(T_Rf_1,T_Rf_2,T_Rf_3)$ with $T_R$ the scalar Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]].

Then there is exactly one field $E\in C^\infty(\overline D;\mathbb C^3)$ with
$$(\Delta+k^2)E=0\ \text{on }D,\qquad \operatorname{div}E=0\ \text{on }D,\qquad E_{\text{tangential}}=e_T\ \text{on }\partial O,$$
which is outgoing on the sphere $S_R$ in the modal sense of that lemma: its trace $f:=E|_{S_R}$ lies in $H^{1/2}(S_R;\mathbb C^3)$ and the normal derivative of $E$ on $S_R$ equals $T_Rf$ componentwise in the weak trace sense of the sphere DtN lemma. With these data the normal boundary values of $E$ on $\partial O$ satisfy the closure relation
$$\partial_nE_n+(\operatorname{div}n)E_n=-\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T$$
as an identity of $C^\infty$ functions on $\partial O$. No scalar Dirichlet condition is imposed on the three Cartesian components of $E$, and no decay rate, asymptotic expansion or pointwise Sommerfeld formula beyond the stated modal outgoing class is assumed.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); a bounded $C^\infty$ obstacle $O$ with connected exterior $D$; $k>0$; $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$; the truncated annulus $A=B_R(0)\setminus\overline O$ with outward unit normal $n$ and $\kappa=\operatorname{div}n|_{\partial O}$; a smooth $\mathbb C$-valued tangential field $e_T$ on $\partial O$; the conventions of the fields $E_n$, $\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T$, $T_Rf$ explained in the Statement, and the notation $H^m$, $H^m_{\mathrm{loc}}$ of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]].

[L1] Sphere Dirichlet-to-Neumann lemma: for $k,R>0$ the map $T_Rf=\sum_{l,m}t_lf_{lm}Y^R_{lm}$ is bounded $H^{1/2}(S_R)\to H^{-1/2}(S_R)$ with $\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0$ and $\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2>0$ for $f\ne0$; for every $f\in H^{1/2}(S_R)$ the outgoing series $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)\,R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$, $r\ge R$, is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy exterior solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$ and normal derivative $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense; it is smooth away from the sphere, and for smooth $f$ it satisfies the ordinary Sommerfeld condition ([[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]).

[L2] Exterior scalar uniqueness: if $O$ has bounded $C^\infty$ boundary, $D$ is connected, $k>0$, $u\in C^\infty(\overline D)$ solves $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ on $D$, vanishes on $\partial O$ and is outgoing in the class of [L1], then $u=0$ on $D$ ([[lem-em-exterior-outgoing-scalar-uniqueness]]).

[L3] Weak prescribed-trace Dirichlet existence: for a bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega$, a uniformly elliptic measurable coefficient $\varepsilon$, $\rho\in L^2(\Omega)$ and $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$, there is exactly one $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $Tu=g$ solving $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=\int_\Omega\rho v$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$, with $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|\rho\|_{L^2}+\|g\|_{H^{1/2}})$ ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]).

[L4] Smooth-domain elliptic regularity: on a bounded $C^\infty$ domain with smooth uniformly positive $\varepsilon$ and smooth $\rho$ on the closure, the weak solution with smooth Dirichlet data $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ is $C^\infty$ on the closure and satisfies the classical equation and boundary values ([[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]).

[L5] Bounded-potential unique continuation: for nonempty open connected $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, $V\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ and $\psi\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ with $\Delta\psi=V\psi$ distributionally, vanishing of $\psi$ on a nonempty open subset of $\Omega$ forces $\psi=0$ on $\Omega$ ([[thm-bounded-potential-weak-unique-continuation-in-three-dimensions]]).

[L6] Interior $H^2$ regularity: if $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ is a local weak solution of $-\Delta u=f$ with $f\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, then $u\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ ([[thm-interior-h-two-regularity-for-divergence-form-equations]]).

[L7] Interior $H^{k+2}$ regularity: if $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ is a local weak solution of $-\Delta u=f$ with $f\in H^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, $k\ge0$, then $u\in H^{k+2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ ([[thm-interior-h-k-plus-two-elliptic-regularity]]).

[L8] Riesz representation: every bounded linear functional on a real or complex Hilbert space is represented by a unique vector ([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]).

[L9] Fredholm alternative: for a compact operator $K$ on a Banach space, $I-K$ is injective if and only if it is surjective, and in that case it is boundedly invertible ([[thm-fredholm-alternative-for-identity-minus-compact]]).

[L10] Trace operator: on a bounded $C^1$ domain the trace $T:W^{1,p}(\Omega)\to L^p(\partial\Omega)$ is bounded and equals classical restriction on continuous Sobolev functions ([[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]).

[L11] Sobolev-Gauss-Green formula: for a bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega$, $u,v\in W^{1,2}(\Omega)$ and every $i$, $\int_\Omega u\,\partial_iv=-\int_\Omega(\partial_iu)v+\int_{\partial\Omega}(Tu)(Tv)\nu_i\,dS$ ([[thm-sobolev-gauss-green-formula-on-c-one-domains]]).

[L12] Half-space strip trace estimate: for $u$ smooth with compact support in the closed half-space and $g=u(\cdot,0)$ one has $h|g(x')|^2\le 2(\int_0^h|u|^2dt+h^2\int_0^h|\partial_nu|^2dt)$ for a.e. $x'$ and every $h>0$ ([[thm-trace-estimate-on-the-half-space]]).

[L13] Extension theorem for bounded smooth domains: every bounded $C^\infty$ domain is a $W^{k,2}$-extension domain ([[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]).

[L14] Subcritical Sobolev compactness: for a bounded extension domain $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $p=2<n$, every sequence bounded in $W^{1,2}(\Omega)$ has a subsequence converging in $L^2(\Omega)$ ([[cor-bounded-sobolev-sequences-have-strongly-convergent-subsequences]]).

[L15] Sequential compact-embedding criterion: under Countable and Dependent Choice, $X\Subset Y$ holds if and only if every bounded sequence in $X$ has a subsequence converging in $Y$ ([[def-compactly-embedded-normed-spaces]]).

[L16] In ZF the Axiom of Choice implies the Axiom of Dependent Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[L17] Difference-quotient product identity: $\delta_h^i(\eta^2\delta_h^iu)=\eta^2\delta_h^i\delta_h^iu+(\delta_h^i\eta^2)(\tau_{-he_i}\delta_h^iu)$ on the common domain, with $\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p}\le\|\partial_iu\|_{L^p}$ on the enlarged set ([[lem-cutoff-difference-quotient-commutator-estimate]]).

[L18] Higher-order Sobolev embedding: on a bounded extension domain, $W^{m,2}$ membership with $m>j+\tfrac32$ yields a $C^j$ representative on the closure, compatibly for different $j$ ([[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]]).

[L19] $L^2$ Cauchy-Schwarz: $\int|fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_2\|g\|_2$, and $2ab\le\delta a^2+\delta^{-1}b^2$ for $a,b\ge0$, $\delta>0$ ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]).

[L20] Clairaut-Schwarz: mixed partial derivatives of a $C^2$ function commute ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]).

**Choice accounting.** The Axiom of Choice is assumed in the Statement. It supplies the Fredholm alternative [L9], the tensor/frame and Sobolev suppliers' own choice assumptions, and through [L16] the Countable and Dependent Choice used by the sequential compactness criterion [L15] and by the trace and difference-quotient interfaces of [L10], [L12] and [L17]. No other choice principle is used, and no choice is made in the explicit finite constructions below.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The data and conventions of the Given paragraph above; in particular the truncated annulus $A=B_R(0)\setminus\overline O$, its outward unit normal $n$, the coefficient $\kappa=\operatorname{div}n$ on $\partial O$, and the smooth tangential field $e_T$ on $\partial O$.

1.1 **The test space and the variational form.** Define $X:=\{v\in H^1(A;\mathbb C^3):v_{\text{tangential}}=0\text{ on }\partial O\}$, the tangential part being taken with respect to the trace of $v$ on the smooth boundary component $\partial O$; by the boundedness of the trace operator [L10] applied componentwise, $X$ is a closed subspace of the complex Hilbert space $H^1(A;\mathbb C^3)$, hence complete. Define the sesquilinear form $a(E,v):=\int_A(\nabla E:\overline{\nabla v}-k^2E\cdot\overline v)\,dx+\int_{\partial O}\kappa\,E_n\overline{v_n}\,dS-\langle T_RE,v\rangle_{S_R}$, where $\nabla E:\overline{\nabla v}:=\sum_{i,m}\partial_iE_m\overline{\partial_iv_m}$ and $\langle T_RE,v\rangle_{S_R}:=\sum_{m=1}^3\langle T_RE_m,v_m\rangle$ uses the scalar DtN pairing of [L1] on the components. Then $|a(E,v)|\le C\|E\|_{H^1(A)}\|v\|_{H^1(A)}$: the first two terms are bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz [L19]; the boundary term is bounded by $\|\kappa\|_\infty\|E\|_{L^2(\partial O)}\|v\|_{L^2(\partial O)}\le C'\|E\|_{H^1}\|v\|_{H^1}$ by [L10]; and the last by the boundedness of $T_R:H^{1/2}(S_R)\to H^{-1/2}(S_R)$ [L1] combined with trace continuity for $H^1(A)$ functions on the smooth sphere $S_R$. [given, L1, L10, L19]

1.2 **Collar trace inequality on the inner boundary.** For every $\delta>0$ there is $C_\delta$ such that every $u\in H^1(A;\mathbb C^3)$ satisfies $\|u\|_{L^2(\partial O)}^2\le\delta\|\nabla u\|_{L^2(A)}^2+C_\delta\|u\|_{L^2(A)}^2$. Indeed, cover $\partial O$ by finitely many flattening charts of the smooth boundary ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) and let $\chi$ be a smooth cutoff, equal to $1$ near $\partial O$ and supported in the resulting collar. On the collar, in normal coordinates $x=\Phi(y,t)$ with $t$ proportional to the distance to $\partial O$, the strip estimate [L12] with $p=2$, divided by $h$ and integrated over $y$ with the bounded chart Jacobians, gives $\|u\chi\|_{L^2(\partial O)}^2\le C(h^{-1}\|u\chi\|_{L^2(A)}^2+h\|\nabla(u\chi)\|_{L^2(A)}^2)$ for every smooth $u$; choosing $h$ so small that $2Ch\le\delta$, expanding $\nabla(u\chi)=\chi\nabla u+u\nabla\chi$ and absorbing the cutoff terms into $C_\delta\|u\|_{L^2(A)}^2$ yields the claim for smooth $u$, and both sides are continuous in the $H^1(A)$ norm (boundary term by [L10]), while products of global $C_c^\infty$ approximations with a fixed cutoff are dense in the $H^1$ classes supported in the collar by [[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]] and [L13]; the inequality therefore extends to all $u\in H^1(A;\mathbb C^3)$. [L10, L12, L13]

1.3 **Smooth componentwise lift of the tangential datum.** For $j=1,2,3$ let $(e_T)_j\in C^\infty(\partial O)$ be the Cartesian components of $e_T$ and extend them by zero to $\partial A=\partial O\cup S_R$, obtaining smooth functions $g_j\in C^\infty(\partial A)$. By [L3] with $\varepsilon=I$, $\rho=0$ there is a unique $G_j\in H^1(A)$ with trace $g_j$ and $\int_A\nabla\overline v\cdot\nabla G_j=0$ for all $v\in H_0^1(A)$; by [L4] with $\rho=0$ and the smooth Dirichlet data $g_j$, each $G_j$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline A$, is harmonic on $A$, and $G_j|_{\partial A}=g_j$. Hence $G:=(G_1,G_2,G_3)$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline A$, satisfies $\Delta G=0$ componentwise, $G|_{\partial O}=e_T$ and $G|_{S_R}=0$, and is tangential on $\partial O$. [L3, L4]

2.1 **Coercivity of the shifted form.** With $\lambda:=\|\kappa\|_\infty(1+C_1)+k^2+1$, where $C_1$ is the constant of step 1.2 for $\delta:=\tfrac12(\|\kappa\|_\infty+1)^{-1}$, one has $\operatorname{Re}(a(E,E)+\lambda\|E\|_{L^2(A)}^2)\ge c\|E\|_{H^1(A)}^2$ for every $E\in X$, with $c=\tfrac12$. Indeed $\operatorname{Re}a(E,E)=\|\nabla E\|_2^2-k^2\|E\|_2^2+\int_{\partial O}\kappa|E_n|^2-\operatorname{Re}\langle T_RE,E\rangle$; the last term is nonnegative by $\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0$ of [L1] applied componentwise to $f=E|_{S_R}$; and the boundary term obeys $|\int_{\partial O}\kappa|E_n|^2|\le\|\kappa\|_\infty\|E\|_{L^2(\partial O)}^2\le\tfrac12\|\nabla E\|_2^2+\|\kappa\|_\infty C_1\|E\|_2^2$ by step 1.2 and [L19]. [L1, step 1.2, L19, algebra]

3.1 **The shifted form is boundedly invertible.** By the Riesz representation theorem [L8], applied to the bounded conjugate-linear functional $v\mapsto a(E,v)+\lambda(E,v)_{L^2}$ on the complete space $X$, the shifted form is represented by a bounded linear operator $S:X\to X$ with $\operatorname{Re}\langle Sx,x\rangle\ge c\|x\|^2$ and $\|S\|\le M$ for constants $c,M>0$ (step 2.1 and step 1.1). Choose $0<t<2c/M^2$ and put $q:=\sqrt{1-2tc+t^2M^2}<1$. For $x,y\in X$, $\|(I-tS)(x-y)\|^2\le q^2\|x-y\|^2$ by expanding the square and using [L19]; hence for every $f\in X$ the iteration $x_{n+1}:=(I-tS)x_n+tf$ is a strict contraction of the complete space $X$, so it has a unique fixed point $x$, and $Sx=f$. If $Sx=0$ then $c\|x\|^2\le\operatorname{Re}\langle Sx,x\rangle=0$, so $x=0$; thus $S$ is boundedly invertible with $\|S^{-1}\|\le c^{-1}$. [L8, L19, step 1.1, step 2.1, choose, algebra]

3.2 **The kernel of the form is trivial.** Let $E\in X$ satisfy $a(E,v)=0$ for every $v\in X$. Taking $v=E$ and imaginary parts in step 2.1 gives $0=\operatorname{Im}a(E,E)=-\operatorname{Im}\langle T_RE,E\rangle$, where $f=E|_{S_R}$; by [L1] the imaginary pairing equals $\sum_m\sum_{l,m'}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|(f_m)_{lm'}|^2$ with $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$, so every coefficient vanishes, $f=0$ on $S_R$, and consequently $T_Rf=0$. For every $v\in X$ supported away from $\partial O$ the identity $a(E,v)=0$ has no inner-boundary contribution and reads $\int_A(\nabla E:\overline{\nabla v}-k^2E\cdot\overline v)\,dx=\langle T_RE,v\rangle_{S_R}=\langle T_Rf,v|_{S_R}\rangle=0$; in particular every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(D)$, whose restriction to $A$ is an admissible test vanishing near $\partial O$, satisfies $\int_A\nabla E:\overline{\nabla\varphi}\,dx=k^2\int_AE\cdot\overline\varphi\,dx$, and taking $v$ compactly supported in the interior of $A$ gives $-\Delta E=k^2E$ weakly on $A$. Define $\widetilde E:=E$ on $A$ and $\widetilde E:=0$ on $\{|x|>R\}$; these two open sets cover $D$, so $\widetilde E$ is defined on all of $D$, and its only interface is the sphere $S_R$, across which the full trace of the field is $f=0$. For $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(D)$ the Sobolev-Gauss-Green formula [L11] on the bounded $C^1$ domain $A$, applied componentwise with $u=E_m\in W^{1,2}(A)$ and $v=\varphi|_A$, gives $\int_AE_m\overline{\partial_i\varphi}\,dx=-\int_A(\partial_iE_m)\overline\varphi\,dx+\int_{\partial A}(TE_m)(T\varphi)\nu_i\,dS$; the boundary term over $\partial O$ vanishes because $\varphi$ is compactly supported in $D$, and the term over $S_R$ vanishes because $TE_m=f_m=0$ there; hence $\int_D\widetilde E_m\overline{\partial_i\varphi}\,dx=-\int_A(\partial_iE_m)\overline\varphi\,dx$, so the distributional gradient of $\widetilde E$ is the field $(\nabla E)\mathbf 1_A\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$, $\widetilde E\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$, and the weak identity above gives $\int_D\nabla\widetilde E:\overline{\nabla\varphi}\,dx=k^2\int_D\widetilde E\cdot\overline\varphi\,dx$. By [L6] each real and imaginary part of each component of $\widetilde E$ lies in $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ and satisfies $\Delta w=-k^2w$ distributionally; $D$ is nonempty, open and connected and $\widetilde E=0$ on the nonempty open set $D\cap\{|x|>R\}$, so [L5] gives $\widetilde E=0$ on $D$, in particular $E=0$ on $A$. [L1, L5, L6, L11, step 2.1]

4.1 **Compactness of the $L^2$ pairing and the Fredholm reduction.** Let $J:X\to X^*$ be the $L^2$ pairing $\langle Jx,v\rangle:=(x,v)_{L^2(A)}$. The inclusion $X\hookrightarrow H^1(A;\mathbb C^3)$ is continuous and $A$ is a bounded $W^{1,2}$-extension domain [L13], so by [L14] with $p=2<n=3$ every bounded sequence in $H^1(A)$ has an $L^2$-convergent subsequence; by [L16] the Countable and Dependent Choice assumptions of the sequential criterion [L15] are available, so the inclusion $H^1(A)\hookrightarrow L^2(A)$ is compact, and so is its restriction $X\hookrightarrow L^2(A)$, hence also the composition $J$ of that restriction with the bounded pairing $L^2(A)\to X^*$. Therefore $K:=S^{-1}J:X\to X$ is compact, and the operator $A_{\mathrm{op}}:=S-\lambda J$ represented by $a$ satisfies $S^{-1}A_{\mathrm{op}}=I-\lambda K$; by the Fredholm alternative [L9] the operator $S^{-1}A_{\mathrm{op}}$ is boundedly invertible as soon as its kernel is trivial, and its kernel consists exactly of the $E\in X$ with $a(E,v)=0$ for all $v\in X$. [L9, L13, L14, L15, L16, step 3.1]

5.1 **Bounded invertibility of $a$.** By step 3.2 the kernel of $S^{-1}A_{\mathrm{op}}=I-\lambda K$ is trivial, so the Fredholm alternative [L9] makes it boundedly invertible; hence $A_{\mathrm{op}}=S(I-\lambda K)$ and the form $a$ are boundedly invertible: for every bounded conjugate-linear functional $F$ on $X$ there is exactly one $E\in X$ with $a(E,v)=F(v)$ for all $v\in X$, and $\|E\|_{H^1(A)}\le C\|F\|_{X^*}$. [L9, step 4.1, step 3.2]

6.1 **The weak solution with prescribed tangential trace.** Define on $X$ the functional $F(v):=-a(G,v)-\int_{\partial O}(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\overline{v_n}\,dS$. Both summands are bounded in $v$: the first by step 1.1, the second because $\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T\in C^\infty(\partial O)$ and $v\mapsto v_n|_{\partial O}$ is trace-continuous into $L^2(\partial O)$ by [L10], applied in the boundary charts. By step 5.1 there is exactly one $u\in X$ with $a(u,v)=F(v)$ for all $v\in X$; set $E:=G+u\in H^1(A;\mathbb C^3)$. Then $E_{\text{tangential}}=e_T$ on $\partial O$ because $u\in X$ and $G$ is tangential there, and testing the defining identity with $v$ compactly supported in the interior of $A$ gives $-\Delta E=k^2E$ weakly on $A$. Moreover, for every $v\in X$ supported away from $\partial O$ one has $a(E,v)=a(G,v)+a(u,v)=-\int_{\partial O}(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\overline{v_n}\,dS=0$, so the same integration-by-parts computation as in step 3.2 shows that the normal trace of $E$ on $S_R$ equals $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense, where $f=E|_{S_R}=u|_{S_R}\in H^{1/2}(S_R;\mathbb C^3)$. [L10, step 5.1, step 1.3, algebra]

7.1 **Gluing across the artificial sphere and smoothness on the open set $D$.** Let $E_{\mathrm{out}}$ be the outgoing series of [L1] built from the trace $f=E|_{S_R}$, defined on $\{|x|>R\}$; by [L1] it is a finite-local-energy solution there with normal derivative $T_Rf$, and it is smooth away from the sphere. Define $\widetilde E:=E$ on $A$ and $\widetilde E:=E_{\mathrm{out}}$ on $\{|x|>R\}$. The two pieces have the same trace $f$ on $S_R$; applying the Sobolev-Gauss-Green formula [L11] on $A$ and on the exterior annulus $B_M\setminus\overline B_R$ (with the outward normals $+n$ and $-n$ on $S_R$) and adding, the two interface pairings cancel, so $\widetilde E\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ with weak gradient the two-sided gradient. For every test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(D)$ the weak equations on both sides then give $\int_D\nabla\widetilde E:\overline{\nabla\varphi}=k^2\int_D\widetilde E\cdot\overline\varphi$: on $A$ this is the weak identity of step 6.1, on the exterior it is the weak Helmholtz equation satisfied by the outgoing series, and the interface terms have cancelled. Since $k^2\widetilde E\in H^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ for every $k$ as soon as $\widetilde E\in H^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$, repeated application of the interior gain-two estimate [L7] starting from $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ gives $\widetilde E\in H^m_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ for every $m$, hence a $C^\infty(D)$ representative satisfying the classical Helmholtz equation on $D$. [L1, L7, L11, step 6.1]

7.2 **Flattening near $\partial O$ and the local mixed system.** Fix a boundary point and a flattening chart of $\partial O$ with coordinates $(y,s)$, $y\in B\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, $s<0$ inside $A$; shrink it and let $\eta$ be a cutoff equal to $1$ on a smaller half-box and supported in the larger one. Choose a smooth orthonormal frame $Q=(\tau_1,\tau_2,n)$ with $n$ the outward normal of $A$ extended along the normal lines (so that $\partial_s=\partial_n$ in the collar), and write $E=QU$ on the chart. Transporting the form of step 1.1 and localizing by $\eta$, the weak identity $a(E,v)=-\int_{\partial O}(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\overline{v_n}\,dS$ of step 6.1 becomes, for every admissible localized test $V$ (frame components of a field in $X$, compactly supported in the larger half-box, with $V_1=V_2=0$ on $B$), $\sum_m\int a^{ij}\partial_jU_m\overline{\partial_iV_m}\,dyds+\int_B\beta\,U_3\overline{V_3}\,dy=\int f\cdot\overline V\,dyds+\sum_i\int G_i\cdot\overline{\partial_iV}\,dyds+\int_B h\,\overline{V_3}\,dy$, where the principal matrix $a^{ij}$ is smooth, uniformly positive and scalar in the component index $m$ (the frame satisfies $Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I$, so the principal part of $\nabla E:\overline{\nabla V}$ keeps the identity in $m$, multiplied by the chart Jacobian); $\beta=\kappa J_B$ is smooth and possibly signed ($J_B$ the boundary Jacobian); $f=-k^2JU+(\text{smooth})U+(\text{smooth})\partial U\in L^2$; $G_i=(\text{smooth})U\in H^1$; and $h=-(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\circ\psi\,J_B\in C_c^\infty(B)$, with $\psi:B\to\partial O$ the graph parametrization. Every localized $H^1$ triple $V$ with $V_1=V_2=0$ on $B$ and compact support in the chart pulls back to an element of $X$: reflect $V_1,V_2$ oddly and $V_3$ evenly across $s=0$ (these reflections are $H^1$ because the odd components have zero trace and the even one matches), mollify with a kernel even in $s$ to keep the parities and the exact zero traces, multiply by an even cutoff, pull back through the smooth frame and chart, and extend by zero. Hence the displayed identity holds for all such tests, in particular for tangential difference-quotient tests. [L10, L11, step 6.1]

8.1 **Tangential second derivatives and recovery of the normal derivatives.** Let $k\in\{1,2\}$ be a tangential direction, put $W:=\delta_h^kU=(U(y+he_k,s)-U(y,s))/h$ and test the system of step 7.2 with $V:=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2W)$ on a nested pair of half-boxes; this test has $V_1=V_2=0$ on $B$ and compact support, so it is admissible. The discrete integration by parts of [L17] and the shifted product rule give a principal term bounded below by $\alpha\|\eta\nabla W\|_{L^2}^2$ with $\alpha>0$ the ellipticity constant of $a^{ij}$, while all remaining terms involve $\delta_h a$, $\nabla\eta$, $W$, $\nabla U$, $f$ or the transferred quotients of $G$, and are bounded by $\epsilon\|\eta\nabla W\|_2^2+C_\epsilon(\|U\|_{H^1}^2+\|f\|_{L^2}^2+\|G\|_{H^1}^2)$ using [L17], the increment estimate $\|\delta_h^kU\|_{L^2}\le\|\partial_kU\|_{L^2}$, and [L19]. On $B$ the Robin term gives $\int_B\beta(y+he_k)\eta^2|W_3|^2+\int_B(\delta_h^k\beta)U_3\eta^2\overline{W_3}$; the trace estimate $\|Tz\|_{L^2(B)}^2\le\epsilon\|\nabla z\|_{L^2}^2+C_\epsilon\|z\|_{L^2}^2$ of step 1.2 (with $B$ the flattened $\partial O$) absorbs the first term for either sign of $\beta$, and bounded $\delta_h\beta$, the trace bound for $U_3$ and [L19] bound the second; the smooth datum $h$ contributes $\int_B(\delta_h^kh)\overline{W_3}$, bounded by $\|h\|_{H^1(B)}\|T(\eta^2W_3)\|_{L^2(B)}$ and absorbed in the same way. Choosing the finitely many $\epsilon$ small gives $\|\eta\nabla\delta_h^kU\|_{L^2}\le C(\|U\|_{H^1}+\|f\|_{L^2}+\|G\|_{H^1}+\|h\|_{H^1(B)})$ uniformly in $h$, hence every tangential second derivative of $U$ lies in $L^2$ after the limit argument in which the bounded functional $\psi\mapsto\lim_h\int(\partial_iU_m)\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2\psi)$ is represented in $L^2$ by [L8]. From the interior equation $-\partial_i(a^{ij}\partial_jU_m)=f_m-\partial_iG_{i,m}$ one then recovers $a^{33}\partial_{ss}U_m=\partial_iG_{i,m}-f_m-\sum_{(i,j)\ne(3,3)}a^{ij}\partial_{ij}U_m-\sum_{i,j}(\partial_ia^{ij})\partial_jU_m$, whose right side is now $L^2$ and whose coefficient satisfies $a^{33}\ge\alpha>0$; so all second derivatives of $U$ lie in $L^2$ on the smaller half-box, and a finite cover of the compact boundary gives $E\in H^2$ up to $\partial O$. [L8, L19, step 1.2, step 7.2, algebra]

9.1 **Higher-order bootstrap and the classical boundary conclusion.** Suppose $U\in H^{r+1}$ on the larger half-box for some $r\ge1$; the data of the local system then satisfy $f\in H^r$, $G\in H^{r+1}$ and $h\in H^r(B)$ because all coefficients are smooth. For a tangential multi-index $\alpha$ of order $r$ put $Z:=D_y^\alpha U$; differentiating the system of step 7.2 by $D_y^\alpha$ keeps the principal matrix $a^{ij}$ and the Robin coefficient $\beta$, and replaces the data by $f_\alpha\in L^2$, $G_\alpha\in H^1$ and $h_\alpha\in H^1(B)$ built from $D_y^\alpha f$, $D_y^\alpha G$ and the finitely many commutator terms $D_y^\gamma(\text{coefficient})\,D_y^{\alpha-\gamma}U$ with $0<\gamma\le\alpha$, all known by the induction hypothesis; the tangential traces of $Z$ are again zero in the first two components and free in the third, and localized tests for $Z$ are admissible by the gluing argument of step 7.2. Applying step 8.1 to $Z$ gains two further tangential or mixed derivatives, and differentiating the normal-recovery equation of step 8.1 and inducting on the number of normal derivatives recovers the remaining ones; nested half-boxes and a finite boundary cover give $U\in H^m$ on each smaller patch for every $m$, with constants depending on the data, $\kappa$, the chart and the fixed nested covers. By the Sobolev embedding [L18] on the flat half-box (a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, hence an extension domain by [L13]) each $H^m$ class with $m>j+\tfrac32$ has a $C^j$ representative on the closed patch, compatible for different $j$; hence $E$ has a $C^\infty$ representative up to $\partial O$, and the classical integration by parts in the local frame (equivalently [L11] with classical traces) turns $a(E,v)=0$ for admissible tests into the boundary identities $\partial_nE_n+\kappa E_n=-\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T$ and $E_{\text{tangential}}=e_T$ on $\partial O$. [L11, L13, L18, step 7.2, step 8.1, algebra]

10.1 **The divergence constraint.** Let $q:=\operatorname{div}E$ on $D$. By step 9.1 and step 7.1, $E\in C^\infty(\overline D;\mathbb C^3)$ once the two-sided solution is matched at $S_R$; the mixed partials commute [L20], so $\Delta q=\operatorname{div}\Delta E=-k^2\operatorname{div}E=-k^2q$ on $D$. On $\partial O$ the exact boundary identity $\operatorname{div}E=\partial_nE_n+(\operatorname{div}n)E_n+\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}E_{\text{tangential}}$ holds in the classical sense with the chosen normal extension, and its first two terms sum to $-\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T$ by step 9.1 while the third equals $\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T$; hence $q=0$ on $\partial O$. Finally $q$ is outgoing in the class of [L1]: on $\{|x|>R\}$ the field $E$ equals the outgoing series of [L1] by the uniqueness clause of that lemma, and differentiating the series componentwise in the spherical-harmonic expansion and using the spherical-Bessel recurrences $h_l'=h_{l-1}-(l+1)h_l/z$ and $h_l/z=(h_{l-1}+h_{l+1})/(2l+1)$ (which follow from the finite polynomial expression for $h_l$) expresses every radial factor of $q$ as a finite combination of outgoing factors $h_{l'}(kr)$, $l'\in\{l-1,l,l+1\}$; so $q$ has no incoming modal component and satisfies $\partial_rq=T_R(q|_{S_R})$ on $S_R$ in the class of [L1]. The exterior scalar uniqueness lemma [L2] applies to $q$ on the connected $D$ and gives $q=0$ on $D$, that is, the divergence constraint. [L1, L2, L20, step 7.1, step 9.1, algebra]

11.1 **Uniqueness of the classical problem.** Let $E_1,E_2\in C^\infty(\overline D;\mathbb C^3)$ both satisfy the conditions of the Statement. Their difference $W:=E_1-E_2$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$, solves $(\Delta+k^2)W=0$ componentwise on $D$, has $\operatorname{div}W=0$ and $W_{\text{tangential}}=0$ on $\partial O$, and is outgoing on $S_R$. Then $W\in X$ with $W|_{S_R}\in H^{1/2}$, and the integration by parts of step 3.2 and step 6.1 shows that $a(W,v)=0$ for every $v\in X$: the volume terms reproduce the Helmholtz equation, the inner boundary term cancels against $\operatorname{div}W=0$ on $\partial O$ through the exact identity of step 10.1, and the outer term cancels because $\partial_rW=T_R(W|_{S_R})$ by outgoingness. By step 3.2, $W=0$ on $D$. [L1, step 3.2, step 6.1, step 10.1, algebra]

12.1 **Assembly and choice accounting.** Existence is step 6.1 together with the regularity and gluing of steps 7.1, 8.1 and 9.1: the constructed $E=G+u$ has the prescribed tangential trace, satisfies $(\Delta+k^2)E=0$ on $D$, is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$ and outgoing on $S_R$ in the stated weak trace sense, and satisfies the closure relation of step 9.1; its divergence vanishes by step 10.1. Uniqueness is step 11.1. The only choice principle used is the Axiom of Choice assumed in the Statement: it supplies the Fredholm alternative, and through [L16] the Countable and Dependent Choice invoked by the compactness, trace and difference-quotient interfaces [L15], [L10], [L12], [L17]; the lift, the coercive inversion and the boundary bootstrap make only finitely many explicit selections. This proves all assertions. [given, L16, step 6.1, step 9.1, step 10.1, step 11.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in the local graph sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], with outward Euclidean unit normal field $\nu$ on $\partial\Omega$. Restate the class conventions of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: $L^2:=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ is the real Hilbert space of square integrable vector fields with the inner product $\langle u,v\rangle=\int_\Omega u\cdot v\,dx$ induced by the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and
$$H(\operatorname{curl})=\{u\in L^2:\operatorname{curl}u\in L^2\},\qquad H(\operatorname{div})=\{u\in L^2:\operatorname{div}u\in L^2\}$$
are the graph spaces with norms $\|u\|^2_{H(\operatorname{curl})}=\|u\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_2^2$ and $\|u\|^2_{H(\operatorname{div})}=\|u\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}u\|_2^2$, the curl and divergence being taken in the distributional sense; $X$ is the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the fields that are smooth on a neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$ and satisfy $\nu\times u=0$ pointwise on $\partial\Omega$; and $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$, $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$. This is the explicit weak perfect-electric-conductor class of that item, not an identification with every maximal tangential-trace realisation.

Then:

(a) **Smooth PEC cavity.** The curl form $(u,v)\mapsto\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v$ on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, with $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional and with the finite-dimensional zero eigenspace retained. Each eigenfield $u_j\in V$ satisfies $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda_j\int_\Omega u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally together with the PEC trace; and $u_j$ has a $C^\infty$ representative on $\overline\Omega$ for which $\operatorname{div}u_j=0$, $\nu\times u_j=0$ and $\partial_\nu u_{j,n}+(\operatorname{div}\nu)u_{j,n}=0$ hold classically on $\partial\Omega$, where $u_{j,n}=u_j\cdot\nu$ and $\nu$ is extended constant along collar normal lines. For every explicitly chosen positive mathematical speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and every pair of data $q_0\in V$, $q_1\in H$, the associated second-order wave has coefficients solving $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with $a_j(0)=\langle q_0,u_j\rangle$ and $a_j'(0)=\langle q_1,u_j\rangle$, in the modal class of that item: its displacement lies in $C(\mathbb R;V)$ and its velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$, finite modal sums converge in $C(K;V)$ and $C(K;H)$ on every compact time interval $K$, and the finitely many $\lambda_j=0$ modes are $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. The speed is a positive abstract mathematical parameter and has no physical dependency. The shifted scalar auxiliary boundary problems used inside the recorded cavity argument are solvable, with the stated classical regularity, by [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] applied with $\varepsilon=I$.

(b) **Rectangular reflection-parity class.** Let $Q=\prod_{j=1}^3(0,L_j)$ with $L_j>0$ and let $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ be constants. In the reflection boundary class of [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (real $L^2$ fields on the torus $\prod_j\mathbb R/(2L_j\mathbb Z)$ whose components carry the parities of that item and whose distributional divergences vanish), the finite separated Fourier modes are dense at every time, and every initial datum of the class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class, along which $\tfrac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+|B|^2/\mu)\,dx$ is constant.

No completeness is asserted in lossy, open-ended or non-smooth classes, and the constant-Ohmic and open-longitudinal branches are homed separately as physical items on the guide page; they are not mathematical premises or dependencies of this statement.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice; a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ with outward unit normal $\nu$; the graph spaces $H(\operatorname{curl})$, $H(\operatorname{div})$ and the class $X$, subspace $V$ and space $H$ of the Statement; a positive speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}$ and data $q_0\in V$, $q_1\in H$; positive constants $L_j$, $\varepsilon$, $\mu$ for part (b).

[L1] **Smooth PEC cavity spectral closure** ([[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]): for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega$, with $X$ the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth-on-closure fields with $n\times u=0$, $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$, the curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity tending to infinity whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, the zero eigenspace is finite dimensional and retained; each eigenfield $u_j\in V$ satisfies the full graph-class variational identity $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda_j\int_\Omega u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$ and the distributional eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ with the PEC trace; and for every explicitly chosen mathematical speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and all $q_0\in V$, $q_1\in H$ the associated second-order wave has coefficients $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$, displacement in $C(\mathbb R;V)$, velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$, finite modal sums converging in $C(K;V)$ and $C(K;H)$ on every compact time interval $K$, and affine $\lambda=0$ modes $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. The speed is an abstract positive mathematical parameter.

[L2] **Eigenfield boundary regularity** ([[lem-em-pec-cavity-eigenfield-boundary-regularity]]): if $u\in X$ with $X$ as in [L1], $\operatorname{div}u=0$ weakly and $\lambda\ge0$ satisfies $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda\int_\Omega u\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$, then $u\in H^m(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ for every integer $m\ge1$ and $u$ has a $C^\infty$ representative on the closure for which $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u=\lambda u$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, $\nu\times u=0$ and $\partial_\nu u_n+(\operatorname{div}\nu)u_n=0$ hold classically, with $u_n=u\cdot\nu$ and the normal extended constant along collar normal lines; zero eigenvalues and disconnected domains are included.

[L3] **Scalar elliptic boundary existence** ([[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]]): for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, uniformly positive smooth coefficient $\varepsilon$ and smooth right-hand side $\rho$ on the closure, the weak Dirichlet problem with smooth boundary data and the weak compatible Neumann problem each have exactly one solution modulo the stated normalisation, which is $C^\infty$ on the closure and satisfies the classical equation and boundary values; the existence content is that of the weak solvability lemmas and edge, junction and non-smooth regimes are excluded.

[L4] **Rectangular PEC energy completeness** ([[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]]): for $Q=\prod_j(0,L_j)$ with $L_j>0$ and constants $\varepsilon,\mu>0$, in the reflection boundary class with distributional $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}B=0$ the finite separated Fourier modes are dense and the class is $L^2$-complete, every initial datum has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class, and the energy $\tfrac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+|B|^2/\mu)\,dx$ is constant along it; the item assumes Countable Choice and supplies neither trace regularity for arbitrary $H(\operatorname{curl})$ fields nor completeness in lossy, open or non-rectangular guides.

[L5] **Choice principles:** the Axiom of Choice states that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); it implies the Axiom of Dependent Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]), the latter meaning that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[L6] **Conventions:** a map is $C^\infty$ on the closure when it is the restriction of a smooth map on a neighbourhood of the closure ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); the Euclidean inner product is that of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]; and the classical product, sum and chain rules used to read the differentiated identities of [L2] are those of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]].

**Choice accounting.** The Axiom of Choice is assumed in the Statement. It is used by [L1]–[L3], whose statements declare it, and it supplies through [L5] the Countable Choice assumed by the rectangular supplier [L4]. No further choice principle is used, and the wrapper introduces no selection.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, the bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega$, the classes $X$, $V$, $H$ and the data of the Statement.

1.1 **The definitions agree and the cavity conclusions apply.** The class $X$, the subspace $V$ and the space $H$ of the Statement are exactly those of [L1] for the same domain $\Omega$: the same graph-norm closure of the same smooth fields on the closure with $\nu\times u=0$, the same divergence-free subspace and the same closed $L^2$ span, and the Axiom of Choice assumed in the Statement is the choice assumption of [L1], whose meaning is fixed by [L5]. Hence all conclusions of [L1] hold in the present setting: the curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity and $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, the zero eigenspace is finite dimensional and retained, each eigenfield satisfies the full $X$ variational identity and the distributional eigen-equation with the PEC trace, and the modal wave expansion with the chosen positive speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}$ has the stated initial coefficients, the stated continuities on compact intervals and affine zero modes. [L1, L5]

1.2 **Rectangular class.** [L4] states exactly the assertions of part (b) for the reflection boundary class with constants $\varepsilon,\mu>0$: density of the finite separated Fourier modes at every time, unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solutions of the two equations in the class for every initial datum, and constancy of $\tfrac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+|B|^2/\mu)\,dx$. Its Countable Choice hypothesis is available in the present setting: the Statement assumes the Axiom of Choice, and the implication to Countable Choice is the choice supplier [L5]. [L4, L5]

2.1 **Smooth eigenfields.** Fix $j$. By step 1.1, $u_j\in X$, $\operatorname{div}u_j=0$ weakly and the full $X$ variational identity holds for $u_j$ with $\lambda_j\ge0$; hence the hypotheses of [L2] are satisfied and $u_j\in H^m(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ for every integer $m\ge1$ with a $C^\infty$ representative on $\overline\Omega$, for which the classical relations $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$, $\operatorname{div}u_j=0$, $\nu\times u_j=0$ and $\partial_\nu u_{j,n}+(\operatorname{div}\nu)u_{j,n}=0$ hold, with $u_{j,n}=u_j\cdot\nu$ and $\nu$ extended constant along collar normal lines; the Euclidean pairing and the reading of the differentiated identities are those of [L6]. In particular the zero eigenvalues $\lambda_j=0$ are included and no eigenfield is discarded. [L2, L6, step 1.1]

3.1 **Scalar auxiliary boundary problems.** The auxiliary problems used inside the recorded proof of [L1] are scalar Dirichlet or compatible Neumann problems $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla w)=\rho$ with $\varepsilon=I$ on the same bounded $C^\infty$ domain and smooth data on the closure; by [L3] each of them has exactly one weak solution in $H^1(\Omega)$ (modulo the stated normalisation), which is $C^\infty$ on the closure and satisfies the classical equation and boundary values. This is the only role of the scalar elliptic theorem here: the vector eigenfield regularity claimed in part (a) is supplied by [L2] as in step 2.1, not by the scalar theorem. [L3, step 1.1]

4.1 **Assembly, exclusions and choice accounting.** Part (a) is steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1: step 1.1 transfers the spectral completeness, multiplicity, growth, zero-mode retention, full-$X$ identity, distributional eigen-equation and modal wave expansion from [L1]; step 2.1 upgrades every eigenfield to a $C^\infty$ field on the closure satisfying the classical PEC relations, including the zero eigenvalues; and step 3.1 records that the scalar auxiliary solvability used in the cavity argument is that of [L3]. Part (b) is step 1.2, which is [L4] verbatim in the present notation. Nothing outside the declared classes is asserted: no lossy, open-ended or non-smooth spectral completeness, no identification with every maximal tangential-trace realisation, and no physical reading of the abstract speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}$; the constant-Ohmic and open-longitudinal branches are homed on the guide page as separate physical items and are not used here. The Axiom of Choice is used only through [L1]–[L3] and, through its Countable Choice consequence [L5], through [L4]; no other choice principle and no choice of data beyond the explicit open set $\{v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0\}$ occurs. This proves all assertions. [given, L5, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Example

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Three exact boundary checks. (i) The sphere trace $f(n)=n_3$ is the trace of the homogeneous degree-one harmonic polynomial $u(x)=x_3$, so the ball boundary branch of [[thm-em-spherical-multipole-basis]] applies to it; the simultaneous conditions $\Delta u=0$ in the unit ball $B_1$ and $\partial_nu=1$ on $S^2$ are incompatible, because the divergence theorem gives $0=\int_{B_1}\Delta u\,dx=\int_{S^2}\partial_nu\,d\sigma=\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$. (ii) For the coefficient $\varepsilon=1$ on $\{x_1<0\}$ and $\varepsilon=2$ on $\{x_1>0\}$, the function $u=x_1$ on the first side and $u=x_1/2$ on the second is continuous and has weak first derivatives represented by locally integrable functions, and $\varepsilon\partial_1u\equiv1$, so $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=0$ weakly although $u$ is not $C^1$: its first derivative jumps from $1$ to $1/2$ across the interface. Hence the smooth-coefficient statements of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] cannot be extended to this piecewise-constant case, and the correct conclusion there is the piecewise regularity recorded by that item, not a global $C^1$ or $C^\infty$-on-the-closure statement. (iii) The same coefficient configuration is a hypothesis boundary for the smooth-domain spectral completeness of [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]]: the coefficient field is discontinuous across the interface and the explicit weak solution is not classical $C^1$ there, so the configuration lies outside the smooth classes of that theorem, which asserts no completeness or classical boundary regularity in non-smooth classes; the weak formulation nevertheless remains valid. All three parts are exact finite computations or classical divergence-theorem evaluations, and they assert no physical interpretation.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice; the unit ball $B_1=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|<1\}$ and unit sphere $S^2=\{x:|x|=1\}$; the functions $x_3$, $f(n)=n_3$ on $S^2$; the coefficient $\varepsilon=1$ on $\{x_1<0\}$ and $\varepsilon=2$ on $\{x_1>0\}$ with the function $u=x_1$ on the first side and $u=x_1/2$ on the second.

[F1] **Laplacian.** For $C^2$ $f$ on an open set, $\Delta f=\operatorname{div}\nabla f=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i\partial_if$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]); in particular $\Delta x_3=\partial_1\partial_1x_3+\partial_2\partial_2x_3+\partial_3\partial_3x_3=0$ on $\mathbb R^3$.

[F2] **Divergence and curl conventions.** For a $C^1$ field $F$, $\operatorname{div}F$ is the sum of the coordinate partial derivatives of its components ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]); in particular the constant field $(1,0,0)$ has divergence $0$.

[F3] **Polar coordinates.** Under Countable Choice, the polar surface measure $\sigma$ on $S^{n-1}$ is the finite Borel measure with $\int_{\mathbb R^n}f\,d\lambda_n=\int_0^\infty\int_{S^{n-1}}f(r\omega)r^{n-1}\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr$ for every Borel measurable $f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty]$ ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]]).

[F4] **Volume of the closed three-ball.** For $r\ge0$ the closed ball $\overline B_3(0,r)$ has Lebesgue measure $4\pi r^3/3$ ([[cor-volume-of-a-closed-three-ball]]).

[F5] **Divergence theorem on bounded $C^1$ domains.** Under Countable Choice, for a bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega$ and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}F\cdot\nu\,dS$ with the outward unit normal $\nu$ ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]).

[F6] **Weak and distributional derivatives.** A locally integrable $w$ has weak derivative $\partial_iw$ represented by a locally integrable $g$ when $\int w\,\partial_i\varphi=-\int g\,\varphi$ for every test function $\varphi$, and the distributional derivative is defined by the signed test pairing ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]).

[F7] **Ball boundary branch of the multipole theorem.** For $f\in L^2(S^2)$, the series $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}r^lf_{lm}Y_{lm}(n)$ converges in $L^2(S^2)$ as $r\uparrow1$ and its sum is the unique harmonic function on the unit ball with finite radial $L^2$ supremum and boundary limit $f$; for continuous $f$ it equals the Poisson integral and extends continuously to the closed ball ([[thm-em-spherical-multipole-basis]], part (c)).

[F8] **Elliptic boundary problems and their exclusions.** For a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, a uniformly positive smooth coefficient and smooth data on the closure, the weak Dirichlet and compatible Neumann solutions have $C^\infty$ representatives on the closure satisfying the classical equation and boundary values; for finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside the domain with piecewise smooth positive coefficient and sheet charge, the weak solution is $C^\infty$ on each closed side, with the flux jump determined by the sheet charge; edge and junction points, reentrant corners and coefficient loss of regularity are excluded ([[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]]).

[F9] **Waveguide and cavity classes.** The spectral completeness theorem for the smooth PEC cavity and the rectangular reflection class declares its smooth-domain class, its eigenfields and their classical boundary relations, and states explicitly that no completeness is asserted in lossy, open-ended or non-smooth classes ([[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]]).

[F10] **Countable Choice.** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ states that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Verification

1.1 The sphere trace and its harmonic extension. On $S^2$ the outward unit normal is $\nu(n)=n$, so the normal derivative of $x_3$ is $\partial_nx_3=\nabla x_3\cdot n=e_3\cdot n=n_3$; thus $x_3$ is harmonic on $\mathbb R^3$ by [F1] and has boundary trace $f(n)=n_3$ on $S^2$. The function $f$ is continuous, hence in $L^2(S^2)$ with coefficients $f_{lm}$, so the ball boundary branch [F7] applies: the series $\sum_{l,m}r^lf_{lm}Y_{lm}(n)$ is the unique harmonic function on $B_1$ with $L^2$ boundary limit $f$ and continuous extension to $\overline B_1$. Since $x_3$ is such a harmonic function, the branch identifies the extension as $u(x)=x_3$; in particular $f=n_3$ is an admissible ball-boundary datum, not an excluded class. [F1, F7]

1.2 The total mass of the sphere measure. Apply the polar-coordinates identity [F3] with $n=3$ to the indicator of the closed unit ball, a Borel measurable function: $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf 1_{\overline B_1}\,d\lambda_3=\int_0^\infty\int_{S^2}\mathbf 1_{\overline B_1}(r\omega)r^2\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr$; the left side is $\lambda_3(\overline B_1)=4\pi/3$ by [F4], and on the right side $\mathbf 1_{\overline B_1}(r\omega)=1$ for $0\le r\le1$ and every $\omega\in S^2$, so the iterated integral is $\bigl(\int_0^1r^2\,dr\bigr)\sigma(S^2)=\sigma(S^2)/3$; hence $\sigma(S^2)=3\cdot4\pi/3=4\pi$. The argument uses the Countable Choice assumption of the polar identity [F3]. [F3, F4, F10]

1.3 The piecewise-linear function and its weak derivatives. Define $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ by $u(x)=x_1$ for $x_1<0$ and $u(x)=x_1/2$ for $x_1>0$. Both branches tend to $0$ as $x_1\to0$ through their sides, so $u$ is continuous on $\mathbb R^3$, and it is $C^\infty$ on each of the two open half-spaces. Its distributional first derivatives are the locally integrable — indeed bounded — functions $g_1:=\mathbf 1_{\{x_1<0\}}+\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{\{x_1>0\}}$, $g_2=0$, $g_3=0$: for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, integrating by parts on each half-space with the vanishing of the boundary terms (the traces $x_1\varphi$ and $\tfrac12x_1\varphi$ vanish on $\{x_1=0\}$ and at infinity) gives $\int u\,\partial_1\varphi=-\int g_1\varphi$, and the partial derivatives in the other two coordinates vanish identically on each side. Hence the weak first derivatives of $u$ are represented by $g_1,g_2,g_3$, so $u$ satisfies the weak-differentiability part of the definitions in [F6]; and $u$ is not $C^1$ on any neighbourhood of the interface, since its classical one-sided derivatives $1$ and $1/2$ in the $x_1$ direction differ at every point of $\{x_1=0\}$. [F6]

2.1 The weak transmission equation. With $\varepsilon=1$ on $\{x_1<0\}$ and $\varepsilon=2$ on $\{x_1>0\}$, the field $\varepsilon\nabla u$ takes the value $(1,0,0)$ on both sides: on the first side $\varepsilon\partial_1u=1\cdot1=1$ and on the second $\varepsilon\partial_1u=2\cdot\tfrac12=1$, with the other components zero. Hence $\varepsilon\nabla u$ is the constant field $\mathbf c=(1,0,0)$, whose divergence is $0$ by [F2]; equivalently, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ one has $\int(\varepsilon\nabla u)\cdot\nabla\varphi\,dx=\int\mathbf c\cdot\nabla\varphi\,dx=0$, so the distributional equation $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=0$ holds weakly on $\mathbb R^3$. Thus the weak formulation of the transmission problem is satisfied by a function that is not $C^1$, and its one-sided first derivatives jump from $1$ to $1/2$ across the interface. [F2, F6, step 1.3]

2.2 Incompatibility of the two sphere conditions. Suppose $w\in C^2(\overline B_1)$ satisfied $\Delta w=0$ in $B_1$ and $\partial_nw=1$ on $S^2$, and apply the divergence theorem [F5] to $F=\nabla w\in C^1(\overline B_1;\mathbb R^3)$ on the bounded $C^1$ domain $B_1$: $0=\int_{B_1}\Delta w\,dx=\int_{S^2}\partial_nw\,d\sigma=\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ by [F1] and step 1.2, a contradiction. Hence no such $w$ exists, so the conditions are incompatible; by step 1.1 the same trace $f=n_3$ is nevertheless an admissible ball-boundary datum whose harmonic extension has normal derivative $n_3$, not the constant $1$. [F1, F5, step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 Scope of the elliptic conclusions. Step 2.1 produces a weak solution of $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=0$ for a coefficient that is positive and smooth on each open side but discontinuous across the interface $\{x_1=0\}$, and step 1.3 shows the solution fails to be $C^1$ near the interface; the configuration is nevertheless of the finite-interface form in which the piecewise conclusions of [F8] apply, because $\varepsilon$ is piecewise smooth on the closed sides and the interface is a smooth hypersurface. Therefore a global $C^1$ or $C^\infty$-on-the-closure conclusion for the piecewise-constant coefficient case is false, while the recorded one-sided piecewise regularity is the sharp conclusion; the smooth-coefficient statements of that theorem cannot be extended to this case. [F8, step 1.3, step 2.1]

3.2 Scope of the spectral completeness conclusions. The coefficient field of steps 1.3 and 2.1 is discontinuous across $\{x_1=0\}$ and its weak solution is not classical $C^1$ there, so the configuration is not one of the smooth classical configurations to which the smooth PEC cavity or rectangular classes of [F9] refer; that theorem declares its smooth-domain class and asserts in its statement that no completeness is asserted in non-smooth classes. The explicit weak solution of step 2.1 shows that the weak formulation of the equation remains valid in this excluded configuration and does not acquire the missing classical regularity, so it cannot be used to extend the spectral conclusions. [F9, step 1.3, step 2.1]

4.1 Audit. Step 1.1 identifies the admissible ball-boundary datum $f=n_3$ and its harmonic extension; step 1.2 computes the sphere mass $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ from the polar formula and the closed-ball volume; step 2.2 uses the divergence theorem to show that $\Delta u=0$ in $B_1$ and $\partial_nu=1$ on $S^2$ cannot hold simultaneously; steps 1.3 and 2.1 exhibit the continuous, weakly differentiable piecewise-linear solution with $\varepsilon\partial_1u\equiv1$ and show that it is not $C^1$; and steps 3.1 and 3.2 place this witness against the exact hypotheses of the elliptic and spectral results. Countable Choice is used only through the polar-coordinate identity [F3] of step 1.2 and the divergence theorem [F5] of step 2.2, whose own assumptions are those of the Statement; no other choice principle is used. No measurement, physical field interpretation or empirical claim is made. [given, F10, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎
