## Postulate

Under the Countable Choice convention of the stated boundary and sheet-distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]), adopt as a physical model of ideal electrostatic conductors, for the classical laboratory framework of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units and constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: a **conductor configuration** consists of the following data, and every model of this postulate is required to satisfy the clauses below. No experiment is reported and no empirical value is inferred; this is an explicitly adopted equilibrium idealization together with its geometric and source conventions.

(a) [Geometry] a laboratory region $\Omega\times I$ with $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ an arbitrary open ambient region, a finite family $D_1,\dots,D_m$ ($m\ge1$) of bounded $C^\infty$ domains with pairwise disjoint closures in the sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] with closures strictly inside $\Omega$ (the **conductor bodies**), the **conductor** $D:=D_1\cup\cdots\cup D_m$, its **surface** $\partial D$, and the **vacuum region** $\Omega_v:=\Omega\setminus\overline D$. By [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]], $\partial D=\partial D_1\cup\cdots\cup\partial D_m$ is a disjoint union of compact embedded $C^\infty$ hypersurfaces. The vacuum $\Omega_v$ is open, and near each conductor surface it is locally the smooth exterior side of that conductor. No boundedness or regularity of the ambient boundary is inferred from openness. In the additional **bounded smooth ambient branch**, assume that $\Omega$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ domain; only then [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]] gives that $\Omega_v$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ domain with the specified outer/conductor boundary charts; we additionally require $\Omega_v$ to be connected (configurations whose vacuum region is separated by the conductors, for instance by an enclosing closed shell, are outside this model as formulated here).

(b) [Equilibrium and sources] the configuration is in the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] on the vacuum region: $B=0$, $J=0$, $E$ is the fixed-time electric field of [[def-em-fields]], the volume source density $\rho_v$ is a continuous real map on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (C m$^{-3}$, [[def-em-sources]]) extended by zero to $D$; the **conductor charge is a stationary surface charge**, i.e. a continuous density $\sigma:\partial D\to\mathbb R$ (C m$^{-2}$) whose pairing with test functions is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with tangential current $K=0$ and $S=\partial D$; and the field pair $(E,0)$ together with the source pair $(\rho_v+\sigma\,\delta_{\partial D},\ 0)$ satisfies the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]. Inside the conductor the field vanishes: $E\equiv0$ on $D$ (the **equilibrium condition**); equivalently the conductor interior is field-free and carries no volume charge.

(c) [Potential and equipotential convention] there is a function $\varphi\in C^0(\Omega)\cap C^2(\Omega_v)$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\Omega_v$ and with $\varphi$ constant on each conductor body, $\varphi|_{D_j}\equiv V_j$ for real constants $V_j$ (volts, [[def-em-si-conventions]]); by continuity of $\varphi$ the trace of $\varphi$ on each $\partial D_j$ from the vacuum side equals $V_j$ as well. This is the single-function convention of an ideal conductor with no double layer: the model reads the same potential value on both sides of $\partial D_j$, while the normal component of $E$ may jump.

(d) [Data] a model is completed either by the component potentials $V_1,\dots,V_m$ together with the volume source $\rho_v$ and the data on $\partial\Omega$ where the laboratory region is bounded, or by the component total charges $Q_j:=\int_{\partial D_j}\sigma\,dS$ (C) together with those same ambient data. These are two declared data types; the postulate asserts neither that both data types are simultaneously specifiable nor that either is solvable for arbitrary data.

(e) [Scope] This is a static, frame-relative equilibrium idealization: it excludes transient finite-conductivity dynamics, relaxation to equilibrium, moving surface charge, electrode polarization and contact effects, and it is not derived from a microscopic matter model. It asserts no existence or uniqueness theorem (those are separate conditional results), no force, no energy, no radiation, no measurement and no apparatus realization; the value $V_j$ is a model parameter and the surface density $\sigma$ is an idealization variable determined by the equilibrium problem when it is solvable. The general open ambient branch retains compact conductor bodies in exterior configurations. Its additional bounded smooth ambient branch is distinct from the separately declared grounded-half-space and infinite parallel-plane idealizations, whose conductor bodies are themselves noncompact. Those examples retain the equilibrium/equipotential interpretation but their noncompact bodies and plane distributions are not instances of this compact-body configuration or its compact-sheet predicate. No arbitrary exterior solvability is asserted.

## Interpretation and source basis

The postulate records a model choice, not a deduction, and its clauses are the exact objects the rest of this page consumes. The field-free interior with all charge on the surface and the constant-potential (equipotential) surface are the standard ideal-conductor clauses of the source treatments (Griffiths §2.5.1 printed pp. 96-98; Tong §2.4 printed pp. 30-31; Chew §32.1-32.2 printed pp. 351-354), presented there for equilibrium configurations and reproduced here as adopted assumptions rather than as derived theorems. The division into two data types in (d) is the fixed-potential versus fixed-charge distinction of Tong §2.4.2 printed pp. 33-35 and Griffiths §3.1.5-3.1.6 printed pp. 116-121; it is a definitional choice about which quantities are prescribed. Nothing in (e) turns the idealization into a universal statement about real metals: finite conductivity, transients, contact potentials, surface forces and material properties are outside the model, and no numerical or empirical value of any material quantity is asserted.

The mathematical content used to *name* the objects is exact and proved earlier on this page: the surface $\partial D$ of finitely many pairwise disjoint bounded $C^\infty$ bodies is a disjoint finite union of compact embedded smooth hypersurfaces, and in the bounded smooth ambient branch the vacuum region is again a bounded smooth domain whose boundary pieces are the outer boundary and the conductor surfaces. The stationary-sheet pairing $\sigma\,\delta_{\partial D}$ is the surface-distribution object of [[def-em-surface-distribution]] as used by [[def-em-weak-sources]](c), and the solution predicate for the field-source pair is the separately adopted [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]; the postulate itself neither proves that predicate nor asserts that it is satisfiable for the declared data. The countable-choice convention belongs to those measure and distribution interfaces and is carried here explicitly ([[def-countable-choice]]).

The model is deliberately silent about configurations whose conductor bodies enclose a cavity of the vacuum: the bounded smooth ambient branch requires $\Omega_v$ connected, so configurations separated by the conductors are outside the model as formulated. The separately declared grounded-plane and ideal parallel-plate examples are noncompact idealizations and are not instances of this compact-body configuration; they retain their own explicit statements and are not theorems about this postulate.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) inherited from the surface and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(\Omega;D_1,\dots,D_m;\Omega_v;E;\rho_v;\sigma;V_j)$ be a model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] with surface $S:=\partial D$ and vacuum region $\Omega_v$, with the fields of [[def-em-fields]], the constants and units of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] carried by the model, and suppose additionally that the field $E$ satisfies the joint one-sided $C^1$ regularity hypothesis of [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]] across $S$: around every $x_0\in S$ each side of $S$ is the restriction of a $C^1$ field on an open neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller graph chart. Let $n$ denote the unit normal on $S$ pointing from the conductor side into the vacuum side (equivalently: $n$ is the inward normal of $\Omega_v$ and the outward normal of $D$ on $S$, by the local exterior conductor chart; in the bounded smooth ambient branch this is the sign convention of [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](c)), and let $E_+$ denote the vacuum-side trace of $E$ (the field is zero on the conductor side, so $[E]=E_+$). Then, pointwise on $S$:

(a) [Normal sheet charge] $n\cdot E_+=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and $n\times E_+=0$; equivalently $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+$ and the tangential part of the vacuum-side field vanishes: $E_+$ has no component tangent to $S$. In particular a conductor surface with $\sigma=0$ at a point has $E_+=0$ there (both traces vanish), and the sign of $\sigma$ is the sign of the outward normal field component.

(b) [Normal derivative of the potential] with $\varphi$ the model's potential and $\partial\varphi/\partial n:=\nabla\varphi_+\cdot n$ the one-sided normal derivative in the direction $n$ from the conductor into the vacuum ([[def-classical-normal-derivative]]), one has

$$\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial n}=-\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \sigma=-\varepsilon_0\,\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial n}.$$

(c) [Equipotential boundary traces] the trace $\varphi_+$ of $\varphi$ on $S$ is constant on each connected component of $S$, with value $V_j$ on every connected component contained in $\partial D_j$; consequently the boundary value problem in the vacuum region is a Dirichlet problem whose data are the constants $V_j$ on the conductor surfaces.

(d) [Total charges] the total charge of conductor $j$ is

$$Q_j=\int_{\partial D_j}\sigma\,dS=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}n\cdot E_+\,dS=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\nu}\,dS,$$

where $\nu$ is the local outward normal of the vacuum along the smooth conductor interface $S$, without asserting regularity of a general ambient outer boundary (so $\nu=-n$ on $\partial D$ and the last equality uses $\partial\varphi/\partial\nu=-\partial\varphi/\partial n$); the surface integrals exist as integrals of continuous functions over the compact embedded hypersurfaces $\partial D_j$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]]).

(e) [Data reading] the two data types of the model are related through (d): if the component potentials and ambient data are fixed and the equilibrium solution is given, the total charges are determined by (d); prescribing the total charges instead determines the potentials only through the (separate) equilibrium problem, and this theorem asserts no existence or uniqueness for charge data.

(f) [Scope] The statement is pointwise and stationary: it assumes the one-sided joint regularity above, a $C^\infty$ conductor surface, and the pure electrostatic regime; it excludes moving surface charge, normal sheet currents, magnetic sheet sources, nonsmooth or cornered conductors, fields without one-sided traces, forces, energy and any measurement; no self-force or material response is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions


**Given:** A model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] with conductor surface $S=\partial D=\partial D_1\cup\cdots\cup\partial D_m$, vacuum region $\Omega_v$, field $E$ with $E\equiv0$ on $D$, continuous stationary surface density $\sigma$ on $S$, potential $\varphi\in C^0(\Omega)\cap C^2(\Omega_v)$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\Omega_v$ and $\varphi\equiv V_j$ on $D_j$, and the joint one-sided $C^1$ regularity of the statement across $S$.

[F1] The conductor model: $E\equiv0$ on $D$; the pair $(E,0)$ with the source pair $(\rho_v+\sigma\delta_S,0)$, $K=0$, satisfies the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]; $\sigma$ is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) under [[def-em-surface-distribution]]; $\varphi$ is continuous on $\Omega$ and $C^2$ on $\Omega_v$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ there, constant on each $D_j$ with value $V_j$ ([[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]).

[F2] The fixed-vacuum-jump theorem: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the stationary compact embedded $C^2$ interface hypotheses, the joint one-sided $C^1$ field regularity and the weak Maxwell equations with the stationary-sheet source of [F1], one has pointwise on $S$ $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\times[E]=0$, $n\cdot[B]=0$, $n\times[B]=\mu_0K$, with $[F]=F_+-F_-$ and $n$ pointing from the $\Omega_-$ side to the $\Omega_+$ side ([[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]], [[def-em-surface-distribution]]).

[F3] For a bounded $C^\infty$ conductor surface the outward normal of the vacuum region on $\partial D_j$ is $n_j=-n$ (the negative of the conductor's outward normal) whenever the bounded smooth ambient hypothesis of [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](c) is in force; the local exterior conductor chart of the model identifies the vacuum-side normal with the conductor's outward normal in general ([[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]](a), [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](c)).

[F4] Classical one-sided normal derivative: for the vacuum side, $\partial\varphi/\partial n:=\nabla\varphi_+\cdot n$ is the normal derivative of the $C^1$ vacuum-side restriction $\varphi$ in the direction $n$, where $\varphi$ is $C^2$ on the vacuum side and its gradient has the continuous trace $-E_+$ ([[def-classical-normal-derivative]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

[F5] Uniform convergence of derivatives on compact intervals: if $f_s\to f$ pointwise on a compact interval and $f_s'\to g$ uniformly with $f_s$ differentiable, then $f'=g$ ([[thm-uniform-derivative-limit-on-a-closed-interval]]).

[F6] A totally differentiable function on a nonempty connected open Euclidean set is constant if and only if its differential vanishes ([[thm-zero-derivative-on-connected-open-euclidean-set-iff-constant]]); components of a space are its maximal connected subsets and partition it ([[def-connected-component-and-quasicomponent]]).

[F7] $\partial D$ is a finite disjoint union of compact embedded smooth hypersurfaces carrying a finite surface measure on which continuous functions are integrable ([[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]], [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]).

[F8] Euclidean vector decomposition: a vector $v$ with $n\cdot v=0$ and $n\times v=0$ for the unit vector $n$ is $v=0$, since $v=(n\cdot v)n+n\times(v\times n)$ for orthonormal triples ([[def-em-fields]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 By [F2] with the conductor side as $\Omega_-$ and the vacuum side as $\Omega_+$ (the normal $n$ of the statement points from the conductor into the vacuum, matching [F2]), the jump identities $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and $n\times[E]=0$ hold pointwise on $S$; the conductor-side trace vanishes because $E\equiv0$ on $D$ [F1], so $[E]=E_+-0=E_+$. This gives $n\cdot E_+=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+$, and $n\times E_+=0$, which is (a); if $\sigma=0$ at a point then $n\cdot E_+=0$ and $n\times E_+=0$ there, so $E_+=0$ by [F8], and the sign of $\sigma$ is the sign of $n\cdot E_+$ since $\varepsilon_0>0$. [F1, F2, F8, given]

2.1 On the vacuum side $E=-\nabla\varphi$ [F1], so $\nabla\varphi_+=-E_+$ [F4] and $\partial\varphi/\partial n=\nabla\varphi_+\cdot n=-E_+\cdot n=-\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ by [step 1.1]; this is (b). [F1, F4, step 1.1]

2.2 Tangential constancy of the trace. Let $X:B\to S$ be one of the regular graph charts of $S$ (a compact embedded smooth hypersurface [F7]), and for $y\in B$ and small $s>0$ put $x_s:=X(y)+sn(y)$, a point of the vacuum side because $n$ points from the conductor into the vacuum. For fixed $s>0$ small the function $f_s(y):=\varphi(x_s)$ is $C^1$ with $\partial_if_s(y)=\nabla\varphi(x_s)\cdot(\partial_iX(y)+s\,\partial_i n(y))$, and $x_s\to X(y)$, $\nabla\varphi(x_s)\to-E_+(X(y))$ as $s\downarrow0$ because the vacuum-side field has the continuous trace $E_+$ and the chart is smooth [F4]; on each compact coordinate segment the $\partial_if_s$ therefore converge uniformly to $-E_+(X(y))\cdot\partial_iX(y)=0$, since $E_+$ is orthogonal to the tangent vector $\partial_iX(y)$ by $n\times E_+=0$ [step 1.1]; the functions $f_s$ converge to the continuous trace $\varphi_+\circ X$ because $\varphi$ is continuous on $\Omega$ [F1]. Hence $f'=0$ on $B$ by [F5], so $\varphi_+\circ X$ is constant on the connected parameter ball [F6]. As the finitely many graph patches of $S$ cover $S$ and overlap in connected pieces, $\varphi_+$ is locally constant on $S$, hence constant on each connected component of $S$ [F6]. On a component contained in $\partial D_j$ the value is $V_j$, because $\varphi$ is continuous on $\Omega$, equals $V_j$ on $D_j$, and the component of $S$ lies in the closure of $D_j$ [F1]. This is (c). [F1, F4, F5, F6, F7, step 1.1]

3.1 Total charges. The surface integrals in $Q_j=\int_{\partial D_j}\sigma\,dS$ exist as integrals of the continuous density $\sigma$ over the compact embedded hypersurface $\partial D_j$ with finite surface measure [F7]. Substituting $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+$ from [step 1.1] gives the middle expression. For the last expression, on $\partial D_j$ the local outward normal of the vacuum is $\nu=-n$ [F3], so $\partial\varphi/\partial\nu=\nabla\varphi_+\cdot\nu=-\nabla\varphi_+\cdot n=-\partial\varphi/\partial n=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ by [step 2.1]; integrating over $\partial D_j$ gives $Q_j=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\partial\varphi/\partial\nu\,dS$. This is (d). [F3, F4, F7, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Data reading and scope. Clause (e) follows from the definitions in (d): the total charges are determined by the equilibrium solution through the displayed identities, while charge data enter only through a separate equilibrium problem, for which this theorem proves neither existence nor uniqueness [given]. The statement is pointwise on $S$ and stationary: no moving charge, normal sheet current, magnetic sheet source, corner or field without one-sided traces is considered, no product of distributions and no corner equation is formed, and no force, energy, radiation, self-force, material response or measurement is asserted [F1, F2]; the surface integrals exist but no regularity of a general ambient outer boundary is claimed [F7]. [F1, F2, F7, given, step 3.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited weak-solvability and trace suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega_v\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain with finitely many connected components (the vacuum region of the additional bounded $C^\infty$ ambient branch of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]], or any bounded smooth domain), let $\rho$ be continuous on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (the fixed-time volume source density, C m$^{-3}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]), and let $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in C^2(\overline{\Omega_v})$ be real potentials of the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields $E_i:=-\nabla\varphi_i$ of [[def-em-fields]] and

$$-\Delta\varphi_i=\rho/\varepsilon_0\qquad\text{pointwise on }\Omega_v,\qquad \Delta=\operatorname{div}\nabla.$$

The Laplacian convention is [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]. Let $\nu$ denote the outward unit normal of $\Omega_v$ ([[def-classical-normal-derivative]]). Then:

(a) [Classical Dirichlet uniqueness] if $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ on $\partial\Omega_v$, then $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$, and hence $E_1=E_2$. The conclusion holds component by component; each connected component of a bounded $C^\infty$ domain is again a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, to which the connected-domain uniqueness corollary applies.

(b) [Classical Neumann uniqueness and compatibility] if $\partial_\nu\varphi_1=\partial_\nu\varphi_2$ on $\partial\Omega_v$, then $\varphi_1-\varphi_2$ is constant on each connected component of $\Omega_v$, and conversely adding one real constant per component to a solution preserves both the equation and the Neumann data; hence the field $E$ is unique while the potential is determined only up to componentwise constants. Moreover the Neumann data are necessarily compatible:

$$\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\rho\,dx+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega_v^{(j)}}\partial_\nu\varphi\,dS=0\qquad\text{for every connected component }\Omega_v^{(j)}.$$

This compatibility is necessary, not sufficient, and is exactly the flux identity of the divergence theorem for the Poisson equation.

(c) [Weak variants] (i) if $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega_v)$ ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]) is prescribed as a trace and $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in H^1(\Omega_v)$ are weak solutions of the Dirichlet problem with the same trace $g$, then $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$; (ii) if the conormal data are prescribed compatibly, weak $H^1$ solutions are unique modulo constants on each connected component, and for connected $\Omega_v$ this is the normalised solution of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; (iii) [sheet/transmission variant] for the finite disjoint smooth interfaces and outer Dirichlet data of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](c), the globally $H^1$ solution is unique, and for compatible outer Neumann data it is unique modulo componentwise constants until the componentwise means are fixed.

(d) [Physics reading and conductor case] on a star-shaped vacuum domain the curl-free $C^1$ field has an interior $C^2$ potential by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-potential]]. This alone does not supply closure regularity, $H^1$ membership, a trace, or prescribed boundary data; each application of (a)-(c) additionally requires its stated regularity and identical boundary/source data. In the bounded conductor model, prescribed absolute conductor potentials $V_j$ and absolute outer Dirichlet data determine the potential and field uniquely in the admitted classical or weak class. Grounding fixes the additive constant exactly. If only relative potential differences are prescribed and the outer/reference data are also allowed to shift by the same constant, the common gauge constant is free; merely omitting outer boundary data does not establish field uniqueness.

(e) [Scope] uniqueness is conditional on the stated boundary or decay data: on an unbounded exterior region without a decay condition uniqueness fails: on $\Omega_R=\{x:|x|>R\}$ the functions $0$ and $u(x)=1-R/|x|$ are two distinct bounded harmonic functions with the same zero boundary trace and different limits at infinity, so the boundary, decay and regularity hypotheses above cannot be dropped. No existence is inferred from uniqueness; the classical branch requires $C^2$ up to the closure, the weak branches carry their own domain, coefficient and trace hypotheses, and no dielectric material coefficient or empirical claim is included. For the admitted conductor class with connected vacuum, fixed absolute conductor potentials and identical outer Neumann data also give exact uniqueness: this is a mixed boundary problem with a nonempty Dirichlet part, so there is no surviving additive constant. Existence for those mixed data is not asserted here. In that weak mixed branch, write $\mathcal V_D=\{v\in H^1(\Omega_v):Tv=0\text{ on }\partial D\}$. The compared potentials have the same prescribed conductor trace and satisfy $\varepsilon_0\int_{\Omega_v}\nabla v\cdot\nabla\varphi=\int_{\Omega_v}\rho v+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for every $v\in\mathcal V_D$, with the same smooth outer normal datum $g$.

## Facts & Assumptions


**Given:** A bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega_v$ with finitely many connected components, a continuous $\rho$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$, classical potentials $\varphi_i\in C^2(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with $-\Delta\varphi_i=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ on $\Omega_v$ and fields $E_i=-\nabla\varphi_i$, all in the pure electrostatic regime with the SI constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

[F1] Classical Dirichlet and Neumann uniqueness and flux compatibility: for a bounded connected $C^1$ domain with $u_1,u_2\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$, equal $-\Delta u_i$ and equal Dirichlet traces imply $u_1=u_2$ on the closure; equal $-\Delta u_i$ and equal outward normal derivatives imply $u_1-u_2$ constant; and for a solution $-\Delta u=f$, $\partial_\nu u=g$ one necessarily has $\int_\Omega f=-\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,dS$ ([[cor-classical-dirichlet-and-poisson-problems-are-unique]], [[lem-neumann-compatibility-from-the-divergence-theorem]]).

[F2] Componentwise Neumann uniqueness: if a bounded $C^1$ domain has finitely many connected components and $u,v\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ solve the same Poisson equation with the same outward normal derivative on $\partial\Omega$, then $u-v$ is constant on each connected component ([[cor-neumann-solutions-are-unique-modulo-componentwise-constants]]).

[F3] Components of a bounded smooth domain are again bounded smooth domains: each connected component $U$ of $\Omega_v$ is an open bounded $C^k$ domain and its boundary is a union of compact pieces of $\partial\Omega_v$ ([[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](d)); adding constants preserves the Poisson equation and the normal derivative ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]).

[F4] Weak Dirichlet uniqueness with prescribed trace: for a bounded $C^1$ domain and prescribed $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ there is exactly one $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $g$ solving the weak Dirichlet problem; in particular two weak solutions with the same trace and data coincide ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]], [[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]).

[F5] Weak Neumann existence and uniqueness: a weak Neumann solution with data $\ell$ exists exactly when $\ell(1)=0$ and is then unique up to an additive constant, the normalisation $\int_\Omega u=0$ making it unique; on finitely many components both conditions are imposed per component; the transmission problem with sheet charge has the same uniqueness structure ([[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], [[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]).

[F6] Combined elliptic boundary existence and uniqueness: outer Dirichlet data give a globally $H^1$ transmission solution that is unique; compatible outer Neumann data give existence and uniqueness modulo componentwise constants, with zero componentwise means giving uniqueness; the smooth branch is $C^\infty$ on each closed side ([[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](a)-(c)).

[F7] On a star-shaped open set a curl-free $C^1$ field $-E$ has an interior $C^2$ potential $\varphi$ with $\nabla\varphi=-E$ and $-\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}E$; no boundary regularity or normalisation at infinity is supplied ([[pthm-em-electrostatic-potential]]).

[F8] The $n=3$ fundamental solution $\Phi(z)=1/(4\pi|z|)$ is smooth and harmonic off its pole, and constant multiples and sums of $C^2$ functions with zero Laplacian have zero Laplacian; the radius function satisfies $\Delta(1)=0$ and $\Delta(R/|x|)=0$ on $|x|>0$ ([[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]).

[F9] Green's first identity on a bounded $C^1$ domain: $\int_\Omega|\nabla w|^2=\int_{\partial\Omega}w\,\partial_\nu w\,dS$ for $w\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ with the outward normal $\nu$; the nonnegative integral of $|\nabla w|^2$ vanishes exactly when $\nabla w=0$ almost everywhere; a totally differentiable function on a connected open set with vanishing differential is constant ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], [[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]], [[thm-zero-derivative-on-connected-open-euclidean-set-iff-constant]]).

[F10] AC and AC$_\omega$ are declared mathematical assumptions of the cited weak-solvability, trace and measure suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]); $\varepsilon_0>0$ and $\Omega_v$, $\rho$, $\varphi_i$, $E_i$ are the objects of [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] and [[def-em-fields]]; the conductor model supplies the bounded smooth ambient branch and its connectedness requirement ([[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]]), and the mean-zero coercivity inequality is available on each connected bounded component ([[lem-em-mean-zero-coercivity-on-a-c-one-domain]], [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Classical Dirichlet uniqueness. Let $U$ be a connected component of $\Omega_v$. By [F3] $U$ is a bounded connected $C^1$ domain with $\overline U\subseteq\overline{\Omega_v}$ and the restrictions $\varphi_i|_{\overline U}\in C^2(\overline U)$ satisfy $-\Delta(\varphi_i|_U)=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ there, with equal traces on $\partial U$ when $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ on $\partial\Omega_v$. By [F1] claim 1 applied on $U$, $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ on $\overline U$; as $U$ was an arbitrary component, $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ on all of $\overline{\Omega_v}$, and then $E_1=-\nabla\varphi_1=-\nabla\varphi_2=E_2$ by [F3]. This is (a). [F1, F3, given]

1.2 Classical Neumann uniqueness. Assume $\partial_\nu\varphi_1=\partial_\nu\varphi_2$ on $\partial\Omega_v$. Applying [F2] to the bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega_v$ with its finitely many components gives that $\varphi_1-\varphi_2$ is constant on each component. Conversely, if $u$ solves the equation and $c_j$ is a constant on each component that is added to $u$, then $\Delta(u+c_j)=\Delta u$ and $\partial_\nu(u+c_j)=\partial_\nu u$ because the gradient of a constant vanishes [F3], so the equation and the Neumann data are preserved; hence the field $E=-\nabla u$ is unique while the potential is determined only up to componentwise constants. This is the uniqueness half of (b). [F2, F3, given]

1.3 Weak variants. Clause (c)(i) is the uniqueness content of [F4]: two weak $H^1$ Dirichlet solutions with the same prescribed trace and the same right-hand side coincide. Clause (c)(ii) is the uniqueness-modulo-constants and normalisation clause of [F5], with the trace space of [[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]; the componentwise statement is the same clause on each component. Clause (c)(iii) is the uniqueness clause of [F6](c): outer Dirichlet data give a unique globally $H^1$ transmission solution, and compatible outer Neumann data give uniqueness modulo componentwise constants, fixed by zero means. This is (c). [F4, F5, F6, given]

1.4 Physics reading. On a star-shaped vacuum domain, [F7] supplies an interior $C^2$ potential for a curl-free $C^1$ field and nothing more: closure regularity, $H^1$ membership, a trace and boundary data are additional hypotheses, exactly as assumed in (a)-(c). For the bounded conductor model with its connected vacuum region [F10], fixed absolute conductor potentials and identical outer Dirichlet data are the Dirichlet data of (a) or (c)(i), so the difference of two admitted solutions has zero boundary data and is zero by the same uniqueness clause; grounding fixes the additive constant, while shifting both a relative-potential datum and every reference datum by a common constant leaves the difference of two solutions with the same data and hence with the same (fixed) uniqueness conclusion only for identical data — omitting outer data supplies no field uniqueness. This is (d). [F7, F10, given]

2.1 Neumann flux compatibility. Let $U$ be a connected component of $\Omega_v$, with outward normal $\nu$ and boundary $\partial U$ a union of compact pieces of $\partial\Omega_v$ [F3]. Applying [F1] claim 3 (equivalently [[lem-neumann-compatibility-from-the-divergence-theorem]]) to $u=\varphi|_{U}$ with $f=-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $g=\partial_\nu\varphi$ gives $\int_U\rho/\varepsilon_0=-\int_{\partial U}\partial_\nu\varphi\,dS$, that is $\int_U\rho+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial U}\partial_\nu\varphi\,dS=0$, the displayed identity for the component; no solvability is inferred from it. This completes (b). [F1, F3, given, step 1.2]

2.2 Mixed conductor data. Suppose the vacuum region is connected, $m\ge1$, $w$ is the difference of two admitted classical solutions with equal absolute conductor potentials and equal outer Neumann data. Then $w$ is harmonic, $w=0$ on the nonempty conductor boundary $\partial D$ and $\partial_\nu w=0$ on the outer boundary $\partial\Omega$. Green's first identity [F9] gives $\int_{\Omega_v}|\nabla w|^2=\int_{\partial\Omega_v}w\,\partial_\nu w\,dS$, and each boundary piece carries one zero factor, so the integral vanishes; by [F9], $\nabla w=0$ almost everywhere, and since $\nabla w$ is continuous on the connected open $\Omega_v$ it vanishes everywhere, so $w$ is constant by the vanishing-differential characterisation; its zero conductor trace forces the constant to be $0$. In the weak mixed branch, the difference of two admitted solutions has zero conductor trace, so it is an admissible test in the homogeneous difference equation and the same zero-energy argument applies, with the mean-zero coercivity inequality of [F10] converting $\nabla w=0$ into $w=w_{\Omega_v}$ as an $H^1$ class whose constant trace on the nonempty conductor boundary is zero. This sharpens (d); existence for mixed data remains unasserted. [F9, F10, given, step 1.4]

3.1 The unbounded witness and scope. On $\Omega_R=\{x:|x|>R\}$ put $u(x):=1-R/|x|$, and $u=0$, $\varphi\equiv0$. Then $u\in C^\infty(\Omega_R)$; since $R/|x|=4\pi R\,\Phi(x)$ is a constant multiple of the $n=3$ fundamental solution, it is harmonic off the origin [F8], and the constant $1$ has zero Laplacian, so $\Delta u=0$; moreover $u=0$ on $|x|=R$, $0<u<1$ on $\Omega_R$ and $u(x)\to1$ as $|x|\to\infty$. Thus $0$ and $u$ are two distinct bounded harmonic functions with the same zero boundary trace and different limits at infinity, witnessing that the boundary and decay hypotheses of (a)-(c) cannot be dropped. No existence statement is inferred from uniqueness anywhere above; the classical branch requires $C^2$ up to the closure, the weak branches carry their own domain, coefficient and trace hypotheses, and no dielectric coefficient, empirical value or measurement is included. This is (e). [F8, given] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited solvability theorem ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega_v\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in the sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] with finitely many connected components (the vacuum region of the additional bounded $C^\infty$ ambient branch of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]], or any bounded smooth domain), let $\rho$ be smooth on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (fixed-time volume source density, C m$^{-3}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]) and let $\varepsilon_0>0$ be the framework constant. Then the electrostatic boundary value problems on $\Omega_v$ are solvable in the following exact senses, and the solutions are the fields of the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with volume source $\rho$:

(a) [Dirichlet branch] for every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$ there is exactly one $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with

$$-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0\quad\text{on }\Omega_v,\qquad \varphi|_{\partial\Omega_v}=g,$$

with $\Delta$ the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]];
and it is the unique weak $H^1$ solution with trace $g$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] for the class); the field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ ([[def-em-fields]]) is $C^\infty$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ and $(E,0)$ realises the pure electrostatic regime with source $\rho$ on the vacuum region.

(b) [Neumann branch] for every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$ with

$$\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\rho\,dx+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega_v^{(j)}}g\,dS=0\qquad\text{for every connected component }\Omega_v^{(j)}\text{ of }\Omega_v,$$

there is $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with $-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $\partial_\nu\varphi=g$ (outward normal $\nu$, [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]), unique up to one additive constant per connected component; the normalisation $\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\varphi\,dx=0$ for every $j$ selects exactly one. The compatibility is also necessary in the sense of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](b).

(c) [Conductor reading and surface-charge realization] for the separated compact-body conductor geometry and zero-interior-volume convention of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], additionally assuming $\Omega$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ ambient domain, with outer boundary data $g_0\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ on $\partial\Omega$ and constants $V_j$ on the conductor surfaces $\partial D_j$ (constant functions are smooth on the compact disjoint boundary pieces), the combined datum is a special case of (a); the field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\Omega_v$ extended by $E:=0$ on the conductor satisfies the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] with the source pair $(\rho_v+\sigma\,\delta_{\partial D},\,0)$, where $\sigma:=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+\in C^\infty(\partial D)$ is the constructed continuous surface-charge density, agreeing afterwards with [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]] ([[def-em-weak-sources]](c), [[def-em-surface-distribution]], [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]]); the total charges $Q_j=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}n\cdot E_+\,dS$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]) are thereby determined by the data, and $\varphi$ is constant on each $\partial D_j$ with value $V_j$.

(d) [Stationary sheet charge in the vacuum region] for finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces $\Gamma$ strictly inside $\Omega_v$, a smooth sheet density $\sigma_\Gamma$ on them, and outer Dirichlet data $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$, there is a weak solution $\varphi\in H^1(\Omega_v)$ which is $C^\infty$ on the closure of each side of every $\Gamma$, unique by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](c)(iii), solving the weak equation with right-hand side $\int_{\Omega_v}\rho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma_\Gamma\,Tv$; its flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon_0\nabla\varphi]=-\sigma_\Gamma$, equivalently $n\cdot[E]=\sigma_\Gamma/\varepsilon_0$ in the sign convention of [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]]. This is the vacuum ($\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0$) transmission branch; no dielectric coefficient is introduced.

(e) [Scope] all existence statements are the ones proved in [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] for its stated smooth bounded domains, smooth uniformly positive coefficients (here $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 I$), smooth data and finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces; the coefficient is the smooth positive constant $\varepsilon_0I$ on every side in the transmission clause. Excluded: nonsmooth boundaries, corners, edges, coefficient loss of regularity, prescribed total charges for conductor bodies (the free equipotential problem), unbounded exterior regions without a stated decay class, dielectric material response (belonging to the material-response page) and any measurement, apparatus or empirical claim. The theorem asserts existence of the potential, not of a physical equilibrium; the ideal conductor is the adopted model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]].

## Facts & Assumptions


**Given:** A bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega_v$ with finitely many components, smooth $\rho$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$, $\varepsilon_0>0$, and the quoted data of clauses (a)-(d).

[F1] The combined elliptic boundary existence theorem: for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega$, smooth uniformly positive coefficient $\varepsilon$ and smooth $\rho$, (a) every smooth Dirichlet datum $g$ admits exactly one weak $H^1$ solution with trace $g$, continuous in the data, $C^\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$ and pointwise satisfying $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ with the given trace; (b) every smooth conormal datum $g$ with $\int_{\Omega_j}\rho+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$ on every component admits a weak solution, unique up to componentwise constants, normalised by zero componentwise means, smooth on each closed component; (c) the transmission problem with finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth uniformly positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth $\rho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$ has, with outer Dirichlet data, a unique globally $H^1$ solution that is $C^\infty$ on each closed side with equal one-sided traces, and with outer Neumann data existence exactly under the componentwise compatibility $\int_{\Omega_j}\rho+\sum_{\Gamma\subset\Omega_j}\int_\Gamma\sigma+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$, uniqueness modulo componentwise constants, smoothness on each closed side, and flux jump $n\cdot[\varepsilon\nabla u]=-\sigma$ ([[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]], [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]).

[F2] The pure electrostatic reduction: with $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0I$, $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon_0\nabla\varphi)=\rho$ is $-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$; $E=-\nabla\varphi$ then satisfies $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=0$, the fixed-time reduced equations of the regime ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](c), [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

[F3] The conductor model and its vacuum geometry: in the bounded smooth ambient branch $\Omega_v$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ domain whose boundary pieces are $\partial\Omega$ and the conductor surfaces $\partial D_j$, and the model supplies the zero interior field, the connectedness requirement and the potential convention ([[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]]).

[F4] Surface-charge identities: for a model of [F3] whose field has the joint one-sided $C^1$ regularity, $n\cdot E_+=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\times E_+=0$, and $Q_j=\int_{\partial D_j}\sigma\,dS=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\partial_\nu\varphi\,dS$ with $\nu=-n$ on $\partial D_j$ ([[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]], [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]).

[F5] Interface differentiation: for a compact embedded $C^2$ interface $S$ with unit normal $n$ from $\Omega_-$ to $\Omega_+$ and a field $F$ that is $C^1$ on each side with one-sided $C^1$ traces, the distributional identities $\operatorname{div}F=\{\operatorname{div}F\}_{\text{piecewise}}+n\cdot[F]\delta_S$ and $\operatorname{curl}F=\{\operatorname{curl}F\}_{\text{piecewise}}+n\times[F]\delta_S$ hold, where the bracket term is the locally integrable function equal to the classical operator on each side ([[lem-em-interface-derivatives]], [[def-em-surface-distribution]]).

[F6] The adopted distributional Maxwell equations and the jump theorem's identities: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the weak equations of [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] are exactly the solution predicate of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e), and the stationary-sheet jump theorem gives $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\times[E]=0$ under its one-sided regularity hypotheses ([[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], [[def-em-weak-sources]], [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]]).

[F7] Uniqueness and compatibility: the classical and weak uniqueness and compatibility statements of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]] hold for bounded smooth vacuum domains with finitely many components, including the componentwise Neumann compatibility and the transmisson uniqueness clause ([[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]]).

[F8] A bounded smooth domain, in particular the vacuum region $\Omega_v$ of [F3], has the boundary-chart presentation of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] used by the solvability theorem [F1], with the finite boundary atlas and outward normals of that definition ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]).


## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Dirichlet branch. By [F8] the bounded smooth domain $\Omega_v$ carries the boundary-chart presentation required by the solvability theorem [F1]. With $\varepsilon:=\varepsilon_0I$, smooth and uniformly positive on $\overline{\Omega_v}$, and smooth $\rho$, [F1](a) gives exactly one $u\in H^1(\Omega_v)$ with trace $g$, $C^\infty$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$, satisfying $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon_0\nabla u)=\rho$ pointwise and $u|_{\partial\Omega_v}=g$; the weak uniqueness in the $H^1$ class with trace $g$ is part of the same clause. Dividing by $\varepsilon_0>0$ gives $-\Delta u=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and the equation and trace displayed in (a), so $\varphi:=u$ is the asserted solution and it is unique in the stated class by [F7](a) as well. The field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ and satisfies $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$ by [F2], which is the fixed-time reading of the pure electrostatic regime with source $\rho$; hence $(E,0)$ realises that regime on the vacuum region. This is (a). [F1, F2, F7, F8]

1.2 Neumann branch. Let $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$ satisfy the componentwise compatibility of (b); with $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0I$ the conormal datum of [F1](b) is $\varepsilon_0 g$ and its compatibility $\int_{\Omega^{(j)}}\rho+\int_{\partial\Omega^{(j)}}\varepsilon_0g=0$ is exactly the displayed hypothesis, so [F1](b) gives a weak solution, $C^\infty$ on each closed component, unique up to one constant per component and normalised by zero componentwise means; after division by $\varepsilon_0$ the equation is $-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and the conormal trace is $\partial_\nu\varphi=g$ by the definition of the conormal derivative and the classical normal derivative [F1, F2]. The necessity of the compatibility is [F7](b), whose flux identity gives $\int_{\Omega^{(j)}}\rho+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega^{(j)}}g\,dS=0$ for any classical solution. This is (b). [F1, F2, F7]

1.3 Transmission branch. Let the finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces $\Gamma$, sheet density $\sigma_\Gamma$ and outer Dirichlet data $g$ be as in (d); with $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0I$ on each side, piecewise smooth $\rho$ and smooth $\sigma_\Gamma$, [F1](c) gives a globally $H^1$ weak solution with outer Dirichlet data, $C^\infty$ on the closure of each side, equal one-sided traces, unique by [F7](c)(iii), and flux jump $n\cdot[\varepsilon_0\nabla\varphi]=-\sigma_\Gamma$. Since $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on each side, $[\varepsilon_0\nabla\varphi]=\varepsilon_0[\nabla\varphi]=-\varepsilon_0[E]$, so $n\cdot[E]=\sigma_\Gamma/\varepsilon_0$, the sign convention of [F6]; the weak right-hand side is $\int_{\Omega_v}\rho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma_\Gamma\,Tv$ as stated. No dielectric coefficient is introduced because $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0I$ on every side. This is (d). [F1, F6, F7]

2.1 Conductor reading. Assume the bounded $C^\infty$ ambient branch with outer data $g_0$ and conductor data $V_j$. The boundary of $\Omega_v$ is the disjoint union of the compact boundary pieces $\partial\Omega,\partial D_1,\dots,\partial D_m$ [F3], and the function equal to $g_0$ on $\partial\Omega$ and to the constant $V_j$ on $\partial D_j$ is smooth on each piece, hence admissible in (a) [step 1.1]; let $\varphi$ be the resulting solution and $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\Omega_v$, extended by $E:=0$ on the conductor. Then $\varphi$ is continuous on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ with the constant trace $V_j$ on each $\partial D_j$ [F3], and $E$ has the joint one-sided $C^1$ regularity across $S=\partial D$ because $E$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ and $0$ is smooth on the conductor side [F2]. By [F4] applied to this model, $\sigma:=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+\in C^\infty(\partial D)$ — the density $\sigma$ is continuous and its pairing is the stationary-sheet source — and $Q_j=\int_{\partial D_j}\sigma\,dS=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\partial_\nu\varphi\,dS$, so the total charges are determined by the data. For the distributional equations: [F5] applied on the compact embedded interface $S$ with $\Omega_-$ the conductor, $\Omega_+$ the vacuum and the normal $n$ from conductor to vacuum gives $\operatorname{div}E=\{\operatorname{div}E\}_{\text{piecewise}}+(n\cdot[E])\delta_S$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=\{\operatorname{curl}E\}_{\text{piecewise}}+(n\times[E])\delta_S$; the piecewise parts are $\rho_v/\varepsilon_0$ on the vacuum side and $0$ on the conductor side, and $[E]=E_+$ with $n\cdot E_+=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\times E_+=0$ [F4], so the identities are exactly the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations with the source pair $(\rho_v+\sigma\,\delta_{\partial D},0)$ [F6]. This is (c). [F3, F4, F5, F6, step 1.1]

3.1 Scope. All existence and regularity statements above are exactly the clauses of [F1] for the smooth bounded domains of the statement, the constant coefficient $\varepsilon_0I$, smooth data and finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces; the conductor clause additionally uses only the bounded smooth ambient branch of [F3] and the constant data there. No nonsmooth boundary, corner, edge, coefficient irregularity, prescribed-total-charge problem, unbounded exterior region without a decay class, dielectric response, measurement, apparatus or empirical claim is asserted; existence of the potential is not asserted to be a physical equilibrium, which is the adopted model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] [F3]. This is (e). [F1, F3] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) inherited from the Newtonian, polar and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let

$$H:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:x_3>0\},\qquad \Pi:=\{x_3=0\},\qquad p:=a e_3\ (a>0),$$

let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a charge parameter (coulombs) and $\varepsilon_0>0$ the framework constant ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). Define, with arbitrary values on the exceptional sets,

$$\varphi_I(x):=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac1{|x-p|}-\frac1{|x+ae_3|}\right)\quad(x\in H\setminus\{p\}),\qquad E_I:=-\nabla\varphi_I.$$

The map $E_I$ is a spatial field of [[def-em-fields]] in the fixed-time reading, with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Then:

(a) [Candidate field] $\varphi_I\in C^\infty(H\setminus\{p\})$ and $\Delta\varphi_I=0$ pointwise on $H\setminus\{p\}$: the first term is the Coulomb potential of $p$, whose $n=3$ fundamental solution is harmonic off its pole ([[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]], [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d)), and the second term is $C^\infty$ and harmonic on the whole of $H$ because its pole $-ae_3$ lies outside $H$; $E_I$ is $C^\infty$ on $H\setminus\{p\}$.

(b) [Distributional point source] $\varphi_I\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$ and

$$-\Delta T_{\varphi_I}=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\,\delta_p\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(H),$$

where $T_{\varphi_I}$ is the regular distribution of $\varphi_I$ ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and $\delta_p$ the Dirac distribution at $p$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]); moreover the field satisfies $\operatorname{div}E_I=(q/\varepsilon_0)\delta_p$ and $\operatorname{curl}E_I=0$ in $\mathcal D'(H)$, where the divergence and curl of $E_I$ are the distributional derivatives of its components ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). Thus $(E_I,0)$ is a pure electrostatic model on $H$ with the fixed-time point source $q\delta_p$, the static reading of the stationary point charge of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](e)).

(c) [Boundary trace and decay] $\varphi_I$ extends continuously to $\overline H\setminus\{p\}$ with $\varphi_I=0$ on $\Pi$ (the two denominators are equal there), and for $|x|\ge2a$ the cancellation bound holds:

$$|\varphi_I(x)|\le\frac{2|q|\,a}{\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^2}.$$

The bound follows by applying the mean value theorem along the segment from $-ae_3$ to $ae_3$ to the function $y\mapsto|x-y|^{-1}$, whose gradient is bounded by $(|x|-a)^{-2}$ there ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). In particular $\varphi_I(x)\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$ in $H$.

(d) [Uniqueness in the declared class] let $\psi:H\setminus\{p\}\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ and harmonic on $H\setminus\{p\}$, continuous on $\overline H\setminus\{p\}$, with $\psi=0$ on $\Pi$, $|x-p|(\psi(x)-\varphi_I(x))\to0$ as $x\to p$ and $\psi(x)\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$ in $H$. Then $\psi=\varphi_I$ on $H\setminus\{p\}$. Equivalently, the Dirichlet problem $\Delta\psi=0$ on $H\setminus\{p\}$, $\psi=0$ on $\Pi$, with the leading singularity of the point charge at $p$ and decay at infinity, has exactly one solution in the stated class.

(e) [Physics reading: ideal grounded plane in the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]] the ideal grounded conducting half-space $\{x_3<0\}$ with the field $E_I$ on $H$, $E\equiv0$ below $\Pi$ and the induced density $\sigma:=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+|_\Pi=-\varepsilon_0\,\partial_3\varphi_I|_\Pi$ (using the normal $n=e_3$ from the conductor into the vacuum; $\sigma\in C^\infty(\Pi)$) is a model of the same equilibrium structure as [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]]: it is a pure electrostatic field on $H$ with the point source at $p$ and the equipotential boundary condition $\varphi_I=0$ on $\Pi$; the pair $(E_I,0)$ satisfies the static electrostatic equations with source $q\delta_p$ on $H$, and the induced density is explicitly $\sigma(x_1,x_2)=-qa/[2\pi(x_1^2+x_2^2+a^2)^{3/2}]$, is absolutely integrable over the plane, and has total charge $\int_\Pi\sigma\,dS=-q$. However, the half-space conductor is not a compact conductor body: the plane is not a compact embedded hypersurface, $\Pi$ and $\{x_3<0\}$ are not among the geometric objects of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], the density $\sigma$ is not a declared stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c), and the noncompact plane pairing is not an adopted compact-sheet source of that definition. As a separately specified mathematical idealization, extending $E_I$ by zero below the plane gives $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=(q\delta_p+\sigma\delta_\Pi)/\varepsilon_0$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=0$ on $\mathbb R^3$, where $(\sigma\delta_\Pi)(\eta)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\sigma(x')\eta(x',0)dx'$. This verified identity does not extend the framework postulate to arbitrary noncompact sheets. The clause is the explicitly declared idealization whose exact mathematical content is (a)-(d).

(f) [Scope] the statement concerns the ideal point charge above an ideal grounded plane in the declared decay class; it excludes finite-plane edge effects, conductor thickness, transients, moving charges, radiation, self-force and any measurement; no uniqueness is asserted outside the class of (d), and the point-source singularity is never evaluated.

## Facts & Assumptions


**Given:** The half-space $H$, the plane $\Pi$, the point $p=ae_3$, $a>0$, the charge parameter $q$, the constant $\varepsilon_0>0$, and the candidate $\varphi_I$ and field $E_I$ of the statement.

[F1] The $n=3$ fundamental solution is $\Phi(z)=1/(4\pi|z|)$, smooth and harmonic on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$; the Coulomb point-charge branch of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d) identifies the point-charge potential $\varphi_q^p=(q/\varepsilon_0)\Phi(\cdot-p)$ as locally integrable with distributional Laplacian $-\Delta T_{\varphi_q^p}=(q/\varepsilon_0)\delta_p$ on $\mathbb R^3$ and field $E_q^p=-\nabla\varphi_q^p$ satisfying $\operatorname{div}E_q^p=(q/\varepsilon_0)\delta_p$, $\operatorname{curl}E_q^p=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$ ([[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]], [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]).

[F2] A $C^1$ function on an open set represents its regular distribution and its distributional first derivatives are the regular distributions of its classical derivatives; distributional differentiation is linear and the Laplacian of a classical harmonic function therefore represents the zero distribution ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-distribution]], [[thm-integration-by-parts]], [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]).

[F3] Local integrability in dimension three: the radial integral of $|z|^{-1}$ over a ball is finite by polar coordinates, products and sums of locally integrable measurable functions on an open set are locally integrable, and continuous functions are Borel measurable ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]).

[F4] Mean value theorem and derivative calculus: for $g(y):=|x-y|^{-1}$ with $x$ fixed, $g$ is $C^\infty$ off $x$ and $\nabla g(y)=-(x-y)/|x-y|^3$, so $|\nabla g(y)|=|x-y|^{-2}$; the mean value theorem bounds $|g(p)-g(-p)|$ by $|p-(-p)|\sup|\nabla g|$ on the segment ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

[F5] The half-space uniqueness lemma: a function continuous on $\overline H\setminus\{p\}$, $C^2$ and harmonic on $H\setminus\{p\}$, zero on $\Pi$, sub-Coulomb at $p$ and vanishing at infinity in $H$ is identically zero ([[lem-em-half-space-harmonic-uniqueness-with-decay]]).

[F6] The polar/Fubini calculus on the plane: integrals over $\mathbb R^2$ may be computed in polar coordinates, the product and Euclidean measures agree on Borel sets, the plane is Lebesgue null in $\mathbb R^3$, and the one-dimensional fundamental theorem computes the radial primitive ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]], [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]], [[prop-degenerate-boxes-and-coordinate-hyperplanes-are-lebesgue-null]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]).

[F7] Framework readings: the fixed-time reading of the pure electrostatic regime identifies the static fields and the stationary point charge of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) with $q\delta_p$; the units are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; and the adopted distributional equations are those of [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](e), [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-weak-sources]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Clause (a). Write $\varphi_I=(q/\varepsilon_0)\Phi(\cdot-p)-(q/\varepsilon_0)\Phi(\cdot+ae_3)$ [F1]. The first term is smooth and harmonic off its pole $p$; the second has its pole at $-ae_3$, which lies outside the closed half-space $\overline H$, so it is $C^\infty$ on $H$ and harmonic there by [F1] and linearity of the Laplacian [F2]; hence $\varphi_I\in C^\infty(H\setminus\{p\})$, $\Delta\varphi_I=0$ there, and $E_I=-\nabla\varphi_I$ is $C^\infty$ on $H\setminus\{p\}$. [F1, F2]

1.2 Local integrability and distributional identities. $\varphi_I$ is locally integrable on $H$: $|x-p|^{-1}$ is locally integrable in dimension three and $|x+ae_3|^{-1}$ is continuous on $H$, and sums and scalar multiples of locally integrable measurable functions are locally integrable [F3]. Its regular distribution is $T_{\varphi_I}=(q/\varepsilon_0)T_{\Phi(\cdot-p)}-(q/\varepsilon_0)T_{\Phi(\cdot+ae_3)}$ [F2, F3]. On $H$ the second term is $C^\infty$ with classically vanishing Laplacian, so its distributional Laplacian is the regular distribution of the zero function [F2]; the first term has $-\Delta T=(q/\varepsilon_0)\delta_p$ on $\mathbb R^3$, hence on the open subset $H$ [F1]. Summing gives $-\Delta T_{\varphi_I}=(q/\varepsilon_0)\delta_p$ in $\mathcal D'(H)$. For the field, $E_I=E_q^p-E_q^{-p}$ where $E_q^{-p}:=-\nabla((q/\varepsilon_0)\Phi(\cdot+ae_3))$ is smooth on $H$ with $\operatorname{div}E_q^{-p}=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E_q^{-p}=0$ there [F2]; componentwise $T_{E_{I,i}}=-\partial_iT_{\varphi_I}$ on $H$ by the same representation and [F2], so the distributional divergence and curl of $E_I$ are those of the sum, giving $\operatorname{div}E_I=(q/\varepsilon_0)\delta_p$ and $\operatorname{curl}E_I=0$ in $\mathcal D'(H)$ [F1, F2]. This is (b); taking it together with [F7] reads $(E_I,0)$ as the pure electrostatic model on $H$ with the fixed-time point source $q\delta_p$, as asserted. [F1, F2, F3, F7]

1.3 Clause (c). On $\Pi$ one has $|x-p|=|x+ae_3|$ for every $x$ with $x_3=0$, so the bracket in $\varphi_I$ vanishes and $\varphi_I$ extends continuously (indeed $C^\infty$ away from $x=p\notin\Pi$) with value $0$ on $\Pi$. For the decay, fix $x$ with $|x|\ge2a$ and apply the mean value theorem to $g(y):=|x-y|^{-1}$ on the segment from $-ae_3$ to $ae_3$: since every point $y$ of that segment satisfies $|x-y|\ge|x|-a\ge a>0$, one has $|\nabla g(y)|=|x-y|^{-2}\le(|x|-a)^{-2}$ and therefore $|g(p)-g(-p)|\le 2a(|x|-a)^{-2}$ [F4]. Multiplying by $|q|/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$ gives $|\varphi_I(x)|\le |q|a/(2\pi\varepsilon_0(|x|-a)^2)\le 2|q|a/(\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^2)$ because $|x|\le 2(|x|-a)$ for $|x|\ge2a$. This is (c). [F4]

2.1 Clause (d). Let $\psi$ be as in the statement and put $w:=\psi-\varphi_I$ on $H\setminus\{p\}$. Then $w$ is $C^2$ and harmonic on $H\setminus\{p\}$ and continuous on $\overline H\setminus\{p\}$ by (a) [step 1.1]; $w=0$ on $\Pi$ because both functions vanish there [step 1.3]; $|x-p|w(x)\to0$ as $x\to p$ by the assumed leading-singularity condition; and $w(x)\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$ in $H$ because both $\psi$ and $\varphi_I$ do. By [F5] applied to $w$, $w=0$ on $H\setminus\{p\}$, so $\psi=\varphi_I$. This is (d). [F5, step 1.1, step 1.3]

2.2 Clause (e), first part. On the plane, $n=e_3$ and $\sigma=-\varepsilon_0\partial_3\varphi_I|_\Pi$; differentiating the two Coulomb terms, whose gradients are $-(x\mp p)/|x\mp p|^3$ [F4], at $x_3=0$ gives $\partial_3|x-p|^{-1}=a/(x_1^2+x_2^2+a^2)^{3/2}$ and $\partial_3|x+ae_3|^{-1}=-a/(x_1^2+x_2^2+a^2)^{3/2}$, so $\partial_3\varphi_I=qa/[2\pi\varepsilon_0(x_1^2+x_2^2+a^2)^{3/2}]$ and hence $\sigma(x_1,x_2)=-qa/[2\pi(x_1^2+x_2^2+a^2)^{3/2}]$, a smooth bounded function; the boundary condition $\varphi_I=0$ on $\Pi$ is the equipotential (zero) trace of the ideal grounded plane, and $(E_I,0)$ satisfies the static equations with source $q\delta_p$ on $H$ by (b) [step 1.2]. The total induced charge is
$$\int_{\mathbb R^2}\sigma\,d\lambda_2=-\frac{qa}{2\pi}\int_0^\infty\frac{2\pi r\,dr}{(r^2+a^2)^{3/2}}=-qa\Bigl[-\frac1{\sqrt{r^2+a^2}}\Bigr]_{r=0}^{\infty}=-q,$$
with the polar-coordinate computation and the improper radial primitive justified by [F6]; the integral is absolutely convergent because $|\sigma|\le qa/(2\pi(r^2+a^2)^{3/2})2\pi r$ is integrable. [F4, F6, step 1.2]

3.1 Clause (e), extension identity. Let $\widetilde E$ be $E_I$ on $H$ and $0$ on $\{x_3\le0\}$, and let $\sigma\delta_\Pi$ be the plane distribution $\eta\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^2}\sigma(x')\eta(x',0)\,dx'$, a well-defined finite-order functional by the boundedness of $\sigma$ and the nullity of the plane in $\mathbb R^3$ [F6]. For a test $\eta\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^3)$ and $0<\varepsilon<M$, integrate $\nabla\varphi_I\cdot\nabla\eta=\operatorname{div}(\eta\nabla\varphi_I)-\eta\Delta\varphi_I$ over the truncated region $H\cap B_M(0)\setminus\overline B_\varepsilon(p)$, where $\Delta\varphi_I=0$ [step 1.1]; the divergence theorem gives the boundary terms on $\Pi\cap B_M$, on the sphere $|x|=M$ and on the sphere $|x-p|=\varepsilon$. As $M\to\infty$ the outer term vanishes because $|\nabla\varphi_I(x)|\le C_M/|x|^2$ for $|x|\ge2a$ by the same mean value estimate applied to the gradient [F4] and the area grows like $M^2$; as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ the inner term tends to $(q/\varepsilon_0)\eta(p)$ because $\varphi_I-(q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0))|x-p|^{-1}$ is $C^1$ near $p$ and the outward normal of the truncated region on that sphere is $-(x-p)/|x-p|$, the flux of $-(q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0))|x-p|^{-1}$ being $+q/\varepsilon_0$ per the spherical-area computation; the plane term is $-\int_\Pi\eta\,\partial_3\varphi_I=\int_\Pi\eta\,\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ since the outward normal at $x_3=0$ is $-e_3$. Hence $\langle\operatorname{div}\widetilde E,\eta\rangle=-\int_H E_I\cdot\nabla\eta=\int_H\nabla\varphi_I\cdot\nabla\eta=\frac1{\varepsilon_0}\bigl(q\,\eta(p)+\int_\Pi\sigma\,\eta\bigr)$, which is the identity $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=(q\delta_p+\sigma\delta_\Pi)/\varepsilon_0$ on $\mathbb R^3$. For the curl, the identity $\operatorname{div}(\eta\times E_I)=\operatorname{curl}\eta\cdot E_I-\eta\cdot\operatorname{curl}E_I$ integrated over the same truncated region, with $\operatorname{curl}E_I=0$ classically on $H\setminus\{p\}$ [step 1.1] and the boundary term on $\Pi$ equal to $\eta\cdot(e_3\times E_+|_\Pi)$, vanishes because $E_+$ has vanishing tangential part on $\Pi$ ($\varphi_I=0$ on $\Pi$ forces its tangential derivatives to vanish there [step 1.3]); the sphere terms vanish in the limits as above, so $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=0$ on $\mathbb R^3$. [F1, F2, F4, F6, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.2]

4.1 Scope. The computations above concern exactly the ideal point charge above the ideal grounded plane in the declared class: the plane is not a compact embedded hypersurface and $\Pi$, $\{x_3<0\}$ and the plane pairing are not among the declared conductor or compact stationary-sheet objects of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] and [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) [F7]; the extension identity of [step 3.1] is a verified statement about the idealization and does not extend the framework postulate to arbitrary noncompact sheets. No finite-plane edge effect, conductor thickness, transient, moving charge, radiation, self-force or measurement is asserted, the singularity at $p$ is never evaluated, and uniqueness is claimed only in the class of (d) [step 2.1]. This is (f). [F7, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎
