## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the cited unit-Dirichlet solvability and trace interfaces, and its Countable Choice consequence for surface and integral interfaces ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(\Omega;D_1,\dots,D_m;\Omega_v)$ be the conductor geometry of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], additionally with $\Omega$ a bounded $C^\infty$ ambient domain and $\Omega_v$ connected and with the **outer boundary $\partial\Omega$ grounded**: the data on $\partial\Omega$ are the constant Dirichlet datum $0$; let $\rho_v\equiv0$ on $\Omega_v$ (the pure capacitor configuration: no volume source), and let the framework constants be those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. For each $j\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ let $\varphi_j\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ be the unit-potential solution of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c) with the smooth data
$$\varphi_j|_{\partial D_k}=\delta_{jk},\qquad \varphi_j|_{\partial\Omega}=0,$$
so that $-\Delta\varphi_j=0$ on $\Omega_v$ with the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], and let $\nu$ be the outward normal of $\Omega_v$ (so on $\partial D_j$ the normal $\nu$ points into the conductor). Define the **capacitance matrix** by
$$C_{jk}:=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi_k}{\partial\nu}\,dS,\qquad j,k=1,\dots,m,$$
the flux integrals of continuous functions over the compact embedded hypersurfaces $\partial D_j$ (normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]) ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]]). Then:
(a) [Linearity and matrix form] for every $V=(V_1,\dots,V_m)\in\mathbb R^m$ the unique equilibrium potential with conductor potentials $V$ and grounded outer boundary is $\varphi^V=\sum_{j=1}^mV_j\varphi_j$, and the conductor charges of [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]](d) are
$$Q_j(V)=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi^V}{\partial\nu}\,dS=\sum_{k=1}^mC_{jk}V_k,\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad Q=CV.$$
(b) [Reciprocity] $C$ is symmetric: $C_{jk}=C_{kj}$ for all $j,k$; the symmetry is Green's symmetric pairing of the harmonic potentials $\varphi_j,\varphi_k$.
(c) [Energy identity] the field energy of the configuration is
$$U(V)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\Omega_v}|\nabla\varphi^V|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12V^{T}CV=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^mV_jQ_j(V),$$
and $U(V)>0$ for every $V\ne0$: $C$ is symmetric positive definite. In particular $U(V)\ge0$, with equality exactly for $V=0$, so every nonzero conductor-potential data set stores positive field energy.
(d) [Two-conductor reading] with only conductor $1$ driven and every other conductor grounded, $V=te_1$: $Q_1=C_{11}t$, $Q_j=C_{j1}t$ for $j\ne1$, and $U=\tfrac12C_{11}t^2=\tfrac12Q_1V_1=Q_1^2/(2C_{11})$; the **capacitance of the arrangement** at conductor $1$ with respect to the grounded reference is the positive geometric number $C_{11}>0$, with $C_{11}=Q_1/V_1$ when $t=V_1\ne0$, and the energy identities $U=\tfrac12QV=Q^2/(2C)=\tfrac12CV^2$ hold with $C=C_{11}$, $Q=Q_1$, $V=V_1$. By (c) the positivity holds for every diagonal entry, $C_{jj}>0$.
(e) [Assembly reading] use the family $V_j(s)=sV_j$, $\varphi_s=s\varphi^V$, $Q_j(s)=sQ_j(V)$ for $0\le s\le1$, with fixed geometry and grounded reference. Prescribe the quasistatic external charge-transfer work by $dW_{\rm ext}=\sum_jV_j(s)dQ_j(s)$. Then $W_{\rm ext}=\int_0^1s\,ds\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)=U$. The potentials vary during assembly; only the final potentials and geometry are fixed. This derives the sheet-charge accounting directly and does not apply the volume-source theorem [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] to singular sheets. The family is an accounting prescription, not an asserted time-dependent Maxwell/material solution.
(f) [Scope] the theorem assumes: the compact separated conductor geometry, the additional bounded smooth ambient domain, and connected vacuum region of the model, the grounded outer boundary $\partial\Omega$, zero volume source, and the existence and uniqueness of the unit-potential Dirichlet solutions ([[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c), [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](a)). It asserts no solvability for arbitrary boundary data (the existence theorem is used only for the constant data above), no prescribed-total-charge problem, no dielectric or material response, no finite-conductivity or transient charging dynamics, no radiation, and no measurement; the matrix $C$ is a geometric object of the ideal electrostatic model, and the ideal parallel-plate and similar formulas are statements about this model only.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared in the statement; the conductor geometry $(\Omega;D_1,\dots,D_m;\Omega_v)$ of the model in the bounded smooth ambient branch with $\Omega$ a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, $\Omega_v$ connected, outer boundary grounded and $\rho_v\equiv0$; the unit-potential solutions $\varphi_j\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with $-\Delta\varphi_j=0$, $\varphi_j|_{\partial D_k}=\delta_{jk}$, $\varphi_j|_{\partial\Omega}=0$; the outward unit normal $\nu$ of $\Omega_v$; and the capacitance matrix $C_{jk}=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\partial\varphi_k/\partial\nu\,dS$.

[F1] The model and its vacuum geometry: in the bounded smooth ambient branch of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]] the vacuum region $\Omega_v$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ domain (in particular a bounded $C^1$ domain), its boundary is the disjoint union $\partial\Omega\cup\partial D_1\cup\cdots\cup\partial D_m$ of nonempty compact embedded smooth hypersurfaces, and $\partial\Omega$ is nonempty; the model requires $\Omega_v$ connected and nonempty, carries the pure electrostatic regime and the fields of the framework, and its constants are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]] ([[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]], [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], [[def-em-fields]]).

[F2] Unit-potential solvability and uniqueness: the datum equal to $\delta_{jk}$ on $\partial D_k$ and $0$ on $\partial\Omega$ is constant on each compact boundary piece, hence smooth on the disjoint union $\partial\Omega_v$; with $\rho_v\equiv0$ the conductor reading of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c) is a special case of its Dirichlet branch, so there is exactly one $\varphi_j\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with $-\Delta\varphi_j=0$ on $\Omega_v$ and the prescribed boundary values; uniqueness in the class of $C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ functions with identical boundary data is the Dirichlet uniqueness clause ([[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](a),(c), [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](a), [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

[F3] Surface charges and fluxes: for an equilibrium solution of the model with the joint one-sided regularity, $Q_j=\int_{\partial D_j}\sigma\,dS=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\partial\varphi/\partial\nu\,dS$, where $\nu$ is the outward normal of the vacuum; the integrals exist as integrals of the continuous flux over the compact embedded hypersurfaces $\partial D_j$ ([[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]](d), [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]).

[F4] Green's first identity on the bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega_v$: for real $u\in C^2(\overline{\Omega_v})$ and $v\in C^1(\overline{\Omega_v})$, $\int_{\Omega_v}(v\Delta u+Du\cdot Dv)\,d\lambda_3=\int_{\partial\Omega_v}v\,\partial_\nu u\,dS$ with the outward normal $\nu$; the boundary integral splits over the disjoint pieces $\partial\Omega,\partial D_1,\dots,\partial D_m$ ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], [F1]).

[F5] Positivity and constancy tools for (c): a continuous function on the compact $\overline{\Omega_v}$ is bounded and Borel, so for $\varphi^V\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ the function $|\nabla\varphi^V|^2$ is nonnegative, Borel, bounded and integrable over $\Omega_v$; a nonnegative measurable $f$ with $\int f\,d\lambda_3=0$ vanishes almost everywhere, and a continuous such $f$ on the connected open $\Omega_v$ then vanishes everywhere (otherwise a positive value would stay bounded below on a small Euclidean ball of positive finite measure); a totally differentiable function on a nonempty connected open Euclidean set with vanishing differential is constant; a function constant on the connected open $\Omega_v$ and continuous on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ has that constant equal to its value $0$ on the nonempty boundary piece $\partial\Omega$ ([[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]], [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]], [[thm-zero-derivative-on-connected-open-euclidean-set-iff-constant]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]).

[F6] Path-work reading and the elementary integral: for open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, $\phi\in C^1(U)$ and a piecewise $C^1$ path $\gamma:[a,b]\to U$, $\int_\gamma\nabla\phi\cdot d\mathbf r=\phi(\gamma(b))-\phi(\gamma(a))$; and $\int_0^1s\,ds=\tfrac12$ by the one-dimensional fundamental theorem ([[thm-gradient-theorem-for-line-integrals]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Setup and well-definedness: by [F1] the vacuum region $\Omega_v$ is a bounded $C^1$ domain (indeed $C^\infty$), connected, nonempty, with boundary the disjoint union of the nonempty compact pieces $\partial\Omega,\partial D_1,\dots,\partial D_m$, and with $\partial\Omega$ nonempty. By [F2] each unit-potential solution $\varphi_j\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ exists and is unique with $-\Delta\varphi_j=0$ and $\varphi_j|_{\partial D_k}=\delta_{jk}$, $\varphi_j|_{\partial\Omega}=0$. The normal $\nu$ is the outward unit normal of $\Omega_v$; it points into the conductor on each $\partial D_j$ [F1]. Each flux $\int_{\partial D_j}\partial\varphi_k/\partial\nu\,dS$ exists because $\partial\varphi_k/\partial\nu$ is continuous on the compact embedded hypersurface $\partial D_j$ carrying finite surface measure [F3], so $C_{jk}$ is well defined. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Linearity and the charge-potential map (a): fix $V\in\mathbb R^m$ and put $\varphi^V:=\sum_{j=1}^mV_j\varphi_j\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$. By linearity of the Laplacian, $-\Delta\varphi^V=\sum_jV_j(-\Delta\varphi_j)=0$ on $\Omega_v$; on $\partial D_k$ one has $\varphi^V=\sum_jV_j\delta_{jk}=V_k$, and on $\partial\Omega$, $\varphi^V=0$. By the uniqueness clause of [F2], $\varphi^V$ is the unique equilibrium potential with conductor potentials $V$ and grounded outer boundary, and the solution is linear in $V$ by construction. Its charges are given by [F3] and the definition of $C$: for each $j$, $Q_j(V)=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\partial\varphi^V/\partial\nu\,dS=\varepsilon_0\sum_{k=1}^mV_k\int_{\partial D_j}\partial\varphi_k/\partial\nu\,dS=\sum_{k=1}^mC_{jk}V_k$, that is $Q=CV$. [F2, F3, given, step 1.1]

2.2 Reciprocity (b): apply Green's first identity [F4] on the bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega_v$ twice, first with $u=\varphi_j$, $v=\varphi_k$ and then with $u=\varphi_k$, $v=\varphi_j$; both functions lie in $C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ and $\Delta\varphi_j=\Delta\varphi_k=0$, so subtracting the two identities gives $0=\int_{\partial\Omega_v}(\varphi_j\,\partial_\nu\varphi_k-\varphi_k\,\partial_\nu\varphi_j)\,dS$. The boundary splits into $\partial\Omega$ and the conductor surfaces [F4]; on $\partial\Omega$ both traces of $\varphi_j,\varphi_k$ vanish, so the outer piece contributes $0$, while on $\partial D_\ell$ the traces are $\delta_{j\ell}$ and $\delta_{k\ell}$, so the total reduces to $\int_{\partial D_j}\partial_\nu\varphi_k\,dS-\int_{\partial D_k}\partial_\nu\varphi_j\,dS$. Multiplying by $\varepsilon_0$ gives $C_{jk}=C_{kj}$ for all $j,k$; the symmetry is exactly Green's antisymmetric pairing of the two harmonic potentials. [F4, given, step 1.1]

3.1 Energy identity and positivity (c): apply Green's first identity [F4] once more with $u=v=\varphi^V$: $\int_{\Omega_v}(\varphi^V\Delta\varphi^V+|\nabla\varphi^V|^2)\,d\lambda_3=\int_{\partial\Omega_v}\varphi^V\partial_\nu\varphi^V\,dS$. The Laplacian term vanishes by [step 2.1], the outer boundary contributes $0$ because $\varphi^V$ vanishes on $\partial\Omega$, and on $\partial D_j$ the trace of $\varphi^V$ is the constant $V_j$, so $\int_{\partial\Omega_v}\varphi^V\partial_\nu\varphi^V\,dS=\sum_{j=1}^mV_j\int_{\partial D_j}\partial_\nu\varphi^V\,dS$. By [F3] and [step 2.1] this equals $\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)/\varepsilon_0=\frac1{\varepsilon_0}\sum_{j,k}V_jC_{jk}V_k=\frac1{\varepsilon_0}V^{T}CV$; multiplying by $\varepsilon_0/2$ gives the identity $U(V)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\Omega_v}|\nabla\varphi^V|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12V^{T}CV=\frac12\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)$. The energy is nonnegative because the integrand is; if $U(V)=0$, then $\int_{\Omega_v}|\nabla\varphi^V|^2\,d\lambda_3=0$, so $|\nabla\varphi^V|^2=0$ almost everywhere by [F5], hence everywhere by continuity on the connected open $\Omega_v$ [F5]; thus $\varphi^V$ is constant on $\Omega_v$ by [F5], and the constant is $0$ because $\varphi^V=0$ on the nonempty boundary piece $\partial\Omega$ and $\varphi^V$ is continuous on the closure [F5]; consequently $V_j=\varphi^V|_{\partial D_j}=0$ for every $j$, i.e. $V=0$. Hence $U(V)\ge0$ with equality exactly at $V=0$, and since $C$ is symmetric by [step 2.2], the symmetric bilinear form $V\mapsto\frac12V^{T}CV$ is positive definite. [F3, F4, F5, given, step 2.1, step 2.2]

4.1 Two-conductor reading (d): take $V=te_1$ with $t\in\mathbb R$. By [step 2.1], $\varphi^V=t\varphi_1$, $Q_1=C_{11}t$ and $Q_j=C_{j1}t$ for $j\ne1$; by [step 3.1], $U=\frac12C_{11}t^2=\frac12Q_1V_1$. For $t=0$ all charges and the energy vanish while the unit flux defining $C_{11}$ is unchanged; for $t\ne0$ one may divide by $t=V_1$ to obtain $C_{11}=Q_1/V_1$ and $U=Q_1^2/(2C_{11})$, using $C_{11}>0$ from the positive definiteness of [step 3.1] (take $V=e_1$: $U(e_1)=\frac12C_{11}>0$). Hence $C_{11}$ is the positive geometric capacitance of conductor $1$ with respect to the grounded reference, and the displayed identities $U=\frac12QV=Q^2/(2C)=\frac12CV^2$ hold with $C=C_{11}$, $Q=Q_1$, $V=V_1$. [given, step 2.1, step 3.1]

4.2 Assembly reading (e): for $0\le s\le1$ put $V(s):=sV$, $\varphi_s:=\varphi^{sV}=s\varphi^V$ by [step 2.1], and $Q_j(s):=Q_j(sV)=sQ_j(V)$, so that $dQ_j(s)=Q_j(V)\,ds$. The prescribed quasistatic external charge-transfer work is $dW_{\rm ext}=\sum_jV_j(s)\,dQ_j(s)=\sum_j(sV_j)Q_j(V)\,ds=s\,ds\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)$, and summing over the conductors and integrating over $s\in[0,1]$ gives $W_{\rm ext}=\bigl(\int_0^1s\,ds\bigr)\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)=\frac12\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)=U$ by [F6] and [step 3.1]. The family is an accounting prescription on the fixed geometry with grounded reference: the potentials vary during assembly, only the final potentials and geometry are fixed, and the sheet-charge accounting is derived directly rather than from the volume-source theorem [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]]; the path-work identity of [F6] gives the endpoint potential-drop reading along any interior piecewise $C^1$ path, with boundary endpoints understood as limits of the continuous closure traces. This is (e). [F6, given, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 Scope (f): the theorem used the compact separated conductor geometry and bounded smooth ambient branch with connected vacuum region [F1], the grounded outer boundary, the zero volume source, and the existence and uniqueness of the unit-potential Dirichlet solutions [F2]; the existence theorem was applied only to the constant data $V$ and $0$, so no solvability for arbitrary boundary data or for prescribed total charges is asserted, and no dielectric coefficient, material response, finite-conductivity or transient charging dynamics, radiation, measurement or apparatus claim enters [F1, F2]. The matrix $C$ is a geometric object of the ideal electrostatic model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], and the ideal parallel-plate and related formulas are statements about that model only; this completes (f) and the theorem. [F1, F2, given, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2] ∎

## Example

Assume the Countable Choice convention of [[pthm-em-image-method-certificate]] and [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] ([[def-countable-choice]]). In the ideal grounded-plane configuration of [[pthm-em-image-method-certificate]]: vacuum half-space $H=\{x_3>0\}$, point charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ at $p=ae_3$ ($a>0$), field $E_I$ given by the image potential, and $E_I$ has the Coulomb singularity $(q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0))(x-p)/|x-p|^3$ of the source charge as $x\to p$ ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d), [[def-em-fields]]). Split the field near $p$ as

$$E_I(x)=E_q(x)+E_{\rm ext}(x),\qquad E_q(x):=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{x-p}{|x-p|^3}\quad(x\ne p),$$

the **self-field** $E_q$ of the source charge and the **external (mirror) field** $E_{\rm ext}:=E_I-E_q$, which is $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $p$ (it is minus the gradient of the smooth mirror term $-q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)|x+ae_3|^{-1}$). Then:

(a) [External field at the charge] the external field at the location of the charge is

$$E_{\rm ext}(p)=-\frac{q}{16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2}\,e_3 .$$

It is the gradient of the mirror term evaluated at $p$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

(b) [Force on the held charge] under the adopted external Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](i) at zero velocity, a test particle of charge $q$ held at $p$ experiences the electric force

$$F=q\,E_{\rm ext}(p)=-\frac{q^2}{16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2}\,e_3,$$

strictly attractive toward the plane when $q\ne0$ and zero when $q=0$, of magnitude $q^2/(16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2)$; the particle's own field is excluded from the coupling by the postulate, so the result is a two-body-style external force of the mirror field and is not a self-force.

(c) [Reading and scope] for either nonzero sign of $q$ the force is attractive (the magnitude depends on $q^2$), while $q=0$ gives zero force; the induced total plane charge is $-q$ and its distribution is concentrated under the charge; the example is the exact ideal-model result for a held point charge, an ideal grounded plane and the adopted static external force law. It asserts no measurement, no dynamics of the charge (no motion or radiation), no finite-plane or finite-conductor correction, no self-force and no claim that the pair of idealisations is realised by an apparatus; the source is the idealised stationary point charge of [[pthm-em-image-method-certificate]](e), not a declared compact-source model. Here the displayed force is the electric contribution at rest. Holding the charge at $p$ requires a balancing support force $F_{\rm support}=-F$; the held trajectory is not asserted to solve the equation with the electric Lorentz force as its sole force.

## Facts & Assumptions


**Given:** The ideal grounded-plane configuration of [[pthm-em-image-method-certificate]] with charge parameter $q$, location $p=ae_3$, $a>0$, field $E_I=-\nabla\varphi_I$ and the split $E_I=E_q+E_{\rm ext}$ of the statement.

[F1] The image certificate supplies the candidate potential and field; the mirror term $u(x):=-(q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0))|x+ae_3|^{-1}$ is $C^\infty$ on the ball $|x-p|<a$ because $|x+ae_3|\ge a>0$ there, and off the pole $E_I=-\nabla\varphi_I$ with $\varphi_I=\varphi_q^p+u$, where $\varphi_q^p=(q/\varepsilon_0)\Phi(\cdot-p)$ is the point-charge potential of the fundamental solution and $E_q=-\nabla\varphi_q^p$ ([pthm-em-image-method-certificate](a),(b); pthm-em-coulomb-solution(d); lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole).

[F2] Derivative calculus for the mirror term: for fixed $c\ne0$ the function $x\mapsto|x+c|^{-1}$ is $C^\infty$ on $\{|x+c|>0\}$ with $\nabla|x+c|^{-1}=-(x+c)|x+c|^{-3}$, by the chain and power rules and the Euclidean inner product ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

[F3] The adopted external Lorentz coupling at zero velocity: [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](i) adopts the covariant Lorentz-force equation with a prescribed external field and excludes the particle's own field; at zero coordinate velocity the magnetic term vanishes and the coordinate force is $q$ times the external electric field, in the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]] ([[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]).

[F4] The ball $|x-p|<a$ contains $p$ and is an open neighbourhood of $p$ ([[def-metric-ball]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 External field. By [F1], $E_{\rm ext}=E_I-E_q=-\nabla(\varphi_I-\varphi_q^p)=-\nabla u$ on the punctured half-space, and $u$ is $C^\infty$ on the ball $|x-p|<a$ [F1, F4]. By [F2] with $c=+ae_3$, $\nabla u(x)=+\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{x+ae_3}{|x+ae_3|^3}$ there, so at $x=p=ae_3$ one has $\nabla u(p)=\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{2ae_3}{(2a)^3}=\dfrac{q\,e_3}{16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2}$ and $E_{\rm ext}(p)=-\nabla u(p)=-\dfrac{q}{16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2}e_3$. This is (a). [F1, F2, F4]

2.1 Force. By [F3] applied at the instantaneous rest state of the held charge, the force is $F=qE_{\rm ext}(p)$; substituting [step 1.1] gives $F=-\dfrac{q^2}{16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2}e_3$. This is (b). [F3, step 1.1]

3.1 Signs, magnitude and scope. Since $q^2\ge0$ with equality exactly for $q=0$, the vector $F$ is a nonpositive multiple of $e_3$: for $q\ne0$ it points from $p$ toward the plane and has magnitude $q^2/(16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2)$, while $q=0$ gives $F=0$. The self-field $E_q$ is excluded from the coupling by [F3], so the computation is the external mirror force and not a self-force; the induced total plane charge $-q$ and the concentration of the induced distribution under the charge are the ideal-plane statements of [[pthm-em-image-method-certificate]](e), and the held trajectory is not claimed to solve any dynamics. This is (c). [F1, F3, given, step 2.1] ∎

## Example

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the integral and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). **Declare the ideal parallel-plate model** of two infinite parallel charged planes in vacuo, read as equipotential ideal conductor surfaces of the same equilibrium structure as [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] (the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields [[def-em-fields]]): for a separation parameter $d>0$, half-separation $h=d/2$, a surface-density parameter $\sigma>0$ (C m$^{-2}$) and the framework constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], the model consists of the field
$$E(x):=\begin{cases}-\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}e_3,&|x_3|<h,\\[2pt]0,&|x_3|>h,\end{cases}\qquad x=(x_1,x_2,x_3),$$
together with the plane densities $+\sigma$ on $\Pi_+:=\{x_3=h\}$ and $-\sigma$ on $\Pi_-:=\{x_3=-h\}$, and with the piecewise potential $\varphi(x):=+\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}x_3$ for $|x_3|\le h$, $\varphi:=+\dfrac{\sigma h}{\varepsilon_0}$ for $x_3\ge h$ and $\varphi:=-\dfrac{\sigma h}{\varepsilon_0}$ for $x_3\le-h$. Then:
(a) [Direct distributional verification] $E$ and $\varphi$ are locally integrable and $C^\infty$ off $\Pi_+\cup\Pi_-$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ there, $\varphi$ is continuous on $\mathbb R^3$ and constant on each plane with the values $\varphi|_{\Pi_+}=+\sigma h/\varepsilon_0$, $\varphi|_{\Pi_-}=-\sigma h/\varepsilon_0$; and in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$
$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\bigl(\delta_{\Pi_+}-\delta_{\Pi_-}\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0,$$
where $\delta_{\Pi_\pm}(\psi):=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\psi(x_1,x_2,\pm h)\,dx_1\,dx_2$ for compactly supported smooth $\psi$ are the plane distributions defined by the iterated Lebesgue integrals. Equivalently, the model realises the static electrostatic equations with the declared pair of plane densities and no other source, and the potential differences read off $\varphi$ are $\varphi(h)-\varphi(-h)=2\sigma h/\varepsilon_0=\sigma d/\varepsilon_0$.
(b) [Uniform field and voltage] the field between the planes has constant magnitude $|E|=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and is normal to the planes, and the potential difference between the plates is $V:=\varphi|_{\Pi_+}-\varphi|_{\Pi_-}=\sigma d/\varepsilon_0$.
(c) [Charge, capacitance and energy of the ideal model] for any Lebesgue-measurable region $P\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ with finite positive area $A=\lambda_2(P)>0$ the charge on the portion of area $A$ of the positive plate is $Q:=\sigma A$, so $Q=(\varepsilon_0A/d)V$ with the geometric ratio
$$C:=\frac QV=\frac{\varepsilon_0A}{d}>0,$$
independent of $\sigma$ and $V$; and the field energy contained in the slab of area $A$ between the plates is
$$U=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\text{slab of area }A}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac{\sigma^2Ad}{2\varepsilon_0}=\frac12QV=\frac{Q^2}{2C}=\frac12CV^2 .$$
(d) [Relation to the bounded-conductor theorem and scope] the linearity $Q=CV$, the positivity $C>0$ and the energy identities $U=\frac12QV=\frac{Q^2}{2C}=\frac12CV^2$ are exactly the conclusions that [[pthm-em-capacitance-energy]] proves for bounded conductor configurations with prescribed potentials and a grounded reference; this example verifies them directly for the ideal model because the infinite planes and the unbounded declared field are outside that theorem's hypotheses (compact conductors in a bounded vacuum region) and outside the declared stationary-sheet source type of [[def-em-weak-sources]], exactly as the ideal line source lies outside the compact-source types of the electrostatic page. No approximation theorem from finite plates to the infinite model is asserted; for a finite real plate pair the uniform-field model neglects the fringing field near the edges, which is not computed here, and the idealisation also omits the finite-thickness, material, transient and measurement content of any real capacitor.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice; the parameters $d>0$, $h=d/2$, $\sigma>0$ and $\varepsilon_0>0$; the declared field $E$, plane densities $\pm\sigma$ on $\Pi_\pm$, and potential $\varphi$ of the statement; and the plane distributions $\delta_{\Pi_\pm}$.

[F1] The model data and elementary regularity: $E$ is bounded, equal to $-(\sigma/\varepsilon_0)e_3$ on the open slab $\{|x_3|<h\}$ and to $0$ outside it, hence locally integrable; $\varphi$ is bounded, affine on the closed slab, constant on the two open half-spaces, and continuous on $\mathbb R^3$ with equal one-sided values on each plane: $\varphi|_{\Pi_+}=\sigma h/\varepsilon_0$, $\varphi|_{\Pi_-}=-\sigma h/\varepsilon_0$; on each of the three open regions $\{|x_3|<h\}$, $\{x_3>h\}$, $\{x_3<-h\}$ the maps are $C^\infty$ (affine or constant), and $E=-\nabla\varphi$ there by the classical gradient of affine functions; on the slab $|E|=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and $E$ is normal to the planes, outside it $E=0$; the plane functionals $\delta_{\Pi_\pm}$ are finite-order distributions on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]]).

[F2] Distributional calculus and integration: a locally integrable function represents a regular distribution, its distributional partial derivatives act by $\langle\partial_iT_F,\psi\rangle=-\int F\,\partial_i\psi\,d\lambda_3$, and differentiability distinguishes the constant slab-indicator part; test functions are smooth and compactly supported, sums and scalar multiples of L¹ functions are L¹, and the iterated integrals over $\mathbb R^2\times(-h,h)$ may be computed by Fubini, with the one-dimensional fundamental theorem giving $\int_{-h}^h\partial_3\psi(x_1,x_2,s)\,ds=\psi(x_1,x_2,h)-\psi(x_1,x_2,-h)$ for smooth compactly supported $\psi$, the comparison of Riemann and Lebesgue integrands being available throughout ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], [[thm-integration-by-parts]], [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]]).

[F3] Slab measure for measurable bases: for a Lebesgue-measurable $P\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ with $A=\lambda_2(P)$, choosing a Borel set $P_0$ equal to $P$ off a Borel $\lambda_2$-null set, the product $P_0\times(-h,h)$ is Borel with $\lambda_3(P_0\times(-h,h))=\lambda_2(P_0)\cdot2h=A\cdot2h$ by the product-measure identification and Tonelli, while $(P\triangle P_0)\times(-h,h)$ is contained in the null set $N\times(-h,h)$; completeness of Lebesgue measure then gives $\lambda_3(P\times(-h,h))=A\cdot2h$, and the same argument applies to any nonnegative integrand constant on the slab ([[cor-lebesgue-sigma-algebra-is-the-completion-of-borel-lebesgue-measure]], [[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]], [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]], [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]).

[F4] The relation to the bounded-conductor theorem: [[pthm-em-capacitance-energy]] proves $Q=CV$ with symmetric positive definite $C$ and the energy identities for bounded conductor bodies in a bounded vacuum region with grounded outer boundary; its hypotheses concern compact conductor bodies and the declared stationary-sheet source type, and the infinite planes of the present model satisfy neither ([[pthm-em-capacitance-energy]], [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], [[def-em-weak-sources]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Local integrability, classical relations and continuity: $E$ is bounded by $\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and continuous off the two planes, so for every compactly supported smooth test the product $E\cdot\nabla\psi$ is compactly supported and the integral is finite; $\varphi$ is bounded by $\sigma h/\varepsilon_0$, hence locally integrable, and continuous because the slab formula, the two constants and the plane values match at $x_3=\pm h$. On each of the three open regions $E=-\nabla\varphi$ classically, with $|E|=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and normal direction inside the slab and $E=0$ outside; this is the regularity asserted in (a) and the uniform-field statement of (b). [F1, given]

1.2 Distributional divergence: for $\psi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^3)$, the definition of the distributional derivative gives $\langle\operatorname{div}E,\psi\rangle=-\int_{\mathbb R^3}E\cdot\nabla\psi\,d\lambda_3$, and since $E$ vanishes off the slab and equals $-(\sigma/\varepsilon_0)e_3$ on it, this is $\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf 1_{\{|x_3|<h\}}\partial_3\psi\,d\lambda_3$. Fubini writes the integral as the iterated integral $\int_{\mathbb R^2}\bigl(\int_{-h}^{h}\partial_3\psi(x_1,x_2,s)\,ds\bigr)dx_1dx_2$, and the inner integral equals $\psi(x_1,x_2,h)-\psi(x_1,x_2,-h)$ by the fundamental theorem; hence $\langle\operatorname{div}E,\psi\rangle=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}(\delta_{\Pi_+}-\delta_{\Pi_-})(\psi)$ for every test $\psi$, i.e. $\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}(\delta_{\Pi_+}-\delta_{\Pi_-})$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$, with no other source. [F2, given]

1.3 Distributional curl: $E_1=E_2=0$ are the zero distribution; $E_3=-(\sigma/\varepsilon_0)\mathbf 1_{\{|x_3|<h\}}$ is a function of $x_3$ alone, so pairing its distributional $\partial_1$- and $\partial_2$-derivatives against a test gives integrals of $\partial_1\psi$ and $\partial_2\psi$ over the slab, and each inner one-dimensional integral over $\mathbb R$ of a compactly supported derivative vanishes by the fundamental theorem; hence $\partial_1E_3=\partial_2E_3=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$, while $\partial_3E_1=\partial_3E_2=0$ because $E_1,E_2$ vanish identically. All three components of $\operatorname{curl}E=(\partial_2E_3-\partial_3E_2,\ \partial_3E_1-\partial_1E_3,\ \partial_1E_2-\partial_2E_1)$ therefore vanish: $\operatorname{curl}E=0$. Together with the divergence identity above this is the asserted static electrostatic realization of (a) with the declared plane sources, and no other source. [F2, given]

1.4 Potential difference and voltage (b): the trace values of [F1] give $\varphi|_{\Pi_+}-\varphi|_{\Pi_-}=\sigma h/\varepsilon_0-(-\sigma h/\varepsilon_0)=2\sigma h/\varepsilon_0=\sigma d/\varepsilon_0$ because $d=2h$; combined with the constant normal field of magnitude $\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ between the planes and the zero field outside, this is (b), and it also exhibits the potential difference of (a). [F1, given]

2.1 Charge, capacitance and energy (c): fix a Lebesgue-measurable $P\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ with finite positive area $A=\lambda_2(P)$. The positive plate carries the constant density $+\sigma$, so the charge on the portion over $P$ is $Q=\sigma\lambda_2(P)=\sigma A$. The slab of area $A$ between the plates is $P\times(-h,h)$, and on it $|E|^2=\sigma^2/\varepsilon_0^2$ is constant; by [F3] the slab has $\lambda_3$-measure $A\cdot2h=Ad$, so Tonelli gives $\int_{P\times(-h,h)}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=(\sigma^2/\varepsilon_0^2)Ad$ and $U=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\cdot\frac{\sigma^2}{\varepsilon_0^2}Ad=\frac{\sigma^2Ad}{2\varepsilon_0}$. With $V=\sigma d/\varepsilon_0$ from [step 1.4], the ratio $C:=Q/V=(\sigma A)/(\sigma d/\varepsilon_0)=\varepsilon_0A/d$ is positive and independent of $\sigma$ and $V$; and the four displayed energies agree: $\frac12QV=\frac12\sigma A\cdot\frac{\sigma d}{\varepsilon_0}=\frac{\sigma^2Ad}{2\varepsilon_0}$, $Q^2/(2C)=(\sigma A)^2\cdot\frac{d}{2\varepsilon_0A}=\frac{\sigma^2Ad}{2\varepsilon_0}$ and $\frac12CV^2=\frac12\cdot\frac{\varepsilon_0A}{d}\cdot\frac{\sigma^2d^2}{\varepsilon_0^2}=\frac{\sigma^2Ad}{2\varepsilon_0}$. This is (c). [F1, F3, given, step 1.4]

3.1 Relation to the bounded-conductor theorem and scope (d): the relations $Q=CV$, $C>0$ and $U=\frac12QV=\frac{Q^2}{2C}=\frac12CV^2$ verified in [step 2.1] are exactly the conclusions [[pthm-em-capacitance-energy]] establishes for bounded conductor configurations with prescribed potentials and grounded reference [F4]; the present verification is direct, from the explicitly declared piecewise model, because the infinite planes, the unbounded field and the plane densities are outside that theorem's compact-conductor and declared sheet-source hypotheses, and no approximation theorem from finite plates to the infinite model is asserted. The uniform-field idealization neglects the fringing field near finite edges, which is not computed, and omits finite thickness, material, transient and measurement content; the direct argument retains only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as declared, and no empirical claim is made. This is (d). [F4, given, step 2.1] ∎

The item is an impossibility statement about the ideal boundary value problem and asserts no measurement, no apparatus, no material property and no conclusion beyond the displayed data."

## Example

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the cited Sobolev trace/weak-solvability interfaces and Countable Choice for the surface-measure interfaces ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $B:=B_1(0)=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|<1\}$ be the open unit ball, a bounded $C^\infty$ (in particular $C^1$) domain with $\partial B=S^2$ and outward normal $\nu(x)=x$ ([[lem-em-euclidean-balls-and-annuli-are-bounded-c-one-domains]], [[def-metric-ball]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and consider the pure electrostatic Neumann problem on $B$ (regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], fields [[def-em-fields]], constants [[def-em-si-conventions]]) with **zero volume source and unit normal field**:
$$-\Delta\varphi=0\ \text{ in }B,\qquad \partial_\nu\varphi=1\ \text{ on }\partial B .$$
Then:
(a) [No classical solution] there is no real $\varphi\in C^2(\overline B)$ satisfying these equations: if such a $\varphi$ existed, [[lem-neumann-compatibility-from-the-divergence-theorem]] with $f=-\Delta\varphi=0$ and $g=\partial_\nu\varphi\equiv1$ would give
$$0=\int_B f\,d\lambda_3=-\int_{\partial B}g\,dS=-|S^2|=-4\pi,$$
because the surface area of the unit sphere is $|S^2|=4\pi$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]); the contradiction is the failure of the necessary flux compatibility of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](b).
(b) [No weak solution] more generally there is no $u\in H^1(B)$ with $\int_B\nabla v\cdot\nabla u\,d\lambda_3=\langle g,Tv\rangle$ for all $v\in H^1(B)$ with $g\equiv1$ read as an element of the dual trace space ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]): testing $v\equiv1$ would force $\ell(1)=\int_{\partial B}1\,dS=4\pi=0$, and the weak Neumann existence lemma states existence exactly when $\ell(1)=0$ ([[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]); equivalently the unit ball's boundary flux budget fails already in the weak formulation.
(c) [Physics reading and scope] in the pure electrostatic regime the datum $\partial_\nu\varphi\equiv1$ on the whole boundary of the unit ball is inadmissible: no electrostatic potential with zero volume source satisfies it, and the obstruction is the strictly positive total boundary flux $4\pi$, not a smoothness or compactness artefact. The admissible Neumann data are exactly those satisfying the necessary compatibility $\int_{\partial B}g\,dS=0$ for the zero-source problem, which is a flux budget and not an existence theorem (sufficiency at the smooth level is the separate content of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](b) under its hypotheses). The item is a mathematical impossibility statement about the ideal boundary value problem: it reports no measurement, no apparatus and no material property, and the companion failure with unit source and zero boundary field is the same flux obstruction, obtained by evaluating that lemma with $f\equiv1$ and $g\equiv0$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared in the statement; the open unit ball $B=B_1(0)$, its boundary $S^2=\partial B$, the outward normal $\nu(x)=x$ on $S^2$, the pure electrostatic regime with zero volume source, and the displayed boundary value problem $-\Delta\varphi=0$ in $B$, $\partial_\nu\varphi=1$ on $\partial B$.

[F1] Classical Neumann compatibility: for a bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega$, a real $u\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$, $f:=-\Delta u$ and $g:=\partial_\nu u$, one has $\int_\Omega f\,d\lambda_3=-\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,dS$ ([[lem-neumann-compatibility-from-the-divergence-theorem]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]).

[F2] The unit ball is a bounded $C^\infty$ domain (in particular a bounded $C^1$ domain) with $\partial B=S^2$, outward normal $\nu(x)=x$ on $S^2$, a compact embedded $C^\infty$ hypersurface carrying its finite surface measure; moreover $|S^{n-1}|=n|B_1|$, and with $V_3(1)=\pi^{3/2}/\Gamma(5/2)$, $\Gamma(5/2)=\frac32\cdot\frac12\,\Gamma(1/2)=\frac{3\sqrt\pi}{4}$ and $\Gamma(1/2)=\sqrt\pi$, one computes $V_3(1)=4\pi/3$ and $|S^2|=3\cdot4\pi/3=4\pi$ ([[lem-em-euclidean-balls-and-annuli-are-bounded-c-one-domains]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]], [[thm-real-gamma-functional-equation]], [[cor-real-gamma-one-half-is-root-pi]], [[def-metric-ball]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

[F3] Boundary trace space: with the Axiom of Choice there is a unique bounded linear trace operator $T:W^{1,2}(B)\to L^2(S^2)$ with $Tu=u|_{S^2}$ for every $u\in C(\overline B)\cap W^{1,2}(B)$; the boundary fractional space $H^{1/2}(S^2)=W^{1/2,2}(S^2)$ is defined by the finite graph atlas and partition norm whose localised terms are Slobodeckij norms, each dominating the corresponding localised $L^2$ term, and the smooth graph densities are bounded on the compact supports of the partition, so there is a constant $C$ with $\|h\|_{L^2(S^2)}\le C\|h\|_{H^{1/2}(S^2)}$ for every $h\in H^{1/2}(S^2)$ ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]], [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]).

[F4] The weak Neumann solvability interface: for a bounded connected $C^1$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, $\varepsilon$ measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic, $\rho\in L^2(\Omega)$, $g\in H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ and $\ell(v)=\int_\Omega\rho v\,d\lambda_3+\langle g,Tv\rangle$ on $H^1(\Omega)$, a weak Neumann solution $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u\,d\lambda_3=\ell(v)$ for every $v\in H^1(\Omega)$ exists if and only if $\ell(1)=0$; in particular for $\varepsilon=I$, $\rho=0$ and $g\in H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ the solvability criterion is $\langle g,T1\rangle=0$ ([[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], [[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]).

[F5] Cauchy-Schwarz for $L^2$: $\int|fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_2\|g\|_2$ for $f,g\in\mathcal L^2$ ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]).

[F6] The constant function $1\in C^\infty(\overline B)$ satisfies $T1=1$ in $L^2(S^2)$, the trace of the restriction, by the agreement of $T$ with restriction on $C(\overline B)\cap W^{1,2}(B)$ in [F3]; and $1\in L^2(S^2)$ with $\|1\|_{L^2(S^2)}=|S^2|^{1/2}=2\sqrt\pi$ ([[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], [F2]).

[F7] Regime and reading: in the pure electrostatic regime with $J=0$, $B=0$ and volume density $\rho=0$, the compatibility identity of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](b) is the necessary flux budget for the smooth Neumann problem, and the sufficiency statement in the smooth class is [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](b) under its hypotheses; the constants, fields and units are those of the framework ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]], [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Geometry and area of the unit ball: $B$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ domain with $\partial B=S^2$ and outward normal $\nu(x)=x$; it is connected and nonempty. The area is $|S^2|=4\pi$: by $|S^{n-1}|=n|B_1|$ and $V_n(1)=\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2+1)$, the functional equation gives $\Gamma(5/2)=\frac32\Gamma(3/2)=\frac32\cdot\frac12\Gamma(1/2)=\frac{3\sqrt\pi}{4}$ with $\Gamma(1/2)=\sqrt\pi$, so $V_3(1)=\pi^{3/2}/(3\sqrt\pi/4)=4\pi/3$ and $|S^2|=3V_3(1)=4\pi$. [F2, F6]

2.1 Classical exclusion (a): suppose a real $\varphi\in C^2(\overline B)$ satisfies $-\Delta\varphi=0$ in $B$ and $\partial_\nu\varphi=1$ on $\partial B$; put $f:=-\Delta\varphi=0$ and $g:=\partial_\nu\varphi\equiv1$. By [F1] applied on the bounded $C^1$ domain $B$ with the outward normal $\nu$, $0=\int_B f\,d\lambda_3=-\int_{\partial B}g\,dS=-|S^2|=-4\pi$ by [step 1.1], a contradiction since $4\pi\ne0$; hence no such $\varphi$ exists. This is (a), and it exhibits the failure of the necessary compatibility of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](b). [F1, F7, given, step 1.1]

2.2 The datum $g\equiv1$ as an element of the dual trace space: $1\in L^2(S^2)$ by [F6], so for $h\in H^{1/2}(S^2)$ the integral $\int_{S^2}h\,dS$ is absolutely convergent, and Cauchy-Schwarz together with the inclusion bound of [F3] gives $|\int_{S^2}h\,dS|\le|S^2|^{1/2}\|h\|_{L^2(S^2)}\le C|S^2|^{1/2}\|h\|_{H^{1/2}(S^2)}$; hence $g\equiv1$ defines a bounded linear functional $\langle g,\cdot\rangle$ on $H^{1/2}(S^2)$, i.e. an element of $H^{-1/2}(\partial B)$, with $\langle g,h\rangle=\int_{S^2}h\,dS$. [F3, F5, F6, step 1.1]

2.3 Companion failure with unit source and zero boundary field: for $f\equiv1$ on $B$ and $g\equiv0$ on $\partial B$, any hypothetical $\varphi\in C^2(\overline B)$ with $-\Delta\varphi=f$ and $\partial_\nu\varphi=g$ would satisfy, by [F1], $\int_B f\,d\lambda_3=|B_1|=V_3(1)=4\pi/3\ne0=-\int_{\partial B}0\,dS$, a contradiction; thus the same flux budget excludes the unit-source datum, and in the weak formulation the corresponding functional $\ell'(v)=\int_B v\,d\lambda_3$ has $\ell'(1)=4\pi/3\ne0$, excluding weak solutions by [F4] as well. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 The functional $\ell(v):=\langle g,Tv\rangle=\int_{S^2}Tv\,dS$ on $H^1(B)$: it is well defined because $Tv\in L^2(S^2)$ by [F3] and $L^2(S^2)\subset L^1(S^2)$ with $\int_{S^2}|Tv|\,dS\le|S^2|^{1/2}\|Tv\|_{L^2(S^2)}$ by Cauchy-Schwarz and $|S^2|<\infty$ [F5, F6]; it is linear and bounded, $|\ell(v)|\le|S^2|^{1/2}\|Tv\|_{L^2(S^2)}\le C'\|v\|_{H^1(B)}$, by the trace bound [F3]. At the constant function $v\equiv1$ one has $\ell(1)=\int_{S^2}T1\,dS=\int_{S^2}1\,dS=|S^2|=4\pi\ne0$ by [F6] and [step 1.1]. [F3, F5, step 1.1, step 2.2]

4.1 Weak exclusion (b): with $\Omega=B$ (bounded, connected, $C^1$), $\varepsilon=I$ (symmetric, uniformly elliptic), $\rho=0\in L^2(B)$ and $g\equiv1\in H^{-1/2}(\partial B)$ from [step 2.2], the data functional of the weak Neumann problem is exactly $\ell$ of [step 3.1]; by the criterion [F4], a weak solution $u\in H^1(B)$ with $\int_B\nabla v\cdot\nabla u\,d\lambda_3=\ell(v)=\langle g,Tv\rangle$ for all $v\in H^1(B)$ exists if and only if $\ell(1)=0$, but $\ell(1)=4\pi\ne0$ by [step 3.1]; hence no such $u$ exists. The obstruction is already visible by testing $v\equiv1$: the left side vanishes and the right side is $4\pi$. This is (b). [F4, given, step 3.1]

5.1 Reading and scope (c): on the unit ball with zero volume source the unit outward normal-derivative datum is inadmissible in both the classical $C^2(\overline B)$ class and the weak $H^1(B)$ class; the obstruction is the strictly positive total boundary flux $|S^2|=4\pi$, not smoothness or compactness, and the necessary compatibility $\int_{\partial B}g\,dS=0$ for the zero-source problem is a flux budget whereas sufficiency in the smooth class is the separate content of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](b) under its hypotheses [F7]. No step uses the ball's symmetry beyond the area computation of [step 1.1]; no measurement, apparatus or material property is asserted, and the companion failure of [step 2.3] is the same flux obstruction evaluated at $f\equiv1$, $g\equiv0$. This is (c). [F7, given, step 2.1, step 4.1, step 2.3] ∎

## Definition

For the Lebesgue branches (a) and (b) assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the exact measure interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); the finite sums in branch (c) are defined and computed without Choice. Let the laboratory region, its chart, its spatial Euclidean structure and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $\delta_{ij}$ be the Kronecker symbol in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame, with $|y|$ the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. This definition assigns **source moments** to a static charge distribution in the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (d) and (e). Three branches are declared.

(a) [Absolutely continuous branch] Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real ([[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]) and vanish $\lambda_3$-almost everywhere outside the closed ball $\overline B_a(0)=\{y:|y|\le a\}$ ([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]). The **total charge** $Q$, the **dipole moment** $p$, the **degree-$l$ Cartesian moments** $M_{i_1\dots i_l}$ and the **traceless quadrupole** $Q_{ij}$ are

$$Q:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\,d\lambda_3,\qquad p_i:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}y_i\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),\qquad M_{i_1\dots i_l}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\ (l\ge1),$$

$$M^{(0)}:=Q,\qquad M_i:=p_i,\qquad Q_{ij}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\bigl(3y_iy_j-|y|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$

with $l\ge1$ and indices in $\{1,2,3\}$; units are C for $Q$, C m for $p$, C m$^l$ for the degree-$l$ Cartesian moment and C m$^2$ for $Q_{ij}$, and all integrals are in the sense of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]] and [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]. Each integral is absolutely convergent: since $\rho=0$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. off $\overline B_a(0)$, and the maps $y\mapsto y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}$ and $y\mapsto 3y_iy_j-|y|^2\delta_{ij}$ are bounded $\lambda_3$-a.e. on that ball by $a^l$ and by $4a^2$ respectively, the integrands are dominated $\lambda_3$-a.e. by $a^l|\rho|$ and $4a^2|\rho|$, which lie in $L^1$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). The traceless quadrupole is traceless,

$$\sum_{i=1}^3Q_{ii}=0,$$

because $\sum_{i=1}^3(3y_i^2-|y|^2)=0$ pointwise, and summing the three integrable functions $3y_i^2\rho-|y|^2\rho$ and applying finite linearity of the integral on $L^1$ ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]) evaluates the sum as the integral of the pointwise-zero function; replacing $\rho$ by an equal $\lambda_3$-a.e. density changes no moment ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]).

(b) [General locally integrable branch] If instead $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$ is real and $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^l|\rho(y)|\,d\lambda_3(y)<\infty$ for a given integer $l\ge0$, then the degree-$l$ Cartesian moments of the same formula are absolutely convergent and defined; if the absolute weighted moment $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^L|\rho(y)|\,d\lambda_3(y)$ is finite for some real $L\ge0$, then every integer Cartesian degree $0\le l\le L$ is defined, and in particular $Q=\int\rho\,d\lambda_3$ is absolutely convergent, so that $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ is a conclusion of this branch and not an added hypothesis. Here $\rho$ is restricted to the closed unit ball, where it is integrable by local integrability, and outside it $|y|^l\le|y|^L$; splitting the nonnegative integral over these two measurable sets and applying monotonicity and additivity of the integral gives $\int|y|^l|\rho|\le\int_{\overline B_1(0)}|\rho|+\int_{\{|y|>1\}}|y|^L|\rho|<\infty$ ([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[def-metric-ball]]). The convention $|y|^0=1$ includes the origin, no compact support and no $L^1$-membership is assumed in this branch, and Cartesian monomials of degree $l$ have modulus at most $|y|^l$, so all lower moments, including $Q$, exist together with the degree-$l$ moment.

(c) [Finite system of stationary point charges] Let $N\ge0$, let $x_1,\dots,x_N\in\mathbb R^3$ and let $q_1,\dots,q_N\in\mathbb R$ be charge parameters ([[def-em-sources]] (a)), read as the stationary point charges $q_k\delta_{x_k}$ in the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e); for $N=0$ the lists are empty and every sum below is the empty sum $0$. Define

$$Q:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_k,\qquad p:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_kx_k,\qquad M_{i_1\dots i_l}:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_k\,x_{k,i_1}\cdots x_{k,i_l}\ (l\ge1),\qquad M^{(0)}:=Q,$$

$$Q_{ij}:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_k\bigl(3x_{k,i}x_{k,j}-|x_k|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr),$$

finite sums in the sense of [[def-finite-sum]] ([[lem-finite-sum-laws]]); again

$$\sum_{i=1}^3Q_{ii}=0,$$

by finite distributivity. The points need not be distinct; charges at a common point add in every sum.

(d) [Reference point and scope] Every moment of (a)-(c) is computed about the chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; this origin is part of the definition. These are source moments of a prescribed static distribution, not momenta, rest masses, intrinsic spins, self-energies or dynamical quantities, and no field, force, equation of motion, equilibrium or empirical claim is made here; the static regime in which the source is read is the adopted idealisation of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (f). Every Cartesian degree $l$ in this definition is a nonnegative integer (the number of Cartesian indices); only the absolute weighted exponent $L$ in (b) may be any nonnegative real number.

## Statement

For the density-integral branch assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) through the Lebesgue interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); the finite-point branch of all identities below is choice-free. Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and vanish $\lambda_3$-a.e. outside $\overline B_a(0)$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), or let $(x_k,q_k)_{k=1}^N$ be a finite system of stationary point charges, with the source moments of [[def-em-electric-moments]] branches (a) and (c) respectively. For $b\in\mathbb R^3$ define the moments **about the reference point $b$** by replacing, in each integrand of [[def-em-electric-moments]] (a) and in each summand of (c), the vector $y$ by $y-b$ (respectively $x_k$ by $x_k-b$):

$$Q^{(b)}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\,d\lambda_3,\qquad p^{(b)}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(y-b)\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$

$$M^{(b)}_{i_1\dots i_l}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\prod_{r=1}^l(y-b)_{i_r}\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\quad(l\ge1),\qquad M^{(b,0)}:=Q^{(b)},$$

$$Q^{(b)}_{ij}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\bigl(3(y-b)_i(y-b)_j-|y-b|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$

and analogously with the finite sums $M^{(b)}_{i_1\dots i_l}=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_k\prod_{r=1}^l(x_k-b)_{i_r}$ $(l\ge1)$ and $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_k\bigl(3(x_k-b)_i(x_k-b)_j-|x_k-b|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)$ in the point-charge branch; for $N=0$ the sums are the empty sum $0$. Every displayed integral is absolutely convergent: since $\rho=0$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. off $\overline B_a(0)$, the estimates $|(y-b)_{i_1}\cdots(y-b)_{i_l}|\le(|y|+|b|)^l\le(a+|b|)^l$ and $|3(y-b)_i(y-b)_j-|y-b|^2\delta_{ij}|\le4(|y|+|b|)^2\le4(a+|b|)^2$ hold $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support, so each integrand is dominated $\lambda_3$-a.e. by a finite constant times $|\rho|\in L^1$ ([[def-em-electric-moments]] (a), [[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then:

(a) $Q^{(b)}=Q$ for every $b$;

(b) $p^{(b)}=p-Qb$, so the dipole moment is independent of the reference point exactly when $Q=0$;

(c) for every $l\ge0$,

$$M^{(b)}_{i_1\dots i_l}=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,l\}}(-1)^{|S|}\Bigl(\prod_{r\in S}b_{i_r}\Bigr)M_{S^{c}},$$

where for a subset $S\subseteq\{1,\dots,l\}$ we write $S^{c}:=\{1,\dots,l\}\setminus S$ and $M_{S^{c}}$ for the Cartesian moment whose index list is $(i_r)_{r\in S^{c}}$ in increasing order of $r$, with the empty index list read as $M_{\emptyset}:=Q$; in particular

$$M^{(b)}_{ij}=M_{ij}-b_ip_j-b_jp_i+b_ib_jQ;$$

(d) $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=Q_{ij}-3\bigl(b_ip_j+b_jp_i\bigr)+2(b\cdot p)\delta_{ij}+\bigl(3b_ib_j-|b|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)Q$; consequently, if $Q=0$ and $p=0$, then $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=Q_{ij}$ for every $b$;

(e) [Scope] this is an exact identity between the declared source moments of [[def-em-electric-moments]]; it asserts nothing about fields, forces, dynamics or nature, and the reference point is a choice of coordinate origin, not an operation performed on the source.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the density branch, let $a>0$, $b\in\mathbb R^3$, and let either a real $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ vanishing $\lambda_3$-a.e. off $\overline B_a(0)$, with source moments as in [[def-em-electric-moments]] (a), or a finite system $(x_k,q_k)_{k=1}^N$ of stationary point charges with source moments as in [[def-em-electric-moments]] (c), be given. All moments are read about the chart origin of the laboratory frame.

[F1] For $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ vanishing $\lambda_3$-a.e. outside $\overline B_a(0)$, the moments $Q=\int\rho$, $p=\int y\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)$, $M_{i_1\dots i_l}=\int y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}\rho\,d\lambda_3$ and $Q_{ij}=\int(3y_iy_j-|y|^2\delta_{ij})\rho\,d\lambda_3$ are absolutely convergent, dominated $\lambda_3$-a.e. by $a^l|\rho|$ and $4a^2|\rho|$ on the support, with $\sum_iQ_{ii}=0$ ([[def-em-electric-moments]]).

[F2] For a finite system of stationary point charges the moments $Q=\sum_kq_k$, $p=\sum_kq_kx_k$, $M_{i_1\dots i_l}=\sum_kq_kx_{k,i_1}\cdots x_{k,i_l}$ and $Q_{ij}=\sum_kq_k(3x_{k,i}x_{k,j}-|x_k|^2\delta_{ij})$ are finite sums with $\sum_iQ_{ii}=0$, defined without Choice, and empty sums are $0$ ([[def-em-electric-moments]]).

[F3] If $f,g\in L^1$ and $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$, then $\int(\alpha f+\beta g)\,d\lambda_3=\alpha\int f\,d\lambda_3+\beta\int g\,d\lambda_3$; this extends to finite linear combinations ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]).

[F4] If $f$ and $g$ agree $\lambda_3$-a.e. then $\int f\,d\lambda_3=\int g\,d\lambda_3$ whenever either side is defined ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]).

[F5] $|\int f\,d\lambda_3|\le\int|f|\,d\lambda_3$, and for measurable $0\le u\le w$ one has $\int u\,d\lambda_3\le\int w\,d\lambda_3$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]).

[F6] Finite sums are distributive, may be reindexed over a bijection of their index set, and the empty sum is $0$ ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]).

[F7] With the Euclidean inner product and norm, $|y-b|\le|y|+|b|$ and $|(y-b)_i|\le|y-b|$ for every $y,b\in\mathbb R^3$; the inner product is bilinear and the components are read in the frame basis ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]]).

[F8] A polynomial identity between the coordinate functions of $\mathbb R^3$ that holds pointwise may be integrated and differentiated with the usual polynomial calculus; the coordinate maps of $\mathbb R^3$ are smooth in the componentwise sense ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

[F9] $\overline B_a(0)=\{y\in\mathbb R^3:|y|\le a\}$ ([[def-metric-ball]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Establish that every integral in the definition of the $b$-moments is absolutely convergent. For $\lambda_3$-a.e. $y$ outside $\overline B_a(0)$ the integrands vanish, and for $y\in\overline B_a(0)$ one has $|y|\le a$ by [F9], so $|(y-b)_{i_1}\cdots(y-b)_{i_l}|\le(|y|+|b|)^l\le(a+|b|)^l$ and $|3(y-b)_i(y-b)_j-|y-b|^2\delta_{ij}|\le3|y-b|^2+|y-b|^2\le4(a+|b|)^2$ by [F7]; hence each integrand is bounded $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support by a finite constant times $|\rho|\in L^1$, and the triangle and monotonicity rules [F5] give absolute convergence. [F1, F5, F7, F9, given]

1.2 Prove the polynomial expansion identity: for every $l\ge0$, all indices $i_1,\dots,i_l\in\{1,2,3\}$ and every $y\in\mathbb R^3$, $\prod_{r=1}^l(y-b)_{i_r}=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,l\}}(-1)^{|S|}\bigl(\prod_{r\in S}b_{i_r}\bigr)\bigl(\prod_{r\in S^{c}}y_{i_r}\bigr)$, where empty products are $1$ and $S^{c}=\{1,\dots,l\}\setminus S$. The case $l=0$ is $1=1$, the unique subset being $S=\emptyset$; for $l\ge1$ write the product as $\bigl(\prod_{r=1}^{l-1}(y-b)_{i_r}\bigr)(y_{i_l}-b_{i_l})$, apply the induction hypothesis to the first factor and distribute: the subsets $S$ of $\{1,\dots,l-1\}$ that avoid $l$ and the subsets to which $l$ is adjoined are in bijection and reindex the same finite sum, giving the displayed identity. [F6, F8, algebra]

2.1 In the density branch, substitute step 1.2 into the definition of $M^{(b)}_{i_1\dots i_l}$ and integrate term by term. Each summand is a real constant $(-1)^{|S|}\prod_{r\in S}b_{i_r}$ times the $L^1$ function $y\mapsto(\prod_{r\in S^{c}}y_{i_r})\rho(y)$, which is dominated $\lambda_3$-a.e. by $|b|^{|S|}a^{l-|S|}|\rho|$ by [F1] and [F7]; finite linearity [F3] and the a.e. support convention [F4] therefore give $M^{(b)}_{i_1\dots i_l}=\sum_{S}(-1)^{|S|}\bigl(\prod_{r\in S}b_{i_r}\bigr)M_{S^{c}}$ with $M_{\emptyset}:=Q$. Specialising to $l=0$ gives $Q^{(b)}=Q$, which is (a). Specialising to $l=1$ gives $p^{(b)}_i=p_i-b_iQ$, which is (b): if $Q=0$ then $p^{(b)}=p$ for every $b$; conversely, if $p^{(b)}=p$ for every $b\in\mathbb R^3$, then $Qb=0$ for every $b$, and taking $b=e_r$ for $r=1,2,3$ shows that all three frame components of $Q$ vanish, so $Q=0$, and the dipole moment is independent of the reference point exactly when $Q=0$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, F3, F4, F7]

3.1 Evaluate the $l=2$ instance of step 2.1: $M^{(b)}_{ij}=M_{ij}-b_ip_j-b_jp_i+b_ib_jQ$. Summing over $i=j$ and using finite linearity [F3] gives $\sum_{k=1}^3M^{(b)}_{kk}=\sum_{k=1}^3M_{kk}-2b\cdot p+|b|^2Q$, where $b\cdot p=\sum_kb_kp_k$ is the Euclidean inner product [F7]. [step 2.1, F3, F7]

4.1 Compute the traceless quadrupole about $b$. By [F1], $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=3M^{(b)}_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\sum_kM^{(b)}_{kk}$ and $Q_{ij}=3M_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\sum_kM_{kk}$, so substituting step 3.1 into the first identity gives $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=Q_{ij}-3(b_ip_j+b_jp_i)+2(b\cdot p)\delta_{ij}+(3b_ib_j-|b|^2\delta_{ij})Q$, which is the displayed identity of (d); every step is a finite algebraic rearrangement [F3]. [step 3.1, F1, F3, algebra]

5.1 Read off the invariant case: if $Q=0$ and $p=0$, then all four $b$-dependent terms of step 4.1 vanish, so $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=Q_{ij}$ for every $b$, which is the final clause of (d). [step 4.1]

6.1 Repeat the argument in the finite point-charge branch and complete the choice accounting. The same expansion identity of step 1.2 is substituted into the finite sums of [F2]; finite distributivity, reindexing and the empty-sum convention [F6] produce the identical identities (a)-(d) with sums in place of integrals, without any convergence hypothesis, and the case $N=0$ makes both sides $0$ at every step. The identities are therefore choice-free in this branch, while the density branch used only the declared Countable Choice of the measure interface. [step 1.2, step 5.1, F2, F6]

7.1 Combine the branches and record the scope. Replacing $\rho$ by an equal $\lambda_3$-a.e. density leaves every $b$-moment unchanged by [F4], so (a)-(d) hold as stated for the declared representatives; the density branch is established in steps 2.1, 4.1 and 5.1, the finite-point branch in step 6.1, and the identities are those of the source moments of [[def-em-electric-moments]] about the chart origin, the reference point $b$ being a choice of coordinate origin only; no field, force or dynamical content is asserted, which is clause (e). [step 6.1, F4] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the Lebesgue interface ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and vanish $\lambda_3$-a.e. outside $\overline B_a(0)$; let $E_{\mathrm{ext}}:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be a prescribed external vector-field datum, with electric-field units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], that is continuous on $\overline B_a(0)$ and Lipschitz there with constant $L\ge0$, i.e. $|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(x)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(x')|\le L|x-x'|$ for all $x,x'\in\overline B_a(0)$. Consider the matter model in which the prescribed static distribution $\rho$ is carried by a body at rest in the laboratory frame and adopt additionally the prescribed external force model $f_{\mathrm{ext}}=\rho E_{\mathrm{ext}}$. This is a declared extension to these locally integrable charge data and Lipschitz fields, motivated by the smooth continuum coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] (ii); that postulate covers smooth sources and does not itself establish this extension. The only force counted by the present model is $f_{\mathrm{ext}}$; the self-field of $\rho$, all other fields, mechanical support and back-reaction are excluded by this model. Define the **total external force** and the **total external torque about the origin** by the componentwise Lebesgue integrals

$$F:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y)\,E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\in\mathbb R^3,\qquad \tau:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y)\,\bigl(y\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)\bigr)\,d\lambda_3(y)\in\mathbb R^3,$$

absolutely convergent because on the support $|E_{\mathrm{ext}}|\le|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|+La$ and $|y\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}|\le a(|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|+La)$, so each component is dominated by a constant times $|\rho|\in L^1$ ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[thm-cross-product-norm-is-the-two-vector-gram-determinant]], [[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Then:

(a) [Uniform force and torque expansions]

$$F=Q\,E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+R_F,\qquad |R_F|\le L\,a\,\|\rho\|_1,\qquad \tau=p\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+R_\tau,\qquad |R_\tau|\le L\,a^2\|\rho\|_1,$$

where $Q$ and $p$ are the total charge and dipole moment of [[def-em-electric-moments]] (a) and $\|\rho\|_1=\int|\rho|\,d\lambda_3$;

(b) [Neutral distribution] if $Q=0$ then the leading force term vanishes, $F=R_F$ with $|R_F|\le La\|\rho\|_1$, and the torque is the ideal-dipole torque $p\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$ up to the bound $|R_\tau|\le La^2\|\rho\|_1$; in this sense a neutral distribution of size $a$ in a field with Lipschitz constant $L$ carries the dipole torque $p\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$ with an explicit remainder;

(c) [Reference-point shift] for any reference point $o\in\mathbb R^3$, the torque about $o$, $\tau_o:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y)\,(y-o)\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)$, equals $\tau-o\times F$ exactly;

(d) [Ideal pair of test charges at rest] let $q\in\mathbb R$ and $d\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, put $a=|d|/2$, and consider the two stationary point charges $+q$ at $d/2$ and $-q$ at $-d/2$ ([[def-em-electric-moments]] (c)), each treated as a test charge at rest in the laboratory chart in the same prescribed external field $E_{\mathrm{ext}}$, with the mutual interaction and the self-field of each charge excluded by the model. Adopt for this finite prescribed-charge branch the external force assignment $F_k=q_kE_{\rm ext}(x_k)$ and torque $x_k\times F_k$. It is defined for merely continuous external field values at the two points, independently of a worldline equation. For the same Lipschitz bound as above, finite summation gives the expansions of (a),(b), with $Q=0$, $p=qd$, and total variation $2|q|$: $|R_F|\le2|q|La$, $|R_\tau|\le2|q|La^2$. More generally the exact finite force/torque sum requires only the specified field values; no Lipschitz estimate is asserted without its hypothesis.

(d1) [Covariant sufficient specialization] If, in addition, an actual prescribed electromagnetic tensor $F$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of each massive future-timelike $C^2$ test worldline with constant charge $q'$ and supplied rest mass $m>0$, and the external-field coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] (i) applies, then at an instant with zero coordinate velocity $U=(c,0,0,0)$ its spatial force is $q'E_{\rm ext}$, because $U_0=-c$ and $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$. This reproduces the prescribed point-force assignment at that instant. Similarly the smooth-source $J=0$ matter-coupling branch of postulate (ii) reproduces the continuum force assignment when its own source/field/matter hypotheses hold. No $C^1$ tensor or worldline is inferred from merely continuous $E$ data, and no two-charge trajectory existence or permanent rest is claimed.

(e) [Scope] the statement is conditional on the explicitly stated matter model: only the prescribed external field acts on the distribution, the distribution is prescribed and at rest, and no self-force, back-reaction, mechanical equilibrium, stability or dynamics of the body is asserted; the external field is a datum, not solved for. Clause (d) is an instantaneous idealisation of two ideal point test charges with mutual interaction excluded; it is not a two-body dynamics, a bound-state or a stability statement. No radiation, medium response or empirical claim is made. The prescribed finite force assignment and finite moment algebra in (d) are choice-free; the volume integrals in (a)-(c) carry their explicit measure premise, while (d1) is a separate conditional instantiation of the exact physical coupling.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; let $a>0$, let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and vanish $\lambda_3$-a.e. outside $\overline B_a(0)$, let $E_{\mathrm{ext}}:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous on $\overline B_a(0)$ and Lipschitz there with constant $L\ge0$, and adopt the prescribed external force model $f_{\mathrm{ext}}=\rho E_{\mathrm{ext}}$ on the prescribed distribution at rest in the laboratory frame.

[F1] For $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ vanishing $\lambda_3$-a.e. outside $\overline B_a(0)$, the total charge $Q=\int\rho\,d\lambda_3$ and the dipole moment $p=\int y\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)$ about the chart origin are absolutely convergent, and in the finite system of stationary point charges $(x_k,q_k)_{k=1}^N$ one has $Q=\sum_kq_k$ and $p=\sum_kq_kx_k$ as finite sums ([[def-em-electric-moments]]).

[F2] The electric field carries V m$^{-1}$, a force carries the newton, and $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}>0$; the laboratory structure is that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] ([[def-em-si-conventions]]).

[F3] An electric field of class $C^k$ is a map $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$, and at fixed $t$ the map $E(\cdot,t):\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ is a real spatial vector field read in the frame basis; no value at a point of singular source support is asserted ([[def-em-fields]]).

[F4] The postulate's external-field coupling (i) is $m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$ with $\Phi$ the raised-index operator $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$ of the field, equivalently $m\,dU^\mu/d\tau=qF^{\mu\nu}U_\nu$, for a constant charge, a supplied rest mass $m>0$ and a future timelike $C^2$ worldline, with the particle's own field excluded; clause (ii) adopts the continuum force density $\rho E+J\times B$ for a smooth source interacting through a matter model to which the coupling applies ([[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]).

[F5] In the chart the electromagnetic two-form has $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ for the field pair $(E,B)$ ([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]).

[F6] A massive worldline is a $C^k$ future timelike curve, $k\ge1$, with everywhere nonzero future timelike tangent; its four-velocity satisfies $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$; and a massive $C^2$ worldline with laboratory reading $t\mapsto r(t)$ satisfies $|r'(t)|<c$ with four-velocity $U=\gamma(c,r')$ and Lorentz factor $\gamma=(1-|r'|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, so that at a parameter with $r'=0$ one has $\gamma=1$ and $U=(c,0,0,0)$ ([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]).

[F7] On $\mathbb R^3$ the cross product is bilinear and alternating, and $|w\times z|^2=|w|^2|z|^2-\langle w,z\rangle^2$, so $|w\times z|\le|w|\,|z|$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[thm-cross-product-norm-is-the-two-vector-gram-determinant]]).

[F8] For the Euclidean inner product, $|\langle u,w\rangle|\le|u|\,|w|$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]).

[F9] If $f,g\in L^1$ and $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$, then $\int(\alpha f+\beta g)=\alpha\int f+\beta\int g$; if $f$ and $g$ agree a.e. their integrals agree; and $|\int f|\le\int|f|$ with monotonicity for nonnegative integrands ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]], [[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]], [[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]).

[F10] Finite sums are distributive and may be reindexed, and the empty sum is $0$ ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]).

[F11] $\overline B_a(0)=\{y:|y|\le a\}$ and $|y|\le a$ holds $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support of $\rho$; the Euclidean norm obeys the reverse triangle inequality $|\,|u|-|w|\,|\le|u-w|$ ([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Establish that $F$ and $\tau$ are well defined. For $\lambda_3$-a.e. $y$ either $\rho(y)=0$ or $y\in\overline B_a(0)$, and then $|y|\le a$ by [F11]; the Lipschitz property gives $|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)|\le|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|+L|y|\le|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|+La$ and hence $|y\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)|\le|y|\,|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)|\le a(|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|+La)$ by [F7] and [F8]. Each component of the integrands is therefore dominated $\lambda_3$-a.e. by a finite constant times $|\rho|\in L^1$, so the componentwise integrals converge absolutely by the triangle and monotonicity rules, and no value of $E_{\mathrm{ext}}$ on a null set matters [F9]. [F7, F8, F9, F11, given]

2.1 Expand the force and bound its remainder. Write $E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)=E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)$ and integrate: by finite linearity of the componentwise integral [F9], $F=\bigl(\int\rho\,d\lambda_3\bigr)E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+\int\rho(y)\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)d\lambda_3(y)=QE_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+R_F$ with $Q$ as in [F1]. If $R_F\ne0$, test against the unit vector $u:=R_F/|R_F|$: $|R_F|=u\cdot R_F=\int\rho(y)\,u\cdot\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)d\lambda_3(y)\le\int|\rho(y)|\,|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le L\int|y|\,|\rho(y)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le La\|\rho\|_1$, using [F8] for $u\cdot v\le|v|$, the Lipschitz hypothesis, the monotonicity rule, and $|y|\le a$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support [F11]; the case $R_F=0$ is trivial. This is the force statement of (a). [step 1.1, F1, F8, F9, F11]

3.1 Expand the torque and bound its remainder. Since $y\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)=y\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+y\times\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)$, finite linearity of the componentwise integral and the bilinearity of the cross product [F7] give $\int\rho(y)\,y\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\,d\lambda_3(y)=\bigl(\int y\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\bigr)\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)=p\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$ with $p$ as in [F1], so $\tau=p\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+R_\tau$ with $R_\tau:=\int\rho(y)\,y\times\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)d\lambda_3(y)$. For the bound, $|R_\tau|\le\int|\rho(y)|\,|y|\,|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le L\int|y|^2|\rho|\,d\lambda_3\le La^2\|\rho\|_1$ by [F7], [F9] and [F11]. This is the torque statement of (a). [step 2.1, F1, F7, F9, F11]

4.1 Specialise to the neutral case (b): if $Q=0$, the leading force term $QE_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$ vanishes and step 2.1 leaves $F=R_F$ with $|R_F|\le La\|\rho\|_1$, while step 3.1 gives the torque as the ideal-dipole torque plus the stated bound. [step 3.1]

5.1 Prove the reference-point shift (c). For any $o\in\mathbb R^3$, $(y-o)\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)=y\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-o\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)$ by bilinearity [F7]; integrating, $o$ is a constant vector and $\int\rho(y)E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)=F$, so finite linearity [F9] gives $\tau_o=\tau-o\times F$ exactly. [step 4.1, F7, F9]

6.1 Treat the ideal pair of test charges (d). Under the explicitly adopted finite force assignment $F_k=q_kE_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_k)$, the total force is $F=qE_{\mathrm{ext}}(d/2)-qE_{\mathrm{ext}}(-d/2)=q\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(d/2)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(-d/2)\bigr)$, and inserting $\pm E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$ gives $F=R_F$ with $R_F=q\bigl[(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(d/2)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0))-(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(-d/2)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0))\bigr]$ and $|R_F|\le|q|(L|d/2|+L|d/2|)=2|q|La$; the total torque is $\tau=(d/2)\times qE_{\mathrm{ext}}(d/2)+(-d/2)\times(-q)E_{\mathrm{ext}}(-d/2)=q(d/2)\times\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(d/2)+E_{\mathrm{ext}}(-d/2)\bigr)=q\,d\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+R_\tau$ with $R_\tau=q(d/2)\times\bigl[(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(d/2)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0))+(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(-d/2)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0))\bigr]$ and $|R_\tau|\le|q|a\cdot2La=2|q|La^2$, using [F7], the Lipschitz hypothesis and [F10]; the finite-branch moments are $Q=0$ and $p=qd$ by [F1], and no convergence or Lipschitz hypothesis is needed for the bare finite sums themselves. All these sums are finite and choice-free. [step 5.1, F1, F7, F10]

7.1 Instantiate the exact coupling at an instant of rest, proving (d1). Under the additional hypotheses of (d1) the postulate gives $m\,dU^i/d\tau=q'\Phi(U)^i=q'F^{i\nu}U_\nu$ [F4]; at an instant with $r'=0$ the chart reading of the four-velocity is $U=(c,0,0,0)$ by [F6], so the spatial components $U_j$ vanish, $U_0=\eta_{00}U^0=-c$, and only the term $q'F^{i0}U_0$ survives; with $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ from [F5] this equals $q'(-E_i/c)(-c)=q'E_i$. Hence the covariant equation reproduces the prescribed assignment $F_k=q_kE_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_k)$ at that instant and nothing more: no $C^1$ tensor or massive worldline is inferred from the continuous datum $E_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and no trajectory or permanent-rest claim is made. In the same way the smooth source branch of the postulate reproduces the continuum density $\rho E$ only when its own stated smoothness and matter hypotheses hold [F4]. [step 6.1, F4, F5, F6]

8.1 Record the scope (e) and close the argument. The prescribed data carry the field units and laboratory conventions of [F2], and the derived member $E=-\nabla\varphi$ would be the fixed-time spatial field object of [F3]; only the prescribed external field acts in the model, the self-field, other fields, mechanical support and back-reaction are excluded by hypothesis, the external field is a datum rather than a solution of any field equation, and clauses (a)-(c) concern the declared source moments of a prescribed distribution without asserting force dynamics, equilibrium or stability; clause (d) is an instantaneous idealisation with mutual interaction and self-fields excluded, and clause (d1) is a conditional instantiation of the exact coupling, so no empirical, radiative or medium-response content is introduced. The volume integrals used the declared Countable Choice through the Lebesgue interface, while the finite-point algebra of (d) is choice-free. [step 7.1, F2, F3, given]

9.1 Combine the clauses: step 2.1 and step 3.1 give (a) with the stated bounds, step 4.1 gives (b), step 5.1 gives the exact reference-point shift (c), step 6.1 gives the finite two-charge expansions and their choice-free status (d), and step 7.1 gives the conditional covariant specialization (d1), all under the model assumptions of the statement and with the exclusions of step 8.1, which is (e). [step 8.1] ∎
