## Definition

For the Lebesgue/surface/distributional source and admissibility branches (c)-(d), assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). The smooth formulation in (a) and the smooth conserved-current predicate in (b) do not themselves use Choice. Let the laboratory region and its chart, the field and source objects and the units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-sources]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and fix $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

**(a) [Steady-current regime].** A steady-current (magnetostatic) configuration on $\Omega\times I$ consists of a field pair $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ and source fields $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that are independent of $t$ and satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with the operators of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. For such a configuration the formal distributional branch of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives $\operatorname{div}J=0$ distributionally; this is pointwise when $J$ is $C^1$. In the jointly $C^2$ field/$C^1$ source branch its classical proof applies directly. The locally integrable distributional reading here inherits Countable Choice, whereas the stated classical $C^2/C^1$ compatibility calculation is choice-free, and the four adopted equations are equivalent to the electrostatic pair and the magnetostatic pair
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J .$$

**(b) [Compact smooth current class].** The compact smooth current class of this framework consists of the currents $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$. A magnetostatic field of such a current is a field $B$ of class $C^1$ on $\mathbb R^3$ satisfying $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ on $\mathbb R^3$ with the extended $J$. This is the hypothesis class of the vector-potential, Biot-Savart and dipole theorems of this page; this definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of $B$ in the class.

**(c) [Ideal source objects].** Define three ideal current source objects outside the compact class, together with the data selecting their fields.

**(c1) [Closed thin loop].** For a closed embedded $C^2$ curve $\gamma:\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R^3$ with $|\gamma'|\equiv1$ ($L>0$) and $I\in\mathbb R$, the ideal loop current is the distribution
$$\langle J_\gamma,\psi\rangle:=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\cdot\psi(\gamma(s))\,ds,\qquad \psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3),$$
with $\rho_\gamma:=0$.

**(c2) [Infinite straight wire].** For $\gamma(s)=(0,0,s)$, $s\in\mathbb R$, and $I\in\mathbb R$, the ideal wire current is
$$\langle J_{\rm w},\psi\rangle:=I\int_{\mathbb R}\psi_3(0,0,s)\,ds,$$
with $\rho_{\rm w}:=0$.

**(c3) [Infinite cylindrical sheet].** For $a>0$, $S=\{\rho=a\}$, $\rho=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}$, and $K\in\mathbb R$, the ideal solenoid sheet current is
$$\langle J_S,\psi\rangle:=K\int_S e_\varphi\cdot\psi\,dS$$
([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], read on compact cylinder segments), with $\rho_S:=0$. All three pairings are finite because $\psi$ has compact support.

**(c4) [Admissibility].** A field $B$ is admitted for one of these declared models when: $B$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ (hence a distribution by [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and $C^1$ off the support of the current; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ hold pointwise off that support; the distributional identities $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ hold against every scalar divergence test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and vector curl test $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ in the sense of [[def-distributional-derivative]]; $B$ has the model's declared symmetry (invariance under translations along and rotations about the axis in (c2) and (c3); no symmetry is required in (c1)); and $B$ obeys the decay requirement: $|B(x)|\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$ in (c1), and in (c2), (c3) the supremum of $|B|$ over every compact set of cross-sectional parameters tends to $0$ as the transverse radius $\rho\to\infty$. The companion examples exhibit and verify the fields of the two axisymmetric models in this class; the definition itself asserts no existence, uniqueness, finite energy or limiting relation for the declared models, and no compact-class theorem of this page applies to them.

**(d) [Scope].** This is a model restriction: the steady-current regime for compact smooth currents, and three explicitly declared ideal noncompact or singular models. It excludes point charges, weaker-regularity volume sources, moving sheets, normal sheet currents and any claim of empirical exactness; the equations in (c4) define a mathematical admissibility predicate; its physical adoption for these source objects is a separate postulate, and no product of distributions is formed.

## Remarks

**Well-definedness of the clauses.** In (c1)-(c3) the pairings are order-zero continuous linear functionals on the test spaces of [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]: on a fixed compact test support their absolute values are bounded by $|I|L\|\psi\|_\infty$, by $|I|$ times the finite length of the axis projection times $\|\psi\|_\infty$, and by $|K|$ times the finite area of a containing compact cylindrical face times $\|\psi\|_\infty$, respectively. The cylinder chart $X(\theta,z)=(a\cos\theta,a\sin\theta,z)$ has Gram density $a$, and finitely many angular charts cover each compact face, so the surface pairing is the chart-defined integral of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]; the scalar triple product and the direction $e_\varphi$ are those of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. The divergence pairing uses scalar tests and the curl pairing vector tests under [[def-distributional-derivative]], a vector distribution being a triple of scalar distributions in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$ of [[def-distribution]]; a locally integrable field is a distribution in the sense of the regular-distribution embedding [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]. Smoothness statements use [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. The finite area of a compact angular face is the Riemann integral of the constant function one over its rectangular chart domain, with the properties of [[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]. The declared ideal objects lie outside the source classes of [[def-em-weak-sources]]: that definition excludes line and noncompact sheet currents, so no equation for these singular objects is inherited from it, and Countable Choice is inherited only through the compact-face surface and regular-distribution interfaces.

## Source notes

Griffiths, Section 5.2.1, printed pp. 215-216, and the opening of Tong, Chapter 3, printed pp. 41-42, describe steady currents and the reduction to $\nabla\cdot J=0$ and the static field equations; Griffiths, Section 5.1.3, printed pp. 208-214, supplies the line, surface and volume current-density conventions reproduced in (c). Landau-Lifshitz, Section 43, printed pp. 101-103, and Chew, Lecture 4 Section 4.1, printed pp. 39-41, give the constant-field equations and the vector-potential formulation in the same regime. The ideal noncompact models are declared modelling hypotheses of this framework, not measurements or exact descriptions of any apparatus.

## Postulate

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. In the named inertial laboratory model of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the positive constants and SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]], adopt the following additional classical physical idealization: a loop, infinite straight line or infinite cylindrical sheet source defined by [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1)-(c3), with zero charge density, is modeled by a time-independent $B$ satisfying exactly the admissibility predicate (c4), together with $E=0$ and $\rho=0$. Thus $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ hold distributionally on $\mathbb R^3$, with the stated off-source regularity, symmetry and decay; the electrostatic and temporal Maxwell identities are zero. This physical adoption extends to these explicitly declared source types only. It is separate from the earlier $L^1$-source and point/compact-sheet postulates, which do not include these line and noncompact sheet sources. No existence, uniqueness, finite self-energy, force product, self-force, apparatus accuracy, matter dynamics or empirical certainty is asserted.

## Status and scope

This is an adopted physical assumption, not a theorem: it states which ideal models this framework elects to use, and it is not deduced from the vacuum equations or from any experiment. The mathematical content it refers to — the exact source functionals of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1)-(c3) and the admissibility predicate (c4) — is fixed by that definition; the postulate adds the physical decision to treat those declared objects as sources of fields in the named laboratory. Existence and distributional consistency of the fields for the line and sheet models are established separately by the mathematical lemmas of this page, and the physical reading of the compact thin-loop limit remains a declared idealization rather than a measured property of any coil. The assumption carries no empirical uncertainty record because it reports no measurement; any later empirical comparison must state its own preparation, apparatus and sampling assumptions, and agreement would support the model under those conditions rather than establish it.

## Source notes

Tong, Chapter 3, printed pp. 41-46 and 51, adopts neutral steady currents, the infinite wire, the infinite cylindrical solenoid and the thin-wire model as idealizations of a long straight conductor and a tightly wound solenoid. Those bounded passages are the source context for the adopted models. The exact source functionals, the admissibility predicate and the field objects are this framework's own precise formulation, not claims reproduced verbatim from the source; no source is claimed to prove the idealization exact for any apparatus.

## Definition

Let the compact smooth current class and the declared ideal models be those of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

**(a) [Compact smooth currents].** Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$. The **magnetic dipole moment** of $J$ is the vector
$$m:=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}y\times J(y)\,dy\in\mathbb R^3,$$
of unit A m$^2$. The integral is computed componentwise over any nondegenerate closed bounding rectangle $Q$ containing $\operatorname{supp}J$, using the continuous functions $y\mapsto(y\times J(y))_i$ on $Q$ and their zero extension outside $Q$. Its value is independent of the chosen larger bounding rectangle by finite rectangular subdivision and vanishing of the integrand off its support; the support itself need not be Jordan measurable. Thus this is a Riemann integral of continuous compactly supported functions ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); it is absolutely finite because $J$ is bounded with compact support.

**(b) [Declared ideal thin loop].** For a closed embedded $C^2$ curve $\gamma:\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R^3$ with $|\gamma'|\equiv1$ and $I\in\mathbb R$, the **magnetic moment** of the ideal loop current of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1) is
$$m:=\frac I2\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\gamma'(s)\,ds,$$
again a componentwise Riemann integral over the compact interval $[0,L]$ of continuous functions; for the circle $\gamma(s)=a(\cos(s/a),\sin(s/a),0)$ traversed in the positive orientation this is $m=I\pi a^2e_3$.

**(c) [Status and scope].** In both clauses $m$ is a source moment of the declared current model: it is not a rest mass, not an intrinsic spin and not an observed quantity. The definition asserts no far-field property of $m$ (that is the content of [[pthm-em-magnetic-dipole-field]] under its hypotheses), no agreement between the two clauses in a common limit, and no moment for currents outside the two classes; no higher multipole is defined here. The finite Riemann moment definitions and circular-loop evaluation themselves are choice-free; no distribution-embedding or surface-measure theorem is used to compute these moments.

## Remarks

**Well-definedness and units.** In (a), $y\mapsto y\times J(y)$ is continuous on the compact rectangle $Q$ and vanishes off $\operatorname{supp}J$, so each component is Riemann integrable on $Q$ by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]] and bounded there, hence the integral of [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]] is finite. Two bounding rectangles are compared through a common larger rectangle subdivided at their face coordinates: every added cell lies outside $\operatorname{supp}J$, where the integrand vanishes, so finite additivity of the integral ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]) identifies both values without integrating over the support itself. The cross product is that of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. Since $y$ carries the metre and $J$ the ampere per square metre, the product $y\times J$ carries A m$^{-1}$ and the volume integral A m$^2$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). In (b), $\gamma$ and $\gamma'$ are continuous on the compact circle and periodic, so each component of $\gamma\times\gamma'$ is a continuous periodic function on $[0,L]$ and the componentwise Riemann integral exists; $|\gamma'|\equiv1$ makes the parametrization unit-speed so that the value is independent of the chosen unit-speed parameter. The circular evaluation is the componentwise computation $\gamma\times\gamma'=ae_3$ and $\int_0^{2\pi a}ae_3\,ds=2\pi a^2e_3$. No measurement, apparatus or uncertainty enters either clause.

## Source notes

Griffiths, Section 5.4.3, printed pp. 242-246, introduces $m=(I/2)\int d\mathbf l'\times\mathbf r'$ for line currents and $m=\frac12\int(\mathbf r\times\mathbf J)\,d\tau$ for volume currents (eqs. (5.84) and (5.91)); Tong, Sections 3.3.1-3.3.2, printed pp. 54-57, gives $m=\frac12\int d^3r'\,r'\times J(r')$ (eq. (3.24)); Landau-Lifshitz, Section 44, printed pp. 103-105, gives the corresponding charged-particle moment in Gaussian units, re-expressed here in SI. The definition keeps the moment a declared source quantity of the two explicit models and defers every far-field interpretation to the dipole theorem.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$ be a compact smooth current of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](b), extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$, and let $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ be the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Define, for $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$,
$$A_i(x):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J_i(y)}{|x-y|}\,dy=\mu_0\,N(J_i)(x),\qquad A:=(A_1,A_2,A_3),$$
the componentwise Newtonian potentials of [[lem-em-smooth-newtonian-upgrade]]. Then:

(a) $A\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $-\Delta A=\mu_0J$ pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$, componentwise ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]);

(b) $\operatorname{div}A=0$ pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$: the Coulomb-gauge condition holds;

(c) the field $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$ is of class $C^\infty$ and satisfies the magnetostatic pair of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](a) pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$,
$$\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J ;$$
consequently $E=0$, $\rho=0$, with $B,J$ independent of time, gives an explicit full smooth-Maxwell completion on $\mathbb R^3\times I$ for every open time interval $I$ under [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. More generally any compatible steady electrostatic pair satisfying $\operatorname{curl}E=0$ and $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ can be combined with $B,J$; no electrostatic existence theorem is implied;

(d) [Scope] $A$ is a vector potential for $B$ in the Coulomb gauge; the gauge condition is a construction choice and no uniqueness of $A$ or of $B$ is asserted. The construction is carried out for the compact smooth class only: nothing is claimed for the declared ideal models of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c), for noncompact currents or for currents of weaker regularity.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$; let $\mu_0,c,\varepsilon_0$ be as in [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $A$ be as in the Statement.

[F1] For $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ the Newtonian potential satisfies $Nh\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, $-\Delta Nh=h$ pointwise, and $D^\alpha Nh=N(D^\alpha h)$ for every multi-index $\alpha$ ([[lem-em-smooth-newtonian-upgrade]]).

[F2] The Laplacian is $\Delta F=(\Delta F_1,\Delta F_2,\Delta F_3)$ componentwise, and $\Delta f=\operatorname{div}\nabla f=\sum_i\partial_i\partial_if$ for $C^2$ scalars ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]); divergence and curl are the coordinate expressions $\operatorname{div}G=\sum_i\partial_iG_i$ and $\operatorname{curl}G=(\partial_2G_3-\partial_3G_2,\ \partial_3G_1-\partial_1G_3,\ \partial_1G_2-\partial_2G_1)$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), with partial derivatives as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

[F3] For a $C^2$ field $G$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$, $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}G)=0$ ([[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]]).

[F4] For a $C^2$ field $G$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$, $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}G=\nabla\operatorname{div}G-\Delta G$ ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]]).

[F5] The compact smooth current class is the class of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](b): $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$, extended by zero; the magnetostatic pair $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ is the time-independent reduction of clause (a) there, and the adopted smooth equations with these constants are [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]](a).

[F6] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the countable-choice principle assumed here and inherited by the Newtonian-potential supplier ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; componentwise reduction to the smooth Newtonian upgrade and the standard second-derivative vector identities.

1.1 For each $i$ the datum $J_i$ is smooth and compactly supported, so [F1] gives $A_i=\mu_0N(J_i)\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, the derivative identity $D^\alpha A_i=\mu_0N(D^\alpha J_i)$ for every multi-index $\alpha$, and $-\Delta A_i=\mu_0J_i$ pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$; since all components are smooth, $A\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ by [F2], and $-\Delta A=\mu_0J$ holds pointwise componentwise. This is (a). [given, F1, F2]

2.1 Taking $\alpha=e_i$ in the derivative identity of step 1.1 and summing, $\operatorname{div}A=\sum_i\partial_iA_i=\mu_0\sum_iN(\partial_iJ_i)$; $N$ is componentwise linear by finite additivity of the integral over the compactly supported data, so this equals $\mu_0N(\sum_i\partial_iJ_i)=\mu_0N(\operatorname{div}J)$ pointwise, and $\operatorname{div}J=0$ gives $\operatorname{div}A=0$ on $\mathbb R^3$. This is (b), and the hypothesis $\operatorname{div}J=0$ is used in no other step. [step 1.1, F2, F5]

3.1 Since $A$ is $C^\infty$, the field $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$ is $C^\infty$ by [F2]. Then $\operatorname{div}B=\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}A=0$ by [F3], and $\operatorname{curl}B=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A=\nabla(\operatorname{div}A)-\Delta A$ by [F4]; substituting step 2.1 and step 1.1 gives $\operatorname{curl}B=0-(-\mu_0J)=\mu_0J$. Hence the magnetostatic pair of [F5] holds pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F2, F3, F4, F5]

4.1 Read step 3.1 inside the framework: [F5] identifies the pair $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ with the time-independent reduction of the adopted equations, and the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]](a) then holds for the fields $E:=0$, $\rho:=0$ on $\Omega\times I$ and the time-independent $B,J$ restricted to $\Omega\times I$: indeed $\operatorname{div}E=0=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$ and $\partial_tB=0$ give $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, and $\partial_tE=0$ with $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ gives $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. More generally a compatible steady electrostatic pair satisfying $\operatorname{curl}E=0$ and $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ may be combined with $B,J$; no existence theorem for such a pair is asserted here. [step 3.1, F5]

5.1 Clauses (a)-(d) are steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1 together with the scope statement: $A$ is a vector potential for $B$ in the Coulomb gauge, the gauge condition $\operatorname{div}A=0$ is a construction choice, and no uniqueness of $A$, no uniqueness of $B$ and no statement for the ideal noncompact models of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c) is claimed. Countable Choice is used only through the Newtonian-potential supplier [F1] and the measure interfaces it inherits [F6]; no stronger choice principle occurs, and the vector identities of [F3], [F4] are choice-free. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F5, F6] ∎

## Source notes

Griffiths, Section 5.4.1, printed pp. 234-240, derives the Poisson equation $\nabla^2A=-\mu_0J$ in the Coulomb gauge and gives the integral solution (5.63); Tong, Sections 3.2-3.2.3, printed pp. 46-52, and Chew, Lecture 4 Section 4.1, printed pp. 39-41, give the same componentwise construction; Landau-Lifshitz, Section 43, printed pp. 101-103, gives the corresponding constant-field formulation in Gaussian units, re-expressed here in SI. The proof above is the exact componentwise version: smoothness and the Poisson identity come from the smooth Newtonian upgrade, and the divergence-free hypothesis enters only through step 2.1.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$ be a compact smooth current of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](b), extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$, let $A$ be the vector potential of [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ its magnetostatic field, with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Then for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ the absolutely convergent Biot-Savart integral represents the field,
$$B(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J(y)\times(x-y)}{|x-y|^3}\,dy .$$
Moreover the same formula holds in the declared thin-loop limit: if $\gamma:\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R^3$ is a closed embedded $C^2$ curve parametrized by arc length ($|\gamma'|\equiv1$), $I\in\mathbb R$, and $j_\varepsilon=j*\eta_\varepsilon$ are the mollified divergence-free compact currents of [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]] associated with the tangent line current of $\gamma$, then their fields (given by the displayed formula with $J:=j_\varepsilon$) converge, with every derivative uniformly on every compact $K$ disjoint from $\gamma$, to
$$B_\gamma(x)=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi}\int_0^L\frac{\gamma'(s)\times(x-\gamma(s))}{|x-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds,$$
a locally integrable global distributional field with $\operatorname{div}B_\gamma=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B_\gamma=\mu_0J_\gamma$, smoothness off the curve and decay at spatial infinity, hence the admitted field of the declared ideal thin loop under [[post-em-ideal-magnetostatic-models]]. Its almost-everywhere representative on $\mathbb R^3$ is supplied by [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]], independently of the away-from-curve convergence. Nothing is asserted on the wire, about line self-energy, about the infinite-wire or sheet models, or for currents outside the compact smooth class and its declared thin-loop limit.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$; let $A$, $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ be as in [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

[F1] The vector potential satisfies $A_i=\mu_0N(J_i)$ componentwise and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ is $C^\infty$ with $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]], clauses (a)-(c)).

[F2] For $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ the curl of the Newtonian potential is $\operatorname{curl}N(f)(x)=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{f(y)\times(x-y)}{|x-y|^3}\,dy$ at every $x\in\mathbb R^3$, the integral being absolutely convergent, and the estimate $|f(y)\times(x-y)|\le\|f\|_\infty|x-y|$ with $\int_{B_R(x)}|x-y|^{-2}d\lambda_3<+\infty$ underlies it ([[lem-em-newtonian-kernel-curl-identity]]).

[F3] For a closed embedded $C^2$ arc-length curve $\gamma$ and $I\in\mathbb R$, the tangent line current $j$ has $\operatorname{div}j=0$ distributionally; for any family of nonnegative smooth radial unit-mass kernels supported in $B_\varepsilon(0)$ the mollified fields $j_\varepsilon=j*\eta_\varepsilon$ are smooth, compactly supported and divergence-free; their Biot-Savart fields converge with every derivative uniformly on every compact $K$ disjoint from $\gamma$ to $B_\gamma(x)=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi}\int_0^L\frac{\gamma'(s)\times(x-\gamma(s))}{|x-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds$; and the same field has a locally integrable representative on $\mathbb R^3$, is smooth off $\gamma$, satisfies $\operatorname{div}T_{B_\gamma}=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}T_{B_\gamma}=\mu_0j$ globally, and decays with $|B_\gamma(x)|\le\frac{\mu_0|I|L}{4\pi(|x|-a)^2}$ for $|x|>a$ when $\gamma\subset B_a(0)$ ([[lem-em-thin-current-limit]]).

[F4] The compact smooth current class is [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](b); the ideal closed thin loop is [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1); and a field is admitted for it exactly when the predicate (c4) holds, which includes local integrability, $C^1$ regularity and vanishing divergence and curl off the source, the two global distributional identities, the model symmetry and the decay requirement ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]]).

[F5] The physical reading of the declared ideal models is the separate adoption [[post-em-ideal-magnetostatic-models]]; it asserts no existence, uniqueness, finite self-energy, force, self-force or apparatus accuracy, and it is an adopted assumption rather than a deduction.

[F6] The cross product is that of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], volume integrals are over measurable sets in the sense of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], and the modulus of an integral is bounded by the integral of the modulus ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]]).

[F7] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the countable-choice principle assumed here and inherited by the cited measure, regular-distribution and Newtonian interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; the differentiated-kernel identity for the compact class, then the declared thin-current limit with its supplier-supplied global properties.

1.1 By [F1], $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ with $A_i=\mu_0N(J_i)$. Applying [F2] to $f:=J$ and multiplying by $\mu_0$ gives, at every $x\in\mathbb R^3$, $B(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J(y)\times(x-y)}{|x-y|^3}\,dy$, with the integral absolutely convergent by the estimate $|J(y)\times(x-y)|\le\|J\|_\infty|x-y|$ and $\int_{B_R(x)}|x-y|^{-2}d\lambda_3<+\infty$ for a ball containing $\operatorname{supp}J$; this proves the first assertion at every point, including points of the support of $J$. [given, F1, F2, F6]

2.1 By [F3], the tangent line current $j$ of the declared loop is divergence-free, its mollified currents $j_\varepsilon$ are smooth, compactly supported and divergence-free, so each $j_\varepsilon$ is a compact smooth conserved current of the class [F4](b); step 1.1 applied with $J:=j_\varepsilon$ identifies the field of $j_\varepsilon$ with its displayed Biot-Savart integral. The supplier's every-derivative uniform convergence on every compact $K$ disjoint from $\gamma$ therefore identifies the limit field with $B_\gamma(x)=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi}\int_0^L\frac{\gamma'(s)\times(x-\gamma(s))}{|x-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds$ on the complement of $\gamma$. [step 1.1, F3, F4]

3.1 The same supplier [F3] supplies, independently of the away-from-curve convergence, the globally locally integrable representative of $B_\gamma$ on $\mathbb R^3$, its smoothness off $\gamma$, the global distributional identities $\operatorname{div}T_{B_\gamma}=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}T_{B_\gamma}=\mu_0j$, and the decay bound. Together with the symmetry requirement (vacuous for the loop clause) these are exactly the clauses of the admissibility predicate [F4](c4), so $B_\gamma$ is an admitted field of the declared ideal thin loop; the physical reading of that declaration is the separate adopted assumption [F5], which asserts no existence, uniqueness, self-energy or force content. [step 2.1, F3, F4, F5]

4.1 Clauses (a) and (b) of the Statement are steps 1.1 and 2.1-3.1; the scope clause records that no formula is asserted for noncompact currents (the infinite-wire model is verified separately on the companion examples page), and that no near-wire, self-energy, radiation or force claim is made. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$ and $\operatorname{supp}J\subset B_a(0)$ for some $a>0$, let $A$ be the vector potential of [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ its magnetostatic field, and let $m=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}y\times J(y)\,dy$ be the magnetic moment of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](a). Then for $r=|x|\ge2a$, uniformly in the unit vector $n=x/r$,
$$A(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{m\times x}{r^3}+O\!\left(\frac{\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1}{r^3}\right),\qquad B(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{3n(m\cdot n)-m}{r^3}+O\!\left(\frac{\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1}{r^4}\right),$$
where $\|J\|_1=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|J|\,d\lambda_3$ and the constants implicit in the $O$ terms are absolute: one constant works for all $r\ge2a$ and all unit $n$. This is a controlled two-term far-field estimate: nothing is asserted for $r<2a$ or at the support, no higher multipole is defined here, and the leading dipole term is not claimed to be exact.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; let $J\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$ and $\operatorname{supp}J\subset B_a(0)$; let $A$, $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ be as in [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and $m$ be as in [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](a).

[F1] The vector potential satisfies $A_i=\mu_0N(J_i)=({\mu_0}/{4\pi})\int_{\mathbb R^3}J_i(y)|x-y|^{-1}dy$ componentwise and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ is its magnetostatic field ([[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]], clauses (a)-(c)).

[F2] The magnetic moment of the compact smooth current is the source moment $m=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}y\times J(y)\,dy$ of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](a), computed componentwise as a Riemann integral over a nondegenerate closed bounding rectangle $Q\supset\operatorname{supp}J$ of the continuous compactly supported integrand, with the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; clause (c) records that $m$ is a model quantity and that its far-field interpretation is the content of this theorem under its hypotheses.

[F3] Under the stated hypotheses, with $m=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}y\times J(y)\,dy$ (Lebesgue), $r=|x|\ge2a$ and $n=x/r$, one has uniformly in $n$: $A=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{m\times x}{r^3}+O(\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1r^{-3})$ and $B=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{3n(m\cdot n)-m}{r^3}+O(\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1r^{-4})$, with absolute constants and $\|J\|_1=\int|J|$ ([[lem-em-magnetic-dipole-remainder]]).

[F4] If $f$ is a bounded Borel real function on a nondegenerate closed rectangle $Q$ and $f$ is Riemann integrable there, then $f$ is Lebesgue integrable with the same integral; equivalently, for smooth compactly supported integrands the Riemann integral over a bounding rectangle equals the Lebesgue integral of their zero extension ([[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]).

[F5] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the countable-choice principle assumed here and inherited by the cited comparison and measure interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct transport of the explicit uniform-remainder lemma to the framework's objects, with a Riemann-Lebesgue comparison for the two displayed moments.

1.1 The hypotheses of [F3] are exactly the hypotheses stated here for $J$ (smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free, contained in $B_a(0)$), and the objects of [F3] are the objects of this theorem: $A=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int J(y)|x-y|^{-1}dy$ componentwise and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ by [F1]. The moment of [F2] agrees with the Lebesgue moment of [F3]: each component $y\mapsto(y\times J(y))_i$ is smooth and compactly supported, hence bounded Borel and Riemann integrable on any nondegenerate closed rectangle $Q$ containing $\operatorname{supp}J$; by [F4] its Riemann integral over $Q$ equals its Lebesgue integral over $Q$, and since the integrand vanishes off $\operatorname{supp}J\subset Q$ this equals the Lebesgue integral over $\mathbb R^3$. Hence $\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}y\times J(y)\,dy$ is the same vector in both items. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4]

2.1 Substituting the identifications of step 1.1 into the conclusion of [F3] gives, for $r=|x|\ge2a$ and uniformly in the unit vector $n=x/r$, the displayed estimates $A(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{m\times x}{r^3}+O(\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1r^{-3})$ and $B(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{3n(m\cdot n)-m}{r^3}+O(\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1r^{-4})$ for the framework's $A$ and $B$, with the lemma's uniformity and absolute constants and with $\|J\|_1=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|J|\,d\lambda_3$ as in the Statement. [step 1.1, F3]

3.1 The estimates of step 2.1 are the content of the Statement; no assertion is made for $r<2a$ or at the support, no higher multipole is defined, and the leading dipole term is not claimed to be exact. Countable Choice is used only through the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison [F4] and the measure and Newtonian interfaces [F5] of the cited suppliers; no stronger choice principle occurs. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F3, F4, F5] ∎

## Source notes

Griffiths, Section 5.4.3, printed pp. 242-247, expands the vector potential and gives the dipole field (5.85)-(5.87) with the coordinate-free form and its delta term (5.90); Tong, Sections 3.3.1-3.3.2, printed pp. 54-57, gives the loop far field and the general moment (3.24); Landau-Lifshitz, Section 44, printed pp. 103-105, gives the first-order average field in Gaussian units, re-expressed here in SI. ## Statement

Let $\gamma:[0,L]\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^2$ curve parametrized by arc length ($|\gamma'|\equiv1$) that is either closed ($\gamma(0)=\gamma(L)$ with matching one-sided derivatives) or a wire segment with free endpoints, let $I\in\mathbb R$, let $m=\frac I2\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\gamma'(s)\,ds$ be the finite Riemann source moment defined by this displayed integral in the closed case. For an embedded closed loop this agrees with [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](b); embeddedness is not required for the present parametrized-curve calculation. Let $B$ be a prescribed external magnetic field, of class $C^0$ on a neighbourhood of the trace of $\gamma$ in part (a) and of class $C^2$ on an open set containing the closed ball $\overline{B_a(0)}$ in parts (b)-(d). Adopt the thin-wire coupling hypothesis (W): for a general closed parametrized curve use the stated direct neutral-wire Riemann coupling (with multiplicity of traversal retained); in the embedded closed-loop specialization its source interpretation is exactly [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1); for an open curve use a compact segment of a fed or closed neutral circuit, including a segment of the declared infinite wire of (c2). Adopt separately for that parametrized wire or local segment the direct external magnetic coupling $dF=I\,d\gamma\times B$ and $dN=\gamma\times dF$, as an ideal extension motivated by the smooth continuum Lorentz law [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](ii); that smooth-source postulate does not itself include singular currents. An isolated static neutral open segment is not asserted: its standalone current satisfies $\operatorname{div}J_{\rm seg}=I(\delta_{\gamma(0)}-\delta_{\gamma(L)})$, so its endpoint feed/return cannot be suppressed in a global model. Force and torque here concern only the specified local segment under this adopted coupling. Then:

**(a) [Force and torque under (W)]**
$$F:=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\,ds,\qquad N:=I\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\bigl(\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\bigr)\,ds,$$
the componentwise Riemann integrals of continuous functions on the compact interval $[0,L]$ ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]).

**(b) [Constant field]** If $\gamma$ is closed and $B$ is constant on a neighbourhood of the loop, then $F=0$ and $N=m\times B$ exactly.

**(c) [Slowly varying field]** Let $\gamma$ be closed with $|\gamma(s)|\le a$ for all $s$, let $B$ be $C^2$ on an open set containing $\overline{B_a(0)}$ with constants $M_1,M_2$ such that $|B(x)-B(y)|\le M_1|x-y|$ and $|B(x)-B(0)-DB(0)x|\le\frac12M_2|x|^2$ for $|x|,|y|\le a$, and suppose $\operatorname{div}B=0$ on $B_a(0)$ (as holds for the external part of any smooth-branch vacuum field by [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]). Then
$$F=\nabla(m\cdot B)(0)+R_F,\qquad N=m\times B(0)+R_N,$$
with $|R_F|\le\frac12|I|\,L\,a^2M_2$ and $|R_N|\le|I|\,L\,a^2M_1$, where $\nabla(m\cdot B)(0)$ is the gradient at $0$ of $x\mapsto m\cdot B(x)$ for the fixed vector $m$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

**(d) [Sufficient condition]** If the external field is the magnetostatic field of a compact smooth steady current $J_{\rm ext}\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J_{\rm ext}=0$ ([[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]], [[pthm-em-biot-savart]]), then it is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3$, satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$, and meets the hypotheses of (c) on every ball $\overline{B_a(0)}$ with finite constants $M_1,M_2$.

**(e) [Scope]** Only the external field acts on the loop: the loop's own field, self-force, radiation reaction, mechanical support and material response are outside the statement, and no claim is made about the loop's dynamics, deformation or failure. The coupling (W) is an explicit idealisation of a neutral thin wire at rest in the laboratory frame; it is adopted, not derived, and the theorem is conditional on it. No measurement or uncertainty is involved. Parts (a)-(c), conditional on the explicit coupling (W) and the supplied curve and external field, are finite Riemann-integral calculations and use no Choice axiom. Part (d), transporting the Newtonian-potential construction, assumes Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The $C^2$ arc-length curve $\gamma$, the real $I$, the prescribed field $B$, the coupling (W) of the Statement, and, in parts (b)-(d), the ball containment and regularity hypotheses stated there.

[F1] Under the coupling (W), the force and torque on the parametrized wire are the componentwise Riemann integrals $F=I\int_0^L\gamma'\times B(\gamma)\,ds$ and $N=I\int_0^L\gamma\times(\gamma'\times B(\gamma))\,ds$ of the Statement; continuous integrands on the compact interval are Riemann integrable ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]).

[F2] The cross product is $u\times v=(u_2v_3-u_3v_2,\ u_3v_1-u_1v_3,\ u_1v_2-u_2v_1)$ with $(u\times v)_i=\varepsilon_{ijk}u_jv_k$, the inner product is $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_iu_iv_i$, and the identities $a\times(b\times c)=b(a\cdot c)-c(a\cdot b)$ and $\varepsilon_{ijk}\varepsilon_{ljp}=\delta_{il}\delta_{kp}-\delta_{ip}\delta_{kl}$ hold ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

[F3] The Riemann integral on a compact rectangle is linear, monotone, satisfies $|\int f|\le\int|f|$, and the integral of a constant $c$ over $[0,L]$ is $cL$; these properties are used for the remainder estimates ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]], [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]).

[F4] A $C^2$ field on an open set containing $\overline{B_a(0)}$ satisfies the second-order Taylor identity $B(x)=B(0)+DB(0)x+\frac12D^2B(\xi_x)(x,x)$ for $|x|\le a$ (the case $k=1$ of the multivariable Taylor formula componentwise), so that the stated bounds $|B(x)-B(y)|\le M_1|x-y|$ and $|B(x)-B(0)-DB(0)x|\le\frac12M_2|x|^2$ are the hypotheses available in part (c) ([[thm-multivariable-taylor-formula-with-lagrange-remainder]]).

[F5] The moment of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](b) for a closed embedded arc-length loop is exactly $m=\frac I2\int_0^L\gamma\times\gamma'\,ds$; the declared ideal loop source is [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1) and the declared infinite wire is [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c2) ([[def-em-magnetic-moment]], [[def-em-steady-current-regime]]).

[F6] The compact smooth current class is [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](b); its magnetostatic field construction is [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and its Biot-Savart representation is [[pthm-em-biot-savart]]: the external field of a compact smooth conserved current is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3$ with $\operatorname{div}B=0$ ([[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]], [[pthm-em-biot-savart]]); the smooth-branch vacuum equations are [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and the smooth continuum Lorentz coupling that motivates (W) is [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](ii).

[F7] Distributional derivatives act by signed test differentiation, $\langle\partial^\alpha u,\chi\rangle=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\langle u,\partial^\alpha\chi\rangle$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]); a $C^1$ composition $\varphi\circ\gamma$ has derivative $(\varphi\circ\gamma)'=(\nabla\varphi)(\gamma)\cdot\gamma'$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) and satisfies the fundamental theorem $\int_0^L(\varphi\circ\gamma)'ds=\varphi(\gamma(L))-\varphi(\gamma(0))$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]); the Dirac distribution at a point $p$ acts by $\delta_p(\varphi)=\varphi(p)$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]).

[F8] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the countable-choice principle assumed in part (d) and inherited by the Newtonian-potential suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct evaluation of the pairings under the coupling, the antisymmetric first-moment identities for a closed curve, one Taylor expansion with an explicit remainder, and the compact-current sufficient condition.

1.1 Under the adopted coupling (W) the total force and torque of the parametrized wire are the integrals of the Statement: at arc-length parameter $s$ the element $d\gamma=\gamma'(s)ds$ carries current $I$, so $dF=I\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))ds$ and $dN=\gamma(s)\times dF$. The integrands are compositions and products of continuous maps on the compact interval $[0,L]$, hence continuous and Riemann integrable, so the componentwise integrals of [F1] are finite. This is (a). [given, F1, F2]

1.2 Let $B$ be constant on a neighbourhood of the closed curve. Then $F=I\left(\int_0^L\gamma'(s)ds\right)\times B=I(\gamma(L)-\gamma(0))\times B=0$. For the torque, $F$'s definition and [F2] give $\gamma\times(\gamma'\times B)=(\gamma\cdot B)\gamma'-(\gamma\cdot\gamma')B$, so with the matrix $M_{jl}:=\int_0^L\gamma_j\gamma'_l\,ds$ one has $N=I\int_0^L(\gamma\cdot B)\gamma'\,ds-I\left(\int_0^L\gamma\cdot\gamma'\,ds\right)B=I\,B_jM_{jl}e_l$. The scalar $\gamma\cdot\gamma'=\frac12\frac{d}{ds}|\gamma|^2$ integrates to $0$ over the closed curve, and integrating $\frac{d}{ds}(\gamma_j\gamma_l)=0$ gives $M_{jl}+M_{lj}=0$, so $M$ is antisymmetric. For antisymmetric $M$, the moment $m_p=\frac I2\varepsilon_{pab}M_{ab}$ satisfies $I M_{jl}=\varepsilon_{jlp}m_p$ because $\varepsilon_{abp}\varepsilon_{pcd}=\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}-\delta_{ad}\delta_{bc}$ gives $\varepsilon_{abp}m_p=\frac I2(M_{ab}-M_{ba})=IM_{ab}$. Substituting, $N=\varepsilon_{jlp}m_pB_j e_l=m\times B$ by the cyclic identity of the alternating symbol, and this is (b). [given, F1, F2, F5]

1.3 Let $J_{\rm seg}$ be the standalone open-segment current defined by $\langle J_{\rm seg},\psi\rangle:=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\cdot\psi(\gamma(s))\,ds$ for vector tests $\psi$. With the componentwise distributional divergence pairing of [F7], $\langle\operatorname{div}J_{\rm seg},\varphi\rangle=-I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\cdot\nabla\varphi(\gamma(s))\,ds=-I\int_0^L(\varphi\circ\gamma)'(s)\,ds=I(\varphi(\gamma(0))-\varphi(\gamma(L)))=I(\delta_{\gamma(0)}-\delta_{\gamma(L)})(\varphi)$ for every scalar test $\varphi$, the chain rule and the fundamental theorem of [F7] giving the middle equality. This is the endpoint identity asserted in the Statement, and it shows why the segment is treated as a local part of a fed or closed circuit. [given, F7]

2.1 Under the hypotheses of (c), step 1.1's formulas apply, and [F4] gives the decomposition $B(x)=B(0)+DB(0)x+R(x)$ with $|R(x)|\le\frac12M_2|x|^2$ for $|x|\le a$, together with the Lipschitz bound $|B(x)-B(y)|\le M_1|x-y|$ on the ball. [step 1.1, F4]

3.1 For the force in (c), the constant term vanishes as in step 1.2, and the linear term is $I\varepsilon_{ijk}\partial_lB_k(0)M_{lj}e_i$ with the matrix $M$ of step 1.2. Substituting $IM_{lj}=\varepsilon_{ljp}m_p$ from step 1.2 and contracting by [F2], $I\varepsilon_{ijk}\partial_lB_k(0)M_{lj}e_i=(\delta_{il}\delta_{kp}-\delta_{ip}\delta_{kl})\partial_lB_k(0)m_pe_i=\bigl(\partial_i(m\cdot B)(0)-m_i\operatorname{div}B(0)\bigr)e_i=\nabla(m\cdot B)(0)$, since $m$ is constant and $\operatorname{div}B(0)=0$. By [F3] and step 2.1 the remainder obeys $|I\int_0^L\gamma'\times R(\gamma)\,ds|\le|I|\int_0^L|\gamma'|\,|R(\gamma)|\,ds\le\frac12|I|La^2M_2$, because $|\gamma'|\equiv1$ and $|\gamma(s)|\le a$. This proves the force assertion of (c) with $|R_F|\le\frac12|I|La^2M_2$. [step 1.2, step 2.1, F2, F3]

3.2 For the torque in (c), split $B(\gamma(s))=B(0)+(B(\gamma(s))-B(0))$. The first part is the constant-field torque of step 1.2 with the constant field $B(0)$, that is $m\times B(0)$. For the remainder, [F2] gives $\gamma\times(\gamma'\times(B(\gamma)-B(0)))=\gamma'(\gamma\cdot(B(\gamma)-B(0)))-(B(\gamma)-B(0))(\gamma\cdot\gamma')$ and hence, by [F3] and step 2.1, $\left|I\int_0^L\gamma\times(\gamma'\times(B(\gamma)-B(0)))\,ds\right|\le|I|\int_0^L|\gamma|\,|\gamma'|\,|B(\gamma)-B(0)|\,ds\le|I|\,a\cdot1\cdot M_1a\cdot L$. This proves the torque assertion of (c) with $|R_N|\le|I|La^2M_1$. [step 1.2, step 2.1, F2, F3]

3.3 For (d): by [F6] the external field of a compact smooth conserved current satisfies $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, hence is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3$ with $\operatorname{div}B=0$; on the compact ball $\overline{B_a(0)}$ the suprema $M_1:=\sup|DB|$ and $M_2:=\sup|D^2B|$ of the continuous derivative norms are finite by compactness and a continuous function on a compact set attaining its bounds, and the mean-value estimate gives $|B(x)-B(y)|\le M_1|x-y|$ while the second-order Taylor identity of [F4] gives $|B(x)-B(0)-DB(0)x|\le\frac12M_2|x|^2$ for $|x|,|y|\le a$. Hence the hypotheses of (c) are met on every such ball with finite constants. [step 2.1, F4, F6]

4.1 Parts (a), (b), (c), (d) are steps 1.1, 1.2, 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3; the endpoint identity quoted in the Statement is step 1.3. The scope clause (e) records that only the external field acts, that the coupling (W) is an adopted idealisation motivated by the smooth continuum law [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](ii) rather than derived from it, and that no self-field, self-force, radiation reaction, mechanical support, deformation or dynamical claim is made. Parts (a)-(c) are finite Riemann-integral calculations and use no Choice axiom; part (d) inherits Countable Choice only through the Newtonian-potential suppliers [F8]. The moment identity is contracted without dividing by $I$; for $I=0$ the moment, force, torque and both remainders vanish, and the algebra applies to every stated closed parametrized $C^2$ curve, including multiply traversed and self-intersecting ones, since only closure, unit speed and the finite moment integral are used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 3.3, F5, F8] ∎

## Source notes

Griffiths, Section 5.1.3, printed pp. 208-214, gives the wire force $\mathbf F=\int I\,d\mathbf l\times\mathbf B$ (5.17), and Section 6.1.2, printed pp. 255-260, gives $\mathbf N=\mathbf m\times\mathbf B$ in a uniform field (6.1), the vanishing net force in a uniform field, and $\mathbf F=\nabla(\mathbf m\cdot\mathbf B)$ for a small loop in a nonuniform field (6.3), with Problems 6.2 and 6.4; Tong, Sections 3.4.1-3.4.2, printed pp. 57-62, performs the Taylor expansion over a small localised current and the moment manipulations; Landau-Lifshitz, Section 45, printed pp. 105-106, gives the average moment $K=m\times H$ (45.1), re-expressed here in SI. The theorem above is the exact conditional version for the declared parametrized wire under the explicitly adopted coupling (W); the texts do not supply the neutral-wire hypothesis, which is stated here as an idealisation.

## Example

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $a>0$, $I\in\mathbb R$, let $\gamma(s)=a(\cos(s/a),\sin(s/a),0)$, $s\in[0,2\pi a]$, be the circle of radius $a$ in the plane $x_3=0$ parametrized by arc length, let the declared ideal thin-loop current of amplitude $I$ run along $\gamma$ in the sense of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1), with moment $m=I\pi a^2e_3$ ([[def-em-magnetic-moment]](b)), and let $\mu_0$, $c$, $\varepsilon_0$ be the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Then for every point $x=ze_3$ on the axis ($z\in\mathbb R$, $\operatorname{dist}(x,\gamma)=\sqrt{a^2+z^2}>0$) the field of the ideal loop is the absolutely convergent line integral
$$B(ze_3)=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi}\int_0^{2\pi a}\frac{\gamma'(s)\times\left(ze_3-\gamma(s)\right)}{|ze_3-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds=\frac{\mu_0Ia^2}{2(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}}\,e_3,$$
i.e. the Biot-Savart field of [[pthm-em-biot-savart]] and the declared thin-current limit of [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]] agree on the axis, with the sign fixed by the positive (counterclockwise) orientation of $\gamma$ and by the sign of $I$; in particular $B(0)=\frac{\mu_0I}{2a}e_3$. This is a property of the declared idealisation; it is not the field of any physical finite-radius coil, nothing is claimed at points off the axis or on the wire, and no measurement is involved. The explicit finite Riemann axis evaluation and circle moment calculation alone are choice-free. Countable Choice is inherited by the asserted global distributional model and thin-current supplier.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; let $a>0$, $I\in\mathbb R$ and the circle $\gamma(s)=a(\cos(s/a),\sin(s/a),0)$ with $s\in[0,2\pi a]$; let the ideal loop model be the declared one of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1) with physical adoption [[post-em-ideal-magnetostatic-models]].

[F1] The field of the declared ideal thin loop is $B_\gamma(x)=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi}\int_0^L\frac{\gamma'(s)\times(x-\gamma(s))}{|x-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds$ for $x$ off the curve: this is the Biot-Savart representation of the compact smooth class together with its declared thin-loop limit, and the ideal loop's admissibility is supplied by the strengthened thin-current supplier together with the declared adoption ([[pthm-em-biot-savart]], [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]], [[def-em-steady-current-regime]], [[post-em-ideal-magnetostatic-models]]).

[F2] The moment of clause (b) of the definition is $m=\frac I2\int_0^L\gamma\times\gamma'\,ds$; for the present circle $\gamma\times\gamma'=ae_3$ and the integral evaluates to $2\pi a^2e_3$, so $m=I\pi a^2e_3$ ([[def-em-magnetic-moment]]).

[F3] For $u,v\in\mathbb R^3$, $u\times v=(u_2v_3-u_3v_2,\ u_3v_1-u_1v_3,\ u_1v_2-u_2v_1)$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); components of continuous integrands on the compact interval $[0,2\pi a]$ are Riemann integrable ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]).

[F4] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the countable-choice principle assumed here and inherited by the asserted global distributional model and thin-current supplier ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; identify the axis field with the declared line integral, evaluate the integral by the substitution $t=s/a$, and read off the center value and the moment.

1.1 Every axis point $ze_3$ lies at distance $\sqrt{a^2+z^2}\ge a>0$ from the circle, so it is off the curve; by [F1] the field of the declared ideal loop there is the absolutely convergent line integral $B(ze_3)=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi}\int_0^{2\pi a}\frac{\gamma'(s)\times(ze_3-\gamma(s))}{|ze_3-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds$, the same integral being the Biot-Savart field of the compact smooth currents in the declared thin-current limit. [given, F1]

1.2 Substituting $t=s/a$, so that $ds=a\,dt$ and $\gamma'(s)=(-\sin t,\cos t,0)$ while $ze_3-\gamma(s)=(-a\cos t,-a\sin t,z)$, one has $\gamma'(s)\times(ze_3-\gamma(s))=(z\cos t,\ z\sin t,\ a)$ by [F3] (the first two components carry the factor $a\cos t\cdot z$ and $a\sin t\cdot z$ respectively, and the third is $a\cos^2t+a\sin^2t=a$), and $|ze_3-\gamma(s)|=(a^2+z^2)^{1/2}$ is constant. Hence the component integrals are continuous functions of $t$ on the compact interval $[0,2\pi]$. [given, F3]

2.1 By steps 1.1 and 1.2, $B(ze_3)=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi}\cdot\frac{a}{(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}}\int_0^{2\pi}(z\cos t,z\sin t,a)\,dt=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi}\cdot\frac{2\pi a^2}{(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}}\,e_3=\frac{\mu_0Ia^2}{2(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}}\,e_3$, the first two components vanishing because $\cos$ and $\sin$ have vanishing integral over a full period. At $z=0$ this gives $B(0)=\frac{\mu_0I}{2a}e_3$, and the sign is the product of the orientation sign of $\gamma$ and the sign of $I$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F3]

3.1 The computation also fixes the source moment: with $\gamma\times\gamma'=ae_3$ and $\int_0^{2\pi a}ae_3\,ds=2\pi a^2e_3$, clause (b) of [F2] gives $m=I\pi a^2e_3$, the value quoted in the Example. The whole verification is a conditional ideal-model computation on the axis only: nothing is claimed off the axis or on the wire, no apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty or empirical inference is involved, and Countable Choice enters only through the asserted global distributional model and thin-current supplier [F4]. [step 2.1, F2, F4] ∎

## Source notes

Griffiths, Example 5.6, printed pp. 217-218, evaluates the axis field (5.38) $\mu_0IR^2/[2(R^2+z^2)^{3/2}]$; Tong, Section 3.2.3 and Section 3.3.1, printed pp. 49-56, gives the thin-wire Biot-Savart integral and the loop far field; Chew, Lecture 5 Section 5.1, printed pp. 49-52, gives the current-element form. The example verifies the declared ideal loop's axis field against those formulas; it is explicitly not a statement about any physical coil.

## Example

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]].

**(a) [Ideal infinite straight wire].** Let $\gamma(s)=(0,0,s)$, $s\in\mathbb R$, let $J_{\rm w}$ be the declared ideal line current of amplitude $I$ along $\gamma$ ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c2)), and define, on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\gamma$,
$$B(x):=\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi\rho}\,e_\varphi,\qquad \rho=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2},\qquad e_\varphi=\rho^{-1}(-x_2,x_1,0).$$
Then $B$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ and of class $C^\infty$ off $\gamma$; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ pointwise off $\gamma$; $B$ is invariant under translations along $\gamma$ and rotations about it, and its transverse far-zone supremum tends to $0$ as $\rho\to\infty$; the circulation of $B$ around every circle of radius $r>0$ centred on $\gamma$, at any height, is $\mu_0I$ ([[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]); and $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J_{\rm w}$ hold in the distributional sense of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c4). Hence $B$ is an admitted field of the declared wire model; the transverse decay excludes an added homogeneous longitudinal field, and no further selection, uniqueness or energy claim is made.

**(b) [Ideal infinite cylindrical sheet].** Let $a>0$, $S=\{\rho=a\}$, $K\in\mathbb R$, let $J_S$ be the declared ideal sheet current of amplitude $K$ along $S$ ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c3)), and define $B:=\mu_0Ke_3$ for $\rho<a$ and $B:=0$ for $\rho>a$. Then $B$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ and of class $C^\infty$ off $S$; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ pointwise off $S$; $B$ has the declared symmetry (translations along and rotations about the axis) and its transverse far-zone supremum is $0$; the one-sided jump across $S$, with $n=e_\rho$ from the interior to the exterior and $[B]=B_+-B_-$, is $n\times[B]=\mu_0Ke_\varphi$ and $n\cdot[B]=0$, the stationary tangential-sheet jump for this noncompact cylinder, established by the test-localized [[lem-em-ideal-cylindrical-sheet-field]] for the current density $Ke_\varphi$ (computed directly as $e_\rho\times(0-\mu_0Ke_3)=\mu_0Ke_\varphi$); and $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J_S$ hold in the distributional sense of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c4). Hence $B$ is an admitted field of the declared solenoid model.

**(c) [Scope].** Both models are declared noncompact idealisations: they are not finite-energy localized-current theorems; nothing is asserted about self-energy, inductance, self-force, the fields on the sources, or the approximation of any physical apparatus; and the fields are selected within the declared symmetry and decay class, not shown to be the only solutions of the magnetostatic equations off the sources without that class. The external force between two such wires is treated in [[ex-em-wire-force-coupling]] under the adopted thin-wire coupling.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; let the ideal line current $J_{\rm w}$ and the ideal sheet current $J_S$ be the declared objects of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c2) and (c3); let $B$ be the fields defined in (a) and (b) of the Example.

[F1] The field $f:=\rho^{-1}e_\varphi$ on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\gamma$ is locally integrable, is $C^\infty$ off $\gamma$ with $\operatorname{div}f=\operatorname{curl}f=0$ there, has circulation $2\pi$ around every circle of radius $r>0$ centred on $\gamma$, and satisfies $\langle\operatorname{curl}T_f,\psi\rangle=2\pi A(\psi)$ with $A(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\psi_3(0,0,x_3)\,dx_3$ and $\langle\operatorname{div}T_f,\varphi\rangle=0$ for all scalar and vector tests ([[lem-em-ideal-line-current-field]]).

[F2] The piecewise constant field $g=e_3\mathbf 1_{\{\rho<a\}}$ extended by zero outside the cylinder satisfies $\langle\operatorname{curl}T_g,\psi\rangle=\int_S e_\varphi\cdot\psi\,dS$ and $\langle\operatorname{div}T_g,\varphi\rangle=0$ for all tests, with the one-sided values satisfying $g_+-g_-=-e_3$, $e_\rho\times(g_+-g_-)=e_\varphi$ and $e_\rho\cdot(g_+-g_-)=0$ ([[lem-em-ideal-cylindrical-sheet-field]]).

[F3] The declared line current acts as $\langle J_{\rm w},\psi\rangle=I\int_{\mathbb R}\psi_3(0,0,s)\,ds$ and the declared sheet current as $\langle J_S,\psi\rangle=K\int_S e_\varphi\cdot\psi\,dS$ ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c2)-(c3)), and the admissibility predicate (c4) requires local integrability, $C^1$ regularity and vanishing divergence and curl off the source, the two global distributional identities, the declared symmetry and the stated decay ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]]).

[F4] The cross product and the identities $e_3\times e_\rho=e_\varphi$, $e_\rho\times e_3=-e_\varphi$ hold ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); divergence and curl are the coordinate expressions of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]; the circulation is the vector line integral of [[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]; surface integrals over the cylinder are those of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], with the compact-face area computed through the Riemann integral of [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]] and [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]].

[F5] The physical reading of these declared ideal models is the separate adopted assumption [[post-em-ideal-magnetostatic-models]], which asserts no existence, uniqueness, finite self-energy, force, self-force or apparatus accuracy ([[post-em-ideal-magnetostatic-models]]).

[F6] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the countable-choice principle assumed here and inherited by the cited measure, surface, regular-distribution and Newtonian interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; the two explicit fields are scalar multiples of the fields of the two mathematical lemmas, so their pointwise, symmetry and distributional properties transport, and the admissibility predicate is then checked clause by clause.

1.1 The field of (a) is $B=\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi}f$ with $f=\rho^{-1}e_\varphi$; by [F1] it is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ and $C^\infty$ off $\gamma$, with $\operatorname{div}B=\operatorname{curl}B=0$ pointwise off $\gamma$, and all these properties are stable under multiplication by the constant $\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi}$. [given, F1]

1.2 The field of (b) is $B=\mu_0Kg$ with $g$ the piecewise constant cylinder field: it is bounded, hence locally integrable, constantly $\mu_0Ke_3$ for $\rho<a$ and $0$ for $\rho>a$, so it is $C^\infty$ off $S$ with $\operatorname{div}B=\operatorname{curl}B=0$ there; it is invariant under translations along and rotations about the third axis, and its supremum on any compact set of cross-sectional parameters is $0$ for every $\rho>a$, hence its transverse far-zone supremum is $0$. [given, F2]

2.1 For the wire, $\langle\operatorname{curl}T_B,\psi\rangle=\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi}\langle\operatorname{curl}T_f,\psi\rangle=\mu_0I\,A(\psi)=\mu_0\langle J_{\rm w},\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\operatorname{div}T_B,\varphi\rangle=0$ for all tests by [F1] and [F3]; moreover $B$ depends only on $\rho$ through the scalar factor $\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi\rho}$ multiplying $e_\varphi$, so it is invariant under translations along $\gamma$ and rotations about it, and its transverse far-zone supremum is $\frac{\mu_0|I|}{2\pi\rho}\to0$. The circulation of $B$ around the circle of radius $r>0$ at height $h$ is $\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r}$ times the circulation $2\pi$ of $f$, that is $\mu_0I$, by [F1] and the linearity of the line integral [F4]. [step 1.1, F1, F3, F4]

2.2 For the sheet, $\langle\operatorname{curl}T_B,\psi\rangle=\mu_0K\langle\operatorname{curl}T_g,\psi\rangle=\mu_0K\int_S e_\varphi\cdot\psi\,dS=\mu_0\langle J_S,\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\operatorname{div}T_B,\varphi\rangle=0$ for all tests by [F2] and [F3]. The one-sided values across $S$ are $B_+=\mu_0Ke_3$ and $B_-=0$ in the direction from the interior to the exterior, so $[B]=B_+-B_-=-\mu_0Ke_3$ and, by [F4], $n\times[B]=e_\rho\times(-\mu_0Ke_3)=\mu_0Ke_\varphi$ and $n\cdot[B]=0$; this is the jump displayed in (b), computed directly from the one-sided values of the declared field. [step 1.2, F2, F3, F4]

3.1 For the wire, every clause of the admissibility predicate [F3](c4) holds: local integrability and off-source $C^\infty$ regularity from step 1.1, the two pointwise vanishing identities off $\gamma$ from step 1.1, the two distributional identities and the line-measure value from step 2.1, the translation and rotation symmetry from step 2.1, and the transverse decay from step 2.1. Hence the field of (a) is admitted for the declared wire model; the decay requirement is what rules out adding a constant longitudinal field, and nothing else is claimed. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F3]

3.2 For the sheet, every clause of [F3](c4) holds: local integrability, off-source $C^\infty$ regularity, the two pointwise vanishing identities and the symmetry and the vanishing transverse far-zone supremum from step 1.2, and the two distributional identities from step 2.2, with the one-sided jump of step 2.2 as the interface content. Hence the field of (b) is admitted for the declared solenoid model. [step 1.2, step 2.2, F3]

4.1 Steps 3.1 and 3.2 prove that both explicit fields are admitted under the predicate (c4) of [F3]; the physical reading of the declared models is the separate adopted assumption [F5], which adds no existence, uniqueness, self-energy, inductance, force or apparatus claim. Both models are declared noncompact idealisations: no finite-energy or localized-current conclusion is drawn, nothing is asserted on the sources, and the fields are selected within the declared symmetry and decay class rather than shown to be the only solutions off the sources. Countable Choice is inherited only through the cited measure, surface, regular-distribution and Newtonian interfaces [F6]; no stronger choice principle occurs. [step 3.1, step 3.2, F3, F5, F6] ∎

## Source notes

Griffiths, Example 5.5 and Examples 5.7 and 5.9, printed pp. 215-217 and 226-228, evaluates the wire field $\mu_0I/(2\pi r)$ and the infinite-solenoid field $\mu_0nI$ inside and zero outside; Tong, Sections 3.1.1-3.1.2, printed pp. 42-46, gives the wire field, the surface-current discontinuity (3.5)-(3.6) and the solenoid field (3.7); Chew, Lecture 4 Section 4.3.3-4.3.4, printed pp. 46-48, gives the current-sheet jump and the normal-field continuity. The verification above is the exact ideal-model check against the framework's admissibility predicate; no measurement, apparatus or uncertainty is involved, and the idealizations are not claimed to describe any real conductor or coil.

## Example

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $d>0$ and $I_1,I_2\in\mathbb R$; let wire 1 be the declared ideal line current of amplitude $I_1$ along the third coordinate axis and wire 2 the translate of that ideal line current by $d\,e_1$, of amplitude $I_2$ ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c2)), and adopt for the force on wire 2 the thin-wire coupling (W) of [[pthm-em-magnetic-loop-force-torque]], restricted to the external field of wire 1. Then the force per unit length on wire 2 is
$$\mathbf f=\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,e_3\times e_2=-\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,e_1,$$
i.e. attraction towards wire 1 (direction $-e_1$) for currents in the same direction ($I_1I_2>0$), repulsion for opposite directions, and magnitude $\mu_0|I_1I_2|/(2\pi d)$ per unit length. The comparison uses only the external field of wire 1 at the position of wire 2; the self-fields and the mechanical support forces of the two infinite wires are excluded, no claim is made about the total force on either infinite wire, and no measurement is involved.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; let $d>0$, $I_1,I_2\in\mathbb R$; wire 1 and wire 2 are the declared ideal line currents of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c2) along the third axis and its translate by $d\,e_1$; the coupling (W) of [[pthm-em-magnetic-loop-force-torque]] is restricted to the external field of wire 1.

[F1] The declared ideal wire 1 has the admitted field $B_1(x)=\frac{\mu_0I_1}{2\pi\rho}e_\varphi$ on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\gamma$, with $\rho=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}$ and $e_\varphi=\rho^{-1}(-x_2,x_1,0)$, verified as an admitted field of the declared wire model ([[ex-em-infinite-wire-and-solenoid]], [[def-em-steady-current-regime]], [[post-em-ideal-magnetostatic-models]]).

[F2] Under the coupling (W) of the force theorem, the force on a parametrized wire segment $\gamma:[0,L]\to\mathbb R^3$ of the declared model in a prescribed external field is $F=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\,ds$, a componentwise Riemann integral of a continuous integrand ([[pthm-em-magnetic-loop-force-torque]], clause (a)).

[F3] For $u,v\in\mathbb R^3$, $u\times v=(u_2v_3-u_3v_2,\ u_3v_1-u_1v_3,\ u_1v_2-u_2v_1)$; in particular $e_3\times e_2=-e_1$. The Riemann integral on a compact interval is linear and the integral of a constant $c$ over $[-S,S]$ is $2Sc$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]).

[F4] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the countable-choice principle assumed here and inherited by the asserted ideal-line model; the final constant-force computation is finite ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the external field of wire 1 on the line of wire 2, integrate the coupling over a compact straight segment, and divide by its length.

1.1 On the points $(d,0,x_3)$ of wire 2 one has $\rho=d$ and $(-x_2,x_1,0)=(0,d,0)$, so $e_\varphi=e_2$ and, by [F1], $B_1(d,0,x_3)=\frac{\mu_0I_1}{2\pi d}e_2$, constant along the whole line of wire 2. [given, F1]

2.1 Fix $S>0$ and let $\gamma(x_3):=(d,0,x_3)$, $x_3\in[-S,S]$, a compact straight segment of wire 2 parametrized by arc length, so $\gamma'=e_3$ and $|\gamma'|=1$. By [F2] the force on this segment under (W), restricted to the external field $B_1$ of wire 1, is $I_2\int_{-S}^{S}e_3\times B_1(d,0,x_3)\,dx_3=I_2\bigl(\frac{\mu_0I_1}{2\pi d}\bigr)(e_3\times e_2)\int_{-S}^{S}1\,dx_3=2S\,\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,(e_3\times e_2)$, using that the integrand is constant and the integral of a constant over $[-S,S]$ is $2S$ times it by [F3]. [step 1.1, F2, F3]

3.1 Dividing the force of step 2.1 by the segment length $2S$ gives the force per unit length $\mathbf f=\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}(e_3\times e_2)$; by [F3], $e_3\times e_2=-e_1$, so $\mathbf f=-\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}e_1$, which for $I_1I_2>0$ points from wire 2 towards wire 1 (attraction) and for $I_1I_2<0$ away from it (repulsion), with magnitude $\frac{\mu_0|I_1I_2|}{2\pi d}$; the result is independent of $S$, so it is a force per unit length of the comparison. Only the external field of wire 1 is used: the self-field of wire 2 and the support forces of both infinite wires are excluded, the compact segment is a local part of a fed or closed circuit (the endpoint identity of [[pthm-em-magnetic-loop-force-torque]] applies to the standalone segment), and no dynamics, circuit model, material response or measurement is claimed. Countable Choice enters only through the asserted ideal-line model [F4]. [step 2.1, F2, F4] ∎

## Source notes

Griffiths, Section 5.2.2, printed pp. 217-218, computes the attraction between two long parallel wires from the field $\mu_0I_1/(2\pi d)$ and the line-current force law; Tong, Section 3.4.1, printed pp. 57-59, gives $f=-(\mu_0I_1I_2/2\pi d)\hat x$ (3.25) with attraction for equal directions and repulsion for opposite ones; Landau-Lifshitz, Section 42, printed pp. 100-101, describes the interaction of two systems through their fields, re-expressed here in SI. The computation above is the exact local external-force comparison for the declared ideal wires under the adopted coupling; it is not a solution of the two-wire dynamics.
