## Statement

Let $c>0$, let $k\ge2$ be an integer, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open set that is star-shaped with respect to a point $a\in\Omega$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]), and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]). Joint regularity on $\Omega\times I$ is read in the restriction convention of [[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]]: a map on $\Omega\times I$ is **jointly $C^m$** when it is the restriction of a $C^m$ map on some open neighbourhood of $\Omega\times I$ in $\mathbb R^4$. For open $I$ this is the ordinary open-domain class of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] and agrees with the field class of [[def-em-fields]]; for non-open $I$ it is the convention that makes the statements below meaningful, and no time jet is asserted beyond the restricted values.

Let $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be jointly $C^k$ and satisfy the two source-free Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] pointwise on $\Omega\times I$:

$$\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,$$

with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] (at included endpoints of a non-open $I$, as relative derivatives in the restriction convention). Then there are a scalar potential $\varphi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ that is jointly $C^{k-1}$ and a vector potential $A:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is jointly $C^k$, both in the restriction convention, with

$$B=\operatorname{curl}A,\qquad E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I,$$

so that $(\varphi,A)$ is a potential pair whose field pair is $(E,B)$, in the vocabulary of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]. If $E$ and $B$ are jointly $C^\infty$, then $\varphi$ and $A$ may be chosen jointly $C^\infty$. Conversely, if $\varphi$ and $A$ are jointly $C^\infty$ on $\Omega\times I$ in the restriction convention and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$ are their field pair, then $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ on $\Omega\times I$.

The theorem asserts existence on the stated star-shaped domain only: it claims no global potential on a general open set, no boundary, decay or growth condition on the potentials, and no uniqueness. Potentials are auxiliary objects of the framework and are not claimed to be observable.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A constant $c>0$, an integer $k\ge2$, an open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ star-shaped with respect to $a\in\Omega$, an interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ with at least two elements, and fields $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that are jointly $C^k$ in the restriction convention and satisfy the two source-free equations of the Statement pointwise.

[F1] Joint regularity and radial witnesses: for an open star-shaped $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ with centre $a$ and a jointly $C^m$ field $B:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$, $m\ge1$, with $\operatorname{div}B(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t\in I$, the radial integral $A(x,t)=\int_0^1s\,B(a+s(x-a),t)\times(x-a)\,ds$ is jointly $C^m$ with $\operatorname{curl}A(\cdot,t)=B(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$; for a jointly $C^m$ field $C$ with $\operatorname{curl}C(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$ the negative radial scalar witness $\phi(x,t)=-\int_0^1\langle C(a+s(x-a),t),x-a\rangle\,ds$ is jointly $C^m$ with $\nabla\phi(\cdot,t)=-C(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$; jointly $C^\infty$ data give jointly $C^\infty$ witnesses; and the restriction convention carries the same conclusions at included endpoints of a non-open interval ([[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]]).

[F2] The smooth branch of the adopted vacuum Maxwell equations holds pointwise for jointly $C^1$ fields and contains, among its four equations, $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$; the postulate contains no magnetic charge ([[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]).

[F3] Potential-pair vocabulary: for a potential pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^m$, $m\ge1$, on an open set the electric and magnetic fields are $E(\varphi,A)=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B(\varphi,A)=\operatorname{curl}A$, and both are of class $C^{m-1}$; the definition asserts no existence of potentials for a given field pair ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]).

[F4] Euclidean calculus: a map is of class $C^m$ when each component is, the class is closed under sums and compositions of class, and sums, scalar multiples and products of differentiable real functions obey the usual derivative rules ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]).

[F5] Linearity: for $C^1$ fields $F,G$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ and reals $\alpha,\beta$, $\operatorname{curl}(\alpha F+\beta G)=\alpha\operatorname{curl}F+\beta\operatorname{curl}G$, and the divergence is likewise linear ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]).

[F6] Clairaut--Schwarz: for a $C^2$ function on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$ mixed coordinate partial derivatives commute, so for a jointly $C^2$ field the time derivative of each spatial first partial derivative equals the spatial first partial derivative of the time derivative ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]).

[F7] For a $C^2$ field on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ the divergence of its curl vanishes pointwise ([[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]]).

[F8] For a $C^2$ scalar function on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ the curl of its gradient vanishes pointwise ([[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]]).

[F9] The divergence of a $C^1$ field is $\operatorname{div}F=\sum_i\partial_iF_i$, the curl is $\operatorname{curl}F=(\partial_yF_z-\partial_zF_y,\ \partial_zF_x-\partial_xF_z,\ \partial_xF_y-\partial_yF_x)$, the gradient is the tuple of first coordinate partial derivatives, and partial derivatives are one-variable derivatives along coordinate lines ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; apply the radial vector witness to $B$, apply the radial scalar witness to the auxiliary field $E+\partial_tA$, and verify the converse by the standard curl and divergence identities.

1.1 Hypothesis check and vector step. The set $\Omega$ is open and star-shaped with centre $a$ and $I$ is an interval, and by [F2] the field $B$ is jointly $C^k$ with $\operatorname{div}B(\cdot,t)=0$ on $\Omega$ for every $t\in I$, the divergence being that of [F9]. Since $k\ge2\ge1$, the vector witness of [F1] applies and produces the field $A(x,t):=\int_0^1s\,B(a+s(x-a),t)\times(x-a)\,ds$, which is jointly $C^k$ on $\Omega\times I$ and satisfies $\operatorname{curl}A(\cdot,t)=B(\cdot,t)$ for every $t\in I$. [given, F1, F2, F9]

1.2 Converse. Let $\varphi$ and $A$ be jointly $C^\infty$ on $\Omega\times I$ and put $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$. All functions are restrictions of $C^\infty$ maps on an open neighbourhood of $\Omega\times I$, so the identities below may be checked there and restricted. The field $A$ is $C^\infty$, hence $C^2$, and [F7] gives $\operatorname{div}B=\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}A=0$. For the curl of $E$, the linearity of the curl [F5] gives $\operatorname{curl}E=-\operatorname{curl}\nabla\varphi-\operatorname{curl}\partial_tA$; the first term vanishes by [F8] applied to the $C^2$ function $\varphi$, and for the second, the component formula of [F9] turns each coordinate of $\operatorname{curl}\partial_tA$ into a difference of mixed derivatives $\partial_t\partial_x$ and $\partial_x\partial_t$ of the $C^2$ components of $A$, which [F6] identifies, so $\operatorname{curl}\partial_tA=\partial_t\operatorname{curl}A=\partial_tB$. Hence $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ on $\Omega\times I$. [given, F5, F6, F7, F8, F9]

2.1 The auxiliary field $C:=E+\partial_tA$. The fields $E$ and $A$ are restrictions to $\Omega\times I$ of $C^k$ maps on a common open neighbourhood; the time partial derivative of each component of the $C^k$ map extending $A$ exists and is $C^{k-1}$ there by [F4] and [F9], and the class is closed under sums by [F4], so $C$ is jointly $C^{k-1}$ on $\Omega\times I$ in the restriction convention. [step 1.1, F1, F4, F9]

2.2 The auxiliary field is curl-free at every time. Fix $t\in I$. By linearity of the curl [F5] and the componentwise commutation of $\partial_t$ with the spatial partial derivatives of the jointly $C^2$ field $A$, which is [F6] applied to the component functions, $\operatorname{curl}C(\cdot,t)=\operatorname{curl}E(\cdot,t)+\partial_t(\operatorname{curl}A)(\cdot,t)$, the operators and the derivative being those of [F9]. By step 1.1, $\operatorname{curl}A(\cdot,t)=B(\cdot,t)$ as functions of the position variable, so $\partial_t(\operatorname{curl}A)(\cdot,t)=\partial_tB(\cdot,t)$; by [F2], $\operatorname{curl}E(\cdot,t)=-\partial_tB(\cdot,t)$. Substituting gives $\operatorname{curl}C(\cdot,t)=-\partial_tB(\cdot,t)+\partial_tB(\cdot,t)=0$. [step 1.1, F2, F5, F6, F9]

3.1 Scalar step and the pair identities. By step 2.1 the field $C$ is jointly $C^{k-1}$ with $k-1\ge1$, and by step 2.2 it satisfies $\operatorname{curl}C(\cdot,t)=0$ on $\Omega$ for every $t\in I$; the scalar witness of [F1] therefore gives the jointly $C^{k-1}$ function $\varphi(x,t):=-\int_0^1\langle C(a+s(x-a),t),x-a\rangle\,ds$ with $\nabla\varphi(\cdot,t)=-C(\cdot,t)$ for every $t\in I$. Since $C=E+\partial_tA$ by step 2.1, this reads $\nabla\varphi=-E-\partial_tA$, that is $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ on $\Omega\times I$; together with $\operatorname{curl}A=B$ from step 1.1 this exhibits $(\varphi,A)$ as a potential pair with field pair $(E,B)$ in the sense of [F3], with $\varphi$ jointly $C^{k-1}$ and $A$ jointly $C^k$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, F1, F3]

4.1 Smooth clause. If $E$ and $B$ are jointly $C^\infty$, the vector witness of [F1] applied to $B$ gives a jointly $C^\infty$ field $A$ with $\operatorname{curl}A=B$, the field $C=E+\partial_tA$ is jointly $C^\infty$ by the closure and differentiation rules of [F4], and the scalar witness of [F1] applied to $C$ gives a jointly $C^\infty$ scalar $\varphi$ with $\nabla\varphi=-C$; the identities of step 3.1 then hold with both potentials jointly $C^\infty$. [step 3.1, F1, F4]

5.1 Conclusion and bookkeeping. Steps 1.1 through 3.1 produce, for every integer $k\ge2$, a jointly $C^{k-1}$ scalar $\varphi$ and a jointly $C^k$ vector $A$ with $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ and $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ on $\Omega\times I$; step 4.1 supplies the jointly $C^\infty$ choice when the data are jointly $C^\infty$; and step 1.2 proves the converse implication. The construction used star-shapedness and the joint class only through the witnesses of [F1], used the source-free equations through [F2], and used the potential vocabulary of [F3]; no global potential on a general open set, no boundary or decay condition, no uniqueness and no observability claim is made, and at included endpoints of a non-open interval all conclusions are those of the restriction convention recorded in [F1]. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 3.1, step 4.1, F1, F2, F3] ∎

## Remarks

- **The star-shaped hypothesis is substantive.** On a general open $\Omega$ the two source-free equations need not admit a global potential pair; the divergence-free radial witness of [F1] and its scalar companion both use the radial segments from the centre, and the companion examples page records the obstruction on a punctured region.
- **No uniqueness is claimed.** The witnesses of [F1] are single specimens; different potentials of the same field pair differ by gauge transformations, a freedom analyzed on this page after the gauge vocabulary is introduced.

## Definition

Let $c>0$, let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with its restricted inertial chart, let fields and units be those of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let the scalar-vector potential vocabulary on that region be that of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]: a **potential pair** $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^k$ on $\Omega\times I$ consists of $\varphi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $A:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^k$ jointly in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], and for a non-open time interval $I$ the joint classes in this item are read in the open-neighbourhood restriction convention of [[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]] (for open $I$ this is the ordinary class of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); for $k\ge1$ the **field pair** is

$$E(\varphi,A):=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA,\qquad B(\varphi,A):=\operatorname{curl}A,$$

where $\nabla$ is the gradient, $\operatorname{div}$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ are those of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], and $\partial_t$ is the partial derivative at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. For $k\ge1$ the **Lorenz divergence** of the pair is $G(\varphi,A):=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$. The definitions in this item are stated on the laboratory region; the framework's fields are those of [[def-em-fields]], and no field equation is assumed anywhere below.

(a) [Representations] Let $k\ge2$ be an integer and let $(E,B)$ be a field pair of class $C^{k-1}$ on $\Omega\times I$, meaning $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly as in [[def-em-fields]]. A **potential representation of class $C^k$** of $(E,B)$ is a potential pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^k$ on $\Omega\times I$ whose field pair is $(E,B)$, that is, $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ on $\Omega\times I$. This definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of a representation: existence on a star-shaped spatial region under the stated hypotheses is the content of [[pthm-em-spacetime-potentials]], and two representations of one field pair differ by a gauge transformation as in (b).

(b) [Gauge functions and gauge equivalence] A **gauge function** of class $C^m$, $m\ge2$, on $\Omega\times I$ is a function $\chi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^m$ jointly; its **gauge transformation** sends a potential pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^m$ to

$$T_\chi(\varphi,A):=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+\nabla\chi),$$

a potential pair of class $C^{m-1}$. Two potential pairs are **gauge related** when one is the gauge transform of the other by some gauge function. On pairs and generators of class $C^\infty$, $T_0$ is the identity and $T_{\chi_1}\bigl(T_{\chi_2}(\varphi,A)\bigr)=T_{\chi_1+\chi_2}(\varphi,A)$ for all $C^\infty$ generators $\chi_1,\chi_2$; hence gauge relatedness is an equivalence relation on the $C^\infty$ potential pairs, the inverse of $T_\chi$ being $T_{-\chi}$. For a fixed finite class the transform drops one order, and relatedness is used only through the transform it records.

(c) [Conditions] A potential pair is **in Lorenz gauge** on $\Omega\times I$ when $G(\varphi,A)=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi=0$ throughout $\Omega\times I$, and **in Coulomb gauge** in the chosen spatial chart when $\operatorname{div}A=0$ throughout $\Omega\times I$. These are properties of a pair in the stated conventions. The existence of a gauge function achieving either condition, with or without prescribed initial or boundary data, is a separate PDE conclusion with its own hypotheses and is not asserted by this definition.

(d) [Physical status] The physical content of a representation is its field pair $(E,B)$ of [[def-em-fields]]; the values of $\varphi$, of $A$ and of any gauge function are convention dependent and are auxiliary, and gauge related representations have the same field pair. The scalar potential $\varphi$ carries the volt and the vector potential $A$ carries the tesla metre, consistently with [[def-em-si-conventions]]. No value of $\varphi$ or $A$ is by itself an observable or evidence for a field.

## Remarks

- **The composition identity is forced by linearity.** Componentwise, $\partial_t(\chi_1+\chi_2)=\partial_t\chi_1+\partial_t\chi_2$ and $\nabla(\chi_1+\chi_2)=\nabla\chi_1+\nabla\chi_2$, because partial derivatives are one-variable derivatives ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]) and differentiation is additive ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]); substituting into $T_{\chi_1}(T_{\chi_2}(\varphi,A))$ gives $T_{\chi_1+\chi_2}(\varphi,A)$. Reflexivity is $T_0=\mathrm{id}$, and symmetry is the inverse $T_{-\chi}$, with $\chi$ and $-\chi$ of the same class. No choice principle is used by the composition computation.
- **What is deliberately absent.** This is a vocabulary and bookkeeping definition: it draws no conclusion that a pair can be put in either gauge, no statement about prescribed boundary or initial data, and no Maxwell equation. The two gauge conditions are recorded as properties, not as achievable normal forms.
- **Signs and spelling.** The signs $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ and $\varphi-\partial_t\chi$ are the conventions of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]; a different sign convention would produce a different but equivalent calculus. *Lorenz* here refers to Ludvig Lorenz; the condition is the coordinate form of $\partial_\mu A^\mu=0$ under these conventions and is not a consequence of any field equation.

## Statement

Let $c>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]), let $k\ge2$ be an integer, let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ and let $\chi$ be a gauge function of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$, all in the conventions of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] and [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]: $E(\varphi,A)=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B(\varphi,A)=\operatorname{curl}A$ and $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+\nabla\chi)$; for a non-open $I$ the joint $C^k$ classes are read in the open-neighbourhood restriction convention of [[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]] (for open $I$ this is the ordinary class of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

Then $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is a potential pair of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ and its field pair is the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$:

$$E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=E(\varphi,A),\qquad B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=B(\varphi,A)\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I,$$

the common values being maps $\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly, that is, fields of the framework in the sense of [[def-em-fields]]. In particular gauge related potential representations of one field pair have equal field pairs: the electric and magnetic fields are gauge invariants of the framework, and no value of $\varphi$, of $A$ or of $\chi$ is asserted to be observable.

The proof uses only the defining formulas, the vanishing of $\operatorname{curl}\nabla\chi$ for the $C^2$ function $\chi$ and the equality of the time-space mixed partials $\partial_t\partial_i\chi=\partial_i\partial_t\chi$; no Maxwell equation, no hypothesis on $\Omega$ beyond openness, and no choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, an interval $I$ with at least two elements, $c>0$, an integer $k\ge2$, a jointly $C^k$ potential pair $(\varphi,A)$ and a jointly $C^k$ gauge function $\chi$ on $\Omega\times I$.

[F1] Potential-pair formulas: for a pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^m$, $m\ge1$, $E(\varphi,A)=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B(\varphi,A)=\operatorname{curl}A$ are of class $C^{m-1}$, the transform of a $C^m$ pair by a $C^m$ generator is $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,A+\nabla\chi)$ and is of class $C^{m-1}$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]); for a non-open $I$ the joint classes and the componentwise computations are read in the open-neighbourhood restriction convention of [[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]], whose relative time derivatives at included endpoints reproduce the two identities below pointwise on $\Omega\times I$.

[F2] Framework vocabulary: a potential representation of a field pair is a potential pair with that field pair, a gauge function of class $C^m$ has $m\ge2$, two pairs are gauge related when one is the gauge transform of the other, and the field pair of a representation is its physical content ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]).

[F3] Linearity of the curl: for $C^1$ fields $F,G$ and reals $\alpha,\beta$ one has $\operatorname{curl}(\alpha F+\beta G)=\alpha\operatorname{curl}F+\beta\operatorname{curl}G$ ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]).

[F4] For a $C^2$ scalar function $\chi$ the field $\nabla\chi$ is $C^1$ and $\operatorname{curl}\nabla\chi=0$ ([[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]]).

[F5] For a $C^2$ function on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$ the mixed coordinate partial derivatives commute, so $\partial_t\partial_i\chi=\partial_i\partial_t\chi$ for the jointly $C^2$ function $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]).

[F6] Differentiability and class bookkeeping: sums of totally differentiable maps are totally differentiable with the sum of the derivatives and a map is of class $C^m$ when all its componentwise iterated partial derivatives up to order $m$ exist and are continuous, partial derivatives being one-variable derivatives along coordinate lines ([[thm-algebra-of-total-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]).

[F7] The electric and magnetic fields of the framework are maps $\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ at fixed time, read in the frame basis with the stated regularity and polar/axial conventions ([[def-em-fields]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the two field formulas of the transformed pair and use the vanishing curl of a gradient and the commutativity of mixed partials.

1.1 The transformed pair and its class. The partial derivatives $\partial_t\chi$ and $\nabla\chi$ of the jointly $C^k$ function $\chi$ are jointly $C^{k-1}$, and the pair members $\varphi$ and $A$ are jointly $C^k$, hence jointly $C^{k-1}$; by the closure of the class under sums and the componentwise reading of [F6], the maps $\varphi-\partial_t\chi$ and $A+\nabla\chi$ are jointly $C^{k-1}$, so $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is a potential pair of class $C^{k-1}$ in the sense of [F1] and [F2]. Since $k-1\ge1$, its field pair is defined by [F1]. [given, F1, F2, F6]

1.2 Magnetic field. $\operatorname{curl}(A+\nabla\chi)=\operatorname{curl}A+\operatorname{curl}\nabla\chi$ by the linearity of the curl [F3]; the function $\chi$ is jointly $C^k$ with $k\ge2$, hence jointly $C^2$, so $\operatorname{curl}\nabla\chi=0$ by [F4]; therefore $B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=\operatorname{curl}(A+\nabla\chi)=\operatorname{curl}A=B(\varphi,A)$ on $\Omega\times I$. [given, F1, F3, F4]

1.3 Electric field. Expanding with the definitions of [F1] and the componentwise linearity of the total derivative for sums [F6], $E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=-\nabla(\varphi-\partial_t\chi)-\partial_t(A+\nabla\chi)=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA+\partial_t\nabla\chi-\nabla\partial_t\chi=E(\varphi,A)+(\partial_t\nabla\chi-\nabla\partial_t\chi)$. The bracket vanishes componentwise: its $i$-th component is $\partial_t\partial_i\chi-\partial_i\partial_t\chi$, and the jointly $C^2$ function $\chi$ has commuting mixed partials by [F5]. Hence $E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=E(\varphi,A)$ on $\Omega\times I$. [given, F1, F5, F6]

2.1 Conclusion. Step 1.1 shows that the transform is a potential pair of class $C^{k-1}$; steps 1.2 and 1.3 show that its magnetic and electric fields equal those of $(\varphi,A)$, and by [F1] both are jointly $C^{k-1}$, hence framework fields of the shape recorded in [F7]. Gauge relatedness of two pairs means exactly that one is the transform of the other by some gauge function [F2], so gauge related representations have equal field pairs, and the only physical content attached to a representation in [F2] is its field pair. No Maxwell equation, domain hypothesis beyond openness, or choice principle was used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, F1, F2, F7] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why $k\ge2$ and not $k\ge1$.** The scalar identity uses $\operatorname{curl}\nabla\chi=0$, which needs $\chi$ to be $C^2$, and the electric identity uses the symmetry of the second mixed partial of $\chi$. For a merely $C^1$ generator the two field expressions are still formally equal, but the intermediate quantities $\operatorname{curl}\nabla\chi$ and the mixed partials are then not defined.
- **No converse.** The theorem says gauge transformations do not change the fields. Which potential pairs represent the same field pair, and which gauge conditions are reachable, are separate questions treated elsewhere on this page.

## Statement

Let $c>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ in the restriction convention of [[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]] ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]): for open $I$ this is the ordinary open-domain class of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], and for non-open $I$ the pair is the restriction of a $C^2$ pair on an open neighbourhood of $\Omega\times I$, with relative derivatives at included endpoints and no time jet beyond the restricted values. Write $(E,B)$ for the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$ ([[def-em-fields]]) and

$$G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi,\qquad W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$$

for the Lorenz divergence and the wave expression of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], with $\Delta$ the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]. Let $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous source fields of the framework ([[def-em-sources]]).

(a) [Exact identities] Independently of any field equation,

$$\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+\nabla G\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$

Consequently the sourced Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold for $(E,B,\rho,J)$ if and only if

$$W\varphi-\partial_tG=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad WA+\nabla G=\mu_0J\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I,$$

with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ the constant of that postulate.

(b) [Gauge shift] If $\chi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ is a gauge function of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]), then $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi$ on $\Omega\times I$ and the transformed pair has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]); hence $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge if and only if $W\chi=G$ on $\Omega\times I$.

(c) [Decoupling in Lorenz gauge] Suppose in addition that the given pair is in Lorenz gauge, $G=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. Then its field pair solves the sourced Maxwell system of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] if and only if the pair satisfies the decoupled sourced wave equations

$$W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad WA=\mu_0J\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$

The two source-free equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ hold automatically for every potential pair of class $C^2$. For an arbitrary given potential pair, the conjunction of Lorenz gauge with these two wave equations implies the sourced Maxwell system, but Maxwell's equations alone do not impose $G=0$ on that representative: their exact equivalent conditions remain the residual equations of (a), whose right-hand sides retain $\partial_tG$ and $\nabla G$.

(d) [Residual generators] If $W\chi=0$ on $\Omega\times I$, then the transform of a pair in Lorenz gauge is again in Lorenz gauge and has the same field pair; hence the Lorenz condition does not determine the potential pair.

(e) [Scope] The identities and equivalences are properties of the given $C^2$ representation. No gauge function with $W\chi=G$, and no generator meeting prescribed initial or boundary values, is asserted to exist; that is a separate PDE conclusion with its own hypotheses, treated by the gauge-reachability theorem later on this page. No boundary, decay or initial condition on the pair is imposed, and no empirical claim or observability of $\varphi$ or $A$ is included. A pair of class $C^1$ defines $E$, $B$ and $G$ but need not possess the second derivatives appearing in $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\Delta$ or $\partial_tG$, so $C^2$ is the exact standing regularity here.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A constant $c>0$, an open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, an interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, a potential pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ in the restriction convention, its field pair $(E,B)$, the functions $G$ and $W$ displayed in the Statement, and continuous source fields $\rho,J$.

[F1] Potential-pair vocabulary: for a pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^m$, $m\ge1$, on an open set the electric and magnetic fields are $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ and are of class $C^{m-1}$; the Lorenz divergence is $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$, of class $C^{m-1}$; for $k\ge2$ the gauge transform of a class $C^k$ pair by a class $C^k$ function is $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+\nabla\chi)$, of class $C^{k-1}$; the wave expression is $Wu=c^{-2}\partial_t^2u-\Delta u$ for class $C^2$ scalar and componentwise vector arguments; a pair is in Lorenz gauge when $G=0$; the definition asserts no existence or solvability ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]).

[F2] Restriction convention for a possibly non-open time interval: joint $C^m$ regularity on $\Omega\times I$ means restriction of a $C^m$ map on an open neighbourhood of $\Omega\times I$ in $\mathbb R^4$, spatial identities hold at every point of $\Omega\times I$ and time derivatives at included endpoints are the relative one-sided derivatives of the restriction; for open $I$ this is the ordinary class ([[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]]).

[F3] Framework vocabulary: $E$ and $B$ are the fixed-time spatial fields of the framework with the stated regularity and the polar/axial convention ([[def-em-fields]]); a smooth source field $(\rho,J)$ consists of maps continuous on $\Omega\times I$ and of class $C^1$ wherever a displayed equation differentiates them ([[def-em-sources]]).

[F4] Linearity and algebra of derivatives: for $C^1$ fields $F,H$ on an open set and reals $\alpha,\beta$, $\operatorname{div}(\alpha F+\beta H)=\alpha\operatorname{div}F+\beta\operatorname{div}H$ and $\operatorname{curl}(\alpha F+\beta H)=\alpha\operatorname{curl}F+\beta\operatorname{curl}H$; partial derivatives are one-variable derivatives along coordinate lines and obey the sum and product rules componentwise ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]).

[F5] Clairaut--Schwarz: mixed coordinate partial derivatives of a $C^2$ function on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$ commute, so for the jointly $C^2$ functions $\varphi$, $A$ and $\chi$ the identities $\partial_t\partial_i=\partial_i\partial_t$ hold componentwise and $\partial_i\partial_j=\partial_j\partial_i$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]).

[F6] Vector identity and Laplacian: for a $C^2$ field $F$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$, $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}F=\nabla\operatorname{div}F-\Delta F$, and $\Delta F$ is the componentwise Laplacian defined by $\Delta f=\operatorname{div}\nabla f=\sum_i\partial_i\partial_if$ ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]).

[F7] Automatic source-free identities: for a $C^2$ field $F$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ one has $\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}F=0$, and for a $C^2$ scalar $f$ one has $\operatorname{curl}\nabla f=0$ ([[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]], [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]]).

[F8] The adopted microscopic vacuum Maxwell equations in their smooth branch: for jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation and continuous sources, $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$, with $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$ and $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ ([[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]).

[F9] Gauge invariance: if $(\varphi,A)$ is a potential pair of class $C^k$ jointly with $k\ge2$ and $\chi$ a gauge function of class $C^k$ jointly, then $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ has the same field pair as $(\varphi,A)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]], [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; expand the two second-order combinations of $E$ and $B$ defined by the potential formulas with the linearity, mixed-partial and curl-of-curl identities, then compare the resulting equations with the sourced postulate and expand the gauge transform of $G$.

1.1 Regularity bookkeeping. The pair $(\varphi,A)$ is $C^2$, so by [F1] the field pair $(E,B)$ and the Lorenz divergence $G$ are of class $C^1$ and the expressions $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\partial_tG$ and $\nabla G$ are defined and continuous on $\Omega\times I$; at included endpoints of a non-open $I$ all derivatives are those of the restriction convention [F2]. Hence both identities displayed in (a) are equalities of continuous functions on $\Omega\times I$. [given, F1, F2]

2.1 First identity. By [F1] and the linearity of the divergence [F4], $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}(-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA)=-\operatorname{div}\nabla\varphi-\operatorname{div}\partial_tA$. The definition of the Laplacian [F6] gives $\operatorname{div}\nabla\varphi=\Delta\varphi$, and the componentwise commutation of the time and space partial derivatives of the $C^2$ field $A$ [F5] gives $\operatorname{div}\partial_tA=\partial_t\operatorname{div}A$. On the other hand, expanding $G$ [F1] and using the linearity of $\partial_t$ and of $\Delta$ [F4] with [F5], $W\varphi-\partial_tG=(c^{-2}\partial_t^2\varphi-\Delta\varphi)-(\partial_t\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t^2\varphi)=-\Delta\varphi-\partial_t\operatorname{div}A$. The two right-hand sides agree, so $\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG$ on $\Omega\times I$. [step 1.1, F1, F4, F5, F6]

2.2 Second identity. By [F1] and the linearity of the curl and of $\partial_t$ [F4], $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\nabla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A$. The curl-of-curl identity [F6] rewrites the first term as $\nabla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A$; the componentwise commutation [F5] for the $C^2$ function $\varphi$ rewrites $c^{-2}\partial_t\nabla\varphi$ as $c^{-2}\nabla\partial_t\varphi=\nabla(c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi)$; and the last term is one of the two summands of $WA$ [F1]. Collecting terms, $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=(\nabla\operatorname{div}A+\nabla(c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi))+(c^{-2}\partial_t^2A-\Delta A)=\nabla G+WA$ by the linearity of $\nabla$ [F4] and the definition of $G$, that is $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+\nabla G$ on $\Omega\times I$. [step 1.1, F1, F4, F5, F6]

2.3 Automatic source-free equations. For the potential pair, $\operatorname{div}B=\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}A=0$ by [F7], and $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}(-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA)=-\operatorname{curl}\nabla\varphi-\operatorname{curl}\partial_tA$ by linearity [F4]; the first term vanishes by [F7] applied to the $C^2$ function $\varphi$, and the second equals $\partial_t\operatorname{curl}A=\partial_tB$ by the componentwise commutation [F5], so $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ on $\Omega\times I$. [step 1.1, F1, F4, F5, F7]

2.4 Gauge shift and the Lorenz condition. Let $\chi$ be a gauge function of class $C^2$ jointly. By [F1] the transform $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+\nabla\chi)$ is a potential pair of class $C^1$, so its Lorenz divergence is defined; expanding it with the linearity of $\operatorname{div}$ [F4] and the definitions [F1], $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=\operatorname{div}A+\operatorname{div}\nabla\chi+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi-c^{-2}\partial_t^2\chi=G+\Delta\chi-c^{-2}\partial_t^2\chi=G-W\chi$, the middle identity using $\operatorname{div}\nabla\chi=\Delta\chi$ [F6] and the last the definition of $W$ [F1]. Thus $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=0$ if and only if $W\chi=G$ on $\Omega\times I$; and the field pair is unchanged by [F9], so the transformed pair represents the same $(E,B)$ of [F3]. [step 1.1, F1, F4, F6, F9]

3.1 Equivalence with the sourced system. By [F8] the sourced Maxwell equations for $(E,B,\rho,J)$ are the four identities $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ on $\Omega\times I$; the pair $(E,B)$ is of class $C^1$ by step 1.1 with all derivatives required by those equations existing and continuous, and $\rho,J$ are continuous by [F3]. The second and third identities hold identically by step 2.3. The first is equivalent, by step 2.1, to $W\varphi-\partial_tG=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, and the fourth is equivalent, by step 2.2, to $WA+\nabla G=\mu_0J$. Hence the sourced Maxwell equations hold for $(E,B,\rho,J)$ if and only if the two residual equations of (a) hold. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, F3, F8]

3.2 Residual generators. If in addition to $G=0$ the gauge function satisfies $W\chi=0$ on $\Omega\times I$, then step 2.4 gives $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi=0$, so the transformed pair is again in Lorenz gauge, and by [F9] it has the same field pair; consequently distinct pairs in Lorenz gauge can represent the same $(E,B)$ of [F3], and the Lorenz condition does not determine the pair. [step 2.4, F9]

4.1 Decoupling under the Lorenz condition. Assume additionally $G=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. Then the $C^1$ function $G$ has $\partial_tG=0$ and $\nabla G=0$ on $\Omega\times I$ by [F4], so the residual equations of step 3.1 read $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$ there; conversely, if these two wave equations hold then the residual equations hold and, by step 3.1, the sourced Maxwell system holds for the pair. This equivalence is asserted only under the explicitly imposed hypothesis $G=0$: for a general representative the equivalent conditions are the residual equations of step 3.1, which contain the derivatives $\partial_tG$ and $\nabla G$ of the representative's own Lorenz divergence, and no step infers $G=0$ from the Maxwell equations. [step 2.3, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Conclusion and scope. Step 2.1 and step 2.2 give the exact pointwise identities of (a), and step 3.1 identifies the two residual equations with the sourced Maxwell system; step 2.3 records the two automatic source-free equations. Step 2.4 gives the gauge shift and the equivalence of the Lorenz condition for the transform with $W\chi=G$; step 4.1 gives the decoupling inside $G=0$, with the explicit warning that Maxwell alone does not impose that condition; and step 3.2 gives the residual generators. Throughout, no existence of a solution of $W\chi=G$ or of a generator with prescribed data is asserted, no boundary, decay or initial condition is imposed, and $C^2$ is the exact standing regularity: for a merely $C^1$ pair the expressions $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\Delta$ and $\partial_tG$ of the Statement need not exist. No choice principle is used, and no hypothesis is made on the shape of $\Omega$ beyond openness. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.1, step 2.4, step 4.1, step 3.2, F1, F2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Direction of the gauge statement.** The identities of (a) hold with no field equation at all. The hypothesis $G=0$ in (c) is an extra condition on the representative; the theorem never claims that every pair can be brought to Lorenz gauge, only that *if* $G=0$ then the sourced system is exactly the two decoupled wave equations, and that a gauge generator can enforce $G=0$ only under the separate hypotheses of the reachability theorem on this page.
- **Constant bookkeeping.** The identity $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+\nabla G$ produces the two Maxwell source constants directly: comparing with [F8] gives $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$ in Lorenz gauge with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, so no separate factor is introduced anywhere.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in branch (a), and the Axiom of Choice together with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as declared by its weak-solvability lemmas in branch (b) ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $c>0$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of the framework ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ and Lorenz divergence $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$.

(a) [All-space slab; Lorenz gauge] Let $t_0<T$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ (the restriction of a $C^\infty$ pair on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ with $\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $W\chi=G$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$; the transformed pair $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, has the same field pair $(E,B)$, and any two such gauge functions differ by a solution of $W\chi=0$. This is the exact content of [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] read for potential pairs of the framework; its physical content is that every smooth potential representation of a field pair on a slab admits a Lorenz-gauge representative with zero gauge Cauchy data at $t_0$, without changing the fields.

(b) [Bounded smooth domain; Coulomb gauge with admissible boundary families] Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ graph domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an arbitrary interval, possibly unbounded, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be $C^\infty$ on an actual neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$. Prescribe either (i) a Dirichlet family $g_D(p,t)$ smooth in boundary charts on a neighbourhood of $\partial\Omega\times\overline I$, or (ii) an outward conormal family $\kappa(p,t)$ with the same smoothness and the compatibility $\int_{\Omega_j}\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A(\cdot,t)\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)\,dS=0$ for every connected component $\Omega_j$ of $\Omega$ and every $t\in I$. Then there is a gauge generator $\psi$, the restriction of one $C^\infty$ function on an actual open neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$, such that $\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. In case (i), $\psi(p,t)=g_D(p,t)$ on $\partial\Omega\times I$, and its restriction to $\Omega\times I$ is unique with those Dirichlet values. In case (ii), $\varepsilon_0\partial_\nu\psi(p,t)=\kappa(p,t)$ there, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}\psi(\cdot,t)\,dx=0$ for every component and every $t$ gives a unique generator on $\Omega\times I$; without that normalization it is unique modulo smooth time-dependent spatial constants on each component. The transformed pair $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge and has the same physical field pair ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Any two Coulomb-gauge generators differ by a function spatially harmonic at every $t$; equal Dirichlet data eliminate that residual freedom, whereas equal Neumann data leave only the componentwise constants just described. Zero Dirichlet data are the corresponding special case. Auxiliary ambient continuations away from the physical region need not be unique.

(c) [Residual freedom on star-shaped domains] Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $(\varphi,A)$, $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)$ be two potential pairs of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-interval]]) with the same field pair, both in Lorenz gauge. If $I$ is non-open, these $C^2$ classes and the resulting generator use the open-neighbourhood restriction convention of [[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]]; for the physical open laboratory interval they have their ordinary $C^2$ meaning. If a degenerate $I$ is used in this branch, choose the ambient $C^2$ extensions as part of the data: the same-field and Lorenz conditions refer to these extensions on an ambient time neighbourhood before restriction, and their time jets are not determined uniquely by the restricted values alone. Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^2$ jointly with $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)=T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ and $W\chi=0$ on $\Omega\times I$.

(d) [Scope] Nothing is asserted about gauge functions meeting arbitrary prescribed boundary or initial restrictions: in (a) the gauge function has zero Cauchy data at $t_0$ and no spatial boundary condition or decay, and $\Omega$ is all of $\mathbb R^3$; in (b) the datum is either a smooth time-dependent Dirichlet family or a smooth outward conormal family satisfying the stated componentwise compatibility at every physical time, with zero-mean normalization for Neumann uniqueness; the older promise of a global Lorenz gauge on a bounded domain with prescribed boundary data is explicitly outside this result. The Coulomb-gauge statement concerns the spatial divergence in the chosen inertial chart, and the instantaneous appearance of the Coulomb potential is a property of the representation, not a signal: only the field pair $(E,B)$ is physical content ([[def-em-fields]]).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A constant $c>0$; a potential pair $(\varphi,A)$ of the framework with field pair $(E,B)$ and Lorenz divergence $G$; in branch (a) times $t_0<T$ and the joint class hypotheses of the Statement; in branch (b) a bounded $C^\infty$ graph domain $\Omega$, an interval $I$, the potentials on a neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$, and one of the two boundary families with its compatibility; in branch (c) an open star-shaped $\Omega$, an interval $I$, and two $C^2$ pairs $(\varphi,A)$, $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)$ with the same field pair and both in Lorenz gauge. The choice assumptions of the two branches are as stated.

[F1] Potential-pair vocabulary: $E(\varphi,A)=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B(\varphi,A)=\operatorname{curl}A$, $G(\varphi,A)=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$, $Wu=c^{-2}\partial_t^2u-\Delta u$, the gauge transform $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+\nabla\chi)$ of a class $C^m$ pair by a class $C^m$ generator with $m\ge2$ is a class $C^{m-1}$ pair, a pair is in Lorenz gauge when $G=0$ and in Coulomb gauge when $\operatorname{div}A=0$, and the definition asserts no solvability ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-gauge-transformation]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]).

[F2] Framework vocabulary: the fields $E,B$ are the fixed-time spatial fields of the framework with the stated regularity, and the physical content of a representation is its field pair ([[def-em-fields]]).

[F3] Gauge invariance: for a potential pair and a gauge function of class $C^k$ jointly with $k\ge2$, the transform has the same field pair as the original pair ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]).

[F4] Gauge shift of the Lorenz divergence: for a class $C^2$ pair and a class $C^2$ generator, $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G(\varphi,A)-W\chi$ on the region of definition ([[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]]).

[F5] Slab reachability ([[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]]): under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, for a potential pair of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on the slab $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense with $\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $W\chi=G$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$ (a); the transformed pair is of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense with $E,B$ unchanged (b); it is in Lorenz gauge (c); and any two functions of class $C^2$ in the extension sense with $W\chi_1=W\chi_2=G$ satisfy $W(\chi_1-\chi_2)=0$ (d). No spatial boundary condition, decay or cavity statement is included.

[F6] Parameter-dependent smooth solvers (the pure-mathematical supplier `lem-em-parameter-dependent-smooth-poisson-boundary-solvers` on the wave-equation prerequisites page, quoted here at its declared scaffold interface): under AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ carried by its variational and Sobolev suppliers, for a bounded smooth graph domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, a constant $\epsilon>0$ and an open interval $J$, and for a bulk datum $f$ jointly smooth up to $\overline\Omega\times J$ and boundary families $g_D$, $\kappa$ smooth in a fixed finite boundary atlas times $J$: the Dirichlet problem $-\epsilon\Delta u=f$, $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g_D$ has a unique solution on $\Omega\times J$, the restriction of a single smooth ambient function on a neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times J$; the Neumann problem $-\epsilon\Delta u=f$, $\epsilon\partial_\nu u=\kappa$ has such a solution precisely when $\int_{\Omega_j}f(\cdot,t)+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)=0$ for each component and every $t\in J$, is unique modulo a separately chosen spatial constant on each component at each time, and its zero-mean normalization $\int_{\Omega_j}u(\cdot,t)=0$ gives a unique smooth family; both operations are linear in their data, time differentiation commutes with them, smoothness and estimates are local in compact time subintervals, and the ambient continuations are auxiliary and not unique off the closed spatial domain. This interface is established from [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]], [[lem-em-zero-boundary-coercivity]], [[thm-higher-order-boundary-regularity-for-dirichlet-problems]] and [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]], whose choice assumptions it carries.

[F7] First Green identity ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]): under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, for a bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega$ and real $u\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$, $v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, $\int_\Omega(v\Delta u+\nabla u\cdot\nabla v)\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}v\,\partial_\nu u\,dS$.

[F8] Radial witnesses ([[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]]): on an open star-shaped $\Omega$ with centre $a$ and an interval $I$, for a jointly $C^2$ field $C$ with $\operatorname{curl}C(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$, the negative radial integral $\phi_C(x,t)=-\int_0^1\langle C(a+s(x-a),t),x-a\rangle\,ds$ is jointly $C^2$ with $\nabla\phi_C(\cdot,t)=-C(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$; the proof constructs both witnesses as restrictions of $C^2$ functions on an open radial-admissibility neighbourhood of $\Omega\times I$; the same open-neighbourhood restriction convention governs non-open $I$.

[F9] Calculus and topology toolkit: mixed partial derivatives of $C^2$ functions commute ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]); the divergence and curl are linear and computed from first partial derivatives ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); the chain rule, the sum and product rules for partial derivatives and the componentwise $C^k$ class hold ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); a continuous function on an interval with vanishing derivative at every interior point is constant, with the second form for functions with a common derivative ([[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]]); the oriented integral $x\mapsto\int_{t_*}^x h$ of a continuous $h$ on an interval with at least two elements is a primitive of $h$ ([[cor-primitives-of-a-continuous-function]], [[def-oriented-integral]]); star-shapedness is the radial-segment condition ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]); and the intervals and the bounded graph-domain charts are those of [[def-interval]] and [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]].

[F10] Choice assumptions: the formulations of the Axiom of Choice and of Countable Choice used in the branches ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]), and the Sobolev spaces $H^1$, $H_0^1$ with the $W^{k,p}$ norm convention ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; branch (a) is the slab lemma read for framework pairs; branch (b) applies the parameter-dependent Poisson solver to the corrected datum and identifies two generators through the Green identity; branch (c) constructs the gauge generator from the radial scalar witness and a time primitive.

1.1 Branch (a). The pair $(\varphi,A)$ satisfies the hypotheses of [F5] verbatim: it is of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on the slab and $G$ is its Lorenz divergence, with $E,B$ its field pair in the vocabulary of [F1] and [F2]. By [F5](a) there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense with $\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $W\chi=G$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$; by [F5](b) the transformed pair has the same $E$ and $B$, and by [F5](c) it is in Lorenz gauge because $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi=0$ there; by [F5](d) two such gauge functions differ by a solution of $W\chi=0$. The countable-choice assumption is carried by [F5]. This is exactly assertion (a). [given, F1, F2, F5, F10]

1.2 Branch (b): data class and an open time interval. Let $N$ be the actual neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$ on which $(\varphi,A)$ is $C^\infty$, and let $N_\partial$ be a neighbourhood of $\partial\Omega\times\overline I$ on which the chosen boundary family is smooth in boundary charts. Since $\overline\Omega$ is compact ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), the set of times $t$ for which a product neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times\{t\}$ is contained in $N$ is open in $\mathbb R$, and it contains $\overline I$; let $J$ be its connected component containing $I$, and likewise choose $J_\partial$ for $N_\partial$ and replace $J$ by $J\cap J_\partial$. Then $J\supseteq\overline I$ is an open interval, and the potentials, the bulk datum $F:=\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A$ and the chosen boundary family are smooth on $\overline\Omega\times J$ and in its boundary atlas times $J$, in the sense required by [F6]; the derivative bounds below use only $\overline\Omega\times K$ with compact $K\subset J$, never compactness of all of $\overline I$. If $I$ is empty then $\Omega\times I$ is empty and the conclusions of (b) are vacuous; the construction below therefore assumes $I$ nonempty. [given, F9, F10]

1.3 Branch (c): the difference of two representations. Assume first that $I$ has at least two elements, and put $\delta\varphi:=\tilde\varphi-\varphi$ and $\delta A:=\tilde A-A$, which are jointly $C^2$ on $\Omega\times I$ in the convention of [F8]. Equality of the field pairs gives, by the componentwise linearity of $\nabla$, $\partial_t$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ [F9], $\operatorname{curl}\delta A=B(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)-B(\varphi,A)=0$ and $\nabla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\delta A=-E(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)+E(\varphi,A)=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. Both pairs being in Lorenz gauge means $G(\varphi,A)=G(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. [given, F1, F9]

2.1 Branch (b), Dirichlet case. Apply [F6] with $\epsilon=\varepsilon_0>0$ and bulk datum $F=\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A$ on the open interval $J$, and with the Dirichlet family $g_D$; the data are smooth in the required sense by step 1.2. This gives a unique solution $\psi$ on $\Omega\times J$, the restriction of one $C^\infty$ ambient function on a neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times J$, with $-\varepsilon_0\Delta\psi=F$ on $\Omega\times J$ and $\psi=g_D$ on $\partial\Omega\times J$. On $\Omega\times I\subseteq\Omega\times J$ we get $\Delta\psi=-\operatorname{div}A$ (since $\varepsilon_0>0$), hence $\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)=\operatorname{div}A+\operatorname{div}\nabla\psi=\operatorname{div}A+\Delta\psi=0$ by the definitions [F1]; on $\partial\Omega\times I$, $\psi=g_D$. Therefore $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge on $\Omega\times I$ and, by [F3], has the same field pair as $(\varphi,A)$. [step 1.2, F1, F3, F6, F9]

2.2 Branch (b), Neumann case. Let $\Omega_j$ be a connected component of $\Omega$ and define, for $t\in J$, $c_j(t):=\int_{\Omega_j}F(\cdot,t)\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)\,dS$. The bulk integral is a parameter integral of the smooth family $F$ over the fixed compact set $\overline\Omega_j$, and the boundary integral is a finite sum of chart parameter integrals of the smooth family $\kappa$ over the fixed boundary atlas, so $c_j$ is $C^\infty$ on $J$ by differentiation under the integral sign; the compatibility hypothesis gives $c_j(t)=0$ for $t\in I$. Put $\widehat F:=F-c_j(t)/|\Omega_j|$ on each $\Omega_j$. Then $\widehat F$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline\Omega\times J$, $\widehat F=F$ on $\Omega\times I$, and for every $t\in J$ and component $\Omega_j$, $\int_{\Omega_j}\widehat F(\cdot,t)+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)=\int_{\Omega_j}F(\cdot,t)-c_j(t)+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)=0$, so the compatibility required by [F6] holds throughout $J$. Apply [F6] with the zero-mean normalization on each component and the datum $(\widehat F,\kappa)$: this gives a unique normalized solution $\psi$ on $\Omega\times J$, the restriction of one smooth ambient function, with $-\varepsilon_0\Delta\psi=\widehat F$ on $\Omega\times J$ and $\varepsilon_0\partial_\nu\psi=\kappa$ on $\partial\Omega\times J$. On $\Omega\times I$ we have $\Delta\psi=-\operatorname{div}A$ as before, hence $\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)=0$; on $\partial\Omega\times I$, $\varepsilon_0\partial_\nu\psi=\kappa$. Hence $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge on $\Omega\times I$ with the same field pair by [F3]. [step 1.2, F1, F3, F6, F9]

2.3 Branch (c): the radial scalar witness. By step 1.3 the field $\delta A$ is jointly $C^2$ on the open star-shaped $\Omega$ times the interval $I$ and satisfies $\operatorname{curl}\delta A(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$; the scalar clause of [F8] applied with $C=\delta A$ gives the jointly $C^2$ function $\chi_0:=-\phi_{\delta A}$, that is $\chi_0(x,t)=\int_0^1\langle\delta A(a+s(x-a),t),\,x-a\rangle\,ds$, with $\nabla\chi_0(\cdot,t)=\delta A(\cdot,t)$ for every $t\in I$, and $\chi_0(a,t)=0$ for every $t\in I$. The construction is the radial one of that lemma, so $\chi_0$ is the restriction of a $C^2$ function on an open radial-admissibility neighbourhood of $\Omega\times I$. [step 1.3, F8, F9]

3.1 Branch (b): uniqueness and residual freedom. Let $\psi'$ be any other generator of the statement's class on $\Omega\times I$: it is $C^\infty$ near $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$, and on $\Omega\times I$ it satisfies $\Delta\psi'=-\operatorname{div}A$ as well as the same boundary data in the relevant case. Then $\chi:=\psi'-\psi$ is $C^\infty$ near $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$ and $\Delta\chi(\cdot,t)=0$ on $\Omega$ for every $t\in I$, i.e. $\chi$ is spatially harmonic at every $t$; this proves the general residual sentence. Fix $t\in I$ and apply Green's identity [F7] on $\Omega$ with $u=v=\chi(\cdot,t)$: $\int_\Omega(\chi\Delta\chi+|\nabla\chi|^2)\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}\chi\,\partial_\nu\chi\,dS$, whose right-hand side vanishes in the Dirichlet case because $\chi=0$ on $\partial\Omega$ (both generators have the value $g_D$) and in the Neumann case because $\partial_\nu\chi=0$ (both have conormal datum $\kappa/\varepsilon_0$); the first term vanishes because $\Delta\chi=0$, so $\int_\Omega|\nabla\chi(\cdot,t)|^2=0$ and hence $\nabla\chi(\cdot,t)=0$ on $\Omega$ (the integrand is continuous and nonnegative). Therefore $\chi(\cdot,t)$ is constant on each connected component of $\Omega$; in the Dirichlet case the constant is the boundary value of $\chi$, which is zero, so $\chi(\cdot,t)=0$ and $\psi'=\psi$ on $\Omega\times I$; in the Neumann case the constants are the only freedom, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}\psi'(\cdot,t)=\int_{\Omega_j}\psi(\cdot,t)=0$ makes each of them zero. This proves uniqueness with the stated data, the componentwise constant freedom without normalization, and the elimination of the residual freedom by equal Dirichlet data. The Green identity carries its own $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypothesis, already assumed in branch (b). [step 2.1, step 2.2, F7, F9]

3.2 Branch (c): the auxiliary scalar has zero gradient. By [F9] the mixed partials of the jointly $C^2$ function $\chi_0$ commute, so $\partial_t\nabla\chi_0=\nabla\partial_t\chi_0$ componentwise; by step 2.3 and the identity $\nabla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\delta A=0$ of step 1.3, $\nabla(\delta\varphi+\partial_t\chi_0)=\nabla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\nabla\chi_0=\nabla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\delta A=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. [step 1.3, step 2.3, F9]

4.1 Branch (c): the auxiliary scalar is position independent. Fix $t\in I$. The function $x\mapsto g(x,t):=\delta\varphi(x,t)+\partial_t\chi_0(x,t)$ is $C^1$ on $\Omega$ with $\nabla g(\cdot,t)=0$ by step 3.2, and $\Omega$ is star-shaped with centre $a$, so for $x\in\Omega$ the radial path $s\mapsto g(a+s(x-a),t)$ is defined on $[0,1]$ and, by the chain rule [F9], has derivative $\langle\nabla g(a+s(x-a),t),x-a\rangle=0$ at every interior point; the zero-derivative corollary [F9] applied on $[0,1]$ makes it constant, so $g(x,t)=g(a,t)$ for every $x\in\Omega$. In particular the common value depends on $t$ only. [step 3.2, F9]

5.1 Branch (c): construction of the gauge generator. Assume first that $I$ is open, and put $h(t):=g(a,t)=\delta\varphi(a,t)+\partial_t\chi_0(a,t)$ for $t\in I$; since $\chi_0(a,t)=0$ for every $t$, step 2.3 gives $h(t)=\delta\varphi(a,t)$, a $C^1$ function of $t$ on the open interval $I$. By [F9] the function $\eta(t):=-\int_{t_*}^t h(u)\,du$, with a fixed $t_*\in I$, is a primitive of $-h$ on $I$, hence $C^2$ because $h$ is $C^1$, and $\eta$ is independent of $x$. Put $\chi:=\chi_0+\eta$ on $\Omega\times I$, which is jointly $C^2$ there. Then $\nabla\chi=\nabla\chi_0=\delta A$ by step 2.3, and $\partial_t\chi=\partial_t\chi_0-h$; since $h(t)=g(x,t)=\delta\varphi(x,t)+\partial_t\chi_0(x,t)$ for every $x$ by step 4.1, this reads $\partial_t\chi=-\delta\varphi$. Hence $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+\nabla\chi)=(\varphi+\delta\varphi,\ A+\delta A)=(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)$ on $\Omega\times I$. For a non-open interval $I$ the same construction is performed with the ambient $C^2$ extensions supplied by the restriction convention of [F8]: $\chi_0$ is already a restriction from an open radial-admissibility set, the common value admits the ambient $C^1$ representative $t\mapsto\tilde\varphi(a,t)-\varphi(a,t)+\partial_t\chi_0(a,t)$ on an open time interval around $I$, its primitive is added to $\chi_0$ inside that neighbourhood, and the resulting function is a $C^2$ restriction whose values on $\Omega\times I$ satisfy the two displayed identities by the same pointwise computation. [step 2.3, step 4.1, F8, F9]

6.1 Branch (c): the generator has vanishing wave expression. The pair $(\varphi,A)$ is jointly $C^2$ and the generator $\chi$ of step 5.1 is jointly $C^2$, so the gauge-shift identity [F4] applies and gives $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G(\varphi,A)-W\chi$ on $\Omega\times I$. By step 5.1 $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)$, and both pairs are in Lorenz gauge by step 1.3, so $0=0-W\chi$, that is $W\chi=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. [step 1.3, step 5.1, F1, F4]

7.1 Branch (c): degenerate and empty intervals. If $I=\varnothing$, then $\Omega\times I=\varnothing$ and the assertion is vacuous: there are no points at which an identity is required. If $I=\{t_0\}$ is a singleton, then by the convention stated in (c) the ambient $C^2$ extensions and the same-field and Lorenz conditions on an ambient open time neighbourhood $J\ni t_0$ are part of the data; apply the construction of step 1.3 and steps 5.1 and 6.1 with $I$ replaced by $J$ (a nondegenerate open interval) and restrict the resulting generator, its transform identity and $W\chi=0$ to $\Omega\times\{t_0\}$. This covers every degenerate case and completes (c). [step 1.3, step 5.1, step 6.1, F9]

8.1 Scope and conclusion. Step 2.1 and step 2.2 construct the required Coulomb generators in the two declared boundary families, and step 3.1 proves the uniqueness clauses and the residual classification, so (b) is complete up to the auxiliary non-uniqueness of ambient continuations recorded in [F6]. Step 1.1 is (a). Step 1.3 and steps 4.1 through 7.1 construct, for two Lorenz $C^2$ representations of one field pair on a star-shaped domain, a $C^2$ gauge generator with $W\chi=0$, completing (c). Nothing in the branches asserts a gauge function meeting arbitrary prescribed boundary or initial restrictions: in (a) the gauge Cauchy data are zero and the spatial domain is all of $\mathbb R^3$; in (b) the boundary family and its compatibility are those stated; and the instantaneous character of the Coulomb potential is a property of the chosen representation, since by [F2] only the field pair $(E,B)$ is physical content. The Axiom of Countable Choice is used in (a) through [F5] and in (b) through [F6] and [F7]; the full Axiom of Choice is used in (b) through [F6] and its Sobolev suppliers. No empirical claim is made anywhere. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 7.1, F2, F5, F6, F7] ∎

## Remarks

- **What "reachability" does and does not mean here.** The two branches solve the specific PDE problems of their declared data; they do not assert that every pair can be brought to a named gauge with arbitrary data. In particular the all-space branch fixes zero gauge Cauchy data at $t_0$, and the bounded branch controls the boundary family but not initial gauge data; the older global promise for a bounded domain with prescribed data is outside the statement.
- **Choice accounting.** Branch (a) carries only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, through the free-space wave solution. Branch (b) carries AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, declared by the variational, chart and Sobolev suppliers of [F6]; the Green identity [F7] also assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Branch (c) uses no choice principle: its construction is the explicit radial witness and a one-variable primitive.
- **Open supplier obligations.** The quantitative bounds and the ambient-continuation construction of branch (b) are consumed through the interface of `lem-em-parameter-dependent-smooth-poisson-boundary-solvers`, whose carrier on the wave-equation prerequisites page is still to be authored at the time of this item's writing; the use of that supplier in steps 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1 is conditional on its completed statement matching the interface quoted in [F6].
