## Statement

Assume the constant isotropic inertial-rest material branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] with $\varepsilon,\mu>0$, $\sigma\ge0$, $D=\varepsilon E$, $H=B/\mu$, $J_{\rm ext}=0$. The exact broadband physical reading additionally requires $\varepsilon\mu\ge c^{-2}$ as in that closure; otherwise the positive coefficients define its finite-band effective phase model without a universal front-speed claim. Put $v^2=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}$ and $\gamma=\sigma/\varepsilon$. The smooth equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] with initially zero volume charge give $E_t=v^2\operatorname{curl}B-\gamma E$, $B_t=-\operatorname{curl}E$ and zero divergences; in the finite-energy classes below these first-order equations with the declared PEC weak/variational boundary realization are adopted explicitly, rather than deduced from a smooth-only postulate. The quadratic stored energy is $\mathcal U(t)=\tfrac12(\varepsilon\|E(t)\|_2^2+\mu^{-1}\|B(t)\|_2^2)$, consistent with [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]].
(a) [Rectangular cavity] In the exact zero-normal-$B$ reflection-parity and divergence class of [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] and [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]](c), every initial pair has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ distributional solution of this damped system in the same class. Finite Fourier mode sums converge in energy norm uniformly on compact time intervals and are dense at every time. The Fourier coefficient equations at $k_j=\pi n_j/L_j$ are $\widehat E_t=iv^2 k\times\widehat B-\gamma\widehat E$, $\widehat B_t=-ik\times\widehat E$, with both transverse constraints and the original parities retained.
(b) [Smooth closed PEC cavity] Assume the full Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the smooth spectral and elliptic suppliers. On a bounded smooth cavity $\Omega$, let $X,V,H$ and its smooth orthonormal eigenfields $u_j$, $\lambda_j\ge0$, be exactly [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] and [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]]. Define the full weak normal-zero divergence-free magnetic space $$M:=\{B\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\int_\Omega B\cdot\nabla\psi=0\text{ for every smooth scalar }\psi\text{ on }\overline\Omega\}.$$ This is the distributional divergence constraint together with weak zero normal flux; for smooth fields it is $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $n\cdot B=0$. For every positive eigenvalue put $w_j=\operatorname{curl}u_j/\sqrt{\lambda_j}$ and put $K_M=\{B\in M:\operatorname{curl}B=0\text{ distributionally}\}$. Then $$M=\overline{\operatorname{span}\{w_j:\lambda_j>0\}}^{L^2}\mathbin{\oplus}K_M.$$ The declared first-order PEC modal energy class is $H\times M$, with weak modal equations $a_j'=v^2\sqrt{\lambda_j}b_j-\gamma a_j$, $b_j'=-\sqrt{\lambda_j}a_j$ for positive modes, $a_j'=-\gamma a_j$ for electric zero modes, and $(B,K_M)'=0$ for every kernel test. Define $D_M$ as the graph-norm completion of finite $w_j$ sums plus $K_M$, with norm squared $\|w\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{curl}w\|_2^2$. The equivalent weak-in-time variational equations are $\langle E_t,\phi\rangle=v^2\langle B,\operatorname{curl}\phi\rangle-\gamma\langle E,\phi\rangle$ for $\phi\in V$, and $\langle B_t,\psi\rangle=-\langle E,\operatorname{curl}\psi\rangle$ for $\psi\in D_M$. They use the actual electric tangential-zero domain $V$ and magnetic normal-zero space $M$, with no claim of maximal-trace equality. For every initial pair in $H\times M$ there is a unique $C(\mathbb R;H\times M)$ solution of that declared realization, which also satisfies the displayed evolution equations distributionally in the interior. Finite electric and paired-magnetic modal sums, with the exact static magnetic kernel component retained, converge uniformly on compact time intervals in energy norm. No equality with every maximal rough tangential-trace realization is asserted.
(c) [Exact energy balance, decay and zero sectors] In both declared classes, for every $t_0<t_1$, $$\mathcal U(t_1)+\sigma\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\|E(t)\|_2^2\,dt=\mathcal U(t_0),\qquad \mathcal U'(t)=-\sigma\|E(t)\|_2^2\le0.$$ For positive smooth-cavity modes $a_j''+\gamma a_j'+v^2\lambda_ja_j=0$. If $\Delta_j=\gamma^2/4-v^2\lambda_j$ is positive, the two roots are $-\gamma/2\pm\sqrt{\Delta_j}$; if negative they are $-\gamma/2\pm i\sqrt{-\Delta_j}$; at zero include $(A+Bt)e^{-\gamma t/2}$. This finite scalar characteristic classification applies to every parameter $\lambda\ge0$ and uses no choice principle; its general zero-eigenvalue associated-wave solutions and the narrower first-order compatibility are stated separately in (d). The full Choice premise belongs to the smooth-cavity spectral realization, not to these finite root formulas. For $\sigma>0$ every positive mode decays, electric zero modes obey $a_j(t)=a_j(0)e^{-\gamma t}$, and magnetic kernel data stay constant. In the smooth class the solution therefore tends in energy norm as $t\to+\infty$ to $(0,P_{K_M}B(0))$. For $\sigma=0$ energy is constant, electric zero modes are static and the original lossless branch is recovered. The zero sectors are retained, not divided by their eigenvalues; no universal decay to zero in the presence of magnetic kernel data is claimed.
(d) [Associated second-order branch] Independently of first-order compatibility, the same spectral basis gives the damped associated electric wave for every $q_0\in V$, $q_1\in H$, with $q\in C(\mathbb R;V)$, $q'\in C(\mathbb R;H)$ and modal convergence uniformly on compact times. Its coefficients satisfy $a_j''+\gamma a_j'+v^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with arbitrary prescribed initial coefficients. At $\lambda_j=0$ they are $\alpha_j+\beta_j(1-e^{-\gamma t})/\gamma$ when $\gamma>0$, and $\alpha_j+t\beta_j$ when $\gamma=0$. Such arbitrary second-order data need not arise from the first-order Maxwell system: its zero modes additionally satisfy $a_j'=-\gamma a_j$. This broader wave is retained alongside the physical first-order branch. All square roots and real derivatives use [[thm-of-square-roots]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and the real-component exponential formula [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]].
(e) [Scope] The conductor occupies the declared cavity interior while its stationary walls obey the independent ideal PEC boundary model. No arbitrary loss tensor, memory law, changing interface, open-end, rough-wall or empirical conclusion is made. Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) suffices for the rectangular/Fourier branch; the smooth branch retains its actual full Choice premise. Weak energy balance is proved by modal limits and does not assert an unprovided nonlinear weak local Poynting theorem.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The constant isotropic inertial-rest branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] with constants $\varepsilon,\mu>0$, $\sigma\ge0$, relations $D=\varepsilon E$, $H=B/\mu$, $J_{\rm ext}=0$ (the isotropic broadband condition $\varepsilon\mu\ge c^{-2}$ is additional and is not used); the smooth equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] with initially zero volume charge; the PEC guide/cavity geometry and weak reflection class of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]]; $v^2:=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}$ and $\gamma:=\sigma/\varepsilon$.

[F1] The first-order system and energy: with initially zero volume charge the macroscopic equations give $E_t=v^2\operatorname{curl}B-\gamma E$, $B_t=-\operatorname{curl}E$ and zero divergences, and the quadratic stored energy is $\mathcal U(t)=\tfrac12(\varepsilon\|E(t)\|_2^2+\mu^{-1}\|B(t)\|_2^2)$, consistent with [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]] ([[post-em-material-closure]], [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]], [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]]).

[F2] Rectangular energy class: [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] states that for a rectangular box $Q=\prod_j(0,L_j)$, in the reflection-parity and distributional-divergence class defined there, the finite separated Fourier modes are dense and the class is complete for the $L^2$ pairing, and every initial datum of the class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of the lossless system $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class with constant energy. Its system is written for the wavevector $k_j=\pi n_j/L_j$ and the finite-dimensional Fourier coefficients; the class and completeness are the objects used below, and Countable Choice is assumed as there ([[def-countable-choice]], [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]).

[F3] Smooth PEC cavity classes (supplied by the completed in-run items): [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] and [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]] declare, under the full Axiom of Choice, a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, the graph-norm completion $X$ in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$, the subspace $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$, and supply a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ of $H$ with nonnegative finite-multiplicity eigenvalues $\lambda_j$, the distributional equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ with PEC trace, the full-$X$ variational identity $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda_j\int_\Omega u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$, and $C^\infty$ eigenfields on the closure. Their statements are the sole premises taken from them, and the proof steps below name the supplier consumed at each use.

[F4] Elliptic solvability: [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] (a) supplies, under the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain and smooth data the unique smooth solution of the Dirichlet problem $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$, $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$.

[F5] Hilbert-space tools: orthogonal decomposition by a closed subspace and Fourier expansion ([[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]], [[thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion]]); Cauchy–Schwarz and completeness of the complex and real $L^2$ pairings ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]], [[lem-complex-lp-completeness-density-and-inner-product]]).

[F6] Distributional and one-variable tools: distributional derivative and its compatibility with $C^1$ regular distributions, with differentiation commuting with the embedding ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]); a distribution with zero derivative on a connected open set is constant ([[thm-a-distribution-with-zero-derivatives-on-a-connected-open-set-is-constant]]); the oriented primitive of a continuous function is $C^1$ with the given derivative and continuous functions on compact intervals are Riemann integrable ([[thm-ftc-first-part]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]); dominated convergence for passing integrals of uniformly convergent families ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

[F7] ODE tools: globally Lipschitz autonomous systems on a finite-dimensional real space have unique global solutions ([[cor-globally-lipschitz-odes-have-global-solutions]]); the scalar characteristic alternatives are the elementary algebra of $a''+\gamma a'+v^2\lambda a=0$ with the real square roots of [[thm-of-square-roots]], the real exponential limits ([[thm-exponential-limits-and-range]], [[thm-exponential-beats-every-polynomial]]) and the sine/cosine derivative rules with the real cartesian form of the complex exponential ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]); for a nonnegative real $\lambda$ the positive square root $\sqrt\lambda$ is the one of [[thm-of-square-roots]].

[F8] Vector-calculus identities: $\operatorname{div}(a\times b)=b\cdot\operatorname{curl}a-a\cdot\operatorname{curl}b$, the curl of a gradient vanishes, the divergence theorem on bounded $C^1$ domains, the cross product is bilinear, alternating and orthogonal, and the Euclidean inner product is the coordinate dot product ([[lem-the-divergence-and-curl-of-a-cross-product]], [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]], [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]).

[F9] Collar and cutoff: a bounded smooth domain has a tubular neighbourhood of its boundary, and the standard smooth step function supplies the cutoff used in the pairing argument ([[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]], [[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]]). Complex modulus and conjugation laws are [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]].



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct: solve the finite-dimensional damped modal systems, sum the exact energy identities, pass finite sums to the energy-norm limit, classify the scalar characteristics, and identify the limiting zero sectors.

1.1 [Rectangular damped modal system] Assume Countable Choice. Fix the box $Q$ and the reflection class of [F2], and let $(E,B)$ be a $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ distributional solution of the damped first-order system of [F1] in that class. The finite separated Fourier modes are dense in the class by [F2], and for a wavevector $k\in(\pi/L_1)\mathbb Z\times(\pi/L_2)\mathbb Z\times(\pi/L_3)\mathbb Z$ the coefficient system of the damped system reads $\widehat E_t=iv^2\,k\times\widehat B-\gamma\widehat E$, $\widehat B_t=-ik\times\widehat E$: this is [F2]'s recorded coefficient system with the additional scalar term $-\gamma\widehat E$ of [F1], and the algebraic constraint $k\cdot(k\times w)=0$ preserves $k\cdot\widehat E=k\cdot\widehat B=0$, while the finite Fourier modes carry the parities of the class because the reflection rules are diagonal in the separated basis. [F1, F2]

1.2 [Smooth PEC cavity spaces and the magnetic decomposition] Assume the full Axiom of Choice as in [F3], let $\Omega$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain and let $X,V,H$, $\{u_j\}$, $\lambda_j\ge0$ be the classes and eigenbasis of [F3]. Put $M:=\{B\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\int_\Omega B\cdot\nabla\psi=0\text{ for every smooth scalar }\psi\text{ on }\overline\Omega\}$, the weak normal-zero divergence-free space, and $K_M:=\{B\in M:\operatorname{curl}B=0\text{ distributionally}\}$. For each positive eigenvalue put $w_j:=\operatorname{curl}u_j/\sqrt{\lambda_j}$. Then the $w_j$ are orthonormal, $w_j\in M$, and $M=\overline{\operatorname{span}\{w_j:\lambda_j>0\}}^{L^2}\oplus K_M$. Orthonormality: the full-$X$ identity of [F3] with the test $v=u_l\in V\subseteq X$ gives $(\operatorname{curl}u_j,\operatorname{curl}u_l)=\lambda_j(u_j,u_l)=\lambda_j\delta_{jl}$, so $(w_j,w_l)=\delta_{jl}$. Membership and the forward inclusion: for a smooth scalar $\psi$, [F8] gives $\operatorname{div}(u_j\times\nabla\psi)=\nabla\psi\cdot\operatorname{curl}u_j-u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}\nabla\psi=\nabla\psi\cdot\operatorname{curl}u_j$, and its integral over $\Omega$ is the boundary integral $\int_{\partial\Omega}(n\times u_j)\cdot\nabla\psi=0$ because $u_j$ is smooth on the closure with $n\times u_j=0$ [F3]; hence $w_j\in M$, and the closed span of the $w_j$ lies in $M$. For an element $u\in V$, the $V$-norm identity of [F3] with $\|u_j\|_V^2=1+\lambda_j$ gives the expansion $u=\sum_j(u,u_j)u_j$ in $L^2$, and applying the bounded operator $\operatorname{curl}$ on $V$ gives $\operatorname{curl}u=\sum_j(u,u_j)\sqrt{\lambda_j}w_j$ in $L^2$; hence $\overline{\operatorname{curl}V}=\overline{\operatorname{span}\{w_j\}}$, and both lie in the closed subspace $M$. Decomposition: the orthogonal decomposition theorem [F5] applied to the closed subspace $\overline{\operatorname{span}\{w_j\}}$ of $M$ writes $B\in M$ as the sum of its projections onto that span and onto its orthogonal complement inside $M$; it remains to identify the complement with $K_M$. If $B\in M$ is orthogonal to every $\operatorname{curl}v$ with $v\in V$ and $\varphi$ is smooth and compactly supported in $\Omega$, then the smooth Dirichlet solver [F4] with coefficient identity, zero boundary trace and source $-\operatorname{div}\varphi$ supplies a smooth $f$ on the closure with $\Delta f=\operatorname{div}\varphi$; then $\varphi-\nabla f$ is smooth on the closure with $\operatorname{div}(\varphi-\nabla f)=0$ and with vanishing tangential trace on $\partial\Omega$ (the first term is compactly supported, and $f|_{\partial\Omega}=0$ forces the tangential derivatives of $f$, hence $n\times\nabla f$, to vanish there), so $\varphi-\nabla f$ lies in $V$; since $\operatorname{curl}(\varphi-\nabla f)=\operatorname{curl}\varphi$ by [F8], we obtain $(B,\operatorname{curl}\varphi)=0$; as $\varphi$ is an arbitrary compactly supported smooth test, this is exactly the distributional statement $\operatorname{curl}B=0$, i.e. $B\in K_M$. Conversely, if $B\in K_M$ then for each eigenfield $u_j$ the collar cutoff of [F9] yields compactly supported smooth approximants $\eta_\delta u_j$ with $\eta_\delta u_j\to u_j$ and $\operatorname{curl}(\eta_\delta u_j)\to\operatorname{curl}u_j$ in $L^2$ (the boundary layer has width $2\delta$ and $n\times u_j=0$ makes the boundary term vanish in the limit), so the distributional pairing $\int B\cdot\operatorname{curl}(\eta_\delta u_j)=0$ passes to the limit and gives $(B,\operatorname{curl}u_j)=0$, hence $(B,w_j)=0$; by continuity of the pairing and closedness of the span, $B$ is orthogonal to $\overline{\operatorname{span}\{w_j\}}$, which is the claimed complement and finishes the decomposition. [F3, F4, F5, F8, F9]

1.3 [Scalar characteristic classification] For parameters $\gamma\ge0$, $v>0$, $\lambda\ge0$, the solutions of $a''+\gamma a'+v^2\lambda a=0$ are classified by $\Delta:=\gamma^2/4-v^2\lambda$: if $\Delta>0$ the characteristic roots are $-\gamma/2\pm\sqrt\Delta$ and the general solution is $Ae^{(-\gamma/2+\sqrt\Delta)t}+Be^{(-\gamma/2-\sqrt\Delta)t}$; if $\Delta<0$ the roots are $-\gamma/2\pm i\sqrt{-\Delta}$ and the general solution is $e^{-\gamma t/2}(A\cos(\sqrt{-\Delta}t)+B\sin(\sqrt{-\Delta}t))$; if $\Delta=0$ it is $(A+Bt)e^{-\gamma t/2}$; and if $\lambda=0$ the solutions are $A+Be^{-\gamma t}$ for $\gamma>0$ and $A+Bt$ for $\gamma=0$. These are finite real computations with the square roots of [F7] and the real exponential and trigonometric solutions certified by [F7]; no choice principle is used. [F7]

2.1 [Rectangular class: global solutions, energy and convergence] For every initial pair in the rectangular class of [F2] the damped system of [F1] has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ distributional solution in the class, finite Fourier mode sums converge in energy norm uniformly on compact time intervals and are dense at every time, and the coefficient equations of step 1.1 hold for every wavevector. Indeed, for each $k$ the right-hand side of the finite-dimensional system of step 1.1 is globally state-Lipschitz (it is affine), so [F7] gives a unique global solution through the initial coefficients; differentiating the per-mode energy $\varepsilon|\widehat E|^2+\mu^{-1}|\widehat B|^2$ and using $\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\widehat E}\cdot(k\times\widehat B))+$ its conjugate $=0$ (the scalar triple-product identity of [F8] with complex conjugation, [F9]) gives $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(\varepsilon|\widehat E|^2+\mu^{-1}|\widehat B|^2\bigr)=-2\sigma|\widehat E|^2\le0$, so each modal energy is nonincreasing forward and bounded by $e^{2\gamma T}$ times its initial value on $[-T,T]$ (multiply by $e^{2\gamma t}$ and differentiate); Parseval for the complete class [F2] therefore controls the energy-norm of every omitted tail uniformly on compact times. Finite solutions converge in $C_tL^2$ to a limit in the class, and the linear distributional equations pass to the limit against compactly supported smooth periodic tests by Cauchy–Schwarz [F5] on a compact time support, exactly as in the lossless argument of [F2]; the constraints $k\cdot\widehat E=k\cdot\widehat B=0$ and the parities are preserved by step 1.1, so the limit lies in the same class. Uniqueness: a $C_tL^2$ weak solution has continuous coefficients whose distributional derivatives equal the displayed continuous right-hand sides; for each coefficient equation, subtract the oriented primitive of the continuous right-hand side, which is $C^1$ with that derivative by [F6], use the $C^1$ regular-distribution compatibility of [F6] to identify its distributional derivative, conclude that the difference has zero distributional derivative, hence is constant by [F6], and match the initial value; global uniqueness of the finite system identifies the coefficients, and completeness of the Fourier class identifies the fields. [step 1.1, F2, F5, F6, F7, F8, F9]

3.1 [Smooth PEC cavity: modal system, variational equations and uniqueness] Assume the full Axiom of Choice as in [F3]. Let $H\times M$ be the energy class of steps 1.2, with $M=\overline{\operatorname{span}\{w_j\}}\oplus K_M$. For coefficients $a_j=(\cdot,u_j)$, $b_j=(\cdot,w_j)$ declare the first-order modal system $a_j'=v^2\sqrt{\lambda_j}\,b_j-\gamma a_j$, $b_j'=-\sqrt{\lambda_j}\,a_j$ for $\lambda_j>0$, and $a_j'=-\gamma a_j$ for the electric zero modes, and declare the magnetic kernel data constant, $(B,K_M)'=0$ for every kernel test. Endow the paired-magnetic space with the completion $D_M$ of finite $w_j$-sums plus $K_M$ for the norm $\|w\|_{D_M}^2:=\|w\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{curl}w\|_2^2$, and consider the weak variational equations $\langle E_t,\phi\rangle=v^2\langle B,\operatorname{curl}\phi\rangle-\gamma\langle E,\phi\rangle$ for $\phi\in V$ and $\langle B_t,\psi\rangle=-\langle E,\operatorname{curl}\psi\rangle$ for $\psi\in D_M$. Then every initial pair in $H\times M$ has a unique $C(\mathbb R;H\times M)$ solution of this declared realization, it satisfies the modal equations distributionally, and finite electric and paired-magnetic modal sums together with the static kernel component converge uniformly on compact time intervals in energy norm. Existence and uniqueness are finite-dimensional: each paired system is a globally Lipschitz constant-coefficient system solved by [F7], and the kernel data are constant, so a candidate solution is the norm-limit of its finite modal sums; the sums converge because the energy $\sum_j(\varepsilon|a_j|^2+\mu^{-1}|b_j|^2)$ is controlled as in step 2.1 and the kernel component is retained exactly. For the variational equations, the finite sums satisfy them against finite spectral tests by the full-$X$ identity of [F3], and the density of the finite spectral tests in $V$ and in $D_M$ passes the identities to the limit by Cauchy–Schwarz [F5], since uniform energy convergence on compact times controls both pairings. Conversely, testing the variational equations against $u_j$ (for $\phi$) and $w_j$ or kernel vectors (for $\psi$) recovers the modal equations, so the weak realization and the modal system are equivalent in the stated class; uniqueness follows from the scalar ODE uniqueness and the complete decomposition of step 1.2. For strong first-order solutions with $E\in C^1_tH\cap C_tV$ and $B\in C^1_tL^2\cap C_tH(\operatorname{curl})$, the same pairing gives $a_j'=v^2(B,\operatorname{curl}u_j)-\gamma a_j$ and, differentiating with $B'=-\operatorname{curl}E$ and the full-$X$ identity, $a_j''+\gamma a_j'+v^2\lambda_j a_j=0$ with $a_j'=-\gamma a_j$ at $\lambda_j=0$. No maximal rough tangential-trace realisation is claimed. [step 1.2, F3, F5, F7]

4.1 [Exact energy balance] In both declared classes, for every $t_0<t_1$, $\mathcal U(t_1)+\sigma\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\|E(t)\|_2^2dt=\mathcal U(t_0)$ and $\mathcal U'(t)=-\sigma\|E(t)\|_2^2\le0$. In the rectangular class, sum the finite per-mode identities of step 2.1 over the wavevectors of a finite modal projection, integrate over $[t_0,t_1]$ with [F6], and pass to the limit using the uniform energy-norm convergence of step 2.1 to pass both the energy and the continuous $\|E(t)\|_2^2$-integral terms; in the smooth class, do the same with the paired modal energies of step 3.1 and the retained kernel component, whose curl vanishes. The derivative form then follows from the integral form by [F6]; the boundary term of a smooth local Poynting identity is not used, so no unprovided nonlinear weak local identity is asserted. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F6]

4.2 [Associated second-order branch] Independently of first-order compatibility, the same spectral basis gives the damped associated electric wave for every $q_0\in V$, $q_1\in H$, with $q\in C(\mathbb R;V)$, $q'\in C(\mathbb R;H)$ and modal convergence uniform on compact times: its coefficients satisfy $a_j''+\gamma a_j'+v^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with prescribed initial coefficients $a_j(0)=(q_0,u_j)$, $a_j'(0)=(q_1,u_j)$, and at $\lambda_j=0$ they are $\alpha_j+\beta_j(1-e^{-\gamma t})/\gamma$ for $\gamma>0$ and $\alpha_j+t\beta_j$ for $\gamma=0$. Indeed, for $\lambda_j>0$ the function $Q_j=|a_j'|^2+v^2\lambda_j|a_j|^2$ satisfies $Q_j'=-2\gamma|a_j'|^2\le0$ by [F7], and the positive eigenvalues, being finite in multiplicity and tending to infinity, have a positive lower bound, so compact-time exponential bounds on $Q_j$ control the $V$ displacement and $H$ velocity tails by the weighted $V$-norm identity of [F3]; the finitely many zero modes have the displayed solutions by step 1.3, and the finite-sum FTC estimate of [F6] passes the $H$ derivative to the limit and identifies the variational second-order equation against compact-time tests. Such arbitrary second-order data need not arise from the first-order Maxwell system: its zero modes additionally satisfy $a_j'=-\gamma a_j$, and the broader wave is retained alongside the physical first-order branch. All square roots and real derivatives are those of [F7]. [step 1.2, step 1.3, step 3.1, F3, F6, F7]

5.1 [Decay, zero sectors and long-time limits] For $\sigma>0$ (so $\gamma>0$) every positive mode decays: if $\Delta_j=\gamma^2/4-v^2\lambda_j>0$ the two real roots $-\gamma/2\pm\sqrt{\Delta_j}$ are negative; if $\Delta_j<0$ the complex roots have real part $-\gamma/2<0$, and the oscillatory factor is bounded by the cosine and sine identities of [F7]; if $\Delta_j=0$ the factor $t e^{-\gamma t/2}$ tends to zero by [F7]. Electric zero modes obey $a_j(t)=a_j(0)e^{-\gamma t}$ by step 1.3, and magnetic kernel data stay constant by step 1.2, so in the smooth class the solution tends in energy norm as $t\to+\infty$ to $(0,P_{K_M}B(0))$, where $P_{K_M}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $K_M$ of step 1.2; the finite-head/finite-tail argument of step 3.1 passes the modewise convergence to the whole energy norm. For $\sigma=0$ the energy is constant by step 4.1, the electric zero modes are static by step 1.3 and the original lossless branch is recovered. The zero sectors are retained, not divided by their eigenvalues, and no universal decay to zero in the presence of magnetic kernel data is claimed. [step 1.2, step 1.3, step 3.1, step 4.1, F7]

6.1 [Scope] Clauses (a) and (b) are steps 2.1 and 3.1: the rectangular class has a unique finite-energy distributional solution with dense finite modes at every time, and the smooth PEC class has the declared weak realization with a unique solution and energy-norm convergence of finite modal sums; the decomposition of the magnetic space, including arbitrary kernel data, is step 1.2. Clause (c) is steps 4.1 and 5.1. Clause (d) is step 4.2. Clause (e): the argument used only the declared constant Ohmic branch, the ideal PEC boundary model, the finite-energy classes and the recorded spectral and elliptic suppliers; Countable Choice suffices for the rectangular branch, the smooth branch retains its full Choice premise, no arbitrary loss tensor, memory law, changing interface, open-end, rough-wall or empirical claim is made, and weak energy balance was proved by modal limits without asserting an unprovided nonlinear weak local Poynting theorem. [step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2, step 5.1, F1] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the constant isotropic material branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] with $\varepsilon,\mu>0$, $\sigma\ge0$, $J_{\rm ext}=0$ and initially zero volume charge. For an exact broadband physical interpretation retain the closure condition $\varepsilon\mu\ge c^{-2}$; without it this is the declared effective model with no universal front-speed claim. Put $v^2=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}$, $\gamma=\sigma/\varepsilon$. On the infinite straight rectangular guide $Q=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]], declare the finite-energy reflection class as follows. Extend in the two transverse variables to $T_{ab}^2\times\mathbb R$, $T_{ab}^2=\mathbb R/(2a\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb R/(2b\mathbb Z)$. The electric components have transverse parities even/odd, odd/even, odd/odd respectively; magnetic components have odd/even, even/odd, even/even respectively. Require the extended real fields to be $L^2$ and have both divergences zero distributionally. For smooth fields this gives the four-wall conditions $n\times E=0$, $n\cdot B=0$; it is a precise weak PEC realization, not an assertion about every rough trace class. There is no end cap and no junction or open-end scattering datum.
(a) [Complete mixed transform] Let $\phi_{mn}(x_t)=(4ab)^{-1/2}e^{i\pi(mx_1/a+nx_2/b)}$, $(m,n)\in\mathbb Z^2$, be the orthonormal transverse characters. For each component first form $F_{mn}(z)=\int_{T_{ab}^2}F(x_t,z)\overline{\phi_{mn}(x_t)}\,dx_t$, then apply the exact negative-sign $2\pi$ Fourier transform $\mathcal F_2$ of [[thm-plancherel]] in $z$. Write $\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)=\mathcal F_2F_{mn}(\xi)$ and $\beta=2\pi\xi$. The transform is a unitary representation of $L^2(T_{ab}^2\times\mathbb R)$ by $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^2;L^2(\mathbb R))$, with inverse in $L^2$ from [[thm-l-two-fourier-inversion]], and $$\|F\|_{L^2(Q)}^2=\tfrac14\sum_{m,n}\int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)|^2\,d\xi$$ for these reflection fields. The parity and reality relations are retained, including $\widehat F_{-m,-n}(-\xi)=\overline{\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)}$. With $K=(\pi m/a,\pi n/b,2\pi\xi)$, the divergence constraints become $K\cdot\widehat E=K\cdot\widehat B=0$ for almost every $\xi$. This is a complete transverse sin/cos and longitudinal $L^2$ Fourier representation, not pointwise Fourier convergence or a finite-energy monochromatic plane wave.
(b) [Unique energy evolution] Adopt in that weak reflection class the constant-Ohmic first-order material evolution $E_t=v^2\operatorname{curl}B-\gamma E$, $B_t=-\operatorname{curl}E$, distributionally, consistent with the smooth [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] and [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]] branches. For every initial pair in the class there is a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2(Q))$ solution in the same class. Its mixed coefficients solve, for every transverse index and almost every $\xi$, $$\partial_t\widehat E=iv^2K\times\widehat B-\gamma\widehat E,\qquad\partial_t\widehat B=-iK\times\widehat E.$$ Finite transverse sums and bounded longitudinal frequency truncations reconstruct the solution in energy norm uniformly on compact time intervals; such reconstructed fields are dense in the class at every time. They retain the divergence constraints and the original parities, including zero coefficient cases without dividing by $K$ or $|K|$.
(c) [Energy and dispersion] The total stored energy of this whole infinite guide is finite and equals $$\mathcal U(t)=\tfrac18\sum_{m,n}\int_{\mathbb R}(\varepsilon|\widehat E|^2+\mu^{-1}|\widehat B|^2)\,d\xi.$$ For every $t_0<t_1$, $\mathcal U(t_1)+\sigma\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\|E(t)\|_{L^2(Q)}^2dt=\mathcal U(t_0)$, and $\mathcal U'(t)=-\sigma\|E(t)\|_2^2$. At $\sigma=0$ energy is conserved and each constrained electric coefficient satisfies $\widehat E''+v^2|K|^2\widehat E=0$, so $\omega^2=v^2[(\pi m/a)^2+(\pi n/b)^2+\beta^2]$. These are the exact finite transverse-mode matrices of the approved K10 branch; individual separated TE/TM candidate fields still have their own cutoff and zero-profile restrictions, and no TE$_{00}$ mode is created by a scalar constant coefficient. For $\sigma>0$ the electric equation is $\widehat E''+\gamma\widehat E'+v^2|K|^2\widehat E=0$ with the distinct/repeated-root alternatives of the choice-free finite-parameter clause of [[pthm-em-uniform-ohmic-modal-decay]](c), here at $\lambda=|K|^2\ge0$. Its full-Choice smooth-cavity realization is not used. At $K=0$ keep the direct first-order equations $\widehat E\prime=-\gamma\widehat E$, $\widehat B\prime=0$, without dividing by $K$; the original parity and $L^2$ relations still apply. No signal-speed or empirical inference is made.
(d) [Scope] This theorem supplies the previously missing complete longitudinal $L^2$ expansion of the declared straight rectangular guide, including its lossless and constant-Ohmic energy evolutions. It makes no completeness claim for arbitrary non-rectangular, dispersive, nonlocal, nonlinear, rough-wall or open-end/junction problems. The weak energy result is proved by linear mixed-transform evolution and modal limits, not by applying a nonlinear smooth Poynting identity to rough data.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]); the constant isotropic material branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] with constants $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ and $\sigma\ge0$, $J_{\rm ext}=0$ and initially zero volume charge (with the closure condition $\varepsilon\mu\ge c^{-2}$ retained for the exact broadband interpretation); $v^2=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}$, $\gamma=\sigma/\varepsilon$; the infinite straight rectangular guide $Q=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times\mathbb R$ and its geometry of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]]; the finite-energy reflection class of the Statement, defined by transverse extension to $T_{ab}^2\times\mathbb R$ with the stated electric and magnetic parities, $L^2$ membership and distributionally zero divergences.

[F1] The material and evolution branch: $D=\varepsilon E$, $B=\mu H$, and with initially zero volume charge the macroscopic equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] give the first-order system $E_t=v^2\operatorname{curl}B-\gamma E$, $B_t=-\operatorname{curl}E$ and zero divergences; the stored energy is $\mathcal U=\frac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+\mu^{-1}|B|^2)$ ([[post-em-material-closure]] (b), [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] (b), [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]]).

[F2] Transverse completeness: the characters $\phi_{mn}(x_t)=(4ab)^{-1/2}e^{i\pi(mx_1/a+nx_2/b)}$ are orthonormal in $L^2$ of the fundamental rectangle of $T_{ab}^2$ by elementary exponential integration, and the product families of cosines and sines are complete orthogonal systems ([[lem-em-rectangular-transverse-mode-completeness]] (a),(b), [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (i), [[thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion]]); Fubini and Tonelli apply to the product spaces ([[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

[F3] Fourier analysis in $z$: the unitary Plancherel transform $\mathcal F_2$ with inverse in $L^2$, the derivative Fourier identity on Schwartz functions, and Schwartz cutoffs from the standard smooth step function ([[thm-plancherel]], [[thm-l-two-fourier-inversion]], [[thm-fourier-transform-maps-schwartz-space-continuously-to-itself]], [[lem-schwartz-cutoffs-from-the-standard-smooth-step]]).

[F4] Distributional and integration tools: distributional derivative and its regular-distribution compatibility, a distribution with zero derivative on a connected open set is constant, the oriented primitive of a continuous function is $C^1$ with that derivative, continuous functions on compact intervals are integrable, and dominated convergence ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], [[thm-a-distribution-with-zero-derivatives-on-a-connected-open-set-is-constant]], [[thm-ftc-first-part]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]], [[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

[F5] ODE tools: globally Lipschitz finite-dimensional systems have unique global solutions and their solutions depend continuously on initial data and parameters ([[cor-globally-lipschitz-odes-have-global-solutions]], [[thm-continuous-dependence-of-odes-on-initial-data-and-parameters]]); the characteristic alternatives for $\widehat E''+\gamma\widehat E'+v^2\lambda\widehat E=0$ at $\lambda\ge0$ are the finite-parameter classification of [[pthm-em-uniform-ohmic-modal-decay]] (c), whose smooth-cavity, full-Choice clauses are not used.

[F6] Algebra and estimates: the componentwise cross product and its identities, complex conjugation and modulus laws, the cartesian form of the complex exponential, Cauchy–Schwarz, and completeness/density in complex $L^2$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]], [[lem-complex-lp-completeness-density-and-inner-product]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-of-square-roots]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct: build the mixed transverse-character and longitudinal-Fourier representation, transport the divergence constraints and the evolution into coefficient form, solve the finite dimensional modal systems with uniform energy bounds, and pass cutoffs to the limit.

1.1 [Complete mixed transform] With the characters of [F2], first form for each component the transverse coefficients $F_{mn}(z)=\int_{T_{ab}^2}F(x_t,z)\overline{\phi_{mn}(x_t)}dx_t$ and then $\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)=\mathcal F_2F_{mn}(\xi)$ for the exact $2\pi$-convention transform of [F3]; write $\beta=2\pi\xi$. Then the map $F\mapsto(\widehat F_{mn})_{(m,n)\in\mathbb Z^2}$ is a unitary isomorphism of $L^2(T_{ab}^2\times\mathbb R)$ onto $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^2;L^2(\mathbb R))$ and, for the reflection fields of the Statement, $\|F\|^2_{L^2(Q)}=\frac14\sum_{m,n}\int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)|^2d\xi$. Indeed the characters are orthonormal on the fundamental rectangle and, being products of the complete one-dimensional character systems, their finite span is dense in the transverse $L^2$ of each torus fibre by [F2]; Fubini–Tonelli therefore gives, for almost every $z$, the transverse expansion together with $\int_{T_{ab}^2}|F(x_t,z)|^2dx_t=\sum_{m,n}|F_{mn}(z)|^2$ and, after integration in $z$, $\|F\|^2_{L^2(T_{ab}^2\times\mathbb R)}=\sum_{m,n}\|F_{mn}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb R)}$. Applying the unitary Plancherel transform [F3] to each of the countably many scalar functions $F_{mn}\in L^2(\mathbb R)$ gives the coefficient map and the isometry on the torus product, with inverse from the $L^2$ inversion theorem of [F3]; the reflection extension doubles each transverse period, so the torus fundamental rectangle has $4ab$-area and the physical norm is one quarter of the extended norm, which is the displayed factor $\frac14$. The parity relations follow from $\phi_{-m,-n}=\overline{\phi_{mn}}$ and the transverse parities by the coordinate changes $x_j\mapsto-x_j$ on the torus, and the reality relation $\widehat F_{-m,-n}(-\xi)=\overline{\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)}$ holds first for real integrable compactly supported longitudinal data by the defining integral and passes to $L^2$ by density and continuity of the transform [F3]. No pointwise reconstruction is asserted. [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Divergence constraints in coefficient form] For $K:=(\pi m/a,\pi n/b,2\pi\xi)$ the distributionally zero divergence of the extended field is equivalent to $K\cdot\widehat E=K\cdot\widehat B=0$ for almost every $\xi$, and the finite-energy reflection class is exactly the class of coefficient families satisfying these almost-everywhere constraints together with the parities and $L^2$ summability. The derivative correspondence is proved on the dense test class of finite transverse-character sums times longitudinal Schwartz functions: for such a test $\psi$, finite transverse integration by parts and the exact identity $\mathcal F_2(\partial_z\psi)=2\pi i\xi\widehat\psi$ of [F3] turn the pairing $\int F\cdot\nabla\psi$ into the sum of the coefficient pairings against $iK\cdot\widehat F$, and the compactly supported smooth tests used in the definition are obtained by multiplying with cutoffs $\chi_R$ of [F3] and passing to the limit, since the tests and their first derivatives converge in $L^2$ and all pairings are bounded by Cauchy–Schwarz [F6]; conversely a test with $K\cdot\widehat F=0$ almost everywhere has zero weak divergence pairing, and the general compact smooth tests are reached through the transverse $L^2$ expansions of their derivatives and the Schwartz transform isomorphism [F3]. Hence the exact constrained class corresponds to the stated almost-everywhere coefficient constraints, not merely to a scalar basis without Gauss equations; for smooth fields the divergences vanish pointwise and the four-wall PEC conditions hold by the reading of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]]. [step 1.1, F2, F3, F6]

3.1 [Unique energy evolution in the class] Adopt the constant-Ohmic first-order system of [F1] distributionally in the reflection class of step 2.1. For every initial pair in the class there is a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2(Q))$ solution in the same class, its mixed coefficients satisfy, for every $(m,n)$ and almost every $\xi$, $\partial_t\widehat E=iv^2K\times\widehat B-\gamma\widehat E$ and $\partial_t\widehat B=-iK\times\widehat E$, and finite transverse sums with bounded longitudinal frequency truncations reconstruct the solution in energy norm uniformly on compact time intervals and are dense in the class at every time, retaining the divergence constraints and parities without dividing by $K$ or $|K|$. Existence: for each $(m,n,\xi)$ the real and imaginary parts of the displayed system form a real finite-dimensional constant-coefficient linear system on all of $\mathbb R$, hence a globally Lipschitz system with a unique global solution through the initial coefficients by [F5]; the solution matrix depends continuously on $\xi$ uniformly on compact parameter and time sets by the continuous-dependence theorem [F5] (applied on a common bounded state cylinder, which the uniform energy bound below supplies), so multiplying the measurable initial coefficient vector by the continuous fundamental matrix gives measurable coefficient trajectories [F6]; no uncountable choice of solutions is made, and the construction uses only the countable families of coefficients. Energy: with $q:=\varepsilon|\widehat E|^2+\mu^{-1}|\widehat B|^2$, conjugation and the triple-product cancellation of the displayed system give $q'=-2\sigma|\widehat E|^2$, whence $q(t)\le e^{2\gamma T}q(0)$ for $|t|\le T$ and forward contractivity at $\sigma\ge0$; the constraints $K\cdot\widehat E=K\cdot\widehat B=0$ and the parity and reality relations of step 1.1 are preserved because the right-hand side is linear, $K\cdot(K\times\widehat B)=0$ and the parities are respected by the cross product with $K$. Cutoffs $|m|,|n|\le N$, $|\xi|\le N$ preserve every relation; their initial energy tails tend to zero by Tonelli and dominated convergence [F4], and the uniform bound makes the time-dependent tails tend to zero uniformly on compact times; each truncated solution is strongly differentiable in $L^2$ with bounded multiplier $K$ on the cutoff, and its linear equations follow from the test derivative identity of step 2.1, so the compact-time $L^2$ limits are continuous, have the prescribed data and satisfy the equations against compact smooth tests. Uniqueness: for any weak $C_tL^2$ reflection solution and bounded spectral cutoff $N$, project to the cutoff coefficients; the test identity of step 2.1 turns the evolution into $f'=A_Nf$ distributionally in time in the cutoff Hilbert space with bounded constant matrix $A_N$, and the finite transverse tests and smooth frequency tests supported in the cutoff interval, whose inverse transforms are Schwartz, are dense in the cutoff space, so the identity extends to every cutoff vector by the bounded multiplier and Cauchy–Schwarz [F6]. Subtracting the continuous Hilbert-valued primitive of $A_Nf$, constructed as the norm limit of finite Riemann sums (which is independent of the tags by the uniform oscillation bound on a compact interval, exists by completeness of $L^2$, has the correct derivative by the average-increment bound, and is the vector version of the primitive argument of [F4]), pairing with every fixed cutoff vector and applying the scalar zero-derivative distribution theorem [F4] identifies the difference with its constant initial value; the difference $d$ of two solutions with zero data satisfies $d(t)=\int_0^tA_Nd(s)ds$, so on an interval of length $h$ with $h\|A_N\|<1$ the supremum norm forces $d=0$, and finitely iterating these intervals in either direction on any compact time interval gives $d=0$; letting the cutoffs exhaust the representation gives uniqueness of the whole field. The zero coefficient $K=0$ is treated directly by the same equations with $K=0$, without division by $K$ or $|K|$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, F3, F4, F5, F6]

4.1 [Energy and dispersion] The total stored energy of the whole infinite guide is finite and equals $\mathcal U(t)=\frac18\sum_{m,n}\int_{\mathbb R}(\varepsilon|\widehat E|^2+\mu^{-1}|\widehat B|^2)d\xi$, and for every $t_0<t_1$ one has $\mathcal U(t_1)+\sigma\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\|E(t)\|_{L^2(Q)}^2dt=\mathcal U(t_0)$ with $\mathcal U'(t)=-\sigma\|E(t)\|_2^2$. Indeed, summing the finite/cutoff modal identities $q'=-2\sigma|\widehat E|^2$ of step 3.1 over the bounded cutoffs, integrating in $\xi$ and summing the finite transverse indices gives the truncated balance, and dominated convergence with the compact-time tail bound of step 3.1 passes it to the limit; the physical energy carries the factor $\frac12\cdot\frac14=\frac18$ from step 1.1, and the dissipation term is continuous in time, so ordinary FTC [F4] gives the derivative form. At $\sigma=0$ the energy is constant, and on the constrained coefficient subspace differentiating the first-order equation once and using $K\times(K\times e)=K(K\cdot e)-|K|^2e$ together with $K\cdot\widehat E=0$ gives $\widehat E''+v^2|K|^2\widehat E=0$, that is $\omega^2=v^2[(\pi m/a)^2+(\pi n/b)^2+\beta^2]$ with $\beta=2\pi\xi$; at $K=0$ the direct equations $\widehat E'=-\gamma\widehat E$, $\widehat B'=0$ are retained without dividing by $K$. For $\sigma>0$ the electric equation is $\widehat E''+\gamma\widehat E'+v^2|K|^2\widehat E=0$ at $\lambda=|K|^2\ge0$ with the distinct/repeated-root alternatives of the finite-parameter classification [F5], including the zero-$K$ case; the zero-profile restrictions and individual cutoffs of the separated TE/TM candidates are unaffected, and no TE$_{00}$ mode is created by a scalar constant coefficient. [step 1.1, step 3.1, F4, F5, F6, algebra]

5.1 [Scope] Clause (a) is steps 1.1 and 2.1, clause (b) is step 3.1, and clause (c) is step 4.1. The theorem supplies the complete longitudinal $L^2$ expansion of the declared straight rectangular guide with its lossless and constant-Ohmic energy evolutions and makes no completeness claim for arbitrary non-rectangular, dispersive, nonlocal, nonlinear, rough-wall or open-end/junction problems; the weak energy result is proved by linear mixed-transform evolution and modal limits, not by applying a nonlinear smooth Poynting identity to rough data, and no signal-speed or empirical inference is made. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F1] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited mathematical suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]), the lossless isotropic scalar constant branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] with $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ and $\sigma=0$, the source-free smooth macroscopic equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] in the smooth branches, with $\rho_f=0$, $J_f=0$, and the explicitly declared weak first-order material equations in the weak cavity branches below, and the guide, cavity, PEC and reflection-class conventions of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]].
(a) [Transverse profile completeness] For the cross-section $(0,a)\times(0,b)$, the families $\{h_{mn}\}_{m,n\ge0}$ and $\{e_{mn}\}_{m,n\ge1}$ of [[lem-em-rectangle-mode-profile-identities]] are orthogonal complete systems in $L^2$ of the rectangle ([[lem-em-rectangular-transverse-mode-completeness]]); The full scalar Neumann and Dirichlet families have these $L^2$ expansions. The physical TE candidate family excludes $h_{00}=1$ by the full Maxwell equations: the remaining $h_{mn}$ are complete in the zero-mean subspace $\{f\in L^2:\int_Rf=0\}$, not in all scalar $L^2$. The Dirichlet TM profiles retain their full scalar completeness. The constant Neumann scalar profile is retained in the mathematical basis but is not asserted to be a nonzero positive-frequency TE mode.
(b) [Rectangular cavity reflection class] For the box $Q=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times(0,d)$ with the reflection class and distributional constraints $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}B=0$ of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]](c): the finite separated Fourier modes are dense in the class at every time; every initial datum in the class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of the lossless first-order system $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the same class, with derivatives as in [[def-distributional-derivative]]; this lossless first-order distributional system is the explicitly adopted weak material evolution of the reflection model, not inferred from the smooth-only hypotheses of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]]; along the solution the total stored energy $\int_Q u\,dx$ equals $\frac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+|B|^2/\mu)\,dx$ and is constant, where the weak stored-energy density is defined almost everywhere by this nonnegative quadratic expression, consistent with the smooth local definition of [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]]. Its integrability and constancy are furnished by the mathematical reflection-class energy result; no nonlinear weak Poynting identity is asserted. For $C^1$-in-time solutions the four macroscopic equations with $D=\varepsilon E$, $B=\mu H$ hold distributionally.
(c) [Smooth PEC cavity] For a bounded $C^\infty$ cavity domain $\Omega$ and the PEC class $X,V,H$ of [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]](a): the curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and a finite-dimensional zero eigenspace that is retained; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally with the PEC trace, and each $u_j$ has a $C^\infty$ representative on the closure. Put $v_{\mathrm{wave}}=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1/2}>0$. The associated second-order electric wave has the full supplied interface: for arbitrary initial displacement in $V$ and velocity in $H$, its displacement is in $C(\mathbb R;V)$, its velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$, and finite modal sums converge in these respective norms uniformly on compact time intervals. Its zero eigenmodes may be affine in time. Separately, let $J$ be an open time interval and let a strong first-order solution obey $E\in C^1(J;H)\cap C(J;V)$ and $B\in C^1(J;L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))\cap C(J;H(\operatorname{curl}))$, with the first-order equations as $L^2$ identities and both distributional divergence constraints. Electric tangential-zero boundary data are encoded by $E(t)\in V$. The magnetic normal-zero condition is declared weakly by $\int_\Omega B(t)\cdot\nabla\psi=0$ for every smooth scalar $\psi$ on the closure; when $B\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ this is $n\cdot B=0$, using $\operatorname{div}B=0$. No magnetic membership in the electric tangential-zero class $X$ is assumed. Then $a_j(t):=\langle E(t),u_j\rangle$ is $C^2$ and satisfies $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$. For $\lambda_j=0$, the admissible first-order coefficients satisfy $a_j'=0$ and are constant, with the zero eigenfields retained. This extra compatibility distinguishes first-order Maxwell data from arbitrary second-order $V\times H$ data; it does not remove the broader supplied second-order wave or its affine zero modes.
(d) [Scope] The theorem asserts completeness only for the transverse $L^2$ profiles and for the two declared cavity classes with their exact hypotheses; this lossless theorem does not itself supply the longitudinal expansion or dissipative evolution. Those approved additional classes are supplied separately by [[pthm-em-open-rectangular-guide-completeness]] and [[pthm-em-uniform-ohmic-modal-decay]], respectively. None of these statements supplies arbitrary lossy, dispersive, open-end scattering, non-smooth or exterior problems, or arbitrary non-rectangular guide problems beyond the explicitly declared smooth-cavity spectral class, no trace regularity for arbitrary $H(\operatorname{curl})$ fields, and no identification of the weak classes with every maximal tangential-trace realization. The zero eigenvalues and zero modes are retained throughout.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]); the lossless isotropic scalar constant branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] with $\varepsilon,\mu>0$, $\sigma=0$; the source-free smooth macroscopic equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] with $\rho_f=0$, $J_f=0$; the explicitly declared weak first-order material equations in the weak cavity branches; the guide, cavity, PEC and reflection-class conventions of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]]; the fields of [[def-em-fields]].

[F1] Transverse completeness: for the cross-section $(0,a)\times(0,b)$ the families $\{h_{mn}\}_{m,n\ge0}$ and $\{e_{mn}\}_{m,n\ge1}$ of [[lem-em-rectangle-mode-profile-identities]] are orthogonal complete systems in $L^2$ of the rectangle, with the full-family expansions of [[lem-em-rectangular-transverse-mode-completeness]] (b) and [[thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion]]; the profile identities include $\int_Rh_{mn}h_{m'n'}=0$ unless $(m,n)=(m',n')$ and $\int_Rh_{00}^2=ab>0$, so $\int_Rh_{mn}=0$ for $(m,n)\ne(0,0)$ by pairing with $h_{00}=1$ ([[lem-em-rectangle-mode-profile-identities]] (c)); $L^2$ completeness supplies the Hilbert-space structure ([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]).

[F2] Rectangular reflection class: [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] states that the finite separated Fourier modes are dense in the reflection class, that every initial datum of the class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class, and that the energy $\frac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+|B|^2/\mu)$ is constant along the solution; distributions and their derivatives are those of [[def-distributional-derivative]], and the class is the one of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]] (c); the packaged rectangular branch of [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]] (b) repeats these assertions.

[F3] Smooth PEC cavity (supplied by the completed in-run items): [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]] (a) and [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] state, under the full Axiom of Choice, that for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega$ the graph-norm class $X$ of smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$, its divergence-free subspace $V$ and $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$ carry a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ of the curl form with nonnegative finite-multiplicity eigenvalues $\lambda_j$, the distributional eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ with the PEC trace, $C^\infty$ eigenfields on the closure, the full-$X$ variational identity $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda_j\int_\Omega u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$, and the associated second-order wave at $v_{\mathrm{wave}}=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1/2}>0$ for arbitrary $V\times H$ data with $C_tV$ displacement and $C_tH$ velocity. Their statements are the premises used here, and the proof steps below name the supplier consumed at each use.

[F4] Paring tools: for $F\in H(\operatorname{curl})$, a compactly supported smooth test $\varphi$ satisfies the distributional identity $\langle\operatorname{curl}F,\varphi\rangle=\langle F,\operatorname{curl}\varphi\rangle$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]); Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the pairings; a bounded smooth boundary has a collar with the inward normal coordinate, and the standard smooth step builds the cutoff $\eta_\delta$ used below ([[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]], [[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]], [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]).

[F5] The smooth stored-energy density $u=\frac12(E\cdot D+B\cdot H)$ of [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]] reduces to $\frac12(\varepsilon|E|^2+\mu^{-1}|B|^2)$ in the lossless scalar branch.

**Proof technique:** direct: instantiate the transverse completeness and its zero-mean restriction, read the rectangular weak branch from its supplier and verify the macroscopic rewriting, then derive the first-order modal equation for the smooth cavity by a collar pairing and differentiate it once.

1.1 [Clause (a)] The families $\{h_{mn}\}$ and $\{e_{mn}\}$ are orthogonal complete systems in $L^2(R_{ab})$ by [F1], which gives the expansion statement. Each member with $(m,n)\ne(0,0)$ has zero integral over $R_{ab}$ by the orthogonality of [F1] against $h_{00}=1$, so the closed linear span $S$ of $\{h_{mn}:(m,n)\ne(0,0)\}$ is contained in the closed zero-mean subspace $Z=\{f\in L^2(R_{ab}):\int_{R_{ab}}f=0\}$; conversely, if $f\in Z$, the expansion theorem [F1] applied to the complete orthonormal family obtained by normalizing all the $h_{mn}$ writes $f$ as the norm limit of its finite partial sums, and the coefficient of $h_{00}$ is $\langle f,h_{00}\rangle/\|h_{00}\|^2=\int_{R_{ab}}f/ab=0$, so those partial sums use only indices $(m,n)\ne(0,0)$ and $f\in S$. Hence $S=Z$: the remaining Neumann profiles are complete in the zero-mean subspace and not in all of $L^2(R_{ab})$ because the constant function is orthogonal to them and nonzero. The constant $h_{00}=1$ stays in the full mathematical basis, while the physical TE candidate family excludes it by the Maxwell index restriction of [[pthm-em-rectangular-mode-candidates]] (c), so no nonzero positive-frequency TE reconstruction is asserted from the constant scalar profile; the Dirichlet profiles keep their full scalar completeness. [F1, algebra]

1.2 [Clause (b)] By [F2] the finite separated Fourier modes are dense in the rectangular reflection class at every time, every initial datum in the class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of the lossless first-order system in the class, and the energy $\frac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+|B|^2/\mu)$ is constant along the solution; this distributional system is the explicitly adopted weak material evolution of the reflection model. The energy equals $\int_Qu$ for the weak stored-energy density $u=\frac12(\varepsilon|E|^2+\mu^{-1}|B|^2)$ of [F5], which is defined almost everywhere and nonnegative; its integrability and constancy are furnished by the supplier, and no nonlinear weak Poynting identity is asserted. Finally, the four macroscopic equations with $D=\varepsilon E$ and $H=B/\mu$ follow distributionally from the two evolution equations and the divergence constraints of the class: $\operatorname{div}D=\varepsilon\operatorname{div}E=0$ and $\operatorname{div}B=0$ are the class constraints, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ is the second evolution equation, and $\operatorname{curl}H=\mu^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B=\mu^{-1}(\varepsilon\mu)\partial_tE=\partial_tD$ uses the first evolution equation $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$. [F2, F5, algebra]

1.3 [Clause (c), spectral content] Assume the full Axiom of Choice as in [F3], let $\Omega$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ cavity and let $X,V,H$, $\{u_j\}$, $\lambda_j\ge0$ be the classes and eigenbasis of [F3]. Then the curl form on $V$ has the complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis with nonnegative finite-multiplicity eigenvalues tending to infinity when $H$ is infinite dimensional and a finite-dimensional zero eigenspace retained; the eigen-equation holds distributionally with the PEC trace, each $u_j$ has a $C^\infty$ representative on the closure, and the full-$X$ variational identity holds for every $v\in X$. With $v_{\mathrm{wave}}=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1/2}>0$, the associated second-order electric wave has displacement in $C(\mathbb R;V)$ and velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$ for arbitrary initial data in $V\times H$, finite modal sums converge in these norms uniformly on compact times, and its zero eigenmodes may be affine in time. These are the spectral and wave assertions of [F3], taken with the exact hypotheses of the suppliers. [F3]

2.1 [Clause (c), first-order modal equation] Let $J$ be an open time interval and let a strong first-order solution obey the hypotheses of the Statement: $E\in C^1(J;H)\cap C(J;V)$, $B\in C^1(J;L^2)\cap C(J;H(\operatorname{curl}))$, with the first-order equations holding as $L^2$ identities and both distributional divergence constraints, the magnetic normal-zero condition $\int_\Omega B(t)\cdot\nabla\psi=0$ for every smooth scalar $\psi$ on the closure, and $E(t)\in V$ encoding the electric tangential-zero data; no magnetic membership in $X$ is assumed. To pair $\operatorname{curl}B$ against the smooth eigenfield $u_j$, use the collar cutoff of [F4]: write $s$ for the inward normal coordinate in a tubular neighbourhood of the compact boundary, so that $|n\times u_j|\le Cs$ in the collar because $u_j$ is smooth on the closure with $n\times u_j=0$, and let $\eta_\delta$ be the standard smooth step with $\eta_\delta=0$ for $s\le\delta$ and $1$ for $s\ge2\delta$. Then $\eta_\delta u_j\to u_j$ and $\operatorname{curl}(\eta_\delta u_j)\to\operatorname{curl}u_j$ in $L^2$ as $\delta\to0$, since the derivative-cutoff term is supported on a layer of volume $O(\delta)$ and is bounded by $C/\delta$ times $O(s)$; the distributional identity of [F4] on the compactly supported smooth test $\eta_\delta u_j$ gives $\langle\operatorname{curl}B,\eta_\delta u_j\rangle=\langle B,\operatorname{curl}(\eta_\delta u_j)\rangle$, and Cauchy–Schwarz with the two limits gives $\langle\operatorname{curl}B,u_j\rangle=\langle B,\operatorname{curl}u_j\rangle$ for the actual graph-regular field $B$. Hence $a_j'=\langle E',u_j\rangle=v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\langle\operatorname{curl}B,u_j\rangle=v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\langle B,\operatorname{curl}u_j\rangle$ on $J$. If $\lambda_j=0$, the same identity at $v=u_j$ gives $\|\operatorname{curl}u_j\|_2^2=0$, so $\operatorname{curl}u_j=0$ and $a_j'=v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\langle B,\operatorname{curl}u_j\rangle=0$: the electric zero modes are constant under first-order Maxwell evolution, while the unrestricted second-order wave of step 1.3 retains its affine zero modes. This distinguishes first-order Maxwell data from arbitrary second-order $V\times H$ data; the pairing imposed no magnetic electric-type trace, and the divergence constraints and the declared weak magnetic normal condition remain part of the model. [step 1.3, F3, F4]

3.1 [Clause (d)] Clause (a) is step 1.1, clause (b) is step 1.2, and clause (c) is steps 1.3 and 2.1. ## Example

Let $\varepsilon,\mu>0$, $a,b>0$, $\omega>0$, $\beta>0$ with $\beta^2=\omega^2\varepsilon\mu-(\pi/a)^2>0$, and put $\omega_c:=\pi/(a\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu})$, $\theta:=\beta x_3-\omega t$. In the rectangular guide of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]] with cross-section $(0,a)\times(0,b)$, take the TE candidate of [[pthm-em-rectangular-mode-candidates]](a) with $(m,n)=(1,0)$, whose amplitudes are $$\tilde E=\bigl(0,\,i\omega\mu\tfrac{a}{\pi}\sin\tfrac{\pi x_1}{a},\,0\bigr),\qquad \tilde H=\bigl(-i\beta\tfrac{a}{\pi}\sin\tfrac{\pi x_1}{a},\,0,\,\cos\tfrac{\pi x_1}{a}\bigr).$$ Then the real fields $E=\operatorname{Re}(\tilde Ee^{i\theta})$, $B=\mu\operatorname{Re}(\tilde He^{i\theta})$ are smooth, have $E_z=0$ (TE) with $E$ linearly polarized along $e_2$, satisfy the source-free lossless macroscopic equations and the PEC wall conditions, and carry a half-sine standing profile $\sin(\pi x_1/a)$ in $x_1$ with a traveling wave in $x_3$. The cutoff of this mode is $\omega_c=\pi/(a\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu})$: real nonzero $\beta$ exists exactly for $\omega>\omega_c$, at $\omega=\omega_c$ the mode is at cutoff ($\beta=0$), and for $\omega<\omega_c$ it is evanescent. If $a\ge b$, then $\omega_c=\pi/(a\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu})$ is the lowest cutoff of all TE indices and of all modes (attained also by $(m,n)=(0,1)$ when $a=b$); the case $(m,n)=(0,0)$ is not a mode by the index restriction of the theorem. This is an explicit conditional candidate of the adopted model; it asserts no measurement and no completeness.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Constants $\varepsilon,\mu>0$, $a,b>0$, $\omega>0$, $\beta>0$ with $\beta^2=\omega^2\varepsilon\mu-(\pi/a)^2>0$, $\omega_c:=\pi/(a\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu})$ and $\theta:=\beta x_3-\omega t$; the rectangular guide of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]] with cross-section $(0,a)\times(0,b)$ and the SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

[F1] The TE candidate theorem [[pthm-em-rectangular-mode-candidates]] (a): for indices $(m,n)\ne(0,0)$ with $h_{mn}=\cos\frac{m\pi x_1}{a}\cos\frac{n\pi x_2}{b}$ and $k_{mn}^2=(\frac{m\pi}{a})^2+(\frac{n\pi}{b})^2$, and with $\beta^2=\omega^2\varepsilon\mu-k_{mn}^2$, the amplitudes $\tilde E=-\frac{i\omega\mu}{k_{mn}^2}e_z\times\nabla_th_{mn}$, $\tilde H=\frac{i\beta}{k_{mn}^2}\nabla_th_{mn}+e_zh_{mn}$ give smooth real fields $E=\operatorname{Re}(\tilde Ee^{i\theta})$, $B=\mu\operatorname{Re}(\tilde He^{i\theta})$ that are TE, satisfy the four source-free lossless macroscopic equations and the PEC wall conditions, and whose cutoff is $\omega_c=k_c/\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu}$ with the alternatives of clause (d); clause (c) excludes $(0,0)$.

[F2] The profile identities of [[lem-em-rectangle-mode-profile-identities]] for $(m,n)=(1,0)$: $h_{10}=\cos\frac{\pi x_1}{a}$, $k_{10}=\pi/a$, $\Delta_th_{10}=-(\pi/a)^2h_{10}$, $\partial_1h_{10}=0$ at $x_1\in\{0,a\}$ and $\partial_2h_{10}=0$ at $x_2\in\{0,b\}$.



## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct: instantiate the TE candidate at $(1,0)$, read off the amplitudes and the wall conditions, and evaluate the cutoff and the index comparison.

1.1 [Instantiation] With $(m,n)=(1,0)$ one has $k_c:=\pi/a$, $\nabla_th_{10}=-\frac{\pi}{a}\sin\frac{\pi x_1}{a}e_1$ and $e_z\times\nabla_th_{10}=-\frac{\pi}{a}\sin\frac{\pi x_1}{a}e_2$ by [F2] and the coordinate formula for the cross product, so the amplitudes of [F1] become $\tilde E=-(i\omega\mu a/\pi)(-\sin\frac{\pi x_1}{a})e_2=(0,i\omega\mu\frac{a}{\pi}\sin\frac{\pi x_1}{a},0)$ and $\tilde H=(i\beta a^2/\pi^2)(-\frac{\pi}{a}\sin\frac{\pi x_1}{a})e_1+\cos\frac{\pi x_1}{a}e_z=(-i\beta\frac{a}{\pi}\sin\frac{\pi x_1}{a},0,\cos\frac{\pi x_1}{a})$, exactly as displayed. The theorem supplies smoothness, the four source-free equations, the TE property $E_z=0$ and the PEC wall conditions, and the first component $\tilde E_1=\tilde E_3=0$ shows that $E$ is polarized along $e_2$; the real fields are $E=\omega\mu\frac{a}{\pi}\sin\frac{\pi x_1}{a}\operatorname{Re}(ie^{i\theta})\,e_2$ and $B=\mu\operatorname{Re}(\tilde He^{i\theta})$, so the transverse factor $\sin(\pi x_1/a)$ is a fixed half-sine standing profile and the phase $\theta=\beta x_3-\omega t$ is a traveling wave in $x_3$. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Cutoff and propagation alternatives] Applying clause (d) of [F1] with $k_c=\pi/a$ gives $\omega_c=\pi/(a\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu})$: real longitudinal wave numbers with $\beta^2=\omega^2\varepsilon\mu-(\pi/a)^2$ exist exactly for $\omega\ge\omega_c$, with $\beta\ne0$ exactly for $\omega>\omega_c$ and $\beta=0$ at $\omega=\omega_c$; for $\omega<\omega_c$ the two algebraic roots are $\beta=\pm i\sqrt{(\pi/a)^2-\omega^2\varepsilon\mu}$ and the same verified fields carry the factor $e^{-\operatorname{Im}\beta\,x_3}$, so the mode is evanescent. [step 1.1, F1]

2.2 [Lowest cutoff for $a\ge b$] Let $(m,n)\ne(0,0)$ be any TE index pair and let $k_{mn}^2=(\frac{m\pi}{a})^2+(\frac{n\pi}{b})^2$. If $m\ge1$ then $k_{mn}^2\ge(\pi/a)^2$; if $m=0$ then $n\ge1$ and $k_{mn}^2\ge(\pi/b)^2\ge(\pi/a)^2$ because $a\ge b$. Hence $k_{mn}^2\ge\pi^2/a^2=k_{10}^2$, with equality possible only for $m=1,n=0$, or for $m=0,n=1$ when $a=b$; since the cutoff $\omega_c=k_c/\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu}$ is increasing in $k_c$, the cutoff $\pi/(a\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu})$ of the $(1,0)$ candidate is the lowest cutoff of all TE indices. Every TM index has $m,n\ge1$ by [F1], so its $k_{mn}^2\ge\pi^2/a^2+\pi^2/b^2>\pi^2/a^2$ and its cutoff is strictly larger; and $(m,n)=(0,0)$ is not a mode by the index restriction of [F1]. Thus $\omega_c=\pi/(a\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu})$ is the lowest cutoff of all modes, attained also by $(0,1)$ at $a=b$. [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 [Scope] The displayed fields are an explicit conditional candidate of the adopted lossless model, with the stated cutoff and lower-bound comparison; the quantities are declared model parameters, no measurement, resonance observation, completeness or uniqueness is asserted, and no empirical premise is used. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, F1] ∎

## Example

Let $a,b,d>0$ and $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ be constants, put $E_{\mathrm{sp}}(x):=e_1\sin\frac{\pi x_2}{b}\sin\frac{\pi x_3}{d}$, and for $\omega>0$ define $E(x,t):=E_{\mathrm{sp}}(x)\cos(\omega t)$ and $B(x,t):=-\frac1\omega(\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}})(x)\sin(\omega t)$, where the curl is the fixed-time spatial curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Then $E,B$ are smooth, $\operatorname{div}E_{\mathrm{sp}}=0$, $\Delta E_{\mathrm{sp}}=-[(\pi/b)^2+(\pi/d)^2]E_{\mathrm{sp}}$, and $E,B$ satisfy the four source-free macroscopic equations on the box $\Omega_c=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times(0,d)$ in the lossless isotropic scalar branch exactly when $$\omega^2=\frac{1}{\varepsilon\mu}\Bigl[\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{b}\Bigr)^2+\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{d}\Bigr)^2\Bigr];$$ with that resonance, $n\times E=0$ and $n\cdot B=0$ hold on all six walls, so $(E,B)$ is a PEC cavity mode. It is the cutoff instance $\beta=0$ of the TM family of [[pthm-em-rectangular-mode-candidates]](b) taken with axis $e_1$, cross-section $(0,b)\times(0,d)$ and indices $(m,n)=(1,1)$: the field is independent of $x_1$, which is why it also satisfies the $x_1=0$ and $x_1=a$ end-cap conditions for every box length $a>0$. The example asserts a conditional model solution, not an observed resonance.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Constants $a,b,d>0$ and $\varepsilon,\mu>0$; $E_{\mathrm{sp}}(x):=e_1\sin\frac{\pi x_2}{b}\sin\frac{\pi x_3}{d}$; for $\omega>0$ the fields $E(x,t):=E_{\mathrm{sp}}(x)\cos(\omega t)$ and $B(x,t):=-\frac1\omega(\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}})(x)\sin(\omega t)$ on the box $\Omega_c=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times(0,d)$; the fixed-time spatial curl and divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]; the box geometry, its six open walls and the PEC conditions of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]].

[F1] Profile identities: with $e_{11}(y_1,y_2):=\sin\frac{\pi y_1}{b}\sin\frac{\pi y_2}{d}$ on the rectangle $(0,b)\times(0,d)$ one has $\Delta e_{11}=-k_{11}^2e_{11}$ with $k_{11}^2=(\pi/b)^2+(\pi/d)^2$, $\partial_1e_{11}=0$ at $y_1\in\{0,b\}$... the traces are $e_{11}=0$ on the rectangle boundary; in particular $\sin0=\sin\pi=0$ and the second derivatives of the sine factors are $-\frac{\pi^2}{b^2}\sin\frac{\pi y_1}{b}$ and $-\frac{\pi^2}{d^2}\sin\frac{\pi y_2}{d}$ ([[lem-em-rectangle-mode-profile-identities]] (b), (a)).

[F2] Transverse identities with axis $e_1$: for a $z$-independent profile $h$ regarded on the splitting $\mathbb R^3=\mathbb R^2\oplus\mathbb Re_1$ with coordinates $(x_2,x_3)$, $\operatorname{curl}(e_1h)=-e_1\times\nabla^{(2,3)}h$, $\operatorname{div}(e_1h)=\partial_1h=0$, and $e_1\times(e_1\times v)=-v$ for transverse $v$ ([[lem-em-transverse-vector-identities]] (a),(b) applied with $e_z:=e_1$).

[F3] The TM family of [[pthm-em-rectangular-mode-candidates]] (b) with axis $e_1$, cross-section $(0,b)\times(0,d)$, indices $(1,1)$ and $\beta=0$: $k_c^2=k_{11}^2$, and the amplitudes $\tilde E=\frac{i\beta}{k_c^2}\nabla_te+e_ze$, $\tilde H=\frac{i\omega\varepsilon}{k_c^2}e_z\times\nabla_te$ at $\beta=0$ become $\tilde E=e_1e_{11}$ and $\tilde H=\frac{i\omega\varepsilon}{k_{11}^2}e_1\times\nabla e_{11}$; the theorem gives smoothness, the four source-free equations at the cutoff $\omega^2=k_c^2/(\varepsilon\mu)$, and the PEC conditions on the four faces with normals $\pm e_2,\pm e_3$ ([[pthm-em-rectangular-mode-candidates]] (b),(d)).



## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct: compute the divergence, Laplacian and curl of the explicit spatial profile, verify the four equations and the six wall conditions, and identify the field with the cutoff TM instance.

1.1 [The spatial profile, the equations and the resonance] The profile has only its first component, independent of $x_1$, so $\operatorname{div}E_{\mathrm{sp}}=\partial_1(\sin\frac{\pi x_2}{b}\sin\frac{\pi x_3}{d})=0$ and $\Delta E_{\mathrm{sp}}=e_1(\partial_2^2+\partial_3^2)e_{11}=-\bigl[(\pi/b)^2+(\pi/d)^2\bigr]E_{\mathrm{sp}}=-k_{11}^2E_{\mathrm{sp}}$ by [F1]. Hence $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}E_{\mathrm{sp}}\cos\omega t=0$ and $\operatorname{div}B=-\frac1\omega\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}})\sin\omega t=0$ (a divergence of a curl vanishes componentwise by the equality of mixed partials of the smooth profile). Further $\operatorname{curl}E=(\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}})\cos\omega t$ and $-\partial_tB=(\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}})\cos\omega t$, so Faraday's law holds identically. For Amp\`ere's law compute $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}}$: by [F2] $\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}}=\operatorname{curl}(e_1e_{11})=-e_1\times\nabla e_{11}=(0,\partial_3e_{11},-\partial_2e_{11})$, whose curl is $\bigl(\partial_2(-\partial_2e_{11})-\partial_3(\partial_3e_{11}),0,0\bigr)=-(\Delta e_{11})e_1=k_{11}^2e_1e_{11}=k_{11}^2E_{\mathrm{sp}}$ by [F1]; therefore $\operatorname{curl}H=\frac1\mu\operatorname{curl}B=-\frac{1}{\omega\mu}k_{11}^2E_{\mathrm{sp}}\sin\omega t$ and $\partial_tD=\varepsilon\partial_tE=-\varepsilon\omega E_{\mathrm{sp}}\sin\omega t$, which agree exactly when $k_{11}^2=\omega^2\varepsilon\mu$, i.e. when $\omega^2=\frac{1}{\varepsilon\mu}[(\pi/b)^2+(\pi/d)^2]$. The fields are smooth because $E_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is a product of sines and $\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}}$ a finite combination of such products, and both are independent of $x_1$. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [The six wall conditions] On the walls $x_1=0$ and $x_1=a$ with normals $\mp e_1$: $n\times E=\mp e_1\times E=\mp\cos\omega t\,e_1\times E_{\mathrm{sp}}=0$ since $E_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is parallel to $e_1$, and $n\cdot B=\mp B_1=\pm\frac1\omega(\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}})_1\sin\omega t=0$ because $(\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}})_1=\partial_2(E_{\mathrm{sp}})_3-\partial_3(E_{\mathrm{sp}})_2=0$. On the walls $x_2=0$ and $x_2=b$ with normals $\mp e_2$: $e_2\times E=E_1(e_2\times e_1)=-E_1e_3$ and $E_1=\sin\frac{\pi x_2}{b}\sin\frac{\pi x_3}{d}\cos\omega t$ vanishes because $\sin\frac{\pi x_2}{b}=0$ there, so $n\times E=0$; and $n\cdot B=\mp B_2=\pm\frac1\omega(\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}})_2\sin\omega t$ with $(\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}})_2=\partial_3(E_{\mathrm{sp}})_1-\partial_1(E_{\mathrm{sp}})_3=\frac{\pi}{d}\sin\frac{\pi x_2}{b}\cos\frac{\pi x_3}{d}$, which vanishes at $x_2=0,b$. On the walls $x_3=0$ and $x_3=d$ with normals $\mp e_3$: $e_3\times E=E_1e_2$, whose coefficient $E_1$ vanishes because $\sin\frac{\pi x_3}{d}=0$ there, so $n\times E=0$; and $n\cdot B=\mp B_3=\pm\frac1\omega(\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}})_3\sin\omega t$ with $(\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}})_3=\partial_1(E_{\mathrm{sp}})_2-\partial_2(E_{\mathrm{sp}})_1=-\frac{\pi}{b}\cos\frac{\pi x_2}{b}\sin\frac{\pi x_3}{d}$, which vanishes at $x_3=0,d$. Thus all six walls satisfy $n\times E=0$ and $n\cdot B=0$ at resonance. [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

3.1 [Identification with the cutoff TM instance] In the setting of [F3] with axis $e_1$, cross-section $(0,b)\times(0,d)$, indices $(1,1)$ and $\beta=0$, the dispersion relation $\beta^2=\omega^2\varepsilon\mu-k_{11}^2$ at $\beta=0$ is exactly the resonance $k_{11}^2=\omega^2\varepsilon\mu$ of step 1.1, $e_{11}=\sin\frac{\pi x_2}{b}\sin\frac{\pi x_3}{d}$, and the amplitudes become $\tilde E=e_1e_{11}$ and $\tilde H=\frac{i\omega\varepsilon}{k_{11}^2}e_1\times\nabla e_{11}$. Then $\theta=-\omega t$, $E=\operatorname{Re}(\tilde Ee^{-i\omega t})=e_1e_{11}\cos\omega t=E_{\mathrm{sp}}\cos\omega t$, and $B=\mu\operatorname{Re}(\tilde He^{-i\omega t})=\mu\frac{\omega\varepsilon}{k_{11}^2}(e_1\times\nabla e_{11})\sin\omega t=-\frac1\omega\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}}\sin\omega t$ because $\operatorname{curl}E_{\mathrm{sp}}=-e_1\times\nabla e_{11}$ [F2] and $\mu\omega\varepsilon/k_{11}^2=1/\omega$ at resonance. The amplitudes are independent of $x_1$, which is why the end-cap conditions on $x_1=0,a$ hold for every box length $a>0$; the theorem's clause (d) supplies the resonance condition and clause (b) the guide-wall conditions on the four faces with normals $\pm e_2,\pm e_3$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F2, F3, algebra]

4.1 [Scope] The displayed pair is an explicit conditional standing-wave mode of the lossless isotropic scalar branch in the rectangular perfectly conducting cavity, with the exact resonance condition and the full wall check, identified as the cutoff $\beta=0$ TM$(1,1)$ instance with axis $e_1$; the example asserts a model solution and not an observed resonance, and no measurement, completeness or empirical claim is made. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F3] ∎
