## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the point-source change-of-variables suppliers below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]] ($c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$), let $q\in\mathbb R$ and let $z$, $v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline of a point charge, [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the constant $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), and let $\rho,J$ be the point-source distributions of that charge on the worldline in the declared point-source class of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) (the $C^3$ branch of the point-current construction). Let $(\varphi,A)$ be the retarded history pairings of [[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]](b) -- the framework's retarded construction for this source under the adopted selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]] -- and define $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ on the off-worldline domain $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]). Then:

(a) [Potentials] $\varphi=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A=\beta\varphi/c$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, where $r,\kappa,\beta$ are the retarded data of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]](b); the zero extensions of $\varphi,A$ to $\Gamma$ are locally integrable on $\Omega$.

(b) [Exact fields] On $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, $$E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}},\qquad E_{\mathrm{vel}}=\frac{C(1-|\beta|^2)(n-\beta)}{\kappa^3r^2},\qquad E_{\mathrm{acc}}=\frac{C\,n\times\bigl((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta\bigr)}{c\,\kappa^3r},\qquad B=\frac{n\times E}{c},$$ and $E,B$ are of class $C^1$ there; the velocity part obeys $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$.

(c) [Uniform far-zone remainder] For every emission event $s_0$ and direction $n\in S^2$, with $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$, $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\dot\beta_0:=z''(s_0)/c$ and $\kappa_0:=1-n\cdot\beta_0$: $(x_r,t_r)\in\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, and $$E(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C\,n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0\bigr)}{c\,\kappa_0^3\,r}+\rho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad|\rho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C|\frac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}\,r^{-2},\qquad B(x_r,t_r)=\frac{n\times E(x_r,t_r)}{c};$$ the bound is uniform in $n$ at fixed $s_0$.

(d) [Scope] These are the stipulated retarded model fields of the prescribed charge: the item identifies, through the same adopted causal selection used by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]] for the compact branch, the point-source potentials and fields of the model, and proves their exact form and bounds. It asserts no value of the fields on the worldline $\Gamma$ (where the formulas are undefined and the self-field is singular), no integral or energy statement, no self-force and no radiation reaction, and derives no mass. The uniform bound $v_*<c$ and the exclusion of $\Gamma$ are essential hypotheses; the companion example page shows that a merely pointwise subluminal curve can fail to have a retarded root, and no uniformity in the emission event $s_0$ is claimed ($z''$ is not assumed bounded). The signed constant $C$ is retained in every displayed formula while absolute-value bounds use $|C|$.

(e) [Constructed weak solution] Let $\Phi,\Upsilon$ be the global regular potential distributions in (a), and let $\mathcal E=-\nabla\Phi-\partial_t\Upsilon$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{curl}\Upsilon$. By [[thm-em-retarded-point-distributional-maxwell]], their representatives are exactly the locally integrable zero extensions of the displayed off-worldline fields. They satisfy all four identities of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) with the proper all-time point pair $\rho,J$; the volume source parts are zero. Thus they are an admitted point-source model of the explicit physical adoption [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], under the same retarded selection. The potentials satisfy $W\Phi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $W\Upsilon=\mu_0J$ and the distributional Lorenz identity. This existence and solution property is supplied by the mathematical theorem, not by the selection postulate or by the compact-source theorem. The zero extensions on the null graph give no physically defined self-field and no nonlinear products there. All original exact field, regularity and uniform far-zone branches remain as stated. On each product neighborhood disjoint from $\Gamma$ the fields satisfy the smooth source-free Maxwell equations. Consequently any use of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] by the radiation items is local on such neighborhoods, with $\rho=J=0$; it neither applies that smooth theorem across the point source nor forms self-work or a global finite-energy identity.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]); the laboratory chart, units and constants of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]]; a retarded point-geometry datum: $q\in\mathbb R$, $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^3$ with $|z'(s)|\le v_*<c$, and the off-worldline domain $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ with the retarded data $s,r,n,\beta,\kappa,\dot\beta$ of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]]; the constant $C=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$.

[F1] Retarded point geometry: on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ the root $s=s(x,t)<t$ solves $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$, is $C^3$, satisfies $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$ and $\nabla_xs=-n/(c\kappa)$, and $\kappa=1-n\cdot\beta\in[1-v_*/c,1+v_*/c]$; at an emission event $s_0$ and direction $n\in S^2$, the event $(x_r,t_r)=(z(s_0)+rn,s_0+r/c)$ lies in $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ and has root $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$. ([[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (a)-(c))

[F2] Point-source history pairings: for the point-source distributions $\rho,J$ attached to $q$ and $z$, the retarded-history pairings $\Phi,\Upsilon$ define distributions on $\Omega$, are finite for every test, and satisfy $\langle\Phi,\psi\rangle=\int_{\Omega\setminus\Gamma}C\psi/(\kappa r)$ and $\langle\Upsilon,\psi\rangle=\int_{\Omega\setminus\Gamma}(\beta/c)C\psi/(\kappa r)$ componentwise; consequently $\varphi=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A=\beta\varphi/c$ are $C^2$ functions off the worldline whose locally integrable zero extensions have $\Phi,\Upsilon$ as their regular distributions. ([[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]] (b))

[F3] Exact fields: with $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, one has $E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}}$ with the displayed velocity and acceleration parts, $B=n\times E/c$, both fields $C^1$ off the worldline, and $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$. ([[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]] (c))

[F4] Uniform far-zone remainder: at the emission sphere $E(x_r,t_r)=C\,n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)/(c\kappa_0^3r)+\rho_E$ with $|\rho_E|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$ uniformly over $n\in S^2$ at fixed $s_0$, and $B(x_r,t_r)=n\times E(x_r,t_r)/c$. ([[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]] (d))

[F5] Distributional point-source Maxwell theorem: $W\Phi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $W\Upsilon=\mu_0J$ and $\operatorname{div}\Upsilon+c^{-2}\partial_t\Phi=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega)$; the distributions $\mathcal E=-\nabla\Phi-\partial_t\Upsilon$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{curl}\Upsilon$ satisfy the four distributional Maxwell identities with the point pair; and off $\Gamma$ they restrict to the exact $C^1$ fields of [F3], the locally integrable zero extensions of the field formulas being their regular representatives. ([[thm-em-retarded-point-distributional-maxwell]] (a)-(c))

[F6] Weak source class and solution predicate: the all-time $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline with its proper graph is an admitted point source, the predicate consists of the four vanishing distributional pairings with the source pairings of the declared point class, and no product of two distributions is formed anywhere. ([[def-em-weak-sources]] (b),(e),(f))

[F7] Adopted singular-source physics: point-source models satisfying the weak predicate are the adopted physical models of the separate postulate, which the earlier smooth-source postulate neither covers nor implies. ([[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]])

[F8] Adopted selection: the retarded branch with no free addition is the framework's selected branch, and for the point-source branch the same selection is adopted in the weak equations of the singular-source model. ([[post-em-radiation-selection]] (b),(c))

[F9] Conventions: $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\nabla\times A$ are those of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] with field classes of [[def-em-fields]]; $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $C=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$ are the SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the curve $s\mapsto(z(s),s)$ is the laboratory reading of a prescribed massive future timelike worldline by [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]. ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]])

[F10] The same adopted causal selection is used by the compact-source theorem [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]] for its branch, and that theorem explicitly leaves point sources to the point-source items of its page; the uniform speed bound and the exclusion of $\Gamma$ are essential hypotheses of the point construction. ([[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]] (b),(g))

[F11] Local Poynting balance: for jointly $C^1$ fields solving the smooth source-free vacuum Maxwell equations on a region, the local identity $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E$ of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] holds there, and on a product neighborhood disjoint from $\Gamma$ the point pair restricts to zero. ([[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] (a),(c))

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct identification; clauses (a)-(d) instantiate the retarded point-geometry datum and the two point-source suppliers, and clause (e) instantiates the distributional point-source theorem and the weak solution predicate, with the physical adoption supplied separately by the postulates.

1.1 Potentials (a). By [F1] the root and retarded data $s,r,n,\beta,\kappa$ are defined and $C^3$-regular on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ with $\kappa\ge1-v_*/c>0$, and $C=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$ is the stated signed constant [F9]. Clause (b) of [F2] identifies the retarded-history pairings with the exact integrals $\int_{\Omega\setminus\Gamma}C\psi/(\kappa r)$ and $\int_{\Omega\setminus\Gamma}(\beta/c)C\psi/(\kappa r)$, and states that the potentials are the $C^2$ functions $\varphi=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A=\beta\varphi/c$ off the worldline whose zero extensions to $\Gamma$ are locally integrable. This is (a). [F1, F2, F9, algebra]

2.1 Exact fields (b). Clause (c) of [F3] gives, at every event of $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, the split $E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}}$ with the displayed velocity and acceleration parts, the relation $B=n\times E/c$, the $C^1$ regularity of both fields, and the velocity bound $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$; the fields are defined as $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ with the conventions of [F9], and the constant $C$ is retained with its sign in the field formulas while the bound uses $|C|$. This is (b). [step 1.1, F3, F9, algebra]

2.2 Uniform far-zone remainder (c). Fix $s_0\in\mathbb R$ and $n\in S^2$; by [F1](c) the event $(x_r,t_r)=(z(s_0)+rn,s_0+r/c)$ lies in $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ and its root is $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, so the retarded data at that event are exactly $\beta_0,\dot\beta_0,\kappa_0$ and $r$. Clause (d) of [F4] then gives the displayed decomposition of $E(x_r,t_r)$ with the uniform bound $|\rho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$ over $n\in S^2$ at fixed $s_0$, together with $B(x_r,t_r)=n\times E(x_r,t_r)/c$. This is (c). [step 1.1, F1, F4, algebra]

3.1 Scope (d). The identification of the retarded construction of clause (a)-(b) with the model fields of the prescribed charge is the adopted causal selection of [F8], the same selection used by the compact-source theorem [F10]; nothing in steps 1.1-2.2 assigns a field value on $\Gamma$ (the formulas require $r>0$), forms a product of the singular source with a field, or proves a self-force, radiation-reaction, energy or mass statement, and [F10] records that the compact-source branch explicitly leaves point sources to this page. The bound in (c) is uniform in $n$ at fixed $s_0$ only, since $\dot\beta_0$ and $\kappa_0^{-3}$ depend on the emission event and $z''$ is not assumed bounded. This is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.2, F8, F10, algebra]

4.1 Constructed weak solution (e) and conclusion. By [F5](a) the potential distributions of [F2] satisfy $W\Phi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $W\Upsilon=\mu_0J$ and the distributional Lorenz identity, and by [F5](b) the field distributions $\mathcal E,\mathcal B$ satisfy all four distributional Maxwell identities with the point pair $\rho,J$; [F5](c) identifies their representatives with the locally integrable zero extensions of the off-worldline fields of [F3] and records that the off-worldline $C^1$ fields satisfy the source-free classical Maxwell equations. The all-time $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline with its proper graph is an admitted point source of the declared class [F6], the source pairings are those of the predicate, and the volume source parts vanish; hence the four identities are exactly the solution predicate of [F6](e) with $(\rho,J)$, and by the explicit physical adoption [F7] under the same retarded selection [F8] these constructed weak fields are the model fields of the point charge. This is the solution property claimed in (e); it is supplied by the mathematical theorem and not by the selection postulate. No product of distributions is formed anywhere ([F6](f)), and the zero extension on the null graph gives no physically defined self-field there. Finally, on a product neighborhood disjoint from $\Gamma$ the point pair restricts to the zero source so that the smooth source-free Maxwell equations of [F5](c) hold and the local Poynting identity [F11] applies there with $\rho=J=0$; it is never applied across the point source and forms no self-work or global finite-energy identity. This completes (e) and, with steps 1.1-3.1, all clauses (a)-(e). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, F5, F6, F7, F8, F11, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $q\in\mathbb R$, let $z,v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline, $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), let $s_0$ be an emission event with $z'(s_0)=0$ (the charge is momentarily at rest in the laboratory chart), and put $a:=z''(s_0)$ and, for $n\in S^2$, $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$. Let $E,B$ be the retarded fields of the charge given by [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] and $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Then:

(a) [Field on the emitted sphere] For every $r>0$ and $n\in S^2$, $$E(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C\,n\times(n\times a)}{c^2r}+\rho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad|\rho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C|\frac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}r^{-2},\qquad B(x_r,t_r)=\frac{n\times E(x_r,t_r)}{c}.$$

(b) [Angular flux density] The limits $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n):=\lim_{r\to\infty}r^2\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C^{2}\,|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}},\qquad P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\int_{S^2}\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)\,d\sigma(n),$$ exist with the convergence uniform in $n\in S^2$; $d\sigma$ is the polar surface measure of the unit sphere (equal to the chart surface measure by [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]).

(c) [Total power] $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\cdot\frac{8\pi}{3}|a|^{2}=\frac{q^2|a|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ the Larmor power of the momentarily resting prescribed charge.

(d) [Angular distribution] Writing $\theta$ for the angle between $n$ and $a$ (with $\theta$ undefined only when $a=0$, in which case $dP/d\sigma\equiv0$), $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)=\frac{q^2|a|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\sin^2\theta:$$ the radiation pattern vanishes along the instantaneous acceleration axis and is maximal in the perpendicular plane; $\int_{S^2}dP/d\sigma\,d\sigma=P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$. If $a=0$ all displayed radiation quantities vanish.

(e) [Scope and conventions] The result is exact at an emission event at which the charge is instantaneously at rest in the laboratory chart: then $\kappa_0(n)=1$ for every $n$, so no retarded-time conversion factor appears and the displayed limits are simultaneously the fixed-sphere flux and the emitted power per unit emission time. The item uses only the prescribed worldline and the retarded model fields -- it is not a mechanical evolution law, does not assert a self-force or radiation reaction, derives no mass, and makes no empirical or measurement claim. For a general emission event the exact formula and its low-speed comparison are supplied by clause (f); 'slow' motion alone is never substituted for an error bound. The prescribed curve, the uniform subluminal bound and $z'(s_0)=0$ are hypotheses; for a varying-velocity worldline the instantaneous rest event is a single parameter value, not an interval.

(f) [General low-speed branch] At any emission event, without imposing $z'(s_0)=0$ for this clause, define emitted power by the weighted far-zone flux integral $\kappa_0(n)\,r^2\,n\cdot S$ on the emitted spheres, with $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot\beta_0$, $\beta_0=z'(s_0)/c$ and $|\beta_0|\le v_*/c$. The same field formula and angular computation give $$P_{\mathrm{em}}=\gamma_0^{6}\bigl(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\bigr)\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}.$$ Put $P_{\mathrm L}=q^{2}|a|^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$. For $|\beta_0|\le\delta<1$, $$P_{\mathrm L}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}\le(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L},\qquad |P_{\mathrm{em}}-P_{\mathrm L}|\le3\delta^{2}(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L}.$$ This includes $q=0$ or $a=0$ without division by $P_{\mathrm L}$. Uniform angular comparison is also explicit: if $N_\beta=n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)$, $N_0=n\times(n\times a)$ and $H_\beta=q^{2}|N_\beta|^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3}\kappa_0^{5})$, $H_0=q^{2}|N_0|^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3})$, then $$|H_\beta-H_0|\le\frac{q^2|a|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^3}\,\delta\left[\frac{2+\delta}{(1-\delta)^5}+\frac{5}{(1-\delta)^6}\right]$$ for all $n$. The exact rest-event clauses (a)-(e) retain their hypotheses; this additional branch supplies the general low-speed comparison, not a mechanical loss law.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]); the laboratory chart, units and constants of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]]; a retarded point-geometry datum with the off-worldline retarded data $s,r,n,\beta,\kappa,\dot\beta$ of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] and the point charge parameter $q$, $C=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$; the retarded fields $E,B$ of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] with $S=E\times B/\mu_0$; the rest event $s_0$ with $z'(s_0)=0$, $a=z''(s_0)$, and in clause (f) a general emission event with $\beta_0=z'(s_0)/c$, $|\beta_0|\le v_*/c$, $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot\beta_0$.

[F1] Lienard-Wiechert point fields: off the worldline $E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}}$ with $E_{\mathrm{vel}}=C(1-|\beta|^{2})(n-\beta)/(\kappa^{3}r^{2})$, $E_{\mathrm{acc}}=C\,n\times((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta)/(c\kappa^{3}r)$, $B=n\times E/c$, $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$; at an emission event $(x_r,t_r)=(z(s_0)+rn,s_0+r/c)$ the retarded data are $\beta_0,\dot\beta_0=a/c,\kappa_0$ and $r$, and the same formulas and remainder bound hold there. ([[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] (b),(c))

[F2] Retarded emission geometry: $(x_r,t_r)$ lies off the worldline, $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, $r>0$, $\kappa_0=1-n\cdot\beta_0\in[1-v_*/c,1+v_*/c]$. ([[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (b),(c))

[F3] Sphere moments of the polar measure $\sigma$: $\int_{S^2}F(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^1F(u)du$, $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi a_3\int_{-1}^1uf(u)du$, $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi a_3^2\int_{-1}^1u^2f+\pi(a_1^2+a_2^2)\int_{-1}^1(1-u^2)f$, and $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$, $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$, $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$. ([[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] (a)-(d))

[F4] Cross-product and inner-product identities: $u\times v$ is bilinear and alternating, $u\times(v\times w)=(u\cdot w)v-(u\cdot v)w$, $|n\times(n\times w)|=|n\times w|\le|w|$ for $|n|=1$, $|u\times v|^2=|u|^2|v|^2-(u\cdot v)^2$, and $n\cdot(E\times F)=(n\times E)\cdot F$ for $|n|=1$; the Euclidean norm is that of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]])

[F5] Flux and power reading: $S=E\times B/\mu_0$ is the Poynting energy-flux density and the boundary flux term of the Poynting balance is the field energy leaving a volume. ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] (a), [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] (a),(c))

[F6] Integral inequalities: $|\int f|\le\int|f|$; monotonicity for the nonnegative integral; $\sigma(S^2)<\infty$. ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] (d))

[F7] Dominated convergence on a finite measure space. ([[thm-dominated-convergence]], [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] (d))

[F8] SI relations: $C=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$, $C^2/(\mu_0c^5)=q^2/(16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^3)$, since $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$. ([[def-em-si-conventions]])

[F9] One-variable calculus: the second fundamental theorem for continuous derivatives, the chain and power rules and the derivative of $y^m$ for integers $m$, and the mean value theorem; together with the continuity of the power functions on their domains. ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[cor-mean-value-theorem]])

[F10] The polar measure equals the chart surface measure on $S^2$. ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]])

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the rest-case field on the emitted sphere, convert the flux to the angular power density with the uniform remainder, integrate it with the sphere moments for the Larmor power and the $\sin^2$ pattern, and then repeat the computation for a general emission event with the weighted flux integral and explicit low-speed comparisons.

1.1 Field on the emitted sphere (a). At the rest event $z'(s_0)=0$, so at the emitted sphere the retarded data are $\beta=0$, $\kappa=1$, $\dot\beta=a/c$ [F2]; [F1] then gives $E_{\mathrm{vel}}=C(1-0)(n-0)/(1\cdot r^{2})=Cn/r^{2}$ and $E_{\mathrm{acc}}=C\,n\times((n-0)\times a/c)/(c\cdot1\cdot r)=C\,n\times(n\times a)/(c^{2}r)$, together with $B=n\times E/c$. Writing $\rho_E:=Cn/r^{2}$ gives $E(x_r,t_r)=C\,n\times(n\times a)/(c^{2}r)+\rho_E$ and $|\rho_E|=|C|/r^{2}\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$, because both factors in the last expression are at least $1$. This is (a). [F1, F2, F8, algebra]

2.1 Angular flux limit (b). Write $E(x_r,t_r)=E_{\mathrm{lead}}+\rho_E$ with $E_{\mathrm{lead}}:=C\,n\times(n\times a)/(c^{2}r)$ and $|\rho_E|\le D_E r^{-2}$, where $D_E:=|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}$ [step 1.1]. Since $B=n\times E/c$, the identity $n\cdot(E\times(n\times E))=|n\times E|^{2}$ of [F4] gives $n\cdot S=n\cdot(E\times B)/\mu_0=|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)$. Now $|n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}|=C|n\times(n\times(n\times a))|/(c^{2}r)=C|n\times a|/(c^{2}r)$ and $|n\times a|=|n\times(n\times a)|$ by [F4], so $$r^{2}n\cdot S=\frac{C^{2}|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}+R_r(n),\qquad |R_r(n)|\le r^{2}\frac{2|n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}||n\times\rho_E|+|n\times\rho_E|^{2}}{\mu_0c}\le\frac{K}{r}$$ for all $r\ge1$ and all $n\in S^2$, with $K:=2C|a|D_E/(\mu_0c^{3})+D_E^{2}/(\mu_0c)$ independent of $n$ and $r$ [F6]. Hence $r^{2}n\cdot S\to C^{2}|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})$ uniformly in $n$; the limit function is continuous on $S^2$, and $\int_{S^2}|R_r|\,d\sigma\le K r^{-1}\sigma(S^2)\to0$, so by [F6] and [F7] $\int_{S^2}r^{2}n\cdot S\,d\sigma$ converges to $\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}d\sigma$. By [F10] the chart surface measure may be read as the polar measure $d\sigma$. This is (b), including the finiteness and continuity of $dP/d\sigma$. [step 1.1, F4, F6, F7, F10, algebra]

3.1 Total power (c). By [F4], $|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}=|n\times a|^{2}=|a|^{2}-(n\cdot a)^{2}$; integrating over $S^2$ with [F3] gives $\int_{S^2}|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}d\sigma=4\pi|a|^{2}-(4\pi/3)|a|^{2}=(8\pi/3)|a|^{2}$. Substituting into step 2.1, $P_{\mathrm{em}}=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\cdot\frac{8\pi}{3}|a|^{2}$; and $\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}=\frac{q^{2}}{16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0^{2}\mu_0c^{5}}=\frac{q^{2}}{16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3}}$ by [F8] (using $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^{2}=1$), so $P_{\mathrm{em}}=\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}$. This is (c). [step 2.1, F3, F4, F8, algebra]

4.1 Angular distribution (d). Let $\theta$ be the angle between $n$ and $a$ when $a\ne0$. By [F4], $|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}=|a|^{2}-(n\cdot a)^{2}=|a|^{2}(1-\cos^{2}\theta)=|a|^{2}\sin^{2}\theta$; since $\sin^{2}\theta=0$ exactly for $\theta\in\{0,\pi\}$ [F9], the pattern vanishes precisely along $\pm a$ and is maximal where $\sin^{2}\theta=1$, i.e. in the plane perpendicular to $a$; its coefficient is $\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}=\frac{q^{2}}{16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3}}$ [F8]. If $a=0$, then $|n\times(n\times 0)|^{2}=0$ for every $n$, so $dP/d\sigma\equiv0$ and $P_{\mathrm{em}}=0$ by (c). Finally $\int_{S^2}\frac{dP}{d\sigma}d\sigma=P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$ is (c). This is (d). [step 2.1, step 3.1, F3, F4, F8, F9, algebra]

5.1 General far-zone limit and weighted power (f, first part). Now let $s_0$ be an arbitrary emission event with $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $|\beta_0|\le v_*/c$, and $a:=z''(s_0)$; the same computation as steps 1.1-2.1 applies with $\beta_0$ in place of $0$ and $\kappa_0$ in place of $1$ [F2]. By [F1], $E_{\mathrm{lead}}:=C\,n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)/(c^{2}\kappa_0^{3}r)$ is the acceleration part and $E_{\mathrm{vel}}$ is the remainder with $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le D_Er^{-2}$; writing $N_\beta:=n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)$ and repeating the flux identity of step 2.1, $r^{2}n\cdot S=\frac{C^{2}|N_\beta|^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}\kappa_0^{6}}+R_r(n)$ with $|R_r(n)|\le K'r^{-1}$ for $r\ge1$, uniformly in $n$ and with $K'$ independent of $n$; here $1-\delta\le\kappa_0\le1+\delta$ keeps every power of $\kappa_0$ bounded on the compact $S^2$ [F2, F6]. Hence $\kappa_0(n)\,r^{2}n\cdot S\to H_\beta(n):=\frac{C^{2}|N_\beta|^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}\kappa_0^{5}}$ uniformly, and the weighted emitted power $P_{\mathrm{em}}:=\int_{S^2}\kappa_0\lim_{r\to\infty}(r^{2}n\cdot S)\,d\sigma=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}\frac{|N_\beta|^{2}}{\kappa_0^{5}}\,d\sigma$ is the dominated-convergence limit of the weighted fluxes, the weight $\kappa_0$ being bounded and continuous [F6, F7]. [step 2.1, step 4.1, F1, F2, F6, F7, algebra]

6.1 Evaluation of the weighted angular integral (f, second part). By [F4], $N_\beta=(n\cdot a)(n-\beta_0)-(1-n\cdot\beta_0)a$, so with $b:=|\beta_0|\in[0,v_*/c)$ and $u:=n\cdot\beta_0/b$ (any unit vector $e_3$ along $\beta_0$ when $b>0$; the case $b=0$ is step 3.1) one gets $$|N_\beta|^{2}=-(1-b^{2})(n\cdot a)^{2}+2(1-bu)b\,a_\parallel(n\cdot a)+(1-bu)^{2}|a|^{2},$$ where $a_\parallel$ is the component of $a$ along $\beta_0$. Averaging the $\varphi$-dependence over the sphere with [F3] (the linear term in the tangential component of $n$ integrates to $0$, and the square of that component integrates to $\pi\int(1-u^{2})f$), the parallel coefficient of $|N_\beta|^{2}/(1-bu)^{5}$ reduces to $1-u^{2}$ and the perpendicular coefficient to $(1-bu)^{2}-\tfrac{1-b^{2}}{2}(1-u^{2})$. Hence, with $J_5:=\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})(1-bu)^{-5}du$ and $J_3:=\int_{-1}^{1}(1-bu)^{-3}du$, $$\int_{S^2}\frac{|N_\beta|^{2}}{\kappa_0^{5}}d\sigma=2\pi a_\parallel^{2}J_5+2\pi a_\perp^{2}\Bigl[J_3-\frac{1-b^{2}}{2}J_5\Bigr].$$ The substitution $y=1-bu$ (for $b>0$, with $du=-dy/b$) and the second fundamental theorem [F9], with the antiderivatives $-y^{-2}/2$ and $b^{-3}\bigl[(1-b^{2})y^{-4}/4-2y^{-3}/3+y^{-2}/2\bigr]$, give $J_3=2/(1-b^{2})^{2}$ and $J_5=4/(3(1-b^{2})^{3})$; at $b=0$ the same formulas follow by direct integration ($J_3=2$, $J_5=4/3$) and all expressions are continuous in $b$, so no division by $b$ is needed in the conclusion. Therefore $$\int_{S^2}\frac{|N_\beta|^{2}}{\kappa_0^{5}}d\sigma=\frac{8\pi}{3}\Bigl[a_\parallel^{2}(1-b^{2})^{-3}+a_\perp^{2}(1-b^{2})^{-2}\Bigr]=\frac{8\pi}{3}\gamma_0^{6}\bigl(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\bigr),$$ because $(1-b^{2})^{-1}=\gamma_0^{2}$, $(1-b^{2})^{-3}=\gamma_0^{6}$ and $|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}=a_\parallel^{2}+(1-b^{2})a_\perp^{2}$ by [F4]. Substituting into step 5.1 and converting the constant with [F8] gives $P_{\mathrm{em}}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}$, the displayed general formula. [step 5.1, F3, F4, F8, F9, algebra]

7.1 Uniform low-speed comparisons (f, third part). Write $P_{\mathrm L}=q^{2}|a|^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ and $P_{\mathrm{em}}=\gamma_0^{6}(a_\parallel^{2}+\gamma_0^{-2}a_\perp^{2})\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}$ [step 6.1]. Since $\gamma_0\ge1$, one has $\gamma_0^{6}a_\parallel^{2}\ge a_\parallel^{2}$ and $\gamma_0^{4}a_\perp^{2}\ge a_\perp^{2}$, so $P_{\mathrm{em}}\ge P_{\mathrm L}$; and $\gamma_0^{6}a_\parallel^{2}+\gamma_0^{4}a_\perp^{2}\le\gamma_0^{6}|a|^{2}$, so $P_{\mathrm{em}}\le\gamma_0^{6}P_{\mathrm L}$. If $b=|\beta_0|\le\delta<1$ then $\gamma_0^{2}=(1-b^{2})^{-1}\le(1-\delta^{2})^{-1}$, hence $P_{\mathrm L}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}\le(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L}$. Moreover $P_{\mathrm{em}}-P_{\mathrm L}=\bigl[(\gamma_0^{6}-1)a_\parallel^{2}+(\gamma_0^{4}-1)a_\perp^{2}\bigr]\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\le(\gamma_0^{6}-1)P_{\mathrm L}\le\bigl[(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}-1\bigr]P_{\mathrm L}\le3\delta^{2}(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L}$, where the last step is the elementary inequality $(1-t)^{-3}-1\le3t(1-t)^{-3}$ at $t=\delta^{2}$; all these inequalities are valid also when $a=0$ or $q=0$, with both sides zero, and no division by $P_{\mathrm L}$ is performed. For the angular comparison fix $n$ and use coordinates with $n=e_3$: writing $p=(a_1,a_2)$, $q=(\beta_{0,1},\beta_{0,2})$, $t=a_3$ and $\beta_{0,3}$, one has $N_0=-p$ and $N_\beta=-(\kappa_0p+tq)$ by [F4], so with $D:=|N_\beta|^{2}\kappa_0^{-5}-|N_0|^{2}$, $$D=|p|^{2}(\kappa_0^{-3}-1)+2\kappa_0^{-4}t(p\cdot q)+\kappa_0^{-5}t^{2}|q|^{2}.$$ Since $1-\delta\le\kappa_0\le1+\delta$, the mean value theorem [F9] gives $|\kappa_0^{-3}-1|\le3\delta(1-\delta)^{-4}$ and $|\kappa_0^{-4}|\le(1-\delta)^{-4}$, $\kappa_0^{-5}\le(1-\delta)^{-5}$; also $|q|\le\delta$ and $|p|,|t|\le|a|$, and $2|t||p|\le|t|^{2}+|p|^{2}$. Hence $|D|\le|a|^{2}\bigl[4\delta(1-\delta)^{-4}+\delta^{2}(1-\delta)^{-5}\bigr]$, and this is at most $|a|^{2}\delta\bigl[(2+\delta)(1-\delta)^{-5}+5(1-\delta)^{-6}\bigr]$ because, after dividing by $\delta(1-\delta)^{-4}$, the inequality reduces to $4-3\delta\le2+\delta+5(1-\delta)^{-1}$, whose left side is at most $4$ and whose right side exceeds $5$. Multiplying by $\frac{q^{2}}{16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3}}$ gives the displayed bound on $|H_\beta-H_0|$. [step 6.1, F2, F4, F9, algebra]

8.1 Scope and conclusion (e). At a rest event $z'(s_0)=0$ one has $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot 0=1$ for every $n\in S^2$ [F2], so the emission-time Jacobian is identically $1$ and no retarded-time conversion factor appears: the limits of (b) are simultaneously the fixed-sphere flux and the emitted power per unit emission time, and the angular and total powers of (c)-(d) are the emitted quantities of the rest event. The computation used only the prescribed worldline, the retarded model fields and the adopted causal selection of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] and [[post-em-radiation-selection]]; it forms no product of distributions, asserts no self-force, radiation reaction, mass derivation or mechanical evolution law, and makes no empirical or measurement claim, while clause (f) records the general low-speed comparison as a separate quantified statement rather than a loss law. Steps 1.1-7.1 together with this clause prove (a)-(f). [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, step 7.1, F2, F5, F10, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the setting be that of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]]: a charge $q\in\mathbb R$ ($C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$) on a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline $z$ in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], with retarded fields $E,B$ off the worldline and the uniform far-zone remainder of that item; let $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]). Let $s_0$ be an emission event, $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\gamma_0:=(1-|\beta_0|^2)^{-1/2}$, $a:=z''(s_0)$, and for $n\in S^2$ put $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$, $\kappa_0(n):=1-n\cdot\beta_0$. Define the **emitted power at the emission event $s_0$** by the $\kappa_0$-weighted far-zone flux

$$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}\kappa_0(n)\,r^{2}\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)\,d\sigma(n),$$

$d\sigma$ the polar surface measure (equal to the chart surface measure). The weight $\kappa_0$ is the emission-time/observation-time conversion factor of the retarded root, $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$, equivalently the moving-boundary correction $S\cdot n-(z'\cdot n)u$ at leading radiation order, where $u=|S|/c$ for the transverse far field. Then:

(a) [Weighted flux limit] The limit exists and $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}\frac{\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}}{\kappa_0(n)^{5}}\,d\sigma(n).$$

(b) [Closed form and four-acceleration form] If $b:=|\beta_0|<1$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp$ is decomposed along $\beta_0=|\beta_0|e_3$ and perpendicular to it, then $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{q^{2}\gamma_0^{6}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\bigl(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\bigr)=\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\,\eta(A,A),$$ where $A$ is the four-acceleration of the worldline at $s_0$ and $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](e)). At $\beta_0=0$ the weight is $1$ and (b) reduces to the instantaneous-rest Larmor power of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]].

(c) [Low-speed comparison] For every $\delta\in(0,1)$ and every emission event with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$, $$\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)\le\frac{(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},\qquad\text{hence}\qquad \Bigl|P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)-\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\Bigr|\le\frac{3\delta^{2}}{(1-\delta^{2})^{3}}\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ a comparison uniform over the events with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. In particular the instantaneous-rest formula is the exact $\delta=0$ case, and no term of the comparison is asserted to be small without the explicit hypothesis $|\beta_0|\le\delta$.

(d) [Scope] $P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$ is the power emitted at the single retarded event $s_0$ per unit emission time, defined by the weighted far-zone flux; it is not a coordinate-time loss rate of a dynamical particle, and no dynamics (self-force, radiation reaction, mass), no uniformity in $s_0$, and no empirical or measurement claim is made. The near fields are $O(r^{-2})$ with their uniform remainder as in [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]](c), so their contribution to the weighted $r^2$ flux vanishes; the $\kappa_0$-weighting is part of the definition of emitted power and is not an additional physical assumption.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]); the setting of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]]: charge $q$, constant $C$, prescribed uniformly subluminal $C^3$ worldline $z$, retarded fields $E,B$ and $S=E\times B/\mu_0$; an emission event $s_0$ with $\beta_0=z'(s_0)/c$, $\gamma_0$, $a=z''(s_0)$, and the emission spheres $x_r=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r=s_0+r/c$, $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot\beta_0$.

[F1] Emitted-power branch: for a general emission event the $\kappa_0$-weighted far-zone flux has the limit $P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}\kappa_0^{-5}d\sigma$ (the uniform pointwise convergence and the interchange of limit and integral being established in its proof), and this equals $\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})q^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$; for $|\beta_0|\le\delta<1$ it satisfies $P_{\mathrm L}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}\le(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L}$ and $|P_{\mathrm{em}}-P_{\mathrm L}|\le3\delta^{2}(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L}$ with $P_{\mathrm L}=q^{2}|a|^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$, and at $\beta_0=0$ it reduces to the exact rest-event Larmor power. ([[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]] (a)-(d),(f))

[F2] Point fields and remainder: on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, $E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}}$, $B=n\times E/c$, with the velocity part $O(r^{-2})$ bounded by $|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$ and the acceleration part the leading term; at $(x_r,t_r)$ the retarded data are those of the emission event and $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$. ([[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] (b),(c), [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]] (c),(d))

[F3] Four-acceleration identity: for a $C^2$ chart worldline $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ with coordinate velocity $w(t)=r'(t)$ and acceleration $a(t)=w'(t)$, the four-acceleration satisfies $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_w^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_w^{6}(w\cdot a)^{2}/c^{2}\ge0$, vanishing exactly when $a=0$. ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e))

[F4] Retarded root: $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$ off the worldline, and $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot\beta_0\in[1-v_*/c,1+v_*/c]$. ([[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (a),(b))

[F5] Conventions: $|u\times v|^{2}=|u|^{2}|v|^{2}-(u\cdot v)^{2}$ with the Euclidean inner product; the polar measure equals the chart surface measure; $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^{2}=1$ and $C=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$. ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[def-em-si-conventions]])

[F6] Flux reading and integral rules: $S$ is the Poynting energy-flux density; $|\int f|\le\int|f|$, monotonicity holds, and dominated convergence applies on the finite-measure sphere. ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]], [[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[thm-dominated-convergence]])

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct translation of the emitted-power branch already proved on this page, together with the four-acceleration identity and the scope reading of the weighted definition.

1.1 Weighted flux limit (a). The definition of $P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$ in the Statement is the limit of the $\kappa_0$-weighted far-zone fluxes, and the corresponding limit and its value $\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}\kappa_0^{-5}d\sigma$ are exactly clause (f) of [F1], whose proof establishes the uniform pointwise convergence of $\kappa_0r^{2}n\cdot S$ to the displayed integrand and the domination needed to pass the limit through the sphere integral [F6]; the same clause uses $\kappa_0=1-n\cdot\beta_0$ and $r=c(t_r-s_0)$ on the emitted spheres [F2]. This is (a). [F1, F2, F4, F6, algebra]

2.1 Closed form and four-acceleration form (b). Clause (f) of [F1] evaluates the integral as $\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})q^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$, which is the first displayed equality; at $\beta_0=0$ the weight is $1$ and the formula reduces to the rest-event Larmor statement of [F1]. 3.1 Low-speed comparison (c). The eventwise inequalities $P_{\mathrm L}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}\le\gamma_0^{6}P_{\mathrm L}$ and the uniform bounds $P_{\mathrm L}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}\le(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L}$, $|P_{\mathrm{em}}-P_{\mathrm L}|\le3\delta^{2}(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L}$ for $|\beta_0|\le\delta<1$ are clause (f) of [F1], transported verbatim to this setting; the case $|\beta_0|=0$ gives the exact rest formula and is the $\delta=0$ endpoint of the comparison. The statement adds no smallness assertion beyond the explicit hypothesis $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. This is (c). [step 2.1, F1, algebra]

4.1 Scope (d). The definition is per unit emission time at the single event $s_0$: the weight is the retarded Jacobian of [F4], not a dynamical rate, and no worldline evolution, self-force, radiation reaction or mass is introduced anywhere in steps 1.1-3.1. ## Example

Let $c>0$ and $a>0$, and define $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ by $z(s):=(\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}},0,0)$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[thm-of-square-roots]]). Then:
(a) $z$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ and $|z'(s)|<c$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$; nevertheless there is no constant $v_*<c$ with $|z'(s)|\le v_*$ for all $s$, because $|z'(s)|\to c$ as $s\to\pm\infty$;
(b) at the event $(x,t)=(0,0)$ the retarded equation $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$ of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] has no solution in $\mathbb R$: the equation reads $-s=\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}/c$, whose right-hand side is at least $a/c>0$, and squaring both sides would give $c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}=c^{2}s^{2}$, i.e. $a^{2}=0$, contrary to $a>0$. Hence pointwise subluminality of a smooth curve does not by itself produce the retarded root, and the uniform bound $v_*<c$ of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]], or an explicit cone-intersection hypothesis, cannot be dropped; the supplier [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]] indeed assumes such a uniform bound.
(c) [Scope] This is a mathematical example about the prescribed curve and the root equation. The curve is future timelike pointwise ($|z'(s)|<c$ for every $s$) but not uniformly subluminal; it is not asserted to be the worldline of any physical charge, and no measurement is reported. The example contradicts no theorem: it exhibits a curve lying outside the hypotheses of the root lemma.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** constants $c>0$, $a>0$ and the curve $z(s)=(\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}},0,0)$; the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the absolute value of [[def-abs-value]].

[L1] $c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}\ge a^{2}>0$ for every $s$, and $\sqrt{\cdot}$ is continuous and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ with $\frac{d}{dt}\sqrt t=\frac{1}{2\sqrt t}=t^{-1/2}$; general power derivatives and continuity are as in [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]. ([[thm-of-square-roots]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]])

[L2] Chain rule and algebra of derivatives for composites of differentiable maps, and the notion of the derivative of a vector-valued curve with its componentwise computation. ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]])

[L3] Monotonicity of squares and square roots on nonnegative reals: for $p,q\ge0$, $p<q$ if and only if $p^{2}<q^{2}$. ([[lem-of-square-monotone]], [[thm-of-square-roots]])

[L4] The retarded equation and the uniform-bound hypothesis are those of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]]; the cited root lemma states its existence and uniqueness result for curves with $|z'(s)|\le v_*<c$ for all $s$. ([[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]], [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]])

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct computation and contradiction.

1.1 Smoothness and speed (a). The map $s\mapsto c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}$ is a polynomial, hence $C^\infty$, with values in $[a^{2},\infty)\subseteq(0,\infty)$; by [L1] the square root is $C^\infty$ on $(0,\infty)$, so the composite $s\mapsto\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}$ is $C^\infty$ and $z$ is $C^\infty$ into $\mathbb R^3$ [L2]. Its derivative is $z'(s)=(c^{2}s/\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}},0,0)$ by the chain rule [L1, L2], so $|z'(s)|=c^{2}|s|/\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}$ [L2]. If $s=0$ this is $0<c$; if $s\ne0$, dividing numerator and denominator by $c|s|>0$ gives $|z'(s)|=c/\sqrt{1+a^{2}/(c^{2}s^{2})}<c$ because $a^{2}/(c^{2}s^{2})>0$ [L3]. Hence $|z'(s)|<c$ for every $s$. [given, L1, L2, L3, algebra]

2.1 No uniform bound (a, continued). For $s>0$, $|z'(s)|=c/\sqrt{1+a^{2}/(c^{2}s^{2})}\to c$ as $s\to\infty$, since $a^{2}/(c^{2}s^{2})\to0$ and the square root and reciprocal are continuous on their domains [L1]; the same limit holds as $s\to-\infty$ by symmetry. Consequently, for every $v_*<c$ there is $s$ with $|z'(s)|>v_*$: choose $s$ so large that $|z'(s)|>v_*$, possible because the values approach $c$ from below and $v_*<c$; thus no $v_*<c$ bounds $|z'|$ on all of $\mathbb R$. [step 1.1, L1, L3, algebra]

3.1 No retarded root at $(0,0)$ (b) and scope. At $(x,t)=(0,0)$ the equation $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$ of [L4] reads $-s=|z(s)|/c=\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}/c$, and the right-hand side is $\ge a/c>0$; hence any solution would satisfy $s<0$, so both sides are nonnegative and squaring is equivalent. Squaring gives $s^{2}=(c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2})/c^{2}$, that is $c^{2}s^{2}=c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}$ and then $a^{2}=0$, contradicting $a>0$; therefore no solution $s\in\mathbb R$ exists at this event. Since $z$ is pointwise subluminal by step 1.1 but carries no uniform bound by step 2.1, this exhibits a smooth curve outside the hypotheses of the root lemma [L4] for which the retarded equation fails: the uniform bound cannot be dropped, and no theorem is contradicted because the curve is not in its hypothesis class. Clause (c) records that the curve is a mathematical object, not the worldline of a physical charge, and that no measurement is reported. [step 1.1, step 2.1, L3, L4, algebra] ∎

## Example

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the surface and finite-source branches. Adopt the electric-dipole radiation-law idealization whose leading far fields and angular flux are the dipole expressions of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], evaluated for the prescribed smooth waveform $p(u)=p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ with $\omega>0$ and $p_0\ne0$. This is an explicit ideal radiation-law model, not an eternal compact-time source claimed to satisfy that theorem with $D=0$. The waveform is a moment convention of [[def-em-electric-moments]], not measured data. All exact quantities below refer to that ideal leading radiation law. Then:

(a) [Fields] With $n=\sin\theta\cos\varphi\,e_1+\sin\theta\sin\varphi\,e_2+\cos\theta\,e_3$, $\theta\in[0,\pi]$, the leading far fields are $$E_{\mathrm{lead}}(rn,u+r/c)=-\frac{\mu_0\omega^{2}p_0\cos(\omega u)}{4\pi r}\,n\times(n\times e_3),\qquad B_{\mathrm{lead}}=\frac{n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}}{c},$$ with $|n\times(n\times e_3)|=|\sin\theta|$, so the amplitude pattern is $\propto\sin\theta$ and vanishes on the dipole axis $\theta\in\{0,\pi\}$.

(b) [Angular power density] The retarded-time angular power density of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] is $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n,u)=\frac{\mu_0|n\times p''(u)|^{2}}{16\pi^{2}c}=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{16\pi^{2}c}\,\sin^{2}\theta,$$ the $\sin^{2}\theta$ pattern with zeros along $\pm e_3$ and maximum in the equatorial plane; its integral over the sphere is $$\int_{S^2}\frac{dP}{d\sigma}d\sigma=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{6\pi c},$$ using $\int_{S^2}\sin^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=8\pi/3$ from [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](a).

(c) [Period average] The mean of the total power over one retarded-time period $u\in[0,2\pi/\omega]$ is $$\frac{\omega}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi/\omega}\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{6\pi c}\,du=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}}{12\pi c}.$$

(d) [Scope] The computation is the exact dipole law of the model; a finite prescribed source realizes it only within the absolute error bound of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] with its $D(u)$, and a physical antenna's feed, current distribution and material realization are additional source models not supplied here. The average in (c) is taken in the retarded-time variable, not in observation time; no measurement, radiation resistance, matching condition or effective area is reported, and no empirical claim is made.

(e) [Actual compact-window realization] Choose a compact smooth time cutoff $\eta\equiv1$ near one selected period, a nonnegative $C^\infty$ bump $\sigma$ supported in $B_a$ with integral $1$, and $p_\eta(u)=\eta(u)p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$. Define $\rho(y,u)=-p_\eta(u)\cdot\nabla\sigma(y)$, $J(y,u)=p_\eta'(u)\sigma(y)$. These are smooth compact spacetime sources, satisfy continuity, carry zero total charge and have moment $p_\eta$. On the chosen period the moment equals the harmonic waveform, while the actual retarded field has the full $D(u)$, $\Gamma_E/r^{2}$ and $(\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c)/r^{2}$ errors of the dipole theorem. Its asymptotic total-power deviation from the ideal law is bounded by that theorem's explicit $R(u)$; its period-averaged deviation is bounded by the average of $|R(u)|$. The condition $V=p''$ is a sufficient ideal transverse-moment condition; it is not equivalent to $D=0$. No eternal nonzero harmonic moment is asserted for a compact-time source.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]); the dipole theorem [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] with its source class and constants; the waveform $p(u)=p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$, $\omega>0$, $p_0\ne0$; the construction data $\eta,\sigma,p_\eta,\rho,J$ of clause (e).

[L1] Dipole theorem: for a source of the compact smooth conserved class, $p\in C^\infty$ with $p''(u)=\int J_t(y,u)dy$, $|V(n,u)-p''(u)|\le D(u)$ with $D(u)=\frac{a}{c}\int_{B_a}\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|dy$; the leading far fields are $E_{\mathrm{lead}}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$, with errors $\Gamma_E/r^{2}$ and $(\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c)/r^{2}$, and the angular power density limit is $\mu_0|n\times V|^{2}/(16\pi^{2}c)$ with total error $|R(u)|\le\mu_0(2|p''|D+D^{2})/(4\pi c)$. ([[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] (a)-(d))

[L2] Sphere integrals: $\int_{S^2}F(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}F(u)du$, so $\int_{S^2}\sin^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=\int_{S^2}(1-n_3^{2})\,d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})du=\frac{8\pi}{3}$, and $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^{2}d\sigma=\frac{8\pi}{3}|a|^{2}$. ([[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] (a),(d))

[L3] Sine and cosine derivatives and identities: $(\cos)'=-\sin$, $(\sin)'=\cos$, parity, $\sin^{2}+\cos^{2}=1$, and the double-angle form $\cos^{2}t=\frac{1+\cos 2t}{2}$. ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]])

[L4] Fundamental theorem and derivative algebra for the one-variable computations below. ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]])

[L5] Constructions and integration by parts in Euclidean space: a nonnegative $C^\infty$ bump of unit mass supported in a prescribed ball exists; a smooth compact time cutoff equal to $1$ near a chosen period exists; for compactly supported $C^1$ fields the divergence theorem gives $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\partial_jF\,dy=0$, hence $\int_{\mathbb R^3}y_i\partial_j\sigma\,dy=-\delta_{ij}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sigma\,dy$. ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]], [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]], [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]], [[thm-integration-by-parts]])

[L6] Conventions: $e_3$ is a unit vector, the moment convention is that of [[def-em-electric-moments]], $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^{2}=1$ and the dipole theorem's source class is the compact smooth conserved one whose retarded fields are constructed by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]. ([[def-em-electric-moments]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]])

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct substitution in the exact dipole law, followed by explicit constructions.

1.1 Leading fields (a). By [L3], $\frac{d}{du}\cos(\omega u)=-\omega\sin(\omega u)$ and $\frac{d^{2}}{du^{2}}\cos(\omega u)=-\omega^{2}\cos(\omega u)$; hence $p'(u)=-p_0\omega\sin(\omega u)e_3$ and $p''(u)=-\omega^{2}p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ [L4]. Substituting into the leading field of [L1] with $V=p''$ gives $E_{\mathrm{lead}}=\mu_0n\times(n\times p'')/(4\pi r)=-\frac{\mu_0\omega^{2}p_0\cos(\omega u)}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times e_3)$ and $B_{\mathrm{lead}}=n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}/c$. For a unit vector $n$, $|n\times(n\times e_3)|=|n\times e_3|=(1-(n\cdot e_3)^{2})^{1/2}=\sin\theta$, which vanishes exactly when $n=\pm e_3$, i.e. $\theta\in\{0,\pi\}$, and is maximal for $\theta=\pi/2$ [L3, L6]. This is (a). [given, L1, L3, L4, L6, algebra]

2.1 Angular power density (b). By [L1] the angular density limit of the dipole law is $\mu_0|n\times V|^{2}/(16\pi^{2}c)$; substituting $V=p''=-\omega^{2}p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ gives $|n\times V|^{2}=\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)|n\times e_3|^{2}=\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)\sin^{2}\theta$ [step 1.1, L3]. Hence $\frac{dP}{d\sigma}=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{16\pi^{2}c}\sin^{2}\theta$, which vanishes on the axis and is maximal in the equatorial plane. Integrating with [L2], $\int_{S^2}\sin^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=\frac{8\pi}{3}$, so $\int_{S^2}\frac{dP}{d\sigma}d\sigma=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{16\pi^{2}c}\cdot\frac{8\pi}{3}=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{6\pi c}$. This is (b). [step 1.1, L1, L2, L3, algebra]

3.1 Period average (c). By [L3], $\cos^{2}(\omega u)=\frac{1+\cos(2\omega u)}{2}$, whose antiderivative $\frac u2+\frac{\sin(2\omega u)}{4\omega}$ has endpoint increment $\pi/\omega$ over $[0,2\pi/\omega]$; hence $\int_0^{2\pi/\omega}\cos^{2}(\omega u)du=\frac12\cdot\frac{2\pi}{\omega}=\frac{\pi}{\omega}$ by [L4]. Multiplying the total power of step 2.1 by $\omega/(2\pi)$ gives the period mean $\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}}{6\pi c}\cdot\frac12=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}}{12\pi c}$, the average being taken in the retarded-time variable as stated. This is (c). [step 2.1, L3, L4, algebra]

4.1 Realization, scope and error control (d),(e). With $\eta,\sigma$ as in [L5], the functions $\rho(y,u)=-p_\eta(u)\cdot\nabla\sigma(y)$ and $J(y,u)=p_\eta'(u)\sigma(y)$ are $C^\infty$ and compactly supported in a set $B_a\times[t_0,T]$, and $\partial_u\rho+\operatorname{div}J=-p_\eta'\cdot\nabla\sigma+p_\eta'\cdot\nabla\sigma=0$; the total charge is $\int\rho\,dy=-p_\eta\cdot\int\nabla\sigma\,dy=0$, and the moment is $p_i(u)=\int y_i\rho\,dy=-\sum_jp_{\eta,j}(u)\int y_i\partial_j\sigma\,dy=-p_{\eta,i}(u)(-\int\sigma\,dy)=p_{\eta,i}(u)$ by [L5]. On the selected period $p_\eta=p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$, so that source realizes the harmonic moment there, while by [L1] its actual retarded fields are those of the compact smooth branch constructed in [L6] and carry the full $D(u)$, $\Gamma_E/r^{2}$ and $(\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c)/r^{2}$ errors around the ideal dipole expressions; the asymptotic total-power deviation from the ideal law is bounded by $R(u)$ of [L1] and its period average by the mean of $|R(u)|$ over the selected period. The non-equivalence in (e) is witnessed explicitly: add to $J$ the term $\varepsilon\varphi'(u)\gamma(y)$ with $\gamma=(\partial_2a,-\partial_1a,0)$ for a compactly supported smooth $a$ with $\partial_2a\not\equiv0$ and with a compactly supported smooth $\varphi$ chosen so that $\varphi'''(u)\ne0$ (for small $\varepsilon$ and $\rho$ unchanged): then $\operatorname{div}\gamma=0$ and $\int\gamma\,dy=0$, so continuity, total charge and the moment are unchanged, while $J_{tt}=p_\eta'''\sigma+\varepsilon\varphi'''\gamma$ does not vanish identically and hence $D(u)>0$, whereas $V(n,u)=\int J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)dy=p''(u)+0$ for every $n$; conversely $D=0$ gives $V=p''$ by [L1], so $V=p''$ is sufficient for the ideal leading field but is not equivalent to $D=0$. Clause (d) records the scope: no feed, matching, radiation-resistance, measurement or observation-time power statement is made, and no eternal nonzero harmonic moment is asserted for the compact-time source. [step 3.1, L1, L2, L5, L6, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Adopt the following idealized, hypothetical setup of a prescribed slowly orbiting charge; it is a thought experiment with explicit premises, not a reported measurement. (H) Let $m>0$ be an externally supplied rest mass and $q\ne0$ a charge parameter ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]), let $\kappa>0$, and let the particle move on a circle of radius $r(t)>0$ about a fixed centre in the laboratory chart ([[def-em-lab-geometry]]) so that the mechanical orbit is governed by the attractive potential $V(r)=-\kappa/r$: the circular-orbit energy is $E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r)=-\kappa/(2r)$ and the circular orbit with speed $v$ satisfies $mv^{2}=\kappa/r$, with centripetal acceleration $a=\kappa/(mr^{2})$. Assume the adiabatic separation of timescales: the mechanical parameters change on a timescale long compared with the orbital period, the speed is small compared with $c$, and the electromagnetic energy emitted per unit time is instantaneously taken to be the Larmor value $q^{2}a(t)^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]] evaluated at the instantaneous centripetal acceleration, so that the adopted energy balance of the reduced model reads

$$\frac{d}{dt}E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r(t))=-\frac{q^{2}a(t)^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}.$$

Then, with $A:=q^{2}\kappa/(3\pi\varepsilon_0m^{2}c^{3})>0$:

(a) the reduced model implies $r'(t)=-A/r(t)^{2}$ for all $t$ where the model applies, and the circular orbit radius in the reduced model obeys $$r(t)^{3}=r_{0}^{3}-3A(t-t_{0})$$ on any interval containing $t_0$ on which $r>0$;

(b) consequently $r$ is strictly decreasing, and the cubic reaches $r=0$ at the finite reduced-model time $t_{*}:=t_{0}+r_{0}^{3}/(3A)$, with $r(t)\downarrow0$ as $t\uparrow t_{*}$;

(c) [Scope and qualifications] the deduction is conditional on (H). The low-speed premise $v^{2}=\kappa/(mr)\ll c^{2}$ necessarily fails as $r\to0$, so the model's own hypotheses break down near the collapse time and the computation is not a proof that a physical orbit reaches $r=0$; it is not a derivation of atomic lifetimes, not a coupled point-particle self-force calculation (that dynamics is not available in this framework), and it supplies no empirical evidence. The reduced-model finite-time collapse is retained as a mathematical property of (H), while all conclusions about nature remain conditional on (H) and on its regime of validity. No measurement, dataset, statistical model or uncertainty is introduced.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the hypothetical setup (H): external parameters $m>0$, $q\ne0$, $\kappa>0$; a circular orbit of radius $r(t)>0$ about a fixed centre in the laboratory chart with $E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r)=-\kappa/(2r)$, $mv^{2}=\kappa/r$ and centripetal acceleration $a=\kappa/(mr^{2})$; the adopted energy balance $\frac{d}{dt}E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r(t))=-\frac{q^{2}a(t)^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}$; $A:=q^{2}\kappa/(3\pi\varepsilon_0m^{2}c^{3})>0$; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] Units and model reading: the parameters $m,q,\kappa$ carry the SI meanings of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], and the orbit is read in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]. ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]])

[F2] The Larmor value $q^{2}a^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]] is the exact instantaneous-rest emitted power of the point-source model; in (H) it is adopted as the instantaneous loss rate of the reduced model, an additional modelling assumption. ([[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]])

[F3] One-variable calculus on intervals: the power rule for $u\mapsto u^{n}$ and the chain rule, the algebra of derivatives, the fundamental theorem for a continuous derivative, and the interval conventions of [[def-interval]]. ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[def-interval]])

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct conditional computation from (H); differentiate the orbital energy along the prescribed radius, substitute the circular-orbit acceleration, integrate the resulting ODE, and read off the finite-time collapse with its scope qualifications.

1.1 The radius ODE (a, first part). Along $t\mapsto r(t)$, the orbital energy satisfies $\frac{d}{dt}E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r(t))=\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(-\frac{\kappa}{2r(t)}\bigr)=\frac{\kappa}{2}\frac{r'(t)}{r(t)^{2}}$ by the power rule and the chain rule [F3]. Equating this to the adopted balance in (H), $\frac{\kappa r'}{2r^{2}}=-\frac{q^{2}a^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_{0}c^{3}}$, and substituting the centripetal acceleration $a=\kappa/(mr^{2})$ gives $\frac{\kappa r'}{2r^{2}}=-\frac{q^{2}\kappa^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_{0}c^{3}m^{2}r^{4}}$, hence $r'=-\frac{q^{2}\kappa}{3\pi\varepsilon_{0}m^{2}c^{3}r^{2}}=-\frac{A}{r^{2}}$, which is the displayed ODE; here $\kappa>0$ and $r>0$ legitimize the divisions [F1]. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 The cubic (a, second part). Multiplying the ODE of step 1.1 by $3r^{2}$ gives $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(r(t)^{3}\bigr)=3r^{2}r'=-3A$, a constant right-hand side; applying the fundamental theorem on any interval containing $t_0$ on which $r>0$ [F3] yields $r(t)^{3}-r(t_{0})^{3}=-3A(t-t_{0})$, that is the displayed cubic. Conversely, differentiating the cubic on that interval recovers the ODE, so the two descriptions are equivalent within the reduced model. This is (a). [step 1.1, F3, algebra]

3.1 Monotone decrease and the finite collapse time (b). Since $A>0$ and $r>0$, the ODE gives $r'=-A/r^{2}<0$ wherever the model applies, so $r$ is strictly decreasing. From the cubic, $r(t)^{3}=r_{0}^{3}-3A(t-t_{0})>0$ exactly for $t<t_{*}:=t_{0}+r_{0}^{3}/(3A)$, and $r(t)^{3}\to0$ as $t\uparrow t_{*}$; since $r(t)>0$ is decreasing and its cube tends to $0$, given $\varepsilon>0$ the inequality $r(t)^{3}<\varepsilon^{3}$ holds for all $t$ close enough to $t_{*}$ from below [F3], so $r(t)<\varepsilon$ there and $r(t)\downarrow0$ as $t\uparrow t_{*}$. For $t>t_{*}$ the cubic expression is negative, which is recorded as the breakdown of the reduced model rather than as a negative radius. This is (b). [step 2.1, F3, algebra]

4.1 Scope and qualifications (c). The deduction is conditional on (H) throughout: the balance is the adopted premise, and the Larmor expression is only the prescribed-source rest-event emitted power of [F2], converted into a mechanical loss rate solely by the assumption (H) and not by any derived equation of motion. The low-speed premise of (H), $v^{2}=\kappa/(mr)\ll c^{2}$, fails as $r\to0$ because $v^{2}=\kappa/(mr)\to+\infty$ with $\kappa>0$, so the model's own regime of validity excludes the collapse point: $t_{*}$ is a formal finite-time limit of the reduced model, not the predicted time at which a physical orbit reaches the centre. No coupled self-force dynamics, no lifetime derivation, no measurement, dataset, statistical model or uncertainty is introduced, and nothing here contradicts a theorem: the reduced model lies outside the hypotheses of the point-field and emitted-power theorems precisely through its adopted mechanical balance. This is (c), and with steps 1.1-3.1 it completes the conditional deduction from (H). [step 1.1, step 3.1, F1, F2, algebra] ∎
