## Statement

Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ with its inertial chart $x$,
the electric and magnetic fields $E,B$ of [[def-em-fields]], the source fields
$(\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] and the SI conventions of
[[def-em-si-conventions]] with $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ be those of the
framework. Let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with the components fixed there,
$F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$,
$F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ and
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let $j=(c\rho,J)$ carry the
tensor-component identification adopted in [[def-em-sources]]. Write
$\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ and $\partial_i$ for the coordinate partial
derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and
$\operatorname{div},\operatorname{curl}$ for those of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Assume the smooth branch of
the vacuum Maxwell postulate [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]: $E,B$ are jointly
$C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ with the additional derivatives required by each
displayed equation existing and continuous, and $\rho,J$ are continuous. Then:

(a) [Equivalence] On $I\times\Omega$ the four smooth-branch equations

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$

hold if and only if the two systems

$$(\mathrm{TM1})\quad \partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0\,j^\nu\quad(\nu=0,1,2,3),$$

$$(\mathrm{TM2})\quad \partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu}=0\quad(\lambda,\mu,\nu\in\{0,1,2,3\})$$

hold on $I\times\Omega$. Every instance of (TM2) with a repeated index vanishes
identically because $F$ is alternating, so (TM1) and (TM2) carry exactly eight
independent scalar equations: (TM1) with $\nu=0$ is
$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ (using $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$),
(TM1) with $\nu=i$ is the $i$-th component of
$\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$, (TM2) with
$(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=(1,2,3)$ is $\operatorname{div}B=0$, and the three cyclic
triples $(0,i,j)$ are the three components of
$\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$; conversely these eight scalar equations
reproduce the two systems.

(b) [Form invariance under a change of inertial description] Let $x'$ be another
inertial chart with transition $x'=\Lambda x+b$, $\Lambda$ a proper
orthochronous Lorentz matrix (the changes of inertial description adopted in
[[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]), and let the primed components of the same
objects be the tensor components of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]
(iii): $F'^{\,ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$,
$F'_{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a(\Lambda^{-1})^d{}_bF_{cd}$,
$j'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bj^b$. Then (TM1) holds in $x$ if and only if (TM1) holds in
$x'$ with $j'$, and (TM2) holds in $x$ if and only if it holds in $x'$; by (a)
applied in both charts the four smooth-branch equations are likewise
form-invariant, the primed fields satisfying the primed equations with the
primed sources.

(c) [Hypotheses actually used] Only first derivatives of $E,B$ occur; the
equivalence uses exactly the component dictionary, the alternating character of
$F$, the constants $\mu_0,c,\varepsilon_0$ and the identification
$j=(c\rho,J)$, and the covariance clause uses the constant-coefficient
component law and the invertibility of $\Lambda$. No potential, no second
derivative, no boundary, decay or smoothness hypothesis beyond the stated
class, and no converse from the wave equations to the Maxwell equations is used
or asserted.

(d) [Scope] Only the smooth branch is covered; the weak branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and field or source points of singular support are
excluded. The conventions $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ fix the
signs of (TM1), and the alternative sign convention, which reverses the form of
the sourced equation, is not mixed with them. The statement is conditional on
the adopted postulates, uses no choice principle and makes no empirical claim.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ with its inertial chart
$x$ ($x^0=ct$); the jointly $C^1$ fields $E,B$ with the additional derivatives
required by each Maxwell equation existing and continuous; the continuous
source fields $(\rho,J)$; the electromagnetic two-form $F$ with the component
dictionary and index conventions of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]; the
four-current $j=(c\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]]; the constants $\mu_0,c>0$ and
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the smooth-branch
Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; and a second inertial chart
$x'=\Lambda x+b$ with $\Lambda$ a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix as adopted
in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]].

[F1] In the chart $x$ the electromagnetic two-form has components
$F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F_{ab}=-F_{ba}$,
$F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, and
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; here $\epsilon_{ijk}$ is the spatial
permutation symbol, so $\epsilon_{ijk}=+1$ for even and $-1$ for odd
permutations of $(1,2,3)$ and $\epsilon_{ijk}=0$ if two indices coincide
([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a), [[def-em-si-conventions]]). The
four-current components are $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$
([[def-em-sources]] (c)).

[F2] On $U$ the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell postulate holds:
$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$,
$\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and
$\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$, for jointly $C^1$ fields with
the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous
and continuous sources ([[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] (a)).

[F3] For a $C^1$ vector field $G=(G_1,G_2,G_3)$ on an open subset of
$\mathbb R^3$, $\operatorname{div}G=\partial_1G_1+\partial_2G_2+\partial_3G_3$
and $\operatorname{curl}G=(\partial_2G_3-\partial_3G_2,\ \partial_3G_1-\partial_1G_3,\ \partial_1G_2-\partial_2G_1)$,
so $(\operatorname{curl}G)_i=\epsilon_{ijk}\partial_jG_k$ for $i=1,2,3$
([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]).

[F4] The coordinate $x^0$ of the chart is $x^0=ct$, so
$\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$, where $\partial_t$ is the partial derivative at
fixed position and $\partial_i$ are the spatial partial derivatives of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]
([[def-em-lab-geometry]] (a), (c), [[def-em-si-conventions]] (a)).

[F5] The constants satisfy $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, hence
$\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$ and $c^{-2}=\mu_0\varepsilon_0$
([[def-em-si-conventions]] (a)).

[F6] A change of inertial description is an affine map $x'=\Lambda x+b$ whose
linear part $\Lambda$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix; such a
$\Lambda$ is invertible, with inverse matrix $(\Lambda^{-1})^a{}_b$ satisfying
$\Lambda^a{}_b(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_c=\delta^a_c$ and
$(\Lambda^{-1})^a{}_b\Lambda^b{}_c=\delta^a_c$
([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] (ii)).

[F7] For the same tensor field $F$ and vector field $j$ read in the two charts,
the components transform as $F'^{\,ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$,
$F'_{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a(\Lambda^{-1})^d{}_bF_{cd}$,
$j'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bj^b$, and the coordinate partial derivatives satisfy
$\partial'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\partial_c$ wherever the derivatives exist
([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (i), (iii), (iv)).

[L1] Because $F$ is alternating, $F_{ab}=-F_{ba}$ and $F_{aa}=0$ for all
$a,b\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ ([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct component computation in the fixed dictionary,
followed by the constant-coefficient transformation law.

1.1 (Sourced equation, $\nu=0$) On $I\times\Omega$ the equation (TM1) with $\nu=0$ holds if and only if $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$. Indeed $\partial_\mu F^{\mu0}=\partial_0F^{00}+\partial_iF^{i0}=0+\partial_i(-E_i/c)=-\operatorname{div}E/c$ by [F1] and [F3], using $F^{00}=0$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$; the right-hand side is $-\mu_0j^0=-\mu_0c\rho$ by [F1]; the identity $-\operatorname{div}E/c=-\mu_0c\rho$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{div}E=\mu_0c^2\rho=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ by [F5] and $c>0$. [given, F1, F3, F5, algebra]

1.2 (Sourced equations, $\nu=i$) On $I\times\Omega$ the three equations (TM1) with $\nu=i$, $i=1,2,3$, hold if and only if $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Indeed $\partial_\mu F^{\mu i}=\partial_0F^{0i}+\partial_jF^{ji}=c^{-2}\partial_tE_i+\epsilon_{jik}\partial_jB_k=c^{-2}\partial_tE_i-(\operatorname{curl}B)_i$: the first term uses $F^{0i}=E_i/c$ and $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ from [F4], the second uses $F^{ji}=-\epsilon_{ijk}B_k=\epsilon_{jik}B_k$ by [F1] and [L1], and the last equality is $(\operatorname{curl}B)_i=\epsilon_{ijk}\partial_jB_k$ from [F3] together with $\epsilon_{jik}=-\epsilon_{ijk}$. Equating with $-\mu_0j^i=-\mu_0J_i$ by [F1] gives $(\operatorname{curl}B)_i=\mu_0J_i+c^{-2}\partial_tE_i$ for each $i$, that is $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. [given, F1, F3, F4, L1, algebra]

1.3 (Repeated-index instances of (TM2) vanish) If two of $\lambda,\mu,\nu$ coincide, the cyclic sum in (TM2) vanishes identically on $U$. For $\lambda=\mu$ the sum is $\partial_\lambda F_{\lambda\nu}+\partial_\lambda F_{\nu\lambda}+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\lambda}=\partial_\lambda(F_{\lambda\nu}+F_{\nu\lambda})+0=0$ by [L1]; the cases $\lambda=\nu$ and $\mu=\nu$ are the same computation with the terms relabelled, since in each case two of the three terms are $\pm$ the same derivative and the third contains the vanishing diagonal entry $F_{aa}=0$. [given, F1, L1, algebra]

1.4 (Instance $(1,2,3)$ is the Gauss law for $B$) The instance $(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=(1,2,3)$ of (TM2) reads $\partial_1F_{23}+\partial_2F_{31}+\partial_3F_{12}=\partial_1B_1+\partial_2B_2+\partial_3B_3=\operatorname{div}B$, because $\epsilon_{231}=\epsilon_{312}=\epsilon_{123}=+1$ gives $F_{23}=B_1$, $F_{31}=B_2$ and $F_{12}=B_3$ in [F1], and [F3] identifies the sum with $\operatorname{div}B$. Hence this instance is equivalent to $\operatorname{div}B=0$. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

1.5 (Cyclic instances $(0,i,j)$ are the Faraday components) For each cyclic ordering $(i,j,k)$ of $(1,2,3)$ the instance $(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=(0,i,j)$ of (TM2) reads $\partial_0F_{ij}+\partial_iF_{j0}+\partial_jF_{0i}=c^{-1}\partial_tB_k+c^{-1}\partial_iE_j-c^{-1}\partial_jE_i=c^{-1}\bigl(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\bigr)$, using $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ [F4], $F_{ij}=B_k$ for the cyclic index order [F1], $F_{j0}=-F_{0j}=E_j/c$ and $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ [F1], [L1], and $(\operatorname{curl}E)_k=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j=\partial_iE_j-\partial_jE_i$ for the cyclic order [F3]. Hence these three instances are equivalent to the three components of $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$. [given, F1, F3, F4, L1, algebra]

1.6 (Transformation data) In the second chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$ the component laws of [F7] hold, with the invertible matrix $\Lambda$ and its inverse entries $(\Lambda^{-1})^a{}_b$ as in [F6]. The primed component functions are constant-coefficient finite linear combinations of the unprimed components, so on the overlap of the two chart restrictions they are again jointly $C^1$ with the same additional derivatives existing and continuous. [given, F6, F7, algebra]

2.1 (Reduction of all instances of (TM2)) Every instance of (TM2) is either a repeated-index instance, which vanishes identically by step 1.3, or an instance with distinct indices. For distinct indices, interchanging two of $\lambda,\mu,\nu$ changes the cyclic sum's sign: with $S(\lambda,\mu,\nu):=\partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu}$ one has $S(\lambda,\nu,\mu)=\partial_\lambda F_{\nu\mu}+\partial_\nu F_{\mu\lambda}+\partial_\mu F_{\lambda\nu}=-(\partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu})=-S(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ by [L1], and the other two transpositions are the same computation after relabelling. Since transpositions generate the symmetric group, each of the $24$ distinct-index instances equals $\pm S$ of one of the four index sets $\{1,2,3\}$, $\{0,1,2\}$, $\{0,2,3\}$, $\{0,3,1\}$; by steps 1.4 and 1.5 the system (TM2) is therefore equivalent to the four scalar equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and the three components of $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$. [given, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 1.5, F1, L1, algebra]

2.2 ((TM1) is form-invariant) Using [F7], whose $\partial'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\partial_c$ has constant coefficients, $\partial'_aF'^{\,ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\partial_c(\Lambda^a{}_e\Lambda^b{}_fF^{ef})=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\Lambda^a{}_e\Lambda^b{}_f\partial_cF^{ef}=\delta^c_e\Lambda^b{}_f\partial_cF^{ef}=\Lambda^b{}_f\partial_cF^{cf}$, the third equality by the inverse-matrix identity of [F6]. Since also $j'^b=\Lambda^b{}_fj^f$ by [F7], the equation (TM1) in $x'$ is $\Lambda^b{}_f(\partial_cF^{cf}+\mu_0j^f)=0$ for every $b$; multiplying by $(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_g$ and summing over $b$ gives $\partial_cF^{cg}=-\mu_0j^g$ for every $g$, and substitution gives the converse. Hence (TM1) holds in $x$ if and only if it holds in $x'$ with $j'$. [given, step 1.6, F6, F7, algebra]

2.3 ((TM2) is form-invariant) Write $S_{abc}:=\partial_aF_{bc}+\partial_bF_{ca}+\partial_cF_{ab}$. By [F7] the three terms of the primed cyclic sum are $\partial'_\lambda F'_{\mu\nu}=(\Lambda^{-1})^a{}_\lambda(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_\mu(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_\nu\partial_aF_{bc}$, $\partial'_\mu F'_{\nu\lambda}=(\Lambda^{-1})^a{}_\lambda(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_\mu(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_\nu\partial_bF_{ca}$ and $\partial'_\nu F'_{\lambda\mu}=(\Lambda^{-1})^a{}_\lambda(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_\mu(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_\nu\partial_cF_{ab}$, the second and third after relabelling the dummy summation indices $a,b,c$. Their sum is $S'_{\lambda\mu\nu}=(\Lambda^{-1})^a{}_\lambda(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_\mu(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_\nu S_{abc}$; hence $S=0$ implies $S'=0$, and conversely $S_{abc}=\Lambda^\lambda{}_a\Lambda^\mu{}_b\Lambda^\nu{}_cS'_{\lambda\mu\nu}$ by the inverse-matrix identity of [F6], so $S'=0$ implies $S=0$. Thus (TM2) holds in $x$ if and only if it holds in $x'$. [given, step 1.6, F6, F7, algebra]

3.1 (Equivalence of clause (a)) If the four smooth-branch equations hold on $I\times\Omega$, then (TM1) holds by steps 1.1 and 1.2 and (TM2) holds by steps 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 and 2.1: the repeated-index instances vanish, the instance $(1,2,3)$ is $\operatorname{div}B=0$, and the three cyclic instances vanish because $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$. Conversely, if (TM1) and (TM2) hold, then steps 1.1 and 1.2 give $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and the three components of $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$, while steps 1.4 and 1.5 give $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and the three components of $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$. This proves the biconditional and identifies the eight scalar equations: (TM1)'s four components and, from the reduction of step 2.1, the distinct group $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and the three Faraday components; all remaining instances of (TM2) are repeats of these up to sign. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.4, step 1.5, step 2.1, F2, algebra]

4.1 (Form invariance of the four equations) The computation of steps 1.1-3.1 is a statement about an inertial chart and its component dictionary and applies verbatim in the chart $x'$, whose primed fields and sources are again of the required class by step 1.6: the four primed smooth-branch equations hold if and only if (TM1) and (TM2) hold in $x'$ with $j'$. By steps 2.2 and 2.3 the primed tensor systems hold if and only if the unprimed ones do; by step 3.1 the latter hold if and only if the four equations hold in $x$. Therefore the four smooth-branch equations hold in $x$ if and only if the same four equations, with the primed fields and primed sources, hold in $x'$. This is conditional on the adopted covariance premise [F6] and proves no physical equivalence of descriptions beyond it. [given, step 3.1, step 1.6, step 2.2, step 2.3, F6]

5.1 (Hypotheses and scope) Steps 1.1-4.1 used only first derivatives of $E,B$; the equivalence used the component dictionary [F1], the alternating character of $F$ [L1], the constants $\mu_0,c,\varepsilon_0$ [F5] and the identification $j=(c\rho,J)$; the covariance clauses used the constant-coefficient component law [F7] and the invertibility of $\Lambda$ [F6]. No potential, no second derivative, no boundary, decay or additional smoothness hypothesis was used, no converse from the wave equations to the Maxwell equations is asserted, and no step covers the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] or singular source support; the signs are fixed by the conventions $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ and no alternative dictionary is mixed in. The argument is finite linear algebra over the fixed component functions; it uses no choice principle and makes no empirical claim. [given, step 1.1, step 4.1, F1, F2, F5, F6, F7] ∎

## Source notes

The three cited treatments present the antisymmetric field tensor, the
inhomogeneous equation in the form $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ (in
suitable conventions) and the homogeneous cyclic identity, and derive the
component dictionary from the laboratory fields with sign and index conversions
recorded in the locators. The deduction above is the component check that the
two systems say exactly the same thing as the four laboratory equations in the
framework's conventions, together with the constant-coefficient form invariance;
the textbook treatments state these facts for their own conventions, and the
conversion to the framework's dictionary is carried out here rather than
assumed.

## Statement

Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region
$U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart $x$ of the framework
([[def-em-lab-geometry]]), $k\ge1$, with the SI units of
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components
$F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$,
$F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$,
$v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $\Lambda_\beta$ be the explicit boost of
[[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] with
$\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_0=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_1=\gamma$,
$\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_1=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$,
$\Lambda_\beta{}^2{}_2=\Lambda_\beta{}^3{}_3=1$ and all other entries zero. Let
$x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the corresponding inertial chart, and for every event
$p$ in the overlap of the two chart restrictions define the primed field
components by reading the components of the same $F$ in $x'$ through the
dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], so that $F'_{0i}=-E'_i/c$,
$F'_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B'_k$ at $p$. Then:

(a) [Boosted fields] at every such $p$, with $\parallel$ and $\perp$ the
components along and orthogonal to $e_1$ in the spatial Euclidean structure of
the chart,
$$E'_1=E_1,\quad B'_1=B_1,\qquad E'_\parallel=E_\parallel,\quad B'_\parallel=B_\parallel,\qquad E'_\perp=\gamma\,(E+v\times B)_\perp,\qquad B'_\perp=\gamma\,(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp,$$
equivalently, componentwise,
$E'_2=\gamma(E_2-\beta cB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+\beta cB_2)$,
$B'_2=\gamma(B_2+\beta E_3/c)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$.

(a′) [Arbitrary boost direction] For a velocity vector $v\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$|v|<c$, use the actual vector boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]], with
$\gamma_v=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. If $v\ne0$, decompose the fields along
$\widehat v=v/|v|$ and its orthogonal complement. Then $E'_\parallel=E_\parallel$,
$B'_\parallel=B_\parallel$, $E'_\perp=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and
$B'_\perp=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$. Equivalently, for every $v$,
including $v=0$,
$$E'=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot E)}{c^2},\qquad B'=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot B)}{c^2}.$$
At $v=0$ these are the identity and no preferred parallel direction is
assigned.

(b) [Invariants] at every such $p$,
$$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=E\cdot B;$$
equivalently the scalar fields $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$
and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]
(b) take the same values whether computed from the components in $x$ or in
$x'$.

(c) [General proper orthochronous changes] for any proper orthochronous Lorentz
matrix $\Lambda$ with chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$, the primed components of $F$ are
given by the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii),
$F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$; in particular, if
$\Lambda=\widehat R$ is the extension of a spatial rotation $R$ of the frame
([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]), then $E'=RE$ and $B'=RB$, and
by the unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of
[[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii) every proper
orthochronous change acts first by $(E,B)\mapsto(RE,RB)$ and then by the
arbitrary-direction boost law (a′) with velocity $-c\beta$, where $\beta$ is
the vector parameter of that factorization. The axis-only law (a) is not
substituted for a general vector boost.

(d) [Form invariance of the Maxwell branch] if $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfy the
smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in $x$ on the overlap, and
$(\rho',J')$ are the components of the same four-current in $x'$, then
$(E',B',\rho',J')$ satisfy the same four equations in $x'$, by
[[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]].

(e) [Scope] All clauses are pointwise on the overlap $U\cap U'$ of the two
chart restrictions, are conditional on the adopted postulates, and concern the
smooth classical flat branch; no accelerating coordinates, curved spacetime,
material medium, apparatus or empirical claim is involved; the transformation
is exact algebra, and the primed component functions are $C^k$ wherever the
overlap is open. The invariants clause uses only the proper orthochronous
changes of description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]];
orientation-reversing changes are outside the framework's field conventions
([[def-em-fields]]).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The inertial chart $x$ of the framework's laboratory region with the
fields $E,B$ (jointly $C^k$, $k\ge1$) and the continuous sources $(\rho,J)$, and
the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the electromagnetic two-form $F$ with
the dictionary, invariants and conventions of [F1]; the axis boost
$\Lambda_\beta$ of [F2] with $0\le\beta<1$ and its chart
$x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$; a velocity vector $v\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|v|<c$ and the
vector boost $B(v/c)$ of [F2]; a general proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix
$\Lambda$ with chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$; and the postulates [F4] and [F9]. Every
primed component is read through the dictionary [F1].

[F1] In the chart $x$ the electromagnetic two-form has components
$F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F_{ab}=-F_{ba}$ and
$F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, where $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$
and $\epsilon_{ijk}=+1$ for even, $-1$ for odd permutations of $(1,2,3)$ and
$0$ for repeated indices; its Hodge dual is
$(*F)_{ab}=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ and its scalar contractions
are $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and
$I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$, with $|\cdot|$ and $\cdot$ the spatial
Euclidean structure of the frame
([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a), (b),
[[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] (a), (c)). The fields carry
V m$^{-1}$ and T, $E$ is a polar and $B$ an axial vector relative to the
orientation of the spatial basis, only orientation-preserving changes of
inertial description are adopted, and no value of a field at a point of
singular source support is asserted
([[def-em-fields]] (a)-(c), [[def-em-si-conventions]] (b)). The four-current is
$j^0=c\rho$, $j^i=J^i$ ([[def-em-sources]] (c)).

[F2] For $0\le\beta<1$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ the map $\Lambda_\beta$
with matrix $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_0=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_1=\gamma$,
$\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_1=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$,
$\Lambda_\beta{}^2{}_2=\Lambda_\beta{}^3{}_3=1$ and all other entries zero is a
proper orthochronous Lorentz map with $\det\Lambda_\beta=1$ and
$\Lambda_\beta^{-1}=\Lambda_{-\beta}$
([[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] (a)-(d)). For
$\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ and
$\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)=(1-|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$, the vector boost
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ has matrix $B^0{}_0=\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)$,
$B^0{}_i=B^i{}_0=-\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)\beta_i$,
$B^i{}_j=\delta^i{}_j+\frac{\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^2}\beta_i\beta_j$
for $\boldsymbol\beta\ne0$, and $B(\boldsymbol 0)=\operatorname{id}_V$; it is a
proper orthochronous Lorentz map with
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)^{-1}=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$, and for
$\boldsymbol\beta\ne0$ one has
$\frac{\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^2}=\frac{\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)^2}{\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)+1}$
([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (i)).

[F3] For a second inertial chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$ with $\Lambda$ proper
orthochronous, the components of the same tensor and vector fields satisfy
$F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$,
$F'_{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a(\Lambda^{-1})^d{}_bF_{cd}$ and
$j'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bj^b$, and every contraction of one contravariant with one
covariant index is invariant
([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (i), (iii)).

[F4] A change of inertial description is an affine map $x'=\Lambda x+b$ whose
linear part $\Lambda$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix ($\eta$-preserving,
$\det=+1$, $C^+$-preserving), and such a $\Lambda$ is invertible
([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] (ii)). Every vector boost $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$
with $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ and every spatial rotation of the frame belongs to
$SO^+(V,\eta)$, and every $L\in SO^+(V,\eta)$ has a unique factorization
$L=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$ with $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ and $\widehat R$
the extension of a spatial rotation of the frame, where
$\boldsymbol\beta=u_{\mathrm{vec}}/u^0$ for $u=Le_0$
([[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (i)-(iii)).

[F5] A spatial rotation $R$ of the frame fixes $e_0$, preserves the spatial
three-space $S$, satisfies $\delta(Rw,Rz)=\delta(w,z)$ on $S$, and its
restriction has determinant $+1$ in the ordered basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$; under the
identification of $S$ with $\mathbb R^3$ by that basis, the maps of these
conditions are exactly those with block matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,A)$ where
$A^{\mathsf T}A=I_3$ and $\det A=+1$, so the columns of $A$ are an orthonormal
family of $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]).

[F6] For coordinate columns in $\mathbb R^3$ the cross product is
$u\times v=(u_2v_3-u_3v_2,\ u_3v_1-u_1v_3,\ u_1v_2-u_2v_1)$
([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); it is bilinear and alternating,
$u\times v$ is orthogonal to $u$ and $v$, and
$\langle u\times v,w\rangle=\det[u\ v\ w]$, where the bracket denotes the
$3\times3$ matrix with these columns
([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]); moreover
$\lVert u\times v\rVert_2^2=\lVert u\rVert_2^2\lVert v\rVert_2^2-\langle u,v\rangle^2$
([[thm-cross-product-norm-is-the-two-vector-gram-determinant]]). The Euclidean
inner product is bilinear, symmetric and positive definite, so
$\langle z,z\rangle=0$ implies $z=0$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

[F7] For a real $n\times n$ matrix $A$ one has
$\det A=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i<n}A^{\sigma(i)}{}_i$
(sum over columns $i$); permuting the columns by a permutation $\pi$ multiplies
the determinant by $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$, so a determinant with two equal
columns vanishes and $\det I_n=1$
([[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]); $\det(A^{\mathsf T})=\det A$
([[thm-determinant-of-transpose]]); $A$ is invertible if and only if
$\det A\ne0$
([[thm-real-square-matrix-invertible-iff-determinant-nonzero]]); and the
determinant of a linear operator is the determinant of its coordinate matrix
([[def-determinant-of-a-linear-operator]]).

[F8] [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]: under that theorem's hypotheses,
stated for the framework's chart $x$, the four smooth-branch Maxwell equations
hold on the laboratory region if and only if the two tensor systems
$(\mathrm{TM1})$ $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ and $(\mathrm{TM2})$
$\partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu}=0$
hold there; and for a second inertial chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$ with proper
orthochronous $\Lambda$, $(\mathrm{TM1})$ holds in $x$ if and only if it holds
in $x'$ with $j'$, and $(\mathrm{TM2})$ holds in $x$ if and only if it holds in
$x'$; consequently the four smooth-branch equations are form-invariant, the
primed fields satisfying the primed equations with the primed sources (clauses
(a), (b)).

[F9] The smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell postulate: for jointly $C^1$ fields
with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and
continuous, and continuous sources,
$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$,
$\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and
$\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$
([[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] (a)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct component computation in the fixed dictionary, the
explicit conjugation of the vector boost by a rotation, and the constant
component law.

1.1 (Clause (a): the axis boost components) For a spatial vector $W$ write $W_\parallel:=(W\cdot e_1)e_1$ and $W_\perp:=W-W_\parallel$. By [F2] and [F3](iii), $F'^{ab}=\Lambda_\beta{}^a{}_c\Lambda_\beta{}^b{}_dF^{cd}$ on the overlap; substituting the nonzero entries of [F2] and the components of [F1] gives $F'^{01}=\Lambda^0{}_0\Lambda^1{}_1F^{01}+\Lambda^0{}_1\Lambda^1{}_0F^{10}=\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)F^{01}=F^{01}$, $F'^{02}=\Lambda^0{}_0\Lambda^2{}_2F^{02}+\Lambda^0{}_1\Lambda^2{}_2F^{12}=\gamma(E_2/c-\beta B_3)$, $F'^{03}=\gamma(E_3/c+\beta B_2)$, $F'^{12}=\Lambda^1{}_0\Lambda^2{}_2F^{02}+\Lambda^1{}_1\Lambda^2{}_2F^{12}=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$, $F'^{13}=-\gamma(B_2+\beta E_3/c)$ and $F'^{23}=F^{23}=B_1$, because $F^{00}=F^{11}=0$, $F^{10}=-E_1/c$, $F^{02}=E_2/c$, $F^{03}=E_3/c$, $F^{12}=B_3$, $F^{13}=-B_2$ and $F^{23}=B_1$ by [F1]. Reading the dictionary [F1] in the primed chart, $E'_i=cF'^{0i}$ and $F'^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B'_k$, gives $E'_1=E_1$, $E'_2=\gamma(E_2-\beta cB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+\beta cB_2)$, $B'_1=B_1$, $B'_2=\gamma(B_2+\beta E_3/c)$ and $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$. Since $v=\beta ce_1$, the coordinate formulas of [F6] give $v\times B=\beta c\,(0,-B_3,B_2)$ and $v\times E=\beta c\,(0,-E_3,E_2)$; hence $(E+v\times B)_\perp=(0,E_2-\beta cB_3,E_3+\beta cB_2)$ and $(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp=(0,B_2+\beta E_3/c,B_3-\beta E_2/c)$, so the transverse formulas and the unchanged parallel components read $E'_\parallel=E_\parallel$, $B'_\parallel=B_\parallel$, $E'_\perp=\gamma(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$, as claimed. [given, F1, F2, F3, F6, algebra]

1.2 (Clause (c), rotation case; the orientation identity) Let $A\in M_3(\mathbb R)$ satisfy $A^{\mathsf T}A=I_3$ and $\det A=+1$, and let $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(1,A)$; then the components $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$ of [F3] satisfy $E'=AE$ and $B'=AB$. First $F'^{0i}=A^i{}_jF^{0j}$, so $E'_i=cF'^{0i}=A^i{}_jE_j$. For the magnetic block, the dictionary gives $B'_q=\tfrac12\epsilon_{qij}F'^{ij}$, since inserting $F'^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijp}B'_p$ yields $\tfrac12\epsilon_{qij}\epsilon_{ijp}B'_p=\delta_{qp}B'_p$ by the elementary contraction $\epsilon_{qij}\epsilon_{ijp}=2\delta_{qp}$ (direct enumeration of the two contributing index pairs). Hence $B'_q=\tfrac12\epsilon_{qij}A^i{}_kA^j{}_l\epsilon_{klm}B_m$, and the matrix $A$ satisfies the cofactor identity $\epsilon_{qij}A^i{}_kA^j{}_l=A^q{}_m\epsilon_{mkl}$ for all $q,k,l$: the determinant of the matrix with columns $(c_m,c_k,c_l)$ of $A$ equals $\epsilon_{mkl}\det A=\epsilon_{mkl}$ by column alternation [F7], and it also equals $\sum_{n,i,j}\epsilon_{nij}A^n{}_mA^i{}_kA^j{}_l$ by the permutation expansion [F7]; multiplying that equality by $A^q{}_m$ and summing over $m$ turns the factor $A^q{}_mA^n{}_m$ into $(AA^{\mathsf T})^{qn}=\delta^{qn}$ and yields the identity, where $AA^{\mathsf T}=I_3$ holds because $A^{\mathsf T}A=I_3$ with $\det A=1\ne0$ makes $A$ invertible with inverse $A^{\mathsf T}$ [F7]. Then $B'_q=\tfrac12A^q{}_m\epsilon_{mkl}\epsilon_{klm}B_m=\tfrac12A^q{}_m\cdot2B_m=A^q{}_mB_m$ by the elementary identity $\epsilon_{mkl}\epsilon_{klm}=2$ for each $m$ (direct enumeration), so $B'=AB$. If $A$ is the matrix in the basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of a spatial rotation $R$ of the frame, then $A^{\mathsf T}A=I_3$ and $\det A=+1$ by [F5], and $E'=RE$, $B'=RB$, which is the rotation case of clause (c). [given, F1, F3, F5, F6, F7, algebra]

1.3 (Conjugation of the vector boost) Let $v\in\mathbb R^3$ with $0<|v|<c$, put $u:=v/|v|$ and $\beta:=|v|/c\in(0,1)$, so $v/c=\beta u$. Among the standard basis vectors $e_1,e_2,e_3$ at most one is a multiple of $u$ (two independent vectors cannot both be nonzero multiples of one vector), so let $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ be the least index for which $e_j$ is not a multiple of $u$; set $\hat a:=\bigl(e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u\bigr)/\lVert e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u\rVert_2$, whose denominator is nonzero because $e_j$ is not a multiple of $u$, and $b:=u\times\hat a$. Then $(u,\hat a,b)$ is an orthonormal family, since $u\cdot\hat a=0$, $\lVert u\rVert_2=\lVert\hat a\rVert_2=1$, $b$ is orthogonal to $u$ and $\hat a$, and $\lVert b\rVert_2^2=\lVert u\rVert_2^2\lVert\hat a\rVert_2^2-(u\cdot\hat a)^2=1$ [F6]; it is positively oriented because $\det[u\ \hat a\ b]=\langle u\times\hat a,b\rangle=\lVert b\rVert_2^2=1$ [F6]. Let $S$ be the matrix with columns $u,\hat a,b$ and $R:=S^{\mathsf T}$, so the rows of $R$ are $u,\hat a,b$ and $Ru=e_1$; then $S^{\mathsf T}S=I_3$, $\det S=1$ and, since $\det S=1\ne0$, $S$ is invertible with $S^{-1}=S^{\mathsf T}$, so $SS^{\mathsf T}=I_3$, $R^{-1}=R^{\mathsf T}$ and $\det R=\det(S^{\mathsf T})=\det S=1$ [F7]. The conjugation identity $\widehat RB(v/c)\widehat R^{-1}=\Lambda_\beta$, where $\widehat R:=\operatorname{diag}(1,R)$, follows by direct substitution in the matrix of [F2]: for all $x\in V$ set $y:=\widehat Rx$, so $y^0=x^0$, $y_{\mathrm{vec}}=Rx_{\mathrm{vec}}$ and $x_{\mathrm{vec}}=R^{\mathsf T}y_{\mathrm{vec}}$; since $u\cdot x_{\mathrm{vec}}=u\cdot R^{\mathsf T}y_{\mathrm{vec}}=(Ru)\cdot y_{\mathrm{vec}}=y^1_{\mathrm{vec}}$ and $(v/c)\cdot x_{\mathrm{vec}}=\beta y^1_{\mathrm{vec}}$, the formula of [F2] with parameter $\beta u$ gives $(\widehat RB(v/c)x)^0=(B(v/c)x)^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta u\cdot x_{\mathrm{vec}})=\gamma(y^0-\beta y^1_{\mathrm{vec}})$ and $(\widehat RB(v/c)x)_{\mathrm{vec}}=R\bigl(R^{\mathsf T}y_{\mathrm{vec}}+(\gamma-1)y^1_{\mathrm{vec}}u-\gamma\beta y^0u\bigr)=y_{\mathrm{vec}}+(\gamma-1)y^1_{\mathrm{vec}}e_1-\gamma\beta y^0e_1$ using $(Ru)=e_1$; with $\widehat Rx=y$ this is exactly $\Lambda_\beta y$ by the matrix of [F2]. Hence $B(v/c)=\widehat R^{\mathsf T}\Lambda_\beta\widehat R$. [given, F2, F6, F7, choose, algebra]

1.4 (Regularity of the primed components) The overlap $V=U\cap U'$ is open and carries both charts: $x(U)=\{(ct,y):t\in I,\ y\in\Omega\}$ and $x'(U')$ are open in $\mathbb R^4$, the affine map $x\mapsto\Lambda^{-1}(x-b)$ carries $x'(U')$ bijectively onto $x(U')$, and $x$ carries $V$ onto the open set $x(U)\cap x(U')$ because $x$ and $x'$ are bijections [F3, F4]. On $V$ the primed component functions $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$ and $j'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bj^b$ are constant-coefficient finite linear combinations of the unprimed component functions [F3], so $E',B'$ inherit the joint class of $E,B$ under the fixed linear relabelling of the dictionary [F1], the additional derivatives required by each displayed equation exist and are continuous, and $\rho',J'$ are continuous whenever $\rho,J$ are. [given, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 (Clause (a′): arbitrary-direction boost) Let $v\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|v|<c$. If $v=0$, then $B(0)=\operatorname{id}_V$ [F2], the charts differ by the translation $x'=x+b$, the components are unchanged by [F3], so $E'=E$ and $B'=B$, and the closed formulas reduce to the identity because $\gamma_v=1$ and all terms carrying $v$ vanish; no parallel direction is needed. Let $v\ne0$ and use $u,\hat a,b,S,R,\beta$ and the conjugation identity $B(v/c)=\widehat R^{\mathsf T}\Lambda_\beta\widehat R=\operatorname{diag}(1,S)\Lambda_\beta\operatorname{diag}(1,R)$ of step 1.3. By [F3] the total component law of the composite is the matrix product of the factors of $B(v/c)=\widehat R^{\mathsf T}\Lambda_\beta\widehat R$; applied successively, the first stage is the rotation $\widehat R=\operatorname{diag}(1,R)$ (step 1.2 with $A=R$, whose hypotheses $R^{\mathsf T}R=I_3$ and $\det R=1$ hold by step 1.3), giving $E''=RE$, $B''=RB$; the second stage is the axis boost $\Lambda_\beta$ in the intermediate frame, where step 1.1 applies because its proof uses only the dictionary and the component law; the third stage is the rotation $\widehat R^{\mathsf T}=\operatorname{diag}(1,R^{\mathsf T})$ (step 1.2 with $A=R^{\mathsf T}$, whose hypotheses $RR^{\mathsf T}=I_3$ and $\det(R^{\mathsf T})=\det R=1$ hold by step 1.3 and [F7]), giving $E'=R^{\mathsf T}E'''$ and $B'=R^{\mathsf T}B'''$. Writing $\parallel,\perp$ for the components along $e_1$ in the intermediate coordinates, step 1.1 applied in the intermediate frame gives $E'''=E''_\parallel+\gamma(E''+\beta c\,e_1\times B'')_\perp$ and $B'''=B''_\parallel+\gamma(B''-\beta c\,e_1\times E''/c^2)_\perp$; applying $S=R^{\mathsf T}$ to the intermediate vectors and using the cross-product identity $R^{\mathsf T}(p\times q)=(R^{\mathsf T}p)\times(R^{\mathsf T}q)$ for the orthogonal matrix $R$ (obtained from the identity of step 1.2 by applying $R$ to both sides: $R\bigl((R^{\mathsf T}p)\times(R^{\mathsf T}q)\bigr)=(RR^{\mathsf T}p)\times(RR^{\mathsf T}q)=p\times q$) gives $R^{\mathsf T}(E''+\beta ce_1\times B'')=E+\beta c\,(R^{\mathsf T}e_1)\times(R^{\mathsf T}B'')=E+v\times B$, since $R^{\mathsf T}e_1=S e_1=u$ and $v=\beta cu$; moreover $R^{\mathsf T}E''_\parallel=(e_1\cdot E'')R^{\mathsf T}e_1=(u\cdot E)u=E_\parallel$ and $R^{\mathsf T}B''_\parallel=(u\cdot B)u=B_\parallel$. Hence $E'=E_\parallel+\gamma(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'=B_\parallel+\gamma(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$, which is the stated parallel/perpendicular form, and it yields $E'_\parallel=E_\parallel$, $B'_\parallel=B_\parallel$ by taking inner products with $u$. Finally $E_\parallel+\gamma(E+v\times B)_\perp=\gamma(E+v\times B)-(\gamma-1)(u\cdot E)u$ and $(\gamma-1)(u\cdot E)u=\frac{\gamma^2}{\gamma+1}\frac{v(v\cdot E)}{c^2}$, because $(u\cdot E)u=(v\cdot E)v/|v|^2$ and $(\gamma-1)/\beta^2=\gamma^2/(\gamma+1)$ [F2]; the same computation for $B$ gives the displayed closed formulas for every $v\ne0$, with $\gamma_v=\gamma$ since $|v|/c=\beta$. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, F2, F6, algebra]

2.2 (Clause (b): the invariants under the axis boost) Substituting the components of step 1.1, $|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=B_1^2-\frac{E_1^2}{c^2}+\gamma^2\bigl[(B_2+\beta E_3/c)^2+(B_3-\beta E_2/c)^2\bigr]-\frac{\gamma^2}{c^2}\bigl[(E_2-\beta cB_3)^2+(E_3+\beta cB_2)^2\bigr]$; the linear terms cancel in pairs and the transverse contributions combine to $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)\bigl(B_2^2+B_3^2-(E_2^2+E_3^2)/c^2\bigr)=B_2^2+B_3^2-(E_2^2+E_3^2)/c^2$ because $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ [F2], giving the first display. Likewise $E'\cdot B'=E_1B_1+\gamma^2\bigl[(E_2-\beta cB_3)(B_2+\beta E_3/c)+(E_3+\beta cB_2)(B_3-\beta E_2/c)\bigr]=E_1B_1+\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)(E_2B_2+E_3B_3)=E\cdot B$, since the mixed terms cancel in pairs. By [F1] the scalar fields $I_1$ and $I_2$ computed from the components in $x$ are $|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $4E\cdot B/c$, and those computed from the components in $x'$ are the same expressions in the primed fields, so the two displays say exactly that $I_1$ and $I_2$ take the same values in the two charts. [given, step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

3.1 (Clause (c): general proper orthochronous changes) Let $\Lambda$ be proper orthochronous with chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$. By [F3] the primed components are $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$, which is the first assertion. By [F4] there is a unique $\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ and a spatial rotation $R$ of the frame with $\Lambda=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$. Taking the intermediate chart $x''=\widehat Rx$ and the final chart $x'=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)x''+b$ realizes the same transition $x'=\Lambda x+b$; by step 1.2 the intermediate fields are $E''=RE$, $B''=RB$, and by step 2.1 applied with velocity $v=-c\boldsymbol\beta$ — for which $|v|=c|\boldsymbol\beta|<c$ and $B(v/c)=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$ [F2] — the final fields are $E'=E''_\parallel+\gamma_v(E''+v\times B'')_\perp$ and $B'=B''_\parallel+\gamma_v(B''-v\times E''/c^2)_\perp$, with $\gamma_v=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}=(1-|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$. This is exactly the statement that the change acts first by $(E,B)\mapsto(RE,RB)$ and then by the boost law (a′) with velocity $-c\boldsymbol\beta$; the axis-only law of (a) was not substituted for it. [given, step 1.2, step 2.1, F3, F4]

3.2 (Clause (b), general changes: the two scalar combinations) Every proper orthochronous change preserves $|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $E\cdot B$. Indeed, writing $\Lambda=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$ by [F4], the transformation factorizes into the rotation $\widehat R$, the axis boost $\Lambda_\beta$ in the intermediate frame and the inverse rotation, as in step 2.1; a spatial rotation with matrix $A$ satisfying $A^{\mathsf T}A=I_3$ preserves the Euclidean norm and inner product of vectors, $|AE|^2=|E|^2$, $|AB|^2=|B|^2$ and $(AE)\cdot(AB)=E\cdot B$ [F5]; and the axis boost preserves the two combinations $|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $E\cdot B$ by step 2.2. Chaining the three stages gives the invariance for every proper orthochronous change, hence in particular for the boost chart $x'$ of clause (b), and by [F1] the equivalently stated invariance of $I_1$ and $I_2$. [given, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, F1, F5, F6]

4.1 (Clause (d): form invariance of the smooth Maxwell branch) Let $x'=\Lambda x+b$ with $\Lambda$ proper orthochronous, and assume that on $V$ the four smooth-branch equations of [F9] hold for $(E,B,\rho,J)$. By [F8] the two tensor systems $(\mathrm{TM1})$ and $(\mathrm{TM2})$ hold in $x$ on $V$ and therefore also hold in $x'$ on $V$ with the primed components of the same $F$ and the same four-current, and then the four smooth-branch equations hold in $x'$ for the primed dictionary fields; the primed fields are exactly the fields $E',B'$ read in the dictionary [F1], which by step 3.1 are the components of the same $F$ given by the component law, and the primed sources are $(c\rho',J')$ because $j'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bj^b$ with $j^0=c\rho$, $j^i=J^i$ [F3, F1]. The hypotheses of [F8] in the chart $x'$ are met because the primed fields and sources are again of the required class on the open set $V$ by step 1.4. The converse is the same chain with the roles of $x$ and $x'$ exchanged, since $\Lambda^{-1}$ is again a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix [F4]. [given, step 1.4, step 3.1, F1, F3, F4, F8, F9]

5.1 (Hypotheses and scope) Clause (a) is step 1.1, clause (a′) is step 2.1, clause (b) is steps 2.2 and 3.2, clause (c) is steps 1.2 and 3.1, and clause (d) is step 4.1. The argument used only the component dictionary and invariants [F1], the two boost matrices and the identity $(\gamma-1)/\beta^2=\gamma^2/(\gamma+1)$ [F2], the constant component law and the invertibility of the changes of chart [F3, F4], the unique factorization of a proper orthochronous Lorentz map [F4], the matrix form and determinant of a spatial rotation [F5], the cross-product and Euclidean identities [F6], the determinant identities [F7], the tensor equivalence of [F8] and the smooth Maxwell branch [F9]. Only finitely many choices are made (the least index $j$ in step 1.3 and the finite index sets of [F7]); no choice principle, no potential, no derivative of the fields beyond the class required by the cited statements, no boundary, decay or medium hypothesis and no empirical premise are used. All clauses are pointwise on the open overlap of the two chart restrictions and conditional on the adopted postulates; orientation-reversing changes are outside the framework's conventions [F1], and no apparatus, detector or measurement model is introduced. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1] ∎

## Source notes

The three cited treatments present the transformation of the fields under a
passive boost, the rotation embedding and the two independent scalar
contractions of the field tensor in their own conventions. The deduction above
is the component computation in the framework's fixed dictionary (signs
$F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $x^0=ct$, $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$),
the explicit conjugation of the general vector boost by a rotation, and the
resulting invariance of the two scalar combinations and of the smooth Maxwell
branch; the conversion from the sources' conventions is carried out here rather
than assumed.

## Statement

Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] in SI units ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), $k\ge1$, and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $n\in V$ be a future unit observer vector, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest space $n^\perp$ and positive rest metric ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)), and suppose its coordinate velocity in the laboratory frame is $w$, $|w|<c$, so that $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$ with $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (d)-(e)). Then: (a) [Observer split and measured vectors] with $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$ as in [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], one has $e(n)=b(n)=0$, $e^\sharp,b^\sharp\in n^\perp$, the reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ (so the six rest components $(e,b)$ determine $F$ at the event), and in the laboratory frame $$e_i=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}\bigl(E_i+(w\times B)_i\bigr),\qquad b_i=-\gamma_w\Bigl(B_i-\frac{(w\times E)_i}{c^2}\Bigr),\qquad e_0=-\frac{\gamma_w}{c^2}E\cdot w,\qquad b_0=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}B\cdot w.$$ Define the measured electric and magnetic vectors $E_n:=c\,e^\sharp$ and $B_n:=-b^\sharp$, the covectors first restricted to $n^\perp$ and raised with its positive rest metric (equivalently their spacetime metric-dual vectors, since both annihilate $n$); under the model assumption (A1) that an ideal field detector comoving with the observer at the reception event reads the components of $F$ in the observer's rest frame — equivalently that $E_n$ and $B_n$ are the electric and magnetic fields read there — the observed components are, in the observer's inertial rest frame, the arbitrary-direction boosted components of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a′) for the vector parameter $\beta=w/c$: the components along $w$ equal $E_\parallel$ and $B_\parallel$, and the components perpendicular to $w$ equal $\gamma_w(E+w\times B)_\perp$ and $\gamma_w(B-w\times E/c^2)_\perp$. At $w=0$ the observer is the laboratory rest observer and reads $E,B$ themselves; there is no distinguished direction of motion. Orthogonality means $e(n)=b(n)=0$, not vanishing temporal covector components in an unrelated laboratory frame. (b) [Plane wave and exact frequency reading] let $K>0$, $\omega=cK$, a unit vector $s$, and complex amplitudes $e_{\mathrm a},b_{\mathrm a}\in\mathbb C^3$ be the data of a plane wave of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] whose amplitude equations hold as in [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]], so that the pair is a source-free smooth Maxwell field and $s$ is the propagation direction. Then the phase covector with components $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ in the laboratory frame is a nonzero future null covector, and under the ideal-plane-wave reading rule of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (ii) the observer reads the exact angular frequency $$\omega_n:=-c\,k(n)=\gamma_w\Bigl(1-\frac{w\cdot s}{c}\Bigr)\omega>0,$$ with the direction transformation (aberration), longitudinal formulas and two transverse protocols of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] (i)-(v) apply with their nonzero-motion qualifications; at $w=0$ frequency and direction are unchanged. Successive inertial changes act on the same phase covector by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (ii); each stage updates the direction as well as the frequency, and positive successive frequency ratios multiply. This composition statement is a direct covector/reading calculation, not a nonexistent composition clause of the Doppler supplier. (c) [Status and scope] the observer split, the nullity of $k$ and the frequency formula are conditional deductions from the stated items, while the identification of $(E_n,B_n)$ and of $\omega_n$ with apparatus readings is the explicitly adopted ideal-detector model assumption (A1) together with the ideal-plane-wave model [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] for the clock and light readings); no calibration, apparatus, statistical or empirical claim is made, no photon model and no identification of frequency with energy by a factor $\hbar$ is used, and the statement is pointwise at a reception event: the decomposition and the reconstruction of clause (a) hold pointwise for any future unit observer $n$, while the frequency and aberration readings of clause (b) are stated for inertial observers — an accelerating observer requires its own analysis, since differentiating the decomposition adds derivatives of $n$ — and media, dispersion, modulation, boundaries and finite line widths are outside the item.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The inertial chart $x$ of the laboratory region
([[def-em-lab-geometry]]) with its spatial basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and the jointly $C^k$ fields $E,B$ of
[[def-em-fields]], $k\ge1$, in the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the
electromagnetic two-form $F$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with the
dictionary and dual conventions of [F1]; a future unit observer vector $n$ with
coordinate velocity $w$ in the laboratory frame, $|w|<c$, as in [F2]; the
plane-wave data of [F4]; the adopted model postulates [F5], [F6] and [F8] and
the ideal-detector model assumption [A1].

[F1] In the chart $x$, with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$,
$\varepsilon_{0123}=+1$ and $\varepsilon^{0123}=-1$, the electromagnetic
two-form has $F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$,
$F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$; its Hodge dual
is $(*F)_{ab}=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ with $*(*F)=-F$; for a
future unit $n$ the rest components are $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$ and
$b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$, one has $e(n)=b(n)=0$ and the reconstruction
$F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ with $n^\flat=\eta(n,\cdot)$, the six
components $(e,b)$ determining $F$ at the event; for the laboratory rest
observer one has $e_i=E_i/c$ and $b_i=-B_i$, and the contractions are
$\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and
$F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$. The fields carry V m$^{-1}$ and T, and the
fractional structure is that of the frame's spatial Euclidean space
([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a), (b),
[[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] (a), (b), (c),
[[def-em-fields]] (c), [[def-em-si-conventions]] (b)).

[F2] Let $n\in V$ be future unit timelike, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with coordinate
velocity $w$ in the laboratory chart, $|w|<c$, so that
$n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$ with $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. Then $n^\perp$ is a
three-dimensional subspace on which $\eta$ restricts to a positive-definite
form, the map $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ is the linear projection onto $n^\perp$ along
$\operatorname{span}(n)$, each $v$ has the unique decomposition
$v=-\eta(n,v)n+h(v)$, and $w$ is the velocity of the worldline with
four-velocity $cn$ relative to the lab-rest observer
([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c), (d), (e),
[[def-lorentz-boost]]).

[F3] The passive boost $B(w/c)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map; its
matrix in $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $B^0{}_0=\gamma_w$,
$B^0{}_i=B^i{}_0=-\gamma_w w_i/c$ and
$B^i{}_j=\delta^i{}_j+\frac{\gamma_w-1}{|w/c|^2}\frac{w_i}{c}\frac{w_j}{c}$
([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (i)). In
the inertial chart $x'=B(w/c)x+b$ the dictionary components of the same $F$ are
the boosted components of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a′) with vector
parameter $v=w$: $E'_\parallel=E_\parallel$, $B'_\parallel=B_\parallel$,
$E'_\perp=\gamma_w(E+w\times B)_\perp$ and
$B'_\perp=\gamma_w(B-w\times E/c^2)_\perp$ along $\widehat w$, equivalently
$$E'=\gamma_w(E+w\times B)-\frac{\gamma_w^2}{\gamma_w+1}\frac{w(w\cdot E)}{c^2},\qquad B'=\gamma_w(B-w\times E/c^2)-\frac{\gamma_w^2}{\gamma_w+1}\frac{w(w\cdot B)}{c^2},$$
with $E'=E$, $B'=B$ for $w=0$; and the affine change is admissible because
$B(w/c)$ is proper orthochronous
([[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a′), (e),
[[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] (ii)).

[F4] Plane-wave data: $K>0$, $\omega=cK$, a unit vector $s$, and complex
amplitudes $e_{\mathrm a},b_{\mathrm a}\in\mathbb C^3$; the associated plane
wave of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] has wavevector
$\mathbf k:=Ks$ (so $|\mathbf k|=K=\omega/c$ and the propagation direction
$\widehat{\mathbf k}=s$), phase $\theta(x,t)=\mathbf k\cdot x-\omega t$ of class
$C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, and amplitude equations
$\mathbf k\cdot e_{\mathrm a}=0$, $\mathbf k\cdot b_{\mathrm a}=0$,
$\mathbf k\times e_{\mathrm a}=\omega b_{\mathrm a}$ and
$\mathbf k\times b_{\mathrm a}=-(\omega/c^2)e_{\mathrm a}$; by
[[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] (a) the pair is therefore a solution of the four
source-free smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations on
$\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] (a), (b), (c),
[[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] (a), [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]],
[[def-em-si-conventions]].

[F5] Adopted ideal plane-wave reading rule: an ideal observer of the model with
four-velocity $U_o=cn$, $n$ future unit timelike, that receives the wave reads
the angular frequency $\omega_n:=-ck(n)=-k(U_o)$ at the reception event of its
worldline; the ideal wave is the adopted monochromatic plane-wave model with
future null wave covector, and the model carries no quantum photon and no
$\hbar\omega$ identification ([[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (i)-(iv),
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] (ii)).

[F6] The exact classical Doppler theorem
[[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] (i)-(vi) applies to the ideal wave
of [F4]: for inertial charts $x'=B(\beta)x+b$ with $|\beta|<1$ and frame-$x$
data $(\omega,s)$, it gives (i) the frame-$x'$ data $(\omega',s')$ with
$\omega'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\omega>0$ and
$s'=\bigl[s+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\beta|^2}(\beta\cdot s)\beta-\gamma\beta\bigr]/\bigl[\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\bigr]$
(and $s'=s$, $\omega'=\omega$ for $\beta=0$); (ii) the reading
$\omega_o=\gamma_w(1-w\cdot s/c)\omega>0$ of an ideal observer of coordinate
velocity $w$, together with $\nu'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\nu$ and
$\lambda'=\lambda/[\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)]$; (iii) the longitudinal cases
$s=\pm\widehat\beta$; (iv) the two transverse protocols $\beta\cdot s=0$ and
$\beta\cdot s=|\beta|^2$; (v) the aberration relation
$\cos\theta_{x'}=(\cos\theta_x-|\beta|)/(1-|\beta|\cos\theta_x)$ with its
monotonicity; and (vi) its scope and exclusions. Its hypotheses — the adopted
model postulates and frame data with future null covector — are those of the
model it states.

[F7] Covector law and composition: if $\theta(p)=k_ax^a(p)+\theta_0$ is an
affine scalar function with constant covector $k$ and $x'=\Lambda x+b$ is an
inertial chart, then $\theta(p)=k'_ax'^a(p)+\theta'_0$ with
$k'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_ak_b$ and
$\theta'_0=\theta_0-k'_ab^a$; for successive affine transitions
$x_1=\Lambda_1x_0+b_1$ and $x_2=\Lambda_2x_1+b_2$ the composite is
$x_2=\Lambda_2\Lambda_1x_0+(\Lambda_2b_1+b_2)$
([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (ii),
[[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] (ii)).

[F8] Adopted ideal-clock and ideal-light assumptions: an ideal clock carried
along a future timelike $C^1$ curve reads
$c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}\,\mathrm ds$, and the ideal vacuum
light rays are exactly the future null straight lines with coordinate speed $c$
in every inertial chart ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] (i), (ii)).

[A1] Adopted ideal-detector model assumption: an ideal field detector comoving
with the observer at the reception event reads the components of $F$ in the
observer's rest frame; equivalently, the measured vectors $E_n=c\,e^\sharp$ and
$B_n=-b^\sharp$ are the electric and magnetic fields read there. This is an
adopted model assumption of this item, not a theorem, and it carries no
calibration, apparatus, statistical or empirical claim.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct evaluation of the observer decomposition, the
explicit boost to the observer's rest frame, and the exact Doppler theorem for
the plane wave.

1.1 (Clause (a): laboratory components of $e$ and $b$) By [F2], $n^0=\gamma_w$ and $n^i=\gamma_w w_i/c$, so with the dictionary [F1] the covariant components are $e_0=F_{00}n^0+F_{0i}n^i=-(\gamma_w/c^2)E\cdot w$ and $e_i=F_{i0}n^0+F_{ij}n^j=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}E_i+\frac{\gamma_w}{c}\epsilon_{ijk}w_jB_k=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}\bigl(E_i+(w\times B)_i\bigr)$, using $F_{i0}=-F_{0i}=E_i/c$ and $(w\times B)_i=\epsilon_{ijk}w_jB_k$ [F1]. For the dual, the definition $(*F)_{ab}=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ and the components of [F1] give $(*F)_{0i}=B_i$ and $(*F)_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}E_k/c$: indeed $\varepsilon_{0i}{}^{jk}=\varepsilon_{0ijk}=\epsilon_{ijk}$ because raising the two spatial indices is free and $(0,i,j,k)$ is an even permutation of $(0,1,2,3)$ exactly when $(i,j,k)$ is even, so $(*F)_{0i}=\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}=\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}\epsilon_{jk\ell}B_\ell=B_i$ with $\epsilon_{ijk}\epsilon_{jk\ell}=2\delta_{i\ell}$ (direct enumeration); and $\varepsilon_{ij}{}^{0k}=\eta^{00}\eta^{kk}\varepsilon_{ij0k}=-\varepsilon_{ij0k}=-\epsilon_{ijk}$, since $(0,i,j,k)\mapsto(i,j,0,k)$ is an even permutation, so $(*F)_{ij}=\varepsilon_{ij}{}^{0k}F_{0k}=(-\epsilon_{ijk})(-E_k/c)=\epsilon_{ijk}E_k/c$. Hence $b_0=(*F)_{00}n^0+(*F)_{0i}n^i=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}B\cdot w$ and $b_i=(*F)_{i0}n^0+(*F)_{ij}n^j=-\gamma_wB_i+\frac{\gamma_w}{c^2}\epsilon_{ijk}w_jE_k=-\gamma_w\bigl(B_i-\frac{(w\times E)_i}{c^2}\bigr)$. These are the four displayed component formulas of clause (a); in particular the laboratory temporal components $e_0,b_0$ need not vanish, so the orthogonality of the decomposition cannot be read as the vanishing of these laboratory components. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 (Clause (a): annihilation, raising, reconstruction) Since $F$ and $*F$ are alternating, $e(n)=F_{ab}n^an^b=0$ and $b(n)=(*F)_{ab}n^an^b=0$; equivalently $n^ae_a=n^ab_a=0$ [F1]. For the metric-dual vectors $e^\sharp,b^\sharp$, defined by $\eta(e^\sharp,v)=e(v)$ and $\eta(b^\sharp,v)=b(v)$ for all $v$, this gives $\eta(e^\sharp,n)=\eta(b^\sharp,n)=0$, so $e^\sharp,b^\sharp\in n^\perp$; since both covectors annihilate $n$, restricting them to $n^\perp$ and raising with the positive rest metric of [F2] gives the same vectors, and this is the raising used in the definitions $E_n=c\,e^\sharp$, $B_n=-b^\sharp$. By [F1] the reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ holds, and because the dictionary formulas of [F1] recover the six components of $F$ from $(e,b)$, the six rest components determine $F$ at the event. The measured vectors lie in the three-dimensional rest space $n^\perp$; they are not the laboratory coordinate triples $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and $(b_1,b_2,b_3)$. [given, F1, F2]

1.3 (Clause (a): the observer's inertial rest frame and the observed components) Applying the matrix of [F3] to the vector $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$ of [F2] gives $\bigl(B(w/c)n\bigr)^0=\gamma_w\bigl(\gamma_w-\frac{w}{c}\cdot\frac{\gamma_w w}{c}\bigr)=\gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2)=1$ and $\bigl(B(w/c)n\bigr)_{\mathrm{vec}}=\frac{\gamma_w w}{c}+\frac{\gamma_w-1}{|w/c|^2}\Bigl(\frac{w}{c}\cdot\frac{\gamma_w w}{c}\Bigr)\frac{w}{c}-\gamma_w\frac{w}{c}\gamma_w=\gamma_w\frac{w}{c}\bigl[1+(\gamma_w-1)-\gamma_w\bigr]=0$; hence $n$ has coordinates $(1,0,0,0)$ in the chart $x'=B(w/c)x+b$, that is $n=e'_0$: the chart $x'$ is the observer's inertial rest frame, and it is an admissible inertial change of description because $B(w/c)$ is proper orthochronous [F3]. By clause (a′) of [F3] the components of the same $F$ read in $x'$ are the boosted components with vector parameter $v=w$: $E'_\parallel=E_\parallel$, $B'_\parallel=B_\parallel$, $E'_\perp=\gamma_w(E+w\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma_w(B-w\times E/c^2)_\perp$ along $\widehat w$, with the displayed closed formulas, and $E'=E$, $B'=B$ when $w=0$. Reading the dictionary [F1] in the rest frame with $n=e'_0$ gives $e'_0=b'_0=0$, $e'_i=F'_{i0}=-F'_{0i}=E'_i/c$ and $b'_i=(*F')_{i0}=-(*F')_{0i}=-B'_i$; hence the vectors $E_n=c\,e^\sharp$ and $B_n=-b^\sharp$ have rest-frame components $(0,E')$ and $(0,B')$. Under the adopted model assumption [A1] the observed electric and magnetic fields in the rest frame are $E'$ and $B'$, that is: the components along $w$ are $E_\parallel$ and $B_\parallel$, the components perpendicular to $w$ are $\gamma_w(E+w\times B)_\perp$ and $\gamma_w(B-w\times E/c^2)_\perp$, and at $w=0$ the observer is the laboratory rest observer reading $E,B$ themselves with no distinguished direction of motion. The identification of the mathematical vectors with apparatus readings is exactly [A1] and is assumed, not proved. [given, F1, F2, F3, A1, algebra]

1.4 (Clause (b): the phase covector, nonzero, future and null) By [F4] the wavevector is $\mathbf k=Ks$ with $|\mathbf k|=K=\omega/c$ and propagation direction $\widehat{\mathbf k}=s$, and the phase is $\theta(x,t)=\mathbf k\cdot x-\omega t$. Its coordinate derivative components are $k_0=\partial\theta/\partial x^0=c^{-1}\partial_t\theta=-\omega/c$ and $k_i=\partial\theta/\partial x^i=(\omega/c)s_i$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] with $x^0=ct$), so the phase covector is $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ and $\theta(p)=k_ax^a(p)$ up to an additive constant. Raising with $\eta$ gives $k^0=-k_0=\omega/c>0$ and $k_{\mathrm{vec}}=(k_1,k_2,k_3)=(\omega/c)s$, so $\eta(k^\sharp,k^\sharp)=-(\omega/c)^2+(\omega/c)^2|s|^2=0$ and $k^\sharp\ne0$: the phase covector is nonzero, future ($k^0>0$) and null. By the amplitude equations of [F4] the fields are a source-free smooth Maxwell field on the whole-space region. [given, F1, F4, algebra]

2.1 (Clause (b): exact frequency reading) At the reception event the ideal observer of [F5] with four-velocity $U_o=cn$ reads $\omega_n=-ck(n)=-k(U_o)$. With $k(n)=k_an^a=-\frac{\omega}{c}\gamma_w+\frac{\omega}{c}\frac{w\cdot s}{c}\gamma_w=-\frac{\omega}{c}\gamma_w\bigl(1-\frac{w\cdot s}{c}\bigr)$ from [F2] and step 1.4, this gives $\omega_n=\gamma_w\bigl(1-\frac{w\cdot s}{c}\bigr)\omega>0$, where the positivity is clause (ii) of [F6], whose formula this is with the frame-$x$ data $(\omega,s)$ of [F4] and the observer velocity $w$; its hypotheses hold by step 1.4 and the adopted model postulates [F5], [F6]. At $w=0$ one has $\gamma_w=1$ and $\omega_n=\omega$, and the reader is the laboratory rest observer of clause (a) reading $E,B$. [given, step 1.4, F2, F5, F6, algebra]

2.2 (Clause (b): aberration, longitudinal and transverse protocols) The data $(\omega,s)$ of [F4] are exactly the frame-$x$ data of the Doppler theorem [F6] for its future null wave covector (step 1.4), and the ideal plane-wave, ideal-clock and covariance postulates it adopts are those of the framework [F5], [F8]. Hence its clauses (i)-(v) apply verbatim to this wave: (i) in a chart $x'=B(\beta)x+b$ the frame data $(\omega',s')$ satisfy $\omega'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\omega>0$ with the displayed $s'$ satisfying $|s'|=1$ (the direction transformation, i.e. aberration); (iii) $s=\pm\widehat\beta$ give the longitudinal red- and blue-shift factors $\omega\sqrt{(1\mp|\beta|)/(1\pm|\beta|)}$ with the stated wavelength ratios; (iv) $\beta\cdot s=0$ gives $\omega'=\gamma\omega$ and $\beta\cdot s=|\beta|^2$ gives $\omega'=\omega/\gamma$, the two transverse protocols, and the two factors differ when $\beta\ne0$; (v) the aberration relation $\cos\theta_{x'}=(\cos\theta_x-|\beta|)/(1-|\beta|\cos\theta_x)$ with the map a strictly increasing bijection of $[-1,1]$ onto itself and $\cos\theta_x=0\Rightarrow\cos\theta_{x'}=-|\beta|$. For $\beta=0$ clause (i) gives $\omega'=\omega$ and $s'=s$, so frequency and direction are unchanged and no aberration angle is defined; each formula carries its nonzero-motion qualification. [given, step 1.4, F5, F6, F8]

3.1 (Clause (b): composition of successive inertial changes) Let $x_0\to x_1=\Lambda_1x_0+b_1\to x_2=\Lambda_2x_1+b_2$ be successive inertial changes of description with proper orthochronous $\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2$. The phase $\theta$ of step 1.4 is affine in $x_0$, so the covector law [F7] gives $k_{1,a}=(\Lambda_1^{-1})^b{}_ak_{0,b}$ and $k_{2,a}=(\Lambda_2^{-1})^b{}_ak_{1,b}=((\Lambda_2\Lambda_1)^{-1})^b{}_ak_{0,b}$, the affine constants transforming with the translations; in wave data, clause (i) of [F6] gives $\omega_1=\gamma_1(1-\beta_1\cdot s_0)\omega_0$ with $s_1$ updated to the displayed direction, and $\omega_2=\gamma_2(1-\beta_2\cdot s_1)\omega_1$ with $s_2$ updated from $s_1$, all factors positive by clause (i) of [F6] and the reading formula of step 2.1; hence $\omega_2/\omega_0=(\omega_2/\omega_1)(\omega_1/\omega_0)$: each stage updates the direction as well as the frequency and the positive successive frequency ratios multiply. This composition is a direct covector and reading computation, not a composition clause of the Doppler supplier. [given, step 1.4, step 2.1, F6, F7, algebra]

4.1 (Clause (c): status, scope and hypotheses) Clause (a) is steps 1.1-1.3: the four component formulas, the annihilation $e(n)=b(n)=0$, the raising into $n^\perp$, the reconstruction determining $F$ from $(e,b)$ and the identification of the observed rest-frame fields are established there, the last only under the adopted model assumption [A1].
