## Statement

Assume the framework's spacetime, field and worldline objects of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and clause (i) of the adopted Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]: a constant charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-sources]] (a), an externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline $x:J\to A$ with four-velocity $U$, and a prescribed field $F$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle; the adopted equation of motion is $$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),\qquad \eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u),$$ $U$ the four-velocity of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (b) with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $t\mapsto r(t)$ be the laboratory chart reading of the worldline, $v:=r'$ its coordinate velocity and $\gamma:=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, so that $U=\gamma(c,v)$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)). Then, wherever the worldline is $C^2$: (a) [Coordinate force and power] with the coordinate three-momentum $p:=m\gamma v$ of [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a), $$\frac{dp}{dt}=q\,(E+v\times B),\qquad \frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=q\,E\cdot v,$$ the derivatives taken with respect to the chart time $t$ and $E,B$ the components of $F$ in the laboratory frame. (b) [Norm preservation] $s\mapsto\eta(U(s),U(s))$ is constant on $J$ with value $-c^2$; in particular a solution with future timelike initial data remains future timelike, and $|v(t)|<c$ wherever the reading is differentiable ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]). (c) [Controlled low-speed expansion] for every $\delta\in(0,1)$, on any interval where $|v|/c\le\delta$, $$|\gamma-1|\le\frac{|v|^2/c^2}{2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma-1-\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\Bigl(\frac{|v|^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{2},$$ and consequently $$|p-mv|\le m|v|\,\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma mc^2-mc^2-\tfrac12m|v|^2\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\frac{m|v|^4}{c^2};$$ the constants depend only on $\delta$, so the bounds are uniform in $|v|/c\le\delta$. These are pointwise algebraic expansions; they assert no approximation of the trajectory over a time interval, which would require a separate stability argument. (d) [Scope] The charge is constant, $m>0$ is an externally supplied parameter and $F$ is a prescribed exterior field: the particle's own field, radiation reaction and any self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles and zero or variable mass; the nonrelativistic coordinate law is not adopted as exact, and (c) is a controlled kinematic expansion, not a trajectory approximation. The statement is conditional on the adopted postulates and makes no empirical claim.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The spacetime, field and worldline objects of
[[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]],
[[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] with the SI
units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; a constant charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-sources]] (a); an externally supplied rest mass
$m>0$; a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline $x:J\to A$ with four-velocity
$U$ and four-acceleration $A$; a prescribed field $F$ of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph
of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle; the adopted coupling [F2];
and the laboratory chart reading $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$, $v=r'$,
$\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ of the worldline.

[F1] The worldline reading: $t\mapsto r(t)$ is defined on an open interval of
laboratory times, $|v(t)|<c$, and the four-velocity and four-acceleration are
$U=\gamma(c,v)$ and (when $x$ is $C^2$) $A=dU/d\tau$; $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$
([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (b), (c),
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e),
[[def-em-lab-geometry]] (a), (c)).

[F2] Adopted coupling (clause (i) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]): with
$\Phi$ of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]], defined by
$\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$ and given in components by
$\Phi(u)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha\beta}u^\beta$, the equation of motion is
$m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$, equivalently
$m\,dU^\mu/d\tau=qF^\mu{}_\nu U^\nu$ with
$F^\mu{}_\nu=\eta^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha\nu}$ and $U_\nu=\eta_{\nu\beta}U^\beta$;
$q$ is constant, $m>0$ is externally supplied, and $F$ is a prescribed exterior
field with no self-field.

[F3] Components of the field and of the coupling in the laboratory frame: with
the dictionary $F^{0i}=E_i/c=F^{i0}$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a) and the right-handed cross product of
[[def-cross-product-in-r3]], $F^i{}_0=E_i/c$,
$F^i{}_j=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $\Phi(U)^i=\gamma(E_i+(v\times B)_i)$ and
$\Phi(U)^0=\gamma\,E\cdot v/c$; the spatial inner products and norms are those
of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]].

[F4] Momentum and four-force: $P=mU$ with $P$ of unit
kg m s$^{-1}$, the coordinate three-momentum is $p=m\gamma v$, and the four-force
is $\dot P=mA$ ([[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a), (b) with an inertial
frame whose stationary observer is $e_0$, [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]
(i), (iv)).

[F5] Proper time and the chain rule: the parametrization $t\mapsto\tau(t)$ of
the worldline satisfies $\mathrm d\tau/\mathrm dt=\gamma^{-1}$, so
$\mathrm d/\mathrm dt=\gamma^{-1}\mathrm d/\mathrm d\tau$ on functions of the
chart time, and $U=\gamma(c,v)$ as a chart-time curve has the same differentiability as
$v$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e),
[[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]],
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]).

[F6] Orthogonality and norm conservation
([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]): $\eta(u,\Phi(u))=0$ for every
$u\in V$; if $U$ is differentiable on an interval with
$mU'(s)=q\Phi(U(s))$ for constant $m\ne0$ and $q$, then
$s\mapsto\eta(U(s),U(s))$ is constant; the conclusion holds verbatim for a
family of skew forms $F_s$ and their operators $\Phi_s$ with
$mU'(s)=q\Phi_s(U(s))$, with no derivative of $F_s$ required. Also,
differentiability at a point implies continuity there
([[cor-differentiable-implies-continuous]]), and a continuous real function on
an interval that never vanishes has constant sign ([[thm-intermediate-value]]).

[F7] Powers: for $a>0$ and real $\alpha$ the map $x\mapsto x^\alpha$ is
continuous and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ with
$(x^\alpha)'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}$
([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]); the rational power of
[[def-rational-power]] satisfies $a^{r+s}=a^ra^s$ and $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$ for
rationals $r,s$, agrees with the real power at rational exponents
([[lem-rational-power-laws]], [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]]),
and is strictly increasing in the base for positive exponent
([[lem-rational-power-monotone]], [[lem-of-inverse-positive]]).

[F8] Mean value tools: if $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and
differentiable on $(a,b)$ there is $c\in(a,b)$ with
$f(b)-f(a)=f'(c)(b-a)$ ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]); if $f,g$ are continuous on
$[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$ there is $c\in(a,b)$ with
$(f(b)-f(a))g'(c)=(g(b)-g(a))f'(c)$ ([[thm-cauchy-mean-value]]). The absolute
value satisfies $|xy|=|x||y|$ and $|x|\ge0$
([[def-abs-value]], [[lem-of-abs-value]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** contract the field with the four-velocity in the fixed component dictionary, then apply the mean value and Cauchy mean value theorems to $(1-z)^{-1/2}$ and $z^2$ on the compact speed interval.

1.1 (Clause (a): the coordinate force) By [F1] and [F5], $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $U^i=\gamma v_i$ and $\mathrm d/\mathrm d\tau=\gamma\,\mathrm d/\mathrm dt$ (chain rule for the inverse parametrization $t\mapsto\tau(t)$), and $p=m\gamma v$ by [F4]. For a spatial index $i$, the spatial component of the equation of motion [F2] reads $m\,dU^i/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)^i=q\gamma\bigl(E_i+(v\times B)_i\bigr)$ by [F3]. Since $U^i=\gamma v_i$ and $p_i=m\gamma v_i$, the left side is $m\,dU^i/d\tau=m\gamma\,\frac{d}{dt}(\gamma v_i)=\gamma\,\frac{dp_i}{dt}$, so $\gamma\,dp_i/dt=q\gamma(E_i+(v\times B)_i)$ and, dividing by $\gamma>0$, $dp_i/dt=q(E_i+(v\times B)_i)$ for $i=1,2,3$; componentwise this is $dp/dt=q(E+v\times B)$. The derivatives are those of the chart time, and $E,B$ are the laboratory components of $F$. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

1.2 (Clause (a): the power identity) For the temporal index, [F2] and [F3] give $m\,dU^0/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)^0=q\gamma E\cdot v/c$. By [F1] and [F5], $U^0=\gamma c$ and $dU^0/d\tau=\gamma c\,\mathrm d\gamma/\mathrm dt$, so $m\,dU^0/d\tau=\frac{\gamma}{c}\,mc^2\frac{\mathrm d\gamma}{\mathrm dt}=\frac{\gamma}{c}\frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}$; comparing with the right-hand side, $\frac{\gamma}{c}\frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=\frac{q\gamma E\cdot v}{c}$, and multiplying by $c/\gamma>0$ gives $d(\gamma mc^2)/dt=q\,E\cdot v$. [given, F1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

1.3 (Clause (b): norm preservation and the future branch) Since $m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$ with constant $m\ne0$ and $q$ and $F$ possibly varying along the trajectory, the norm-conservation clause of [F6] applies (it needs no derivative of $F$) and gives that $s\mapsto\eta(U(s),U(s))$ is constant on $J$; being the four-velocity of the massive worldline, $U$ has norm $-c^2$ at every point by [F1]. Thus $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ everywhere, and the component identity $(U^0)^2=c^2+|U_{\mathrm{vec}}|^2\ge c^2>0$ shows that $U^0$ never vanishes; $U^0$ is continuous because $U$ is differentiable [F6], so on every interval of $J$ it has constant sign by [F6]. If the initial data are future timelike, $U^0(0)>0$, so $U^0>0$ throughout, the solution remains in the future timelike branch, and $|v|^2/c^2=1-\gamma^{-2}<1$, that is $|v(t)|<c$, wherever the chart reading is differentiable. No existence or continuation of solutions is asserted. [given, F1, F2, F6, algebra]

1.4 (Clause (c): the function and its derivatives) Put $z(t):=|v(t)|^2/c^2$, so that $0\le z\le\delta^2$ on an interval where $|v|/c\le\delta$, $\delta\in(0,1)$, and $\gamma=f(z)$ with $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}$. The function $f$ is continuous on $[0,\delta^2]$ and differentiable on $(0,\delta^2)$: it is the composition of $z\mapsto1-z$ with $y\mapsto y^{-1/2}$, the latter continuous and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ with derivative $-\tfrac12y^{-3/2}$ [F7], and $\gamma=f(z)$ agrees with the rational power of [F1] by [F7]. By the chain rule [F5], $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$ and $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$ on $(0,\delta^2)$. If $z=0$ then $\gamma=1$ and every difference and bound in clause (c) vanishes exactly; hence assume $0<z\le\delta^2$ below, and note $1-\delta^2>0$. [given, F1, F5, F7, algebra]

2.1 (Clause (c): first-order bound) Since $f$ is continuous on $[0,z]$ and differentiable on $(0,z)$, [F8] gives $\xi\in(0,z)$ with $f(z)-f(0)=f'(\xi)z$, and $f(0)=1$; hence $|\gamma-1|=|f'(\xi)|\,z=\tfrac12(1-\xi)^{-3/2}z$. Since $0<\xi\le z\le\delta^2<1$, the base satisfies $1-\xi\ge1-\delta^2>0$, so $0<(1-\xi)^{-3/2}\le(1-\delta^2)^{-3/2}$ by monotonicity of the positive power and positivity of inverses [F7]; therefore $|\gamma-1|\le\frac{z}{2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}}=\frac{|v|^2/c^2}{2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}}$. [given, step 1.4, F7, F8, algebra]

2.2 (Clause (c): second-order bound) Define $q(s):=f(s)-1-\tfrac{s}{2}$ and $g(s):=s^2$ on $[0,z]$; both are continuous on $[0,z]$ and differentiable on $(0,z)$, with $q'(s)=f'(s)-\tfrac12$ and $g'(s)=2s>0$ there [F7, F8]. Cauchy's mean value theorem [F8] gives $\xi\in(0,z)$ with $\bigl(q(z)-q(0)\bigr)g'(\xi)=\bigl(g(z)-g(0)\bigr)q'(\xi)$; since $q(0)=0=g(0)$, $g'(\xi)=2\xi\ne0$ and $q'(\xi)=f'(\xi)-\tfrac12$, this reads $f(z)-1-\tfrac z2=\frac{z^2}{2\xi}\bigl(f'(\xi)-\tfrac12\bigr)$. The mean value theorem [F8] applied to $f'$ on $[0,\xi]$, where $f'$ is continuous on $[0,\xi]$ and differentiable on $(0,\xi)$ (the derivative $f''$ is given on $(0,\delta^2)$ in step 1.4), gives $\eta\in(0,\xi)$ with $f'(\xi)-f'(0)=\xi f''(\eta)$; since $f'(0)=\tfrac12$ this gives $f'(\xi)-\tfrac12=\xi f''(\eta)$, and substitution yields $f(z)-1-\tfrac z2=\frac{z^2}{2\xi}\cdot\xi f''(\eta)=\tfrac12f''(\eta)z^2=\tfrac38(1-\eta)^{-5/2}z^2$. Since $0<\eta\le\xi\le z\le\delta^2$, monotonicity of the positive power [F7] gives $(1-\eta)^{-5/2}\le(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}$, hence $\bigl|\gamma-1-\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2}\bigr|=\bigl|f(z)-1-\tfrac z2\bigr|\le\frac38(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}z^2=\frac38(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\bigl(\frac{|v|^2}{c^2}\bigr)^2$. [given, step 1.4, F7, F8, algebra]

3.1 (Clause (c): the momentum and energy bounds) Multiplying the first-order bound of step 2.1 by $m|v|\ge0$ and using $|xy|=|x||y|$ [F8] gives $|p-mv|=|m\gamma v-mv|=m|v|\,|\gamma-1|\le m|v|\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}}$. Multiplying the second-order bound of step 2.2 by $mc^2>0$ gives $\bigl|\gamma mc^2-mc^2-\tfrac12m|v|^2\bigr|=mc^2\bigl|\gamma-1-\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2}\bigr|\le\frac38(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\frac{m|v|^4}{c^2}$. The constants depend only on $\delta$, so both bounds are uniform on any interval where $|v|/c\le\delta$. These are pointwise algebraic bounds; no approximation of the trajectory over a time interval is asserted. [given, step 2.1, step 2.2, F7, F8, algebra]

4.1 (Clauses (c) and (d): status and scope) Clauses (a) and (b) are steps 1.1-1.3, and clause (c) is steps 1.4, 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1: the two first-order and second-order bounds, the resulting momentum and energy bounds and their uniformity in $|v|/c\le\delta$ are established there, including the exact vanishing at $z=0$. The charge $q$ is a constant parameter of [[def-em-sources]] (a), $m>0$ is an externally supplied rest mass, and $F$ is a prescribed exterior field $C^1$ near the graph: the particle's own field, radiation reaction and any self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles and zero or variable mass [F2]. The nonrelativistic coordinate law is not adopted as exact; clause (c) is a controlled kinematic expansion and asserts no trajectory approximation over time, which would require a separate stability argument. The argument used the metric contraction [F3], the coupling [F2], the momentum and four-force identification [F4], the proper-time chain rule [F5], the orthogonality and norm-conservation lemma [F6] (whose varying-field clause was used so that no derivative of $F$ enters), and the power and mean value tools [F7], [F8]; it is conditional on the adopted postulates, makes no empirical claim and uses no choice principle. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, F2, F5, F6] ∎

## Source notes

The three cited treatments state the covariant force law
$m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$ (equivalently $dP^\mu/d\tau=qF^{\mu\nu}U_\nu$), its
unpacking into the coordinate Lorentz force and the power identity, and the
constancy of the four-velocity norm, each in its own conventions. The deduction
above performs the contraction in the framework's fixed dictionary
($F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $x^0=ct$), uses the framework's
repaired raised-index operator $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$, and derives the
low-speed bounds from the mean value and Cauchy mean value theorems with the
exact constants $1/2$ and $3/8$; the conversion from the sources' conventions
is carried out here rather than assumed.

## Statement

Assume the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]: $E,B$ jointly $C^1$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] with the additional derivatives required by each Maxwell equation existing and continuous, continuous sources $(\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] and the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components, $j=(c\rho,J)$ the four-current, $u$ and $S$ the energy density and Poynting vector of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], and $g$, $\sigma$, $\Pi=-\sigma$ the momentum density, Maxwell stress and momentum flux of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. Define the stress-energy tensor of the field by $$T^{\mu\nu}:=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\Bigl(F^{\mu\alpha}F^\nu{}_\alpha-\frac14\eta^{\mu\nu}F^{\alpha\beta}F_{\alpha\beta}\Bigr).$$ Then: (a) [Object] $T$ is a symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] with $\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}$ continuous on $U$, it is traceless, $\eta_{\mu\nu}T^{\mu\nu}=0$, and under a proper orthochronous change of inertial chart with transition $x'=\Lambda x+b$ its components transform as $T'^{\mu\nu}=\Lambda^\mu{}_\alpha\Lambda^\nu{}_\beta T^{\alpha\beta}$ ([[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]], [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii)). (b) [Components] in the laboratory frame $$T^{00}=u=\frac{\varepsilon_0|E|^2}{2}+\frac{|B|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{0i}=T^{i0}=\frac{S_i}{c}=c\,g_i=\frac{(E\times B)_i}{\mu_0c},\qquad T^{ij}=-\sigma_{ij},$$ where $\sigma_{ij}=\varepsilon_0\bigl(E_iE_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}|E|^2\bigr)+\mu_0^{-1}\bigl(B_iB_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}|B|^2\bigr)$; in particular the spatial block is minus the Maxwell stress of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. (c) [Balance] under the smooth branch, $$\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}=-f^\nu,\qquad f^\nu:=F^{\nu\lambda}j_\lambda,$$ where algebraically $f=(J\cdot E/c,\rho E+J\times B)$. Its interpretation as the electromagnetic four-force density delivered to matter uses the separately adopted continuum coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] (ii) for matter models and sources satisfying that postulate's hypotheses. The component identities are $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E$ and $\partial_tg-\operatorname{div}\sigma=-(\rho E+J\times B)$ of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] (a) and [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]] (a). (d) [Matter coupling and finite-flux conservation] let $T_{\mathrm m}$ be a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field on $U$ satisfying $\partial_\mu T_{\mathrm m}{}^{\mu\nu}=f^\nu$ (an adopted matter model, not derived here); then $\partial_\mu(T+T_{\mathrm m})^{\mu\nu}=0$, on every finite axis-parallel box with an open neighbourhood contained in $U$, the box and slice balance identities of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] hold for the total tensor with zero divergence, retaining all side-flux terms. Constancy of a slice total requires that theorem's vanishing side-flux hypothesis; zero divergence alone does not supply it, and the angular current $M^{\lambda\mu\nu}:=x^\mu T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda\nu}-x^\nu T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda\mu}$ satisfies $\partial_\lambda M^{\lambda\mu\nu}=0$ by symmetry. (e) [Scope] the divergence is a product identity of $C^1$ objects and is not asserted for the weak branch, at singular source support or for any product of distributions; symmetry, zero trace and the component display are algebraic; no matter tensor is derived from vacuum Maxwell, no radiation reaction or self-force is included, and no empirical claim is made.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory
region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]: the jointly $C^1$
fields $E,B$ of [[def-em-fields]] with the additional derivatives required by
each Maxwell equation existing and continuous, the continuous sources
$(\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]], and the constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]]; the electromagnetic two-form $F$ with the components
and conventions of [F2]; the four-current $j=(c\rho,J)$; the objects $u,S$ of
[[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] and $g,\sigma,\Pi=-\sigma$ of
[[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]; the tensor $T$ of the statement's definition;
and, in clause (d), the adopted matter tensor $T_{\mathrm m}$ of [F7].

[F1] The four smooth-branch equations hold pointwise on $\Omega\times I$; by
[[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] (a) the two tensor systems
$(\mathrm{TM1})$ $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ and $(\mathrm{TM2})$
$\partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu}=0$
hold there, and every first partial derivative of a component of $F$ appearing
in $(\mathrm{TM1})$ or $(\mathrm{TM2})$ exists and is continuous
([[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] (a), [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]],
[[def-em-sources]] (c); $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$).

[F2] In the laboratory chart with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ the
components satisfy $F^{00}=0$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$,
$F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, so $F^i{}_0=F^{i0}\eta_{00}=E_i/c$
and $F^i{}_j=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$; the contraction is
$F^{\alpha\beta}F_{\alpha\beta}=2\bigl(|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2\bigr)$, and the elementary
identities $\epsilon_{ijk}\epsilon_{ijk'}=2\delta_{kk'}$ and
$\epsilon_{ikm}\epsilon_{jkn}=\delta_{ij}\delta_{mn}-\delta_{in}\delta_{mj}$
hold, with $|\cdot|$ and $\cdot$ the Euclidean structure
([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a), (b),
[[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

[F3] The definitions: $u=\tfrac{\varepsilon_0}{2}|E|^2+\tfrac{1}{2\mu_0}|B|^2$,
$S=\mu_0^{-1}E\times B$; $g=S/c^2=\varepsilon_0E\times B$;
$\sigma_{ij}=\varepsilon_0(E_iE_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}|E|^2)+\mu_0^{-1}(B_iB_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}|B|^2)$;
$\Pi=-\sigma$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] (a),
[[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]] (a), (b), (c)).

[F4] For a proper orthochronous change of chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$ the components
of the same $F$ satisfy $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$ and
$F'_{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a(\Lambda^{-1})^d{}_bF_{cd}$, every contraction of
one contravariant with one covariant index is invariant, and
$\eta'_{ab}=\eta_{ab}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii),
[[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (c)).

[F5] Regularity criterion: a map assigning to each point a type-$(r,s)$ tensor
is a $\mathcal C^k$ tensor field exactly when all its components in one, or
equivalently every, inertial chart are $\mathcal C^k$ functions of the chart
coordinates, and regularity of components is preserved under the linear
component changes of a chart transition
([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

[F6] The coordinate partial derivatives are those of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and sums and products of
differentiable functions obey the product rule; a finite sum of products of
continuous functions is continuous ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]).

[F7] Balance and interpretation suppliers:
[[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] (a) gives
$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E$ and
[[pthm-em-momentum-balance]] (a) gives
$\partial_tg-\operatorname{div}\sigma=-(\rho E+J\times B)$ componentwise, with
$\operatorname{div}$ at fixed time and $f:=\rho E+J\times B$ the force density;
clause (ii) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] identifies $J\cdot E$ and
$\rho E+J\times B$ as the electromagnetic power and force densities delivered
to a matter model satisfying that clause, and its clause (iii) records the
scope. In clause (d), $T_{\mathrm m}$ is a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field on
$U$ with $\partial_\mu T_{\mathrm m}{}^{\mu\nu}=f^\nu$.

[F8] Finite-flux theorem [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]: for a
$C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field on an open neighbourhood of a closed
axis-parallel box $B=\prod_{a=0}^3[c_a,d_a]$, with $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$, the
box identity and the slice-balance identity hold, the latter stating that
$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)$ equals the integral of $f^b$ over the slab minus the three
side-flux differences; and if $f=0$ on the slab and the side components
$T^{ib}$ vanish on the side faces, then $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$. All face integrals
are Riemann integrals over the remaining coordinates.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct algebra from the component dictionary for the tensor, symmetry and trace; the product rule and the cyclic identity for the divergence; the finite-box theorem for the conservation identities.

1.1 (Clause (a): symmetry, trace and regularity) Since $F^b{}_a=\eta_{ac}F^{bc}$, the first term satisfies $F^{\mu\alpha}F^\nu{}_\alpha=F^{\mu\alpha}\eta_{\alpha\beta}F^{\nu\beta}$, and swapping the two factors and relabelling the dummy indices while using symmetry of $\eta$ gives $F^{\mu\alpha}\eta_{\alpha\beta}F^{\nu\beta}=F^{\nu\beta}\eta_{\beta\alpha}F^{\mu\alpha}$; the second term $\eta^{\mu\nu}$ is symmetric, so $T^{\mu\nu}=T^{\nu\mu}$. For the trace, $\eta_{\mu\nu}T^{\mu\nu}=\mu_0^{-1}\bigl(F^{\mu\alpha}F_{\mu\alpha}-\tfrac14\eta_{\mu\nu}\eta^{\mu\nu}F^{\alpha\beta}F_{\alpha\beta}\bigr)$ and $F^{\mu\alpha}F_{\mu\alpha}=F^{\alpha\beta}F_{\alpha\beta}=F^{2}$, $\eta_{\mu\nu}\eta^{\mu\nu}=4$; hence $\eta_{\mu\nu}T^{\mu\nu}=\mu_0^{-1}(F^2-F^2)=0$. Each component $T^{\mu\nu}$ is a finite sum of products of components of $F$ (a $C^1$ tensor field), so $T$ is a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field by [F5]; by the product rule [F6], $\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}=\mu_0^{-1}\bigl[(\partial_\mu F^{\mu\alpha})F^\nu{}_\alpha+F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F^\nu{}_\alpha-\tfrac12F^{\alpha\beta}\partial^\nu F_{\alpha\beta}\bigr]$, in which the first factor is continuous by $(\mathrm{TM1})$ and the remaining derivative factors exist and are continuous by the smooth-branch hypotheses of [F1]; hence $\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}$ is continuous on $U$. [given, F1, F2, F5, F6, algebra]

1.2 (Clause (a): the transformation law) Let $x'=\Lambda x+b$ be a proper orthochronous change of inertial chart. By [F4], $F'^{\mu\alpha}F'^\nu{}_\alpha=\Lambda^\mu{}_e\Lambda^\alpha{}_fF^{ef}\,\eta_{\alpha\beta}\Lambda^\nu{}_c\Lambda^\beta{}_dF^{cd}=\Lambda^\mu{}_e\Lambda^\nu{}_cF^{ef}F^c{}_f$, because $\eta_{\alpha\beta}\Lambda^\alpha{}_f\Lambda^\beta{}_d=\eta_{fd}$ and $F^{ef}\eta_{fd}=F^e{}_d$; similarly $F'{}^{2}=F'_{ab}F'^{ab}=F_{ab}F^{ab}=F^{2}$ by the two component laws and the inverse-matrix identity, and $\eta'=\eta$. Substituting in the definition gives $T'^{\mu\nu}=\mu_0^{-1}\bigl(\Lambda^\mu{}_e\Lambda^\nu{}_cF^{ef}F^c{}_f-\tfrac14\eta^{\mu\nu}F^{2}\bigr)=\Lambda^\mu{}_e\Lambda^\nu{}_cT^{ec}$, the stated type-$(2,0)$ transformation law. [given, F4, algebra]

1.3 (Clause (b): the components) Substituting [F2] into the definition: $T^{00}=\mu_0^{-1}\bigl(F^{0i}F^0{}_i-\tfrac14\eta^{00}F^{2}\bigr)=\mu_0^{-1}\bigl(|E|^2/c^2+\tfrac14\cdot2(|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2)\bigr)=\mu_0^{-1}\bigl(\tfrac12|E|^2/c^2+\tfrac12|B|^2\bigr)=\varepsilon_0|E|^2/2+|B|^2/(2\mu_0)=u$, using $\eta^{00}=-1$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and [F3]. Next $T^{0i}=\mu_0^{-1}F^{0j}F^i{}_j=\mu_0^{-1}(E_j/c)\epsilon_{ijk}B_k=(E\times B)_i/(\mu_0c)=S_i/c=c\,g_i$, because $\eta^{0i}=0$ and [F3]. Finally $T^{ij}=\mu_0^{-1}\bigl(F^{i0}F^j{}_0+F^{ik}F^j{}_k-\tfrac14\delta_{ij}F^{2}\bigr)$; here $F^{i0}F^j{}_0=(-E_i/c)(E_j/c)=-E_iE_j/c^2$ and $F^{ik}F^j{}_k=\epsilon_{ikm}\epsilon_{jkn}B_mB_n=\delta_{ij}|B|^2-B_iB_j$ by [F2], so with $F^{2}=2(|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2)$, $T^{ij}=\mu_0^{-1}\bigl(-E_iE_j/c^2+\delta_{ij}|B|^2-B_iB_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}(|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2)\bigr)=-\varepsilon_0\bigl(E_iE_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}|E|^2\bigr)-\mu_0^{-1}\bigl(B_iB_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}|B|^2\bigr)=-\sigma_{ij}$, again by $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. This is the displayed component identification, and the spatial block is minus the Maxwell stress of [F3]. [given, F2, F3, algebra]

1.4 (Clause (c): the divergence identity) By the product rule [F6], $\mu_0\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}=(\partial_\mu F^{\mu\alpha})F^\nu{}_\alpha+F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F^\nu{}_\alpha-\tfrac12F^{\alpha\beta}\partial^\nu F_{\alpha\beta}$, the last term from $\partial_\mu(\eta^{\mu\nu}F^{2})=\partial^\nu(F^{2})=2F^{\alpha\beta}\partial^\nu F_{\alpha\beta}$ and the factor $-\tfrac14$. The first term is $-\mu_0j^\alpha F^\nu{}_\alpha=-\mu_0F^{\nu\lambda}j_\lambda$ by $(\mathrm{TM1})$ of [F1] and $j_\lambda=\eta_{\lambda\alpha}j^\alpha$. For the cancellation, contract $(\mathrm{TM2})$ in the form $\partial_\mu F_{\nu\alpha}+\partial_\nu F_{\alpha\mu}+\partial_\alpha F_{\mu\nu}=0$ with $F^{\mu\alpha}$ and fix the free index $\nu$: the first term is $C_\nu:=F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F_{\nu\alpha}$, the third is $F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\alpha F_{\mu\nu}=F^{\alpha\mu}\partial_\mu F_{\alpha\nu}$ after relabelling $\alpha\leftrightarrow\mu$, which equals $C_\nu$ because $F^{\alpha\mu}=-F^{\mu\alpha}$ and $F_{\alpha\nu}=-F_{\nu\alpha}$, and the middle term is $\tfrac12\partial_\nu(F^{2})$, since $F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\nu F_{\alpha\mu}=\tfrac12\partial_\nu(F^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha\mu})=\tfrac12\partial_\nu(F^{2})$ (the two terms of the derivative of the product are equal after relabelling). Hence $2C_\nu+\tfrac12\partial_\nu(F^{2})=0$, that is $C_\nu=-\tfrac14\partial_\nu(F^{2})$. Raising the free index, $F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F^\nu{}_\alpha=\eta^{\nu\rho}C_\rho=-\tfrac14\partial^\nu(F^{2})=\tfrac12F^{\alpha\beta}\partial^\nu F_{\alpha\beta}$, so the second and third terms of the product-rule expression cancel. Therefore $\mu_0\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0F^{\nu\lambda}j_\lambda$, and dividing by $\mu_0$ gives $\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}=-f^\nu$ with $f^\nu=F^{\nu\lambda}j_\lambda$. Algebraically $f^0=F^{0i}j_i=(E_i/c)J_i=J\cdot E/c$ and $f^i=F^{i0}j_0+F^{ij}j_j=(-E_i/c)(-c\rho)+\epsilon_{ijk}B_kJ_j=\rho E_i+(J\times B)_i$, so $f=(J\cdot E/c,\rho E+J\times B)$; its reading as the electromagnetic four-force density delivered to matter uses the separately adopted clause (ii) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] [F7]. [given, F1, F2, F6, F7, algebra]

2.1 (Clause (c): component identities and comparison) Reading the balance of step 1.4 with $\nu=0$ and using $T^{00}=u$, $T^{i0}=S_i/c$ from step 1.3 and $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ gives $\partial_\mu T^{\mu0}=c^{-1}\partial_tu+c^{-1}\operatorname{div}S=c^{-1}(\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S)$, while $-f^0=-J\cdot E/c$; multiplying by $c$ gives $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E$, which is clause (a) of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] [F7]. Reading it with $\nu=i$ and using $T^{0i}=c\,g_i$, $T^{ji}=-\sigma_{ij}$ gives $\partial_\mu T^{\mu i}=\partial_tg_i-(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i$ and $-f^i=-(\rho E_i+(J\times B)_i)$, that is $\partial_tg-\operatorname{div}\sigma=-(\rho E+J\times B)$, which is clause (a) of [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]] [F7]; by clause (ii) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] those source terms are the power and force densities delivered to the matter model, so the balance reads as the field-matter balance in that interpretation. [given, step 1.3, step 1.4, F7, algebra]

2.2 (Clause (d): matter coupling, total conservation, finite flux and angular current) Let $T_{\mathrm m}$ be the adopted $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field of [F7] with $\partial_\mu T_{\mathrm m}{}^{\mu\nu}=f^\nu$. Adding it to step 1.4 gives $\partial_\mu(T+T_{\mathrm m})^{\mu\nu}=0$ pointwise on $U$, and the total tensor is $C^1$ and symmetric. On every closed axis-parallel box $B=\prod_{a=0}^{3}[c_a,d_a]$ with an open neighbourhood contained in $U$, the box and slice identities of [F8] apply to the total tensor because its divergence vanishes on the box: the box identity has zero left-hand side, and the slice balance expresses $Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)$ as minus the three side-flux differences, all side terms retained; the constancy $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$ requires the vanishing side-flux hypothesis of [F8] and is not implied by zero divergence alone. For the angular current $M^{\lambda\mu\nu}=x^\mu T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda\nu}-x^\nu T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda\mu}$, the product rule and the coordinate identities $\partial_\lambda x^\mu=\delta^\mu_\lambda$ and $\partial_\lambda x^\nu=\delta^\nu_\lambda$ [F6] give $\partial_\lambda M^{\lambda\mu\nu}=\delta^\mu_\lambda T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda\nu}+x^\mu\partial_\lambda T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda\nu}-\delta^\nu_\lambda T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda\mu}-x^\nu\partial_\lambda T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda\mu}=T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\mu\nu}-T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\nu\mu}=0$, the last equality by the symmetry of the total tensor established in step 1.1 and the vanishing divergence. [given, step 1.1, step 1.4, F5, F6, F7, F8, algebra]

3.1 (Clause (e): status and scope) Clauses (a), (b), (c) and (d) are steps 1.1-1.4 and 2.1-2.2: the symmetry, trace and transformation law; the component identification with $u$, $S$, $g$ and $-\sigma$; the divergence identity with the algebraically evaluated four-force density; and the conditional total conservation, finite-box and angular conclusions with the adopted matter tensor. The argument used the smooth-branch hypotheses and the two tensor systems [F1], the dictionary and contractions [F2], the definitions of the energy flux and stress objects [F3], the component transformation law [F4], the tensor-field regularity criterion [F5], the product rule [F6], the independently proved local identities and the adopted continuum coupling [F7], and the finite-box theorem [F8]. The divergence is a product identity of $C^1$ objects: it is not asserted for the weak branch, at singular source support or for any product of distributions; symmetry, zero trace and the component display are algebraic; no matter tensor is derived from vacuum Maxwell, no radiation reaction or self-force is included, and no empirical claim is made. No choice principle is used. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1, step 2.2, F1, F5, F7, F8] ∎

## Source notes

The three cited treatments construct the quadratic stress-energy tensor from
the field tensor, verify its symmetry and tracelessness, compute its components
against the energy density, Poynting flux, momentum density and Maxwell stress,
and derive the divergence identity against the four-force density and the
angular-momentum continuity requiring a symmetric stress tensor, each in its
own conventions. The deduction above performs the component algebra and the
cyclic-identity cancellation in the framework's fixed dictionary
($F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $x^0=ct$,
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$) and compares the result with the
framework's independently proved local balance identities; the conversion from
the sources' conventions is carried out here rather than assumed, and the
four-force-density interpretation is the separately adopted continuum coupling
of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] (ii).

## Example

Let $E_0>0$ carry the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and consider the constant
fields of [[def-em-fields]]

$$E:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3,\quad E\equiv E_0e_2,\qquad B\equiv0,$$

which form a source-free smooth solution of the vacuum Maxwell equations
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] (all first derivatives vanish and
$\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}B=0$,
$\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}B=0$). Let $0\le\beta<1$,
$\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let
$x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the boosted inertial chart of
[[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]]. Then the components of the same field in
$x'$ are

$$E'=\gamma E_0\,e_2,\qquad B'=-\frac{\gamma\beta E_0}{c}\,e_3=-\frac{\gamma |v|E_0}{c^2}\,e_3,$$

so the moving observer reads an electric field of magnitude $\gamma E_0$ along
$e_2$ and, for $\beta>0$, a nonzero magnetic field along $-e_3$: a purely
electric uniform field acquires a magnetic component in the boosted
description. The two invariants check directly: with the spatial Euclidean
structure of the chart ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]],
[[def-cross-product-in-r3]])

$$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=\gamma^2\Bigl(\frac{\beta^2E_0^2}{c^2}-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}\Bigr)=-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=0=E\cdot B,$$

using $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[lem-rational-power-laws]]). At $\beta=0$ the formulas reduce to $E'=E$,
$B'=0$. The computation is exact for the constant field; the example reports no
measurement, identifies no source producing the field, and asserts nothing
about finite-energy or bounded configurations.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The constant $E_0>0$ in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, the fields
$E\equiv E_0e_2$ and $B\equiv0$ on the whole-space laboratory region
$\Omega\times I=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, the boost parameter
$0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, $v=\beta c\,e_1$, and the boosted
inertial chart $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$.

[F1] The fields are those of [[def-em-fields]]: $E$ carries
$\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $B$ the tesla, jointly $C^k$ means $C^k$ in the
chart variables, and the spatial structure is the $\delta$-orthonormal basis
$(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with Euclidean inner product and right-handed cross product
([[def-em-fields]] (c), [[def-em-si-conventions]] (b),
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]).

[F2] Smooth branch: for jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives
required by each equation existing and continuous and continuous sources, the
smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] consists of
$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$,
$\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and
$\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$; for $\rho=0$ and $J=0$ these
are the source-free equations. The divergence and curl are those of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], with partial derivatives at
fixed time.

[F3] Boost components and invariants
([[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a), (b), (c)): for $0\le\beta<1$ and the
chart $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ of the statement, the dictionary components of the
same $F$ satisfy
$E'_2=\gamma(E_2-\beta cB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+\beta cB_2)$,
$B'_2=\gamma(B_2+\beta E_3/c)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$, with the
components along $e_1$ unchanged, and
$|B'|^2-|E'|^2/c^2=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$, $E'\cdot B'=E\cdot B$; at $\beta=0$ the
boost is the identity so $E'=E$, $B'=B$.

[F4] Powers: for $a>0$ and rationals $r,s$ one has $a^r>0$, $a^{r+s}=a^ra^s$;
with $a:=1-\beta^2>0$ this gives $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$
([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]).

[F5] Orthonormality: $|e_2|=|e_3|=1$, $e_1,e_2,e_3$ are pairwise orthogonal,
and $e_2\cdot e_3=0$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]] (b)).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; substitute the constant data into the sourced
smooth branch to verify the source-free solution, apply the axis-boost
components of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a), and evaluate the two
invariants with the orthonormal-basis identities.

1.1 Source-free solution: the field pair $(E,B)$ is constant, hence $C^\infty$ with every first partial derivative continuous and equal to $0$, in particular jointly $C^k$ for every $k\ge1$ [F1]. With the divergence and curl of [F2], $\operatorname{div}E=\partial_1E_1+\partial_2E_2+\partial_3E_3=0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=(\partial_2E_3-\partial_3E_2,\ \partial_3E_1-\partial_1E_3,\ \partial_1E_2-\partial_2E_1)=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$, and $\partial_tE=\partial_tB=0$; hence the four source-free smooth-branch equations of [F2] with $\rho=0$, $J=0$ hold on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Boosted components: substitute $E_1=0$, $E_2=E_0$, $E_3=0$ and $B_1=B_2=B_3=0$ in the formulas of [F3]: $E'_1=E_1=0$, $E'_2=\gamma(E_0-\beta c\cdot0)=\gamma E_0$, $E'_3=\gamma(0+\beta c\cdot0)=0$, $B'_1=B_1=0$, $B'_2=\gamma(0+\beta\cdot0/c)=0$ and $B'_3=\gamma(0-\beta E_0/c)=-\gamma\beta E_0/c$; therefore $E'=\gamma E_0e_2$ and $B'=-(\gamma\beta E_0/c)e_3=-(\gamma|v|E_0/c^2)e_3$, since $|v|=\beta c$ by $v=\beta ce_1$ and the right-handed basis [F1]. This is the asserted pair of components; the magnetic component is nonzero exactly when $\beta>0$, and the direction is $-e_3$. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 Invariants: by [F3] the invariants agree with those computed from $(E,B)$, and directly from step 1.2, $|E'|^2=\gamma^2E_0^2$, $|B'|^2=\gamma^2\beta^2E_0^2/c^2$ and $E'\cdot B'=0$ by [F5] ($e_2\perp e_3$), while $|E|^2=E_0^2$, $|B|^2=0$ and $E\cdot B=0$; hence $|B'|^2-|E'|^2/c^2=\gamma^2E_0^2(\beta^2-1)/c^2=-E_0^2/c^2$ by $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ [F4], which equals $|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$, and $E'\cdot B'=0=E\cdot B$. At $\beta=0$ one has $\gamma=1$ and the formulas of [F3] give $E'=E$, $B'=B=0$, so the boosted description is the laboratory description and no magnetic field appears. [given, step 1.2, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

3.1 Closing: step 1.1 verifies that the constant data solve the source-free smooth branch; step 1.2 gives the exact boosted components and step 2.1 the two invariant checks, with the $\beta=0$ reduction. The computation is exact algebra for the constant field and uses only the dictionary and boost formulas of [F3]; no measurement, source model, finite-energy, boundary or empirical claim is made, and no choice principle is used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, F1, F3] ∎

## Example

Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter, $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass and $E_0>0$ a field strength in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and consider the prescribed exterior field of [[def-em-fields]] $$E\equiv E_0e_1,\qquad B\equiv0,$$ a source-free constant solution of the smooth vacuum Maxwell branch. Put $h:=qE_0/(mc)$, carrying the unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$, and for $r_0\in\mathbb R^3$ define the chart reading $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ by $$r(t):=r_0+\frac{c}{h}\bigl(\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}-1\bigr)e_1\quad(h\ne0),\qquad r(t):=r_0\quad(h=0),$$ $$v(t):=r'(t)=\frac{c\,ht}{\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}}\,e_1\ (h\ne0),\qquad \gamma(t):=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2},\qquad p(t):=m\gamma(t)v(t).$$ Then: (i) [Exact solution] for $h\ne0$ the curve is a future timelike $C^\infty$ curve with coordinate velocity $v(t)$, $|v(t)|<c$ for every finite $t$ and $|v(t)|\to c$ as $t\to\pm\infty$, and $p(t)=qE_0t\,e_1$, so that $$\frac{dp}{dt}=qE_0e_1=q(E+v\times B),\qquad \frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=qE\cdot v$$ hold identically, as required by [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (a); at $h=0$ (equivalently $q=0$) the curve is the constant $r\equiv r_0$ with $v\equiv0$, $p\equiv0$ and the same equations hold trivially. (ii) [Energy] $\gamma(t)mc^2=mc^2\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$ and $\frac{d}{dt}(\gamma mc^2)=qE_0\,v_1(t)$: the field delivers power $qE\cdot v$ to the particle. (iii) [Unscoped Newtonian extrapolation] For $h\ne0$, the Newtonian constant-acceleration prediction $v_N(t):=(qE_0/m)t\,e_1$ satisfies $v(t)=v_N(t)/\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$, so the two agree only to first order in $|ht|$ and $|v_N(t)|=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}\,|v(t)|$ exceeds $c$ for $|t|>1/|h|$, whereas the exact solution of the adopted coupling remains subluminal at every finite time; for this explicit solution the approximation is quantified directly. Put $r_N(t)=r_0+\tfrac12hc t^2e_1$. For $h\ne0$, $$|v-v_N|\le\frac c2|ht|^3,\qquad |r-r_N|\le\frac{c}{8|h|}|ht|^4.$$ Thus on $|ht|\le\delta$ the velocity error is at most $c\delta^3/2$ and the displacement error at most $c\delta^4/(8|h|)$; these are special-model comparisons, not a general trajectory-stability consequence of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (c). When $h=0$ both trajectories and velocities coincide, and the Newtonian superluminal-time condition containing $1/|h|$ is not used. (iv) [Scope] the field is prescribed and external, the particle's own field and any radiation reaction or self-force are excluded, and no measurement or empirical claim is made; the solution is exact for the stated coupling with $E_0>0$ and arbitrary constant $q$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The constant charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$, the rest mass $m>0$,
the field strength $E_0>0$, the prescribed fields $E\equiv E_0e_1$,
$B\equiv0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, the number $h=qE_0/(mc)$ and the
origin $r_0\in\mathbb R^3$; the chart reading $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ with the
functions of the statement; and, where used, the real parameter $h\ne0$.

[F1] The fields are those of [[def-em-fields]] on the whole-space laboratory
region, with $E$ carrying $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$; the chart reading
$t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ of a massive worldline satisfies $|r'(t)|<c$ and has
four-velocity $U=\gamma(c,v)$ with $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and a vector
$(c,w)$ with $|w|<c$ is future timelike
([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (a), (c),
[[def-em-si-conventions]] (c)).

[F2] The smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho=0$, $J=0$
consists of $\operatorname{div}E=0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$,
$\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and
$\operatorname{curl}B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$, with the divergence and curl of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] applied at fixed time; a
constant field has every first partial derivative equal to $0$, so all four
equations hold for $(E,B)$.

[F3] The force and power identities of
[[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (a): for a solution of the adopted
coupling with coordinate velocity $v$, Lorentz factor $\gamma$, coordinate
momentum $p=m\gamma v$ and prescribed field $(E,B)$,
$dp/dt=q(E+v\times B)$ and
$d(\gamma mc^2)/dt=qE\cdot v$; the coordinate derivative $r'$ and the
vector-valued derivative are those of
[[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]] and [[def-rational-power]]. The
raised-index operator $\Phi$ of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]
is defined by $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$ and has components
$\Phi(u)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha\beta}u^\beta$; for the prescribed
field $F^{01}=E_0/c$, $F^{10}=-E_0/c$ and all other components zero
([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a)), so
$\Phi(u)^0=E_0u^1/c$, $\Phi(u)^1=E_0u^0/c$ and
$\Phi(u)^2=\Phi(u)^3=0$, and the adopted equation of motion is
$m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$.

[F4] Powers and roots: for $a>0$ the map $x\mapsto x^{\alpha}$ is continuous
and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ with $(x^{\alpha})'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}$,
and real powers agree with rational powers at rational exponents, so
$x^{1/2}=\sqrt x$ on $(0,\infty)$ with derivative
$\tfrac12x^{-1/2}$; the rational powers satisfy $a^{r+s}=a^ra^s$ and
$a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$, and $\sqrt{\cdot}$ is the nonnegative square root of
[[thm-of-square-roots]]
([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]],
[[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]], [[def-rational-power]],
[[lem-rational-power-laws]]).

[F5] Chain rule and product rule: composites and finite sums and products of
differentiable functions are differentiable with the usual rules
([[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). The Euclidean norm and
inner product are those of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], the cross product
is that of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], and for $a\ge0$, $a\le b$ exactly when
$a^2\le b^2$ ([[lem-of-square-monotone]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct differentiation of the displayed functions, the identity $(1+s^2)^{1/2}\ge1$ and rationalisation of the square root; the special-model error bounds are proved by elementary inequalities.

1.1 The prescribed field is source-free: $E\equiv E_0e_1$ and $B\equiv0$ are constant, so every first partial derivative of every component vanishes; by the component formulas of [F2], $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}B=0$ and $\partial_tE=\partial_tB=0$, so the four source-free smooth-branch equations hold on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 The trajectory and its velocity ($h\ne0$): put $g(t):=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}=(1+h^2t^2)^{1/2}$, a composition of the positive polynomial $t\mapsto1+h^2t^2$ with the power $x\mapsto x^{1/2}$; by [F4] and the chain rule [F5], $g$ is differentiable with $g'(t)=\tfrac12(1+h^2t^2)^{-1/2}\cdot2h^2t=h^2t/g(t)$, and since every derivative is a rational expression with nonzero denominator $g$, iterating the same rules shows $g$ and hence $r(t)=r_0+\tfrac{c}{h}(g(t)-1)e_1$ are $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$. Then $r'(t)=\tfrac{c}{h}g'(t)e_1=\tfrac{c ht}{g(t)}e_1=v(t)$ by [F5], so $|v(t)|=c|ht|/g(t)<c$ because $h^2t^2<1+h^2t^2$ for all real $t$ [F5], and $|v(t)|\to c$ as $|t|\to\infty$ because $|ht|/g(t)\to1$. [given, F4, F5, algebra]

1.3 The branch $h=0$: here $q=0$ since $E_0>0$, $m>0$ and $h=qE_0/(mc)$; the definition gives $r\equiv r_0$, $v\equiv0$, $\gamma\equiv1$ and $p\equiv0$, so $dp/dt=0=q(E+v\times B)$ and $d(\gamma mc^2)/dt=0=qE\cdot v$ hold trivially, and the Newtonian comparison trajectory of clause (iii) is $r_N\equiv r_0$ as well, with $v_N\equiv0$; the formulas containing $1/h$ are not used in this branch. [given, F3, algebra]

2.1 Force and power identities ($h\ne0$): by step 1.2, $\gamma(t)=g(t)$ equals $(1-|v(t)|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, since $1-|v|^2/c^2=1-\frac{h^2t^2}{1+h^2t^2}=\frac{1}{g(t)^2}$; hence $p(t)=m\gamma(t)v(t)=mg(t)\cdot\frac{c ht}{g(t)}e_1=mch t\,e_1=qE_0t\,e_1$, because $mch=qE_0$. Therefore $dp/dt=qE_0e_1=q(E+v\times B)$, since $E=E_0e_1$, $B=0$ and $v\times0=0$ [F5]. For the power identity, $d(\gamma mc^2)/dt=mc^2g'(t)=mc^2h^2t/g(t)=qE_0\cdot v_1(t)$ because $qE_0=mch$ and $v_1(t)=cht/g(t)$. These are the two coordinate identities of [F3]. The covariant equation $m\,dU/d\tau=q\Phi(U)$ of [F3] also holds: with $U^0=g(t)c$, $U^1=cht$ and $U^2=U^3=0$ one has $dU^0/d\tau=g\,d(gc)/dt=c\,g\,g'=ch^2t$ and $dU^1/d\tau=g\,d(cht)/dt=cgh$, so $m\,dU^0/d\tau=mch^2t=qE_0ht=q\Phi(U)^0$ and $m\,dU^1/d\tau=mgch=qgE_0=q\Phi(U)^1$, while the components $2,3$ vanish on both sides; hence the displayed curve is an exact solution of the adopted coupling in this special model. [given, step 1.2, F3, F5, algebra]

2.2 The curve is a future timelike worldline: by step 1.2 the curve is $C^\infty$ with coordinate velocity $v(t)$ and $|v(t)|<c$; its tangent $(c,v(t))$ has $\eta$-square $-c^2+|v(t)|^2<0$ and positive time component $c>0$, so it is future timelike at every $t$, and the chart reading is that of a massive worldline in the sense of [F1]. At $h=0$ the constant curve has tangent $(c,0)$, also future timelike. [given, step 1.2, step 1.3, F1, F5, algebra]

2.3 The unscoped Newtonian extrapolation ($h\ne0$): define $v_N(t):=(qE_0/m)t\,e_1=hct\,e_1$ and $r_N(t):=r_0+\tfrac12hct^2e_1$. Since $qE_0/m=hc$, step 1.2 gives $v(t)=\frac{cht}{g(t)}e_1=\frac{v_N(t)}{g(t)}=\frac{v_N(t)}{\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}}$, and therefore $|v_N(t)|=g(t)|v(t)|=c|ht|$, which exceeds $c$ exactly when $|ht|>1$, while $|v(t)|<c$ for every finite $t$ by step 1.2. The two velocities agree only at $t=0$; $v_N$ is the Newtonian constant-acceleration prediction of the unscoped law. [given, step 1.2, F5, algebra]

3.1 Error bounds ($h\ne0$): put $s:=ht$ and $g=\sqrt{1+s^2}\ge1$. Rationalisation gives $g-1=\frac{s^2}{g+1}\le\frac{s^2}{2}$ and $1-\frac1g=\frac{g-1}{g}\le\frac{s^2}{2}$; hence $|v-v_N|=|v_N|\bigl|1-\frac1g\bigr|=c|s|\bigl(1-\frac1g\bigr)\le\frac{c}{2}|s|^3$, which is the velocity bound. For the displacement, $r(t)-r_N(t)=\frac{c}{h}\bigl(g-1-\tfrac{s^2}{2}\bigr)e_1$, and the elementary identity $1+\tfrac{s^2}{2}-g=\tfrac{(g-1)^2}{2}$ gives $\bigl|g-1-\tfrac{s^2}{2}\bigr|=\tfrac{(g-1)^2}{2}\le\tfrac{s^4}{8}$ by the first inequality; multiplying by $c/|h|$ gives $|r-r_N|\le\frac{c}{8|h|}|s|^4$. Consequently on $|ht|\le\delta$ the velocity error is at most $c\delta^3/2$ and the displacement error at most $c\delta^4/(8|h|)$; these are special-model comparisons for this explicit solution and do not import a general trajectory-stability consequence of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (c). [given, step 1.2, step 2.3, F5, algebra]

4.1 Closing and scope: the prescribed field is a source-free constant smooth-branch solution (step 1.1); for $h\ne0$ the displayed curve is $C^\infty$, future timelike and subluminal at every finite time, and it satisfies the force and power identities with $p=qE_0te_1$ (steps 1.2, 2.1, 2.2); the Newtonian comparison and its exact superluminal condition are step 2.3, and the special-model error bounds are step 3.1; the branch $h=0$ with $q=0$ is step 1.3. The field is prescribed and external, the particle's own field, radiation reaction and any self-force are excluded, no production of the field is described, and no measurement or empirical claim is made. The argument used the field and worldline objects [F1], the smooth-branch equations [F2], the force and power identities [F3], the power and root calculus [F4] and the chain and product rules [F5]; no choice principle is used. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.1, F1, F3] ∎

## Source notes

The three cited treatments present the relativistic motion in a uniform
electric field and its limiting speed in their own conventions. The
verification above differentiates the displayed closed-form trajectory in the
framework's chart ($x^0=ct$, SI units, $h=qE_0/mc$), checks the coordinate
force and power identities of the framework's adopted covariant coupling, and
quantifies the failure of the unscoped Newtonian constant-acceleration
prediction by explicit elementary bounds; the conversion from the sources'
conventions is carried out here rather than assumed.

## Definition

Adopt the laboratory region with its inertial chart and fixed-time reading of
[[def-em-lab-geometry]], the electric and magnetic fields of [[def-em-fields]],
the charge parameter, frame charge and current densities and charge integrals
of [[def-em-sources]], and the SI units and constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]]. This definition fixes the framework's report-record
vocabulary; it selects no experiment, records no value, evaluates no indicator
and asserts no measurement.

(a) [Primary source] A *primary source* is a declared bibliographic
identification of a report (author, title, date, publication, and the
identification of the passages actually inspected) together with the declared
limits of the reading: which parts of the report were read, which were not, and
any carrier defects (for instance corrupted optical-character-recognition text
of formulae or tables).

(b) [Comparison quantity and measurand] Let $d\ge1$ be an integer. A
*comparison quantity* of dimension $d$ is a declared map from a declared
condition set to $\mathbb R^d$, with declared units, whose components are
finite expressions in specified framework quantities. These may include the
values of $E,B,\rho,J$ at declared events, the charge parameter $q$, and the
declared charge or current integrals of [[def-em-sources]]; declared field
circulations and surface fluxes on the admitted fixed geometries of
[[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]; and declared finite-time or period averages of
specified derived field quantities, including $u$ and $S$ of
[[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]. An integral or average is admitted only with its
domain, orientation where needed, integration convention and actual
well-definedness hypotheses declared. For example, a component $Q(t)$
continuous on a declared compact interval $[a,b]$ inside the laboratory time
domain, with $a<b$, has the finite Riemann average
$(b-a)^{-1}\int_a^b Q(t)\,dt$ by [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]; a
period average additionally declares the period and interval. Field fluxes
inherit the regularity, compactness, boundary presentation and measure/choice
conventions of their fixed-test supplier. A declared detector-response
integral may be used only when its declared model and integral suppliers
establish a finite real value. An extended nonnegative integral with value
$+\infty$ is not a component of this real-valued comparison map or a recorded
finite rate. No existence or finiteness of an arbitrary field integral,
distributional product or detector response is asserted. A *measurand* is a
comparison quantity together with a declared condition description under which
it is to be read. All quantities carry the SI conventions of
[[def-em-si-conventions]].

(c) [Apparatus and preparation description] An *apparatus-and-preparation
description* is a declared finite record of the apparatus, the preparation,
the controls and the environment in the report's own terms, with the
identification of the passage of the primary source of (a) from which each
item of the description is taken. The definition asserts only that the
description is declared and finite; it asserts nothing about its correctness
or completeness.

(d) [Recorded data and reported observations] For an integer $d\ge1$, a
*recorded datum* is a vector $z_k\in\mathbb R^{d}$ with declared units
together with a *condition annotation* $a_k$, a declared finite text
identifying the declared run condition of the datum and, when the datum is
taken from a report, its locator in the primary source. A *reported
observation* is a declared finite text recording a qualitative observation of
the report. A *record* is a finite tuple of recorded data and reported
observations together with the declared condition annotations. The record
contains no probability space, random variable, distribution, sampling law,
independence assumption, likelihood or coverage statement.

(e) [Calibration model] A *calibration model* is a tuple $(Z,c,\delta)$ in
which $Z$ is a declared nonempty set of *apparatus-output values*,
$c:Z\to\mathbb R^d$ is a declared *calibration map* and
$\delta\in[0,\infty)$ is a declared *calibration-error bound*: it declares
that for every output $o\in Z$ obtained under the declared conditions, the
value of the comparison quantity of (b) lies in the closed box
$\prod_{j=1}^d[c_j(o)-\delta,\,c_j(o)+\delta]$ in the declared units. A
calibration model is a declaration; the definition asserts no accuracy beyond
the bound $\delta$ and no statistical property of $c$ or $\delta$. A declared
*missing* calibration is recorded as missing, and no value or bound is then
available from this clause.

(f) [Uncertainty record] An *uncertainty record* is a finite tuple of declared
bounds, each carrying a declared *source label* from the finite list
$\{calibration,\ resolution,\ systematic,\ sampling-variability,\ rounding,\ other\}$
and a declared value in the declared units; each entry is a declared
constraint of the form of (e), and the record may state that a bound is
unavailable. No entry is a standard-deviation convention, a coverage
probability, a confidence level, a $p$-value, a posterior or a probability
law.

(g) [Analysis assumptions] An *analysis-assumption list* is a finite tuple of
declared assumptions used to obtain the recorded data or to compare them with
a model (binning, background model, selection rules, corrections, fitting or
estimation procedure, independence or dependence of entries, and the
treatment of the sources of uncertainty); declared omissions are recorded as
omissions and are not filled in by the definition.

(h) [Interpretation] An *interpretation* is a declared statement that
identifies a specified model prediction and declares the result of comparing
the record with it (support, constraint, failure to distinguish, or no
conclusion), conditional on (a)-(g). The interpretation is part of the report
account and not of the data; it asserts no probability, no significance level
and no truth of any framework, and it records a comparison of a specified
model, not of a whole theory.

(i) [Well-definedness and scope] All components of (a)-(h) are finite tuples,
real numbers, declared maps on declared sets and finite text labels; forming
this finite vocabulary uses no choice principle. Evaluating a comparison
quantity inherits every hypothesis and axiom of its actual suppliers,
including countable choice when the selected fixed-test surface or
Lebesgue-measure interface requires it; no measurability, integrability,
completeness or differentiability is inferred merely from the record. A
comparison quantity is evaluated only where the cited items supply its
ingredients and a finite value. Missing source detail stays missing: no
universal sampling law, precision, independence, coverage or calibration
correctness is part of the definition, and none may be inferred from it. The
definition is the framework-local vocabulary for the reports of this page; it
does not assert that any laboratory realises a measurand or that any reported
observation is correct.

## Source notes

The vocabulary above formalises the record fields of the three primary reports
recorded on this page: a declared primary source with its reading limits, an
apparatus-and-preparation description, finite recorded data or reported
qualitative observations with condition annotations, a calibration model that
may be declared missing, an uncertainty record of declared bounds with source
labels, an analysis-assumption list with recorded omissions, and an
interpretation separated from the data. The GUM clauses cited in the frontmatter
supply the metrological vocabulary of measurand, measurement model, error
correction and uncertainty source; the definition keeps every declared bound
distinct from any coverage, confidence or probability statement, and it
performs no numerical evaluation. No measurement, apparatus behaviour, sampling
law, precision or calibration correctness is asserted, and no experiment is
selected.

**Primary source and reading limits.** Michael Faraday, *Experimental Researches in
Electricity*, Volume I, First Series (read 24 November 1831), 1849 collected
second edition, read in the Project Gutenberg transcription derived from
BnF/Gallica images; the First Series paragraphs 1-33 were read completely, and
no claim is made to have read the whole volume. This is an original report
reprint transmitted by a later transcription, not a newly repeated experiment.
The account below is the report's apparatus descriptions and reported
observations, structured by the record contract of
[[def-em-experiment-record-contract]]; it is not a deduction, and 'no perceived
deflection' is everywhere the report's finite-resolution verbal observation.

## Setup

Insulated copper helices wound on a wooden cylinder, each containing about
twenty-seven feet of wire and kept from touching by interposed twine, twelve
helices superposed in the same direction with the first, third, fifth, seventh,
ninth and eleventh joined into one helix and the remainder into a second
(paragraph 6). A pair of two-hundred-and-three-foot coils interleaved as a
spiral on a wooden block with metallic contact prevented by twine (paragraph
10). A small hollow helix wound on a glass tube into which a steel needle could
be inserted (paragraph 13). Insulated zigzag wire boards moved relatively to
one another (paragraph 18). A welded soft-iron ring, seven-eighths of an inch
thick and six inches in external diameter, with three insulated helices of
about twenty-four feet each, later driven by a battery of ten pairs of plates
with a galvanometer connected three feet from the ring (paragraphs 27-28).

## Procedure

Making and breaking the battery circuit of the inducing helix while the
detector loop is kept complete (paragraphs 10-11); removing the inserted needle
before breaking the battery contact, and the reverse order (paragraph 13);
completing the detector circuit before the battery contact is made or broken
(paragraph 17); moving the zigzag boards together and apart with a steady
battery current (paragraphs 18-19); reversing the direction of the battery
connection (paragraph 30); repeating with larger batteries and with charcoal
contacts (paragraphs 31-32).

## Observations

A slight deflection of the galvanometer needle at the moment of completing the
connection, always in one direction, with the opposite deflection at breaking,
and no sustained perceived deflection under the continued steady battery
connection (paragraphs 11 and 28-31); magnetization of an inserted steel needle,
with opposite poles at make and at break and near-cancellation when both
transients act on the same inserted needle (paragraphs 13-17); opposite
transient deflections as the boards approach and recede, with return to the
ordinary position when the movement ceases (paragraphs 18-20); a minute spark
at the secondary helix with charcoal contacts (paragraph 32); and the control
that, after the first effect, the galvanometer needle resumes its position
under the continued battery current (paragraphs 28 and 33). These are reported
finite-resolution qualitative observations.

## Uncertainty

The read passages identify deflection direction, needle-pole comparison,
battery reversal and background and timing controls, but supply no calibrated
conversion from deflection to current, no detector response or transfer
function, no trial-level dataset, no declared sampling law, no error bars and
no formal significance test; dimensions, wire lengths and battery plate counts
are historical approximate apparatus descriptions, not modern precision
estimates. The sign interpretation of the induced current depends on
galvanometer and needle response conventions. Missing information is retained
as missing; no error bars, precision or independence are invented.

## Interpretation

The reported observations support a transient induction model for the described
apparatus under the stated apparatus assumptions and are qualitatively
consistent with conditional framework predictions of transient induction where
those are instantiated for the described circuits; they do not establish a
universal exact induction law, do not isolate all auxiliary assumptions
(magnetic inertia, switching transients, leakage, current history, geometry)
and supply no quantitative model comparison. The empirical support is a
nonlogical relation to the induction predictions, not a proof of any
postulate, and the source limitations of the reading travel into any downstream
conclusion.

**Primary source and reading limits.** Heinrich Hertz, 'On the finite velocity
of propagation of electromagnetic actions' (Berlin Academy, 2 February 1888;
*Wiedemann's Annalen* 34 p. 661), in the authorized English *Electric Waves*
translation (D. E. Jones, Macmillan 1893), Chapter VII, printed pp. 107-123; the
complete chapter narrative was read in the Internet Archive OCR of
`electricwavesbe00hertgoog`, whose tables are visibly scrambled and have not
been reconstructed or recomputed, and the rest of the volume was not read. This
is a primary-report translation with an OCR limitation, not a modern
replication or a measured-$c$ precision source. The account below is the
report's apparatus descriptions, procedures and reported observation
indicators, structured by the record contract of
[[def-em-experiment-record-contract]].

## Setup

A spark-excited primary conductor with brass end plates and a central spark gap
drove rapid oscillations; circular or square secondary conductors with
micrometer-adjusted spark gaps served as qualitative detectors; the comparison
used waves on a long wire versus direct action through air, with tuned
secondary orientations and adjustable additional wire length; the room was
darkened, and reflections and nearby fixtures were apparatus concerns (chapter
VII narrative, printed pp. 107-123).

## Procedure

Locating nodal points of the wire standing wave by moving the tuned secondary
along the wire and marking their positions with paper riders; comparing spark
strength and suppression at different positions along a defined baseline;
changing the wire length in unit steps of the measured nodal distance and
repeating; changing the distance between the primary and secondary circuits;
and comparing the direct air-path action with the wire-wave action (chapter VII
narrative).

## Observations

Orientation-dependent spark responses of the secondary detector; approximately
recurring and roughly equally spaced nodal points along the wire; and changing
signs of the interference indicator as the path length or the distance is
varied. These are the reported observed indicators; the finite phase delay and
the propagation speed of the order of light speed are the author's
model-dependent inferences, requiring his assumed oscillator, detector,
wire-wave and air-path phase interpretation.

## Uncertainty

The report expressly treats its inferred absolute period from circuit theory as
doubtful beyond order of magnitude; it supplies no modern calibrated
spark-intensity transfer function, no independent absolute period calibration,
no trial-level likelihood or sampling model, no confidence interval and no
synchronized-clock travel-time measurement; the numerical tabular signs cannot
be faithfully recovered from the OCR used, and no quantitative fit, exact speed
or uncertainty interval is claimed here. The author's rough order-of-magnitude
remarks are not confidence intervals.

## Interpretation

The described apparatus observations qualitatively support finite-propagation
and wave-interference models under the stated auxiliary assumptions; they do
not deductively prove the Maxwell equations, do not exactly establish the value
of $c$, and do not eliminate every alternative, since the comparison involves
the assumed oscillator, detector and wire-wave models. The historical
decomposition into separately propagating electrostatic and electromagnetic
components is not promoted to a modern Lorentz-covariant theorem. The source
limitations travel into any downstream historical or empirical conclusion, and
the support is a nonlogical relation to the wave predictions.

**Primary source and reading limits.** Henry Cavendish's original manuscripts as
edited by J. Clerk Maxwell, *The Electrical Researches of the Honourable Henry
Cavendish* (Cambridge 1879), 'Experimental determination of the law of electric
force', arts. 217-235, printed pp. 104-113, with the detector and electrometer
descriptions arts. 244-249, printed pp. 119-121; read in the Internet Archive
OCR of `electricalresea00cavegoog`. The original apparatus, procedure, reported
observations and sensitivity check are identifiable, but the fractional
calibration ratios and the exponent computation are corrupted by the OCR and no
numerical exponent limit is transcribed or recomputed here. The account below
is the report's descriptions and observations structured by the record contract
of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]]; it is a reported finite-resolution
null, not a proof that a true charge is exactly zero.

## Setup

A conducting inner globe 12.1 inches in diameter, supported by a glass stick
coated with sealing wax, enclosed between two tinfoil-coated pasteboard
hemispheres 13.3 inches in diameter with a small clearance, the two hemispheres
applied to each other to form a complete sphere; a removable wire connected the
inner globe and the hemispheres, and could be drawn out by a silk string;
linked strings operated the apparatus so that the charging wire, the inner
connecting wire and the hemispheres were successively separated (paragraphs
219-222). A coated glass jar and an electrometer monitored and repeated the
charging level (paragraphs 224-225). The detector was a pair of pith balls
about one-fifth of an inch in diameter on fine linen threads, later a straw
electrometer with cork balls (paragraphs 244-249). A second experiment enclosed
a wooden piece between two wooden drawers forming a hollow box (paragraph 235).

## Procedure

The hemispheres were charged from a Leyden vial through a wire, which was then
withdrawn; immediately afterwards the wire connecting the inner globe and the
hemispheres was drawn out by the silk string, the hemispheres were separated
without touching the inner globe, and the outer shells and charging wire were
discharged; a pith-ball detector was then brought to the inner globe
(paragraphs 220-222 and 226). For greater sensitivity the pith balls were
precharged positively before the charge, the comparison being made against the
negative-precharge case at monitored equal charging levels (paragraphs
228-229). The deliberate sensitivity control repeated the procedure with a
smaller coated glass element carrying a known small charge (paragraph 230).

## Observations

Several repetitions without perceived pith-ball separation or signs of residual
inner charge (paragraph 227); in the precharged-ball comparison, equal small
residual separations for positive and negative precharge rather than a
detectable charge-sign asymmetry (paragraphs 228-229); in the sensitivity
control, the small deliberately imposed charge was visibly distinguished by
the same detector (paragraph 230); and a corresponding qualitative null with
the enclosed-box geometry (paragraph 235). The reported 'must be inversely as
the square' inference (paragraph 232) is recorded as the author's conclusion
from the null under his theory, not as a modern theorem.

## Uncertainty

The read passages supply charge-level monitoring, the precharge comparison, a
deliberate sensitivity check and the pith-ball and electrometer construction,
but no calibrated charge transfer function, no trial-level sampling model, no
confidence interval and no modern SI traceability. Insulation leakage, finite
separation time, imperfect spherical geometry, shell holes, accidental contact
and outside charges are apparatus-model and systematic conditions. The OCR
cannot faithfully recover all fractional calibration ratios or the exponent
calculation, so no numerical exponent bound, precision, likelihood or certainty
is invented.

## Interpretation

An ideal inverse-square enclosed-conductor equilibrium model predicts zero
charge in the connected enclosed interior under its idealization, and the
reported observations support that model within the apparatus sensitivity and
auxiliary assumptions; they constrain specified alternative force laws only
after an explicit response and sensitivity model, which the read passages do
not supply in numerically usable form. A finite null cannot prove an exact
exponent, and the empirical support is a nonlogical relation to the static
prediction.
