## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$,
[[def-countable-choice]]) exactly as inherited from clause (a) of
[[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]], which is used in clause (a)(i) below with its
piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure conventions; no other choice
principle is used. Let the laboratory region, its inertial chart, the fields
$E,B$ and the source fields $\rho,J$ be those named in
[[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]], with its constants and units, and let $R$ be a
record of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]] of dimension $d=1$ (primary
source, apparatus-and-preparation description, recorded data or reported
observations, calibration model, uncertainty record, analysis-assumption list,
interpretation). Write $I_t$ for the laboratory time interval. Let
$I_\theta\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open parameter interval,
$\theta_0\in I_\theta$, and $f:I_\theta\to\mathbb R$ a declared comparison map
of class $C^1$ such that $f(\theta_0)=0$ and $f'(\theta)\ge m>0$ for every
$\theta\in I_\theta$. Suppose the record's declared apparatus-and-calibration
dictionary identifies the comparison quantity with the deviation $y=f(\theta)$
of a declared model family from the exact framework reference prediction $y_0$
of clause (a), and declares the recorded deviation $\hat y$ and the bounds
$|\hat y|\le s$ and $|y-\hat y|\le\delta$ with $s,\delta\ge0$.

(a) [Exact framework reference predictions] (i) [Static branch] Assume the
smooth branch of the adopted vacuum Maxwell equations with the regularity
hypotheses of [[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]] (fields jointly $C^1$ on
$\Omega\times I_t$ with the additional derivatives appearing in the displayed
equations existing and continuous there; for instance $E,B$ jointly of class
$C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$). Let $(V,\nu_V)$ be a volume test geometry
of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]] and let $t\in I_t$ be such that
$\rho(\cdot,t)$ vanishes identically on $V$. Then clause (a) of
[[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]] gives
$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3=0.$$
On the smooth branch every admitted boundary $\partial V$ whose enclosed volume
$V$ is charge-free has vanishing electric flux; charge-freeness of the surface
alone is insufficient, and the exact framework prediction for the
enclosed-flux observable is the value $y_0=0$.

(ii) [Wave branch] Let $(E,B)$ be the plane-wave solution of
[[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]] with data $(k,\omega,e)$ there, and let
$\langle S\rangle$ be the period average of its Poynting vector. Then that item
gives the signed identity
$$\langle S\rangle\cdot n=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2\,(\hat k\cdot n)$$ for
every unit vector $n$; if the declared dictionary fixes the comparison
quantity as the magnitude $|\langle S\rangle\cdot n|$ of the normal
period-averaged flux (a declared intensity convention), then the exact
framework prediction is
$$y_0=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2\,|\hat k\cdot n|.$$ The absolute value is
part of that declared magnitude convention and is not a consequence of the
signed identity.

(b) [Conditional confinement] Under the stated identifications, every
parameter value $\theta\in I_\theta$ compatible with the declared model
family, the apparatus-and-calibration dictionary and the two declared bounds
satisfies
$$|\theta-\theta_0|\le\frac{s+\delta}{m}.$$ Equivalently, a proposed $\theta$
violating this bound is incompatible with the conjunction (specified family,
dictionary, calibration bound, recorded bound); the conclusion is a
deterministic statement about the declared bounds.

(c) [Status and qualifications] The conclusion is conditional on the declared
family, dictionary, calibration and recorded bounds and on the declared
monotonicity margin $m$; it is not a sampling law, a likelihood, a confidence
level, a coverage probability, a $p$-value or a probability that any model or
framework is true, and it asserts no rejection error rate. Agreement of a
record with a specified family, like disagreement with it, concerns the
conjunction of that family with the apparatus, calibration and analysis
assumptions; a discrepancy may lie in the family, the dictionary, the
calibration or the analysis, and neither agreement nor disagreement proves or
deductively falsifies the adopted framework. The three primary reports
recorded on this page supply, in their recorded read extents, no calibrated
response transfer function, no trial-level dataset and no declared sampling
law; accordingly this item asserts no numerical bound and performs no
numerical application for any of them, and their own uncertainty records carry
their source limitations. Empirical support and its constraints are nonlogical
relations, not dependencies, and any consumer of this item inherits $s$,
$\delta$, $m$, the declared family, the record's conditions and the source
limitations.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; the laboratory
region, chart, fields, sources, constants and units named in
[[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]] with its smooth-branch regularity hypotheses; a
volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]] and a time
$t\in I_t$ with $\rho(\cdot,t)$ vanishing identically on $V$; the plane-wave
solution of [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]] with data $(k,\omega,e)$ and a unit
vector $n$; a record $R$ of dimension $d=1$ with the declared
apparatus-and-calibration dictionary, comparison map $f$ of class $C^1$ on the
nonempty open interval $I_\theta$, centre $\theta_0\in I_\theta$,
$f(\theta_0)=0$, $f'\ge m>0$ on $I_\theta$, recorded deviation $\hat y$ and
bounds $|\hat y|\le s$, $|y-\hat y|\le\delta$, $s,\delta\ge0$.

[F1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the
statement that every at most countable family of nonempty sets has a choice
function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F2] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, if the smooth branch of the adopted vacuum
Maxwell equations holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$ for fields jointly $C^1$
with the additional derivatives appearing in the displayed equations existing
and continuous there, then for every volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and
every $t\in I$ the integral form of the Gauss law reads
$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3$$
([[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]], clause (a) and its regularity hypotheses).

[F3] A volume test geometry in $\Omega$ is a pair $(V,\nu_V)$ with
$V\subseteq\Omega$ a nonempty bounded open set, $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$
and a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentation with outward unit
normal $\nu_V$, and its closed-surface flux is the finite face sum
$\oint_{\partial V}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS:=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS$
([[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], clause (a)).

[F4] For the plane-wave solution with data $(k,\omega,e)$ the period average of
the Poynting vector is $\langle S\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2\hat k$,
so
$\langle S\rangle\cdot n=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2(\hat k\cdot n)$ for
every unit vector $n$ ([[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]], clause (b)).

[F5] A record of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]] carries a comparison
quantity that is a declared map on a declared condition set, with declared
units (clause (b)); a calibration model is a tuple $(Z,c,\delta)$ with $Z$ a
declared nonempty set of apparatus-output values and $\delta\in[0,\infty)$ a
declared calibration-error bound (clause (e)); and the analysis-assumption
list contains the declared assumptions used to compare the data with a model
(clause (g)).

[F6] Let $n\ge1$, $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ open, $\theta_0\in U$ and $u\in\mathbb R^n$
with $\lVert u\rVert_2=1$; let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval with
$0\in I$ and $\theta_0+\theta u\in U$ for every $\theta\in I$; let
$F:U\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ with $F(\theta_0)=0$ and
$D_uF(\theta_0+\theta u)\ge m>0$ for every $\theta\in I$. If a recorded scalar
$\hat y$ satisfies $|\hat y|\le s$, $s\ge0$, and the calibration bound
$|y-\hat y|\le\delta$, $\delta\ge0$, holds for $y=F(\theta_0+\theta u)$ at a
candidate $\theta\in I$, then $|\theta|\le(s+\delta)/m$
([[thm-em-uncertainty-analysis]], Statement).

## Proof

1.1 [Static branch] Fix the volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and the time $t\in I_t$ of the statement, with $\rho(\cdot,t)$ vanishing identically on $V$; under the smooth-branch regularity hypotheses of [F2], clause (a) of [F2] gives $\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3$, and the integrand $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is the identically zero function on $V$, so its integral is $0$ and the flux vanishes: $\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=0$, the exact framework prediction for the enclosed-flux observable being $y_0=0$; the test-geometry conventions are those of [F3], and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used here exactly through [F2]. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

1.2 [Wave branch] Let $(E,B)$ be the plane-wave solution with data $(k,\omega,e)$ and let $n$ be a unit vector; clause (b) of [F4] gives the signed identity $\langle S\rangle\cdot n=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2(\hat k\cdot n)$, so if the declared dictionary fixes the comparison quantity as the magnitude $|\langle S\rangle\cdot n|$ of the normal period-averaged flux, the exact framework prediction is $y_0=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2|\hat k\cdot n|$, the absolute value being the declared magnitude convention and not a consequence of the signed identity. [F4, given, algebra]

1.3 [Displacement interval] Put $J_\theta:=\{\,h\in\mathbb R:\theta_0+h\in I_\theta\,\}$, the translate $I_\theta-\theta_0$ of the nonempty open interval $I_\theta$: $J_\theta$ is a nonempty open interval and contains $0$ because $\theta_0\in I_\theta$, and $f'(\theta_0+h)\ge m>0$ for every $h\in J_\theta$ by the hypothesis $f'\ge m$ on $I_\theta$. [given, algebra]

2.1 [Conditional confinement] Apply [F6] with $n=1$, $U:=I_\theta$, base point $\theta_0$, unit direction $u:=1\in\mathbb R^1$ (so $\lVert u\rVert_2=1$), interval $I:=J_\theta$ and $F:=f$: $U=I_\theta$ is open and contains $\theta_0$; for every $h\in J_\theta$ one has $\gamma(h)=\theta_0+h\cdot1=\theta_0+h\in I_\theta=U$ by the definition of $J_\theta$; $f$ is of class $C^1$ on $U$ with $f(\theta_0)=0$; and the directional derivative of $f$ along $u=1$ is the ordinary derivative, $D_1f(\theta_0+h)=f'(\theta_0+h)\ge m>0$, because in $\mathbb R^1$ the difference quotient defining $D_1f$ is the ordinary difference quotient. Hence, for every candidate $h\in J_\theta$ for which the record declares $y=f(\theta_0+h)$ with $|\hat y|\le s$ and $|y-\hat y|\le\delta$, [F6] yields $|h|\le(s+\delta)/m$; writing $\theta:=\theta_0+h\in I_\theta$ for the candidate parameter value of the record's declared dictionary, this is exactly $|\theta-\theta_0|\le(s+\delta)/m$, which is clause (b). [F5, F6, step 1.3, given, algebra]

3.1 [Status] Clause (c) records the scope of steps 1.1-2.1: the result is conditional on the declared family, dictionary, calibration and recorded bounds and on the margin $m$; it is not a sampling law, likelihood, confidence level, coverage probability or $p$-value, and asserts no rejection error rate; the record vocabulary of [F5] supplies only declared comparison quantities, calibration models and analysis assumptions, so the dictionary identification in step 2.1 is a declaration rather than a consequence of the record structure; a discrepancy may lie in the family, the dictionary, the calibration or the analysis, so neither agreement nor disagreement proves or deductively falsifies the framework; the three primary reports recorded on this page supply no calibrated response transfer function, trial-level dataset or sampling law in their recorded read extents, so no numerical bound and no numerical application is asserted for them; and the empirical support relations are nonlogical. [F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, given] ∎

## Remark

Record the established scope limits of the classical electromagnetic results
assembled in this framework, with no speculative content. Each clause names
what is and is not supplied; the remark asserts no theorem and adds no result.

(a) [Continuum and regularity regime] The fields of the framework are the maps
of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region, with the regularity class
carried by each statement; the solved branches are the smooth and stated weak
branches of the adopted equations, and every conclusion holds only under its
own stated regularity, domain and boundary hypotheses. No discrete, atomic or
finite-resolution structure of matter or charge is assumed, and none is
derived.

(b) [Material-model regime] The material results rest on the declared
constitutive branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] (the elementary
inertial-rest linear nondispersive Ohmic branch and the causal memory branch
with its declared kernel or transfer-function hypotheses); arbitrary
nonlinear, nonlocal, hysteretic, or beyond-branch anisotropic and strongly
dispersive response is not established by this framework, and each declared
branch carries its own regime of validity, including the finite-band
qualification of the constant-coefficient branch.

(c) [Singular sources and self-interaction]
[[rem-em-radiation-reaction-limits]] records that the point-source self-field
energy diverges under removal of the cutoff, that a product of the singular
self-field with the charge's own distributional current is not defined by the
adopted source model, and that the emitted-power results are prescribed-source
statements determining no back-reaction. No self-force dynamics, runaway
analysis, finite-size regularization or electromagnetic derivation of rest
mass is supplied by this framework.

(d) [External-force and mechanical coupling] Particle motion enters only
through the adopted Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] with a
prescribed external field; the framework determines the motion of a specified
test charge in a specified field and supplies no material law, no self-field
dynamics and no derivation of the particle parameters. Any coupling to matter
beyond the declared branches is an additional model assumption.

(e) [Quantum and ontological exclusions] The framework adopts no quantisation
of charge, no spin or magnetic-moment degree of freedom, no measurement
postulates and no photon model. Its interference results, such as the coherent
cross term of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]], are deterministic statements
about classical wave fields; classical electromagnetic waves interfere, so an
interference pattern alone neither establishes a quantum description nor
falsifies classical electromagnetism, and the framework's field predictions
do not single out an ontology of the underlying field or of a particle.

(f) [Empirical status] The empirical content of this page is report-backed and
qualitative: the records of the three primary reports, in their stated read
extents, carry no calibrated response functions, trial-level datasets or
declared sampling laws, so they support and constrain the specified models
only within their declared apparatus, calibration and analysis assumptions;
agreement does not prove the framework and disagreement does not deductively
falsify it. No measurement, precision, probability or confidence level is
invented or inferred by this remark.

(g) [Status] This is a scope remark, not an established theorem; it records the
limits of the results assembled here and asserts no new result, no measurement
and no proof.

## Example

Let the record vocabulary be that of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]], and
adopt a declared affine response model in which the model prediction for a
recorded comparison quantity is $$y(s,b):=G\,s+b,$$ where $G>0$ is a declared
response coefficient (with declared units [recorded]/[source]), $s\in\mathbb R$
a declared source-strength parameter and $b\in\mathbb R$ a declared background
parameter in the units of the recorded quantity; the model is part of the
record's analysis assumptions. Then:

(i) [Exact ambiguity] For every $\delta\in\mathbb R$,
$$y(s+\delta,\,b-G\delta)=G(s+\delta)+(b-G\delta)=Gs+b=y(s,b),$$ by the field
arithmetic of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-ordered-field]] makes $\mathbb R$ a
totally ordered field). Hence the two parameter pairs $(s,b)$ and
$(s+\delta,b-G\delta)$ produce the same predicted value at every recorded
coordinate, and every recorded value or declared closed bound interval
compatible with the prediction of one pair is compatible with the prediction
of the other.

(ii) [Nonidentifiability] When $G\ne0$ and $\delta\ne0$ the two pairs are
distinct, yet their model predictions coincide; consequently a comparison of
the record with the affine model alone determines only the combination $Gs+b$,
and cannot distinguish the pairs unless an additional independent declaration
pins one of the two parameters, for example an independent
background-calibration declaration fixing $b$ or an independent
source-strength declaration fixing $s$.

(iii) [Explicit instance] With $G=2$, $s=3$, $b=1$ and $\delta=1$ one has
$y(3,1)=2\cdot3+1=7$ and $y(4,-1)=2\cdot4-1=7$, so the pairs $(s,b)=(3,1)$ and
$(4,-1)$ are indistinguishable by the recorded value $7$ alone; the same holds
for every declared bound interval, since the two predictions coincide exactly.

(iv) [Status] This is a deterministic algebraic nonidentifiability statement
about the declared affine response model. It asserts no property of any
apparatus, no historical value, no dataset and no statistical or probabilistic
claim; it records that a discrepancy (or an agreement) can test the auxiliary
background and calibration parameters as well as the field or source
assumptions of a model, so that attributing a recorded outcome to one premise
requires the independent declarations.

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct substitution in the field $\mathbb R$ and immediate
consequences of the declared record vocabulary.

**Given:** a declared affine response model $y(s,b)=Gs+b$ with $G>0$, and the
record vocabulary of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]]; a parameter
displacement $\delta\in\mathbb R$.

[F1] $\mathbb R$ with its order and field operations is a totally ordered
field ([[thm-reals-ordered-field]]), so distributivity, associativity,
commutativity, additive inverses and the order axioms hold in
$\mathbb R$.

[F2] A record of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]] carries a declared
analysis-assumption list (clause (g)), a calibration model with a declared
error bound when one is available (clause (e)) and an interpretation that
compares the record with a specified model prediction (clause (h)); the affine
model above is such a declared analysis assumption, and no sampling law,
probability or apparatus property is part of the record vocabulary.

1.1 For every $\delta\in\mathbb R$ the predicted value of the displaced pair $(s+\delta,\,b-G\delta)$ is $G(s+\delta)+(b-G\delta)=Gs+G\delta+b-G\delta=Gs+b$: distributivity gives $G(s+\delta)=Gs+G\delta$, associativity and commutativity of addition regroup the four terms as $Gs+(G\delta-G\delta)+b$, and $G\delta-G\delta=0$ with $Gs+0+b=Gs+b$; hence $y(s+\delta,b-G\delta)=y(s,b)$ for every common recorded coordinate, which is clause (i). [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Any recorded value or declared closed bound interval compatible with the prediction of the pair $(s,b)$ is compatible with the prediction of $(s+\delta,b-G\delta)$: a recorded value equal to the predicted value is equal to the other predicted value by step 1.1, and a declared interval of the form $[y-r,y+r]$ with $r\ge0$ is unchanged because its centre is unchanged; the argument applies at every recorded coordinate and to every declared calibration box of clause (e), so no record obeying its declared conditions separates the pairs. [F2, step 1.1]

2.2 If $G\ne0$ and $\delta\ne0$ then the measured coordinates of the two parameter pairs differ: the source-strength coordinates $s+\delta$ and $s$ differ because $\delta\ne0$, and the background coordinates $b-G\delta$ and $b$ differ because $G\delta\ne0$; thus $(s+\delta,b-G\delta)\ne(s,b)$ in $\mathbb R^2$ while their predictions coincide by step 1.1, which is clause (ii). [F1, step 1.1]

2.3 The explicit instance of clause (iii) is the arithmetic evaluation $y(3,1)=2\cdot3+1=7$ and $y(4,-1)=2\cdot4-1=8-1=7$ at $G=2$, $s=3$, $b=1$ and $\delta=1$, where the displaced pair is $(s+\delta,b-G\delta)=(4,1-2)=(4,-1)$. [step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Consequently a comparison of a record with the affine model alone determines only the combination $Gs+b$: two parameter pairs $(s_1,b_1)$ and $(s_2,b_2)$ produce the same predictions at every recorded coordinate exactly when $Gs_1+b_1=Gs_2+b_2$, so with $G\ne0$ fixed the one-parameter family $\{(s+\delta,b-G\delta):\delta\in\mathbb R\}$ consists of distinct pairs with identical predictions, and separating its members requires an additional independent declaration fixing $b$ or fixing $s$, as clause (ii) states. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.2, given]

4.1 Clause (iv) records the status of the preceding steps: the identity is a deterministic algebraic statement about the declared affine response model, registered as the record's analysis assumption by clause (g) of [F2]; no apparatus property, historical value, dataset, sampling law or probability is asserted, and because agreement or discrepancy of a record with the model tests the conjunction of the model with its declared auxiliary parameters, attributing an outcome to a field or source premise requires the independent background or source-strength declarations identified in step 3.1. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.3, given] ∎

## Example

Adopt the two-beam data and conclusions of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]]:
the complex electric amplitude $\alpha(x)=a_1e_1+a_2e_2e^{i\delta(x)}$ and
magnetic amplitude $\beta(x)=a_1b_1+a_2b_2e^{i\delta(x)}$ of its clause (a),
with $\delta(x)=(k_2-k_1)\cdot x$, $b_j=k_j\times e_j/\omega$
([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) and the plane-wave solutions $(E_j,B_j)$ of
[[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]; and its clause (b) averaged energy density
$$\langle u\rangle(x)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{4}|\alpha(x)|^2+\frac{1}{4\mu_0}|\beta(x)|^2$$
with the SI constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) exactly as
inherited by the Lebesgue-measure and integral items cited in clause (ii),
which are stated under that hypothesis; no other choice principle is used.
Assume $a_1=a_2=:a>0$, $e_1=e_2=:e$ with real amplitude vector $e$, and
$k_1\ne k_2$ with $(k_2-k_1)\times e\ne0$; let $x_0$ be a point with
$\delta(x_0)\equiv\pi\pmod{2\pi}$.

(i) [Ideal prediction and its vanishing] At such $x_0$ one has
$\alpha(x_0)=ae(1+e^{i\delta(x_0)})=0$
([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]),
hence the electric field of the superposition vanishes at $x_0$ for every $t$
and the electric term of the averaged energy density vanishes there. The full
averaged energy density need not vanish:
$\beta(x_0)=a(b_1-b_2)=a\bigl((k_1-k_2)\times e\bigr)/\omega\ne0$, so
$\langle u\rangle(x_0)=|a(b_1-b_2)|^2/(4\mu_0)>0$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]] for the positive-definite norm). Thus a claim
that 'the ideal intensity vanishes at $x_0$' must name the quantity that
vanishes.

(ii) [Declared bin response and its finite-rate branch] Adopt a declared
detector model with a Lebesgue-measurable bin $W\subseteq\mathbb R^3$,
$x_0\in W$ and $\lambda_3(W)>0$, a finite real response coefficient
$\kappa\ge0$, and a declared nonnegative density $b:W\to[0,\infty)$ whose zero
extension $\tilde b$ (equal to $b$ on $W$ and to $0$ off $W$) is Lebesgue
measurable; this measurability of the zero extension is a declared hypothesis
of the detector model. The declared response functional is the nonnegative
Lebesgue integral
$$R(W):=\int_W\bigl(\kappa|\alpha(x)|^2+b(x)\bigr)\,d\lambda_3\in[0,+\infty].$$
Here the continuous real function $|\alpha|^2$ is Borel measurable by
[[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]] and Lebesgue measurable by
[[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]; closure under nonnegative scaling
and addition is supplied by
[[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]], and
[[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]] defines the extended integral. No
boundedness or finite-volume condition on $W$ is imposed. If
$\int_W b\,d\lambda_3>0$, monotonicity gives
$$R(W)\ge\int_W b\,d\lambda_3>0$$ even though $|\alpha(x_0)|^2=0$. For a
constant $b=b_0>0$ this lower bound is $b_0\lambda_3(W)$ by
[[def-integral-of-a-nonnegative-simple-function]],
[[prop-the-nonnegative-integral-agrees-with-the-simple-integral]] and
[[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]; it may be
$+\infty$. The *finite predicted rate* branch additionally requires
$R(W)<\infty$ and declared response units. A concrete sufficient case is
$0<\lambda_3(W)<\infty$ and constant $0<b_0<\infty$: the bound
$|\alpha|^2\le4a^2|e|^2$ gives
$$0<b_0\lambda_3(W)\le R(W)\le(4\kappa a^2|e|^2+b_0)\lambda_3(W)<\infty.$$
For $\kappa=0$ the field contribution is the zero function, without forming
$0\cdot(+\infty)$. Identifying a finite predicted response with a recorded
comparison quantity still requires the apparatus, calibration and analysis
declarations of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]]. Thus a finite positive
bin prediction is compatible with the ideal pointwise zero, but an extended
infinite response is not a recorded finite rate, and neither response is an
event probability.

(iii) [Record versus prediction; statistical qualification] The data of
[[def-em-experiment-record-contract]] are a finite tuple of real recorded
values or reported observations with declared conditions, calibration and
uncertainty. The predictions of (i)-(ii) are deterministic field quantities or
a declared extended response functional, with a finite real rate only on its
stated finite branch. Here an ideal fringe pattern describes spatial variation
of a specified intensity or response; a single detection and a finite data
tuple are separate records. Whether a finite record displays a specified
visibility or pattern requires a declared criterion, calibration, binning,
background and sampling assumptions, none supplied by the field calculation
alone. No sampling law, probability of failing a visibility criterion,
detection statistics or measured histogram is asserted. This example
discriminates no classical or quantum ontology: classical electromagnetic
waves interfere and the coherence calculation is a deterministic prediction of
the classical model.

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct substitution, the elementary periodicity of the
complex exponential phase, and the declared measure-theoretic interface.

**Given:** the two-beam data of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]] clauses
(a)-(b) with $a_1=a_2=a>0$, $e_1=e_2=e$, $k_1\ne k_2$,
$(k_2-k_1)\times e\ne0$ and a point $x_0$ with
$\delta(x_0)\equiv\pi\pmod{2\pi}$; the declared detector model of clause (ii)
with measurable bin $W\ni x_0$, $\lambda_3(W)>0$, $\kappa\ge0$ and
nonnegative density $b$ whose zero extension $\tilde b$ is Lebesgue
measurable; the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; the SI
constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

[F1] Clause (a) of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]] gives, at each fixed
$x$, $E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\alpha(x)\,e^{i(k_1\cdot x-\omega t)})$ and
$B(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\beta(x)\,e^{i(k_1\cdot x-\omega t)})$ with
$\alpha(x):=a_1e_1+a_2e_2e^{i\delta(x)}$,
$\beta(x):=a_1b_1+a_2b_2e^{i\delta(x)}$, $\delta(x):=(k_2-k_1)\cdot x$,
$b_j=k_j\times e_j/\omega$ and $\omega>0$.

[F2] Clause (b) of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]] gives
$\langle u\rangle(x)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{4}|\alpha(x)|^2+\frac{1}{4\mu_0}|\beta(x)|^2$
for every $x$.

[F3] For $u,v\in\mathbb R^3$, $u\times v=(u_yv_z-u_zv_y,\,u_zv_x-u_xv_z,\,u_xv_y-u_yv_x)$
([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]).

[F4] The Euclidean inner product is $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_{k<n}x_ky_k$ and
the Euclidean norm is $\lVert x\rVert_2=\sqrt{\langle x,x\rangle}$; the form
is positive definite: $\langle x,x\rangle\ge0$, and $\langle x,x\rangle=0$ if
and only if $x=0$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

[F5] For all $z,w\in\mathbb C$, $z\overline z=|z|^2$, $|z|\ge0$,
$|z|=0\Longleftrightarrow z=0$, $|zw|=|z||w|$ and $|z+w|\le|z|+|w|$

[F6] For real $x,y$ one has $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and

[F8] The framework's magnetic constant satisfies $\mu_0>0$
([[def-em-si-conventions]]).

[F9] The Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the statement that
every at most countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function
([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F10] A set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is Lebesgue measurable when
$\lambda_n^*(A)=\lambda_n^*(A\cap E)+\lambda_n^*(A\setminus E)$ for every
$A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, and $\lambda_n$ is the restriction of $\lambda_n^*$
to the family $\mathcal L(\mathbb R^n)$
([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]).

[F11] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $\mathcal L(\mathbb R^n)$ is a sigma-algebra
on $\mathbb R^n$ and $\lambda_n$ is a measure on it
([[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]], clause 1).

[F12] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, every continuous map
$f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is Borel measurable
([[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]).

[F13] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n)\subseteq\mathcal
L(\mathbb R^n)$: every Borel subset of $\mathbb R^n$ is Lebesgue measurable
([[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]).

[F14] For a measure space $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$, a measurable
$f:X\to[0,+\infty]$ and $E\in\mathcal A$, the integral over $E$ is
$\int_E f\,d\mu:=\int f\chi_E\,d\mu$
([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]).

[F15] If $f,g:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ are measurable and $f+g$ is defined
pointwise, then $f+g$ is measurable; if $c\in\mathbb R$ and $f:X\to\mathbb R$
is measurable, then $cf$ is measurable
([[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]]).

[F16] For measurable $f,g:X\to[0,+\infty]$ and $c\ge0$: if $f\le g$ then

and for $c=0$ the integral of the zero function is $0$
([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]).

[F17] A nonnegative simple measurable function $s=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\chi_{E_j}$

([[def-integral-of-a-nonnegative-simple-function]]).

[F18] If $s$ is a nonnegative simple measurable function, then its
nonnegative Lebesgue integral equals its simple integral,
$\int s\,d\mu=\int_{\mathrm{simple}}s\,d\mu$
([[prop-the-nonnegative-integral-agrees-with-the-simple-integral]]).

[F19] The complex exponential is entire, and $\exp'(z)=\exp z$ for every
$z\in\mathbb C$ ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]]).

[F20] If $f:U\to\mathbb C$ is complex differentiable at $a\in U$, then $f$ is
continuous at $a$ ([[cor-complex-differentiability-implies-continuity]]).

[F21] For $k\in\mathbb N$, finite componentwise sums and products of $C^k$
Euclidean maps are $C^k$, and a composite of composable $C^k$ Euclidean maps
is $C^k$
([[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]]).

[F22] In an ordered field, $a>0$ and $b>0$ imply $ab>0$
([[lem-of-sign-rules]]), and $\mathbb R$ is a totally ordered field
([[thm-reals-ordered-field]]).

[F23] A record of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]] is a finite tuple of
recorded data and reported observations with declared condition annotations,
and it contains no probability space, random variable, distribution, sampling
law, independence assumption, likelihood or coverage statement (clause (d)).

1.1 Since $\delta(x_0)\equiv\pi\pmod{2\pi}$, there is an integer $n$ with $\delta(x_0)=\pi+2\pi n$; the cartesian form of [F6] gives $e^{i\delta(x_0)}=\cos\delta(x_0)+i\sin\delta(x_0)$, and [F7] gives $\cos(y+2\pi)=-\cos(y+\pi)=\cos y$ and $\sin(y+2\pi)=-\sin(y+\pi)=\sin y$ for every real $y$, so by induction on $|n|$ one has $\cos(\pi+2\pi n)=\cos\pi=-1$ and $\sin(\pi+2\pi n)=\sin\pi=0$; hence $e^{i\delta(x_0)}=-1$. 1.2 [Regularity of $\alpha$] The phase $x\mapsto\delta(x)=(k_2-k_1)\cdot x$ is an affine map $\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$, hence of class $C^\infty$; the exponential is entire [F19], hence complex differentiable everywhere and continuous [F20]; by the algebra-and-composition closure of [F21] the composite $x\mapsto e^{i\delta(x)}$ and the finite combinations defining the components of $\alpha=a_1e_1+a_2e_2e^{i\delta(x)}$ of [F1] are continuous, and the modulus squared $|\alpha|^2=\alpha\cdot\overline\alpha$ [F5] is a finite sum of products of continuous real functions, hence continuous on $\mathbb R^3$. [F1, F4, F5, F19, F20, F21, algebra]

1.3 [Constant background] For a constant $b=b_0>0$ the zero extension is the nonnegative simple function $\tilde b=b_0\chi_W$ with $W\in\mathcal L(\mathbb R^3)$ [F10, F11]; its simple integral is $b_0\lambda_3(W)$ by [F17] and equals its Lebesgue integral by [F18], so $\int_W b\,d\lambda_3=b_0\lambda_3(W)$ by [F14], a value in $(0,+\infty]$ that may be $+\infty$ when $\lambda_3(W)=+\infty$. [F9, F10, F11, F14, F17, F18, given, algebra]

1.4 [Zero response coefficient] For $\kappa=0$ the field contribution is the zero function because $|\alpha|^2$ is real-valued, so no product $0\cdot(+\infty)$ is formed; then $\int_W\kappa|\alpha|^2\,d\lambda_3=0$ by the $c=0$ clause of [F16], and $R(W)=\int_W b\,d\lambda_3$; in particular the response remains defined in $[0,+\infty]$ on every measurable bin. [F14, F16, given, algebra]

2.1 Substituting the amplitude data of [F1] and step 1.1 gives $\alpha(x_0)=a_1e_1+a_2e_2e^{i\delta(x_0)}=ae\,(1+(-1))=0$, using $a_1=a_2=a$ and $e_1=e_2=e$. [F1, step 1.1, given, algebra]

2.2 For $\beta(x_0)$: substituting $a_1=a_2=a$, $e_1=e_2=e$ and step 1.1 into [F1] gives $\beta(x_0)=a(b_1-b_2)$, and $b_1-b_2=k_1\times e/\omega-k_2\times e/\omega=\bigl((k_1-k_2)\times e\bigr)/\omega$ by the coordinate bilinearity of [F3]; if $\beta(x_0)=0$ then multiplying by the nonzero scalar $\omega/a$ (nonzero because $a>0$ and $\omega>0$ from [F1]) gives $(k_1-k_2)\times e=-(k_2-k_1)\times e=0$ by [F3], contrary to the hypothesis $(k_2-k_1)\times e\ne0$; hence $\beta(x_0)\ne0$. [F1, F3, given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.3 [Integrand measurability and the response functional] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ the family $\mathcal L(\mathbb R^3)$ is a sigma-algebra and $\lambda_3$ a measure on it [F11], and the bin $W$ is measurable with $\lambda_3(W)$ defined [F10]; $|\alpha|^2$ is continuous by step 1.2, hence Borel measurable [F12] and Lebesgue measurable [F13]; since $\kappa\in\mathbb R$, the scaled function $\kappa|\alpha|^2$ is measurable by [F15], and the sum $\kappa|\alpha|^2+\tilde b$ is measurable by [F15] because $\tilde b$ is real-valued and measurable by the declared detector model; consequently [F14] defines $R(W):=\int_W(\kappa|\alpha|^2+b)\,d\lambda_3=\int(\kappa|\alpha|^2+\tilde b)\chi_W\,d\lambda_3\in[0,+\infty]$. [F9, F10, F11, F12, F13, F14, F15, step 1.2, given, algebra]

2.4 [Finite-rate branch] Suppose $0<\lambda_3(W)<\infty$ and $0<b_0<\infty$. For every $x$ one has $|e^{i\delta(x)}|=1$ by [F6], so $|1+e^{i\delta(x)}|\le1+|e^{i\delta(x)}|=2$ by the triangle inequality of [F5], and $|\alpha(x)|=|a|\,|e|\,|1+e^{i\delta(x)}|\le2a|e|$ by the multiplicative law of [F5], where $|e|^2=\langle e,e\rangle$ is the Euclidean squared norm of the real amplitude [F4]; hence $|\alpha|^2\le4a^2|e|^2$ and, since $\kappa\ge0$, the pointwise bounds $b_0\chi_W\le(\kappa|\alpha|^2+b_0)\chi_W\le C\chi_W$ hold with the finite real constant $C:=4\kappa a^2|e|^2+b_0$. Monotonicity and the simple-integral values of step 1.3 and [F17], [F18] give $0<b_0\lambda_3(W)\le R(W)\le C\lambda_3(W)<\infty$, the strict lower bound by the sign rule $b_0\lambda_3(W)>0$ of [F22] applied to $b_0>0$ and $\lambda_3(W)>0$; thus on this branch $R(W)$ is a finite positive rate. [F1, F4, F5, F6, F14, F15, F16, F17, F18, F22, given, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 By clause (a) of [F1], $E(x_0,t)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\alpha(x_0)\,e^{i(k_1\cdot x_0-\omega t)}\bigr)=\operatorname{Re}(0)=0$ for every real $t$; hence the electric field of the superposition vanishes at $x_0$ at every time, and with step 2.1 the electric term $\frac{\varepsilon_0}{4}|\alpha(x_0)|^2$ of the averaged density of [F2] vanishes there. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 [F2] and step 2.1 give $\langle u\rangle(x_0)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{4}|\alpha(x_0)|^2+\frac{1}{4\mu_0}|\beta(x_0)|^2=\frac{1}{4\mu_0}|\beta(x_0)|^2$; since $\beta(x_0)\ne0$ by step 2.2, positive definiteness [F4] and the modulus law $|z|=0\Longleftrightarrow z=0$ of [F5] give $|\beta(x_0)|^2>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ from [F8] gives $1/(4\mu_0)>0$, so the sign rules [F22] yield $\langle u\rangle(x_0)>0$; thus the full averaged energy density does not vanish at $x_0$, only its electric term does. [F2, F4, F5, F8, F22, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

3.3 [General background lower bound] The functions $\tilde b$ and $\kappa|\alpha|^2+\tilde b$ are measurable, nonnegative and finite-valued, with $\tilde b\le\kappa|\alpha|^2+\tilde b$ pointwise because $|\alpha|^2\ge0$ [F5] and $\kappa\ge0$; the monotonicity clause of [F16] and $R(W)=\int(\kappa|\alpha|^2+\tilde b)\chi_W\,d\lambda_3$ of step 2.3 give $\int_W b\,d\lambda_3=\int\tilde b\chi_W\,d\lambda_3\le R(W)$, so $\int_W b\,d\lambda_3>0$ implies $R(W)\ge\int_W b\,d\lambda_3>0$ even though $|\alpha(x_0)|^2=0$ by step 2.1. [F14, F15, F16, step 2.1, step 2.3, algebra]

4.1 [Record versus prediction] The data of [F23] are finite tuples of recorded values or reported observations with declared conditions, calibration and uncertainty, and contain no sampling law; the predictions of steps 1.1-3.3 are deterministic field quantities or a declared extended response functional with a finite real rate only on the branch of step 2.4; a detection and a finite record are different objects from the ideal intensity, so no sampling law, probability of failing a visibility criterion, detection statistics or measured histogram is asserted here, and the finite positive bin prediction of step 2.4 is compatible with the pointwise ideal zero of steps 2.1 and 3.1 without discriminating the classical and quantum descriptions of light, since classical electromagnetic waves interfere. [F23, F1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.3, step 3.3, step 2.4, given] ∎

## Definition

The laboratory region, its restricted inertial chart $x$ with coordinates
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, $x^0=ct$, the spatial slices and the fixed-time
laboratory fields are those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; the field components,
the Minkowski form $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the potential
dictionary and the index conventions are those of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]; the source fields, the charge parameter and
the four-current convention $j=(c\rho,J)$ are those of [[def-em-sources]];
the units and the constants $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$,
$\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; and
worldlines, four-velocities and proper times are those of
[[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]. For the field sector (a)-(b) assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$,
[[def-countable-choice]]) exactly as inherited from
[[lem-em-compact-field-variation]], whose functional and finiteness statement
this item instantiates; the definition uses no further choice. The
finite-interval Riemann particle sector (c) uses the choice-free curve lemma
and does not require that field-sector measure convention.

(a) [Field action] Let
$U\subseteq x(\text{laboratory region})=cI\times\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$
be a nonempty bounded open set whose closure is a
compact subset of that chart image, let $N\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be an open
neighbourhood of $\overline U$, and let $A:N\to\mathbb R^4$,
$x\mapsto(A^0,A^1,A^2,A^3)$, and $j:N\to\mathbb R^4$ be smooth
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); $A$ is a four-potential in
the sense of clause (c) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and $j=(c\rho,J)$
is the four-current of [[def-em-sources]]. Write $A_\nu:=\eta_{\nu\mu}A^\mu$,
$F_{\mu\nu}:=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$,
$F^{\mu\nu}:=\eta^{\mu\alpha}\eta^{\nu\beta}F_{\alpha\beta}$ and $j^\nu A_\nu$
for the indicated contraction, with $\partial_\mu$ the coordinate partial
derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and define the
**field action** by

$$S[A]:=c^{-1}\int_U\Bigl[-\frac{1}{4\mu_0}F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}+j^\nu A_\nu\Bigr]d\lambda,$$

$d\lambda$ the four-dimensional Lebesgue measure in the chart coordinates, the
integral being that of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. Then $S[A]$ is
a finite real number, in units of $\mathrm{J\,s}$: the density
$-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}+j^\nu A_\nu$ carries
$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $d\lambda$ carries $\mathrm{m^4}$ and $c^{-1}$ carries
$\mathrm{s\,m^{-1}}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). With $\kappa:=\mu_0$,
$J:=j$ and the same bounded open $U$, one has $S[A]=c^{-1}S_{\rm math}[A]$,
where $S_{\rm math}$ is the real functional of
[[lem-em-compact-field-variation]]; since $c^{-1}>0$, the first variation and
the stationarity of $S$ at $A$ are exactly those recorded there.

(b) [Admissible field variations] The field variations are the real maps
$h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$, the real subspace of the test space of
[[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], extended by zero to $N$; for
every real $s$ the field $A+sh$ is smooth on $N$, and $s\mapsto S[A+sh]$ is
the quadratic polynomial of clause (a) of
[[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] with both coefficients multiplied by
$c^{-1}$. The field $A$ is **stationary** for $S$ if
$\frac{d}{ds}\big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=0$ for every such $h$.

(c) [Particle functional] Let $m>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-sources]]
(a)), let $[a,b]$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, let $X:[a,b]\to A$ be a
$C^2$ future timelike massive worldline ([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]
(a)), and let $A_\mu$ be a $C^2$ covector field on a neighbourhood of the
image of $X$. The **particle functional** is the one of
[[lem-em-particle-curve-variation]],

$$S_{\rm pt}[X]:=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}\,ds+q\int_a^bA_\mu(X)\dot X^\mu\,ds,$$

with admissible variations the fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations
$h:[a,b]\to V$, $h(a)=h(b)=0$, of that lemma; $m$ is the external rest-mass
parameter and $q$ the charge parameter of the framework, and $S_{\rm pt}$ is a
finite real number on the declared class, both summands being finite-interval
Riemann integrals of continuous functions on the compact $[a,b]$: the
radicand $-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)$ is continuous and strictly positive, and
$s\mapsto A_\mu(X(s))\dot X^\mu(s)$ is continuous because $X$ and $A_\mu$ are
$C^2$.

(d) [Scope] This item defines only the two functionals, their variation
classes and the stationarity predicate; it asserts no stationarity of any
configuration, no existence or uniqueness of stationary fields or curves, no
boundary conditions, no convergence statement for unbounded regions, no
coupled particle-field action and no dynamics of singular sources. Smooth $A$
and $j$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline U$ are required, and point or sheet
sources are excluded ([[def-em-sources]] (b)). The physical adoption of
stationarity is the postulate recorded later on this page
([[post-em-stationary-action-model]]).

## Source notes

The action density $-(1/4)F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}$ with the source coupling
$j^\nu A_\nu$ and the expansion to
$\varepsilon_0|E|^2/2-|B|^2/(2\mu_0)$ follow Tong §5.5.3 and Binney §§3.2, 3.6,
in each case converted to the framework's $(-,+,+,+)$ dictionary, SI constants
and $j=(c\rho,J)$; the particle functional $-mc\int\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}
\,ds+q\int A_\mu(X)\dot X^\mu\,ds$ follows Tong §5.5.1–§5.5.2, Landau–Lifshitz
§16 and Binney §3.1 with the Gaussian-unit forms re-expressed in the same
dictionary. The finite-region scheme with variations vanishing on the boundary
is Binney §3.2; the exact normalisation $c^{-1}$ and the units $\mathrm{J\,s}$
are the framework's own bookkeeping, and the well-definedness statements are
those of the two cited mathematical suppliers.

## Postulate

Adopt as a physical formulation principle of this framework, as an alternative
to postulating the field equations and the force law directly, the following
assumption about the functionals, variation classes and stationarity predicate
of [[def-em-field-action-definition]].

(i) [Field sector] A smooth field $A:N\to\mathbb R^4$ on the region $U$ of
clause (a) of that definition is dynamically admissible exactly when it is
stationary for the field action $S[A]$ under all compactly supported smooth
variations $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ in the sense of clause (b) of that
definition: $\frac{d}{ds}\big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=0$ for every such $h$.

(ii) [Particle sector] For a prescribed external four-potential $A_\mu$ on a
neighbourhood of the image of a $C^2$ future timelike massive worldline $X$,
the motion is dynamically admissible exactly when $X$ is stationary for the
particle functional $S_{\rm pt}$ of clause (c) of that definition under all
fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations.

This is an adopted assumption of the model, not a theorem, not a derivation
from the remaining postulates and not an empirical result. It asserts
stationarity only: it does not assert that a stationary configuration is a
local or global minimum, that stationary configurations exist or are unique,
that the action functional is uniquely determined or forced by symmetry, that
no other action formulation is possible, or that the two sectors can be
coupled into a single well-posed action for singular sources. No Noether
theorem, no symmetry-to-conservation machinery and no matter dynamics beyond
the prescribed potential are assumed.

The conditional deductions of this pair are: on the declared smooth classes,
(i) is equivalent to the inhomogeneous tensor field equation
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ and, for potential-represented fields, to
the smooth-branch Maxwell equations, and (ii) is equivalent to the framework's
adopted four-force equation $m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$; both deductions are
recorded separately on this page and in
[[pthm-em-action-maxwell-variation]] and
[[pthm-em-particle-action-coupling]], and this postulate asserts neither.

## Source notes

The cited treatments present the action principle of classical
electrodynamics as adopted, not derived: Tong §5.5 introduces the action and
obtains the field equations from its variation, and Landau–Lifshitz §16 states
in the footnote on p. 44 that the form of the interaction term cannot be fixed
on general considerations alone. The Gaussian-unit expressions of the
monograph are read only for the structure of the principle; the functionals
adopted here are exactly the SI functionals of
[[def-em-field-action-definition]]. No measurement, no empirical claim and no
uniqueness of the formulation is contained in this item.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$,
[[def-countable-choice]]), inherited through the componentwise
fundamental-variation step of [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]] and
through [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]. Let
$U,N,A,j,F,S$ and the constants $c,\mu_0,\varepsilon_0$ be as in clauses (a)-(b)
of [[def-em-field-action-definition]]: $U$ bounded open with $\overline U$
compact in the laboratory chart image $cI\times\Omega$, $N$ an open
neighbourhood of $\overline U$, $A$ and $j$ smooth on $N$,
$F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$, $j=(c\rho,J)$ with the
source fields of [[def-em-sources]], and
$S[A]=c^{-1}\int_U\bigl[-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}+j^\nu A_\nu\bigr]d\lambda$.
For $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ write $\partial^\sharp\chi$ for the
vector field with contravariant components
$(\partial^\sharp\chi)^\mu:=\partial^\mu\chi=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu\chi$
([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]],
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). It is a compactly supported
smooth field variation. Thus $A^\mu\mapsto A^\mu+\partial^\mu\chi$ lowers to
$A_\nu\mapsto A_\nu+\partial_\nu\chi$; $A+\partial^\sharp\chi$ denotes this
vector addition.

(a) [Exact gauge difference, no boundary term] For every such $\chi$ one has
$F_{\mu\nu}(A+\partial^\sharp\chi)=F_{\mu\nu}(A)$ on $U$, because
$\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\chi-\partial_\nu\partial_\mu\chi=0$ for the smooth
$\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]); consequently the field term
of $S$ is unchanged and

$$S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]-S[A]=c^{-1}\int_Uj^\mu\,\partial_\mu\chi\,d\lambda=-c^{-1}\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\,\chi\,d\lambda,$$

the second equality being the distributional integration-by-parts identity for
the locally integrable fields $j^\mu$ and the smooth compactly supported
$\chi$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]],
[[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]); no
boundary term arises precisely because $\chi$ is compactly supported in $U$.

(b) [Equivalence for smooth sources] If $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ on $U$ (the
source is conserved), then $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every
$\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$. Conversely, if
$S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every such $\chi$, then
$\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ pointwise on $U$: the function $\partial_\mu j^\mu$ is
continuous on the open $U$ and pairs to zero against every compactly supported
smooth $\chi$, so [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]] applies. Hence for
smooth prescribed sources the invariance of the field action under all compact
gauge variations is equivalent to the conservation of the four-current.

(c) [Maxwell-compatible sources] Suppose in addition that the field pair
$(E,B)$ represented by $A$ through the potential dictionary of clause (c) of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and the source fields $(\rho,J)$ satisfy the
smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell equations on $U$ (equivalently, by clause
(a) of [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]], the tensor system
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ together with the cyclic identity). Then
clause (a) of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives
$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ on $U$
([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), which in the chart reads
$\partial_\mu j^\mu=\partial_0(c\rho)+\operatorname{div}J=c^{-1}\partial_t(c\rho)+\operatorname{div}J=0$;
hence $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every compact gauge variation.

(d) [Distributional reading] If $j^\mu$ is a distribution on $U$
([[def-distribution]]), the gauge-difference pairing
$c^{-1}\langle j^\mu,\partial_\mu\chi\rangle$ is defined for every test
function $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ and equals
$-c^{-1}\langle\partial_\mu j^\mu,\chi\rangle$ by the signed definition of the
distributional derivative; hence the pairing vanishes for every compact gauge
variation if and only if $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ as a distribution. This is a
statement about the pairing only: the smooth $j$ of the definition is retained
whenever the functional $S$ itself is used, and no products of distributions
are formed.

Scope: the item computes the gauge variation of the field action and its
compatibility with source conservation; it does not derive the field equations
from gauge invariance, does not assert that conservation of a source implies
stationarity, does not treat global or topological obstructions, and uses no
Noether machinery.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Axiom of Countable Choice; the bounded open
$U\subseteq cI\times\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact in the chart image, the
open neighbourhood $N$, and the smooth $A,j:N\to\mathbb R^4$ of the
field-action definition; the source convention $j=(c\rho,J)$; the compactly
supported smooth gauge direction $\partial^\sharp\chi$ of $\chi\in
C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$; and the pairing framework of the distributions on
$U$.

[F1] The field action is
$S[A]=c^{-1}\int_U\bigl[-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}+j^\nu A_\nu\bigr]d\lambda$
with $F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$,
$F^{\mu\nu}=\eta^{\mu\alpha}\eta^{\nu\beta}F_{\alpha\beta}$ and the admissible
variations $C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ ([[def-em-field-action-definition]]).

[F2] The test space $\mathcal D(U)=C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb C)$ consists of smooth
functions whose support is a compact subset of $U$, and all constructions may
be restricted to real scalars ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]).

[F3] Coordinate partial derivatives $\partial_\mu$ are the directional
derivatives in the standard directions
([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]).

[F4] The component dictionary of the electromagnetic two-form fixes
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$,
$F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ and $F_{ab}=-F_{ba}$
([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a)).

[F5] If $f$ is $C^2$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$, then
$\partial_i\partial_jf=\partial_j\partial_if$ for every pair of coordinate
indices ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]).

[F6] The Lebesgue integral is linear on $L^1$
([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]).

[F7] For open $\Omega$, a locally integrable $f$ has the regular functional
$\langle u_f,\varphi\rangle=\int_\Omega f\varphi\,dx$
([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]).

[F8] Distributional derivatives commute and, assuming Countable Choice, if
$f\in C^k$ then $\partial^\alpha u_f=u_{\partial^\alpha f}$: distributional
differentiation extends classical smooth differentiation
([[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]).

[F9] Distributional derivatives are defined by
$\langle\partial^\alpha u,\varphi\rangle=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\langle u,\partial^\alpha\varphi\rangle$
([[def-distributional-derivative]]).

[F10] If a continuous $g:U\to\mathbb R^m$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$
satisfies $\int_U\langle g,k\rangle\,d\lambda=0$ for every
$k\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^m)$, then $g=0$ on $U$
([[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]]).

[F11] Clause (a) of the charge-continuity theorem states that for jointly $C^2$
fields and $C^1$ sources satisfying the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell
equations, the continuity equation
$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ holds pointwise
([[pthm-em-charge-continuity]]).

[F12] The four-current convention is $j=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and
$j^i=J^i$ ([[def-em-sources]]).

[F13] The divergence is
$\operatorname{div}J=\partial_1J_1+\partial_2J_2+\partial_3J_3$ for a $C^1$
vector field $J$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]).

[F14] The laboratory chart has $x^0=ct$
([[def-em-lab-geometry]]).

[F15] Clause (a) of the tensor-equivalence theorem states that the four
smooth-branch laboratory equations hold if and only if
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ together with the cyclic identity hold for
the fixed component dictionary ([[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]).

[F16] A distribution on an open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is a continuous
complex-linear map $u:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathbb C$, with the pairing linear
in both arguments ([[def-distribution]]).

[F17] Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the statement that every
sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; the gauge direction is an admissible compact
variation, the field term is invariant by the commuting mixed partials of
$\chi$, and the source term is evaluated first as an integral and then through
the signed distributional pairing.

1.1 For $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ the components $(\partial^\sharp\chi)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu\chi$ are smooth on $U$ by [F4] and [F3], and their support is contained in the compact set $\operatorname{supp}\chi\subseteq U$ by [F2], so $\partial^\sharp\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ is an admissible field variation of [F1]; moreover $\eta_{\nu\mu}\eta^{\mu\alpha}=\delta_\nu^\alpha$ for $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ by [F4], so lowering gives $(A+\partial^\sharp\chi)_\nu=A_\nu+\partial_\nu\chi$. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4]

2.1 Since $\chi$ is smooth, hence $C^2$, [F5] gives $\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\chi=\partial_\nu\partial_\mu\chi$ on $U$; therefore $F_{\mu\nu}(A+\partial^\sharp\chi)=\partial_\mu(A_\nu+\partial_\nu\chi)-\partial_\nu(A_\mu+\partial_\mu\chi)=F_{\mu\nu}(A)+\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\chi-\partial_\nu\partial_\mu\chi=F_{\mu\nu}(A)$ on $U$ by step 1.1 and [F1], so the quadratic field term of $S$ is unchanged along the gauge path. [step 1.1, F1, F4, F5]

3.1 Because the field term is unchanged by step 2.1, the difference of the functionals is the difference of the source terms, and linearity [F6] of the integral gives $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]-S[A]=c^{-1}\int_Uj^\nu\bigl((A+\partial^\sharp\chi)_\nu-A_\nu\bigr)d\lambda=c^{-1}\int_Uj^\mu\partial_\mu\chi\,d\lambda$ by step 1.1; the integrand is smooth and compactly supported in $U$, so the integral is finite. [step 2.1, F1, F6]

4.1 Each $j^\mu$ is smooth, hence locally integrable, with regular distribution $\langle u_{j^\mu},\varphi\rangle=\int_Uj^\mu\varphi\,d\lambda$ by [F7]; the signed definition [F9] gives $\langle\partial_\mu j^\mu,\chi\rangle=-\langle j^\mu,\partial_\mu\chi\rangle$, and [F8] identifies the distributional derivative of $j^\mu$ with the classical one, so $\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\chi\,d\lambda=-\int_Uj^\mu\partial_\mu\chi\,d\lambda$ componentwise for every $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$; substituting into step 3.1 gives $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]-S[A]=-c^{-1}\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\chi\,d\lambda$, with no boundary term because $\chi$ is compactly supported in $U$ by [F2]. This is clause (a). [step 3.1, F2, F7, F8, F9, algebra]

5.1 If $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ on $U$, the identity of step 4.1 gives $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$, which is the forward direction of clause (b). [step 4.1]

6.1 Conversely, suppose $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$; by step 4.1 the continuous function $g:=\partial_\mu j^\mu$ on the open $U$ (sum of the smooth derivatives $\partial_\mu j^\mu$) satisfies $\int_Ug\chi\,d\lambda=0$ for every $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$, so [F10] with $m=1$ gives $g=0$ on $U$, that is $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ pointwise; hence compact-gauge invariance and conservation are equivalent for smooth sources, which is clause (b). [step 5.1, F10, algebra]

7.1 Under the additional hypothesis of clause (c), the represented fields and sources lie in the class of [F11], so $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ holds pointwise on $U$; in the chart $x^0=ct$ of [F14] the four-current identity reads $\partial_\mu j^\mu=\partial_0j^0+\partial_iJ^i=c^{-1}\partial_t(c\rho)+\operatorname{div}J=\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ by [F12] and [F13], where the equivalence of the Maxwell hypothesis with the tensor system is [F15]; step 6.1 then gives $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every compact gauge variation, as asserted in clause (c). [step 6.1, F11, F12, F13, F14, F15, algebra]

8.1 If $j^\mu$ is a distribution on $U$ in the sense of [F16], the signed definition [F9] applied coordinatewise gives $\langle j^\mu,\partial_\mu\chi\rangle=-\langle\partial_\mu j^\mu,\chi\rangle$ for every test function $\chi$, so the gauge-difference pairing $c^{-1}\sum_\mu\langle j^\mu,\partial_\mu\chi\rangle$ equals $-c^{-1}\langle\partial_\mu j^\mu,\chi\rangle$ and vanishes for every compact gauge variation exactly when the distribution $\partial_\mu j^\mu$ is zero, which is clause (d); no product of distributions is formed, and whenever the functional $S$ of step 3.1 is used the smooth $j$ of [F1] is retained, while the only choice assumption is the inherited Countable Choice of [F17]. [given, step 4.1, F2, F9, F16, F17] ∎

## Source notes

The gauge-shift computation is Tong §5.5.3 (printed pp. 125-126), which
computes $S\to S-\tfrac1c\int\chi\,\partial_\mu J^\mu$ and reads invariance as
$\partial_\mu J^\mu=0$; Landau–Lifshitz §§28-29 and Binney §§3.6-3.7 supply the
four-current, continuity and interaction-term context. The exact boundary-free
formulation here uses the framework's own compact-support hypothesis and the
published distribution interface; the converse direction replaces the
sources' informal 'arbitrary gauge direction at a point' step by the
fundamental variation lemma, and no Noether formalism is adopted.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$,
[[def-countable-choice]]), inherited from
[[lem-em-compact-field-variation]]. Let $U\subseteq cI\times\Omega$, $N$, the
smooth fields $A,j$ on $N$, the components $A_\nu$,
$F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$, $F^{\mu\nu}$, the source
convention $j=(c\rho,J)$, the constants $c,\mu_0,\varepsilon_0$ and the field
action $S[A]=c^{-1}\int_U\bigl[-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}+j^\nu A_\nu\bigr]d\lambda$
be as in clauses (a)-(b) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] with the units
of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

Then the following are equivalent: (i) $A$ is stationary for $S$ under all
$h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$, i.e. the adopted field equation of
[[post-em-stationary-action-model]] (i); (ii)
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ at every point of $U$ for every
$\nu\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

Consequently, if $A$ is stationary then:

(a) [Inhomogeneous tensor equations] $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0 j^\nu$ on
$U$;

(b) [Homogeneous tensor equations]
$\partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu}=0$
on $U$, since $A$ is smooth and its mixed partial derivatives commute;

(c) [Laboratory Maxwell equations] define $\varphi:=-cA_0$, the spatial
potential vector $\mathbf A:=(A_1,A_2,A_3)$,
$E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_t\mathbf A$ and
$B:=\operatorname{curl}\mathbf A$ by clause (c) of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and $(\rho,J)$ by $j=(c\rho,J)$
([[def-em-sources]]); then on $U$ the four smooth-branch Maxwell equations
hold, equivalently the eight scalar equations (TM1)-(TM2) of
[[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] hold with these fields and sources,
i.e. $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$,
$\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and
$\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$.

The statement concerns a given smooth pair $(A,j)$ on the declared region: it
asserts no existence of a stationary field, imposes no boundary or decay
condition, and excludes the weak, distributional, singular-support and
non-potential-represented branches. The equivalence is conditional on the
adopted stationary-action postulate and makes no empirical claim.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; the bounded open
$U\subseteq cI\times\Omega$ with closure compact in the chart image, the open
neighbourhood $N$ of $\overline U$, and the smooth maps $A,j:N\to\mathbb R^4$
of the field-action definition; the component and potential dictionaries of
the electromagnetic two-form; the source convention $j=(c\rho,J)$; the
constants $c,\mu_0>0$ and $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$; and the
field-action functional $S$ with its compact-variation stationarity predicate.

[F1] The field-action definition fixes
$$S[A]=c^{-1}\int_U\Bigl[-\frac{1}{4\mu_0}F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}+j^\nu A_\nu\Bigr]d\lambda$$
with $F_{\mu\nu}:=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$,
$F^{\mu\nu}:=\eta^{\mu\alpha}\eta^{\nu\beta}F_{\alpha\beta}$,
$A_\nu:=\eta_{\nu\mu}A^\mu$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ on
$N\supseteq\overline U$, its admissible field variations
$h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$, the quadratic expansion along $A+sh$, and
the stationarity predicate; it identifies $S[A]=c^{-1}S_{\rm math}[A]$ at
$\kappa=\mu_0$, $J=j$ ([[def-em-field-action-definition]]).

[F2] The compact-variation lemma states (clause (c)) that for bounded open
$U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, $N\supseteq\overline U$ open, $\kappa>0$ and smooth
$A,J:N\to V=\mathbb R^4$, the field $A$ is stationary for its functional
$S_{\rm math}$ under all $h\in C_c^\infty(U;V)$ if and only if
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\kappa J^\nu$ for every $\nu$ on $U$, all
derivatives being classical partial derivatives of the smooth field
([[lem-em-compact-field-variation]]).

[F3] Clause (a) of the tensor-equivalence theorem states that, for jointly
$C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation
existing and continuously, continuous sources, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$,
$F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $j=(c\rho,J)$ and
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, the four smooth-branch equations hold if and
only if the systems
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ and
$\partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu}=0$
hold ([[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]).

[F4] The component dictionary of the electromagnetic two-form is
$F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$,
$F^{i0}=-E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, with
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a)).

[F5] The potential dictionary of the same definition states that if a
$C^1$ covector field $A_\mu$ on $U$ satisfies
$F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$, then $E,B$ recovered from
$F$ by the component dictionary obey $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and
$B=\operatorname{curl}A$ with $\varphi:=-cA_0$ and
$A:=(A_1,A_2,A_3)$ ([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (c)).

[F6] The four-current convention is $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and
$j^i=J^i$, with the charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ and smooth source fields
of the framework ([[def-em-sources]]).

[F7] The electric constant is
$\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, so that $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$
([[def-em-si-conventions]]).

[F8] If $f$ is $C^2$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$, then
$\partial_i\partial_jf=\partial_j\partial_if$ for every pair of coordinate
indices ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]).

[F9] Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the statement that every
sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function
([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F10] The adopted field equation of the stationary-action postulate states
that a smooth field $A:N\to\mathbb R^4$ on $U$ is dynamically admissible
exactly when it is stationary for the field action $S[A]$ under all
$h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ ([[post-em-stationary-action-model]] (i)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; identify the physical functional with the
mathematical functional of the compact-variation lemma at $\kappa=\mu_0$,
$J=j$, transport the stationarity equivalence along the positive factor
$c^{-1}$, then translate the two tensor systems into the laboratory equations
through the fixed component dictionary.

1.1 The data of [F1] meet the hypotheses of [F2] at $\kappa:=\mu_0$ and $J:=j$: $U$ is a bounded open subset of $\mathbb R^4$ whose closure is a compact subset of the chart image, $N$ is an open neighbourhood of $\overline U$, $\mu_0>0$ by [F7], and $A,j$ are smooth on $N$; the integrand of [F1] is term-by-term the integrand of [F2] at these parameters, so $S[A]=c^{-1}S_{\rm math}[A]$ and both integrals are finite real numbers by the finiteness clause of [F2]. [given, F1, F2, F7]

2.1 Fix $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$. Clause (a) of [F2] presents $s\mapsto S_{\rm math}[A+sh]=a_0+a_1s+a_2s^2$ with finite real coefficients $a_0=S_{\rm math}[A]$, $a_1=\int_U\bigl(-\mu_0^{-1}F^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu h_\nu+j^\nu h_\nu\bigr)d\lambda$ and $a_2=\int_U\ell_2\,d\lambda$, hence step 1.1 gives $S[A+sh]=c^{-1}a_0+c^{-1}a_1s+c^{-1}a_2s^2$; in particular the first variation of $S$ at $A$ in the direction $h$ is $c^{-1}a_1$, the first variation of $S_{\rm math}$ multiplied by $c^{-1}>0$. [step 1.1, F1, F2]

2.2 Because $A$ is smooth on the open $N\supseteq U$, every second partial derivative $\partial_\lambda\partial_\mu A_\nu$ exists and is continuous on $U$, so [F8] applies: expanding $F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$ from [F1] gives $\partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu}=(\partial_\lambda\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\lambda\partial_\nu A_\mu)+(\partial_\mu\partial_\nu A_\lambda-\partial_\mu\partial_\lambda A_\nu)+(\partial_\nu\partial_\lambda A_\mu-\partial_\nu\partial_\mu A_\lambda)=0$ on $U$, the six terms cancelling in three commuting pairs. This is clause (b). [step 1.1, F1, F8]

3.1 Since $c^{-1}>0$, one has $c^{-1}a_1=0$ exactly when $a_1=0$; as $h$ was an arbitrary element of $C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ and the two variation classes coincide by [F1] and [F2], the field $A$ is stationary for $S$ in the sense of clause (b) of [F1] if and only if $A$ is stationary for $S_{\rm math}$ in the sense of [F2]. [step 2.1, F1, F2]

4.1 Applying clause (c) of [F2] with $\kappa=\mu_0$, $J=j$ and the field $A$ of step 1.1, the field $A$ is stationary for $S_{\rm math}$ if and only if $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ on $U$ for every $\nu\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, the derivatives being classical partial derivatives of the smooth $A$ by [F2]; combined with step 3.1 this proves (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(ii), and it uses $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [F9] exactly through the cited lemma. [step 3.1, F1, F2, F9]

5.1 If $A$ is stationary, then (ii) holds by the equivalence of step 4.1; that consequent statement is clause (a). [step 4.1, given]

6.1 Put $\varphi:=-cA_0$, $\mathbf A:=(A_1,A_2,A_3)$, $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_t\mathbf A$ and $B:=\operatorname{curl}\mathbf A$. Since $A_\mu$ is the lowering of the smooth $A^\mu$ and satisfies $F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$ by [F1], clause (c) of the potential dictionary [F5] identifies these $E,B$ with the fields whose component dictionary [F4] reproduces the same $F_{\mu\nu}$ and $F^{\mu\nu}$; the sources $\rho,J$ satisfy $j=(c\rho,J)$ by [F6], and $E,B$ are smooth and $\rho,J$ continuous on $U$. The source convention and the constant identity $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [F7] place these data in the class of [F3]; the tensor system (TM1) holds by step 5.1 and the cyclic identity (TM2) by step 2.2, since the equivalence of clause (a) of [F3] is a pointwise component statement it restricts from the laboratory region to the open subset $U$, so that clause yields the four smooth-branch equations $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ on $U$, equivalently the eight scalar equations identified there. 7.1 The argument used exactly the smooth class, the fixed component dictionary, the identification $S=c^{-1}S_{\rm math}$ and the positive factor $c^{-1}$; it asserted no existence of a stationary field, imposed no boundary or decay condition, and used no weak, distributional, singular-source or non-potential-represented branch.
