## Postulate

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] and [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the smooth modal full-Choice branch of the latter is not used. Adopt as a model assumption of the framework the following scalar aperture-diffraction model.

**(a) [Data.]** Fix an angular frequency $\omega>0$ and wavenumber $k:=\omega/c$, with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Let $S\subset\{y\in\mathbb R^3:y_3=0\}\cap\{y:|y|\le a\}$ be a nonempty compact subset of a declared aperture plane $y_3=0$ with aperture radius $a>0$ (the screening plane and spatial region are read in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]), and let $\alpha$ be a finite complex measure on $\mathbb R^3$ supported in $S$ ([[def-complex-measure]], [[def-total-variation-of-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]) — the **aperture distribution** — with $\alpha$ read in volts so that the model field below carries the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ of an electric-field component and its pairings are those of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]].

**(b) [Model field.]** The model assigns to every observation point $x$ with $x_3>0$ the complex scalar amplitude

$$u(x):=\int G_k(x-y)\,d\alpha(y),$$

where $G_k(z)=e^{ik|z|}/(4\pi|z|)$ for $z\ne0$ is the outgoing Helmholtz kernel of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], together with the real scalar field $U(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and the model period-averaged squared field $(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. All model predictions are declared comparisons of this squared field between observation points; no absolute radiometric power or intensity calibration is adopted.

**(c) [Adopted regime and status.]** The model is the declared polarization-insensitive scalar approximation of aperture diffraction. It ignores the vector nature and polarization of the electromagnetic field, takes the aperture distribution rather than the exact screen traces as its datum, assigns no back-reaction of the diffracted field on the illumination and no screen interaction beyond the aperture, and is not derived from either branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] or from the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]]; it is a declared optical approximation, not an exact electromagnetic model. It does not assert that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and it does not identify $\alpha$ with the unknown exact Maxwell boundary traces: assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently is not a well-posed exact boundary problem, as recorded in [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]], and the error terms of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] are the controlled content of the model. No measured intensity, apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty budget, empirical comparison or quantitative radiometric calibration is adopted.

### Well-definedness and non-derivation notes

For fixed $x$ with $x_3>0$ and $y$ ranging over the compact support $S$ of $\alpha$, one has $|x-y|\ge x_3>0$, so $y\mapsto G_k(x-y)$ is continuous on $S$, bounded there by $1/(4\pi x_3)$; the pairing $\int G_k(x-y)\,d\alpha(y)$ is therefore the integral of a bounded continuous complex function against a finite complex measure and is defined by [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]], with $|u(x)|\le\|\alpha\|_{\mathrm{TV}}/(4\pi x_3)$ in the total variation of [[def-total-variation-of-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. The model permits the compact closed-radius support $|y|\le a$, including aperture corners: the integral and off-support regularity of the model field are those established for finite measures supported in a containing open ball of radius $A>a$ by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], while the sharp closed-radius estimates at $r\ge2a$ are proved directly in the consuming diffraction theorem and are not obtained by evaluating an open-support hypothesis at a boundary point.

The integral against a finite complex measure, the real-field reading and the squared field $\tfrac12|u|^2$ constitute the whole mathematical content adopted here; the physical reading uses the aperture plane and spatial region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], the relation $k=\omega/c$ and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Neither the smooth nor the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] implies this scalar source model, and the finite-conductivity and material branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no ideal aperture or screen model. The item uses no choice principle beyond those carried by the cited mathematical suppliers; the Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited verbatim from the kernel and boundary-representation suppliers and this postulate adds no choice use of its own. No derivation of the adopted data from the underlying postulates, and no empirical validation of the model, is claimed or implied by this item.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] and [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] ([[def-countable-choice]]), whose trace qualification is used in clause (d); the full-Choice modal branch of the latter is not used. Adopt the scalar aperture model and its notation from [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]: frequency $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, aperture radius $a>0$, finite complex aperture distribution $\alpha$ supported in the planar aperture $S\subset\{y_3=0\}\cap\{y:|y|\le a\}$, model field $u=G_k*\alpha$, real field $U(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and $T=2\pi/\omega$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]). Set $I(x):=(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. Then: (a) [Model field and Fraunhofer estimate] $u$ is $C^\infty$ on the half-space $\{x_3>0\}$ and on $\mathbb R^3\setminus S$, satisfies $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ there, and is outgoing in the sense of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]]: for $x=rn$ with $r\ge2a$ and $n\in S^2$, $$u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)+O\Bigl(\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}}{r}\Bigl[\frac ar+\frac{ka^2}{r}\Bigr]\Bigr)$$ uniformly in direction, and $r(\partial_ru-iku)=O(r^{-1})$ uniformly. (b) [Fresnel estimate] write $y_t=(y_1,y_2)$ and $\xi=(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ for transverse vectors; for the planar aperture and observation $x=(\xi_1,\xi_2,z)$ with $z>0$, $b\ge0$, $|\xi|\le b$ and any declared fixed small-angle range $(a+b)/z\le\eta_0<1$, where $0<\eta_0<1$, the Fresnel approximation replaces $R=|x-y|$ by $z+|\xi-y_t|^2/(2z)$ and $1/R$ by $1/z$ in the model integral with phase error $O(k(a+b)^4/z^3)$, relative amplitude error $O((a+b)^2/z^2)$ and absolute field error $O(\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}z^{-1}[(a+b)^2/z^2+k(a+b)^4/z^3])$. (c) [Intensity and error transfer] at every $x$ with $x_3>0$ the model period average satisfies $\frac1T\int_0^TU(x,s)^2\,ds=I(x)$ ([[lem-em-period-average]]). If $u_{\rm approx}$ is any approximation of $u$ with $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\delta(x)$, then $|\frac12|u_{\rm approx}(x)|^2-I(x)|\le\frac12\delta(x)(|u(x)|+|u_{\rm approx}(x)|)$; if moreover $u(x)\ne0$ and $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\epsilon(x)|u(x)|$, the relative intensity error is at most $2\epsilon(x)+\epsilon(x)^2$. In particular the Fraunhofer and Fresnel field errors of (a) and (b) bound the corresponding intensity errors; no new approximation is introduced by passing to $I$. (d) [Trace and scope] the aperture distribution $\alpha$ is an adopted model datum and is not identified with the exact Maxwell boundary data on the screen; assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently does not produce a well-posed exact boundary problem ([[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]]). The construction ignores polarization and aperture back-reaction, makes no claim that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and makes no measured-intensity, apparatus, sampling or empirical claim; only comparisons of $I$ between observation points are read as model predictions.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The model data of the Statement: $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, $a>0$, the compact planar aperture $S\subset\{y_3=0\}\cap\{|y|\le a\}$, the finite complex measure $\alpha$ supported in $S$, the model field $u=G_k*\alpha$ with $G_k(z)=e^{ik|z|}/(4\pi|z|)$ for $z\ne0$, the real field $U(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and $I=\frac12|u|^2$. All lengths are in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], and $c$, $\varepsilon_0$, $\mu_0$ are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

[F1] Model interface: the aperture distribution is a finite complex measure with total variation $\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}$ supported in the compact $S$, read in volts; for every $x$ with $x_3>0$ the pairing $\int G_k(x-y)\,d\alpha(y)$ is defined by [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]] and equals the model field $u(x)$; the same formula defines $u$ at every $x\notin S$, and $U$, $I$ are as in the Statement ([[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]], [[def-total-variation-of-a-signed-or-complex-measure]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]).

[F2] Outgoing-source and trace suppliers: assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; $G_k$ is locally integrable, $(-\Delta-k^2)G_k=\delta_0$ distributionally, and for a finite complex measure supported in an open ball the field $G_k*\alpha$ is $C^\infty$ outside its support, solves $(\Delta+k^2)w=0$ there, is outgoing with the Fraunhofer and Fresnel error terms of that item, and the aperture data are an explicitly specified scalar source, not the exact Maxwell boundary traces; assigning both aperture values independently is not a well-posed exact boundary problem ([[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]], [[def-countable-choice]]).

[F3] Finite-measure integral bound: let $h$ be Borel measurable and bounded on the support of the finite complex measure $\alpha$, with $M_h:=\sup_{\operatorname{supp}\alpha}|h|<+\infty$; then $h\in L^1(\alpha)=L^1(|\alpha|)$ and $\bigl|\int h\,d\alpha\bigr|\le\int|h|\,d|\alpha|\le M_h\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}$: the modulus bound for a general integrand is [[thm-integrals-against-signed-or-complex-measures-are-bounded-by-total-variation]], integrability in $L^1(\alpha)=L^1(|\alpha|)$ is the definition of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]], and since $\alpha$ is supported in $S$ the variation $|\alpha|$ vanishes off $S$ by its defining supremum over partitions ([[def-total-variation-of-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]) and is finite ([[thm-total-variation-is-a-measure]], [[thm-total-variation-of-a-complex-measure-is-finite]]), so monotonicity of the integral of nonnegative measurable functions gives $\int|h|\,d|\alpha|\le\int M_h\,d|\alpha|=M_h\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}$ ([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]).

[F4] Period average: for $\omega>0$, $T=2\pi/\omega$ and $u\in\mathbb C$, $\frac1T\int_0^T\operatorname{Re}(ue^{-i\omega t})^2\,dt=\frac12|u|^2$ ([[lem-em-period-average]]).

[F5] Modulus and conjugation: $z\overline z=|z|^2$, $|z|\ge0$, $|zw|=|z||w|$, and $\bigl||z|-|w|\bigr|\le|z-w|$ for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$ ([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]).

[F6] Elementary toolbox: $|a+bi|=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ and $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$ for real $\theta$, with $\sin'=\cos$, $\cos'=-\sin$, $|\cos\theta|\le1$ and $\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]); the Taylor remainder bound $|R_{n,a}f(x)|\le Ms^{n+1}/(n+1)!$ when $|f^{(n+1)}|\le M$ on the interval, with $R_{n,a}f=f-T_{n,a}f$ ([[cor-taylor-remainder-bound]], [[def-taylor-polynomial-and-remainder]]); the real-power derivatives $(x^\alpha)'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}$ on $(0,\infty)$ ([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]); the chain and algebra of derivatives ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]); the Euclidean norm and inner product with $\sqrt{\ }$ the nonnegative square root ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[thm-of-square-roots]], [[def-complex-exponential]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the supplier's off-support regularity with a slightly larger containing ball, re-derive the sharp closed-radius Fraunhofer and outgoing estimates from the explicit kernel with elementary Taylor bounds, establish the Fresnel estimates through the exact substitution $R=z\sqrt{1+s}$, and transfer the field errors to the intensity with the modulus inequalities.

1.1 [Off-support regularity and the Helmholtz equation] Since $S$ is compact and contained in the closed ball of radius $a$, choose the open ball $B_A(0)$ with $A:=a+1$, so that $S\subset B_A(0)$ and $\alpha$ is a finite complex measure supported in that open ball. By [F2] the field $G_k*\alpha$ is $C^\infty$ outside the support of $\alpha$ and solves $(\Delta+k^2)w=0$ there; since the support of $\alpha$ is contained in $S$, the field $u$ of [F1] is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\setminus S$ and satisfies $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ there; the half-space $\{x_3>0\}$ is disjoint from the plane containing $S$, hence is contained in $\mathbb R^3\setminus S$, so $u$ is $C^\infty$ there as well. [given, F1, F2]

1.2 [Elementary bounds: phase, radial expansion, kernel residual] First, for every real $\theta$ one has $|e^{i\theta}-1|\le|\theta|$: by [F6], $2(1-\cos\theta)=|e^{i\theta}-1|^2$ and $|\cos\theta|\le1$, and the Taylor bound for $\cos$ at $0$ with $n=1$ gives $|\cos\theta-1|\le\theta^2/2$, because $|\cos''|\le1$; hence $|e^{i\theta}-1|^2=2(1-\cos\theta)\le\theta^2$. Second, fix $y\in S$, $r\ge2a$, $n\in S^2$, and put $R:=|rn-y|$ and $h(s):=|rn-sy|$ for $s\in[0,1]$; then $h$ is $C^2$ on $[0,1]$ with $h(0)=r$, $h(1)=R$, $h'(0)=-n\cdot y$, $h'(s)=-(rn-sy)\cdot y/h(s)$, $h''(s)=|y|^2/h(s)-((rn-sy)\cdot y)^2/h(s)^3$, so $|h''|\le2|y|^2/h(s)\le2a^2/(r-a)\le4a^2/r$ by $h(s)\ge r-a\ge r/2$; the Taylor bound at $0$ with $n=1$ gives $|R-r+n\cdot y|\le2a^2/r$, and then $|r/R-1|=|r-R|/R\le(a+2a^2/r)/(r/2)=2a/r+4a^2/r^2\le4a/r$ since $|r-R|\le|n\cdot y|+2a^2/r\le a+a=2a$, $R\ge r/2$, and $r\ge2a$ gives $4a^2/r^2\le2a/r$. Third, with $R$ as above, $\partial_rR=(r-n\cdot y)/R$ satisfies $|\partial_rR|\le1$ and $|\partial_rR-1|\le|R-r+n\cdot y|/R\le4a^2/r^2$, and the exact kernel derivatives give $\partial_rG_k(rn-y)=\partial_rR\,(ik-1/R)\,e^{ikR}/(4\pi R)$ and hence $|\partial_rG_k-ikG_k|\le(1/(4\pi R))\,[\,k|\partial_rR-1|+|\partial_rR|/R\,]\le2ka^2/(\pi r^3)+1/(\pi r^2)$. [given, F6, algebra]

1.3 [Fresnel substitution and estimates] Fix the planar observation $x=(\xi_1,\xi_2,z)$ with $z>0$, $|\xi|\le b$, and let $y\in S$ with transverse part $y_t$; put $d_0:=a+b$, $s:=|\xi-y_t|^2/z^2$, so that $0\le s\le\eta_0^2<1$ on the declared range. Decomposing the Euclidean norm by [F6], $R=|x-y|=z\sqrt{1+s}$, hence $1/R=(1/z)(1+s)^{-1/2}$ and the Fresnel replacements are $R_F:=z(1+s/2)$ and $1/z$. The Taylor bound of [F6] at $0$ with $n=1$ gives $|\sqrt{1+s}-1-s/2|\le s^2/8$, because $|(d^2/dt^2)\sqrt{1+t}|=|\!-\!\frac14(1+t)^{-3/2}|\le1/4$ on $[0,s]$; the Taylor bound with $n=0$ gives $|(1+s)^{-1/2}-1|\le s/2$, because $|(d/dt)(1+t)^{-1/2}|=\frac12(1+t)^{-3/2}\le1/2$. Consequently the phase error satisfies $k|R-R_F|=kz|\sqrt{1+s}-1-s/2|\le kd_0^4/(8z^3)$, and the relative amplitude error satisfies $|1-(1+s)^{-1/2}|\le s/2\le d_0^2/(2z^2)$, where $s\le d_0^2/z^2$ by $|\xi-y_t|\le d_0$. [given, F1, F6, algebra]

1.4 [Period average equals the model intensity] Fix $x$ with $x_3>0$ and write $u=u(x)\in\mathbb C$; then $U(x,s)=\operatorname{Re}(ue^{-i\omega s})$, so [F4] applied with the complex number $u$ in both slots gives $\frac1T\int_0^TU(x,s)^2\,ds=\frac12|u|^2=I(x)$. [given, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Fraunhofer estimate at the closed radius] Fix $y\in S$, $r\ge2a$ and $n\in S^2$, and write $R=|rn-y|$. Using only the bounds of step 1.2 and the addition law of the exponential for $e^{ik(r-n\cdot y)}=e^{ikr}e^{-ikn\cdot y}$ from [F6], one has $\bigl|G_k(rn-y)-e^{ikr}e^{-ikn\cdot y}/(4\pi r)\bigr|=\bigl|e^{ikR}(r/R-1)+e^{ikR}-e^{ik(r-n\cdot y)}\bigr|/(4\pi r)\le(1/(4\pi r))\,[\,4a/r+k\cdot2a^2/r\,]\le(1/(\pi r))\,[\,a/r+ka^2/r\,]$, since $4/(4\pi)=1/\pi$ and $2/(4\pi)\le1/\pi$, and because the middle term was bounded by $|e^{i\theta}-1|\le|\theta|$ with $\theta:=k(R-r+n\cdot y)$ and $|\theta|\le2ka^2/r$. Integrating against $\alpha$ with the bound of [F3], applied to the bounded continuous function $y\mapsto G_k(rn-y)-e^{ikr}e^{-ikn\cdot y}/(4\pi r)$ on the compact support, gives $|u(rn)-e^{ikr}(4\pi r)^{-1}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)|\le\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}(\pi r)^{-1}[a/r+ka^2/r]$, uniformly in $n$; this is the displayed Fraunhofer estimate with a universal constant. [step 1.2, F1, F2, F3, F6, algebra]

2.2 [Absolute field error of the Fresnel replacement] With the substitutions of step 1.3, for $y\in S$: $\bigl|G_k(x-y)-e^{ikR_F}/(4\pi z)\bigr|\le(1/(4\pi))\,|1/R-1/z|+(1/(4\pi z))\,|e^{ikR}-e^{ikR_F}|\le(1/(4\pi))\,d_0^2/(2z^3)+(1/(4\pi z))\,k\,d_0^4/(8z^3)=(1/(4\pi z))\,[\,d_0^2/(2z^2)+kd_0^4/(8z^3)\,]$, where the first summand used $|1/R-1/z|=(1/z)|(1+s)^{-1/2}-1|\le d_0^2/(2z^3)$ and the second used $|e^{ikR}-e^{ikR_F}|\le k|R-R_F|\le kd_0^4/(8z^3)$ from the phase estimate of step 1.3. Integrating against $\alpha$ with [F3] gives $|u(x)-u_{\rm Fresnel}(x)|\le\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}(4\pi z)^{-1}[d_0^2/(2z^2)+kd_0^4/(8z^3)]$, the displayed absolute field error with universal constants; the phase and relative amplitude errors of step 1.3 are those displayed in (b). [step 1.3, F1, F2, F3, F6, algebra]

3.1 [Outgoing residual] With the third bound of step 1.2 and the same integration against the total variation [F3], $r|\partial_ru(rn)-iku(rn)|\le r\int|\partial_rG_k(rn-y)-ikG_k(rn-y)|\,d|\alpha|(y)\le\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}\,[\,2ka^2/(\pi r^2)+1/(\pi r)\,]$, which is uniformly $O(\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}r^{-1})$ in direction; this and step 2.1 give clause (a). [step 1.2, step 2.1, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.2 [Intensity error transfer] Let $u_{\rm approx}$ satisfy $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\delta(x)$ at the point $x$. By the reverse triangle inequality of [F5], $\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|-|u|\bigr|\le|u_{\rm approx}-u|\le\delta$, and by $|z|^2=z\overline z$ and multiplicativity of the modulus [F5], $\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2\bigr|=\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|-|u|\bigr|\,(|u_{\rm approx}|+|u|)\le\delta(x)(|u(x)|+|u_{\rm approx}(x)|)$; multiplying by $\frac12$ and comparing with step 1.4 gives the first bound of (c). If additionally $u(x)\ne0$ and $|u_{\rm approx}-u|\le\epsilon(x)|u(x)|$, then $|u_{\rm approx}|\le(1+\epsilon(x))|u(x)|$, so the absolute intensity error is at most $\frac12\epsilon(x)|u(x)|\,(2+\epsilon(x))|u(x)|=\bigl(\epsilon(x)+\frac12\epsilon(x)^2\bigr)|u(x)|^2=(2\epsilon(x)+\epsilon(x)^2)I(x)$, which is the stated relative bound; applying these two estimates to the Fraunhofer and Fresnel field errors of steps 2.1, 3.1 and 2.2 gives the final sentence of (c) with no new approximation. [step 1.4, step 2.1, step 2.2, F5, algebra]

4.1 [Trace caveat, scope and choice accounting] The aperture distribution $\alpha$ is the adopted datum of [F1] and is not identified with the exact Maxwell boundary data on the screen; by [F2] assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently is not a well-posed exact boundary problem, so no such identification or well-posedness is made. The construction never asserts that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations; it ignores polarization and aperture back-reaction, and it makes no measured-intensity, apparatus, sampling or empirical claim, only model comparisons of $I$ between observation points; this is clause (d). The only choice principle used is the Countable Choice carried by the two suppliers of [F2] and used in their trace and kernel interfaces; the period average of step 1.4 uses only the choice-free period-average lemma, and all other steps are explicit estimates and finite computations, so no further choice is invoked. [step 3.1, step 2.2, step 3.2, F1, F2, F4, given] ∎

## Remarks

- The two big-O statements of (a) are established by the proof in the quantitative form $|u(rn)-e^{ikr}(4\pi r)^{-1}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}d\alpha|\le\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}(\pi r)^{-1}[a/r+ka^2/r]$ and $r|\partial_ru-iku|\le\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}(2ka^2/(\pi r^2)+1/(\pi r))$, both uniform in direction; the big-O form is the same statement with a universal constant.
- The Fresnel error transfer is an error statement about the adopted model field, not about any measured optical intensity; the model comparison is between observation points of $I=\frac12|u|^2$ only.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice as carried by [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]], whose variational, Sobolev-compactness and compact-spectral steps use it; the algebraic computations below use no further choice. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary, $D:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ connected, $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$; let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline D\subseteq V$, and let $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})$ be a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $V$ ([[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Plane-wave instances are provided by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]]: if $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ and $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, then $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})(x)=(e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x},b\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x})$ satisfies the four phasor equations on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]). Adopt the ideal perfectly conducting (PEC) boundary model: the tangential component of the total electric field vanishes on $\partial O$. This is a declared idealization of the stationary interface conditions of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] with vanishing fields inside the conductor; it is not one of the finite-conductivity branches of [[post-em-material-closure]], and the induced surface charge and current are neither prescribed nor determined here. Let $e_T$ be the tangential projection of $-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$ on $\partial O$, and let $\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ be the unique $C^\infty$ field on $\overline D$ of [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] with $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ on $D$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$ and that lemma's outgoing modal condition on $S_R$. Set $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}:=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ and, on $D$, $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde E_{\rm inc}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$, $\widetilde B_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde B_{\rm inc}+\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$. Then: (a) [Phasor Maxwell] $(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ and $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ are $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pairs on $D$; and for every $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ on an open set $O'\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, the associated real fields of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]] satisfy on $O'\times\mathbb R$ the smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho\equiv0$ and $J\equiv0$. Consequently the associated real total fields $E_{\rm tot},B_{\rm tot}$ satisfy those source-free equations on $D\times\mathbb R$. (b) [PEC boundary condition] the tangential trace of $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}$ on $\partial O$ vanishes; hence for every unit normal field $n$ of $\partial O$ the associated real total electric field $E_{\rm tot}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E_{\rm tot}(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) satisfies $n\times E_{\rm tot}=0$ on $\partial O\times\mathbb R$. (c) [Uniqueness] if $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')$ is a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on an open set $V'\supseteq\overline D$ that is outgoing on $S_R$ in the modal sense of the vector Helmholtz lemma and has tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$, then $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')=(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ on $D$; equivalently $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ is the unique total source-free phasor pair in the corresponding $C^\infty$ closure class with that prescribed incident phasor, vanishing tangential electric trace, and outgoing scattered correction $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$ in the lemma's modal class. The total field itself is not required to be outgoing; an incident plane wave is generally not outgoing. (d) [Scope] one positive frequency $\omega=ck$, one smooth bounded stationary PEC obstacle with connected exterior, and $C^\infty$ incident and scattered classes only; no lossy, impedance, nonsmooth or dispersive obstacle, no determination of the induced surface charge or current, no radiation-zone amplitude or far-field asymptotics beyond the lemma's outgoing modal class, no point or singular source, no finite-energy or empirical claim.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice; the bounded $C^\infty$ obstacle $O$ with connected exterior $D$; $k>0$, $\omega=ck$, $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$; the open $V\supseteq\overline D$ and the $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})$ on $V$; the tangential projection $e_T$ of $-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$ on $\partial O$; the field $\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ and $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ of the Statement; the totals $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ and $\widetilde B_{\rm tot}=\widetilde B_{\rm inc}+\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ on $D$.

[F1] Exterior vector Helmholtz lemma: for the geometry, $k$ and $R$ above and every smooth $\mathbb C$-valued tangential field $e_T$ on $\partial O$, there is exactly one $E\in C^\infty(\overline D;\mathbb C^3)$ with $(\Delta+k^2)E=0$ on $D$, $\operatorname{div}E=0$ on $D$, tangential trace $E_{\rm tangential}=e_T$ on $\partial O$, and the modal outgoing condition on $S_R$ (its trace lies in $H^{1/2}(S_R;\mathbb C^3)$ and its normal derivative on $S_R$ equals the sphere Dirichlet-to-Neumann image of that trace componentwise in the weak trace sense); its normal boundary values satisfy the closure relation; the lemma assumes the Axiom of Choice ([[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]]).

[F2] Phasor conventions: a frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on an open set is a $C^\infty$ pair $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ satisfying $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=0$, $\operatorname{div}\widetilde B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E$ there, with divergence and curl acting componentwise on the complex fields; the associated real fields are $E=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde Ee^{-i\omega t})$, $B=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde Be^{-i\omega t})$ ([[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]).

[F3] Phasor calculus and equivalence: for $C^1$ complex fields the displayed partial-derivative and divergence/curl formulas hold; the real-part evaluation is injective; and the phasor system holds on an open set if and only if the associated real fields satisfy $\operatorname{div}E=0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$, $\operatorname{curl}B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$ there ([[lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence]]).

[F4] Smooth vacuum Maxwell branch at zero sources: for jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous and continuous sources, the adopted vacuum Maxwell postulate consists of the four equations $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$; with $\rho\equiv0$ and $J\equiv0$ this is exactly the source-free system of [F3] ([[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]).

[F5] Plane-wave amplitude equations: for $k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, $\omega>0$ and $e,b\in\mathbb C^3$, the plane-wave fields satisfy the source-free smooth Maxwell equations if and only if $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $\kappa\cdot b=0$, $\kappa\times e=\omega b$ and $\kappa\times b=-(\omega/c^2)e$; on the dispersion relation $|\kappa|=\omega/c$ the solutions are exactly the pairs with $\kappa\cdot e=0$ and $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ ([[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]], [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]).

[F6] Vector-calculus identities: for a $C^2$ real field on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$, $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}F=\nabla\operatorname{div}F-\Delta F$ and $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}F)=0$; divergence and curl are linear over the reals, and both identities and both operators extend to complex fields by applying them to real and imaginary parts componentwise ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]], [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]], [[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]).

[F7] Tangential projection and cross product: for a unit normal field $n$ of $\partial O$ and a field $w$, the tangential projection is $w_{\rm tang}:=w-(w\cdot n)n$ with the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and $n\times w=n\times w_{\rm tang}$ because $n\times n=0$; the cross product is bilinear and alternating ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]).

[F8] Material context: the PEC condition is the declared idealization of the stationary interface conditions of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] with vanishing fields inside the conductor; the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no $\sigma\to\infty$ ideal-conductor branch, and the fields of [[def-em-fields]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]] on the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] are the physical reading adopted by [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]].

[F9] Choice accounting: the Axiom of Choice of the Statement is used exactly through [F1]; all other computations are pointwise algebra and finite sums, and no further selection from infinite families is made ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the exterior vector Helmholtz lemma for the scattered field, verify the four phasor equations algebraically, transfer the real-field Maxwell statement through the phasor equivalence, read the PEC condition off the tangential traces, and reduce uniqueness of any candidate to the lemma's uniqueness clause.

1.1 [Setting and existence of the scattered field] The hypotheses of [F1] are met by the geometry, $k$ and $R$, and $e_T$ is a smooth $\mathbb C$-valued tangential field on $\partial O$ by [F7] applied to the $C^\infty$ incident field; hence [F1] supplies a unique $\widetilde E_{\rm scat}\in C^\infty(\overline D;\mathbb C^3)$ with $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$, $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ on $D$, tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$, and the outgoing modal condition on $S_R$. The field $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}:=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ is $C^\infty$ on $D$ by [F6], and the incident pair together with $e_T$ and the geometry is the data of the Statement. [given, F1, F6, F7]

2.1 [The scattered pair is source-free] On $D$: $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ by step 1.1; $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=i\omega\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ by the definition of $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$; $\operatorname{div}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=0$ by [F6]; and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}(\nabla\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}-\Delta\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=(i\omega)^{-1}k^2\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$, which equals $-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ because $k=\omega/c$ gives $k^2/(i\omega)=-ik^2/\omega=-i\omega c^{-2}$. All four equations of [F2] hold on the open set $D$ for a $C^\infty$ pair, so $(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ is a frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $D$. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F6, algebra]

2.2 [Uniqueness of the outgoing scattered correction] Let $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')$ be a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on an open $V'\supseteq\overline D$, outgoing on $S_R$ in the modal sense of [F1], with tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$. From the phasor equations and [F6], $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=i\omega\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B'=i\omega(-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E')=\omega^2c^{-2}\widetilde E'=k^2\widetilde E'$ and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E'=0$, so [F6] gives $\nabla\operatorname{div}\widetilde E'-\Delta\widetilde E'=-\Delta\widetilde E'=k^2\widetilde E'$, that is $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E'=0$ on $D$. The restriction of $\widetilde E'$ to $\overline D$ is $C^\infty$, has tangential trace $e_T$, divergence zero and the same modal outgoing condition on $S_R$; all hypotheses of the uniqueness clause of [F1] are therefore satisfied, and $\widetilde E'=\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ on $D$. Then $\widetilde B'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ on $D$ by the third phasor equation and the definition of $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F6, algebra]

3.1 [The total pair is source-free] On $D$ the incident pair satisfies the four equations of [F2] because $D\subseteq V$ and the pair is source-free on $V$; the scattered pair satisfies them by step 2.1; the totals $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ and $\widetilde B_{\rm tot}=\widetilde B_{\rm inc}+\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ are $C^\infty$ on $D$ as sums, and each of the four equations is linear over the complex scalars by [F6] applied to real and imaginary parts, so they hold for the totals; hence $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ is as well a frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $D$. [step 2.1, F2, F6, algebra]

4.1 [Real-field Maxwell statement] Let $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ be any $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on an open $O'\subseteq\mathbb R^3$. By [F3] its associated real fields satisfy the real system of [F3] on $O'\times\mathbb R$, and by [F4] that system with zero sources is exactly the smooth branch of the adopted vacuum Maxwell equations at $\rho\equiv0$, $J\equiv0$; the required regularity is the joint $C^1$ (indeed $C^\infty$) calculus supplied by [F3]. Applying this to $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ on $O'=D$, which is admissible by step 3.1, gives the asserted source-free equations for $E_{\rm tot},B_{\rm tot}$ on $D\times\mathbb R$. This proves the two statements of (a), the scattered and total clauses following from steps 2.1 and 3.1. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F3, F4]

4.2 [PEC boundary condition] On $\partial O$ one has $\widetilde E_{\rm tot,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+e_T=0$, because the tangential projection is the real-linear map of [F7] and $e_T$ is the tangential projection of $-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$; thus the tangential trace of $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}$ vanishes. For the associated real field, the tangential projection of $E_{\rm tot}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E_{\rm tot}(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ is $\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E_{\rm tot,tang}(x)e^{-i\omega t})=0$ by the real-linearity of the projection [F7] and of $\operatorname{Re}$; hence $n\times E_{\rm tot}=n\times E_{\rm tot,tang}=0$ on $\partial O\times\mathbb R$ by [F7]. This is (b). [step 3.1, F2, F7, algebra]

5.1 [Equivalent total formulation] Write a candidate total pair as $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc}+\widetilde E'',\widetilde B_{\rm inc}+\widetilde B'')$ on some open $V'\supseteq\overline D$, where $(\widetilde E'',\widetilde B'')$ is the scattered correction, required to be a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair and outgoing on $S_R$ in the modal sense, with the total tangential electric trace vanishing. By linearity [F6] the total tangential trace is $\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+\widetilde E''_{\rm tang}$, so the vanishing of the total trace is equivalent to $\widetilde E''_{\rm tang}=e_T$; by step 2.2 applied to $(\widetilde E'',\widetilde B'')$, the correction equals $(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ on $D$, hence the total equals $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$; conversely the constructed total has these properties by steps 3.1, 4.2 and the outgoing property of $\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ from step 1.1. This is the equivalent formulation of (c). [step 3.1, step 4.2, step 2.2, F6, algebra]

6.1 [Scope and choice accounting] Clause (d) records the exact hypotheses: one positive frequency, one smooth bounded stationary PEC obstacle with connected exterior, and $C^\infty$ incident and scattered classes; no lossy, impedance, nonsmooth or dispersive obstacle, no induced surface charge or current, no radiation-zone asymptotics beyond the modal class, no singular source and no empirical claim enters the argument. The PEC condition is adopted as an idealization by [F8] and is not derived from the material closures; the total field is not asserted to be outgoing, as an incident plane wave generally is not, and the uniqueness statement is exactly about the total-minus-incident correction. The plane-wave instance clause of the Statement is the specialization of the equivalence of [F5] to $|\kappa|=\omega/c$ and $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$, so it introduces no commitment beyond that cited statement. The only choice principle used is the Axiom of Choice assumed in the Statement through [F1], with the accounting of [F9]; all remaining steps are pointwise algebraic identities and finite sums. [step 4.2, step 2.2, step 5.1, F5, F8, F9, given] ∎

## Remarks

- The phrase "outgoing" applies to the scattered correction only. The constructed total field $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ is source-free on $D$ but need not be outgoing, and no decay or far-field asymptotic beyond the lemma's modal class is claimed.
- The ideal PEC condition is a boundary model, not a theorem about any particular conductor; the induced surface charge and current that would accompany it in a microscopic model are neither prescribed nor derived here.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] and [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the period-average and cross-section algebra itself uses no choice. Adopt the ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of [[def-em-ideal-harmonic-dipole-model]] with frequency $\omega>0$, wavenumber $k=\omega/c$ and amplitude $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$; let $E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d},S_{\rm d}$ be its fields and model flux. Let $\kappa\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, $e\in\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b:=\kappa\times e/\omega$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and let $(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ be the corresponding plane-wave fields of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$; by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] they satisfy the smooth-branch source-free vacuum Maxwell equations, and by [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](b) their period-averaged energy flux has magnitude $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). Define the **model differential scattering cross section** by

$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n):=\frac{r^2\langle S_{\rm d}(rn,\cdot)\cdot n\rangle}{\langle S_{\rm inc}\cdot\hat\kappa\rangle},\qquad n\in S^2,\ r>0,$$

where $\hat\kappa:=\kappa/|\kappa|$, $S_{\rm inc}:=E_{\rm inc}\times B_{\rm inc}/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]), and $\langle f\rangle:=\frac1T\int_0^Tf(s)\,ds$, $T=2\pi/\omega$, is the period average at fixed observation point. Then: (a) [Angular pattern] the ratio is independent of $r$ and of the averaging start, and for every $n\in S^2$

$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2|e|^2}.$$

(b) [Total cross section] with $d\sigma_{S^2}$ the surface measure of the unit sphere, $\sigma:=\int_{S^2}\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}\,d\sigma_{S^2}$ equals

$$\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2};$$

if $p_0=\alpha e$ for a complex scalar $\alpha$ (the scalar polarizability, in $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^2$), then $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$ and $\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4}|n\times\hat e|^2$ with $\hat e:=e/|e|$. (c) [Fidelity for arbitrary actual sources and matched windows] Let an actual compact smooth conserved source satisfy the exact hypotheses of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], with spatial support radius $a>0$, source-time interval $[\tau_0,\tau_1]$, moment $p_{\rm act}(u)$, variation bound $D(u)$ and constants $\Gamma_E,\Gamma_B$. These source data are independent of the prescribed model amplitude $p_0$. Put

$$p_{\rm h}(u):=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u}),\qquad M(u):=|p_{\rm act}''(u)-p_{\rm h}''(u)|.$$

For $n\in S^2$, $u\in[\tau_0,\tau_1]$, $r\ge2a$, define

$$H(u,r):=\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}[D(u)+M(u)].$$

The actual retarded fields and the model fields satisfy, uniformly in $n$,

$$|E_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-E_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)|\le H(u,r),$$

$$|B_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-B_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)|\le\frac{\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c}{r^2}+\frac{H(u,r)}c.$$

Also retain the sharper direct source-leading-field consequence

$$|B_{\rm act}-B_{\rm d}|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0[D(u)+M(u)]}{4\pi cr}$$

at the same events. If $p_{\rm act}''=p_{\rm h}''$ on a specified finite window, $M\equiv0$ there and these give the full matched dipole bounds; in particular they imply the coarser electric bound $\Gamma_E/r^2+\mu_0D/(2\pi r)$. Neither moment matching nor $D\equiv0$ is automatic. A sound sufficient matched branch is $p_{\rm act}=p_{\rm h}+a_0+b_0u$ on an open neighbourhood of the window (any fixed real vectors $a_0,b_0$). Such a branch has actual compact realizations over any finite window: choose a smooth time cutoff $\eta$ equal to $1$ near the window, let $p_\eta:=\eta\,(p_{\rm h}+a_0+b_0u)$, choose a nonnegative smooth spatial bump $\sigma$ with support inside $B_a$ and integral $1$, and set $\rho:=-p_\eta\cdot\nabla\sigma$, $J:=p_\eta'\sigma$. Then continuity holds and the actual moment is $p_\eta$; outside the window it is tapered. Apply the actual-source theorem with the resulting $D$ and $\Gamma$, retaining every finite-radius and source-variation error. No eternal harmonic moment of a compact-time source is asserted. (d) [Scope] conditional predictions of the adopted ideal model: no measured cross section, no frequency-domain response law (the amplitude $p_0$ is prescribed model data), no magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole content, no self-force, material response, finite-size or empirical claim; the scalar-$\alpha$ clause records a declared proportional response, not a derived polarizability. In all complex-amplitude formulas $|v|^2=\sum_i|v_i|^2$ is the Hermitian norm square; $n\times v$ is complex-linear for real $n$. The $p_0=0$ case gives zero scattered fields and cross sections while the nonzero incident intensity still defines the ratios. Actual-source fidelity assumes only the explicitly quantified mismatch and source hypotheses; it does not turn the model cross section into a measured or self-consistent scattering prediction.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The model data of [[def-em-ideal-harmonic-dipole-model]]: $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$, the model fields $E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d}$ and flux $S_{\rm d}$ on $(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})\times\mathbb R$; the plane-wave data $\kappa$, $e\ne0$ with $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$, and the fields $E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc}$, $S_{\rm inc}$; the constants $c,\varepsilon_0,\mu_0$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] with $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$; the period $T=2\pi/\omega$ and the cross section of the Statement.

[F1] Model interface: $E_{\rm d}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(w(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ with $w(x):=-\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p_0)e^{ikr}$, $r=|x|$, $n=x/r$; $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$; $S_{\rm d}=E_{\rm d}\times B_{\rm d}/\mu_0$ is the flux of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] evaluated at the model fields ([[def-em-ideal-harmonic-dipole-model]]).

[F2] Incident plane wave: $(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ are the plane-wave fields of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with amplitude $e$ and $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$, $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, satisfying the smooth source-free vacuum Maxwell equations by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]]; their period-averaged flux satisfies $\langle S_{\rm inc}\rangle=I_{\rm inc}\hat\kappa$ with $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ ([[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]).

[F3] Period averages: for $a,d\in\mathbb C$, $\frac1T\int_0^T\operatorname{Re}(ae^{-i\omega t})\operatorname{Re}(de^{-i\omega t})\,dt=\frac12\operatorname{Re}(a\overline d)$; in particular the mean of the real square is $\frac12|a|^2$ ([[lem-em-period-average]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]).

[F4] Cross product and norm identities: the cross product is bilinear and alternating; $|n\times(n\times v)|=|n\times v|\le|v|$ for $|n|=1$; $n\times(u+iv)=n\times u+i\,n\times v$ for real $n$; $|n\times v|^2=\sum_i|(n\times v)_i|^2$ is the Hermitian norm square ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]).

[F5] Sphere moments: for the surface measure $\sigma_{S^2}$ of the unit sphere, $\sigma_{S^2}(S^2)=4\pi$, $\int_{S^2}n\,d\sigma_{S^2}=0$, $\int_{S^2}n_in_j\,d\sigma_{S^2}=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$, and for every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2\,d\sigma_{S^2}=\frac{4\pi}{3}|a|^2$ and $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2\,d\sigma_{S^2}=\frac{8\pi}{3}|a|^2$ ([[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]]).

[F6] Actual-source theorem: under the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] (jointly $C^\infty$ conserved sources vanishing outside $\overline B_a(0)\times[\tau_0,\tau_1]$, $u\in[\tau_0,\tau_1]$), for $n\in S^2$, $r\ge2a$, $|E_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p_{\rm act}''(u))|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0D(u)}{4\pi r}$ and $|B_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-\frac{n\times E_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)}{c}|\le\frac{\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c}{r^2}$, and the sharper bound $|B_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-\frac{n\times E_{\rm lead}(n,u,r)}{c}|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}$ with $E_{\rm lead}=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times V_{\rm act})$; the constants $\Gamma_E,\Gamma_B$ depend only on $a,c,\mu_0$ and the source suprema and the theorem assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], [[def-countable-choice]]).

[F7] Window construction toolbox: smooth compactly supported cutoffs and localized bumps exist with the properties used below ([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]], [[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]]); integration by parts holds on a bounding rectangle ([[thm-integration-by-parts]], [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]]), and the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison identifies the Lebesgue and Riemann integrals of the continuous integrands used there ([[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]); the first fundamental theorem gives the derivative of an integral over a moving endpoint ([[thm-ftc-first-part]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the model flux pointwise from the double cross product, evaluate its period average with the period-average lemma, divide by the incident flux, integrate the pattern against the sphere moments for the total, and obtain the actual-source fidelity bounds by adding the dipole theorem's errors to the moment mismatch through the norm inequalities of the cross product.

1.1 [Model flux along the observation direction] Fix $n\in S^2$ and $r>0$. By [F1], $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$ and $n\cdot E_{\rm d}=0$, since $n\times(n\times p_0)$ is orthogonal to $n$; hence with the vector identity $E_{\rm d}\times(n\times E_{\rm d})=n|E_{\rm d}|^2-E_{\rm d}(n\cdot E_{\rm d})$ of [F4], $S_{\rm d}\cdot n=\frac1{\mu_0}(E_{\rm d}\times B_{\rm d})\cdot n=\frac1{\mu_0c}(E_{\rm d}\times(n\times E_{\rm d}))\cdot n=\frac{|E_{\rm d}|^2}{\mu_0c}$, because $n\cdot n=1$. [given, F1, F4, algebra]

1.2 [The model field is the leading field of the harmonic waveform] For $u=t-r/c$ one has $e^{i(kr-\omega t)}=e^{-i\omega u}$; since $p_{\rm h}''(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$ by [F1] of the harmonic lemma as recorded in [[def-em-ideal-harmonic-dipole-model]], and $n\times(n\times\cdot)$ is real-linear by [F4], $E_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p_{\rm h}''(u))$ and $B_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)=\frac1c n\times E_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)=-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi cr}n\times p_{\rm h}''(u)$, the last identity by the double-cross computation of [F4]. [given, F1, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Period average and the averaged radial power] At fixed $x=rn$ the amplitude $w=w(x)$ of [F1] is independent of $t$, and $E_{\rm d}(rn,t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$; by [F3] with $a=d=w$, $\langle|E_{\rm d}|^2\rangle=\frac12|w|^2$. Evaluating $|w|^2$ with [F4], $|w|^2=\bigl(\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}\bigr)^2|n\times(n\times p_0)|^2=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4}{16\pi^2r^2}|n\times p_0|^2$, because $|n\times(n\times p_0)|=|n\times p_0|$; therefore $r^2\langle S_{\rm d}\cdot n\rangle=\frac{r^2}{\mu_0c}\langle|E_{\rm d}|^2\rangle=\frac{\mu_0\omega^4}{32\pi^2c}|n\times p_0|^2$, independent of $r$. [step 1.1, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

2.2 [Electric and magnetic fidelity bounds] Let $p_{\rm act}$ and $D,\Gamma_E,\Gamma_B$ be the actual-source data of [F6]. Subtracting the two leading fields, $E_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-E_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)=\bigl[E_{\rm act}-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p_{\rm act}'')\bigr]+\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times\bigl(n\times(p_{\rm act}''-p_{\rm h}'')\bigr)$, so taking norms and using $|n\times(n\times w)|\le|w|$ of [F4] and $|p_{\rm act}''-p_{\rm h}''|=M(u)$, the first bound of [F6] gives $|E_{\rm act}-E_{\rm d}|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0D(u)}{4\pi r}+\frac{\mu_0M(u)}{4\pi r}=H(u,r)$, uniformly in $n$ at fixed $u$. For the magnetic field, $|B_{\rm act}-B_{\rm d}|\le|B_{\rm act}-\frac1c n\times E_{\rm act}|+\frac1c|n\times(E_{\rm act}-E_{\rm d})|\le\frac{\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c}{r^2}+\frac{H(u,r)}{c}$ by the second bound of [F6], [F4] and the electric bound just proved. For the sharper direct estimate, [F6] gives $|B_{\rm act}-\frac1c n\times E_{\rm lead}(V_{\rm act})|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}$ with $E_{\rm lead}=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times V_{\rm act})$, and by the double-cross computation of [F4] applied to $V_{\rm act}$ and $p_{\rm h}''$, $\frac1c n\times E_{\rm lead}(V_{\rm act})-B_{\rm d}=-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi cr}n\times(V_{\rm act}-p_{\rm h}'')$; hence $|B_{\rm act}-B_{\rm d}|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0(D(u)+M(u))}{4\pi cr}$ by the triangle inequality and $|V_{\rm act}-p_{\rm h}''|\le D+M$ from the replacement bound of [F6]. When $M\equiv0$ on the window the bounds reduce to $H=\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0D}{4\pi r}\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0D}{2\pi r}$, and neither $M\equiv0$ nor $D\equiv0$ is automatic. [step 1.2, F4, F6, algebra]

3.1 [Independence of the averaging start] For any real $s$, define $G(s):=\int_s^{s+T}|E_{\rm d}(rn,t)|^2dt$. By [F7] the first fundamental theorem gives $G'(s)=|E_{\rm d}(rn,s+T)|^2-|E_{\rm d}(rn,s)|^2=0$, because the exponential encoding of [F1] and the addition law give $e^{-i\omega(t+T)}=e^{-i\omega t}e^{-2\pi i}=e^{-i\omega t}$, so $t\mapsto E_{\rm d}(rn,t)$ is $T$-periodic; hence $G$ is constant and the mean $\frac1T\int_s^{s+T}|E_{\rm d}|^2=\frac1T\int_0^T|E_{\rm d}|^2$ is independent of the start, so the cross-section ratio of step 2.1 is as well. [step 2.1, F1, F7, algebra]

3.2 [Matched compact-window realization] Let the window be a compact interval $W$ in the source-time line and let $a_0,b_0\in\mathbb R^3$. Choose a real $C^\infty$ cutoff $\eta$ in time, equal to $1$ on a neighbourhood of $W$, supported in a compact interval $(t_0,t_1)$ strictly containing $W$, as supplied by [F7], and set $p_\eta:=\eta\,(p_{\rm h}+a_0+b_0u)$. Choose a nonnegative smooth bump $\sigma$ supported in $B_a$ with $\int\sigma=1$ as supplied by [F7] and set $\rho(y,u):=-p_\eta(u)\cdot\nabla\sigma(y)$, $J(y,u):=p_\eta'(u)\sigma(y)$; both are $C^\infty$ and vanish outside $\overline B_a(0)\times[t_0,t_1]$, and $\partial_u\rho+\operatorname{div}J=-p_\eta'\cdot\nabla\sigma+p_\eta'\cdot\nabla\sigma=0$, so the conservation equation holds. Integrating by parts on a rectangle containing $B_a$ and using Fubini as in [F7], $\int_{B_a}\rho(y,u)\,dy=-p_\eta(u)\cdot\int_{B_a}\nabla\sigma=0$, so the total charge vanishes, and $\int_{B_a}y_i\rho(y,u)\,dy=-\sum_jp_{\eta,j}(u)\int_{B_a}y_i\partial_j\sigma(y)\,dy=p_{\eta,i}(u)$ because $\int_{B_a}y_i\partial_j\sigma=-\delta_{ij}\int_{B_a}\sigma=-\delta_{ij}$ by the same integration by parts; hence the actual moment of the source is $p_{\rm act}=p_\eta$. On $W$ one has $\eta\equiv1$, so $p_{\rm act}''=p_{\rm h}''$ there and the mismatch $M$ vanishes on the window; applying the fidelity bounds of step 2.2 to this source preserves every finite-radius and source-variation error term $D,\Gamma_E,\Gamma_B$ computed from it, and outside the window the moment is tapered, so no eternal harmonic moment is asserted. [step 2.2, F6, F7, algebra]

4.1 [Angular pattern] Dividing the averaged radial power of step 2.1 by $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ of [F2] gives $\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2|e|^2}$, and substituting $\mu_0^2=\frac1{\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$ from [[def-em-si-conventions]] gives the displayed second form $\frac{\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}$; with step 3.1 this is clause (a). [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2, algebra]

5.1 [Total cross section] Write $p_0=u+iv$ with $u,v\in\mathbb R^3$; by [F4], $|n\times p_0|^2=|n\times u|^2+|n\times v|^2$ for every $n$, so integrating the pattern of step 4.1 over $S^2$ and using $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma_{S^2}=\frac{8\pi}{3}|a|^2$ of [F5] for the real vectors $u$ and $v$ gives $\int_{S^2}|n\times p_0|^2d\sigma_{S^2}=\frac{8\pi}{3}(|u|^2+|v|^2)=\frac{8\pi}{3}|p_0|^2$; hence $\sigma=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4}{16\pi^2|e|^2}\cdot\frac{8\pi}{3}|p_0|^2=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2}$, and the $\varepsilon_0$ form follows from $\mu_0^2=\frac1{\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$. For the scalar branch $p_0=\alpha e$, [F4] gives $|n\times p_0|^2=|\alpha|^2|n\times e|^2=|\alpha|^2|e|^2|n\times\hat e|^2$ and $|p_0|^2=|\alpha|^2|e|^2$, so both displayed substitutions hold; this is clause (b). [step 4.1, F4, F5, algebra]

6.1 [Scope and choice accounting] Clause (d) is the exact scope: the cross sections are conditional predictions of the adopted model, $p_0$ is prescribed data rather than a derived response, and no measured, material, multipole, self-force or finite-size claim is made; the $p_0=0$ case gives zero model fields and zero cross sections while the nonzero $I_{\rm inc}$ still normalizes the ratios. The only choice principle used is the Countable Choice carried by the actual-source theorem and the sphere-moment interface of [F5], both invoked in the finite-window and integration steps; the period averages, the double-cross algebra, the division by the incident flux and the integration of the pattern use only finite sums and the explicit suppliers [F3], [F4], so no further choice is made. [step 4.1, step 5.1, step 2.2, step 3.2, given] ∎

## Remarks

- The incident intensity used is the framework's own $I_{\rm inc}=\varepsilon_0c|e|^2/2$ from [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](b); no source's printed flux normalisation is used, and the two displayed $\varepsilon_0$ and $\mu_0$ forms of the cross sections are related by $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$.
- The fidelity clause compares the model with actual compact smooth sources through the explicit $D,\Gamma$ bounds plus the moment mismatch $M$; it is not a claim that an actual scatterer's measured cross section equals the model value, and the matched-window branch only shows that the mismatch term is genuinely removable for a realized source class.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]]; the linearization below and [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]] use no choice. Assume the setting and postulates of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] for a test particle with charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-sources]](a)) and externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, in the incident plane-wave field of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with wavevector $\kappa$, complex amplitude $e\ne0$, $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $|\kappa|=\omega/c$ and $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ as in [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]]; write $E_{\rm inc}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x-\omega t)})$ and $B_{\rm inc}=\kappa\times E_{\rm inc}/\omega$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Assume that for some $\eta_0>0$ and a common open interval $I\ni0$, for every $\eta\in(-\eta_0,\eta_0)$ there is a $C^2$ future timelike massive solution $r_\eta:I\to\mathbb R^3$ of the adopted four-force law in the external field $\eta(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ (no self-field, recoil or material force), and that the family admits a uniform first-order expansion: there are $r_1\in C^2(I;\mathbb R^3)$ and, for every compact $K\subset I$, a constant $C_K$ with

$$|r_\eta(t)-x_0-\eta r_1(t)|+|\dot r_\eta(t)-\eta\dot r_1(t)|\le C_K\eta^2\qquad(t\in K,\ |\eta|<\eta_0)$$

about a fixed position $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$. The family time interval $I$ is not required to contain a full period, and no solution $r_\eta$ outside $I$ is assumed. For the periodic-response conclusions (b), (c), impose the following explicit preparation (P): the unique global harmonic-ODE extension of $r_1$ supplied after (a) by [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]](d), with its actual value and derivative at $0$, is $T$-periodic, $T=2\pi/\omega$. Equivalently its affine drift is zero, or $r_1'(0)=\operatorname{Re}(iw/\omega)$ with $w=(q/m)e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$. The linearized equation and affine local/global classification in (a) hold for every stated family even without (P); overlap-only periodicity on a short $I$ is not substituted for (P). Then: (a) [Linearized equation] $\ddot r_1(t)=\frac qmE_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)=\frac qm\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x_0-\omega t)})$ on $I$. (b) [Induced dipole under preparation (P)] $x_0$ is the zeroth-order rest/reference position. Let $a$ be the mean of the global periodic first-order response, so on $I$ one has $r_1=z_p+a$ with $z_p(t)=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$. The arbitrary constant $a$ is retained: no exact mean or periodicity of the full nonlinear family is asserted. The oscillating part of the first-order dipole coefficient $q(r_1-a)$ is $\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega t})$ with complex amplitude

$$p_0=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}\,e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0};$$

equivalently $p_0=\alpha e'$ with $\alpha=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}$ (units $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^2$) and the unimodular factor $e'=e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$, $|e'|=|e|$. (c) [Leading Thomson-model cross section] substituting this $p_0$ into [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]](b) gives

$$\sigma_{\rm T}=\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}=\frac{8\pi}{3}\Bigl(\frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0mc^2}\Bigr)^2,$$

independent of $\omega$ and of the phase factor. (d) [Scope] this is a controlled conditional first variation of the adopted relativistic external-force law under the stated solution-family hypotheses. It is not the exact Newtonian force postulate, it does not assert existence, persistence, stability or self-consistency of the family, it excludes self-force, radiation reaction and material media, and it makes no empirical, measurement, atomic-physics or frequency-response claim. In (a), every local $r_1$ has the unique global harmonic extension $z_p+a+bt$, with $b=r_1'(0)-z_p'(0)$, $a=r_1(0)-z_p(0)$. Thus the general affine-drift response is also retained; preparation (P) sets $b=0$ for (b), (c) and leaves $a$ arbitrary. For a nonzero $\eta$, the associated leading ideal harmonic model has incident amplitude $\eta e$ and induced dipole amplitude $\eta p_0$. Their squared flux factors $\eta^2$ cancel in its cross-section ratio; $\sigma_{\rm T}$ is this leading-model coefficient, not an assertion of the exact nonlinear particle's emitted field or cross section. At $q=0$ the induced amplitude and $\sigma_{\rm T}$ are zero without any division by $q$. All $\eta$ estimates apply only to the open parameter domain on which the family was declared.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The setting, family and preparation (P) of the Statement: charge $q\in\mathbb R$ and mass $m>0$ ([[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]); the plane-wave data $\kappa,e,\omega$ with $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$; the family $r_\eta$ on the common open interval $I\ni0$ with the uniform first-order expansion about $x_0$; the first-order function $r_1\in C^2(I;\mathbb R^3)$; the harmonic data $w=(q/m)e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$ and $z_p(t)=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$.

[F1] Adopted force law (external supplier, whose carrier is the referenced in-run item): under its postulates, with the coordinate reading $r$, velocity $v=r'$ and $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ of a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline in a prescribed exterior field $(E,B)$, the coordinate momentum $p=m\gamma v$ satisfies $\frac{dp}{dt}=q(E+v\times B)$ and $\frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=qE\cdot v$; the norm $\eta(U,U)$ is constant and a solution with future timelike data remains future timelike; and for every $\delta\in(0,1)$, wherever $|v|/c\le\delta$, $|\gamma-1|\le\frac{|v|^2/c^2}{2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}}$ and $|p-mv|\le m|v|\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}}$, with constants depending only on $\delta$; the statement is conditional on the adopted postulates and excludes self-force, radiation reaction and material media ([[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]], [[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]]).

[F2] Plane-wave fields: $E_{\rm inc}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x-\omega t)})$, $B_{\rm inc}=\kappa\times E_{\rm inc}/\omega$ are jointly $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]); in particular, on every compact subset of $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ they are bounded and uniformly continuous with bounded first derivatives, and on a compact interval $L\subset I$ the maps $t\mapsto E_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)$, $t\mapsto B_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)$ are continuous ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]).

[F3] Harmonic response lemma: for $\omega>0$, $T=2\pi/\omega$, $w\in\mathbb C^3$, the particular solution $z_p(t)=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$ is $C^\infty$ with $z_p''=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ and is $T$-periodic; every $C^2$ solution of that equation on $\mathbb R$ is $z_p+a+bt$ with unique $a,b$; it is $T$-periodic if and only if $b=0$; on any nonempty open interval the local solutions have a unique global extension $Z$; with $b=z'(t_*)-z_p'(t_*)$, and for $b=0$ the mean over every complete period is $a$ ([[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]]).

[F4] Cross-section theorem: for the ideal harmonic model with incident amplitude $e$ and dipole amplitude $p_0$, the total model cross section is $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2}$, and the scalar branch with $p_0=\alpha e$ is $\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$; the result assumes Countable Choice as carried by its suppliers ([[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]], [[def-countable-choice]]).

[F5] Elementary calculus and algebra: vector-valued differentiation and integration are componentwise ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]); the second fundamental theorem evaluates $\int_a^bG'=G(b)-G(a)$ for integrable $G'$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]), a continuous real function on a closed interval is Riemann integrable ([[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]), the first fundamental theorem differentiates the integral function ([[thm-ftc-first-part]]), and $m\le f\le M$ on $[a,b]$ gives $m(b-a)\le\int_a^bf\le M(b-a)$ with the corresponding error bound ([[lem-integral-elementary-bounds]]); sums, products and compositions of differentiable maps obey the algebra and chain rules ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]); the cross product is bilinear and alternating with $|u\times v|\le|u||v|$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]); and $|e^{i\theta}|=1$ for real $\theta$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; take the exact integrated coordinate momentum equation of the adopted force law for the family, pass the uniform first-order expansion through the finite-interval integral, differentiate the resulting identity, and then classify the first-order harmonic response with the affine/periodic lemma and substitute into the cross-section theorem.

1.1 [Uniform smallness of the velocity and of $\gamma-1$] Let $K\subset I$ be a nonempty compact interval containing $0$ in its interior (any compact subinterval of $I$ containing $0$ will do); the expansion hypothesis gives $|v_\eta(t)|\le|\eta||\dot r_1(t)|+C_K\eta^2\le|\eta|(\|\dot r_1\|_K+C_K)$ for $|\eta|<\eta_0$ and $t\in K$, where $\|\dot r_1\|_K$ is finite by continuity on the compact $K$. Choose $\eta_1\in(0,\min\{\eta_0,1\})$ with $\eta_1(\|\dot r_1\|_K+C_K)\le c/2$; then for $0<|\eta|<\eta_1$ every $t\in K$ has $|v_\eta(t)|/c\le1/2$, so the low-speed clause of [F1] with $\delta=1/2$ gives $|\gamma_\eta(t)-1|\le\frac{|v_\eta(t)|^2}{2c^2(1-1/4)^{3/2}}\le C_1\eta^2$ for a constant $C_1$ depending only on $K,\eta_1$ and the data, uniformly in $t\in K$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 [Uniform convergence of the scaled momentum and of its derivative] With $\gamma_\eta=(1-|v_\eta|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and $P_\eta:=m\gamma_\eta v_\eta$, write $\frac1\eta P_\eta=m\gamma_\eta\frac{v_\eta}\eta=m\frac{v_\eta}\eta+m(\gamma_\eta-1)\frac{v_\eta}\eta$; by the expansion hypothesis $\frac{v_\eta}\eta\to\dot r_1$ uniformly on $K$ with error $C_K|\eta|$, and by step 1.1 $|\gamma_\eta-1|\le C_1\eta^2$ while $\bigl|\frac{v_\eta}\eta\bigr|\le\|\dot r_1\|_K+C_K|\eta|$ is uniformly bounded, so $\frac{P_\eta}\eta\to m\dot r_1$ uniformly on $K$ as $\eta\to0$ with $\eta\ne0$. Moreover, dividing the exact coordinate force law of [F1] by $\eta$ gives, for $t\in K$ and $\eta\ne0$, $\frac1\eta P_\eta'(t)=q\bigl[E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)+v_\eta(t)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)\bigr]$, and this right-hand side converges uniformly on $K$ to $qE_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)$: the fields are uniformly continuous on a compact tube around $\{x_0\}\times K$ and $r_\eta(t)\to x_0$ uniformly by the expansion, while $|v_\eta(t)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)|\le|v_\eta(t)|\sup|B_{\rm inc}|\le C_2|\eta|$ by [F2] and the bilinearity and norm bound of [F5]. [step 1.1, given, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

3.1 [First-order equation] Fix $\eta\ne0$ with $|\eta|<\eta_1$ and fix a component index $i$. The scalar map $t\mapsto(P_\eta)_i(t)$ is $C^1$ on $K$ with continuous derivative $(P_\eta')_i=q\eta[E_{\rm inc}+v_\eta\times B_{\rm inc}]_i$, so $(P_\eta')_i$ is Riemann integrable on every closed subinterval of $K$ by [F5]; splitting at $0$ and applying the second fundamental theorem [F5] to the intervals $[0,t]$ for $t\ge0$ and $[t,0]$ for $t\le0$ (with the orientation convention of the displayed one-sided differences) gives, for every $t\in K$, $\frac{(P_\eta)_i(t)-(P_\eta)_i(0)}\eta=\int_0^t\frac{(P_\eta')_i(s)}\eta\,ds=q\int_0^t[E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(s),s)+v_\eta(s)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(s),s)]_i\,ds$. By the uniform convergence of step 2.1 applied componentwise, the integrands converge uniformly on $K$ to $qE_{\rm inc}(x_0,\cdot)_i$, so the integral bound of [F5] lets $\eta\to0$: the left side tends to $m[(\dot r_1)_i(t)-(\dot r_1)_i(0)]$ and the right side to $q\int_0^tE_{\rm inc}(x_0,s)_i\,ds$. The fundamental theorem [F5] differentiates the right side in $t$ to $qE_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)_i$, and the left side is differentiable with derivative $m(\ddot r_1)_i(t)$; hence $m\ddot r_1(t)=qE_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)$ componentwise on $K$. Every point $t\in I$ lies in such a compact $K\subset I$ containing $0$, so the identity holds on all of $I$ and is clause (a). [step 2.1, F2, F5, algebra]

4.1 [Harmonic classification and the induced dipole] Equation (a) reads $\ddot r_1(t)=\operatorname{Re}(w e^{-i\omega t})$ on $I$ with $w=(q/m)e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$ by [F2]. By the local-clause of the harmonic lemma [F3], on $I$ one has $r_1=z_p+a+bt$ for a unique pair $(a,b)$, the same formula defines the unique global extension $Z$ of $r_1$, and $b=0$ exactly when $Z$ is $T$-periodic, equivalently when $r_1'(0)=z_p'(0)=\operatorname{Re}(iw/\omega)$ (differentiating $z_p$ at $0$ with the rules of [F5]). Preparation (P) therefore says exactly $b=0$, so on $I$ we have $r_1=z_p+a$ with $a$ the mean of the periodic extension over every complete period by [F3]. Then $q(r_1-a)=qz_p(t)=\operatorname{Re}(-qw\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega t})$ with $p_0=-qw/\omega^2=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$, because $w=(q/m)e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$; writing $e'=e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$ one has $|e'|=|e|$ by [F5], so $p_0=\alpha e'$ with $\alpha=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}$. The arbitrary mean $a$ is retained and no mean or periodicity of the nonlinear family is asserted; this is clause (b). [step 3.1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

5.1 [Thomson cross section] Apply the cross-section formula of [F4] with the incident amplitude $e$ and dipole amplitude $p_0$ of step 4.1: $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}$, and $|p_0|^2=\frac{q^4}{m^2\omega^4}|e|^2$ because $|e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}|=1$; substituting cancels $\omega^4$ and $|e|^2$ and gives $\sigma_{\rm T}=\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}$. Multiplying out, $\frac{8\pi}{3}\bigl(\frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0mc^2}\bigr)^2=\frac{8\pi}{3}\cdot\frac{q^4}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}=\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}$, the same value, and it depends neither on $\omega$ nor on the phase factor beyond the unimodular $e'$; this is clause (c). [step 4.1, F4, F5, algebra]

6.1 [Scope and choice accounting] Clause (d) records the exact content: the result is a conditional first variation of the adopted external-force law under the stated family and preparation hypotheses, with the affine drift retained in general and set to zero only by (P) for (b) and (c); no existence, persistence, stability or self-consistency of the family, no self-force, radiation reaction or material content, and no empirical, atomic or frequency-response claim is made. The $\eta^2$ scaling statement is a remark on the leading model: for nonzero $\eta$ the incident amplitude $\eta e$ and the induced amplitude $\eta p_0$ scale together, so the ratio defining $\sigma_{\rm T}$ is unchanged; at $q=0$ the amplitude $p_0=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$ and $\sigma_{\rm T}$ vanish by direct substitution without any division by $q$. The only choice principle used is the Countable Choice carried by the cross-section theorem [F4]; the uniform-limit, integral and harmonic-classification arguments use only the explicit suppliers [F1], [F3], [F5] and finite compact intervals. [step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, F1, F3, F4, given] ∎
